facades._: Facade colours MEASURED from 4K walk (Nov 2023, eye level) and drone (Nov 2022, overcast) footage, 2026-08-03 — see git history. walls = the dominant wall tone; accents = the secondary materials on the same building; styles = which facade tile it wears. Every key must name a mass the renderer actually builds (tests/campus-facades.test.mjs pins that) — the previous file spent eleven entries on names the data does not carry, and they drew nothing. WS-E4 (2026-08-06) populated the masses section from campus-eighth.json's Eighth College dossier: Sankofa Tower (m:-68,594, #cdc5c7) reuses the fins tile — its measured 2m vertical-bay/glazed-notch precast rhythm is a narrow-pier-over-recessed-glass read that fins already draws. Podemos (m:-56,528, #d4cbc9) reuses eggcrate — its punched-window-grid on precast is a deep two-axis grid, the same rhythm eggcrate was built for. Sankofa Mid (m:-116,613, #efe7e9) and Azad (m:-182,614, #d8d3d3) are ordinary punched-window stucco with no standout rhythm in the footage, so they keep the default band (no style key) rather than force a tile that oversells the read. Pulse Tower (m:-154,556) and Pulse Mid (m:-186,562), both #e2dade from the same source facade (r1c1-plan-00-south.png), share a new `paired` tile: their measured paired-bay rhythm (windows grouped in twos per structural bay) did not fit any of the eight existing tiles cleanly — band, ribbon and bands assume a continuous run, balcony and glass assume a void or curtain wall, fins and eggcrate assume a single-window grid — so one new tile was added rather than force a mismatch; it is the only new tile this workstream introduces. Sankofa Base (m:-97,609) stays out of masses entirely: the dossier resolved only a canopy accent, never a wall colour (occluded in every captured frame), and an unmeasured wall is better absent than guessed. Cross-check: all 6 masses' campus-arcgis.json massing.levels exactly equal the dossier's visually-counted storeys (21/16/10/9/10/9) with h/levels ≈ 3.05m for every one, so there is no GIS-vs-frame storey disagreement for Eighth. 2026-08-06, later: WS-E4 covered six masses but MISSED Survivance, whose two masses therefore fell through to the name key `Survivance` = #c9ad85, a tan that the Apple 3D capture flatly contradicts — it is the same white as its neighbours. Added m:-156,668 (main mass, 33.5 m / 11 levels) = #efebee, sampled from .cache/eighth-area/r4c2-oblique-00-south.png by splitting the facade rectangle at its own median luminance and taking the median of the light half, so windows and shadow do not drag the wall tone down. The sampler was calibrated on this file's own trusted answers before being believed: it returned #efebed for Sankofa Mid (recorded #efe7e9) and #d2cacc for Sankofa Tower (recorded #cdc5c7). Survivance's 6.1 m base (m:-142,666) stays out for the same reason Sankofa Base does — its dark bronze-grey reads clearly in the frames but was not measured, and an unmeasured wall is better absent than guessed. PROVENANCE CORRECTION 2026-08-06 (independent review, verified by recomputing every station-to-mass distance with the repo own toLocal): the sentence above names r4c2-oblique-00-south.png as the source frame for Survivance #efebee. That citation is NOT defensible. r4c2 is indeed the closest capture station to Survivance, but at 55.5 m, and the nearest mass to r4c2 is AZAD at 23 m with Sankofa Mid second at 43 m — Survivance is only third in its own source frame. Without a recorded camera pose for the Apple captures there is no way to project footprints into the frame and prove which facade the patch covered, so #efebee is a NEIGHBOURHOOD reading, not a per-building measurement. It is kept rather than reverted because the direction is not in doubt — Survivance stands plainly the same near-white as its neighbours in the Apple 3D capture, and the tan #c9ad85 it replaced was contradicted by every frame it appears in — but it must be treated as provisional and re-measured from a station-registered capture. The same caution applies to any hex in campus-eighth.json whose station-proximity justification was recomputed and found false. 2026-08-16, Revelle photo pass: York Hall and Argo Hall each carried a wall colour and no style, so both drew the default band — wrong for the two most-seen facades in Revelle Plaza. York Hall = fins is SOURCED: STRUCTURE magazine's account of LPA's seismic rehabilitation states 805 story-tall precast concrete fins wrap its upper floors (https://www.structuremag.org/article/shipshape-the-seismic-rehabilitation-of-york-hall/, with LPA's own project page https://lpadesignstudios.com/projects/york-hall-ucsd for the 300-foot, 35-column arcade beneath them). Argo Hall = fins is MEASURED off dated Wikimedia photographs (Argo_Hall.jpg, 2012; Revelle_Plaza.jpg, 2006): a dense field of vertical precast blade fins runs the full height of every residential floor in front of a continuous glazed band, at ~1.5-1.6 m centres over a ~3.05 m floor-to-floor. Blake Hall was NOT given a style — it is plainly the same family at four storeys, but no clean photograph of it was found and that is an inference, not a measurement. Urey Hall keeps balcony, which is right on its long side wing even though the plaza-facing corner is two blank board-formed stair towers; the corner is built as photo-sourced detail instead of by retuning the tile. R4 RETIREMENT 2026-08-21: Urey Hall left walls and styles. Its GIS prism (m:-10,266) is a declared skipGis retirement in campus-massing.js — the single 30.5 m extrusion was wrong about a four-plateau building and entombed the photo module. campus-photo-urey.js now draws the measured mass with its own sourced facade system (seven gallery bands, pinned channel-mean colours), so a facade tile here would style a prism the renderer no longer builds. The measured wall read #d8d6ce and the balcony tile assignment are preserved in this sentence as the record of what the prism wore. R4 RETIREMENT 2026-08-21 (same mechanism, same day): Bonner Hall left walls and styles. Its GIS prism (m:80,205) joined skipGis — one ring carries two measured roofs (bar plate repo 35.71, west wing 28.0) and a single-lid prism is wrong about one of them at any height; campus-photo-bonner.js ships both plates, the step wall and the full sourced/estimated envelope. The measured wall read #b3a894 and the ribbon tile are preserved in this sentence as the record of what the prism wore.

eighth._: WS-E1 measurement dossier for Eighth College, built 2026-08-06. Every entry keyed by mass hash m:<cx>,<cz> = Math.round(vertex-average centroid) of the docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing ring at build-campus-truecolor.mjs's keyOf() rule (rings /10) — verified against the actual massing polygons, which in one case (Sankofa Base) round 1m differently than the hand-given task centroid, so these keys are the polygon-derived ones, not the hand-rounded ones. Colours sampled with scripts/tmp-sample.mjs (median of a masked pixel patch) from Apple Maps 3D captures ONLY (.cache/apple-flyover, .cache/eighth-area) per the epoch rule — never from .cache/tiles-orbit, which is Google mid-construction imagery used only to cross-check facade geometry. Storey counts are GIS docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing.levels, visually corroborated by counting window rows in a lit frame; bay_m is a VISUAL-ESTIMATE class measurement (piers counted in a near-corner, least-foreshortened crop, scaled by a floor-height calibration derived from the same crop) — treat it as a candidate figure, not survey-grade. Buildings with no captured station within useful range (Survivance tower+low sit toward the uncaptured r3 row) or with a facade never legibly resolved (Podemos low, unnamed dining pavilion, most of Sankofa Base) are OMITTED or marked resolved:false rather than guessed — see the builder report for the full per-mass account. WS-E2 (2026-08-06) added the ground key: 74 ground-plane features for Eighth (1 basketball court, 19 walkway/paving-zone, 7 courtyard, 47 planting-bed), all snapped to already-surveyed docs/data/campus-arcgis.json ground[] polygons (registration arcgis.ground#<index>, ring coords /10 to get metres) rather than hand-measured off Apple pixels, per the tasks own STRONGLY PREFERRED guidance. The basketball court is additionally photo-confirmed (r1c2-plan-00-south.png, blue surface + white key markings) and its surface colour sampled from that frame. courtyard/planting-bed kind is a >200sqm size heuristic (shoelace-formula polygon area, corrected 2026-08-06 cycle-2 from an earlier bounding-box-area computation that had misclassified 10 sub-200sqm polygons as courtyard) over GIS green polygons (GIS does not itself distinguish lawn/courtyard from planting bed) — not individually photo-confirmed per polygon. arcgis.ground#409 (a 9.7sqm sliver on a 21m-long, <0.5m-wide diagonal strip) was dropped rather than mislabeled: its shape is not a real distinct planting/courtyard feature, almost certainly a walkway-edge fragment misrouted into the green layer. Stepped terraces and stair flights were investigated but OMITTED: docs/data/textures ground-texture chunks covering Eighth (chunk_3_8.jpg, chunk_4_8.jpg) are themselves mid-construction-epoch Google imagery (visible scaffolding/bare dirt), so texture-chunk registration is contaminated for this area exactly like .cache/tiles-orbit and cannot be used; a real stair+handrail was located in eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png near a western courtyard, but the flight descends into a photogrammetry mesh reconstruction gap (a jagged dark hole artifact) that makes per-step run/rise unmeasurable to the required confidence, so it was left out rather than guessed (frames tried: r1c2-plan-00-south.png — hard shadow at the Sankofa Base plinth; r1c1-plan-00-south.png — no stair geometry resolved, only a road kerb ramp; r2c1-plan-00-south.png — real stair found but occluded by a mesh gap beyond the top ~5 treads). One oversized arcgis green polygon cluster (#1127, 73.7x184.5m, and #1160, 63.6x46m) was excluded as too large/ambiguous to label a single courtyard-scale feature (likely hillside greenbelt) rather than mislabel it. CORRECTIONS 2026-08-06 (independent review; every figure below recomputed from the manifest with the repo own toLocal and cross-checked against the camera eighth-compare.mjs emits): (1) THREE station-proximity claims in the buildings notes are false by 4-8x and two invert the argument they were written to make. Podemos: stated 7.8 m from r1c3 with the next-nearest Eighth mass 70 m+ away; actual 59.2 m, and Pulse Tower is nearer to r1c3 at 52.2 m. Azad: stated 13.7 m from r2c1 and the closest station-to-mass match in the dossier; actual 65.7 m, and Pulse Mid is nearer at 20.0 m. Sankofa Base: stated 20 m from r2c2; actual 84.4 m. The CONCLUSIONS survive re-derivation on correctly chosen stations — Podemos true nearest station is r1c4 at 16.1 m where Podemos IS the nearest mass, and Azad true nearest is r4c1 at 21.2 m where Azad IS the nearest mass — so no colour is overturned by this, but the stated reasoning was wrong and nothing in the repo would have caught it. (2) The claim that Survivance sits toward an uncaptured r3 row is false: all 25 stations r0c0-r4c4 are on disk, and r3c0 (23:55) and r4c2 (00:44) both predate the WS-E1 commit at 01:10. That false premise is what dropped Survivance from the facade table and required a repair commit. Survivance has no well-registered station either way — its nearest is r4c2 at 55.5 m, where Azad at 23 m and Sankofa Mid at 43 m are both nearer — so its wall colour is a neighbourhood reading, flagged as provisional in campus-facades.json. (3) scripts/tmp-sample.mjs, named above as the provenance of every wall colour in this file, was never committed and does not exist in any commit. No hex here can currently be re-derived or audited. Re-measurement needs a capture rig that records camera pose per frame so footprints can be projected and the sampled patch proven to lie on the intended building.

basketball-court.note: Union bounding rectangle of two adjacent arcgis.ground court polygons (#3898 south half + #3923 north half, both k:"court"); the 4 small #k:"court" rectangles at indices 3785/3806/3918/3921 (~1.8x3.6m each) are the painted free-throw keys visible as white lane markings inside this rectangle, not separate ground features. Plan footprint measures 22.7m x 15.4m — the 15.4m cross-dimension matches a regulation FIBA/NBA court width (15.24m) closely, but the 22.7m long dimension is ~79% of the 28.65m regulation full-court length, so this is NOT a regulation-sized full court (likely a shortened recreational/practice court) — reported as measured, not corrected to regulation. Surface colour #2c4460 is the median of 272 pixel samples of the mid-blue court apron band in r1c2-plan-00-south.png (the darker navy key/lane paint and white line-work were excluded from the sample).

markings._: Generated by scripts/build-campus-markings.mjs — sports-surface markings fitted to the georeferenced satellite chunks. Do not hand-edit.

landmarks._: Campus landmarks researched 2026-08-03 (Stuart Collection pages, press, aerials) for campus-landmarks.js. Fallen Star position was independently georeferenced - Wikipedia's coordinate is ~400 m off. Colours re-measured 2026-08-03 from 4K walk (W:fNNNN) and drone (D:fNNNN) footage; every hex below is a measurement with its frame named in the description, lifted to daylight where the drone frame was overcast or dusk.

fallenStar.cornerEvidence: D:f0034-f0036. The cottage is NOT on a corner of the main block: Jacobs Hall's south face is a comb of slender concrete stair towers, and the house sits on one of them with building mass on both sides. The georeferenced point lands 3.7 m off that south face at x=546 in local metres, west of the footprint's mid-span (504..605) - south-west, agreeing with this tag. The prose in the Fallen Star landmark entry used to say 'northeast corner' and was wrong.

landmarks.name: Sun God
landmarks.description: Niki de Saint Phalle's great bird, repainted from footage. The earlier reading had the body sprayed all over with small bright blotches, and that is wrong in the way that matters: the colour arrives as a handful of very large deliberate motifs on white. Measured D:f0100-f0101 (close aerial) and W:f0059 (eye level, sunlit): WHITE body; a scarlet head with a blue crown band and a big hooked beak a shade darker and more purple than the head itself; and behind the head a gold sunburst crest of about nine tapered spikes radiating up and out in a fan. One big concentric disc on the chest (red outer ring, blue ring, gold sun-centre) and one oval target on each outstretched wing (red, green and gold rings around a blue-red core); feet and legs painted in the same red/blue/yellow/green family. It stands on a low arch that is completely blanketed in ivy - a dark green mass with an arched opening beneath it, not the bare grey concrete assumed before; only the cap the bird stands on shows pale concrete. Bird ~4.3 m over a ~4.5 m arch. Low-poly: ivy piers + ivy lintel + pale cap, white body and wings, scarlet head, gold spike fan, and coaxial ring discs that read from either side.

landmarks.name: Fallen Star
landmarks.description: Do Ho Suh's small blue New England cottage perched at a tilt on Jacobs Hall (roof ~29 m up), cantilevered over the edge as if crash-landed. Measured D:f0034-f0036: powder-blue clapboard walls, white door/window trim, grey shingle pitched roof (lighter and bluer than the near-black the file used to carry), red brick chimney. It sits on one of the slender concrete stair towers that comb the building's SOUTH face - not on a corner of the main block, which is why it has building on both sides of it in the aerials - and hangs off that tower's south-WEST corner, with the rooftop garden (lawn, shrubs, a purple-leaf tree, ivy spilling over the tower edge) filling the rest of the tower roof inboard of the house. Low-poly: simple gabled house box ~5 m tall rotated ~10 deg off the building's grid and pitched ~10 deg over the drop. The rendered spec - position, corner, tilt, dimensions and every colour - lives in the top-level fallenStar block, not here.

landmarks.name: Snake Path
landmarks.description: Alexis Smith's 171 m long, 3 m wide winding footpath shaped like a serpent, running from Warren Mall (east end 32.881275,-117.235907) up the hillside to the Geisel Library terrace (west end 32.881024,-117.237041). Surface is hexagonal slate tiles in a scale pattern: mottled green, grey, and tan. Head (with eyes) at the top near Geisel; tail at the bottom; mid-path it coils around a small walled 'Garden of Eden' with fruit trees and passes an oversized granite book. Low-poly: a flat S-curving ribbon with green/grey checker texture, slightly raised, widening to a spade-shaped head.

landmarks.name: Silent Tree
landmarks.description: Terry Allen's dead eucalyptus tree wrapped entirely in dull grey lead sheet, standing on Library Walk just south of Geisel Library. Bare branching trunk, no leaves, matte lead grey with visible panel seams - measured W:f0151, a warm-neutral gunmetal rather than a blue steel. Classic meeting spot. Low-poly: a leafless tree of 5-8 tapering cylinders, uniform lead grey.

landmarks.name: Trees (Talking Tree)
landmarks.description: Second of Terry Allen's three lead-clad eucalyptus trunks, hidden in the living eucalyptus grove southwest of Geisel; plays spoken poems and stories from concealed speakers. Same look as Silent Tree: bare grey-lead branching trunk among tall living trees. Low-poly: identical grey leafless tree, surrounded by normal green eucalyptus.

landmarks.name: Trees (Singing Tree)
landmarks.description: Third Terry Allen lead-covered eucalyptus, ~70 m west of the Talking Tree in the same grove; emits songs. Matte grey leafless trunk with lead panel seams. Low-poly: same grey tree model reused.

landmarks.name: Bear (Warren Bear)
landmarks.description: Tim Hawkinson's teddy-bear built from eight huge rounded granite boulders (~180 tons), sitting upright in the Jacobs School engineering courtyard between CSE, EBU1, and the Bioengineering building. Warm grey-tan granite, measured twice (W:f0108 eye level, D:f0053 aerial) - a touch warmer and duller than the neutral the model was using; one giant egg boulder for the body, sphere head, four smaller boulders as arms/legs, two small ears. This is what students call the Warren Bear. Low-poly: 8-10 smooth grey spheres/ovoids stacked into a seated teddy bear.

landmarks.name: La Jolla Project (Stonehenge)
landmarks.description: Richard Fleischner's 71 blocks of pink and grey granite scattered across the Revelle College lawn south of Galbraith Hall, some stacked into post-and-lintel doorways, arches, and benches up to ~2.4 m tall — hence the 'Stonehenge' nickname. Low-poly: a dozen clusters of rectangular blocks, alternating warm pink-beige and cool grey granite, on flat green grass.

landmarks.name: Triton Statue
landmarks.description: Manuelita Brown's bronze King Triton on the plaza at the east entrance of Price Center, muscular merman rising from a wave, trident in hand, on a low stone base. Measured D:f0026 (and D:f0128 on the King Triton at the amphitheatre base, #3f4245): the patina reads dark blue-black, not brown-green. Photo spot for grads. Low-poly: dark bronze torso with raised trident, fish-tail base merging into a wave wedge, grey plinth.

landmarks.name: READ/WRITE/THINK/DREAM
landmarks.description: John Baldessari's artwork forming the main east entrance of Geisel Library: a row of tall glass doors and windows in saturated primary colors (red, blue, yellow, green panes) with the words READ, WRITE, THINK, DREAM, plus large photographic panels inside. Low-poly: the library's ground-level entry wall as a strip of vivid colored glass rectangles under the concrete tower.

landmarks.name: Geisel Library
landmarks.description: The campus icon: an 8-level brutalist 'lantern' — a concrete pedestal with four massive splayed diagonal piers holding five progressively larger-then-smaller glass floors, widest in the middle, like a spaceship or tree canopy. Raw grey concrete piers, dark tinted glass bands with narrow concrete floor slabs. Low-poly: stepped stack of square glass floors (widths ~small/large/largest/large/small) on 4 angled concrete legs.

landmarks.name: Vices and Virtues
landmarks.description: Bruce Nauman's band of 2.1 m tall neon words wrapping the top parapet of the Powell Structural Systems Laboratory (crown sits ~25 m up): seven vices superimposed on seven virtues (FAITH/LUST, HOPE/ENVY...) flashing in alternating neon colors. Measured D:f0033, which corrects two things: the host is a plain GREY board-formed concrete box, not an oxblood one, and the crown is an OPEN OXIDE-RED steel frame - an airy lattice you can see sky through, carrying the tubes and running down the building's corners as red columns. The letters are hot pink-red and mint green (daylight readings; at night they are far brighter). NOT YET RENDERED by campus-landmarks.js - the grey box belongs to campus-facades.json, and the red crown + letter band is future work. Low-poly when built: an open red steel frame band around the parapet with a glowing letter strip inside it.

landmarks.name: Two Running Violet V Forms
landmarks.description: Robert Irwin's two V-shaped runs of blue-violet plastic-coated chain-link fence held ~7.6 m in the air on slim stainless steel poles, threading between eucalyptus trunks in the grove west of Library Walk. Translucent purple-blue shimmer against the trees. Low-poly: two long thin semi-transparent violet ribbons in a shallow V plan, on skinny silver posts among eucalyptus.

landmarks.name: What Hath God Wrought
landmarks.description: Mark Bradford's 199 ft white steel pole — the tallest structure on campus — rising from Revelle College plaza, topped with a light that blinks 'What hath God wrought' in Morse code at night. Looks like an impossibly tall slender flagpole. Low-poly: a single thin white tapering cylinder with a small blinking white light cap.

landmarks.name: KAHNOP - TO TELL A STORY
landmarks.description: Ann Hamilton's ~240 m long granite walkway east of Pepper Canyon, on the route from the trolley station into campus, its pale grey stone pavers carved with raised lines of text (Kumeyaay and English words). Low-poly: a flat light-grey stone ribbon path with subtle darker text striping.

landmarks.name: Theodor Seuss Geisel Memorial (Dr. Seuss statue)
landmarks.description: Bronze of Dr. Seuss seated at his drafting desk with a 2 m Cat in the Hat standing beside him, on the terrace just west of the Geisel Library entrance. Dark brown bronze on a low grey plinth. Low-poly: seated figure at a small desk plus a tall thin cat figure with stovepipe hat, all one bronze color.

landmarks.name: Green Table
landmarks.description: Jenny Holzer's leaf-green granite picnic table and benches engraved with texts, in a grove near Peterson Hall on Ridge Walk. Low-poly: a simple picnic table, solid muted green stone.

landmarks.name: Revelle Plaza Fountain
landmarks.description: The centrepiece of Revelle Plaza, and the thing the walk aims at once it leaves Argo: a low ring basin about 8 m across with a single white aerating jet standing in the middle of it, and the tall US flagpole a dozen metres off its north side. Measured W:f0035 (and corroborated W:f0034, W:f0036): the basin is BLACK - a charcoal basalt that samples #151217 raw in the frame, which is the darkest thing on the plaza and the reason the fountain reads as a hole in the concrete rather than an ornament. The rendered #3a3437 is that reading lifted to daylight, a very dark warm charcoal rather than the literal near-black. The jet samples #a5b1b6 backlit and is rendered as lifted white foam - a single column that flares as it rises, not a fan of nozzles. Position is the surveyed OSM point 'Revelle Plaza Fountain' inside the plaza polygon both the router and the walk cross. The flagpole stand-off is parallax between W:f0034 and W:f0035, which puts it 12-17 m from the basin on the side away from the cafe umbrellas; the flag's own red/white/blue are the canonical US flag colours, NOT measurements - at this distance the flag is a handful of sky-mixed pixels. The flag itself is now built to the published US proportions - hoist 1, fly 1.9, thirteen equal stripes with seven red and red at top and bottom, union 7/13 of the hoist tall and 0.76 of the hoist wide over the top seven stripes, fifty stars in the 6/5 nine-row grid - which is a SPECIFICATION, not a measurement. So is everything else new on the pole: the 1.52 m hoist (the conventional flag for a pole this tall), the standing wave the cloth is bent onto and the direction it flies, the gold ball finial and truck (flagGold), the halyard (halyard) and the cleat (cleat). What a source actually settles is only that the pole is there and that it flies the US flag - Revelle College's own page lists 'the May 1970 Peace Memorial and the U.S. Flag' as what the Plaza hosts (revelle.ucsd.edu/events), and W:f0034-f0036 place it. No frame on this campus resolves the hardware at 15 m. Low-poly: charcoal rim cylinder, dark water disc, one flaring foam cone, tapered white pole with ball finial, halyard and cleat, and a thirteen-stripe flag welded into four instanced ribbons.

landmarks.name: Pergola Swings (Ridge Walk at Muir Field)
landmarks.description: One of a pair of identical rest stations the walk passes: a long black steel post-and-beam trellis with a flat roof of pale timber slats, three hanging bench swings on rods under it and fixed grey benches alongside. Measured W:f0013-f0014, where the run stands at the edge of the mown Muir field with the walk on its other side. Every reading in those frames is against the sun, so the steel samples #0c090a to #2f3036 and the slats read as silhouette: the frame black #3a3634 and the lit timber #c9c2b2 are the daylight values, and the benches #8a8378 with them. Placed on the east side of Ridge Walk at the field's edge, beside the route between Muir and Peterson. Low-poly: two rows of posts, two beams, a rack of slats, three swing seats on rods, two fixed benches.

landmarks.name: Pergola Swings (Revelle Walk)
landmarks.description: The second station of the same furniture family, on the Revelle stretch of the walk north of Bonner Hall. Measured W:f0026 (seen up the walk) and W:f0027 (standing in it, a swing seat hanging on its rods a metre from the lens). Same black steel frame, same pale slat roof, same grey benches as the Muir station - which is the point: it is a repeat, and repeats are what make a campus legible. It sits in the planted median between the bike lane and the pedestrian walk, so the route passes within a few metres of it. The colours are the Muir station's daylight values; both frames here are backlit too.

landmarks.name: Mayer/Bonner Folded-Plate Canopy
landmarks.description: The Revelle silhouette, and the one piece of building shape on this walk that a flat wall cannot fake: a continuous eave of literal triangular concrete prisms - a folded plate - running the length of the Mayer and Bonner arcade on slender round columns, cream #d8d4c6. Measured W:f0022-f0023, where the prisms are the whole top-right of the frame; both readings are of the shaded underside (#4a4a3b, #585351) so the cream is the daylight value. The line it runs along is not stored here: the builder takes the WEST edge of each host's own footprint out of campus-3d.json, so the canopy stays welded to the buildings if the massing ever moves. The two hosts present one unbroken west face about 160 m long, which is the whole east side of the Revelle stretch the route walks. Low-poly: one instanced prism per 2.4 m of run with a column every 4.8 m.

landmarks.name: Sun God Lawn reference - Untitled (Asher fountain)
landmarks.description: Michael Asher's granite drinking fountain shaped like a commercial office fountain, oddly alone on the plaza north of Price Center. Speckled grey granite box. Low-poly: a knee-high grey rectangular block with a basin notch.

photo._: INVENTED, PHOTO-SOURCED CONTENT — epoch 2024-2025. NEVER A SOURCE FOR ANY MEASURED CONSUMER. Every entity in this document is modelled from published architectural photography and a 2021 design site plan, not from OSM, not from LiDAR, and not from the ArcGIS survey. Positions are INFERRED: each item names the surveyed polygon it was anchored to (`anchor`), and that anchor is the only measured fact behind it. Nothing here may be read back as a measurement of the campus, quoted as a height, a colour or a position by campus-eighth.js, campus-eighth-furniture.js, the corridor builders, or any gate. It renders and it is labelled; it does not inform. Class rule: docs/js/campus-photo-eighth.js header, and the README's photo-sourced section.

bbq.note: Position inferred from photo geometry. The inventory could not resolve the grill station in the repo frame; it is placed on the north-east edge of the surveyed paved courtyard directly north of Pulse Tower, facing north across the (unsurveyed) lawn, which is the arrangement crop_grill.png shows — grills in front of a paved picnic terrace with a tower behind the camera-facing enclosure. `rotY` aligns every piece with that courtyard's own measured north-east edge (-121.2,524.9)-(-144.3,533.6).

amphitheatre.anchor: band between arcgis.ground#3898 (basketball-court) east edge and arcgis.ground#2144
amphitheatre.note: Position inferred from the 2021 site plan's zigzag tiered edge between court J and lawn A. Only the BAND is anchored — the court's surveyed east edge at x -163.2 and the surveyed planting bed at x -158.9 bracket it. Tier count, length and riser are estimated. Kept 0.9 m clear of the painted court.

meditation.anchor: open paved spine between arcgis.ground#328 and arcgis.ground#329
meditation.note: Location confirmed twice (Eighth's own page: 'between the Pulse and Azad buildings'; the site plan's B label). The photo-to-label assignment of EYRC phf47 is likely-but-unconfirmed. SCALE IS REDUCED FROM THE PHOTO ESTIMATE ON PURPOSE: phf47 reads a 26-30 m roof, but the surveyed open spine between the two courtyard rings is only ~11 x 8 m, and the two planted rings are measured. The composition is fitted to the surveyed opening rather than overrunning it.

teaHouse.note: The plan scales the TEA HOUSE label to about (-145, 592), which lands in the unsurveyed gap between two planting beds. Moved ~6 m south-east onto the nearest surveyed Ramble polygon, per the inventory's own instruction to tie it to a real polygon before shipping. Form, batten module and setting are from z_teahouse.png.

ramble.note: SWA's restored drainage corridor. Every position here is inferred: each field, patch and cluster is placed inside a surveyed planting bed or courtyard, and the extents are fitted to that polygon rather than to the photograph. revelle.supersededNote: RETIRED FROM THE DRAW, KEPT IN THE RECORD. Two mechanisms, both skipped by campus-photo-revelle.js and both reported in counts.superseded. (1) A key naming a whole system — here only `paving` — retires that system entirely. (2) A key of the form `<system>.items[sup]` declares that individual items in that system carry a `sup` field naming the section that supersedes them; the builder skips exactly the flagged items. Per-item flags are used in preference to the index ranges research-plaza.md 1.0 proposed, because ranges are silently invalidated by any reordering of items[] and a flag travels with its item. NOTHING IS EVER DELETED: every superseded item is still fully described above, because the successor sections cite these entries as the thing they improve on and deleting them would destroy the provenance trail. See supersededDetail for the evidence behind each retirement.

supersededDetail.paving: 76 cells at pitch 6.4 over the measured Revelle Plaza polygon, plus the x 20 runner. THE ARGO-SIDE RACK RUN: WHERE THE RACKS WENT. Rewritten in R2 (arbitration item R1) in four parts, because the R1 text led with two grounds and mentioned the evidence last, which read as though the retirement depended on the grounds. It never did. (a) THE RETIREMENT IS UPHELD AND IT RESTS ON ONE THING. The seven hoops at z 362.5, x -53..-39.8 are retired on research-argo.md section 9.3 ALONE: a POSITIVE OBSERVATION of clear ground in a dated Google photosphere of Argo's north entry (Mass Interact, November 2024) which frames the whole boardwalk, planting bed and gravel apron in one shot and shows not one bike hoop anywhere in it. That is evidence, not an epoch tiebreak, and it stands without either ground below. The same frame is why plaza retires the 25 bicycles it drew at x -54..-44.4, z 362.2 — 0.3 m from these hoops, on the same ground, in the same 2012 epoch (plaza.conflicts[3]); nothing in this section contradicts that retirement and this section draws no bicycle. (b) GROUND (1), NARROWED AND KEPT. A row at z 355.5 or z 358.0 is UNBUILDABLE against the shipped blake section OVER x -54..-33 — not over the whole x -59..-33 the relocation proposed. The arithmetic is unchanged: blake.ground.south.terrace is a raised lawn terrace at x -54..-24, z 354..357.4 lifted 1.1 m, so a row at z 355.5 would stand on top of a lawn behind a retaining edge; and blake.ground.south.lavaWall runs at z 357.6 at 0.5 m thick, occupying z 357.35..357.85, so a 0.72 m wide hoop centred at z 358.0 spans z 357.64..358.36 and interpenetrates it by 0.21 m (0.11 m at blake's alternative [estimated] 0.3 m thickness). 21 of the proposed run's 26 m are covered by this ground and 5 m are not. (c) GROUND (2) IS STRUCK AS AN ARGUMENT AND RE-STATED AS A REPRODUCED NEGATIVE. A Blake-roof-lean explanation for the two bright rows in the brightened orthophoto WAS TESTED AND DOES NOT REPRODUCE: at blake's R1-MEASURED 12.4 m height (not the 15.6 m the struck argument used, which blake's own R1 section retired) and argo's 0.208 m/m top displacement at bearing 166 degrees, the roof edge lands at z about 351.2 — 4.3 m from the z 355.5 row and 6.8 m from the z 358.0 row. It is kept as a negative result rather than deleted, because a tested-and-failed explanation is a stronger record than a wrong one and deleting it would invite the next agent to propose it again. (d) THE RELOCATION IS UNRESOLVED OVER x -59..-54 ONLY, AND UNRESOLVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. That 5 m strip is outside ground (1)'s coverage — but it is ALSO outside the November 2024 photosphere's framing, so it has no positive evidence FOR the relocation either. It is unresolved because nothing looks at it, which is a weaker state than a live hypothesis awaiting a tiebreak, and this entry must not be read as a nearly-established relocation held back on a technicality. The 2012 single-row read at z 362.5 and research-argo 9.5's 2026 two-row relocation reading are BOTH on the record, NEITHER is built, and nothing is built over x -59..-54 either way. Better absent than wrong.

derivations.figuresNote: S1(vi) IS A NO-OP IN THIS SECTION AND THAT IS A RECORDED GAP, NOT A PASS. Every entry in `figures` above is a PROSE STRING with no `expr` field, so there is no expression for tests/helpers/axiom-gate.mjs `assertExprs` to evaluate and nothing binds a figure to its inputs except the prose itself. The R2 surgery deliberately did NOT invent exprs to make the gate run — an invented derivation is the defect the gate exists to catch, in a new costume. The suite asserts instead that every figure IS prose (so nothing can masquerade as an evaluable expression) and runs assertExprs the moment any figure becomes an object carrying an `expr`. Converting this table to {value, expr} against `reads` is R2 work and is owed.

counts.note: Declared counts of what is DRAWN, i.e. after the superseded skip. tests/campus-photo-revelle.test.mjs asserts every one of these against the built group, so a builder that silently stops producing a system, or a supersession that quietly widens, fails the gate.

retirements.note: R2 ARBITRATION ITEM S2. `sup` meant two different things — a TRANSFER to a named successor that carries the object, and a DELETION on evidence — and only the prose in `supersededDetail` could tell them apart. `"bins.items[sup]": ["york"]` reads, to any consumer and to any gate, as a transfer to york; york ships nothing and is not meant to. The prose was honest in every case and is unchanged; what was missing was a machine-readable field that says which happened. Every item carrying `sup` now declares `disposition`, and this table declares it per (system, successor) pair with the count it moves, the ground it rests on, and — for a transfer — the reciprocal record the successor must carry. tests/campus-photo-revelle.test.mjs walks this table ACROSS sections: for every `transferred` pair it opens the successor's file, requires the reciprocal, and requires the path the reciprocal names to resolve to something the successor actually ships; for every `deleted-on-evidence` pair it requires a stated ground. That is audit-plaza F4 — mutation X1 deleted york.westGround.racks and this suite passed — turned into a gateable condition. NOTHING HERE CONVERTS A DELETION INTO A TRANSFER: the 13 deleted items are deleted on good evidence and the record is being made to match the decision, not the other way round. THE RECIPROCAL FIELD IS A KEY PREFIX, not an exact key: each successor names the item RANGE it claims (blake.superseded['revelle.lavaWalls#30-44'], plaza.superseded['revelle.benchesA#20-26'], york.superseded['revelle.racks#11-26']), so this field carries 'revelle.<system>' and the walk matches on it. That is deliberate — the range suffix is the successor's business, and this section must not need re-editing when a successor re-describes what it claims.

The recessed balcony stack beside the South Tower's red slot (keeling2/a7_northface.png, one ~2.4 m balcony per floor recessed 1.5-2 m) — cutting a per-floor recess into the measured massing would carve a mass this section is not allowed to touch; the slot and the panel field are built, the recess is not.

The horizontal facade module is unresolved between 1.20 m (two reads of the head-on elevation kt_keeling2.png) and 1.02 m (fin-comb autocorrelation over both towers' full south faces in the georeferenced satellite). 1.20 m is built; see grid.moduleNote.
The inner re-entrant corners where the bar meets the North Tower, and the notches in both tower rings, are skinned as flat faces — no photograph resolves how the two systems turn those corners.

The grating mesh pitch is not measured. The balustrade is built as a semi-transparent aggregate plane plus real bars at 0.30 m, tuned to read at the photographed openness, not to a sourced bar spacing.
The teal glass hex is estimated — every crop of a teal pane in the cached set is contaminated by reflected sky or by the wet-weather cast of ls_016.jpg.
Wet-weather staining. The dark vertical water-stain streaks below every panel's top edge in ls_016.jpg are a state, not a material, and the rest of the model is dry.
Night lighting. No night photograph of this building exists in any source reached; the luminaires are geometry only and emit nothing.

Trees. The measured LiDAR tree layer already owns the eucalyptus, the courtyard sycamores and the redbuds — the building is 2011 and the LiDAR is 2014, so they are in the survey. Nothing here plants anything.
The small red object standing in the courtyard paving at about (-167, 434) in the satellite, also visible in c6_towerB.png — roughly 1.7 m square and unidentifiable at any available resolution.

Building-number graphics. The painted numeral '3' on the South Tower's undercroft wall is legible in ls_016.jpg, but no other number is, and one number without the set would be a false claim about which building is which.
The mechanical plant boxes' louvre bands and the small round vent stacks visible in a4_rightroof.png — below the resolution needed to place them honestly.

The storey arithmetic 10/8/6 x 3.60 + 1.20 = 37.2/30.0/22.8 matches campus-3d's OSM-side heights but NOT the reconciled heights campus-massing draws (34.2/27/18.3 — buildings.*.measured.drawnHeight). Two sources, two epochs, unresolved; LiDAR wins on height, so the drawn plates are lidarHeight/storeys (3.44/3.65/3.03 m) and the 3.60 m photogrammetric plate is NOT drawn anywhere. Recorded 2026-08-17 by the visual-audit repair.

bounds.note: Everything this section draws in plan: the measured ring grown by the registration band, plus every ground field on all four sides. z0 reaches 412 because the three surveyed north beds (arcgis.ground#1764/#1765/#1766) extend to z 412.1, 2.9 m north of the apron that used to pave over them. derivations.why: THE KEELING BAR. The keeling.roofs.pv block states a real product dimension and its own arithmetic for every figure it draws; this block does the same for Galbraith. `readings` are the raw citations — pixel counts in one frame at one depth, orthophoto measurements, repo data-file values — and `figures` is every derived value with the expression that produces it. tests/campus-photo-galbraith.test.mjs recomputes every figure independently from `readings` and fails if the section's own value drifts from its own derivation, so a fabricated figure cannot pass by being self-consistent. COVERAGE LINE, stated so it can be argued with: the number walk covers grid, faces, levels, column, roofEdge, soffit, facade, entry and the roof's scalars. It does NOT walk the ground and roof RECTANGLE coordinates, which are positions read off a named frame rather than dimensions; those are covered group-wise by a reads entry naming the frame and its tolerance, and the test checks every ground and roof group has one.

px.source: oceanlight-21220.jpg (Phillip Colla / OceanLight, https://www.oceanlight.com/spotlight.php?img=21220, ~2007-2012 — the CLICS and Fairbanks Coffee signage dates it pre-2013), near-orthographic SOUTH elevation, crop cached as oceanlight-21220-strut-band.png. Every px below is a length in that one frame and is used as a RATIO against another length in the same frame, never through a px-per-metre constant. TWO OF THEM ARE NOT GRID READINGS AND ARE NOT USED AS ONE — see centreNote.
px.centreNote: `pairGapCentre` (145) and `pairSpacingCentre` (460) are a HEAD-HEIGHT reading of a LEANING PAIR, and their quotient 0.3152 is NOT a grid ratio. R2 arbitration re-read this frame and its 3x east-end crop: these columns are paired and splay-footed, converging at the foot and spreading toward the head bracket, so a pair stands ~16% wider at the head than at the base (head-bracket centres ~360 crop-px apart against ~310 at the bases). A structural grid line lands at the column BASE, on the slab; measuring the separation anywhere above the base measures the LEAN as well as the grid and reports it as the grid. Measured at the base the SAME pair reads 0.221 — which is what the drawing says (0.2219 / 0.2228). These two readings are KEPT because they are a real measurement of a real thing: they are the section's only quantitative corroboration of column.splayHead. They feed no figure.

kda.source: Revelle-College-Sources/plans-and-drawings/KdA_4613_L2_OPTC.jpg — Kevin deFreitas Architects, GALBRAITH HALL RENOVATION, UCSD PROJECT NO. 4613, 'SECOND FLOOR LEVEL PLAN', OPT C, DATE ISSUED 02.17.12, scale 1/8in = 1ft-0in. Bubble centres measured in NATIVE source-image px (2000 x 1429), overlay cached as KdA-L2-grid-bubbles-A-to-L.png. RE-MEASURED at native resolution in the R2 arbitration, replacing a first pass read off a 2.2x crop. Column lines (top margin, threshold <248 over y 34-48): A 102.5, B 290.5, C 343.5, D 531.5, E 585.0, F 772.5, G 826.5, H 1013.5, I 1067.5, J 1254.5, K 1308.5, L ~1497 — one outer single, five pairs, one outer single, symmetric to 0.5 px. Row lines (right margin, x 1508-1532): 192.0, 245.5, 433.0, 486.0, 674.0, 728.0, 915.5, 969.0, 1156.5, 1210.0 — five pairs, no outer singles. The sheet's SCALE does not survive (conflicts.gridScale, conflicts.gridScaleThree); only the RATIOS are used, and a ratio needs no scale.
kda.readingNote: THE RETIRED READING. `rowPairToPair` shipped as 172.6 px, which corresponds to NO interval on this sheet: the row bubbles contain 53.5 (the pair gap), 187.6 (gap-to-gap within the run) and 241.1 (pair to pair), and 172.6 is not within 8 px of any of them. Every figure downstream of it moved with it and 60 gates passed, which is exactly the failure the axiom-layer pins in tests/campus-photo-galbraith.test.mjs now exist to stop. DEVIATION FROM THE ARBITRATION'S OWN SUMMARY LINE, recorded so it can be argued with: item G1's `value` field rounds all four to 53.6 / 241.0, which would make both axes 0.222407 and would NOT reproduce the ratios item G2 orders shipped (0.221900 and 0.222820). G2's value field names its inputs in parentheses — 53.5/241.1 for the rows and 53.7/241.0 for the letters — and those are also the per-bubble means both items' reasoning sections derive. Those four are what is pinned here.

ortho.source: docs/data/textures/chunk_4_7.jpg — the repo's own Google orthophoto tile (source: google, generated 2026-08-04, 0.125 m/px, world mapping x0 -177 z0 402 x1 78 z1 657 in textures/manifest.json). Per CLAUDE.md satellite imagery is a BUILD-TIME measurement source only; nothing here is draped and no height is inferred from it. Overlays cached as ortho2026-galbraith-roof-worldgrid.png and ortho2026-galbraith-skylight-9x9.png.
ortho.blockNote: The raised skylight block's APPARENT plan rectangle, read off chunk_4_7.jpg at 0.125 m/px on the ortho2026-galbraith-roof-worldgrid.png overlay, before the top-displacement correction. Every roof.block figure is this rectangle plus roof.displacement. These four numbers previously existed only as a literal inside tests/campus-photo-galbraith.test.mjs, which meant the document's own derivation could not be run from the document.

sourcedDepths.source: oceanlight-21220.jpg (2007-2012, near-orthographic south elevation), oceanlight-21225.jpg and oceanlight-12848.jpg (2007-2012, south-west corner, 'Galbraith Hall' on the fascia) and dc-bb4438071r_2.jpg (UCSD Library DC ark bb4438071r, SIO Photographic Laboratory, mid-1960s colour) — the glass-to-strut colonnade depth and the two deck projections, read against the 16.6 m grade-to-roof.

ring.source: docs/data/campus-3d.json buildings 'Galbraith Hall' p — the MEASURED OSM ring, copied verbatim, vertex by vertex. `meanFaceLength` and the centroid are arithmetic over those eight numbers and nothing else. The vertices are carried here as named scalars so every face length is a real evaluable expression over them rather than the prose 'hypot(ring[0] -> ring[1])' that nothing could run.

grid.module.why: TWO independent chains, meaned. The orthophoto's own 2.7422 m skylight pitch is two coffer bays (2.7422/2 = 1.3711); the 46 coffers counted across the elevation on the measured 62.0768 m mean face give 1.3495. They are 1.6% apart and the spread is declared in conflicts.cofferModule. The shipped 10.83/8 = 1.354 chain is RETIRED: the drawing's 10.83 m does not reproduce from the sheet (conflicts.gridScale), so a module derived from it rested on nothing.

roof.skylights.pitch.why: One grid or the building is wrong: a skylight is two coffer bays. The RAW orthophoto measurement is 2.7422 m (sigma 0.06); this derivation gives 2.7206, a 0.0216 m per-bay shortfall and 0.173 m across the field's eight bays, inside the +-0.5 m the orthophoto source declares.

draw.registration.why: The least this section may stand outside the OSM ring and still be seen: campus-massing.js extrudes the UNIVERSITY'S ring, which stands 0.799 m outside the OSM trace on the east elevation, and anything closer than that disappears inside the drawn box. It is a REGISTRATION offset, not a dimension of the building.

grid.roofOut.why: The whole outboard band, measured from the glazing plane to the fascia. Two coffer bays: the least that carries a readable coffer field, the head bracket (1.68 m across) and a colonnade behind it. THIS IS NOT AN OVERSAIL PAST THE RING — see conflicts.roofPlate. The retired value was 11.524 m, which put the fascia 12.474 m outside a ring the orthophoto measures the roof plate ON.

facade.wallStandoff.why: The glazing plane is the innermost thing this section may draw, so it sits on the registration offset exactly.

column.standoffBuilt.why: The strut centre line stands one bracket half-width inboard of the fascia, so the head bracket dies INTO the fascia — which is what oceanlight-21220, -21225 and -12848 all show, and the single strongest evidence that the measured ring traces the roof edge. The SOURCED glass-to-strut depth is 3.4 m; only 2.72 m of band exists to hold it, so the colonnade is drawn at 0.553 of its depth (conflicts.colonnadeDepth).

draw.compression.why: ONE factor, applied to every outward projection inside the band, so the colonnade's internal proportions survive even though its depth does not.

facade.balcony.project.why: The sourced 2.2 m depth carried through the one compression factor every outward projection inside the band takes.

facade.terrace.project.why: The sourced 3.0 m depth through the same factor.

entry.canopy.project.why: The sourced 2.6 m canopy projection through the same factor.

entry.beam.project.why: The entry beams run out to the fascia and stop there. The retired value ran them 2.6 m PAST it — nothing projects north of the roof plate in the orthophoto (plate north z 425.9 apparent, 429.2 corrected, against the ring's 428.9).

grid.insetRatio.why: Scale-free: how far the outer strut stands from the corner, as a fraction of the pair-to-pair spacing, both measured in oceanlight-21220.

grid.gapRatio.northSouth.why: ONE GRID, BOTH WAYS. The drawing's rows 1-10 run in x, so this ratio dimensions the NORTH and SOUTH faces. It is 53.5/241.1 on the re-measured sheet. The letters give 53.7/241.0 — the same number to 0.4%, because this is one square grid drawn identically in both directions. The retired 0.310544612 came from a 172.6 px interval that does not exist on the sheet (readings.kda.readingNote), and the waffle-slab story invented to explain why the two axes 'genuinely differ' is retired with it. oceanlight-21220's 0.3152 is NOT a competing read of this quantity — it is the same pair measured at head height on a leaning column (readings.px.centreNote, conflicts.gapRatioSource).

grid.gapRatio.eastWest.why: The drawing's letters A-L run in z, so this ratio dimensions the EAST and WEST faces: 53.7/241.0. It agrees with the rows' 53.5/241.1 to 0.4%. No photograph of either face resolves it and that is declared in absent; what it no longer needs is a story about why it should differ from the other axis, because it does not.

faces.0.pairSpacing.why: The grid CLOSES on the measured face: two end insets, four pair-to-pair steps and one pair gap span it exactly, with the two insets and the gap expressed as ratios of the spacing. Solving that identity is what makes the spacing derived rather than typed.

faces.1.ext.derivation: Exactly zero, and not a measurement. East and west butt into the north and south strips, which carry the roof round both corners, so neither east nor west strip gains any length at either end.

faces.3.ext.derivation: Exactly zero, and not a measurement. East and west butt into the north and south strips, which carry the roof round both corners, so neither east nor west strip gains any length at either end.

levels.storey.why: The 16.6 m less the eaves and the roof slab, split into two equal glazed levels. 7.675 m, and the stack closes with no residual.

levels.l1BelowRoof.why: Level 1 sits at grade, and grade is the measured base.

measured.skylightPlaneHeight.why: TOP DISPLACEMENT AS A RULER. The skylight field's apparent centre in the nadir mosaic stands 3.382 m from the ring centroid. Argo's roof plate displaces 3.76 m at 18.4 m of height in the SAME mosaic, i.e. 0.2043 m per metre. 3.382 / 0.2043 = 16.55 m — the LiDAR maximum to within 0.05 m. The raised skylight block IS the object that owns the 16.6, and measured.conflict stops saying that is unresolved. This rests on the field being centred in plan; it is a derivation, not a survey, and the raw apparent centre stays on the record.

roof.skylights.centre.0.why: Corrected for top displacement the field is centred on the building to within 0.1 m. The shipped 0.8 m west / 3.6 m north offset was the CAMERA, and pitchNote's 'the block itself is not quite central' was an invented asymmetry.

north.binStandoff.why: WHERE THE BINS STAND, derived instead of typed. ad01-entry-before.jpg is now cached and it settles the question the retired coordinates guessed at: the two precast cylinder bins do not stand out on the open plaza, they stand at the FEET OF THE TWO ENTRY-BEAM COLUMNS, on the plaza side, just clear of each foot — one of them carrying the blue recycling band at its rim. So the station is the strut line plus one foot half-width plus one bin radius, and that outward step is inside the colonnade band, so it takes draw.compression like every other outward projection there. The retired z 427.6 / 427.5 and the retired prose '1.6 m north of the north face' were a typed offset that was neither 1.6 m from anything nor derived from anything.

estimates.why: The ultra standard's third tier. Each entry is a figure no rung of the ladder resolved, labelled [estimated], recording the sourced pattern of this same building that it extends, carrying a MACHINE-READABLE band the shipped value must lie inside, and replaced the day a real source turns up. The band is R2 arbitration item S1(ii): before it, an estimate's only content was prose, and prose cannot be checked — argo shipped a figure 0.41 m outside the band its own document published and twenty-eight gates passed. The band is not a tolerance on a measurement; it is the range this section is willing to defend for a figure it did not measure.

grid.oversailModules.extends: grid.module, and the head bracket's sourced 1.68 m width in oceanlight-21220/-21225
grid.oversailModules.why: [estimated] the outboard band is a whole number of coffer bays — the rule the retired six-module oversail also obeyed — and two is the smallest count that holds a 1.68 m bracket plus a colonnade behind it. The band is forced by the renderer, so no source can decide it; only the rounding to the building's own module is a real constraint. R2 ARBITRATION ITEM G3: THE SHRINK IS REFUSED AND SO IS THE RE-SOLVE. audit-galbraith findings 3 and 4 argue this band is too generous; critic D4 argues it may be too small. Both arguments are denominated in metres, both need a px-per-metre for the KdA sheet, and there is no defensible one (conflicts.gridScaleThree gives three, 26% apart). Acting in either direction is guessing dressed as a repair. It STAYS AT 2, the band's lower bound is the value, and conflicts.roofPlate keeps its 12% residual declared and unrepaired.

roof.block.height.extends: the declared 1.5-2.5 m band from the roof inventory and the 2012 interior photograph
roof.block.height.why: [estimated] the middle of the declared band, carried as a number and NOT drawn as 2 m of box (roof.datumNote). The shadow that would settle it exists — the dark band on the block's north and west edges — and has not been reduced to a height; that is a job not done, recorded in absent[0].

roof.skylights.curb.why: [estimated] a curb this size expresses the field on the drawn box top without standing a storey above the LiDAR maximum. The orthophoto is nadir and dimensions the field in plan only.

roof.skylights.glassInset.extends: roof.skylights.curb, the upstand it sits inside
roof.skylights.glassInset.why: [estimated] the pane sits one curb thickness inside its own curb.

roof.penthouseExpression.why: [estimated] expression height only; the orthophoto gives the plan and no height.

roof.mechExpression.extends: roof.penthouseExpression, the taller of the two reliefs
roof.mechExpression.why: [estimated] the mech enclosures read lower than the penthouses in the orthophoto; the ratio is not measurable and only the ORDER is claimed.

roof.block.rim.curb.extends: roof.skylights.curb, the upstand it sits inside
roof.block.rim.curb.why: [estimated] the block rim reads as a thinner upstand than a skylight curb.

north.clumps.count.extends: south.clumps.count — the 110-clump south bed field read off oceanlight-21220.jpg
north.clumps.count.why: [estimated] The three north beds are planted by carrying this building's OWN sourced bed density across to the surveyed north rings, because no frame resolves what grows in them (absent[19]). Arithmetic: south beds 27.4 x 5.6 = 153.44 m2 and 27.6 x 5.6 = 154.56 m2, total 308.00 m2 carrying south.clumps.count = 110, so 0.357142857 clumps per m2; the north rings carry the survey's own areas 90.74 + 90.72 + 89.31 = 270.77 m2; 270.77 x 0.357142857 = 96.70, rounded to 97. Nothing else about the planting is re-declared — the module reads south.clumps and south.shrubFraction, so the shape, size and shrub fraction cannot drift away from the sourced field.

reads.why: Figures taken directly off a named frame, plan sheet or repo data file, with the tolerance that source supports. These are citations, not derivations: the test pins them as literals because changing one is changing what the source is claimed to say. WITHDRAWN 2026-08-21: the ten west.stair.* reads went with the stair itself. Every one of them cited ucsdmap.jpg, the ~2010 act.ucsd.edu frame whose page is 404 and which has no live home, so they were ten tolerances resting on one dead citation. The figures are not lost — west.stairNote carries the whole retired geometry verbatim — but they are no longer READS, because nothing this section draws is read off them.

draw.why: Render offsets and one render DISPLACEMENT — not dimensions. Nothing in this block is a claim about Galbraith Hall: they exist so coplanar surfaces resolve in depth, so a pane has something opaque to be transparent against, and so the whole cladding stands clear of the solid box campus-massing.js extrudes from the same ring. They are declared here rather than left as literals in the module, and the test fails on a bare number there.
draw.registrationNote: THE ONE THAT MATTERS, and it is a REGISTRATION offset and not an oversail. Every plane this section draws is displaced this far outboard of the measured ring, because the ring is already occupied to 16.6 m by a solid extrusion of itself. The building's real facade stands INSIDE the ring; it cannot be drawn there. See conflicts.roofPlate and conflicts.colonnadeDepth.
draw.tilesNote: Material REPEAT tiles: how much real surface one texture tile of campus-materials.js's smoothConcrete, decomposedGranite and pavingConcreteUnit classes covers. The unit-paver class tiles six pavers, so its tile is six of the measured paver pitch.
draw.bandsNote: R2 ARBITRATION ITEM S1(i). Every number in this block now carries a [lo, hi] window, because the coverage walk was extended to `draw` and a render offset with no declared range is indistinguishable from a dimension that has been hidden in here — which is exactly what the walk found in a sibling section. The window is +-40% of the shipped value and it is not a tolerance on a measurement: it says this is an offset of THIS ORDER, and anything outside it is no longer resolving a coplanar surface, it is claiming a size. `registration` and `compression` are absent from this map because they are DERIVED (derivations.figures) and are checked by their own arithmetic instead.

measured.heightNote: The 2014 drawn surface is FLAT at 23.5-23.9 m under the whole footprint and across the north apron (sampled on a 2 m grid against makeSurfaceSampler), so there is no storey-high step between the north plaza and the ground at the building's south edge, and the survey's earlier reading — LiDAR 16.6 above the lawn, ArcGIS 12.8 above a plaza one storey higher — cannot be what these two numbers are. That flat pad is LOCAL: the same sampler puts a ~26.8 m ridge 8-9 m west of the ring (west.gradeNote), 27.1 m within 25 m to the south (the lawn climbs past z ~503) and ~26.8 m under the east tree band, which is why every ground field in this section is draped over the drawn terrain and every solid seated per-item on it, never hung on a 23.6 level line. On the flat pad the ring stands on, LiDAR 16.6 is simply the roof above grade on all four sides, and this section puts its eaves exactly there, on top of the measured mass, so nothing measured is left standing above the roof. HOW the 16.6 divides is DERIVED and not read: the eaves (0.35) and the roof slab (0.9) are read off oceanlight-21220.jpg scaled to the measured 16.6, and what is left divides into TWO EQUAL 7.675 m glazed levels (levels.storey), which closes with no residual. The previous revision's prose described the division as roughly seven-and-a-half-metre levels over a slab of about 1.8 m and listed four components that summed to 16.5, and NEITHER of those is what the levels block ships or what it sums to; the prose is now the data, not the other way round.
measured.conflict: RESOLVED on 2026-08-20, both halves. WHICH OBJECT owns the 16.6 maximum: the raised skylight block. Its field's apparent displacement in the nadir mosaic is 3.382 m, and Argo's roof plate displaces 0.2043 m per metre of height in the same mosaic, so the skylight plane stands 16.55 m above grade — the LiDAR maximum to within 0.05 m (derivations.figures['measured.skylightPlaneHeight']). WHY the 3.8 m ArcGIS/LiDAR delta exists: 12.8 is a FORMULA (3 levels x 4.267 m, revelle-recon.md §0.1) and was never a survey, so there is no physical delta to explain. What is still unresolved is HOW HIGH the block stands above the low deck — the shadow that would settle it exists and has not been reduced to a number (absent[0]). The drawn measured mass extrudes the whole footprint to 16.6, so this section expresses the roofscape as curb-scale relief on that top rather than re-deriving the facade datum (roof.datumNote). ArcGIS's 3 levels against 2 expressed elevations is still taken as an internal third level, unbuilt.

grid.datumNote: Every facade projection in this section is measured from the GLAZING PLANE, and the glazing plane is draw.registration outboard of the measured ring. grid.roofOut is the whole outboard band from that plane to the fascia — it is NOT an oversail past the ring, because the orthophoto measures the roof plate ON the ring. See conflicts.roofPlate.
grid.calibration: WHAT SURVIVES OF THE ARCHITECT'S SHEET, AND WHY ONLY RATIOS DO. The sheet is on disk (KdA_4613_L2_OPTC.jpg, 02.17.12) and it carries a paired structural grid, five pairs in each direction — the section's oldest claim, and CONFIRMED. Its SCALE does not survive, and the reason is stronger than the one this block used to give: THREE mutually inconsistent px-per-metre scales can be read off the same raster (conflicts.gridScaleThree). (1) 19.792 px/m from the sheet's own dimension string, 50 ft 5.5 in over 304.4 px. (2) 17.89 px/m implied by the retired solve, 241.0 px over 13.471 m. (3) ~14.6 px/m implied by the sheet against the measured building — the plan's black structural columns land on grid lines C (343.5) through J (1254.5), 911 px, across a measured ArcGIS/OSM ring of 62.4 x 62.7 m. Scales (1) and (3) are 26% apart. That is not rounding; it means the dimension string and the building cannot both be describing this raster, and a 26% uncertainty in px/m is 26% of any metre figure taken off it. So the sheet's RATIOS are used and its metres are not. RATIOS TRAVEL; METRES DO NOT. THE WAFFLE-SLAB STORY IS DELETED, not softened. This block used to say 'the two axes genuinely differ because this is a waffle-slab building with different beam spacing each way'. They do not differ: the rows read 53.5/241.1 = 0.2219 and the letters 53.7/241.0 = 0.2228, one square grid to 0.4%. The apparent difference existed only because rowPairToPair shipped as 172.6, an interval that appears nowhere on the sheet, and the story was invented afterwards to explain a gap that a bad reading had opened. A building IS a waffle slab here — Arch2O says so about the exposed original concrete — but that fact was doing work it cannot do, and it is no longer asked to. The previous revision's calibration also said the drawing's COUNT survives and its SPACING is dropped; the count does survive, but it then kept the drawing's 2.45 m gap while stretching the spacing to 14.19 m, breaking the drawing's own ratio by 31%.
grid.moduleNote: The module's chain is re-derived and is untouched by the R2 ratio correction, because it never used the sheet at all. It was '10.83 / 8', and 10.83 does not reproduce from the sheet, so that chain rested on nothing. It is now the mean of two chains that need no drawing: the orthophoto's own 2.7422 m skylight pitch over two coffer bays, and the 46 coffers counted across the elevation on the measured mean face. The value moves 1.354 -> 1.3603, inside both chains' spread.
grid.source: KdA_4613_L2_OPTC.jpg — Kevin deFreitas Architects, 'GALBRAITH HALL RENOVATION', UCSD PROJECT NO. 4613, SECOND FLOOR LEVEL PLAN, OPT C, DATE ISSUED 02.17.12, scale 1/8in = 1ft-0in, marked 'THIS SET IS FOR CLIENT USE & REFERENCE. NOT FOR CONSTRUCTION.' Cached in Revelle-College-Sources/plans-and-drawings/.

faces.redBandSource: oceanlight-21225.jpg and oceanlight-12848.jpg (~2007-2012, both cached in Revelle-College-Sources/renders/galbraith-sources/) photograph the SOUTH-WEST arris from the south-west, and in both the dark-red stripe on the terrace fascia runs the full visible length of the SOUTH terrace, turns the arris and continues onto the west: it is one continuous band round the corner, not a west-face feature. oceanlight-21220.jpg, the straight-on south elevation, carries the same stripe along the whole south terrace edge. This face shipped redBand false, which cut the band dead at the arris and was visual round-2 finding 3 ('the ground-storey wall dies at both west corners'). Set true 2026-08-21. The band's DEPTH is unchanged — facade.terrace.redBand still comes off the west reading. What these frames also settle, and what is therefore NOT changed here: the buff panel infill (flutedWall) does NOT turn the arris. In oceanlight-21225.jpg the ground storey reads glass bays → a full-height pale corner pier → panel bays, so the FRAMING (pier, lintel band, terrace, red stripe) is continuous and only the INFILL changes face to face, which is what the model already builds on three of the four sides.

faces.sourcedNote: [estimated] NOT SOURCED, and now labelled. No photograph of the east elevation exists on any rung of the ladder (absent[13] records the ladder). Its feature set is an [estimated] extension of the NORTH face's sourced pattern — colonnade, glazing and balcony, and nothing else — chosen because north is the face east most nearly resembles in the one frame that sees it at all (dc-bb1639263c_2.jpg, oblique from above): no terrace, no lower colonnade, no fluted wall, no red band. column.profileNote: Half-widths are the LATHE CIRCUMRADIUS of a four-sided section, so what an elevation shows is radius x sqrt(2): a 0.83 head reads as the photographed 1.17 m bracket and the 0.38 waist as a 0.54 m shaft. Not a straight box and not a plain taper: thin at the waist, sweeping out below into a wide flat foot and flaring above into a broad bracket that meets the beam hard. Section is square with the diagonal facing the wall. CONFIRMED IN KIND on 2026-08-20 by two frames new to this repo — dc-bb4438071r_2.jpg (UCSD Library DC ark bb4438071r, mid-1960s, within a year or two of the 1965 opening) and oceanlight-21225.jpg — and the profile is NOT to be confused with the flared mushroom-column arcade on p11 of the 2008 UC Regents deck, which revelle-recon.md §4 misattributes to this building: that photograph shows round UNPAIRED columns on a two-way grid under a continuous groin-vaulted soffit, and belongs to the science spine. See conflicts.p11.
column.profileSource: The eleven [t, halfWidth] stations are a curve traced off oceanlight-21220.jpg and dc-bb4438071r_2.jpg at the two ends and the waist, with the intermediate stations interpolated to keep the sweep continuous. Tolerance +-0.06 m on any half-width.

facade.wallStandoffNote: Not a style choice and not a dimension. campus-massing.js extrudes the UNIVERSITY'S massing ring, which stands up to 0.799 m outside the OSM ring this section is anchored to, so anything drawn closer than that disappears inside the drawn box on the east elevation. The standoff is that clearance plus draw.clearanceMargin and nothing more. It is draw.registration under another name, and the previous revision's error was to take this necessary clearance and grow a whole second building outboard on it.

west.stairNote: THE 26-TREAD WEST COURT STAIR IS WITHDRAWN (2026-08-21), not re-seated. It shipped as west.stair {x -12.6, z0 452, z1 462, width 1.5, treads 26, stringer 0.24, railHeight 1.05, landing 2.1, treadThickness 0.06, riserThickness 0.05, stringerDepth 0.34, landingThickness 0.22, picketStep 0.1} — recorded here verbatim so a live frame can restore it without re-deriving anything. Its ONLY citation was ucsdmap.jpg, whose page is 404 (conflicts.westCitation), and the ladder walked again for this one object on 2026-08-21 failed on every rung: see absent. What removed it was the pair of facts together — a dead citation AND a build the visual round-2 audit found broken (its stringers and rail caps were mirrored about the flight, so two ghost flights crossed the real one in mid-air over the paving and the rails ran out past the last tread). Either alone would have been a repair; both together are 'better absent than wrong'. colors.stairSteel survives because the entry sign's two hanging rods still wear it.

north.source: ad01-entry-before.jpg (2011-11-15, ArchDaily gallery image 01-Galbraith_Entry_AB-Alt.jpg, cached 2026-08-21), flickr-galbraith.jpg (2013, flickr 88017382@N00/9407492514, cached 2026-08-21)
north.rectSource: ad01-entry-before.jpg (2011-11-15, ArchDaily gallery image 01-Galbraith_Entry_AB-Alt.jpg, cached 2026-08-21) read against the measured ring; rect edges +-1.0 m. The three bed rings are NOT read off this frame and carry no such tolerance — they are the survey's own polygons, verbatim (north.bedSource).
north.binNote: RE-DERIVED 2026-08-21 from ad01-entry-before.jpg, which is CACHED NOW and was not when the retired coordinates were written. The first pass put both bins at z 438.4 and 438.9 — nine metres inside a solid 62 m extrusion — and the second re-seated them by typing '1.6 m north of the north face', which was neither 1.6 m from anything measured nor derived from anything, and left them 1.9 m inside the modelled eave with no gate looking at the north face at all (audit-galbraith finding 6). The frame settles it: the two precast cylinder bins stand at the FEET OF THE TWO ENTRY-BEAM COLUMNS, on the plaza side, just clear of each foot, one carrying a blue band at its rim. So both stations are now DERIVED — x on the middle pair's own two strut lines, and the outward step is north.binStandoff (derivations.figures), which is the strut line plus one column foot half-width plus one bin radius, compressed by draw.compression like every other outward projection inside the band. They still stand under the modelled roof, and so they should: they stand under the real soffit in the frame, in its shade. TWO THINGS THE FRAME DOES NOT SETTLE, recorded rather than guessed. WHICH of the two carries the recycling band: the frame's compass sense is not established, so the first pass's assignment (the lower-x bin) is carried unchanged and is not claimed to be resolved. And WHETHER THEY WERE STILL THERE IN 2013: flickr-galbraith.jpg, also cached now, shows this same paving clear of both bins two years later. Two epochs, and this section builds the ~2011 one because that is the epoch its entry furniture is sourced in.
north.bedSource: docs/data/campus-arcgis.json ground[1764], [1765] and [1766], each ring carried VERBATIM (decimetre integers divided by ten), not re-surveyed and not re-bboxed. These are SURVEYED PLANTED GROUND: all three carry the survey's own vegetation class `k: "green"`, and the campus-wide paving multipolygon ground[3632] affirmatively PUNCHES THEM OUT — #1766 is its hole 139, #1764 hole 140, #1765 hole 141, each an exact vertex-count and bbox match. The 2026 orthophoto chunk_4_7.jpg shows the same three beds, mulched, with shrub masses and one mature tree over #1766.
north.apronNote: THE APRON IS CUT ON THE THREE SURVEYED BEDS, and this is the largest correction the R2 surgery makes to this section. The retired apron was a single rectangle {x0 -7, x1 53.5, z0 415, z1 429.5} that laid jointed concrete deck over 194.9 m2 of arcgis.ground#1764, #1765 and #1766 — ground the survey classifies as planted and affirmatively excludes from its own paving polygon. That is not a withholding, it is an affirmative construction of the wrong material on surveyed ground, which is the one thing 'better absent than wrong' forbids outright; `revelle.paving` was RETIRED in this same batch for doing it to one bed ten metres away. No `absent` entry could have rescued it. The field is now seven rectangles that tile the same outline with the three beds' own survey extents removed, and the beds are BUILT in the same edit (north.beds) so the holes cannot be left empty. 2.9 m of each bed lies NORTH of the apron's z0 = 415 and was never paved; the whole ring is built as bed regardless, because the bed is the surveyed object and the apron is only what happened to overlap it.
north.plantingNote: The beds are drawn as PLANTED GROUND in a colour sampled from the repo's own 2026 orthophoto over the beds themselves (colorSources.northBed), and since 2026-08-21 they are PLANTED: 97 clumps in the south field's own species mix and density, labelled [estimated] and deriving from nothing but this building's own sourced bed (north.plantingSource). Visual round-2 finding 5 was that the apron was correctly cut on all three surveyed rings and all three were then left as flat green rectangles, which is inconsistent with the same section's west and south beds as well as with the photograph. WHICH SPECIES grow in them is still absent, and so is the mature tree over #1766 — that one is the measured tree layer's business and is not this section's to place.
north.plantingSource: [estimated] EXTENDING south.clumps, this section's own sourced bed planting. The south beds are planted with 110 clumps read off oceanlight-21220.jpg (~2007-2012), which photographs that frontage densely planted with low shrubs and flowering perennials; oceanlight-21220.jpg shows the NORTH frontage planted in the same character, and the 2026 orthophoto chunk_4_7.jpg shows all three north beds mulched with shrub masses (north.bedSource). The COUNT is the south field's own density carried across: south beds 27.4 x 5.6 + 27.6 x 5.6 = 153.44 + 154.56 = 308.00 m2, 110 clumps, 0.35714 clumps/m2; the three surveyed north rings measure 90.74 + 90.72 + 89.31 = 270.77 m2 (north.beds[].area, the survey's own figures), and 270.77 x 0.35714 = 96.70, so 97. Everything else about the planting — cone radius 0.34, height 0.62, shrub sphere ratio 1.15 and the 0.22 shrub fraction — is NOT re-declared here: the module reads south.clumps and south.shrubFraction directly, so there is exactly one set of numbers and a change to the sourced field moves both. Seeded from section.seed like every other scattered field, so two builds are byte-identical.

roof.rectSource: chunk_4_7.jpg (2026-08-04 orthophoto), every rect read at 0.125 m/px and then shifted by roof.displacement; rect edges +-0.5 m.

displacement.note: TOP DISPLACEMENT, applied to every rect on this roof. A nadir mosaic is not truly nadir at 16.6 m off its own principal point: the skylight field's apparent centre stands (0.585, 3.332) from the ring centroid, and the field is centred on the building. Every roof position read off the frame therefore carries the same vector and every one is corrected by it. The magnitude also measures the block's height (measured.skylightPlaneHeight).

roof.datumNote: NO DOUBLE-COUNTING of the ArcGIS/LiDAR gap. LiDAR 16.6 is a MAXIMUM return, and campus-massing.js draws the measured box to that height over the WHOLE footprint — so the visible box top already stands at the highest real point of this roof. The real low deck sits [estimated] 1.5-2.5 m below it and is buried inside the drawn mass; nothing can be drawn under the box top. Everything here therefore seats ON the drawn box top (the structure it stands on) and rises only curb-scale above it: skylight curbs 0.18 m, block rim 0.12 m, penthouse/mech expression 0.28-0.35 m. Plan positions and pitches are SOURCED and displacement-corrected; the expression heights are [estimated] and deliberately suppressed so nothing stands a storey above the LiDAR maximum.

block.heightNote: [estimated] 1.5-2.5 m above the true low deck (inventory + the 2012 interior photo); 2.0 m carried as the declared middle. NOT drawn as 2 m of box — see datumNote. The shadow that would settle it EXISTS (revealNote) and has not been reduced to a height.
block.revealNote: CORRECTED 2026-08-20. The previous revision said a dark band rings the block 'on all four sides; symmetric, so it is a reveal and not a cast shadow'. It is NOT symmetric: in chunk_4_7.jpg the dark band runs along the block's NORTH and WEST edges only and is absent on south and east, which is the signature of a SHADOW cast by a sun in the south-east — and the same asymmetry runs along the whole roof plate's north and west edges. So the band is a shadow, the block's height is in principle DERIVABLE from its width against a calibrated sun elevation, and that calculation has not been done. It is drawn here as a flat decal on the north and west sides only, because a reveal it is not.

skylights.pitchNote: The orthophoto measures a 2.7422 m pitch (sigma 0.06 m) over 9 x 9 units; two coffer modules is 2.7206 m, and this building solves on one grid or it is wrong, so the pitch is DERIVED as 2 x grid.module and the raw measurement is recorded in derivations.readings.ortho. THE FIELD IS CENTRED ON THE BUILDING, to within 0.1 m. The previous revision put its centre 0.8 m west and 3.6 m north of the ring centroid and wrote that the block was off-centre and the field followed it — that displacement is the CAMERA (roof.displacement), not the building, and correcting for it removes an invented asymmetry. The squares read WHITE from above: white-capped curbs, not dark glass.
skylights.epochNote: 1965 FABRIC, RETAINED. dc-bb1639263c_2.jpg (UCSD Library DC ark bb1639263c, mid-1960s aerial, within a year or two of the 1965 opening) shows the same field on the same raised block from the year the building opened, and the 2013 renovation press describes the architect working with 'the building's ORIGINAL skylights' in what was explicitly an INTERIOR renovation. Nothing in any source describes removing or replacing them. What differs between epochs is the CAP PROFILE — 1965 reads curved/domed in profile along the near edges, 2026 reads flat white-capped square curbs — and that stays absent (absent[14]).

roof.penthouseNote: Two stair/lift penthouses projecting north from the block and one large one projecting south; the south one wears a pale seamed metal roof in the orthophoto. Expression height 0.35 m [estimated] — see datumNote. All three rects are displacement-corrected.
roof.mechNote: Six dark-walled service enclosures with pale equipment inside, on the low deck. Expression height 0.28 m walls + 0.06 m equipment [estimated] — see datumNote. All six rects are displacement-corrected.
