The band is real and measured; WHAT it is is not resolved, and it is drawn as a ground band in its own tone rather than as shade (absent[16]).
east.walkNote: ~3.1 m pale tan unit-paver / scored-concrete walk running the full north-south length; a fine banded texture is visible. Band pitch 0.45 m [estimated] off the visible banding. WHERE IT STANDS RELATIVE TO THE MODELLED EAVE, stated because the R1 gate's name claimed more than its assertion checked (audit-galbraith finding 6): the walk starts at x 56.9 and the modelled roof reaches x 58.27, so its first 1.4 m stands UNDER THE MODELLED ROOF. The walk's outer edge does run out past the eave and the gate checks that; what it no longer claims is that the whole walk is clear of it. The east recess is under the eave by definition and always was.
east.footPadNote: A row of pale ~1.0-1.4 m squares along the building side of the walk at ~11-12 m spacing, read as the colonnade column feet showing past the roof edge. Pads are drawn under the BUILT east strut pairs, because pads not under their own columns would be worse than none. TENSION, recorded not resolved: the orthophoto's 11-12 m square spacing sits between the drawing's dropped 10.83 m and this section's derived 13.47 m pair spacing; at 0.125 m/px with ~1.2 m blobs neither is excluded. The tension NARROWED on 2026-08-20 — the retired 14.19 m spacing was 18% off the orthophoto's rhythm and the derived 13.47 m is 12% off it.
east.dgNote: Broad decomposed-granite band under the mature tree canopies out to x~89; the trees themselves stay the measured tree layer's business. Split into two rects because York Hall's measured footprint reaches x 83.9 / z 431.8 at its south-west corner and nothing invented may lie inside a measured building.
east.lawnNote: South-east lawn patch; its shrub masses and the low diagonal wall/step stay absent.
east.constructionNote: EPOCH LIMIT: beyond x ~90 the orthophoto shows the Central Utilities Plant Expansion site in flux — disturbed earth, plant, a temporary haul road, a large white-roofed structure. That ground is left UNBUILT. It is a NEIGHBOURING project (absent[2]), not work on Galbraith.
east.gradeNote: WHY THE EAST BASE READS BURIED, and why nothing here moves. Visual round-2 finding 2 reported the east elevation's foot cut off by a bare tan bank. Every ground field on this side is draped per-vertex on the DRAWN surface (drapedQuad over surfaceAt) and none of them is hung on a level, so this is not a datum error — it is what the 2014 bare-earth grid actually does east of the ring. Sampled off campus-lidar.json terrain (3 m cells, decimetres) on 2026-08-21, at z 434 through 490 in 2 m steps: x 54.6, 56 and 58 all read between 23.5 and 23.9 m, which is FLAT at the wall and the same height as the pad under the footprint; x 60 reads 24.3-26.5 m; and x 62 through 68 reads 26.7-26.9 m and holds that plateau out past x 70 before dropping to 23.4-25.2 m at x 80. (The one cell that is not flat at the wall is z ~430 at x 56-58, reading 25.1 m; that 3 m cell straddles the north apron's own edge at the corner of the face and is not the east grade.) So the ground does not rise against the building: it stands 3.1 m above the building's pad starting about 5 m out from the wall. The az090-low camera stands ON that plateau at x 83.96 with its eye at 26.35 m, and the sightline from there to the wall foot at (55.5, 23.8) falls 0.0896 m per metre — so it passes 24.56 m at x 64, where the surface is 26.9 m, and 25.10 m at x 70, where the surface is 26.5 m. The crest stands 1.4-2.3 m above the line of sight and occludes the whole base. WHAT the plateau is, is not resolved and is not asserted: it runs the full length of the face under the mature tree canopies the dg band is drawn for (east.dgNote) and it carries a 22.3-23.8 m trough at x 68-70 over z 470-480, which is 4.6 m of relief inside its own plateau and the signature of a bare-earth classifier working under canopy — the same condition west.gradeNote already declines to call topography 8-9 m west of the ring. No retaining condition is modelled because no source shows one. See absent.

treeOverrides.note: Photo-layer re-skin of measured LiDAR trunks whose rendered blob crowns would pierce a slab this section draws. Each item is a row copied VERBATIM from campus-lidar.json trees ([x, z, h, r] as key x,z); the trunk stays measured — position, height and spread are not this section's to move. Only the RENDERED canopy changes: it is pruned below the ceiling named by the item's `ceiling` (the roof soffit by default, the balcony soffit where the item says so), the way the real understorey tree under the NE roof corner is kept. That canopy shaping is INVENTED (no photograph resolves either of these trees against its slab); its species tint comes from the same campus-species table the measured blob renderer uses, so no new colour enters this file, and nothing measured may read from this block.
treeOverrides.wiringNote: campus-walk.js and campus-scooter.js must union these keys into the createTrees skipKeys set alongside plaza.treeOverrides.skipMeasuredKeys, or the measured blob renderer draws the same stem a second time, through the slab.

canopy.note: Shaping constants for the pruned canopy. Every one is INVENTED expression, not a measurement — they decide how a clamped crown is distributed, not how big the tree is (that is the measured row). They live here so the module carries no bare number.

items.why: stands 0.5-1.5 m outside the measured ring at the NE corner and under the roof band, whose north-east corner now reaches 3.67 m past the ring on both axes (draw.registration + grid.roofOut); its measured 18.3 m top rises past the soffit and the blob crown punched through the slab (visual audit 2026-08-17, az045-high/roof nadir). RE-DERIVED 2026-08-20: the retired reason cited a twelve-and-a-half-metre NE roof oversail, which no longer exists. At the built 3.67 m band this trunk is still 1.8 m INSIDE the roof corner in x and 1.5 m inside it in z, so the prune still stands — but by 1.8 m, not by 11 m, and if the band is ever cut further this override must be re-checked rather than assumed.

VISUAL ROUND-2 FINDING 4: this stem rendered as a trunk standing inside the east elevation, occluded by the projecting level-2 deck where it passed it and reappearing above with its crown against the glass. It is a MEASURED LiDAR trunk — campus-lidar.json trees row [55.9, 455.2, 13.9, 7.5], copied verbatim — so nothing about it moves. What puts it inside the envelope is this section's own draw.registration: the ring traces the ROOF PLATE (conflicts.roofPlate), the real facade stands INSIDE it, and every plane this section draws is displaced 0.949 m OUTBOARD of the ring because the ring is already occupied by a solid extrusion of itself. That puts the drawn glazing at x 55.549 and the drawn balcony edge at x 56.766, with the trunk at x 55.9 between them — 0.35 m outboard of the glass and 0.87 m inboard of the deck edge. On the real building the facade is inboard of x 54.6 and this tree stands in front of it. The re-skin is therefore the same treatment as the NE-corner stem and for the same reason, with one difference recorded in the data rather than in the module: the ceiling it is pruned below is the BALCONY soffit (facade.balcony.deck under levels.l2BelowRoof), not the roof soffit, because the balcony is the slab it was passing through. `ceiling` is what says so. The measured 13.9 m height is unchanged in the data and is not claimed by the drawn crown, which stands about 6.6 m — see absent.

conflicts.why: Declared, never averaged. Each entry names two sources or two readings that disagree, says what each one is describing, and says which one this section draws.
conflicts.roofPlate: THE LARGEST CORRECTION IN THIS SECTION. The measured OSM/ArcGIS ring traces the ROOF EDGE, not the wall line: chunk_4_7.jpg measures the roof plate at 62.45 x 61.9 m against the ring's 62.4 x 62.7, the SAME SIZE, offset by a constant (-0.9, -3.4) which is top displacement and not a real shift (Argo's plate displaces the same vector in the same mosaic 110 m away). The previous revision built a second roof 12.474 m OUTSIDE that ring — an 87.4 x 87.7 m plate, 40% oversized — and then laid its own sourced east and west ground furniture underneath it. What this section draws instead: the roof plate stands draw.registration + grid.roofOut = 3.67 m outside the ring, ALL of which is the registration band forced by campus-massing.js's solid extrusion of the same ring, and NONE of which is claimed as an oversail. The modelled plate is 69.7 x 70.0 m against the measured 62.45 x 61.9: still 12% oversized, and that residual is the price of cladding a solid box from the outside. It is the section's largest remaining error and it is declared, not hidden. OPEN FOR ARBITRATION.
conflicts.colonnadeDepth: The photographs read 3.4 m between the glass and the strut line. Only grid.roofOut = 2.72 m of band exists between the glazing plane and the fascia, and 1.68 m of that is the head bracket, so the built glass-to-strut depth is column.standoffBuilt = 1.88 m: 0.553 of the sourced figure. Every outward projection inside the band carries the same factor (draw.compression), so the colonnade's proportions survive even though its depth does not. Both numbers ship: column.standoff is the building, column.standoffBuilt is the drawing. OPEN FOR ARBITRATION.
conflicts.oversailCount: RETIRED CLAIM. The previous revision counted 'six coffer modules of oversail' in ad01-entry-before.jpg and wm-from-below.jpg — 8.12 m of roof past the strut line. Two frames new to this repo on 2026-08-20 (oceanlight-21225.jpg and oceanlight-12848.jpg, both south-west corner obliques with 'Galbraith Hall' on the fascia) show the head brackets DYING INTO the fascia: there is no metre of roof past the strut heads, let alone eight. The six-module count is not reproducible and is not carried. What the six modules probably measured is the whole soffit from the wall to the edge, which is a different span.
conflicts.gridScale: The KdA sheet's RATIOS reproduce and its METRES do not. The shipped 2.45 m pair gap and the 10.83 m pair spacing both need 22.2 px/m; the sheet's own dimension string gives 19.79 px/m. Being 12% small TOGETHER is one bad scale factor. Ratios are used; metres are not. See grid.calibration.
conflicts.gapRatioSource: REWRITTEN IN R2 ARBITRATION; THE PREVIOUS ENTRY WAS FALSE IN BOTH HALVES. It said the sheet reads 0.3105 on the north and south faces and oceanlight-21220 reads 0.3152 on the same faces, 1.5% apart, and it presented that agreement as a corroboration. Both numbers were wrong and their agreement was the most dangerous shape a corroboration can take. The 0.3105 came from a 172.6 px interval that does not exist on the sheet. The 0.3152 is a real measurement of a DIFFERENT QUANTITY: readings.px measures its gap at pairGapCentre, the pair's mid/centre height, and these columns lean, so above the slab that measures the lean as well as the grid. WHAT THE TWO SOURCES ACTUALLY SAY. The drawing gives the grid ratio AT THE SLAB: 0.2219 in the rows and 0.2228 in the letters, one value both ways. The photograph gives the built pair's separation at HEAD height: 0.257 to 0.315 depending on how high it is sampled, and 0.221 when it is sampled at the bases. The difference between them is the columns' declared lean, and it is a measurement OF the lean, not a disagreement about the grid. This gives the section a corroboration it did not previously have and could not have claimed: column.splayHead is [estimated] at 1.15 m and until now nothing in any frame put a number on it. RESOLVED, not open.
conflicts.cofferModule: The coffer module derives 1.3711 m from the orthophoto's skylight pitch and 1.3495 m from the 46 counted coffers on the measured mean face — 1.6% apart. The mean, 1.3603, ships; neither chain is discarded and neither is presented as the measurement.
conflicts.outerGridLines: The KdA sheet's letters A-L carry a SINGLE grid line outside the outermost pair at each end, and its rows 1-10 carry five pairs and no outer singles. conflicts.p11: revelle-recon.md §4 describes p11 of the 2008 UC Regents deck as showing 'Galbraith's flared mushroom-column arcade'. IT IS NOT GALBRAITH. That photograph shows round, UNPAIRED columns on a two-way grid flaring into four-way hyperbolic-paraboloid capitals that meet to form a continuous groin-vaulted soffit with pointed-arch openings. Galbraith's order is PAIRED, LEANING, splay-footed, square in section on the diagonal, flaring into a broad flat head bracket under a coffered WAFFLE-SLAB soffit — two frames now on disk show it (dc-bb4438071r_2.jpg, oceanlight-21220.jpg). conflicts.gridScaleThree: THREE px-PER-METRE SCALES OFF ONE RASTER, NONE OF WHICH AGREE, and this is the real reason the sheet's metres are not used. (1) 19.792 px/m — the sheet's own dimension string, 50 ft 5.5 in = 15.3797 m over 304.4 px. At this scale the measured A-L span of 1394.5 px is 70.46 m and pair-to-pair is 12.177 m. (2) 17.89 px/m — implied by this section's own shipped solve, 241.0 px over the derived 13.471 m spacing. (3) ~14.6 px/m — implied by the sheet against the measured building: thresholding the plan area at <90 puts the black structural columns on grid lines C (343.5) through J (1254.5), 911 px, and the measured ArcGIS/OSM ring is 62.4 x 62.7 m. (1) and (3) are 26% apart. WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS RATHER THAN A RE-SOLVE. Exactly one of the three scales — (1) — makes the pleasing coincidence appear that A-L at 70.46 m sits within 0.1 m of the modelled 70.04 m roof plate; (2) gives 77.9 m and (3) gives 95.5 m. Choosing the scale that produces the coincidence and then citing the coincidence as support for that scale is circular, and the R2 arbitration declined to do it and declined to let this surgery do it. The 13.471 m spacing is NOT re-solved, grid.oversailModules is NOT shrunk, and conflicts.roofPlate keeps its 12% residual declared and unrepaired. R2 should re-source the scale from a dimensioned drawing or a measured control length in a photograph. OPEN FOR ARBITRATION.

conflicts.columnTone: A CONSEQUENCE OF THE R2 COLOUR RULING, DECLARED RATHER THAN TIDIED AWAY. `column` was deleted as a boilerplate [estimated] hex and re-earned by SAMPLING the cached crop, which is what the ruling required. THE WEST COURT STAIR AND ITS RAILS. A 26-tread flight from the west paving up to the terrace shipped at west.stair and is WITHDRAWN (west.stairNote). Its only citation was ucsdmap.jpg, the ~2010 act.ucsd.edu campus-map photograph whose page returns 404 and whose frame has no live home (research-galbraith.md §6.1, conflicts.westCitation). The ultra ladder was walked again for this one object on 2026-08-21 and every rung failed. PHOTOGRAPHS: oceanlight-21219.jpg, -21220.jpg, -21225.jpg and -12848.jpg are all cached and all four see the court paving at the terrace foot; NONE of them shows a flight rising out of it. The only exterior stair any live frame carries is a STEEL SWITCHBACK from the terrace deck up to level 2, hard against the wall at the south face's west end (oceanlight-21220.jpg, crop x 60-420 / y 200-400) — a different object at a different datum, on the deck and not on the ground, and it is not built either because one oblique frame gives it no measurable plan position. STREET VIEW: Revelle is pedestrian; no trekker or photosphere coverage of the west court was found. DRONE/VIDEO: none. PLANNING DOCS/DRAWINGS: KdA_4613_L2_OPTC.jpg and _L3_ (02.17.12) are floor plans and stop at the building line; no site or elevation sheet was found. ARCHIVES: dc-bb4438071r_2.jpg (mid-1960s) and dc-bb1639263c_2.jpg do not see this court. A 26-tread flight is far too large an object to keep standing on a dead citation.

WHETHER THE 3.1 m EAST BANK IS GROUND. The 2014 drawn surface stands 3.1 m above the building's own pad from x ~62 out past x ~70 along the whole east face, and that bank occludes the foot of the east elevation from any eye-level station east of it (east.gradeNote has the sampled profile and the sightline arithmetic). Nothing in this section moves because of it — every east ground field is draped per-vertex on that surface, which is the rule — but TWO readings survive it and no source separates them. (a) Real topography: the York service apron east of Galbraith genuinely sits higher, and the bank is the cut between them, in which case a retaining wall or a bank planting exists there and is unbuilt. (b) A bare-earth classifier artefact under the mature tree canopies, the same shape west.gradeNote declines to call topography 8-9 m west of the ring; the 4.6 m trough at x 68-70 over z 470-480 inside the plateau argues for this one. The 2026 orthophoto is nadir and cannot see a vertical face, and the east face has no photograph at all (its own absent entry, faces[3].sourced = false). Resolving it needs an oblique frame or a spot elevation, and neither was found. Until then no retaining condition is invented and the burial is declared rather than dressed.

HOW TALL THE TWO RE-SKINNED EAST TREES REALLY STAND AGAINST THE FACADE. campus-lidar.json measures them at 18.3 m (55.9, 427.4) and 13.9 m (55.9, 455.2) and neither figure is touched, but the drawn crowns are clamped below the slab each stem was passing through — the roof soffit for the first, the balcony soffit for the second — which leaves the second reading about 6.6 m rather than 13.9 m. That clamp is a consequence of draw.registration displacing this section's whole facade 0.949 m outboard of the ring (treeOverrides.items[1].why, and the plan-oversize entry that displacement also causes) and NOT a claim that either tree was topped. What no source resolves is what the real trees do where they meet the real building: the east elevation has no photograph at all, and the 2026 orthophoto is nadir and sees canopy over roof, not the gap between them. Restore the measured heights the day an oblique east frame appears.

counts.note: Terrain-independent counts, every one asserted against what the module actually builds. `pickets`, `coffers`, `downlights` and `lowerColumns` fall out of the derived grid and the derived module rather than being chosen, which is why they are the counts that move when a derivation moves. `northBeds` is 3 and is not a choice either: it is how many surveyed planted rings the north apron was paving over (north.apronNote), and the ground-furniture gate fails if the apron is ever re-laid across one of them.

plaza.label: Revelle Plaza landscape — trees, ground features and furniture of Zone 1 (the ground between Keeling, York, Argo, Blake and Galbraith)
plaza.epoch: Photographs 2006-2026 decide what exists and how it looks; the georeferenced satellite plan (Google chunks, generated 2026-08-04) decides plan positions; LiDAR 2014 decides every re-skinned trunk's position, height and crown radius. The coral tree post-dates the LiDAR (planted February 2014) and is the one tree here with no measured trunk. R1 (2026-08-20) added two older rungs at the archive end of the ladder — UCSD DC bb5393567s (SIO Photographic Laboratory Collection, the plaza's early decades) and bb1741784h (Robert Glasheen Photograph Collection, colour, 1980s) — so this section now spans roughly sixty years and every figure below says which year it is describing.
plaza.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. Everything here is modelled off dated photographs and a plan-only satellite read. Nothing measured may ever read from this section. The treeOverrides re-skin measured LiDAR trunks by position key: heights and crown radii are copied VERBATIM from docs/data/campus-lidar.json (whose r is clamped at 7.5 m and h at 30 m — floors, not measurements, see treeOverrides.clampNote). No colour here is sampled from raw satellite pixels; the orthophoto is a build-time PLAN instrument and every colour it contradicts is recorded in `conflicts` rather than repainted from it. NO PALMS: twelve palm taxa are on the campus list and zero appear in any Zone 1 photograph, and the rule survived contact in R1 with two new sources at opposite ends of the epoch ladder — the 2026 orthophoto over the whole plaza envelope, where palms would be unmistakable from above, and UCSD DC bb1741784h and bb91478709 at the archive end. R1 (2026-08-20) took ownership of the plaza's paving from the legacy revelle section, adopted the surveyed lawn and north bed, added the five flanking beds, clipped the DG belt on Galbraith's measured ring, and gave all 42 hexes a provenance tier. Every figure it changed is derived in `derivations` with its arithmetic; every figure it declined to change is in `conflicts` with both readings.

treeOverrides.note: Position-keyed re-skins of measured LiDAR trunks (key = 'x,z' exactly as in docs/data/campus-lidar.json trees). This module builds the ultra models; MAIN MUST SKIP the default blob rendering for every key in skipMeasuredKeys or each tree draws twice. Species verdicts are photo-sourced (zone1-plaza-landscape.md §1): the York belt is Torrey pine (the h>=16 heuristic mislabels it eucalyptus), the plaza/Argo broadleafs are ficus, eucalyptus only east of York and on the Keeling west road. Groups E-north and G stay generic blobs — per-tree confidence is too low to re-skin them. The trunk at 55.9,427.4 is re-skinned by the galbraith section instead (its canopy must clear the oversail slab), so it is not in this roster.

pines.source: Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012), Revelle_Plaza_Path,_UCSD.jpg (2011); Pinus torreyana on the official campus species list. Clear bole 55-65% of height, open irregular candelabra crown reading ~40-50% sky.

ficus.source: Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) — pale sinuous multi-stem trunks under tight dark canopies; Ficus microcarpa/retusa/rubiginosa all on the official list. Plaza-core group C plus the two small trees hard against Argo's south side.

eucalyptus.source: Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012) — the grove edge east of York (group B), plus the tall road-frontage trees on the Keeling west road (group F, h>=14; keeling-inventory.md corroborates).

coral.source: today.ucsd.edu/news_uploads/memorial1.jpg (Feb 2014) — multi-stem, smooth pale grey-green bark, sparse open branching, planted in a ~2.5 m bare-earth ring for the memorial unveiling. NOT in the 2014 LiDAR (planted at/after that epoch).
coral.tag: [measured] spread — the 2026 orthophoto measures this canopy directly, and two independent reads of the same frame give 7.9 x 7.3 m (mean 7.6) and 7.3 x 7.1 m (mean 7.2); shipped at their mean, 7.4 m. That REPLACES a spread of 9 that was extrapolated growth. [estimated] height — h 8 is still a 5 m nursery specimen in 2014 grown to a 12-year irrigated coral tree, now constrained by a measured spread; the canopy's own shadow lies inside the lawn's tonal range and cannot be used. [estimated] species — unresolved among three Erythrina on the campus list, so it is generic and unflowered. The position was already right: shipped (32, 378) against a measured canopy centre of (32.3, 378.1) and (32.5, 377.8), i.e. 0.32 m and 0.51 m.

treeOverrides.clampNote: ELEVEN of the 39 roster entries sit at a LiDAR clamp (r = 7.5 or h = 30) and those are FLOORS, NOT MEASUREMENTS. Three are in the plaza core and are drawn at exactly the clamp because the module has no way to draw an open bound: (51, 399.1) h 10 r >=7.5, (1, 380.2) h 8.9 r >=7.5, (80.9, 351.4) h 25.9 r >=7.5. Their crowns are AT LEAST 7.5 m and unbounded above; the 2026 ortho cannot close the bound because at those three positions the canopies merge with their neighbours. Declared here and in absent rather than left to read as measurements.

fountain.source: Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012 aerial) + Revelle_Plaza.jpg (2006) + Galbraith Hall with Revelle Fountain (2024) for the running jet, and from R1 (2026-08-20) two instruments that were not available before. (a) UCSD DC bb5393567s, SIO Photographic Laboratory Collection (SAC 44), a ground-level three-quarter frame: it resolves the plinth's BATTERED sides, the flat deck used as seating, the circular basin recessed into that deck, and a jet that is a central plume plus a ring of discrete arcing perimeter nozzles rather than a smooth cone skirt. Black and white — authoritative for form, worthless for colour. (b) the 2026 orthophoto at 8 px/m, which measures the plinth and both basin rings in plan. The centre stays the landmark's surveyed OSM point: position from OSM wins over any photo or satellite read, and it is now corroborated to 0.23 m by an independent instrument (derivations.reads.fountainCentre).
fountain.replacesNote: MAIN MUST SUPPRESS the landmark ring-fountain basin + jet (campus-landmarks 'Revelle Plaza Fountain') when this section is present, exactly as skipMeasuredKeys suppresses the blob trees — its builder draws an 8 m basin and jet at this same surveyed point, so without suppression two fountains interpenetrate. KEEP the landmark's flagpole, flag and hardware: they are that entry's, not this section's.
fountain.rotNote: [measured] 0, i.e. the plinth is square to the world axes, to better than 0.5 degrees. Three independent tests, all in derivations.figures.fountainRotation. This REPLACES a shipped 0.26 rad (14.9 degrees), which swung the corners of a 7.6 m square by 1.9 m.
fountain.jetNote: RE-MODELLED IN R1 off UCSD DC bb5393567s. The shipped jet was a central foam column inside a smooth 2.6 m radius, 1.5 m high cone skirt. The photograph shows the skirt is a COUNTABLE RING OF DISCRETE ARCS springing from the basin rim and falling inward toward the plume, so it is now built as `nozzles` individual arcing streams. The central plume (coreHeight, coreRadius) is unchanged and is corroborated in colour by UCSD DC bb1741784h. See derivations.figures.nozzleCount for the count and the conflict it carries, and derivations.estimates.nozzleRadius, .nozzleRise, .nozzleReach and .streamRadius for what is not measured and the band each is held inside.

memorial.source: today.ucsd.edu memorial1.jpg + memorial2.jpg (February 2014). Half-disc concrete slab FLUSH in the lawn, brick soldier trim on the straight edge, ~15 flush light lenses in a star figure with engraved connecting lines, curved concrete bench on a lava-rock rubble base. R1 (2026-08-20) verified the POSITION three independent ways and upgraded it from a press-photo read to a corroborated one — see derivations.reads.memorialPosition. Independent 2014 dedication coverage describes the object as 'a semicircle plaque with a constellation of lights, a coral tree and a bench', which corroborates every element built here. The SLAB'S OWN GEOMETRY is NOT corroborated: the coral canopy (7.4 m across) completely occludes a 7.5 m half-disc from above, so the ortho confirms the tree and says nothing about the slab.
memorial.lensNote: [estimated] layout — a star figure of ~15 lenses radiating from an off-centre node, as memorial1.jpg shows; the exact chart is not resolvable in either frame

lawns.source: arcgis.ground#2323 — the facilities GIS green polygon, ONE panel, 1498 m2, x -0.6..46.9, z 377.3..409.7. This REPLACES two photo-read rectangles split by an invented 6 m paved cross-walk. Measured beats photo-read for a plan boundary. The 1.3 m edging band that actually crosses the lawn is measured off the 2026 orthophoto (derivations.figures.lawnEdging); the ortho and the survey agree to about 1 m on every outer edge (derivations.reads.lawnOuterEdge). lawns.edgingNote: A 1.30 m pale paved lip and dark brick edging band crossing the lawn — a mow strip, not a walk. It is drawn as a decal on the same rung the retired cross-walk used, so the lawn reads as one continuous panel banded across, which is what the instrument shows.
lawns.crossWalkNote: RETIRED, NOT DELETED — see superseded.crossWalk. A 6 m paved cross-walk that does not exist; the object at that place is the 1.30 m edging band above.

arcs.source: Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) mid-ground — at every band crossing the panel corners are struck with a 1.5-2.0 m radius and the brick coursing FANS to follow each arc. R1 (2026-08-20): the crossings are now derived from THIS section's own paving cells rather than reaching across into revelle.paving, and pitch tracks paving.pitch (6.4 -> 6.65). band 0.42 and radius 1.8 are unchanged and were both re-confirmed against the 2026 orthophoto at 64 px/m — see derivations.reads.bandAndRadius.

dgBelt.source: satellite plan — bare tan ground under the York-belt Torrey pines; decomposed granite is confirmed on the north approach behind the lava walls. R1 (2026-08-20) CLIPPED THE SOUTH END from z 470 to z 428.9. galbraith.east.dg is x 60..89, z 428.9..491.1, so the two belts overlapped over x 66..82, z 428.9..470 — a 16 x 41 m rectangle, 656 m2 of decomposed granite built twice on two overlay rungs. 428.9 is exactly min z of the Galbraith Hall ring in campus-3d.json and exactly galbraith.east.dg's own north edge, so the two decals now abut on one measured line with neither gap nor overlap.
dgBelt.tag: [estimated] extent — the belt's edges are read off the satellite plan, its surface off the north-approach photographs. The Torrey pine canopy occludes this ground COMPLETELY from above: sampling the 2026 ortho over x 66..82 returns #5c5b4f and #525544, which is canopy, not ground. The ladder is genuinely exhausted from above and the tag stays. The south edge alone is now measured, not estimated — see source.

lamp.source: Revelle_Plaza__UCSD.JPG (2011), Revelle_Plaza_Path,_UCSD.jpg (2011), Revelle_Plaza.jpg (2006) — three frames agree; scaled off the published 54-inch banner. Pole 5.5-6.0 m built at 5.75; section built square 0.12 (round-vs-square unresolved at plaza distance). Crossarm pair of 20x54-inch banners, bottom bracket 2.8-3.1 m, top 4.2-4.5 m; gold-dominant design. The photographed pair contradicts the newer one-banner brand rule — epoch conflict, photos win for this model. R1 (2026-08-20) changed the ROSTER, not the type: four bannered poles at x 79 transferred in from revelle.lamps with the DG belt they stand in (revelle.supersededDetail); two unbannered posts were added on measured pads in the north bed; and the post at (24, 377.8) moved to its measured pad at (21.9, 377.1). Every item now carries an explicit `banner` flag, because the north-bed pair is a position read and not a banner read.
lamp.positionNote: [measured] for the item at (21.9, 377.1) — two independent reads of its pad, see derivations.figures.lawnLampPad — and for the two north-bed items. [estimated] for the other five plaza-side items and for the four transferred belt poles: they are 2006-2012 photo reads and only one of the six lawn-edge pads resolves cleanly enough in the ortho to move a post on. See absent.

benches.source: REBUILT IN R1 (2026-08-20) FROM THE 2026 ORTHOPHOTO. The shipped row (9 items at z 377.8, x 16..44.8, 3.6 m pitch, 2.2 m long) and revelle.benchesA's row (7 items at z 379.2) were 1.46 m apart and overlapped in plan; the instrument then showed NEITHER is where the objects are. Seven objects read at 8 px/m as dark red-brown bars set against a paving panel's north edge, in two rows, both on the paving module's own 6.65 m pitch: four at z 344.6 and three at z 375.2, all over x 0..24, the plaza's west half. Footprints and positions are measured (derivations.figures.benchRows). IDENTITY IS NOT — see absent and conflicts[2]; they are built as the type revelle.benchesB already sources from a 2011 frame, which is the reading UCSD DC bb1741784h supports.
benches.heldNote: HELD OUT OF THE DRAW, KEPT IN THE RECORD — see conflicts[7]. The three south-row objects are measured to the instrument, and the shipped corridor-staging centreline does not merely pass close to them: IT RUNS THROUGH ONE. Its vertices here are (6.1, 376.0), (8.1, 375.6), (10.0, 374.9), (11.8, 374.0), and THE VERTEX (10.0, 374.9) LIES INSIDE the first bench's 3.9 x 0.88 m footprint, x 6.74..10.64 by z 374.68..375.56. This is a PLAN INTERSECTION, not a clearance. Measured footprint-to-centreline, the two held objects stand at 0.09 m and 1.58 m against a campus-wide rule of 3 m (re-measured in this surgery at 0.00 m for the first — an intersection is a clearance of zero, and the critic's 0.09 m figure is the same fact stated as a near miss). The record previously said '0.48 m of clearance', which understated it. The third south-row object at (22.0, 375.19) clears by 5.96 m footprint-to-centreline and IS built, as are all four north-row objects — the hold is exactly the two the rule condemns and not one object wider. NOTE WHAT THE SECOND BENCH PROVES: its CENTRE clears the centreline by 3.10 m and its FOOTPRINT by 1.58 m, so a centre-only test would have passed an object the rule condemns. That is evidence the 3 m furniture-clearance gate is calibrated correctly rather than pedantically, and the R2 arbitration REFUSED any proposal to widen it. THE OBJECTS ARE NOT WRONG and the gate is not wrong: this is a survey-versus-survey disagreement between an 8 px/m ortho read of the bench row and the OSM footway the router followed. Held rather than deleted, and rather than loosening a gate, because this agent does not own the corridor: scripts/build-corridor.mjs and tests/corridor.test.mjs gate the centreline and CLAUDE.md forbids relaxing either.

binPairs.source: Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) square precast bin + the aerial's cylindrical bins standing in pairs at the lawn edge

bikes.source: Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) — 25+ bicycles double-parked on the Argo rack run; at plaza distance the bikes are the object, so the bikes are built over the existing rack row
bikes.retiredNote: RETIRED 2026-08-21 by R2 arbitration item R2 — count 25 -> 0, the run is no longer drawn. The record is kept in place, with its 2012 read intact, because a claim this section can no longer support moves to `superseded` rather than being deleted; see superseded['furniture.bikes'] for the evidence and conflicts[3] for the chain. tests/campus-photo-plaza.test.mjs asserts count === 0 rather than dropping the assertion, because that gate is what forced the question into the open (it caught the audit's P9 mutation) and it must keep standing between this row and a silent resurrection.

terraces.source: satellite plan (2026 imagery — current epoch) — two cafe terraces with round umbrellas: the plaza north-east terrace and a larger mixed blue/orange terrace at Revelle Commons / 64 Degrees. R1 (2026-08-20) re-measured the plaza terrace: it is a 2 x 2 block plus one detached umbrella, not the five-item zigzag row that shipped (derivations.figures.terraceUmbrellas). The Commons terrace (items 5-12) is untouched and held for R2 — see boundsExceptions.

umbrella.radiusNote: [measured, two reads disagreeing] KEPT AT 1.25. Masking the saturated blue canopy core at 8 px/m gives five diameters of 2.21-2.29 m (radius 1.13); research-plaza.md section 6 reads the same canopies at 3.1 m (radius 1.57), taking the shaded rim in. The shipped 1.25 sits between the two reads and inside both error bars, so it is not moved on either. Recorded rather than averaged — see conflicts[4].

absent: Palms — twelve taxa on the campus list, zero in any Zone 1 photograph. Not present, not built.
Jacarandas — present on campus, no evidence inside Zone 1. Not added to make the plaza prettier.
The salmon/copper lawn tree (~x 5-15, z 385-395) — candidate Koelreuteria bipinnata, unconfirmed and possibly not surviving to 2026; a wrong salmon tree mid-lawn is a very visible error.
The coral tree's Erythrina species and its flowers — three candidates on the campus list, the leafed-out photo cannot settle it; built generic and unflowered.
Drinking fountains — one ambiguous ~1.0 m object that is equally likely a bollard. Ladder exhausted.
The memorial's 'marble plaque' — whether it is the inscribed slab itself or a separate element is unresolved in both photographs.
The memorial's chiselled inscription lettering — the curved line of hand-cut capitals is real but below geometry resolution here.
El Mac's mural 'An Enduring Spell' on Argo — still no photograph. Not invented.
The north-west terrace steps — riser/tread never resolved in any frame.
Curbs and ramps — not resolved anywhere in the zone.

The flagpole — built and kept by the campus-landmarks 'Revelle Plaza Fountain' entry, not this section. The inventory's §3i correction (both the 2006 photo and the ~2012 aerial put it in or at the edge of the lawn on a small concrete pad, not out in the open paving, and 18-22 m tall not 15) is DECLARED here but not applied — campus-landmarks is outside this section's scope. Its finial, halyard and cleat remain specification, not measurement.

The wayfinding blade sign (§3f, measured in Argo_Hall.jpg — ~0.35 x 0.9 m panel on a post, top ~2.2 m) — its dims are measured but no source resolves its plan position; better absent than guessed onto the paving.

The two free-standing information-panel types (§3f, measured in Revelle_Plaza_Path__UCSD.jpg — a ~0.5 x 0.7 m board on a slim post, and a larger ~0.9 x 1.3 m directory on legs) — dims measured, plan positions unresolved; left unbuilt.

The yellow-topped Argo-side bulletin kiosk (§3d, Argo_Hall.jpg — ~x -50, z 400) — its position is inferred from the building's framing, not measured in plan, and the revelle section's gold-top kiosk at (48, 340) is the plaza NE one, not this. Left unbuilt rather than placed on an inference.

The Galbraith frontage planting beds — CORRECTED IN R1. The entry read 'z 415-423' and described one band; the survey shows THREE discrete beds, arcgis.ground#1764 (91 m2, x 12.4..22.0, z 412.2..421.9), #1765 (91 m2, x 24.7..34.3, z 412.2..421.8) and #1766 (89 m2, x 37.0..46.6, z 412.1..421.6). The z range is 412.1-421.9, not 415-423. They are real and they belong to the Galbraith/Revelle building passes, not to this ground module; the three ring numbers are handed over here so whoever builds them does not re-survey.

SUPERSEDED IN PLACE by the named-keys entry below: 'Group E-north and Group G trees — per-tree species confidence too low to re-skin; they keep the measured blob rendering.' It named no keys, which under the ultra standard is not a declaration. Kept because the list does not shrink.
Bench type B (wood-topped) near Mayer — part 1's find, not re-verified; left to the revelle section.
Lamppost section round vs square — invisible at plaza distance; built square 0.12 m.

The identity of the seven measured bench objects (A1) — POSITIONS AND FOOTPRINTS ARE MEASURED, identity is not. A 3.9 x 0.88 m dark red-brown bar at 0.125 m/px is equally consistent with a back-to-back timber bench pair, a raised brick planter and a flush planting pit. Ladder climbed: the 2026 ortho resolves the objects but not what they are; UCSD DC bb1741784h shows a dark reddish-brown bench-like element at this lawn's edge but not this row; UCRegents 2008-11-18 p6-p9 were rendered at 200 dpi and opened in R1 and are a VERIFIED NEGATIVE — all four site photographs are of the Revelle College Apartments site on North Torrey Pines Road, not of the plaza; p11 'TRANSPARENCY' was opened too and is six eye-level frames of Revelle BUILDING undercrofts, with no plaza deck at grazing range. Built as the timber type revelle.benchesB already sources. What would settle it: a plaza-level ground photograph looking ALONG one of these rows.

The paving panel and band COLOURS (A2) — the geometry is measured (band 0.42, radius 1.8, module 6.65) and the two-colour model stands on a 2012 close-range read, but that frame is not cached in this repo and could not be re-sampled. The 2026 ortho separates the band geometrically and NOT chromatically, and it is a cross-check that may not become a source. See conflicts[1]. What would settle it: re-acquiring Argo_Hall.jpg, or any close-range colour frame of the panel field.

The north bed's PLANTING (A3) — roughly 20-30 low shrubs, scattered and irregular, individually unresolvable at 0.125 m/px, species unknown; the campus species list carries no zone attribution. The bed's measured outline and a dormant-turf ground ship; the shrubs do not.

The north bed's TRUE SURFACE COLOUR — no photograph of this bed exists at any epoch. colors.northBedTurf is an [estimated] extension of this section's own sourced decomposed-granite tan, chosen because the 2026 ortho cross-check lands 8/2/5 RGB units from it. That is a defensible extension and it is not a measurement.

The north bed's KERB — the ortho resolves a dark raised kerb on all four sides of the bed, roughly 0.4 m wide in plan, which is what makes it read as a contained panel rather than a lawn running out to the paving. Its HEIGHT is not resolvable from above and no ground photograph shows it. The bed floor ships; the kerb does not.

The plaza's lawn-flanking WALKS — the paved strips between the lawn and arcgis.ground#2161 to the east (x 46.9..52.6) and between the lawn and #2160/#2151 to the west (x -6.6..-0.6). They exist: the legacy cell list carried six panels over them and the orthophoto shows paving there. They are NOT built, because they are not on the deck's 6.65 m module — a grid panel centred x 48.444 lies 1.78 m across the surveyed lawn, and one centred x -4.756 lies 1.48 m into bed #2160 — and no instrument resolves what module they ARE on. Same reasoning as the A4 court: better an unpaved strip than a panel laid across a surveyed lawn. What would settle it: a joint read along either walk at better than 0.125 m/px.

The paved court east of the north bed (A4) — x 25.4..41.7, z 329.9..343.4, on a module of roughly 5.4-6.1 m that is NOT the plaza's 6.65 m. Its extent is measurable and its surface material is not; no ground photograph of this specific court was found. It is deliberately excluded from paving.cells rather than covered with plaza panels, because covering it would assert a module the instrument refutes.

The white flat-roofed pavilion at x 43.9..48.9, z 330.8..334.5 (A5) — about 5.0 x 3.7 m, confirmed in plan by two independent ortho reads in R1. It is in neither arcgis.massing nor OSM, and no photograph of it was found. Height, material and function are all unknown. Better absent than a guessed box.

The four unre-skinned trunks at the plaza's north entrance (A8), NAMED: (1, 329) h 20.8 r 5.4; (32.3, 326.5) h 5.4 r 7.5; (50.4, 325.2) h 21.9 r 7.2; (64.5, 329) h 26.7 r 5.6. LiDAR gives every position and height; SPECIES does not resolve. Ladder climbed again in R1: UCSD DC bb91478709 shows young Torrey pines framing this exact approach, which establishes the planting INTENT but cannot be mapped from a 1960s sapling to a 2014 trunk key; and a 40 px/m ortho crop of each trunk shows crowns that are bright mid-green rounded broadleaf masses, not the open olive candelabra the roster's known Torrey pines read as. Intent and appearance disagree, so all four keep the measured blob rendering. This entry REPLACES the earlier 'Group E-north and Group G trees' entry, which named no keys and was therefore a shrug rather than a declaration.

The three crown-clamped plaza trees (A7): (51, 399.1), (1, 380.2) and (80.9, 351.4) all carry r = 7.5, which is the LiDAR clamp and a FLOOR, not a measurement. Their crowns are at least 7.5 m and unbounded above. The ortho cannot close the bound because at all three positions the canopies merge with their neighbours. They are drawn at exactly 7.5 because the module has no way to draw an open bound; treeOverrides.clampNote says so on the record.

The fountain plinth's BATTER ANGLE and the exact plinth HEIGHT (A9) — UCSD DC bb5393567s proves the batter exists and shows adults using the deck as seating, which is what now sources plinthHeight 0.48; but the frame is a wide-angle three-quarter with no in-frame scale at the plinth's depth, so the rake is [estimated] at 0.17 m of inset and the height carries only a +/- 0.06 m seating argument. No drawing was found. The frame's near corner reads 0.6-0.9 m and that reading is recorded and NOT built.

The fountain's exact perimeter NOZZLE COUNT (A10) — the arcs are discrete and are counted in R1 at 7-8 per visible quadrant, so 28 ships. It is not certified: the far half of the ring is hidden behind the central plume and the near arcs cross. research-plaza.md reads the same frame at 20-26. What would settle it: a frame from above, or one with the far rim unobscured.

The five flanking beds' SHRUBS and bed-edge KERBS (arcgis.ground#2151, #2160, #2161, #2697, #2698) — the 2026 ortho shows all five as planted beds with shrubs and dark kerbs, but individual shrubs are unresolvable at 0.125 m/px and no ground photograph of these beds was found. The measured bed floors ship; the planting does not.

Five of the six lawn-edge lamp POSITIONS, and all four DG-belt poles transferred from revelle — only one pad (21.9, 377.1) resolves cleanly enough in the ortho to move a post on, and it was moved. The rest keep their 2006-2012 photo-read positions and are labelled [estimated] rather than silently carried as measured.

Two measured south-row bench objects, at (8.69, 375.12) and (15.38, 375.19) — HELD OUT OF THE DRAW, not absent for want of evidence. Their positions and 3.9 x 0.88 m footprints are measured and are kept in furniture.benches.items with held: 'corridor'; what is missing is a ruling on the shipped scooter route, whose centreline vertex (10.0, 374.9) lies INSIDE the first object's footprint (x 6.74..10.64, z 374.68..375.56) and which clears the two footprints by 0.09 m and 1.58 m against a 3 m rule. See conflicts[7], where it is classified as a survey-versus-survey disagreement between the bench row's ortho-read z and the OSM footway alignment near (10, 375). This is the one entry in this list that a decision rather than a source would close.

The DG belt's SURFACE — the Torrey pine canopy occludes this ground completely from above and the ortho samples canopy (#5c5b4f), not ground. The [estimated] extent tag is honest and the ladder is genuinely exhausted from that direction. Only the belt's south edge is now measured, against Galbraith's ring.

Whether the flagpole is 18-22 m — DECLARED, not resolved, and not built here in any case (it belongs to the campus-landmarks entry). UCSD DC bb1741784h shows it rising white out of the top of frame past the ~25 m eucalyptus, which corroborates the 18-22 m claim. A shadow measurement on the 2026 ortho returns 9.6 m and is WRONG: the shadow loses contrast where it crosses onto the bright paving, so the method under-reads across a tonal boundary. Recorded so nobody repeats it.

THE PLAZA'S EAST BELT (R2 P5/A5, not to be confused with this list's own A5, the white pavilion at absent[25]) — x 52..66 over z 343..428.9, about 1,200 m2 gross and about 840 m2 net of the one thing in it that IS built. Inside this section's declared bounds, built by nobody, and declared nowhere until R2 arbitration item P5/A5 named it. WHAT IS THERE. The surveyed bed arcgis.ground#2161 (106 m2, x 52.6..60.3, z 377.2..391.6) lies in the strip and IS built by this section, with its shrubs and kerbs already declared absent. The rest reads, in the 2026 orthophoto at 8 px/m over x 52..66 and z 344..428, as two things and no third: a warm tan-buff ground running #b5a193 to #d4b69b, which is the decomposed-granite and paving family this section already ships, and dark #39..#5c patches from about x 56 eastward at most z, which is York-belt Torrey pine canopy and its shadow — the same occlusion that stops dgBelt's own surface being sampled (absent[33]). WHY IT IS NOT BUILT. The deck's measured 6.65 m module stops at x 51.77 and no joint resolves east of it, so the strip's surface MODULE is unmeasured; the canopy hides the ground over roughly half of it; and the OSM `walk` polygon that covers it (arcgis.ground#3632) is a campus-wide catch-all, not a read of this strip. Paving it on the deck's module would assert a module the instrument does not show, which is the same error the lawn-flanking walks (absent[23]) are withheld for. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ground-level frame looking north or south along the belt under the pines, or any joint read there at better than 0.125 m/px.

THE WEST WALK (R2 P5/A6) — x -19.9..-16 over the full height of the section, the 3.7 m strip between Argo's ring (x -19.9) and Blake's (x -19.7) and this section's former west edge. Assigned to this section by R2 arbitration item P5/A6 and bounds.x0 moved from -16 to -19.9 to take it, because this section already stands lamp items on that walk. THE SURFACE ITSELF IS NOT BUILT. No frame in this section's ladder looks along it: the 2006 and 2012 plaza photographs face east across the deck, and the 2026 orthophoto shows a narrow strip between two building rings that is mostly building shadow at 0.125 m/px. Its material and its module are both unresolved, and the same rule that withholds the lawn-flanking walks withholds this one. What would settle it: a ground-level frame looking along the walk between Argo and Blake, or the Argo/Blake site drawings if either surfaces.
plaza.boundsNote: The plaza's GROUND envelope, for the critic's framing and for the ownership lines R1 and R2 settled. West x -19.9: EXTENDED 2026-08-21 from x -16 by R2 arbitration item P5/A6. Argo's ring ends at x -19.9 and Blake's at -19.7, so the 3.7 m west walk between them and the old boundary had no owner at all; this section already builds the lamp at (-6, 368) and the retired revelle post at (-10, 365) on that walk, so the section that owns the objects now owns the surface they stand on. The walk's own paving is NOT built — see absent. East x 82: york.westGround.source cedes everything west of x 82 to this section and york's own beds start at x 82.1, so this section owns x 66..82 entire, dgBelt included. THE EAST BELT x 52..66 IS ALSO INSIDE THIS CLAIM AND IS NOT BUILT: it was silent here until R2 item P5/A5 named it, and silence inside your own declared bounds is the one disposition not available. It now carries an absent entry with what the instrument reads there and what would settle it. North z 326: north of that is arcgis.ground#1174's apron and then the science spine, which is R4's. South z 428.9: exactly min z of the Galbraith Hall ring in campus-3d.json, which is also where galbraith.east.dg begins — dgBelt is clipped on that same line so the two decomposed-granite decals abut rather than overlap. NOT EVERY ITEM THIS SECTION CARRIES IS INSIDE IT, and the ones that are not are listed in boundsExceptions; bounds is a statement about the plaza's ground, not a container.
boundsExceptions: furniture.terraces.items indices 5-12 — the Revelle Commons / 64 Degrees terrace at x -92..-72, z 381.5..388. Held for R2 (the Commons cluster); it was read off the same 2026 satellite plan and is left in place rather than dropped, because the record does not shrink.
furniture.lamp.items index 5 — the post at (-82, 384), the Commons terrace's own lamp. Held for R2 with the terrace it lights.

furniture.benches.items — the two singles at (26, 318) and (44, 318), in front of the north-approach lava walls, z 8 m north of bounds.z0. That ground is revelle.lavaWalls#0-29's, held for R4/R6; the benches are held with it.

furniture.bikes — 25 bicycles at x -54..-44.4, z 362.2, on Argo's north frontage. RETIRED 2026-08-21 (count 0), so nothing is now drawn outside bounds here; the record stays listed because the exception list does not shrink either. See conflicts[3] and superseded['furniture.bikes'].

treeOverrides — the eucalyptus roster is east of York (x 98..151) and on the Keeling west road (x -192..-116), and four York-belt pines stand at z 431..467. The roster is a re-skin of measured LiDAR trunks across the whole of Zone 1 and is deliberately NOT bounded by the plaza; treeOverrides.note and the skip-list gate govern it instead.
dgBelt — x 66..82 is inside bounds, and z 333..428.9 is inside bounds after the R1 clip. No exception; listed here only to record that it used to run to z 470 and no longer does.

paving.source: MOVED FROM revelle.paving IN R1 (2026-08-20) AND RE-DERIVED. The field is now measured off docs/data/textures/chunk_4_6.jpg — the repo's own Google orthophoto, zoom 20, 2040 x 2040, 8 px/m, generated 2026-08-04 — by locating the dark joint lines themselves rather than by scaling a panel against a 1.7 m figure in a 2006 oblique. pitch and the grid phase are new (derivations.figures.pavingPitch, .pavingPhase); band 0.42 and radius 1.8 survived re-measurement unchanged and are carried across verbatim. The satellite is a BUILD-TIME PLAN MEASUREMENT here and nothing else: no colour in this section is sampled from it, and it is never draped. The retired 2006/2012 read is kept in revelle.paving and in revelle.supersededDetail.paving.
paving.gridOriginNote: The first resolved joint on each axis, in world metres. Panel centres are gridOrigin + pitch x (k + 0.5); the cells array below is exactly that, filtered to the measured plaza polygon and off the surveyed lawn. A rebuild must reproduce cells from these three numbers alone — tests/campus-photo-plaza.test.mjs regenerates them and deepEquals.
paving.runnerNote: The wide central runner, unchanged in x, width, length and 4 m step — it is a photo read off Revelle_Plaza.jpg (2006) and is not derived from the paving module, so re-deriving the module does not re-derive it. The three segments the legacy list carried at z 331.9, 335.9 and 339.9 ARE retired: they stood inside the surveyed north bed (campus-3d surfaces[90], arcgis.ground#2377), which is planted ground and not deck. Retired, not deleted — the full 12-value list is in revelle.paving.runner.

northBed.source: THE PLAZA'S WHOLE NORTH THIRD, UNBUILT UNTIL R1. Three independent surveys of one rectangle agree to within 1 m on every edge: campus-3d surfaces[90] (kind green, x -13.2..25.4, z 330.0..343.1, 493 m2), arcgis.ground#2377 (k green, x -12.7..26.3, z 330..344, 528 m2) and a 2026 orthophoto read. The outline shipped is the mean of the two SURVEYS (derivations.figures.northBedOutline); the ortho is recorded as the third reading and not averaged in, because its edges are contaminated by the apron bed north of it.
northBed.lampNote: Two lamp posts stand in the bed at its south edge, on square pads the ortho resolves cleanly at 1.38 x 1.38 m. Positions are the mean of two independent reads of the same image (derivations.figures.northBedLamps). They are built with THIS SECTION'S already-sourced lamp standard and are the only two lamp items carrying banner: false, because nothing resolves a banner on them and the plaza poles' banner pair is a separate, separately-sourced claim.
northBed.epochNote: AN EPOCH CONFLICT, DECLARED AND NOT RESOLVED — see conflicts[0]. OSM and the facilities GIS both classify this panel `green`; the newest imagery shows it dormant, unirrigated, patchy olive-tan with scattered low shrubs. Both are describing different years. The measured outline is built and the surface is NOT repainted #61740c to match the south lawns, because that would be inventing irrigation.

beds.source: The five surveyed planting beds inside the plaza window that no section built. Under the ultra standard a treated area is never partially detailed, so they ship as measured ground panels. Every outline is the ring's own bbox, cited by index and never renumbered. The 2026 orthophoto shows all five as real planted beds with shrubs and dark bed-edge kerbs; the SHRUBS and the KERBS are declared absent (they are individually unresolvable at 0.125 m/px and no ground photograph of these beds was found), so what is built is the bed floor.

crossWalk.why: A 6 m wide paved cross-walk at x 1..45, z 398..404, splitting the lawn in two. It does not exist. arcgis.ground#2323 is ONE 1498 m2 polygon with no split, and the 2026 orthophoto resolves the object at that place as a 1.30 m pale lip and dark brick edging band at z 398.36..399.66 with continuous turf either side. The shipped south panel was also 4.4 m out (z 404..414 against a measured 399.66..409.7). Shipped area totalled 1427 m2 against a surveyed 1498 m2, which is why the error survived: the AREA was roughly right.

absent[2].at: the former absent entry 'Fountain basin plan geometry — circular vs straight-sided seat wall unresolved between the 2006 and 2024 photos'
absent[2].why: RESOLVED OUTRIGHT, not merely improved. The three figures that appeared to disagree are three different edges of one nested object: a 7.63 m square plinth, a 5.90-5.97 m circular coping recessed into its deck, and 5.3 m of water inside that. Two instruments sharing no method — a facilities GIS survey (arcgis.ground#3770, 28 m2) and a 2026 satellite raster (27.1 m2) — agree on the coping to 0.03 m of diameter. campus-landmarks' 'a low ring basin about 8 m across' was describing the PLINTH, loosely. The entry is retired into this record and the full derivation is kept; it is not deleted.

furniture.bikes.at: furniture.bikes — 25 bicycles at x -54..-44.4, z 362.2, built from Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) over the run where revelle.racks stood
furniture.bikes.why: DELETED ON EVIDENCE, NOT TRANSFERRED — no section ships bicycles here and none is meant to. The November 2024 Google photosphere of Argo's north entry (research-argo.md section 9.3, Mass Interact) frames the whole boardwalk, planting bed and gravel apron in one shot and shows a clear ground plane: not one bike hoop and not one bicycle. That is a positive observation of an empty surface, not an epoch tiebreak. The seven revelle rack hoops at z 362.5 were retired on exactly this frame in R1; these bicycles stand 0.3 m away at z 362.2, on the same 2012 read, and 7.6 m of their 9.6 m run stands on argo.ground.north.boardwalk (x -52..-40, z 361.2..365.2), which is post-2015 landscape work the photosphere frames directly. Twenty-five bicycles cannot stand without racks; the racks are gone on that photograph and the bicycles are on that photograph's ground. count is 0 and the block stays here with its source, because the record does not shrink.

revelle.benchesA#20-26.retired: revelle.benchesA.items[20..26] — seven benches at z 379.2, x 20..41.6, each flagged sup: 'plaza' in revelle.json and described in revelle.supersededDetail['benchesA.items[sup]'].
revelle.benchesA#20-26.why: RECIPROCAL CLAIM, in the shape blake.superseded['revelle.lavaWalls#30-44'] set — R2 arbitration item S2 makes it the required pattern, because a `sup` flag alone reads as a transfer to any consumer and nothing could detect a successor that had stopped shipping the object. THIS SECTION CLAIMS THESE SEVEN AND SHIPS FOR THEM. revelle's row was a photo read at z 379.2 that overlapped itself in plan (five pairs 1.46 m apart on 2.2-2.7 m benches). The 2026 orthophoto resolves seven objects in TWO rows, at z 344.6 and z 375.2, on the paving module's own 6.65 m pitch, and this section rebuilt both rows from that instrument: furniture.benches.items carries all seven, 3.9 x 0.88 m each. COUNT CHANGE, DECLARED IN counts RATHER THAN ONLY IN PROSE: seven retired, seven carried, counts.benches 5 DRAWN and counts.benchesHeld 2 held out of the draw for the corridor (conflicts[7], absent[32]). The identity of the objects is [estimated] and declared in absent[18].

revelle.lamps#0-3,5.retired: revelle.lamps.items[0..3] — four bannered poles at x 79, z 345/370/395/420 — and revelle.lamps.items[5] at (-10, 365), each flagged sup: 'plaza' in revelle.json and described in revelle.supersededDetail['lamps.items[sup]'].
revelle.lamps#0-3,5.why: RECIPROCAL CLAIM, same pattern and same reason as revelle.benchesA#20-26. THIS SECTION CLAIMS THESE FIVE AND SHIPS FOR THEM. The four at x 79 stand inside plaza.dgBelt (x 66..82): the belt is this section's ground and the poles standing in it come with it, rebuilt at this section's better-sourced lamp type — a 5.75 m pole and 0.51 x 1.37 m banners scaled off the published 54-inch banner rather than read at plaza distance — and they are furniture.lamp.items at (79, 345), (79, 370), (79, 395) and (79, 420). COUNT CHANGE, DECLARED: FIVE retired, FOUR poles added. The fifth, at (-10, 365), is 5.00 m from this section's own post at (-6, 368) on the same west walk — two posts, one object — so it is absorbed rather than rebuilt, and it is one of the reasons bounds.x0 moved west to -19.9 under R2 item P5/A6. Five of the six plaza-side positions and all four belt poles remain [estimated] photo reads; see furniture.lamp.positionNote, derivations.estimates.lampPositions and absent[31].

revelle.paving.retired: revelle.paving — the whole paving system: 76 cells at pitch 6.4 over the measured Revelle Plaza polygon, plus the 12-segment runner at x 20. It is revelle's ONE whole-system retirement (revelle.superseded.paving = ['plaza']) and so carries no per-item sup flags; it is described in revelle.supersededDetail.paving and revelle.retirements['paving@plaza'].
revelle.paving.why: RECIPROCAL CLAIM, in the shape blake.superseded['revelle.lavaWalls#30-44'] set and R2 arbitration item S2 makes required. THIS SECTION CLAIMS THE PAVING FIELD AND SHIPS FOR IT. Without this record the transfer is indistinguishable from a deletion — that is audit-plaza F4, and it matters most here because paving is the retirement carrying the most objects and the only one with no per-item flags to fall back on. WHAT SHIPS: plaza.paving, re-derived rather than copied. The module is 6.65 m, from the 2026 orthophoto's own dark joint lines — least squares over eight resolved x joints gives 6.6685 m (rms 0.075 m over a 46.75 m span) and over three z joints 6.6250 m — against a shipped 6.4 that was low by 0.25 m per bay, i.e. 2.25 m of accumulated error across the field's nine bays. The phase moved too: gridOrigin (-1.431, 350.072) are the intercepts of those same fits, against a legacy list offset ~1.0 m at the west end and drifting to ~1.27 m at the east. band 0.42 and radius 1.8 were re-measured at 64 px/m and CARRIED ACROSS VERBATIM. plaza.arcs.pitch tracks plaza.paving.pitch and the 31 brick-arc crossings are re-derived from the cell list, so the plaza's signature fans on the corrected module. COUNT CHANGE, DECLARED RATHER THAN LEFT IN PROSE: 76 cells retired, 44 carried, and the reduction is three separate corrections, none of them a thinning — (a) the two legacy rows at z 333.1 and 339.5 laid paving straight across the surveyed north bed (campus-3d surfaces[90], arcgis.ground#2377), which is planted ground; (b) six lawn-flanking walk cells lay 1.78 m across the surveyed lawn (arcgis.ground#2323) to the east and 1.48 m into bed arcgis.ground#2160 to the west, because the legacy filter tested a panel's CENTRE and a 6.65 m panel is wider than that — cells are now filtered on FOOTPRINT against every planted polygon this section ships, at one joint band of tolerance; (c) one south-west deck cell at (-4.756, 373.347) fails the same footprint test against #2160. What remains is the measured deck the instrument actually resolves: a 9 x 5 block, which is exactly the nine bays by five rows research-plaza.md section 2.2 counted independently off the outer joints. The runner is carried at 9 of its 12 segments — the three at z 331.9, 335.9 and 339.9 stood inside the same surveyed north bed. The retired walks are declared in absent, not silently dropped; the full 76-cell and 12-segment lists stay in revelle.paving, because the record does not shrink.

plaza.supersededNote: RETIRED FROM THE DRAW, KEPT IN THE RECORD. campus-photo-plaza.js skips exactly these keys at build time and reports counts.superseded. Absent lists and shipped features never shrink by deletion: a claim this section can no longer support moves here with the evidence that retired it, because the successors cite these entries as the thing they improve on. R2 (2026-08-21) added two things here. First, every record now carries an explicit `disposition`: "deleted-on-evidence" for a claim no section carries any more (crossWalk, absent[2], furniture.bikes) and "transferred" for a RECIPROCAL CLAIM — this section naming an object it has taken over from a sibling, in the shape blake.superseded['revelle.lavaWalls#30-44'] set. Arbitration item S2 required it because `sup` alone reads as a transfer whether the object moved or died, and because nothing could otherwise detect a declared successor that had stopped shipping the object. Second, the two reciprocal records claim all twelve revelle items flagged sup: 'plaza' — benchesA[20..26] and lamps[0..3, 5] — and each declares its count change in a number, not only in prose.

colorSources.pineBark: [measured] Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012) — the grey-brown fissured bark of the York-belt Torrey pines, sampled on a sunlit bole.
colorSources.pineFoliageSun: [measured] Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012) — the sunlit face of a Torrey pine crown. Corroborated in colour by UCSD DC bb1741784h (1980s), whose foreground Torrey pine reads the same mid olive-green.
colorSources.pineFoliageShade: [estimated] extends pineFoliageSun into the crown's self-shadow, so a canopy reads as a mass rather than one flat tone. The two-tone split is a rendering device; only the sunlit value is sampled.
colorSources.ficusLeaf: [measured] Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) — the tight dark canopies of the plaza-core ficus.
colorSources.ficusTrunk: [measured] Argo_Hall.jpg (2012) — the pale sinuous multi-stem ficus trunks, which is the feature that identified the species.
colorSources.eucLeaf: [measured] Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012) — the grove edge east of York; grey-green and airier than the pines.
colorSources.eucTrunk: [measured] Revelle_Plaza_looking_south.jpg (~2012) — the pale smooth eucalyptus bole. Corroborated by UCSD DC bb1741784h, where the tall pale-barked eucalyptus behind the fountain read the same.
colorSources.coralBark: [measured] today.ucsd.edu/news_uploads/memorial1.jpg (February 2014) — the smooth pale grey-green bark of the memorial coral tree at planting.
colorSources.coralLeaf: [measured] memorial1.jpg (February 2014) — the coral tree's foliage, leafed out in that frame.
colorSources.coralEarth: [measured] memorial1.jpg (February 2014) — the bare-earth ring the tree was planted in.
colorSources.lawn: [measured] UCSD DC bb1741784h (Robert Glasheen Photograph Collection MSS 154, cached 2026-08-20) — a COLOUR frame looking north-east across this exact lawn with crowds on the grass. Median of 41,048 sunlit turf pixels selected by green dominance. REPLACES #61740c, which had a blue channel of 12 against this frame's 84 and was a saturated chartreuse no turf is; the shipped value had no source at all beyond a note that it was reused from the Keeling agent's read. Cross-checked against the 2026 ortho, which samples this lawn at #5d804a — 18/0/10 RGB units away, where the retired value was 61 units away in blue alone. derivations.instrument: docs/data/textures/chunk_4_6.jpg and chunk_4_7.jpg — the repo's own Google orthophoto, zoom 20, 2040 x 2040 each, 8 px/m (0.125 m/px), generated 2026-08-04, mapped by docs/data/textures/manifest.json. chunk_4_6 covers world x -177..78, z 147..402; chunk_4_7 continues z 402..657. Mosaic them vertically and the transform is px = (x + 177) * 8, py = (z - 147) * 8. THE PLAZA IS GROUND, SO TOP DISPLACEMENT IS ZERO for every figure below — that is why this beats every oblique ground photograph for PLAN, and it is a plan instrument only. Per the two-source rule it is a build-time measurement source: never draped, never a height, never a shipped colour.

figures.pavingPitch: [measured] 6.65 m. Three methods on the deck patch x -7.7..53.2, z 343.7..376.7. (i) AUTOCORRELATION of the detrended mean row/column profile (rolling mean, 65 px window) over lags 24-80 px: the best lag is 53 px on BOTH axes, r = 0.763 in x and r = 0.850 in z, i.e. 53/8 = 6.625 m; the top six lags on both axes cluster 6.375-7.000 m. (ii) DIRECT JOINT FIT. Dark minima in the detrended profiles resolve eight x joints at -1.45, 5.17, 12.05, 18.55, 25.30, 31.80, 38.55, 45.30 and three z joints at 350.07, 356.70, 363.32. Least squares x_k = a + k*p over the eight x joints gives p = 6.6685 m with residuals of -0.019, -0.068, +0.144, -0.025, +0.057, -0.111, -0.030, +0.052 m, rms 0.075 m over a 46.75 m span; over the three z joints p = 6.6250 m with residuals of -0.002, +0.003, -0.002 m. (iii) BAY COUNTING against the joint grid's own extent: x -8.081..51.769 is 59.85 m over 9 bays = 6.650 m, z 343.422..376.672 is 33.25 m over 5 rows = 6.650 m. Shipped at the mean of the two least-squares fits: (6.6685 + 6.6250) / 2 = 6.6468, rounded to 6.65. The shipped 6.4 was low by 0.25 m per bay, i.e. 9 x 0.25 = 2.25 m of accumulated error across the field. research-plaza.md section 3.1 proposed 6.7 on the hypothesis that the module is 22 ft = 6.7056 m; that is 0.037 m from the x fit and 0.081 from the z fit, so it is NOT refuted and it is recorded in conflicts[6], but 6.65 is the figure the joints themselves give and 6.7 was a round number chosen after the fact.
figures.pavingPhase: [measured] gridOrigin x = -1.431, z = 350.072 — the intercepts of the same two least-squares fits, i.e. the first resolved joint on each axis. Panel centres are gridOrigin + 6.65 x (k + 0.5), which puts the first x centre at -1.431 + 3.325 = 1.894 and the first z centre at 350.072 + 3.325 = 353.397. The legacy cells ran x -10, -3.6, 2.8, ... at step 6.4 and z 333.1, 339.5, ... at the same step: a phase offset of about +1.0 m at the field's west end growing to +1.27 m at its east end, on top of the pitch error. The list was therefore regenerated from the grid rather than nudged.
figures.pavingCells: [measured] 44 cells. Every centre on the grid above, kept only where (i) the centre is inside the MEASURED Revelle Plaza polygon (campus-3d surfaces[0]); (ii) z >= gridOrigin.z - pitch = 343.422, which is the deck's own north joint; and (iii) THE CELL'S WHOLE 6.65 m FOOTPRINT, not just its centre, clears every planted polygon this section ships — the lawn, the north bed and the five flanking beds — by more than one joint band (0.42 m). Test (iii) is the one that matters: a panel whose centre is off the lawn can still lie 1.78 m across it. What survives is the measured deck, a 9 x 5 block at x -4.756..48.444, z 346.747..373.347, less the single south-west cell at (-4.756, 373.347) which intrudes 1.48 m into arcgis.ground#2160. 45 - 1 = 44, against 76 hand-placed cells before. The deck's 9 bays x 5 rows is exactly what research-plaza.md section 2.2 counted independently off the outer joints. Test (ii) removes the two legacy rows at z 333.1 and 339.5, which laid paving straight across the surveyed north bed; test (iii) removes the six lawn-flanking walk cells the legacy list carried, which are declared in absent rather than drawn on a module that is the DECK's and demonstrably not theirs. The one intrusion left is 0.13 m of the north deck row into the north bed's shipped z1 — under the 0.42 m band, and far inside the 0.9 m spread between the two surveys that outline is the mean of.
figures.brickArcCrossings: [derived] 31. A crossing exists where a cell has neighbours at (+pitch, 0), (0, +pitch) and (+pitch, +pitch). A full 9 x 5 deck would give 8 x 4 = 32; the missing south-west cell at (-4.756, 373.347) removes the one at (-1.431, 370.022), leaving 31. Each crossing carries four struck panel corners and wedgesPerCorner = 8 fan wedges, so 31 x 4 x 8 = 992 wedges. This count is DERIVED from the cell list and is not free to be typed: the test regenerates the cells from gridOrigin and pitch, then counts the crossings again.
figures.fountainNesting: [measured] THE THREE 'DISAGREEING' FIGURES ARE THREE EDGES OF ONE NESTED OBJECT. (a) PLINTH, square: masking the plinth's blue-grey deck against the warm paving over x 33..44, z 364..375 gives a west edge constant at x = 35.00 down its whole depth (per-row reads 35.00, 35.00, 34.88, 35.00, 35.00, 35.00, 35.00, 35.12), a median east edge at 42.50, a north edge constant at z = 365.75 across x 36..41 and a south edge constant at z = 373.50. So 42.50 - 35.00 = 7.50 m by 373.50 - 365.75 = 7.75 m, mean (7.50 + 7.75)/2 = 7.625 -> shipped 7.63. research-plaza.md read the same plinth at 7.50 x 7.81 (mean 7.66), 0.06 m away in depth. (b) BASIN COPING, circular: arcgis.ground#3770 is a 28 m2 water polygon -> diameter 2 x sqrt(28/pi) = 5.97 m; masking the ortho's bluish basin over the same window gives 27.1 m2 -> 5.87 m. Two instruments sharing NO method, agreeing to 0.10 m of diameter. (c) WATER SURFACE: campus-3d surfaces[34] is 22 m2 -> 2 x sqrt(22/pi) = 5.29 m. Nested: a 7.63 m square plinth, a 5.9-6.0 m coping recessed into its deck leaving a 0.87 m surround, and 5.3 m of water inside the coping. basinRadius 3 is confirmed by (b) to 0.05 m and is UNCHANGED. The shipped plinth of 8.7 was 1.07 m too large.
figures.fountainRotation: [measured] 0 rad, to better than 0.5 degrees. Three tests. (i) THE PLINTH'S OWN WEST EDGE: eight per-row reads over 7.5 m of depth span x 34.88..35.12, a 0.24 m scatter about a vertical, so the edge's bearing is within atan(0.24/7.5) = 1.8 degrees and its best fit is 0. (ii) THE PAVING GRID'S x PHASE, measured independently in three 10 m z bands: the first x joint lands at -1.14, -1.36 and -1.29 across 30 m of z, a 0.22 m spread, bounding any skew at atan(0.22/30) = 0.42 degrees. (iii) THE PAVING GRID'S z PHASE, in three x bands: the first z joint lands at 350.20, 350.11 and 350.11 across 43 m of x, a 0.09 m spread, bounding skew at 0.12 degrees. The plinth is square to the paving and the paving is square to the world. This REFUTES research-plaza.md section 2.4's ~-3 degree skew (-0.052 rad), which was read off a single 470 x 25 px edge, and it demolishes the shipped 0.26 rad. A skew of 3 degrees across the 33 m deep field would smear the x joints by 33 x sin(3 deg) = 1.73 m and could not have produced an autocorrelation peak of r = 0.85.
figures.nozzleCount: [measured, LOW CONFIDENCE] 28. UCSD DC bb5393567s shows the perimeter jets as discrete arcs springing from the basin rim, not as a smooth skirt. Counting separable arc strands descending to the water along the visible near rim gives 7-8 per quadrant on the left crop and 7 on the right, so the full ring is 4 x 7 = 28 at the low end. THE COUNT IS NOT CERTIFIED: the far half of the ring is hidden behind the central plume and the near arcs cross one another. research-plaza.md section 4.3 eyeballs the same frame at 20-26. Shipped at the low end of THIS count because it is the read with the arithmetic recorded; the disagreement is conflicts[7] and the gap stays in absent.
