reads.memorialPosition: The shipped memorial at (32.5, 379.5) is confirmed three ways and its provenance is upgraded from a 2014 press-photo read to a corroborated plan position. (i) The UCSD Emeriti historian places the memorial in the plaza's 'southeast corner'; against the plaza polygon (x -13.2..54.9, z 329.9..401.6) the shipped point normalises to x 0.67, z 0.69 — the south-east quadrant. (ii) 2014 dedication coverage calls it 'adjacent to the Revelle Plaza Fountain'; the distance to the fountain centre (38.6, 369.8) is hypot(6.1, 9.7) = 11.46 m. (iii) THE CORAL TREE ANCHORS IT: the memorial and its coral tree were installed together in February 2014 and photographed together, and the 2026 ortho measures the coral canopy's centre at (32.3, 378.1) and (32.5, 377.8) — 1.61 m and 1.70 m from the shipped memorial centre, exactly the offset a 3.75 m half-disc slab and its tree would have. Tolerance: better than 2 m, from an instrument that shares no method with the press photograph. The SLAB'S OWN GEOMETRY is not corroborated — the 7.4 m canopy completely occludes a 7.5 m half-disc from above.
reads.lawnOuterEdge: The ortho's green blob over x -6..52, z 374..414 spans x -4.12..52.00, z 376.75..414.00 at 1383 m2, against arcgis.ground#2323's x -0.6..46.9, z 377.3..409.7 at 1498 m2. The blob is larger in extent and smaller in area because it also catches the flanking beds' shrubs at x -3.1..-1.7 and 47.9..49.6 and the Galbraith frontage beds to the south, while excluding the 62 m2 edging band. The SURVEY is what ships. Tolerance on the outer edges where the two are comparable: about 1 m.
reads.lawnColour: colors.lawn #6f8054 is the median of 41,048 sunlit turf pixels in UCSD DC bb1741784h selected by green dominance (G - R > 8, G - B > 25, luminance 70..180) over the lawn band of that frame. Cross-check: the 2026 ortho samples the same lawn at #5d804a, a delta of 18/0/10 RGB units. The retired #61740c was 61 units away in the blue channel alone. Tolerance: the photograph is 1980s film with no in-frame grey card, so the value carries the film's own cast; what it certifies is the HUE FAMILY (mid sage green) and that the retired value was not in it.
reads.plinthHeight: plinthHeight 0.48 is KEPT and its provenance is upgraded from unsourced to sourced. UCSD DC bb5393567s photographs three adults SITTING ON THE PLINTH'S TOP DECK with their legs over the outside edge, which makes the deck a seat-height ledge: 0.42-0.50 m for an adult whose feet reach the paving, and the leftmost figure's thigh is visible below the deck line sloping down, so their feet do reach. 0.48 is inside that band. Tolerance: +/- 0.06 m from the seating argument. The frame's near corner reads taller — about 220 px of raked face against a seated figure's 215 px deck-to-head, which would give 0.6-0.9 m — but the corner is at an unknown and nearer depth in a wide-angle three-quarter view and CANNOT be scaled, which is why the seating argument is what ships. The residual is in absent.
reads.treeRoster: All 39 roster entries were re-verified against docs/data/campus-lidar.json in R1 and are UNCHANGED: 39 entries pair 1:1 with 39 skipMeasuredKeys in both directions, every key resolves to a real LiDAR trunk with zero orphans, and every h and r is byte-identical to the survey with zero drift. Tolerance: zero — the gate is an equality against the measured table. This is the best-behaved part of the section and R1 did not refactor it.

estimates.why: [estimated] tier, machine-readable since R2 arbitration item S1(ii). Every entry below carries a numeric `value`, a `band: [lo, hi]` the shipped figure must lie inside, and the sourced pattern it `extends`. Before R2 these were bare prose, which is why argo could ship a figure 0.41 m outside its own published band with 28 gates passing. WHERE A BAND IS THE SHIPPED PRECISION AND NOT A RANGE, the entry says so in as many words: those figures are CARRIES from a named parent, not measurements with an error bar, and the band exists so the number cannot drift silently. Widening any band here to admit a new value is forbidden — if a figure cannot meet its band, the figure is wrong.

nozzleRadius.extends: the MEASURED basin coping — arcgis.ground#3770's 28 m2 water polygon and the 2026 ortho's 27.1 m2 read, which agree on a 5.87-5.97 m diameter, i.e. basinRadius 3.00
nozzleRadius.why: [estimated] the perimeter nozzle RING RADIUS. UCSD DC bb5393567s reads the streams as discrete arcs springing from the basin rim and falling inward; it does not scale the rim they spring from. Banded by two figures the section already holds: the ring must sit INSIDE the measured 3.00 m coping (upper bound) and cannot fall inside the retired skirt's own 2.6 m radius without changing the jet's silhouette (lower bound). 2.75 is 'just inside the coping'.

nozzleRise.extends: the retired cone skirt's own 1.5 m height, carried over so the jet's envelope is unchanged in silhouette while its structure is corrected
nozzleRise.why: [estimated] and it is a CARRY, not a range: the photograph resolves the arcs' existence and not their height. The band is the shipped precision (+/- 0.005 m), stated as a band only because a carried figure must still be unable to move silently. Nothing here measures a jet height.

nozzleReach.extends: the retired cone skirt's 1.5 m height and 2.6 m radius, the two figures whose envelope this jet preserves
nozzleReach.why: [estimated] how far inward each stream throws before it falls. Banded between the two figures the retired skirt carried, which is the whole of what the envelope claim rests on; bb5393567s shows the arcs falling inward toward the plume and gives no scale at the rim's depth.

streamRadius.extends: nothing in this section measures it — it is the scale a garden fountain throws, an invented look figure whose parent is the general type and not a frame
streamRadius.why: [estimated], INVENTED LOOK. Nothing measures it. The band is the shipped precision (+/- 0.0005 m) and exists only so an invented figure cannot drift; it is not an error bar and must never be read as one.

plinthBatter.extends: the plinth's own MEASURED geometry — plinth 7.63 m and plinthHeight 0.48 m — with the rake read qualitatively off UCSD DC bb5393567s
plinthBatter.why: [estimated] horizontal inset per face from deck edge to grade, so plinthBase = 7.63 - 2 x 0.17 = 7.29 m. bb5393567s PROVES the batter exists — both faces at the near corner rake inward toward grade, unmistakably, and the shipped model was a prism — but the frame has no in-frame scale at the plinth's depth, so the ANGLE is not measured. 0.17 m over the 0.48 m height is a 19.5 degree rake, which is the order the photograph reads. This is a CARRY of that single reading and the band is the shipped precision, not an error bar. Replace it the day a drawing or a scaled frame appears; the gap is in absent[28].

northBedTurfColour.extends: colors.dg #a98a68, this section's own [measured] decomposed-granite tan from Revelle_Plaza.jpg (2006) and Argo_Hall.jpg (2012)
northBedTurfColour.why: [estimated] colour, banded on its DISTANCE FROM ITS PARENT rather than on a hex, because that is the only thing an extension can be checked against. The shipped value IS the parent, so the largest per-channel distance is 0. The upper bound is 8 RGB units: the 2026 ortho cross-check over x -10..22, z 332..341 returns #a18c6d, which sits 8/2/5 from #a98a68, and that cross-check is the entire justification for choosing this parent. An extension that drifts further from its parent than the evidence that picked it is no longer an extension. There is no photograph of this bed at any epoch; the true colour is in absent[21].

bedMulchColour.extends: york.westGround's eucalyptus-bark mulch hex #876f5d, read from lpa-york-1.jpg (2024) — a dated photograph of a planted bed on this same frontage
bedMulchColour.why: [estimated] colour, banded on its distance from its parent like northBedTurfColour. This one is carried VERBATIM, so the band is 1 RGB unit — the tightest an ordered band can express — and any drift at all fails it. The 2026 ortho over the five flanking rings samples #455245 to #8a8368, but that is SHRUB CANOPY from above and not the bed floor, so it is not a candidate; the shrubs are declared in absent[30].

lampPositions.extends: the 2006-2012 photo reads of record — Revelle_Plaza__UCSD.JPG (2011), Revelle_Plaza_Path,_UCSD.jpg (2011) and Revelle_Plaza.jpg (2006) — which are what every unmoved post still stands on
lampPositions.why: [estimated] COUNT of lamp items whose POSITION is a photo read rather than a measurement: five of the six original plaza-side items plus the four belt poles transferred in from revelle = 9 of 12. The three that are measured are (21.9, 377.1), from two independent reads of its pad in derivations.figures.lawnLampPad, and the two north-bed pads at (1.4, 342.5) and (21.2, 342.5), from derivations.figures.northBedLamps. Only one lawn-edge pad resolves cleanly enough in the ortho to move a post on, and it was moved. This is an integer; the band is +/- 0.5 because the gate requires an ordered band. benchType.nonNumeric: There is no number to band. This entry estimates an OBJECT'S IDENTITY, not a figure: every number the seven bench objects ship — the 3.9 m length, the 0.88 m depth, all seven positions — is measured off the 2026 orthophoto and gated against it elsewhere. The estimate is only that they are benches of the sourced timber type. It is declared here, held as a conflict in conflicts[2] and as a gap in absent[18], and the test asserts this entry keeps its parent and its [estimated] label rather than pretending a band exists for it.
benchType.extends: revelle.benchesB's timber bench type, sourced from Revelle_Plaza_Path,_UCSD.jpg (2011), plus UCSD DC bb1741784h, which shows a dark reddish-brown bench-like element at this lawn's edge
benchType.why: [estimated] IDENTITY. The seven measured objects are BUILT as timber benches of the type revelle.benchesB already sources: the 0.88 m measured depth is what back-to-back seating gives. The type is EXTENDED from that sourced bench and is not measured here — a 3.9 x 0.88 m dark red-brown bar at 0.125 m/px is equally consistent with a raised brick planter, and the bars' colour matches the brick bands rather than timber. The POSITIONS and FOOTPRINTS are measured and would be right for either object. UCRegents 2008-11-18 p6-p9 and p11, the last unopened rung, were opened in R1 and are a verified negative. See conflicts[2] and absent[18].

draw.rungs: campus-overlay.js's ladder, in painting order. The paving brick field is on `pad`, the rounded buff panel on `carpet`, the central runner and the fan wedges on `paint`, the memorial's engraved lines and lenses on `logo`. The lawn panels and the north bed are on `carpet`; the edging band, the DG belt and the flanking beds are on `pad`. Every one carries the matching OVERLAY renderOrder. Everything SOLID stands on raw surfaceAt, not on a lifted rung, because a bench leg belongs on the ground and not on a decal.
draw.conformingSheets: Every large ground rect — both lawn panels, the edging band, the DG belt, the north bed and the five flanking beds — is a SUBDIVIDED quad whose every vertex is sampled from surfaceAt at about 2 m spacing and stored relative to the centre sample. A single flat quad at one centre sample buries about 1.5 m under the drawn terrain at one end of the DG belt and floats about 2.5 m over it at the other, because the LiDAR ground spans 4.07 m of relief beneath it. The gate builds on a sloped plane and demands every vertex of every named sheet sit its own overlay lift above the drawn ground.
draw.fountainLocal: The fountain is built in a local group placed at (cx, surfaceAt(cx, cz), cz) and rotated by rot about Y, so every part of it rides one ground sample — a fountain is a rigid object and must not be draped. The plinth is a truncated pyramid from plinthBase at grade to plinth at plinthHeight; the deck is inset 0.06 m; the coping wall is recessed basinDepth below the deck; the nozzle streams spring from nozzleRadius at deck level.
draw.treeSeating: Every trunk and stem sits on surfaceAt at its own (x, z), and each carries a root flare that starts BELOW the drawn surface (0.20-0.35 m) so a trunk on a slope never shows daylight under one side. The gate asserts every flare's base is negative on flat ground and no more than 1 m below it.

counts.note: What the module must build if the section is complete. tests/campus-photo-plaza.test.mjs asserts these against the built group, so a builder that silently stops producing a system fails the gate. Terrain-independent counts only.

conflicts: THE NORTH BED: GREEN OR DORMANT? campus-3d surfaces[90] classifies it `green` and arcgis.ground#2377 classifies it `green`; the 2026 orthophoto shows a dry patchy olive-tan turf-and-weed field with scattered low shrubs, sampling at #a18c6d. Both are right about different years — that is the epoch rule, and the resolution is to build the MEASURED OUTLINE and DECLARE the colour disagreement, not to repaint the bed #61740c to match the south lawns. Repainting it would be inventing irrigation.

THE PAVING FIELD'S HUE. Three instruments, three epochs. The 2006/2012 close-range photo reads give a cool grey-buff panel with a mauve joint band (colors.paving #cfcabe, colors.brick #97837a). UCSD DC bb1741784h (1980s, colour) samples the plaza deck at distance at #a7aaaa — near-neutral, agreeing with those reads on HUE. The 2026 orthophoto samples the panel field at #cead9b — a warm pink-buff, disagreeing on hue, and it resolves the joint band geometrically but not chromatically. TWO instruments say near-neutral, one cross-check says warm, and the cross-check is barred from being a source of a shipped hex. Nothing is repainted. UCRegents 2008-11-18 p28-33 was opened for a paver specification and is a verified negative: it is the proposed BUILDING palette for the Revelle College Apartments, names no paver and gives no module.

THE SEVEN MEASURED BENCH OBJECTS: BENCH OR PLANTER? Positions and footprints are measured to the instrument. Identity is not, and the two candidate readings pull opposite ways: the 0.88 m depth is what back-to-back seating gives and UCSD DC bb1741784h shows a bench-like element at this lawn's edge, while the objects' dark red-brown COLOUR matches the brick bands rather than timber. They ship as the already-sourced timber type because that is the reading a dated photograph supports; the planter reading is recorded and is not averaged with it. UCRegents 2008-11-18 p6-p9 and p11, the last unopened rung, were opened in R1 and are a verified negative — see absent.

THE 25 BICYCLES ON ARGO'S NORTH FRONTAGE — RETIRED 2026-08-21 ON THE RACKS' OWN EVIDENCE. furniture.bikes built 25 bicycles at x -54..-44.4, z 362.2 from Argo_Hall.jpg (2012), over the run where revelle.racks used to stand. R1 retired those racks because research-argo.md section 9.3 reports that the November 2024 photosphere of Argo's north entry frames the whole boardwalk, planting bed and gravel apron in one shot and shows NOT ONE bike hoop in it. R1 flagged the bikes against that and did not act. The R2 arbitration ruled, and the chain is short and every link is checkable here: (1) the bikes stand at z 362.2 and the seven retired hoops stood at z 362.5 — 0.3 m, within the width of one hoop, the same ground; (2) both rest on the same 2012 frame and are refuted by the same November 2024 photosphere; (3) argo.ground.north.boardwalk is x -52..-40, z 361.2..365.2, so 7.6 m of the bike run's 9.6 m stands ON that boardwalk — post-2015 landscape work the photosphere frames directly and shows clear; (4) twenty-five bicycles cannot stand without racks, the racks are retired on that photograph, and the bicycles are on that photograph's ground. THE R1 CONDUCT WAS CORRECT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: this section flagged the bikes against itself, wrote 'both go or neither does', and did NOT act, which is exactly right under a brief that forbids a section from retiring a sibling's object. The defect was not the hold; it was that the hold read here as an open question when the answer was already written next to it. See superseded['furniture.bikes'].

THE TERRACE UMBRELLA DIAMETER. Masking the saturated blue canopy core at 8 px/m gives five diameters of 2.21-2.29 m (radius about 1.13); research-plaza.md section 6 reads the same canopies at 3.1 m (radius 1.57) by taking the shaded rim in. The shipped 1.25 sits between the two and inside both error bars, so it is KEPT rather than moved to either. The five POSITIONS, where the two reads agree to 0.20-0.72 m, are updated.

THE FOUNTAIN BASIN'S WATER COLOUR. colors.water #2f4d49 is read off a 2024 photograph of a RUNNING fountain — dark, green, aerated. The 2026 orthophoto samples still, unaerated water at #536e79, a slate blue-green. That is a different STATE of the same water, not a different colour of it, and one satellite frame cannot prove a fountain is off. Recorded as an epoch note; the model still runs its jet and the hex is not repainted.

THE PAVING MODULE: 6.65 m OR 22 FEET? This section ships 6.65 m, the mean of two least-squares joint fits (6.6685 in x over 8 joints, rms 0.075 m; 6.6250 in z over 3 joints). research-plaza.md section 3.1 proposes 6.7 m on the hypothesis that a 1965 American plaza was drawn at 22 ft = 6.7056 m. That hypothesis is 0.037 m from the x fit and 0.081 m from the z fit and is therefore NOT REFUTED — it sits inside the x fit's own rms. It is not shipped because a figure the joints themselves give, with residuals recorded, outranks a round number chosen after the fact; the keeling bar is derivability, and 22 ft has no derivation from this instrument. Recorded so that a drawing, if one ever surfaces, can settle it in one line.

THE MEASURED SOUTH BENCH ROW AND THE SCOOTER CORRIDOR OCCUPY THE SAME GROUND — HELD, NOT DELETED, NOT LOOSENED. RECLASSIFIED 2026-08-21: this is not a furniture problem, it is a SURVEY-VERSUS-SURVEY DISAGREEMENT. Two instruments put two different things on one patch of ground and both of them are measurements, so one of the two is wrong and this batch has no instrument to say which. The two candidates, named so a later pass can re-measure exactly them: (a) THE BENCH ROW'S z — 375.12 and 375.19, read off the 2026 orthophoto at 8 px/m (0.125 m/px) by masking dark red-brown connected components, corroborated by an independent read of the same frame, and landing on the paving module's own 6.65 m pitch; (b) THE OSM FOOTWAY ALIGNMENT NEAR (10, 375), which is what campus-route.js routed the staging centreline over between the raw waypoints (-76.7, 404.1) and (-17.7, 373.6) — everything in between is router-chosen over surveyed footways, not drawn by hand. THE FACTS. The centreline vertex (10.0, 374.9) lies INSIDE the bench centred (8.69, 375.12), whose footprint is x 6.74..10.64 by z 374.68..375.56; footprint-to-centreline clearances are 0.09 m and 1.58 m for the two held objects and 5.96 m for the third, which ships. WHAT WAS REFUSED AND WHY. Moving the ROUTES waypoints is refused: CLAUDE.md is explicit that waypoints are raw points, that a new one snaps to the nearest graph node and hall-adjacent nodes are often dead-end spurs, and that the DRAWN_REFERENCE gate (5 m mean / 12 m worst, plus a doubling-back check) exists because every other gate once passed on a route that was 39 m wrong, twice. Widening the 3 m furniture-clearance gate is refused outright: 'never loosen a gate to make a fix pass', and bench 2's centre clears 3 m while its footprint does not — widening would silently re-admit it. Under 'better absent than wrong' the two objects stay out, fully described, and the hold is bidirectional: declared in counts, here, and in absent[32]. DOCKETED FOR THE GAME'S RETURN: re-check the staging route against the footway alignment near (10, 375). There is nothing to fix today — the game is paused, every tab boots campus-walk.js, no tab rides this corridor and npm run verify:ride is suspended.

THE YORK BELT'S SPECIES, RE-OPENED. treeOverrides.pines calls all twelve York-frontage trunks Torrey pine, overriding the h >= 16 heuristic's eucalyptus label, and UCSD DC bb91478709 (1960s) corroborates that by showing young Torrey pines planted at this approach. But UCRegents 2008-11-18 p11, opened in R1, carries an eye-level 2008 frame captioned York Hall in which the trees standing directly in front of York's west arcade are PALE PEELING MULTI-STEM BROADLEAVES — the eucalyptus/melaleuca habit — not pines. Three of the six frames on that page show the same pale-barked trees against Revelle undercrofts. The roster is NOT changed: it is verified 1:1 against the LiDAR table with zero drift, research-plaza.md section 8.1 records it as the best-behaved part of the section, and a 2008 building-context frame cannot be mapped tree-by-tree onto 2014 trunk keys. Declared for the critic.

york.label: York Hall — four seismically separate structures on the comb footprint: West bar, North wing, South wing, Lecture Hall
york.epoch: 2024 post-retrofit (LPA project record) over 2015-2019 DPR/Sieger geometry; the GRID is measured off the 2008 UC Regents transparency, which is older but is the only frame of the west face on disk and records geometry the 2021-24 preservation retrofit did not change; LiDAR 2014 footprint, ground and height. The 2021-24 retrofit's camouflaged shear walls mean 2024 imagery wins wherever a pre-2021 photo shows an opening; 2008 is NOT a colour source (see colorConflicts).
york.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. Photographs and drawings decide WHAT EXISTS and HOW IT LOOKS; the measured data keeps deciding WHERE and HOW BIG. Every facade layer hangs off the MEASURED York Hall ring in campus-3d.json (endpoints verbatim ring vertices or interpolated points ON a ring edge) and floats at most a metre proud of that face; the measured massing is never moved, carved or replaced. Every one of the 21 hexes now carries a colorSources line with a tier: NONE is `measured` (nothing in this repo re-derives one), nine are `sourced` off a named dated frame that is not on disk, twelve are `estimated` and name what they extend. Every drawn metre is a derivation, a labelled estimate, or a cited read — see derivations, estimates, reads and draw. Nothing measured may ever read from this section.

bounds.note: The drawn ring's plan extent plus a 25 m working pad. Everything this section places — facade layers at their full reach, seated solids and ground decals — lies inside it, and the test checks that rather than trusting it.

measured.note: campus-3d carries h=20 for the survey ring; the DRAWN prism is the facilities ring at the LiDAR massHeights read 15.1 (rim-median base), and the drawn prism wins every dressed datum — see measured.mass. The comb is one uniform-height extrusion: the 'two-storey' West bar read is the plaza-grade slice of the same prism (arcade + 2 storeys reach exactly the drawn parapet from the plaza), and the wings' 4 storeys reach it from the ravine.

mass.source: arcgis.massing 'York Hall' outer ring (decimetres/10, copied verbatim) + campus-lidar.json massHeights['m:115,377'] = 15.1 — the EXACT ring and LiDAR height campus-massing.js extrudes for the drawn York comb. Every dressed datum solves on roofElevation(this ring, this h). The 2026-08-17 audit caught the whole membrane solved on campus-3d's h=20 over the survey ring: copings 6 m over the drawn parapet, the west dressing a metre INSIDE the drawn wall (the plaza frontage showed the massing's generic stripe tile, no tan CMU), the arcade buried below plaza grade.

measured.rimBaseNote: The MEDIAN of the drawn terrain at all 63 vertices of measured.mass.ring, recomputed here — the same statistic scripts/build-campus-lidar.mjs:1686 uses to produce massHeights. The ring's ground spans 20.10 to 24.65 m, a 4.55 m spread, and 36 of the 63 vertices are on the low ravine side; that is why the median lands at 21.222 and why 15.1 is the height of the four-storey east elevation rather than the height of anything on Revelle Plaza.

Same face, its low end — the drawn west wall falls 0.95 m from its south end to its north end

measured.partsNote: The per-face inventory the section lacked. One roof elevation, many heights: the west frontage reads three levels because its ground is 3.4 m above the ravine's, not because the building steps. The two courtyard decks read DEAD FLAT at 23.70 across both courts, which is the confirmation of courtyards.deckNote — a constructed podium, not natural grade — and they sit 0.961 m below the plaza they open off. The south-end faces keep their [estimated] PATTERN and take these MEASURED heights: the label covers what the wall looks like, never how tall it is. EACH PART GROUND IS ASSERTED AGAINST THE TERRAIN READING IT IS (R2 arbitration S1(iii), the prose-relation rule): west-plaza-high is faces.west.max, west-plaza-low is faces.west.min, the two courtyard decks are courtyard1Deck.med and courtyard2Deck.med, east-ravine-north is faces['north-east'].med, east-ravine-south is faces['south-east'].med, north-approach is faces['north-wing'].med, south-end-wing is faces['south-end-wing'].med and south-end-bar is faces['south-end-bar'].med. Stating which statistic each face takes is the difference between a re-sampled reading and a number that merely happens to match one.

derivations.why: THE KEELING BAR, applied to York. Keeling's PV block states a real product dimension and its own arithmetic for every figure it draws; this block does the same. `readings` are the raw citations — counted objects, published feet, pixel counts, stock sizes, LiDAR statistics — and `figures` is every drawn metre with the expression that produces it. tests/campus-photo-york.test.mjs recomputes every one of these independently from `readings` and fails if the section's own value drifts from its own derivation, so a fabricated figure cannot pass by being self-consistent. This section previously shipped 22 presence gates over values with no arithmetic behind them at all; that is the failure this block exists to prevent.

units.note: Inch, foot and pound are exact by definition. 2400 kg/m3 is the standard density of normal-weight structural concrete; it is the only figure here that is a material constant rather than a citation, and it converts STRUCTURE's sourced 500 lb fin into a volume.

imperial.source: STRUCTURE magazine 2024, 'Shipshape: The Seismic Rehabilitation of York Hall': a '300-foot-long column arcade'; exterior CMU. The 8 in / 16 in nominal block module is the American standard unit STRUCTURE's 'concrete masonry unit' names. The 12 ft storey and the 3 ft fin module are the imperial grid those two resolve to — see figures grid.floorToFloor and grid.finModule, each derived twice.

px2008.source: UC Regents, Committee on Grounds and Buildings, 18 Nov 2008, 'UCSD Revelle College Apartments' p11 TRANSPARENCY, top-right photograph — cached in this repo as Revelle-College-Sources/renders/york-sources/UCOP2008-p11_york-west-arcade-COLOUR.png. storeyPitch: the mid-floor precast band's top edge at y=154 to the arcade fascia's top edge at y=404. cmuCoursePeriod: Fourier period of the split-face coursing in the four sunlit panels between fins, agreeing to +/-0.4 px across all four independently. finPitch: mean of the four gaps between fin peaks at x = 426, 518, 610, 700, 791. columnPitch: Fourier period of the bright arcade shafts at y 555-625. ONLY RATIOS BETWEEN TWO HORIZONTAL LENGTHS IN THIS REGION ARE USED FOR THE FIN GRID — the frame is a ground-level shot with an upward keystone, so its vertical and horizontal scales disagree; see conflicts[] entry 'fin module: the 2008 frame's own two scales'.

counted.source: STRUCTURE magazine 2024 (re-read 2026-08-20, cached as Revelle-College-Sources/plans-and-drawings/STRUCTUREmag_2024-07_Shipshape-York-Hall-seismic-rehabilitation.html): 'Thirty-five fluted, cast-in-place concrete columns support the heavy upper structure'; 'Eight-hundred and five vertical, story-tall precast concrete fins ring the upper floors', approximately 500 lb each; four seismically separate structures. LPA Design Studios (cached as LPA_nd_York-Hall-UCSD.html) rounds the fin count to 800 and gives the 10-foot-diameter utility tunnel.

lidar.source: campus-lidar.json massHeights['m:115,377'] = 15.1 is roof minus rimBase, and scripts/build-campus-lidar.mjs:1686 defines rimBase as percentile(rim, 0.5) — the MEDIAN of groundAt() at every vertex of the drawn ring. Recomputed here over all 63 vertices of measured.mass.ring through campus-terrain.js makeHeightSampler, which is the sampler build-campus-lidar uses. LiDAR 2014.

ring.source: The length of the drawn west facade a(83.8, 429.9) -> b(82.8, 338.8), both verbatim vertices of measured.mass.ring (campus-arcgis.json massing 'York Hall' outer ring at /10). This is a MEASURED length off the survey, not a photogrammetric scale, and it is the one metre datum the arcade grid is built on.

product.source: Stock sizes, the Keeling `panel [1.65, 0.99]` class: a single 3'-0" x 7'-0" hollow-metal door leaf is the standard exterior corridor door DPR 523 describes; a loop ('inverted U') bike rack hoop is 30 in wide on 36 in centres; 17 in is the standard finished seat height of a built-in bench.

terrain.source: Sampled here from docs/data/campus-lidar.json `terrain` through docs/js/campus-terrain.js makeSurfaceSampler — the height of the DRAWN triangle, which is what anything seated on the ground actually meets (CLAUDE.md: heightAt is not the surface you can see). Faces are sampled at 41 stations along the facade chord itself; the two courtyard decks over a 17x17 grid of their plan rectangle. LiDAR 2014, the oldest epoch and the only one that measures this ground.
terrain.westPlazaNote: The west frontage sampled 2.75 m OUT ON THE PLAZA rather than at the wall chord. Both are recorded because they differ: the plaza rises away from York's wall, so the ground at the wall (faces.west) is 0.5-0.9 m lower than the ground a person stands on. The arcade floor is a constructed slab at the wall; the frontage a photograph measures is the one out front, and closure.plazaFrontage is checked against THIS band.

grid.cmuCourse.why: 8 in nominal block course, exactly. The shipped 0.203 was this rounded to three places; it is retired in superseded[].

grid.cmuCoursesPerStorey.why: 250 / 13.9 = 17.99. A COUNT of block courses in a photograph: it needs no scale, no camera model and no assumption about the fin module. The bracketing values are not close — 17 courses is 11.33 ft and 19 is 12.67 ft.
grid.cmuCoursesPerStorey.derivation: A COUNT of block courses in a photograph: 250 px per storey over a 13.9 px Fourier course period is 17.99. It needs no scale, no camera model and no assumption about the fin module. The bracketing values are not close — 17 courses is 11.33 ft and 19 is 12.67 ft.

grid.floorToFloor.why: 18 courses x 8 in = 144 in = 12 ft 0 in exactly, and it equals imperial.storeyFeet * foot by a second, independent route. It then CLOSES the building against LiDAR on three faces — see figures grid.parapet and measured.parts. The shipped 3.775 was 15.1/4 back-solved from the prism and is 3.2% high; the inventory's 5.0 is refuted by 3.3 m on a frontage the 2008 frame photographs. Both stay on the record in conflicts[].

grid.parapet.why: THE CLOSURE. 15.1 - 4 x 3.6576 = 0.4696 m of parapet and coping above the fourth floor's roof deck. The residual is a plausible coping and not a fudge: solve the plaza frontage with it and 3f + c = 11.44 m lands inside the 11.10-11.72 m the terrain measures under the west wall, on a face that took no part in producing it. The shipped coping.height 0.35 was a free number; this one is what the drawn prism has left over.

grid.finModule.why: [conflicted, asserted] 3 ft. THE MODULE IS NOT RESOLVED — see conflicts[0], which records that the 2008 frame's own horizontal and vertical scales give 0.911 m and 1.320 m, and that an attempt to break the tie on the CMU coursing FAILED. 0.9144 is ASSERTED, not derived: the arithmetic below is only the conversion of an imperial module this section CHOSE. The three lines that argue for it: (1) COUNT — 805 sourced fins over 871.6 storey-metres of fin-clad facade needs a module of 1.083 m or under, and 1.336 m would still leave the building 19% short; (2) RATIO — the 2008 frame's horizontal fin:column pitch of 268/91.3 = 2.94 fins per bay puts the module at 0.9114 m; (3) GRID — floorToFloor / 4 = 0.9144 exactly. None of the three is a measurement of a metre, and everything the R2 arbitration rules on for this facade is a RATIO to the fin pitch and survives a re-solve. finSystem.widthOfModule and finSystem.windowWidthOfModule exist so that it does.

grid.arcadeBay.why: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-21 AND RE-DECIDED AGAINST THE 35-COLUMN TEXT (visual round 2, MAJOR 4). The bay is now read off the SAME frame and the SAME single scale as everything else on this facade: 268 px of arcade column pitch against 250 px of floor-to-floor is 1.072 storeys, and at the 3.6576 m storey that is 3.9209 m. THE READINGS ARE UNCHANGED AND WERE INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED: a three-band comb fit over UCOP2008-p11_york-west-arcade-COLOUR.png (the column shafts at y 500-600, the spandrels at y 452-500 and the fascia soffit at y 430-470) gives periods of 280.5, 271.0 and 272.8 px, and the pinned 268 sits at the low end of that band. THE RETIRED VALUE WAS 2.6796 m = 91.1055 / 34, i.e. the drawn west edge divided by STRUCTURE's 35 columns, and NOTHING IN THE FRAME SUPPORTS IT: 2.6796 m is 183 px of column pitch in this photograph against a measured 268-280 px, a 46% miss, and the same argument conflicts[0] already accepted for the fin module applies here unchanged — an obliquely photographed facade is compressed horizontally, never stretched, so no viewing geometry turns 268 px into 183 px. The 35 columns and the sourced 300-foot run are NOT deleted: they stay in arcade.columnsSourced, in counted.arcadeColumns, in absent[] and in the new conflicts entry, which records that the count and the photographed rhythm cannot both be true of this wall.

grid.finsPerBay.why: RE-DERIVED 2026-08-21 FROM THE FRAME ALONE, so that it no longer inherits the module dispute. 268 / 91.3 = 2.9353 fins per bay, which rounds to 3; the previous expr was round(arcadeBay / finModule) and therefore moved whenever either disputed figure moved. The pure pixel ratio is the only form of this number the 2008 frame actually measures. IT NOW EXPOSES conflicts[0] AS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN AS PROSE: the shipped module is 0.9144 m, so arcadeBay / finModule = 3.9209 / 0.9144 = 4.29, not 3. The arcade and the fin field are drawn on grids this section's own data cannot reconcile, and that is the module conflict, unresolved and now visible in a division anyone can do.

finSystem.height.why: The VISIBLE fin: one storey less the precast band it lands on at the head. The precast ELEMENT is story-tall [STRUCTURE], so the mass below is spread over the full storey, not over this.

finSystem.volume.why: 500 lb = 226.796 kg at 2400 kg/m3 = 0.094498 m3 of concrete in one story-tall fin.

finSystem.meanProud.derivation: The mean projection of the spindle elevation this section draws. The seven-point profile is (0,0), (haunch,0), (min,haunchHeight), (mid,H/2), (min,H-haunchHeight), (haunch,H), (0,H); the shoelace area over it equals the trapezoid sum written in `expr`, which is the same number in closed form so the derivation can be EVALUATED rather than read. 0.1274 m — the '~0.12 m average' the inventory asserted, now computed from the profile rather than asserted beside it.
finSystem.meanProud.why: [estimated inputs, derived shape] Every input is an [estimated] spindle dimension, so this figure inherits that tier; only the arithmetic is derived.

finSystem.width.why: [conflicted] THE FRAME SETS THE WIDTH, AS A FRACTION OF THE MODULE. R2 arbitration Y1 measures the fin at 0.0761 of the fin pitch on UCOP2008-p11_york-finfield-3x.png; at the asserted 0.9144 m module that is 0.0696 m. THE COMPETING READING IS RETAINED AND NOT DELETED: STRUCTURE's sourced ~500 lb per story-tall fin at 2400 kg/m3 gives a fin VOLUME of 0.094498 m3 and hence a cross-sectional AREA of 0.025836 m2 over a 3.6576 m storey; divided by the drawn profile's 0.127389 m mean projection that is 0.202813 m, which is what this section shipped. The mass constrains AREA, not WIDTH, and the projection it is divided by is itself a stack of [estimated] spindle dimensions — so the two sources do not actually contradict each other, and both survive if the residual goes into DEPTH rather than width. This section does NOT resolve that and must stop presenting 0.2028 m as derived from a published mass. See conflicts[2].

finSystem.windowWidth.why: The slot measured on the section's own frame, as a fraction of the module: 0.0805 x 0.9144 = 0.0736 m. THE RETIRED VALUE WAS 0.425 m, the midpoint of DPR 523's PROSE band of 0.35-0.5 m, whose expr referenced `reads.finSystem.windowBand` — a reading that exists nowhere in this document. That dangling reference is the reason S1(vi) evaluates every expr. DPR's band is 0.38-0.55 OF A MODULE and is now a declared conflict, not a governing figure.

arcade.capital.why: 'fan capitals that nearly meet' [inventory, 'cloister-like domes'] and 'each pair of adjacent capitals flares until they meet' [2008 frame]: the capital radius is half the bay less a joint. It follows the bay, and the bay moved on 2026-08-21. SINCE THE SAME DATE THIS FIGURE IS NO LONGER THE LATHE'S FLARE RADIUS. A lathe flare is a solid of revolution, so a 1.90 m capital bulged 1.90 m into the plaza as well as along the wall, which is not what a fan vault does; the fan is now cut as the spandrel of the arcade screen and the arch it leaves is arcade.archRadius. The figure stays because it is still the true statement of where two adjacent capitals meet.

eastSide.doors.height.why: A 7'-0" leaf. The shipped 2.2 m was a round number.

DPR 523 sources 'numerous single metal doors' but no spacing; the grid supplies the only spacing this building can have. The shipped 2 was on the 1.829 m module and meant a door every 3.658 m — the SAME real spacing, which is why this figure moves while the facade does not.

Same number, honest derivation.

courtyards.deckElevation.why: The podium deck reads DEAD FLAT at 23.70 m across both courts, which is what confirms courtyards.deckNote: this is the roof of the below-grade storey, not natural grade.
courtyards.deckElevation.derivation: The MEDIAN of the drawn terrain over a 17x17 grid of courtyard 1's plan rectangle, carried in derivations.readings.terrain.courtyard1Deck and re-sampled by the test. The podium deck reads DEAD FLAT at 23.70 m across both courts, which is what confirms courtyards.deckNote: this is the roof of the below-grade storey, not natural grade.

courtyards.stepBelowPlaza.derivation: The same drop as measured.courtyardStep, restated over the readings rather than pointing at the other figure, so the two cannot drift apart. Carried in the courtyards block so anything walking from the plaza into the court can find it. Nothing here builds the steps that must cross it — see absent[], which now owes it to R6.

closure.eastElevation.why: 4f + c against LiDAR's 15.1. EXACT BY CONSTRUCTION of grid.parapet, so this is bookkeeping and not evidence; it is recorded so that a later change to f or c cannot quietly stop closing.

closure.plazaFrontage.why: 3f + c = 11.4424 m for the arcade plus two fin storeys, against a west frontage the terrain measures at 11.11-11.97 m out on the plaza (readings.terrain.westPlaza, sampled 2.75 m west of the wall along the face's own outward normal) and 11.48-12.43 m at the wall chord itself. CORROBORATION, not proof: it lands inside the plaza band on a face that took no part in deriving f or c, but that band is wide enough that the retired 3.775 also fits inside it once its own residual parapet is taken as zero. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE COURSE COUNT — see closure.courseCount. What this band DOES decide outright is the inventory's 5.0 m, which needs 15.0 m of frontage where the terrain gives at most 11.72.

closure.podiumStorey.why: Plaza grade less one storey should be the top of the buried podium storey, and rimBase should be near it. 24.65 - 3.6576 = 20.99 against a rimBase of 21.222 — 0.23 m apart on a third face that was not fitted either.
closure.podiumStorey.derivation: Plaza grade (the west chord's median drawn ground) less one storey should be the top of the buried podium storey, and rimBase should be near it. 24.661 - 3.6576 = 21.0034 against a rimBase of 21.222 — 0.22 m apart on a third face that was not fitted either.

closure.courseCount.why: THE DISCRIMINATOR. A CMU wall is built in whole 8 in courses, so a storey height must be a whole number of them, and this must come out an exact integer — it is 18. The retired 3.775 m gives 18.58 courses, which is not a wall anybody can lay, and the inventory's 5.0 m gives 24.61. That, not the frontage band, is what decides between them, and it is a COUNT in a photograph rather than a measurement: it needs no scale, no camera model and no assumption about the fin module.

arcade.archRadius.why: NEW 2026-08-21. THE ARCH IS SEMICIRCULAR AND THIS IS ITS RADIUS: the clear half-span between the faces of two adjacent shafts. Both prior readings of the 2008 frame agree the head is ROUND — the research dossier calls the arcade 'a run of round-headed arches ... the void between two capitals is a near-semicircular arch', and the visual critic independently read 'a round head springing off broad piers'. What shipped was a POINTED lancet, and it was pointed by accident of implementation, not by any source: two power-law lathe flares meeting produce a cusp. The head now springs at capTop - archRadius and its crown reaches capTop, which is what the frame shows — the crown sits just under the fascia soffit, 8 px below it at 68 px/m.

arcade.depth.why: THE ARCADE IS ONE BAY DEEP TO A CONTINUOUS CMU BACK WALL [UCOP2008 p11, the northern bays; see conflicts on the two-row reading]. DECLARED, AND LARGELY NOT DRAWABLE: campus-massing.js extrudes the drawn ring as a SOLID prism and this membrane is a skin on it, so nothing set behind the ring chord can be seen at all. The recess this section can actually draw is draw.columnStandoff less draw.backStandoff = 0.70 m, capped by this section's own rule that no facade layer may reach more than 1.0 m off its measured face. The shortfall is recorded in absent[] as owed to whoever may suppress the massing prism under a photo-detailed building; it is not closed by pretending.

estimates.why: The ultra standard's third tier. Each entry is a figure no rung of the ladder resolved — photographs, Street View, drone/video, planning documents, archives — labelled [estimated], recording the sourced pattern of THIS building that it extends, and replaced the day a real source turns up. EVERY ENTRY ALSO CARRIES A MACHINE-READABLE `band: [lo, hi]` AND A `bandWhy` (R2 arbitration S1(ii)): prose alone cannot be checked, and R1 shipped an estimate elsewhere in this batch that could reach 0.41 m outside its section's own published band with 28 gates passing. The shipped value is asserted inside its band by tests/campus-photo-york.test.mjs. A band is what the evidence allows, never what the shipped number needs — narrowing a band to a shipped value would be the same defect wearing the fix's clothes.

finSystem.proudHaunch.extends: the inventory's spindle read off lpa-york-1.jpg and the lpa-catalyst column sidebar: fuller at the ends where the fin lands on the band
finSystem.proudHaunch.why: [estimated] the SHAPE of the fin. Its one sourced dimension is the width, which figures['finSystem.width'] derives from STRUCTURE's 500 lb; the profile that width multiplies is this estimate and stays exactly as the inventory drew it.
finSystem.proudHaunch.bandWhy: Bounded below by the projection at which the spindle stops reading as a fin at all against a 0.0696 m width, and above by the section's own 'do not model a 0.5 m blade' rule and the arcade shaft it must not out-project.

finSystem.proudMid.extends: the same inventory spindle read off lpa-york-1.jpg
finSystem.proudMid.why: [estimated] the mid-storey projection of the spindle.
finSystem.proudMid.bandWhy: Must be less than the haunch it narrows from and more than the waist it flares out of; the upper bound is the shipped gate.

finSystem.proudMin.extends: the same inventory spindle read off lpa-york-1.jpg
finSystem.proudMin.why: [estimated] the waist projection where the haunch meets the shaft.
finSystem.proudMin.bandWhy: The waist. Bounded above by proudMid, which it must be less than, and below by the projection at which the spindle would be a flat panel.

finSystem.haunchHeight.extends: the same inventory spindle read off lpa-york-1.jpg
finSystem.haunchHeight.why: [estimated] how far the trapezoidal haunch runs before the shaft begins.
finSystem.haunchHeight.bandWhy: Must run less than half the 3.1076 m fin so the two haunches do not meet; the lower bound is the depth below which the trapezoid is a chamfer rather than a haunch.

finSystem.windowSill.extends: the inventory's read that the slot is a punched opening in a CMU field rather than a floor-to-ceiling light
finSystem.windowSill.why: [estimated] how far the slot's sill stands above the floor. No frame stations the opening inside its storey.
finSystem.windowSill.bandWhy: A punched opening in a CMU field, so the sill stands clear of the floor and the head clears the 0.55 m band above; the upper bound leaves a slot at least a metre tall.

arcade.shaftBase.extends: STRUCTURE's and LPA's shared word for these columns, 'thin'
arcade.shaftBase.why: [estimated] the shaft's base radius. 0.48 m across the flats for a hexagonal cast-in-place column carrying four storeys is at the slender end, which is the whole point of the arcade; no source dimensions it.
arcade.shaftBase.bandWhy: 'Thin' [STRUCTURE, LPA]. 0.48 m across the flats is the slender end for a hexagonal column carrying four storeys; the upper bound is where 'thin' stops being true.

arcade.shaftWaist.extends: STRUCTURE: 'narrow slightly from base to mid-height before dramatically flaring outward'
arcade.shaftWaist.why: [estimated] the waist radius. 'Slightly' is taken as 0.79 of the base; the flare above it is the sourced part and is derived in figures['arcade.capital'].
arcade.shaftWaist.bandWhy: 'Narrow SLIGHTLY from base to mid-height' [STRUCTURE]: bounded above by the base it must be under and below by a narrowing that would no longer be slight.

arcade.capitalGap.extends: 'fan capitals that nearly meet' [inventory]; '2008 frame: each pair of adjacent capitals flares until they meet'
arcade.capitalGap.why: [estimated] the joint left between two capitals so they nearly, not exactly, meet.
arcade.capitalGap.bandWhy: 'Fan capitals that NEARLY meet': bounded below by a joint too tight to see and above by a gap that would read as separate capitals rather than a run of arches.

arcade.fascia.height.extends: the 2008 frame, which shows the York Hall lettering set within the fascia band and clear of both its edges
arcade.fascia.height.why: [estimated] the depth of the arcade fascia. absent[3] records the caps as ~0.36 m, so a 0.95 m band holds them with a margin above and below; the fascia itself is not dimensioned anywhere.
arcade.fascia.height.bandWhy: The 2008 frame shows the lettering set WITHIN the band and clear of both edges; absent[3] reads the caps at ~0.36 m, so the band must hold them with a margin above and below and must not swallow the arcade zone.

courtyards.planterRadius.extends: DPR 523 Image 9's hexagonal white concrete planters ringed by built-in benches
courtyards.planterRadius.why: [estimated] the planter's circumradius. The objects and the hexagon are sourced; their size is not.
courtyards.planterRadius.bandWhy: A hexagonal planter a built-in bench ring wraps, in DPR 523 Image 9, read against the people and doors in the same frame.

courtyards.planterHeight.extends: the same frame, which shows the planter rim standing above the bench backs
courtyards.planterHeight.why: [estimated] the planter rim height, a little over the 0.4318 m derived seat.
courtyards.planterHeight.bandWhy: Bounded below by the 0.4318 m derived seat it stands above, and above by the height at which the rim would hide the agave the frame shows over it.

courtyards.benchWidth.bandWhy: A built-in bench seat depth: bounded by what is sittable at one end and by what would read as a plinth at the other.

courtyards.benchGap.extends: the same frame: the bench ring stands clear of the planter it wraps
courtyards.benchGap.why: [estimated] the gap between planter face and bench back.
courtyards.benchGap.bandWhy: The bench ring stands CLEAR of the planter it wraps: bounded below by a gap that would read as touching and above by one the frame would resolve.

courtyards.lecture.ventSize.0.extends: DPR 523 Image 5's two louvered vents on the Lecture Hall's east flank
courtyards.lecture.ventSize.0.why: [estimated] vent width; the objects are sourced, the size is not.
courtyards.lecture.ventSize.0.bandWhy: A louvered wall vent on a lecture-hall flank in DPR 523 Image 5, scaled against the paired 0.9144 m door leaves in the same frame.

courtyards.lecture.ventSize.1.extends: DPR 523 Image 5, the same pair of louvered vents
courtyards.lecture.ventSize.1.bandWhy: The same vent's height, same scale reference, and it must stay under its own 2.4 m centre height plus half itself.

courtyards.lecture.ventSize.2.extends: DPR 523 Image 5, the same pair of louvered vents
courtyards.lecture.ventSize.2.why: [estimated] how far the louvre frame stands proud.
courtyards.lecture.ventSize.2.bandWhy: How far a louvre frame stands proud of a wall: bounded above by the 0.12 m ventProud render offset plus a blade depth.

courtyards.lecture.ventHeight.extends: DPR 523 Image 5, which shows the vents sitting above head height on the flank
courtyards.lecture.ventHeight.why: [estimated] the vents' centre height above their own ground.
courtyards.lecture.ventHeight.bandWhy: 'Above head height on the flank' [DPR 523 Image 5]: bounded below by head height and above by the one-storey lecture box's own wall.

roof.louvreWell.bladeLength.extends: ARK bb8089859p's blades, whose length reads long against their pitch
roof.louvreWell.bladeLength.why: [estimated] blade length in plan. The photograph gives the height and the packing, not the chord.
roof.louvreWell.bladeLength.bandWhy: The blades read LONG against their pitch in ARK bb8089859p; the chord itself is not measurable in the frame, so the band spans what would still read long at a 0.49 m pitch.

roof.louvreWell.closePackFraction.extends: ARK bb8089859p: 'closely packed — pitch small relative to blade length'
roof.louvreWell.closePackFraction.why: [estimated] the pitch as a fraction of the blade, so the figure moves with the blade instead of standing free.
roof.louvreWell.closePackFraction.bandWhy: 'Closely packed — pitch small relative to blade length' [ARK bb8089859p]: bounded above by the fraction at which the packing stops being close, and below by blades that would occlude each other completely.

roof.louvreWell.bladeThickness.extends: the same row of blades, which read as thin sheet in the frame
roof.louvreWell.bladeThickness.bandWhy: They read as thin sheet in the frame: bounded below by what would vanish at this scale and above by what would read as a fin rather than a blade.

roof.louvreWell.bladeTiltDeg.extends: ARK bb8089859p: the blades are TILTED, not upright, and all lean the same way
roof.louvreWell.bladeTiltDeg.why: [estimated] the tilt angle. The lean is sourced and is the visible difference from the shipped upright blades; its magnitude is not measurable in the frame.
roof.louvreWell.bladeTiltDeg.bandWhy: The lean is sourced and its magnitude is not; bounded below by a tilt the frame would not resolve as tilted and above by blades that would lie down on the roof.

eastSide.ramp.width.extends: DPR 523 Image 5's long concrete ramp with a solid parapet descending to the parking
eastSide.ramp.width.bandWhy: A long concrete ramp with a solid parapet descending to parking [DPR 523 Image 5]: bounded below by a single accessible route and above by the drive it is not.

eastSide.ramp.parapet.bandWhy: A solid parapet on a ramp: bounded by guard height at the bottom and by a wall that would hide the ramp at the top.

eastSide.ramp.parapetThickness.extends: DPR 523 Image 5's long concrete ramp and the solid parapet running its length — the same object eastSide.ramp.parapet reads its height off
eastSide.ramp.parapetThickness.bandWhy: A poured parapet's thickness, bounded by what stands up and by what would read as a wall.

westGround.mulch.widthMax.extends: lpa-york-1.jpg's bark-mulch beds at the base of the frontage
westGround.mulch.widthMax.why: [estimated] the widest the bed is allowed to get. The bed's EAST edge now follows the drawn wall chord and its west edge is the sourced dgBelt abutment, so the width is a consequence, not a figure — this caps it where the wedge would otherwise open past what the frame shows.
westGround.mulch.widthMax.bandWhy: A cap, not a figure: the bed's east edge follows the drawn wall chord and its west edge is the sourced dgBelt abutment, so the width is a consequence. The band is what lpa-york-1.jpg's beds could be at their widest before the wedge opens past what the frame shows.

reads.why: Figures taken straight off a named frame, drawing or catalogue, with the tolerance that frame supports. These are citations, not derivations: the test pins them as literals because changing one is changing what the source is claimed to say.

grid.storeys.source: campus-arcgis.json massing 'York Hall' levels = 4, the count campus-massing.js extrudes. The fourth is the PODIUM storey: buried under the plaza and the courtyard decks, emerging only toward the ravine, which is why the west frontage reads three.

arcade.columnsSourced.source: STRUCTURE 2024: 'Thirty-five fluted, cast-in-place concrete columns support the heavy upper structure'. Cross-checked against the same article's 300-foot arcade and the drawn 91.1055 m west edge (298.9 ft) — 0.35% apart, so the count and the wall are the same object.

arcade.sides.source: STRUCTURE 2024: 'hexagonal columns that narrow slightly from base to mid-height before dramatically flaring outward'. LPA Design Studios: 'thin, hexagonal fan-vaulted columns', and the retrofit 'replaced four critical hexagonal fan-vaulted columns'. The renderer has always built six lathe segments; until now nothing in the data said why, so a true fact was shipping unsourced.

finSystem.band.height.source: The inventory's measured read of the smooth white precast mid-floor bands, ~0.55 m, off lpa-york-1.jpg (2024). The band is the element the 2008 frame's storeyPitch is measured to, so its presence and position are independently confirmed; only its depth rests on the missing file.

roof.louvreWell.bladeHeight.source: UCSD Library Digital Collections ARK bb8089859p (colour transparency, mid-to-late 1960s, cached as Revelle-College-Sources/renders/york-sources/ucsddc-bb8089859p_york-roof-looking-SE.jpg): a long single row of tall angled white blades whose height is comparable to the adjacent penthouse, i.e. of the order of 2-2.5 m. The shipped 1.3 m was declared unsourced and is now refuted by a photograph.

roof.penthouse.size.1.source: ARK bb8089859p: a small GLAZED stair bulkhead / penthouse with a light metal frame, glazing on its flanks and a shallow sloped top, roughly 4-5 m x 3 m in plan and ~2.5 m tall. The shipped block was 8 x 2.6 x 5 and 'louvered'; the photograph says glazed, and smaller.

roof.penthouse.size.0.source: ARK bb8089859p, the long dimension of the glazed bulkhead — 'roughly 4-5 m', taken at the midpoint.

roof.penthouse.size.2.source: ARK bb8089859p, the short dimension of the glazed bulkhead — 'roughly 3 m'.

roof.louvreWell.rowCount.source: ARK bb8089859p shows a SINGLE row of blades running the full visible length of the roof. The shipped two parallel rows came from 'STRUCTURE Fig. 6 / LPA BIM axonometric', neither of which is on disk; the photograph is the only image of this roof anyone can currently open.

structures.tower.cap.source: DPR 523 Image 4 (ARG 2015): a blank windowless service/stair tower at the north wing's east corner rising SLIGHTLY above the parapet; 1.8 m is the inventory's read of 'slightly', which is under half of this building's 3.6576 m storey. Corroborated in a second epoch: ARK bb8089859p shows the same blank grey service block over the fin screen on the far wing.

finSystem.widthOfModule.source: R2 arbitration Y1, measured on Revelle-College-Sources/renders/york-sources/UCOP2008-p11_york-finfield-3x.png: proper FWHM per fin against a local CMU floor sampled 60-95 px either side, seven fins reading 7.67/6.33/5.67/6.33/7.33/7.00/8.00 source-px, mean 6.9 px, against a fin pitch of 90.7 source-px (px2008.finPitch 91.3 reproduces to 0.7%). 6.9/90.7 = 0.0761. Photographic bloom WIDENS a bright thin object, so this is an UPPER bound. Band 0.062-0.088 of module.

finSystem.windowWidthOfModule.source: R2 arbitration Y1, same frame: width at half-depth between the CMU level and the slot minimum, 6.33/5.67/8.00/9.33/2.33/1.67/8.00 source-px. The two shallow readings are the two SKY-LIT slots, whose half-depth is measured against a much shallower trough; excluding them the mean is 7.3 px = 0.0805 of the 90.7 px module. Photographic bloom NARROWS a dark thin feature, so this is a LOWER bound. Band 0.065-0.103 of module. DPR 523's prose band of 0.35-0.5 m is 0.38-0.55 OF A MODULE and is a declared conflict, not a governing figure — see conflicts[2].

finSystem.windowsPerFin.source: R2 arbitration Y1, same frame: an adaptive scan around each of the seven fins, in the lower CMU band (y 620-960) and again in the upper storey (y 60-400), excluding the fin itself, finds a dark slot beside EVERY fin in BOTH storeys — fourteen of fourteen. 'One slot per arcade bay' predicts a slot at every third fin and is refuted by the section's own frame. Two independent proofs the slots are GLAZING: the two sky-lit slots read b-r = +17.4 and +15.5 against CMU controls at -15.6 to -18.7 (a shadow on tan block cannot become blue), and the slot offset from its fin sweeps monotonically from +74 to -23 px-3x across the frame, which is parallax off deep members standing proud of the slot plane.

arcade.backGlazing.lightsPerBay.source: UCOP2008-p11_york-arcade-3x.png (UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings, 18 November 2008, p11 'TRANSPARENCY - EXISTING REVELLE COLLEGE BUILDING CONTEXT'): in the bay carrying the bike racks, two thin white mullions divide the full-height glazed back wall into three lights. The frame resolves the back wall in three bays only, so the count is read off one and extended.
arcade.backGlazing.lightsPerBay.note: A COUNT, so the tolerance is zero: three lights or it is not this bay. Extending it to every bay is the [estimated] part and is labelled in arcade.backGlazing.note.

draw.why: Render offsets, not dimensions. Nothing here is a claim about the building: they exist so coplanar surfaces resolve in depth, so the membrane stays proud of a wall that wanders off its own chord, and so no terrain triangle runs through a face. They are declared here rather than left as literals in the module, and the test checks the module carries no numeric geometry of its own. Every numeric leaf here is banded in `draw.bands` — see draw.bandsWhy.
draw.finStandoffNote: The drawn ring wanders up to ~0.06 m off each facade chord, so the membrane must stand at least that far proud of the chord to stay outside the wall everywhere along it.
draw.bayRoundingNote: floor() on a float that lands on an integer from below would drop the last bay of a run whose length divides exactly. It no longer bites on the west edge — since 2026-08-21 the measured 3.9209 m bay divides 91.1055 m into 23.236, not into an integer — but the court faces and any future face may still land on one, so the epsilon stays. It exists so the arithmetic's own answer survives binary rounding, and nothing else.

tiles.note: Material REPEAT tiles, not building dimensions: how much real surface one texture tile of campus-materials.js's brick, decomposedGranite and asphalt classes covers. The brick class tiles 8 courses by 4 units, so its tile is 8 nominal courses square.

draw.bandsWhy: R2 arbitration S1(i). The coverage walk used to stop at the drawn blocks, so every number in here was uncovered — and `draw` is exactly where a metre can hide, because the block declares itself to be render offsets and nothing checked that it still was. Each numeric leaf of `draw` now carries a machine-readable [lo, hi] and the test asserts BOTH that the shipped value is inside its band and that the band table covers every leaf exhaustively, so a new unbanded offset cannot be added. THE BANDS ARE WHAT AN OFFSET MAY BE, NOT WHAT THIS ONE IS: the floors come from the ~0.06 m by which the drawn ring wanders off each facade chord (a standoff under that puts the membrane inside the wall) and from mesh resolutions below which a lathe or a torus stops reading as its object; the ceilings come from the section's own gate that no facade layer may reach more than 1.0 m off its measured face, and from the point at which an offset would be a dimension. Anything in here that ever needs a band wider than a metre is not an offset and belongs in derivations, estimates or reads.
draw.columnStandoffNote: THE DRAWN ARCADE RECESS, and it is not the arcade's depth. How far the pierced arcade screen and the shaft faces flush with it stand proud of the drawn ring chord; the CMU back plane stays at backStandoff, so what a viewer sees into is 0.70 - 0.15 = 0.55 m. The real arcade is ONE BAY deep (arcade.depth, 3.92 m) and cannot be drawn: campus-massing.js extrudes the drawn ring as a solid prism and this membrane is a skin on it, so anything behind the chord is inside solid geometry. Raised from 0.45 on 2026-08-21 because at 0.30 m of recess the arcade read as a row of arch-shaped niches rather than as a covered walk (visual round 2, MAJOR 3). IT STOPS AT 0.70 FOR A MEASURED REASON, not a round one: the drawn west wall is at x = 82.80 at its north end and plaza.dgBelt ends at x = 82.00, so 0.70 m is ALL the ground York owns there. A deeper recess would stand York geometry on the plaza's belt, which this section does not do in either direction. It is also well inside the rule that no facade layer reaches more than 1.0 m off its measured face, and since the shafts are inset by their own base radius to sit flush in the screen, 0.70 is the whole arcade's reach and not just the screen's.
draw.arcadeScreenDepthNote: How thick the pierced arcade screen is extruded, so the semicircular head has a real soffit returning into the recess instead of being a cut in a plane with no thickness. It is also the ruler the other arcade layers are placed against: the soffit's front face sits at columnStandoff - arcadeScreenDepth/2, i.e. buried half-way through the screen, so that no two surfaces in this assembly are coplanar. The pair draw.fasciaProud and draw.fasciaDepth was REMOVED with the separate fascia box they positioned (superseded['arcade.fascia=separate-box']) rather than left banded and unread.
draw.columnWaistFracNote: Where the shaft reaches its waist, as a fraction of the VISIBLE shaft — which since 2026-08-21 runs foot to springing rather than foot to fascia. Its companion offset columnFlareExp is GONE, not merely unused: the lathe flare it shaped is retired (superseded["arcade.capital=lathe-flare"]) because two flares meet in a cusp and gave this arcade pointed lancet arches. A banded offset nothing reads is the rot this block exists to prevent, so it was removed rather than left banded and dead.

grid.source: ONE GRID, AND SINCE 2026-08-21 IT IS NOT ONE GRID. Floor-to-floor is 3.6576 m (12 ft = 18 CMU courses) and closes the drawn prism against LiDAR on three faces. The ARCADE BAY is now measured off the 2008 frame at 3.9209 m — 268 px of column pitch against 250 px of storey pitch — and the fin module still SHIPS ASSERTED at 0.9144 m (3 ft) on the fin-count argument alone, so arcadeBay / finModule is 4.29 where the same frame measures 2.94 fins to a bay. THAT IS conflicts[0], unresolved, and it is now an arithmetic contradiction on the face of this block rather than a paragraph. RETIRED, and kept on the record in conflicts[] and superseded[]: finModule 1.829 (a 2x error, refuted by the 805-fin count on any face selection), arcadeBay 3.658 (the drawing's 12'-0" is the FLOOR-TO-FLOOR, not the bay), arcadeBay 2.6796 (91.1055 / 34, inferred from STRUCTURE's 35 columns and refuted by the frame's own column pitch by 46%), floorToFloor 3.775 (15.1/4 back-solved, 3.2% high) and the inventory's 5.0 (refuted by 3.3 m). SOURCE CONFLICT declared, as before and for the same reason: the inventory's 5.0 m cannot fit the drawn prism.

west.note: West bar. From the plaza the drawn prism reads exactly as sourced: arcade storey + 2 fin storeys to the parapet [STRUCTURE 'two-story...' + 2019/2024 photography]. Its extra drawn storey is below plaza grade (the podium).
west.endWallNote: THE TWO COURTYARD END WALLS, dressed 2026-08-21 on the same reasoning as structures.lecture. DPR Image 9's 'one tall blank white end wall closing the court' is sourced for the absence of fins and for nothing else, and a blank white precast wall in 1966 is still a banded precast wall. They take the same [estimated] extension of the West bar's own storey bands, because they ARE the West bar — both carry structure 'west'.

north.note: 4 fin storeys [measured, DPR Image 4] — the drawn prism's 4 levels read back from the ravine.

lecture.note: SOURCE CONFLICT, declared: DPR Image 5 shows a one-storey Lecture Hall; the drawn prism covers the whole comb at one height and geometry may not change. Its faces are dressed plain white full height; the raked roof and true height are in absent[]. DRESSED, NOT LEFT RAW, SINCE 2026-08-21 (visual round 2, MAJORS 1 and 2). This block closes the gap between the two wings and both courtyards look straight at it, and it was shipping as one flat untextured plane per face from ground to parapet — the largest surface in the east views and indistinguishable from an unfinished wall. The ladder for its elevations runs out at DPR Image 5's 'plain white box', which is a claim about what the wall LACKS (fins) and dimensions nothing, so per the ultra standard its faces now take an [estimated] extension of THIS BUILDING'S OWN sourced pattern and nothing else: the smooth white precast band at every 12 ft storey line that the West bar carries under each fin storey, plus the base band the fin storeys land on and the same white coping. No fins, no window slots and no invented openings — the only openings are DPR Image 5's own louvered vents and paired glazed doors, which were already built. Every figure it uses is the building's own: grid.floorToFloor, finSystem.band.height and grid.parapet.

tower.capNote: Blank service/stair tower at the north wing's east corner, rising slightly above the parapet [measured, DPR Image 4]; 1.8 m rise is the 'slightly above' read. ABSENT from the facilities massing inventory — its three dressed walls + cap keep the survey-ring position and constitute the volume.
tower.blankNote: DELIBERATELY BLANK, DECLARED 2026-08-21 (visual round 2, MAJOR 1). This mass is not untreated: it is a windowless service/stair tower and blankness is what two independent epochs show. DPR 523 Image 4 (ARG 2015) is cited for a 'full-height blank windowless service/stair tower', and ucsddc-bb8089859p_york-roof-looking-SE.jpg (UCSD Library Digital Collections ARK bb8089859p, mid-to-late 1960s) independently shows a blank grey service block standing beside the fin screen on the far wing — a first-decade frame agreeing with a 2015 one, which is as good as this building's sources get. It therefore carries NO fins, NO window slots and NO band, and that is a claim rather than an omission. What it lacked and now has is the coping: its walls used to stop dead at the drawn parapet while every other face on the building terminated in the same white coping, which is what made a sourced blank wall read as an unfinished one.

finSystem.source: Fins: centres at the ASSERTED 3 ft module (grid.finModule is [conflicted, asserted] — see conflicts[0]), THREE per arcade bay. THE FIN'S VISIBLE WIDTH AND ITS WINDOW SLOT ARE MEASURED AS FRACTIONS OF THAT MODULE, not as metres: R2 arbitration Y1 measured UCOP2008-p11_york-finfield-3x.png and gets fin width 0.0761 of module and slot width 0.0805 of module, with ONE SLOT PER FIN (14 of 14 slots found, seven fins in both storeys). The metre values shipped here are those fractions times the module and are therefore CONSEQUENT ON AN UNRESOLVED MODULE — `widthOfModule` and `windowWidthOfModule` are the figures that survive a re-solve. Per module: one fin, one slot, 84.3% solid split-face CMU, which is the wide block panel every source describes. The competing reading of the WIDTH is STRUCTURE's 500 lb mass chain, which is retained in conflicts[] and pins the fin's cross-sectional AREA (0.025836 m2), not its width; the residual can go into DEPTH instead, and this section does not resolve that. Bands: smooth white precast mid-floor bands ~0.55 m [read]. The membrane's standoff is a RENDER offset and lives in draw[].

arcade.note: RE-DECIDED 2026-08-21 (visual round 2, MAJOR 3 and MAJOR 4) AND THE LOSING READ STAYS ON THE RECORD. THE HEAD IS SEMICIRCULAR. What shipped was a pointed lancet arch, which no source claims and which was an artefact of building the capital as a power-law lathe flare: two such flares meet in a cusp. The head is now cut as a true semicircle of radius arcade.archRadius, springing off the shaft faces and crowning at the underside of the fascia, which is what UCOP2008 p11 shows and what both the research dossier and the visual critic independently read off it. THE BAY IS 3.9209 m, MEASURED, NOT 2.6796 m INFERRED FROM THE COLUMN COUNT. See derivations.figures['grid.arcadeBay']: the frame's own column pitch against the frame's own storey pitch. The built row is therefore 24 columns over the drawn 91.1055 m west edge, not 35, and the 35-column claim is NOT deleted — it stays in columnsSourced, in the readings, in absent[] and in a conflicts entry that says plainly that the sourced count and the photographed rhythm cannot both be true of this wall. The columns are HEXAGONAL and fan-vaulted [sourced, STRUCTURE and LPA both]; the shafts are still cut as arcade.sides lathe segments and now run from their own drawn-surface foot to the springing, with the fan carried by the screen's spandrel instead of by a lathe that used to bulge a capital's full radius into the plaza. The same hexagon is the college's signature motif — it is in the Bonner-Mayer-York breezeways and in York's own courtyard planters. IT IS AN OPEN COVERED WALK, NOT A RELIEF. The screen is pierced, there is a shaded soffit over the recess, a paved floor inside it seated on the drawn surface, and the sourced glazed back wall behind. The recess it can draw is 0.70 m against a declared depth of one full bay, because the massing prism under this membrane is solid to the ring — see arcade.depth and absent[]. RE-AUDITED AND CORRECTED 2026-08-21. The first cut of this rebuild put the soffit block's front face and the screen's outer face in the SAME PLANE, and the mullions in the glazing's plane; coplanar surfaces tear rather than blend, and the result was 91 m of broken tan dashes across the white fascia band at eye level and mullions rendering as dots. Every layer of the arcade now has its own depth, the fascia is cut as the screen's head rather than drawn as a separate box behind the recess (superseded['arcade.fascia=separate-box']), and the suite gates the whole assembly on no two faces landing within 0.02 m of each other — a gate demonstrated against both configurations that failed.

backGlazing.note: The arcade's back wall, per bay: a full-height glazed screen divided into three lights by thin white mullions [UCOP2008 p11, the bay with the bike racks, where two mullions divide the opening into three]. Carried across every bay as an [estimated] extension of that one sourced bay — the frame shows the back wall in only three bays. IT RUNS FLOOR TO SPRINGING, NOT FLOOR TO CROWN (re-audited 2026-08-21): the glazed screen is rectangular and the semicircular head above it is the VAULT, which is what the frame shows and what arcade.note has always described as a cloister-vault soffit per bay. Running it to the crown meant the only surface visible through an arch was glass, so the recess had no internal modelling and every opening read as a flat black hole. The mullions stand one leaf PROUD of the glass rather than in its plane; sharing the plane rendered them as broken dotted lines. The dark full-height ENTRY RECESS the same frame shows two bays south of the north end is still NOT built: absent[] records that its position has never been converted to world coordinates, and a door in the wrong bay is worse than no door.
