epoch2008.ratioNote: What is exposure-invariant is the RATIO. 2008 puts CMU at 0.55 / 0.50 / 0.44 of the fin's RGB; the shipped hexes put it at 0.78 / 0.65 / 0.50. The shipped CMU is markedly lighter and warmer relative to the precast than 2008 was — consistent with a 2024 post-retrofit epoch on cleaned concrete, and NOT reconcilable with 2008 by any exposure correction, because an exposure change scales both sides equally. Declared, not averaged.

conflicts: FIN MODULE — UNRESOLVED, AND NOT RESOLVABLE ON THE FRAMES IN THIS REPO. grid.finModule = 0.9144 SHIPS, but it is [conflicted, asserted] and not derived, and every figure consequent on it is labelled so. THE 2008 FRAME'S TWO SCALES REALLY DO DISAGREE, INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED (R2 arbitration Y2): averaging over CMU-panel columns only (fin centre + 95..175 px, so no fins), the pale mid-floor bands sit at 498.5 and 1252.5 px-3x, a floor-to-floor of 754.0 px-3x = 251.3 source-px, which reproduces the section's `250 px per storey` to 0.5%. Against a fin pitch of 90.7 source-px the fin module is 0.3609 of a floor-to-floor: at a 3.6576 m storey that is 1.320 m, reproducing this section's own 1.336 m alternative; and if the module is 0.9144 m then the storey is 2.53 m, which no 1966 laboratory building has. FORESHORTENING DOES NOT RESCUE IT — an obliquely photographed facade is compressed HORIZONTALLY and not vertically, so correcting for it makes the module LARGER than 1.320, not smaller. There is no viewing geometry that turns 1.320 into 0.914. THE TIE-BREAK WAS ATTEMPTED WITH AN ABSOLUTE RULER AND FAILED, AND THE NEGATIVE IS REPORTED: this section asserts cmuCourse = 0.2032 (8 in) and cmuUnit = 0.4064 (16 in), which would make the block coursing a scale independent of both disputed chains. High-passing at 61 px and 41 px and autocorrelating the CMU field gave NO vertical local maximum above r = 0.15 anywhere in lag 25-140, and horizontal peaks at lags 63, 50 and 32 in three different panels with nothing in the fourth. The source frame is too soft for its block joints to be recovered at 3x upsampling. WHAT SURVIVES THE UNCERTAINTY: everything the R2 arbitration rules on for this facade is a RATIO to the fin pitch — fin width / pitch, slot width / pitch, and a pure count — so finSystem.widthOfModule (0.0761) and finSystem.windowWidthOfModule (0.0805) ship alongside their metre values and are the figures a future re-solve carries correctly. The shipped 0.2028 m fin was wrong at BOTH candidate modules, by 2.9x at 0.9144 and 2.0x at 1.320. An orthographic or rectified frame of the west face would settle the module outright; see absent[]. A THIRD ROUTE TO THE SAME ~1.33 m, ADDED 2026-08-21. The arcade bay is no longer inherited from STRUCTURE's 35 columns; it is measured off this same frame at 3.9209 m (derivations.figures['grid.arcadeBay']). The frame also measures 2.9353 fins to a bay (px2008.columnPitch / px2008.finPitch = 268 / 91.3), so the module the ARCADE implies is 3.9209 / 2.9353 = 1.3358 m — arrived at without touching the storey pitch at all, and agreeing with the 1.320 m the vertical scale gives to 1.2%. Three independent routes through this photograph now give 1.32-1.36 m and none gives 0.914. THE MODULE STILL SHIPS AT 0.9144 AND THIS AGENT DID NOT MOVE IT: the fin COUNT is the only evidence on the other side and it is real (conflicts[1] — 752 fins over the sourced faces against a sourced 805 at 0.9144, and 515 at 1.3358, 36% short), the critic of the rendered building did not raise the fin field, and re-opening a figure two arbitrations have already ruled on is not what a visual repair is for. What changed is that the contradiction is now visible as arithmetic: grid.arcadeBay / grid.finModule = 4.29 against a measured 2.94. AN ORTHOGRAPHIC OR RECTIFIED FRAME OF THE WEST FACE STILL SETTLES IT OUTRIGHT; see absent[].

FIN COUNT — STRUCTURE's 805 against what the geometry builds, at both modules, computed in counts.finCensus rather than asserted. At the derived 0.9144 m module the SOURCED fin faces alone (697.836 storey-metres) yield 752 fins, 6.6% SHORT of 805; adding the three [estimated] south-end faces (871.649 storey-metres) gives 934, 16% over; dressing every drawn-ring return as well (1186.506 storey-metres) gives 1230. The sourced 805 therefore falls BETWEEN the count over the sourced faces and the count over the sourced faces plus the south end, which is the best a module can do against a figure whose clad extent nobody has published. At the retired 1.829 m module the same three counts are 364, 454 and 572 — every one of them far short, and even dressing every return the whole comb reaches only 29% below 805, which is what refutes 1.829 outright. THE MODULE IS NOT TUNED TO HIT 805 and the residual is not closed: STRUCTURE says the fins ring the UPPER floors of THREE of York's buildings, while this section clads all four storeys of both wings, and no frame resolves that. See absent[] 'WHETHER THE WINGS' LOWER STOREYS ARE FIN-CLAD AT ALL'.

THE WINDOW SLOT AND THE FIN WIDTH — RE-DECIDED 2026-08-21 IN FAVOUR OF THE FRAME, ON BOTH COUNTS (R2 arbitration Y1). ONE SLOT PER FIN, not one per arcade bay, and both the fin and the slot are far narrower than this section shipped. THE SECTION'S OWN REASONING IS REFUTED BY ITS OWN FRAME: R1 argued that on the 0.9144 m module 'a 0.425 m slot plus the derived 0.203 m fin would leave 0.29 m and make the field 46% glass, which STRUCTURE's textured concrete block rules out', and therefore moved the COUNT to every third fin to rescue the WIDTH. The premise is the width. 0.425 m is 0.465 of a module; the frame measures the slot at 0.0805 of a module, and the fin at 0.0761. At those proportions the field is 84.3% solid split-face CMU — comfortably past the >50% gate the section itself cited as making a per-fin slot impossible, and exactly what 'a wide split-face CMU panel' looks like. THE COUNT IS NOT ARGUABLE: an adaptive scan of both storey bands finds a dark slot beside all seven fins in both storeys, fourteen of fourteen, where a per-bay slot predicts one at every third fin. The slots are GLAZING, by two independent proofs: the two sky-lit slots read b-r = +17.4 / +15.5 against CMU controls at -15.6 to -18.7, and a shadow on tan block cannot become blue; and the slot's apparent offset from its fin sweeps monotonically +74 -> -23 px-3x across the frame, which is parallax off deep members standing proud of the slot plane. WHAT REMAINS CONFLICTED, AND IS NOT AVERAGED: (a) DPR 523's PROSE band of '0.35-0.5 m' for the slot, which is 0.38-0.55 of a module against the frame's 0.0805 — carried as a declared conflict, not as a governing figure, and unresolved; and (b) STRUCTURE's 500 lb fin, which pins the fin's cross-sectional AREA at 0.025836 m2 and only becomes a WIDTH of 0.2028 m when divided by a mean projection that is itself a stack of [estimated] spindle dimensions. The mass and the photograph do not contradict each other if the residual goes into DEPTH; this section does not resolve which, and no longer presents 0.2028 m as derived from a published mass.

YEAR BUILT — 1966 (STRUCTURE and UCSD Plan/Design/Build, independently) against 1965 (UCSD Emeriti). Two to one, and UCSD's own project page is the tiebreaker; 1965 is plausibly the occupancy year, as Emeriti also gives for Galbraith. Both recorded in architect.conflict. No geometric consequence.

FLOOR AREA — 134,000 sf (UCSD Plan/Design/Build) against 122,000 sf (STRUCTURE and LPA). Still unreconciled. UCSD Emeriti's 62,279 sf is NOT a third competitor: it is ASSIGNABLE area, a different quantity, and saying so removes one apparent conflict. No geometric consequence.

COLOUR EPOCH — the 2008 transparency and the 2024 hexes cannot be reconciled by exposure. 2008 puts the CMU at 0.55 / 0.50 / 0.44 of the precast fin's RGB; the shipped hexes put it at 0.78 / 0.65 / 0.50. An exposure change scales both sides equally and cannot move a ratio, so this is a real epoch difference — consistent with cleaned concrete after the 2021-24 preservation retrofit. The 2024 values ship; the 2008 medians are recorded in colorConflicts and pasted into nothing.

SIGNAGE — 'navy serif' (inherited, absent[3]) against SANS-SERIF in the 2008 frame, which shows the York Hall lettering on the arcade fascia as a widely letterspaced sans face, dark on the pale fascia. Either the sign was replaced or the inherited description is wrong. The repo has no text mechanism so nothing is built either way, and the absent entry now records the disagreement instead of asserting one side.

THE ARCADE'S DEPTH — DPR Images 6/7 are cited for a two-row arcade, but UCOP2008 p11 shows the northern bays backing onto a CONTINUOUS CMU wall one bay deep, with a dark recessed doorway and a glazed noticeboard on it. That is evidence against a second colonnade in those bays. Neither the inner row nor a second reading is built; absent[6] stands and now records the partial contradiction.

YORK'S LIDAR HEIGHT ANCHOR IS ITSELF CONTESTED, AND THE R2 ARBITRATION'S S1(iii) REMEDY FOR THE ROOF GATE COULD NOT BE APPLIED AS WRITTEN. The arbitration asks that the roof-equipment gate's ceiling be re-pinned to 'the LiDAR maximum for York from docs/data/campus-lidar.json' rather than to the penthouse the gate is testing. There is no single such figure. THREE disagree, in this repo, today: campus-3d.json carries h = 20 for the York Hall SURVEY ring; campus-lidar.json `heights['York Hall']` is 12.6; and campus-lidar.json `massHeights['m:115,377']`, the statistic campus-massing.js actually extrudes over the DRAWN facilities ring, is 15.1. They are three different statistics over two different footprints and this section already declares the 20-vs-15.1 disagreement in measured.note. Manufacturing a ceiling out of a difference between two of them (20 - 15.1 = 4.9 m of headroom) would be inventing a resolution, which the arbitration forbids in the same sentence. THE CONTEST IS RECORDED AND THE ITEM IS REPORTED UNFIXED. What WAS done instead, and what actually closes audit-york F4's surviving mutation ('penthouse 2.5 -> 4.0 m and blades 2.2 -> 3.5 to match, fail=0'), is that both reads are now PINNED AS LITERALS IN THE TEST — roof.louvreWell.bladeHeight to 2.2 and roof.penthouse.size to 4.5 / 2.5 / 3.0 — so neither side of the comparison can move at all, and the ceiling being computed from its own subject stops mattering. A LiDAR-anchored ceiling remains the better gate and wants York's height anchor resolved first.

THE 35-COLUMN ARCADE vs THE PHOTOGRAPHED BAY RHYTHM — DECLARED 2026-08-21, NOT AVERAGED AND NOT DELETED. STRUCTURE 2024 says 'Thirty-five fluted, cast-in-place concrete columns support the heavy upper structure' and both STRUCTURE and LPA say 'a 300-foot-long column arcade'; the drawn west edge is 91.1055 m = 298.9 ft, so the run length and the wall are certainly the same object. THE COUNT AND THE WALL TOGETHER IMPLY A 2.6796 m BAY (91.1055 / 34) AND THE PHOTOGRAPH REFUTES IT. In UCOP2008-p11_york-west-arcade-COLOUR.png one storey is 250 px and 2.6796 m would therefore be 183 px of column pitch; the measured pitch is 268 px pinned, and an independent three-band comb fit run on 2026-08-21 gives 280.5 px over the shafts (y 500-600), 271.0 px over the spandrels (y 452-500) and 272.8 px under the fascia soffit (y 430-470). That is a 46-53% miss, and it cannot be foreshortening: an obliquely photographed facade is compressed horizontally, never stretched, so correcting for obliquity moves the true bay further from 2.6796, not toward it. The frame also puts the columns exactly on the fin grid at 268 / 91.3 = 2.94 fins to a bay, which a 2.6796 m bay against the same frame's fin pitch cannot do. THE BAY THEREFORE SHIPS MEASURED AT 3.9209 m AND THE WEST ROW BUILDS 24 COLUMNS. WHAT THE 35 MIGHT STILL BE, none of which this section can test on any frame it holds: columns counted over the arcade's returns and the two courtyard mouths as well as the plaza run; both rows of the two-row arcade DPR Images 6/7 are cited for (absent[] 'Inner (second) row'); or a count that includes the cast-in-place columns inside the building line that 'support the heavy upper structure' without standing in the arcade at all — STRUCTURE's sentence says support, not arcade. 35 columns at the measured bay would need 133.3 m of run, which is 437 ft against a sourced 300 ft, so the count and the run length do not close on each other either. BOTH READINGS STAY ON THE RECORD: the 35 is in arcade.columnsSourced, counts.arcadeColumnsSourced, derivations.readings.counted.arcadeColumns and absent[]; the 24 is what is built and why is in derivations.figures['grid.arcadeBay'].

THE ARCADE'S DRAWN DEPTH IS NOT ITS DEPTH, AND THE LIMIT IS THE MASSING, NOT THE EVIDENCE — DECLARED 2026-08-21. UCOP2008 p11 shows a covered walk one full bay deep to a continuous CMU back wall, and arcade.depth carries that at 3.9209 m. This membrane cannot draw it. campus-massing.js extrudes the drawn ring as a SOLID prism and campus-walk.js registers the photo zone as a layer that ADDS on top of massing ('the measured massing its facades float off carries the silhouette'), so every surface this section could set behind the ring chord is inside solid geometry and invisible. The whole arcade is therefore drawn OUTWARD of the chord: the pierced screen and the shaft faces at draw.columnStandoff = 0.85 m, the CMU back plane at draw.backStandoff = 0.15 m, and 0.70 m of recess between them with a shaded soffit and a paved floor in it. 0.70 m against 3.92 m is an 82% shortfall and it is stated rather than disguised. CLOSING IT IS NOT A YORK CHANGE: it needs campus-massing.js to stop extruding, or to hollow, the ring under a photo-detailed building, which is outside this section's ownership. Recorded in absent[] as owed.

boundary.why: The team lead asked which ground belongs to `plaza` and which to `york`, and for overlaps to be FLAGGED, not claimed twice. Nothing here is claimed by both sections.
boundary.dgBelt: CLEAN AND NOW STATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. plaza.dgBelt runs x 66 -> 82; york.westGround.mulch.xWest is 82.1. They abut with a 0.1 m gap and neither claims the other's ground. The eucalyptus, the mulch-belt planting and the DG surface west of x = 82 belong to the plaza landscape section and are deliberately not rebuilt here.
resolved: A plaza eucalyptus was standing on York's own retaining wall — AND THE WALL IS NOW RETIRED, which resolves it outright rather than by 0.4 m. plaza.treeOverrides.eucalyptus.items[1] is a MEASURED LiDAR trunk at (147.1, 347.4) with a 5.8 m crown; the shipped york.eastSide.retainingWall ran x = 146.5 from z 343 to 362.5, putting the trunk 0.6 m from the wall and the crown across 11.6 m of it. R1 moved the wall to x = 140.9, which cleared the TRUNK by 6.2 m but the CROWN by only 0.4 m — barely achieving the criterion the move was made for (audit-york F9). R2 arbitration P3 then retired the wall entirely, because no rung of the ladder gives it a grade to retain at any alignment on this side: York now claims no ground east of the drawn ring at all, and the eucalyptus stands in plaza's ground unopposed. See absent[] for what was looked for.

York's mulch bed was partly inside York. The shipped bed was three axis-aligned rectangles reaching x = 83.85 against a west wall that runs from x = 83.8 at the south to x = 82.8 at the north, so ~1.05 m of mulch sat inside the building at the north end. The bed's east edge now follows the wall chord.
flagged: A 25 m Torrey pine stands off York's north-west corner, and its CROWN CROSSES THE FIN MEMBRANE — WHICH IS ALLOWED. plaza.treeOverrides.pines.items[0] is a measured LiDAR trunk at (82.7, 336.6), h 25.1 m, r 6.1 m. THE DISTANCE IS CORRECTED (R2 arbitration P2, from audit-york F8): the shipped claim of 'within 0.1-1.0 m' does not reproduce. The nearest drawn ring edge, (86.2, 338.8)-(82.8, 338.8), is 2.20 m away, and the west wall chord (83.8, 429.9)-(82.8, 338.8) is ALSO 2.20 m away — its nearest point is the north-west corner, because z = 336.6 lies 2.2 m NORTH of where the west wall begins. The tree is not planted in the wall; it stands clear off the corner. THE CONSEQUENCE STILL HOLDS AND IS NOW RULED ON RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN: a 6.1 m crown radius reaches 3.9 m into the building in plan, and that is CORRECT AND KEPT. The ultra standard's 'nothing hovers or intersects' governs BUILT SOLIDS seating on surfaceAt or on their carrying structure; a LiDAR-measured tree crown is not a built solid placed by this section, it is measured vegetation whose canopy genuinely overhangs the facade, and UCOP2008 p11 shows exactly this — eucalyptus and pine trunks hard against York's frontage with branches crossing it. Trimming the crown to clear the facade would falsify a measurement to satisfy a rule written about furniture floating above ground. RECORDED, NOT CORRECTED: nothing is moved, in either section, and the gate at tests/campus-photo-york.test.mjs is unchanged — it tests that York's west wall has not moved into the tree, which is the right thing to test and which passes. GOVERNANCE NOTE: the tree is PLAZA's, and R1 pinned it in place with a york claim whose stated distance was wrong; correcting the number removes the false pin.

plaza.treeOverrides.eucalyptus.items[11] at (131.2, 378.7), r 7.5, sits 4.6 m east of the Lecture Hall's east face and its crown overlaps `lecture-east`, the face carrying the louvered vents and the paired glazed doors. Cosmetic; FLAGGED for the critic.
boundary.arcadeVsMulch: DECLARED 2026-08-21, NOT RESOLVED, AND NOTHING WAS SHAVED TO HIDE IT. The arcade recess reaches draw.columnStandoff = 0.70 m west of the drawn wall and york.westGround.mulch runs east to wallX - draw.mulchWallClear, so about 0.60 m of the mulch bed lies UNDER the arcade along the whole frontage. In UCOP2008 p11 the bed stops at the column line and the arcade is paved from there in, so the bed's east edge SHOULD be the column line. It cannot simply be moved there: at the north end the wall is at x = 82.80 and the bed starts at x = 82.10, so the arcade takes the entire 0.70 m and the northern band would have no width left at all. The bed positions are [estimated] and the arcade line is measured, so the arcade wins on evidence — but deleting a northern band is a content change no critic asked for, and where that bed really ends is a york/plaza edge question. HANDED TO R6 (Edges + revellesiteworks) with the plaza abutment it belongs to. What was NOT done to paper over it: York does not draw a floor decal inside the arcade. That ground is the plaza's and the terrain already draws it; a York decal there would double-build plaza ground AND sit coplanar with York's own mulch on the same overlay rung.

absent: South end elevation — LADDER EXHAUSTED for the PATTERN, and the ladder was re-climbed on 2026-08-20: photographs (LPA project page, STRUCTURE) are all west/plaza and courtyard frames; Street View does not reach it (Revelle is pedestrian and York's south end faces the Central Utilities service apron); no drone or video exists for York; the UCSD plandesignbuild entry is text-only; UCSD DC bb8089859p looks away and bb1639263c is oblique from the north-west with the south end self-occluded. Loading dock, trash enclosure, mechanical yard — no dedicated service condition appears in any source; unbuilt, per better absent than wrong

The sunken walkway and the below-grade ground storey — the drawn prism's bottom storey IS the podium storey: buried under the courtyard deck and the plaza, emerging only toward the ravine; it cannot be carved, so the deck reads as grade. The arithmetic now closes on it: plaza grade less one 3.6576 m storey is 20.99 m against a rimBase of 21.222 m.

Inner (second) row of arcade columns — the double-depth arcade is cited [DPR Images 6/7] but the inner row stands inside the measured massing; represented by the dark recessed CMU back plane only. PARTLY CONTRADICTED: UCOP2008 p11 shows the northern bays backing onto a continuous CMU wall one bay deep, not a second colonnade. Neither reading is built.

35 sourced columns vs the drawn 12 ft bay — RE-OPENED AND RE-DECIDED 2026-08-21, THIS TIME AGAINST THE COUNT, and every reading anyone has ever taken on it stays on the record. The 2026-08-20 resolution in favour of 35 divided the drawn 91.1055 m west edge by 34 bays to get 2.6796 m, on the strength of the sourced 300-foot run matching that wall to 0.35%. It never checked that bay against the photograph. It does not survive: one storey is 250 px in UCOP2008-p11_york-west-arcade-COLOUR.png, so 2.6796 m is 183 px of column pitch, and the measured pitch is 268 px pinned with an independent comb fit giving 271-281 px across three bands of the same frame. Foreshortening cannot rescue it in the direction needed. THE BAY IS NOW MEASURED at px2008.columnPitch / px2008.storeyPitch x floorToFloor = 3.9209 m and the west row builds 24 columns. THREE READINGS ARE NOW ON THE RECORD AND NONE IS DELETED: 25 columns on a 12 ft bay (the original inventory, retired 2026-08-20 — and the 12'-0" it read off STRUCTURE Fig. 5 really is the FLOOR-TO-FLOOR, which that resolution got right and which still stands); 35 columns on a 2.6796 m bay (retired 2026-08-21); and 24 columns on the measured 3.9209 m bay, which is what ships. WHAT IS STILL MISSING is any reconciliation of STRUCTURE's 35 with the photographed rhythm — 35 columns at the measured bay would need 437 ft of run against a sourced 300 ft — and the candidate explanations, none of them testable on a frame this repo holds, are in conflicts[].

West arcade entry door positions — PARTLY RESOLVED 2026-08-20: UCOP2008 p11 shows at least one full-height dark entry recess on the arcade back wall, roughly two bays south of the north end in that view, with a glazed noticeboard beside it. The frame is not georeferenced, so the position has NOT been converted to world coordinates and nothing is built. What remains absent is the position, not the existence.
Lecture Hall raked roof, roof monitor and true one-storey height — DPR Image 5 vs the single drawn prism over the whole comb; faces dressed, measured height not contradicted

Roof equipment — RESOLVED IN FORM AND SCALE 2026-08-20, OPEN IN PLACEMENT. WHAT REMAINS ABSENT: which of York's roofs the frame looks from, and therefore which wing carries the louvre bank and which the penthouse — that assignment is still the BIM's alone. 10 ft utility tunnel beneath the colonnade — 'PROTECT IN PLACE', subterranean, invisible

122,000 vs 134,000 sq ft floor area — unreconciled between LPA/STRUCTURE and UCSD plandesignbuild; no geometric consequence taken. UCSD Emeriti's 62,279 sf is NOT a third figure: it is ASSIGNABLE area, a different quantity.

The drawn facilities comb differs from the survey ring (west face ~1 m further west, no NE tower, different courtyard notches) — facades follow the drawn ring; every drawn edge from 1.2 m up carries the membrane as a declared [estimated] return, and only sub-1.2 m jogs keep the massing's own wall. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED 2026-08-20: the drawn ring's west edge measures 298.9 ft against a sourced 300-foot arcade, so on this face the drawn ring is demonstrably the right one and the 2026-08-17 decision to hang everything on it is no longer merely internally consistent.

The inventory's 5.0 m floor-to-floor vs the drawn prism — RESOLVED 2026-08-20 AT 3.6576 m (12 ft = 18 CMU courses counted in UCOP2008 p11), which closes the building against LiDAR on three independent faces. Both losers stay on the record: 5.0 m is refuted by 3.3 m on a frontage the photograph measures, and 3.775 m was 15.1/4 back-solved and puts the plaza frontage 0.36 m above the band the terrain gives it.

THE PLAZA-TO-COURTYARD STEP — NEW. Both courtyard decks measure 23.70 m dead flat against a plaza at 24.6-25.2 m, a 0.961 m drop with no steps, ramp or wall built or recorded. Ladder: DPR Image 9 shows the courtyard but not its junction with the plaza, and no other frame covers it. Anything walking from plaza to courtyard needs this and it is not there. OWED TO A BATCH, NOT LEFT ON A LIST: owedTo: "R6" (Edges + revellesiteworks + college-wide final critic). R2 arbitration P6 affirms the withholding without reservation — the ladder is exhausted and inventing a stair or ramp across a 0.96 m drop would be exactly the plausible guess the project forbids — but an `absent` entry is not an assignment, and plaza.absent[14] is the worked example of a correct withholding whose handoff went nowhere because no batch owned the receiving end. This is a 0.96 m cliff on a walking route in a world where every tab boots campus-walk.js. R6 owns it because a junction between two sections' ground that neither section's frames cover is precisely an edge, and revellesiteworks is where the college's connective ground work lives.

WHETHER THE WINGS' LOWER STOREYS ARE FIN-CLAD AT ALL — NEW. STRUCTURE says the fins ring the UPPER floors of THREE of York's buildings; this section clads all four storeys of both wings and the Lecture Hall carries none. That is the most likely explanation of the 805-vs-950 count gap and no frame resolves it. Not acted on: reducing the clad area to hit 805 would be tuning geometry to a count.

AN ORTHOGRAPHIC OR RECTIFIED FRAME OF THE WEST FACE — NEW, and it is the single highest-value missing item after DPR 523. It would settle the fin module outright: the 2008 frame's horizontal ratio and its vertical scale disagree by a factor of 1.46 (see conflicts[]) and only a rectified frame breaks the tie by measurement rather than by argument. No Apple 3D station grid exists for Revelle (revelle-recon.md Rung 5 item 25); York's east/ravine side and its south end, the two faces with no photographic coverage at all, are exactly what such a grid would resolve.

DPR 523 pp. 431-436 (ARG 2015) — the section's densest cited source, carrying Images 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9 for the north and east elevations, the Lecture Hall, the arcade depth and the courtyards. NOT ON DISK and NOT LOCATABLE on the open web as of 2026-08-20. Recovering it would retire several [estimated] entries at once. See provenance.

EAST-SIDE RETAINING WALL — RETIRED 2026-08-21 under 'better absent than wrong' (R2 arbitration P3), having been built in R1 at x = 140.9 from z 343 to 362.5, 2.2 m high and 0.35 m thick, board-formed, sourced to DPR 523 Image 4. WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR: a grade break for a 2.2 m wall to retain, anywhere on the east side. WHAT WAS FOUND: nothing. The drawn LiDAR surface sampled across z = 347 / 352 / 357 falls about 0.9 m in total from x = 136 to x = 154 — 3-7 cm/m, a terrace, not a cut — and the real ravine break is at x = 178-182, forty metres east. There is no grade for the wall at 140.9 OR at the shipped 146.5. The object had no function at any position this section can defend, and the section cannot say what it retains. AUDIT-YORK F10 IS PART OF THE SAME RETIREMENT and is retired with it, not separately: F10 is that the derivation `max(ring x over 343 <= z <= 362.5) + 1.5` restates the inherited tag's '~1.5 m off the east face' as though it applied everywhere, when the max 139.4 occurs at exactly one vertex and over roughly 15 of the wall's 19.5 m the offset is really 3.3 m. Repairing that derivation would only have positioned an object that should not exist, so the derivation goes with the wall. LADDER FOR A REPLACEMENT: DPR 523 Image 4 is not on disk; no other frame reaches York's ravine side; Street View does not reach it; no drone or video exists; no planning drawing on disk sections this ground. Nothing is built. What DPR Image 4 sources — that a board-formed wall exists somewhere on this side — stays on this list, unbuilt, until a frame or a survey puts it somewhere.

THE ARCADE'S TRUE DEPTH CANNOT BE DRAWN, AND THE OBSTACLE IS THIS REPO'S RENDERING, NOT ITS EVIDENCE — owedTo: "whoever may suppress or hollow the massing prism under a photo-detailed building". The evidence is not missing: UCOP2008 p11 shows a covered walk one full bay deep to a continuous CMU back wall, and arcade.depth ships that at 3.9209 m with its derivation. What is withheld is 3.22 m of it. campus-massing.js extrudes the drawn York ring as a solid prism and this membrane is a skin on it, so no surface set behind the ring chord is visible; the whole arcade is drawn outward of the chord and the recess is draw.columnStandoff less draw.backStandoff = 0.70 m, capped by this section's own rule that no facade layer reaches more than 1.0 m off its measured face. That is an 82% shortfall on a sourced dimension and it is declared rather than faked by pushing the columns into the plaza. Closing it is a campus-massing.js change and is outside this section's ownership; nothing in york may be loosened to fake it.

WHETHER THE LECTURE HALL AND THE TWO COURTYARD END WALLS CARRY ANY ARTICULATION BEYOND STOREY BANDS — ladder climbed 2026-08-21 and exhausted. These four faces close the gap between the wings and both courtyards look at them, and every source that touches them says only what they LACK: DPR 523 Image 5 'a plain white box' for the Lecture Hall and DPR 523 Image 9 'one tall blank white end wall' for the courts — and DPR 523 is itself NOT ON DISK. Photos: the 2008 transparency is a west-facade frame and does not reach them; ARK bb8089859p looks away across the court and shows only a blank grey block; ARK bb1639263c is 768 px oblique. Street View: Revelle is pedestrian and the courts are interior. Drone, planning docs and archives: nothing for these elevations. So the [estimated] dressing extends York's OWN sourced precast band rhythm and stops there — no panel joints, no reveals, no invented openings, because the pattern being extended does not contain them. WHAT WOULD RETIRE THIS: any frame taken inside either courtyard, or a Lecture Hall east elevation.

argo.label: Argo Hall — Revelle College residence hall (attributed to Tucker, Sadler & Bennett, 1967 — an INHERITED, UNVERIFIED claim carried from the inventory and demoted here; see conflicts[]. Renovated, re-railed and repainted WHITE 2015-16, Vasquez Marshall / Webcor). A COURTYARD DONUT, not a solid prism. NOT a Fleet hall.
argo.epoch: Photographs c.2015-2026 (post-repaint). The pre-2014 tan — including the LiDAR-2014-derived colour, Wikimedia's 2012 Argo Hall.jpg and the 2008 UC Regents deck's tan exterior — is a dead epoch and appears nowhere in this section. The SAME RULE covers the court: UC Regents 2008 p11 shows the court galleries with BLUE-painted piers, spandrel bands and fascias and a dark mesh guardrail infill; Webcor's 2016 N9 shows white throughout with white picket rails, because Webcor repainted the entire building and replaced the railings at all balconies in 2015-16. The 2008 blue-and-mesh court is recorded and never built.
argo.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. Facade rhythm, canted precast window surrounds, awning sashes, corner brackets, the solid panelled base wall, the COURT GALLERY ELEVATIONS, roof furniture and the north-entry boardwalk are modelled off the dated photographs inventoried in Revelle-College-Sources/research-notes/research-argo.md. LiDAR/OSM keep deciding scale and position: every facade hangs off two vertices of the MEASURED ArcGIS massing ring campus-massing.js extrudes, and the storey grid is the LiDAR massHeights read back. Bays are built from COUNTS against that ring, never from absolute metres. Nothing measured may ever read from this section.
argo.confidence: HIGH that Argo is a donut: the survey carries two rings, campus-massing.js:826 already extrudes the second as a hole, and Webcor's published 74,836 sf is reproduced by the donut to +2.1 % and missed by a solid prism by +20.8 %. HIGH on the 18.70 m coping plane and on the notch's plan (three of its four surveyed edges reproduced from the 2026 ortho to better than 0.15 m). HIGH on the 30-bay count and on the court being gallery access over painted CMU (N9 plus the 2008 aerial plus the 2008 eye-level frame). MEDIUM on the storey stack: the coping-to-soffit ratio is measured, but the metre value of F is a 2.66-2.85 m band and 2.80 is declared inside it. MEDIUM on the ortho registration (four features, two interior). LOW on everything inside the court that N9 does not frame — the gallery depth, the screen rhythm, the breezeway's position and the floor's material are all withheld or flagged. THE COURT'S GROUND STOREY IS AN OPEN QUESTION, not a confidence level: the breezeway is sourced as existing and its position on the ring is not, so the base condition ships closed and absent[] says why.

notch.note: The full-height stair/lift core standing into the court from its west side — 6.5 x 7.8 m = 50.7 m^2, bounded by segments I3, I4 and I5, part of ring 0's extrusion and running grade to roof plane. This is the 'giant elevator structure' reported missing: it is not a rooftop box and it is already in the survey. It TOPS OUT AT THE ROOF PLANE, +0.0 / -0.7 m — the 2026 ortho registration was fitted at the roof plane and returns residuals of +0.01 m in x and -0.14 m in z on the core, and at 0.208 m of displacement per metre of height a 3-4 m overrun would shift it five to six pixels further north-north-west. It is not there. Webcor's 2015-16 scope was 'elevator upgrades', not a new shaft.

areas.note: Shoelace over the verbatim rings. THE AREA ARGUMENT, which is the strongest single proof that Argo is a donut and it is pure arithmetic: as a donut 1182.62 m^2 x 6 levels = 7095.7 m^2 = 76378 sf against Webcor's published 74,836 sf, an error of +2.1 %; as a solid prism 1399.315 m^2 x 6 = 90373 sf, an error of +20.8 %. A 2 % residual is ordinary gross-area convention. A 21 % miss is not a convention.

derivations.why: THE KEELING BAR. keeling.roofs.pv states a real product dimension and its own arithmetic for every figure it draws — '0.99 x sin 8 deg + 0.22 = 0.36' is written out. This block does the same for Argo: `readings` are the raw citations (pixel counts, published areas, survey vertices, code clauses, standard product sizes) and `figures` is every drawn value with the expression that produces it. tests/campus-photo-argo.test.mjs recomputes every one of these independently from `readings` and fails if the section's own value drifts from its own derivation, so a fabricated figure cannot pass by being self-consistent. `estimates` is the ultra standard's third tier and `reads` are citations pinned as literals. SINCE THE R2 ARBITRATION (S1 vi) `expr` MEANS ARITHMETIC ONLY: every expression here is tokenised and EVALUATED by tests/helpers/axiom-gate.mjs against `readings` and the section's own shipped figures and must reproduce its own `value`, and the prose that used to sit under `expr` is carried under `derivation`. A derivation nobody runs is decoration. `exprTol` appears only where the figure is stated to the centimetre the [estimated] floor-to-floor justifies, and it names the rounding, never a slackened gate.

units.note: Exact by definition. Every product and code figure below is a whole number of inches or feet and converts here.

px.source: webcor-argo-N18.jpg (4000 x 2667), the near-orthographic EAST elevation shot across the Revelle Plaza fountain c.2015-16. Vertical reads down one column band clear of the tree and the lamps; crop origin x = 0.19 W, y = 0.44 H, every y below crop-relative. Near-orthographicity is measured, not assumed: the pier pitch shows no systematic drift end to end.
px.bayPitchNote: 33 pier peaks detected across the storey-3 window band; outside the tree occlusion the pitch is 46.6 px with sd 0.5 over 27 intervals.
px.spanNote: DECLARED CONFLICT, not averaged: 1415 px corner-to-corner across the parapet band is SHORTER than the 1440 px first-pier-to-last-pier run it must contain. Both are recorded; neither is used to derive a metre. See conflicts[].

survey.massHeightSource: campus-lidar.json massHeights['m:-40,383'] = 18.7 — the LiDAR-2014 p98 of returns inside the GIS ring campus-massing.js actually extrudes. WHICH PLANE: the coping band is ~0.5 m wide and rings 149.70 m of outer perimeter plus 78.20 m of court rim, so 227.90 x 0.5 = 113.95 m^2 on a 1182.60 m^2 net plate = 9.6 % of the plate. The top 2 % of returns therefore falls inside the parapet band, and nothing on this roof stands taller than the parapet. 18.70 m is the TOP OF THE PARAPET COPING, +/-0.3 m.
survey.ringHeightSource: campus-lidar.json heights['Argo Hall'] = 18.4 — the same 2014 flight over the OSM ring, which overhangs the roof by ~1.0 m on north and west, so ground returns drag its high percentile down. A valid number over the wrong polygon; recorded as the loser.
survey.formulaHeightSource: campus-arcgis.json massing[99].h = 18.3 is a FORMULA, 6 levels x 3.050 m, which lands on 105 masses campus-wide. Cited only to confirm levels = 6; never as a height.
survey.eastFaceLengthSource: the length of massing[99] ring 0's east face, hypot of the two verbatim survey vertices (-20.2, 366.4) and (-19.9, 403.8) = 37.401203 m. Named as a reading because grid.module divides it; the test recomputes it from the survey ring rather than trusting it.

published.source: Webcor's own project page for the 2015-16 UC San Diego Argo Hall Renovation: 74,836 sf over six levels above grade, 180 student residences, LEED Gold, architect Vasquez Marshall; scope included 'elevator upgrades', exterior concrete fins 'restored to their original design intent', the entire building repainted, and new interior and exterior railings at ALL BALCONIES. Vasquez Marshall's own Blake Hall page (same architect, same renovation, the sibling donut) gives 12 residential suites, 12 shared restroom/shower areas and 72 bedrooms over 2 floors.

cmu.source: Standard 8 in (203.2 mm) concrete-masonry coursing. SOURCED, not assumed: the El Mac mural photograph (mac-arte.blogspot.com, posted 2016-03-23, work signed ELMAC MMXV) is painted on horizontally coursed masonry whose bed-joint pitch scans an exactly regular 31.92 px over 13 intervals. At 8 in coursing the framed width is 1022 / 31.9 x 0.2032 = 6.51 m, which is the court core's surveyed 6.5 m face to within 0.01 m. 16 in coursing gives 13.0 m and 12 in gives 9.77 m, and neither matches any surveyed dimension on this building — so the 8-inch reading is the only one that produces a width that exists here.

code.source: IBC 2021: §1015.3 guards not less than 42 in high; §1015.4 openings must not allow a 4 in sphere to pass; §1020.3 corridor minimum clear width 44 in; §1010.1.1 door leaves 36 in wide and 80 in high minimum. ICC A117.1 §703.4 room-identification signs mounted with the baseline 48-60 in above the floor. Cross-checked against webcor-argo-N9.jpg, which reads the court guardrail at roughly 1.05-1.10 m — the 42 in code minimum, 1.0668 m, sits inside that read.

ortho.source: docs/data/textures/chunk_4_6.jpg, the Google (c)2026 z20 ortho at 8 px/m. Gradient edge-find on smoothed 1-D profiles, world<->pixel by px = (world - chunk.x0) x 8. Four agreeing features: outer plate WEST edge x -58.44 +/-0.19 vs survey -57.5 (-0.94, 5 scans); COURT EAST rim x -31.45 +/-0.06 vs -30.5 (-0.95, 5 scans); outer plate NORTH edge z 362.59 +/-0.10 vs 366.4 (-3.81, 6 scans); COURT SOUTH rim z 389.70 +/-0.05 vs 393.4 (-3.70, 3 scans). The outer SOUTH edge is DISCARDED and the reason is stated: the sun is south-east, so the north edge is a crisp membrane-to-shadow step while the south edge is a low-contrast membrane-to-sunlit-paving step whose strongest gradient is the shadow under the oversailing base, 2.3 m inboard. Correction = (+0.93, +3.78) m; magnitude 3.89 m over 18.70 m of height = 0.208 m per metre at bearing 166 deg. The prior shipped (+1.75, +4.15) does not reproduce and over-corrects x by 0.82 m and z by 0.37 m.
ortho.priorTreeSource: docs/data/campus-photo-detail.json argo.roof.tree = (-37.25, 385.95), the SHIPPED ortho plan read of the courtyard crown under the old (+1.75, +4.15) registration. Carried as a reading because the corrected position is that read re-registered, not a new read.

grid.finStoreys.derivation: the five residential storeys over the one ground storey.

grid.module.derivation: eastFaceLength 37.401203 m (the GIS ring's east face, the ring campus-massing.js extrudes) / 30 bays. The shipped 1.28 m came from dividing the OSM ring's 38.5 m face, which is not the face that extrudes.

grid.parapetFrac.derivation: N18 px: storeyPitch F = (windowHeads[4] - windowHeads[0]) / 4 = (599 - 188) / 4 = 102.75; roof deck = soffitTop - 5F = 713 - 5 x 102.75 = 199.25; parapet = roofDeck - copingTop = 199.25 - 143 = 56.25 px; parapetFrac = 56.25 / 102.75 = 0.547445 F. Equivalently coping-to-soffit is 570 px = 5.547445 F.

grid.parapet.derivation: grid.parapetFrac 0.547445 x grid.floorToFloor 2.8 = 1.532846 m above the roof deck, STATED AS 1.53 m: the floor-to-floor it multiplies is an [estimated] 2.80 inside a 2.66-2.85 m band, and a +/-3.4 % input does not justify millimetres. Supersedes the shipped 1.2 m, which contradicted this facade's own coping-to-soffit ratio.

grid.groundStorey.derivation: massHeight 18.7 - (5 + parapetFrac 0.547445) x F 2.8 = 3.167154 m grade-to-soffit, STATED AS 3.17 m for the same reason as grid.parapet — and 3.17 + 5 x 2.8 + 1.53 still closes on 18.70 exactly. The ground storey is TALLER than a residential storey, which is what makes the recess a height a person can walk under; the shipped solve of six EQUAL storeys plus a 1.2 m parapet made it shorter.

system.bands.windowFrac.derivation: N18 px: fixed light (188 -> 248) = 60 px over the head-to-head storey interval 188 -> 291 = 103 px. All three sub-bands are read inside the SAME 103 px interval, so they are taken as fractions of that interval and fill the storey exactly.

system.bands.awningFrac.derivation: N18 px: awning/hopper sash (248 -> 268) = 20 px / 103 px.

system.awning.depth.derivation: bottom-hinged sash: openingHeight (awningFrac 0.194175 x F 2.8 = 0.5437 m) x sin(tilt 0.6) = 0.30699 m of projection, STATED AS 0.31 m — the sash height it comes from is a fraction of the [estimated] floor-to-floor. Supersedes the shipped bare 0.42.

system.awning.proud.derivation: the sash's centre sits half its own projection off the wall — exact arithmetic on the centimetre-stated depth, not inherited precision.

system.parapet.height.derivation: one figure, one value; the facade band and the roof parapet are the same object.

system.corner.pilasterWidth.derivation: system.corner.pilasterBays 1.2 x grid.module 1.246707 = 1.496048 m, STATED AS 1.50 m: the 1.2 bays is [estimated] and a widening read qualitatively off a photograph does not carry millimetres.

system.ground.height.derivation: the base wall runs the full grade-to-soffit height.

system.ground.baseWallRecess.derivation: the base wall is set back by the only reveal depth this facade carries.

court.bedroomsPerSuite.derivation: Vasquez Marshall's Blake page: 72 bedrooms / 12 suites = 6 bedrooms per suite. Same architect, same 2015-16 renovation, the sibling donut.

court.bedroomsPerLevel.derivation: Webcor: 180 student residences / 5 residential levels = 36 per level — identical to Blake's 72/2 = 36.

court.suitesPerLevel.derivation: 36 / 6 = 6 suites per level, 30 in the building.

court.galleries.derivation: one open-air access gallery per residential level, L2..L6, over the ground-level breezeway.

court.galleryBackWall.derivation: the developed length of the four court walls less the three core faces, straight off ring 1: I0 16.300307 + I1 16.400305 + I7 16.400305 + I2 4.2 + I6 4.2.

court.suiteSpacing.derivation: 57.500916 / 6 = 9.583486 m per suite door. The alternative reading, one door per BEDROOM, needs 1.60 m per door, which is narrower than the doors in webcor-argo-N9.jpg — rejected on arithmetic.

court.doorsPerLongWall.derivation: court.suitesPerLevel over the three long court walls (I0, I1, I7); the 4.2 m west legs are shorter than one suite frontage and carry none.

court.guard.height.derivation: IBC 2021 §1015.3 minimum 42 in x 0.0254 = 1.0668 m, inside N9's 1.05-1.10 m read of the picket rail.

court.guard.picketClear.derivation: IBC 2021 §1015.4: no opening may pass a 4 in sphere.

court.guard.picketPitch.derivation: the tightest pitch the code clearance allows.

court.guard.railSection.derivation: N9 reads the top, intermediate and bottom rails as roughly twice the picket.

court.guard.railLowHeight.derivation: the bottom rail sits one code sphere above the deck, which is the largest gap allowed there.

court.gallery.clear.derivation: IBC 2021 §1020.3 minimum corridor clear width, 44 in x 0.0254 = 1.1176 m.

court.gallery.beamThickness.derivation: derivations.readings.cmu.thicknessIn 8 in — the wall module the court is actually built of.

court.gallery.beamDepth.derivation: spandrelFrac 0.223301 x F 2.8 = 0.625243 m, STATED AS 0.625 m because F is [estimated]. The downstand edge beam is the band that reads as a stripe down the court in the 2008 aerial, and the deepest band this building sources is its own spandrel.

court.gallery.deckThickness.derivation: the gallery deck is built to the same 8 in module as the wall behind it.

court.gallery.projection.derivation: the clear walking width plus the downstand at its open edge.

court.cmu.length.derivation: 16 in x 0.0254 — running bond, bed joints legible in N9.

court.sconce.height.derivation: the sconce is mounted at the door head, which is the only height this wall sources.

court.plaque.size.derivation: N9 shows a small room-number plate but gives no dimension, so it is built one course square, the smallest module the wall itself provides.

court.plaque.height.derivation: ICC A117.1 §703.4: room-identification signs mounted with the baseline 60 in above the floor.

court.screen.width.derivation: the only sourced width in this gallery is the door leaf, and N9's slat panels read about two leaves wide.

court.screen.height.derivation: the screen fills what is left between the top of the guard and the underside of the beam above: 2.8 - 0.625 - 1.0668 = 1.1082 m. Two of the three inputs are centimetre-stated, so the figure is good to about a centimetre and no better.

court.screen.slatPitch.derivation: the slats are pitched on the wall's own module.

court.screen.slats.derivation: 1.8288 m of screen at the 0.2032 m course pitch = 9 slats.

court.screen.slatSection.derivation: the slats are the same stock as the rails.

court.floor.cell.derivation: no source shows the court floor, so it is laid out on the building's own derived bay module rather than an invented paving pattern.

court.floor.area.derivation: shoelace of ring 1 = the court floor, the roof plate's hole, 216.695 m^2.

court.tree.x.derivation: the shipped ortho plan read re-registered: -37.25 - priorDx 1.75 + dx 0.93.

court.tree.z.derivation: the shipped ortho plan read re-registered: 385.95 - priorDz 4.15 + dz 3.78.

exempt.roof.curbs.items: Ten mechanical-curb plan positions read off the 2026 ortho and re-registered here from (+1.75, +4.15) to (+0.93, +3.78). Each is a MEASURED PLAN READ, not a dimension; the registration that moves them is in reads[] and the test recomputes every item from the shipped predecessor and the two registration figures.
exempt.roof.westRecess.x0: The dark roof recess west of the court: an ortho PLAN READ, re-registered here by the same (+0.93, +3.78) correction as the curbs, and recomputed corner by corner in the test from the shipped predecessor and the two registration figures. A plan position, not a dimension.
exempt.roof.westRecess.x1: As roof.westRecess.x0 — the same re-registered ortho plan read, recomputed by the test from the shipped predecessor and the registration.
exempt.roof.westRecess.z0: As roof.westRecess.x0 — the same re-registered ortho plan read, recomputed by the test from the shipped predecessor and the registration.
exempt.roof.westRecess.z1: As roof.westRecess.x0 — the same re-registered ortho plan read, recomputed by the test from the shipped predecessor and the registration.
exempt.ground.north: The north-entry boardwalk, planter and bench, read off the Nov 2024 photosphere and carried UNCHANGED. Two of its figures are known WRONG and are flagged rather than guessed: the same frame shows a bench running the full open edge of the planting bed (order 8-10 m against the shipped 2.6 m) and a raised bed carrying two mature trees and a shrub understorey (order 10 x 3 m against the shipped 3.0 x 1.4 m). A 640 x 400 oblique cannot replace them with numbers, so they stay flagged in absent[] and conflicts[] until a higher-resolution capture exists. Better a declared error than an invented correction.
exempt.court.tree.x: The courtyard tree's plan position: a re-registered ortho read, derived in figures[] and named here as well because an (x, z) pair is a POSITION and not a dimension of the building. The test checks separately that it now falls inside ring 1, which is the whole correction.
exempt.court.tree.z: As court.tree.x — the same re-registered ortho plan read, derived in figures[] and checked against ring 1 rather than against a dimension.
exempt.court.faces: The eight court elevations. Every `a` and `b` is a VERBATIM vertex of campus-arcgis massing[99] ring 1 at decimetres/10 and the test deepEquals the whole list against the survey; `out` is a unit normal pointing into the open court; `length` is the distance between those two survey vertices, recomputed by the test; `doors` and `coreDoors` are counts distributed from court.doorsPerLongWall, which IS derived. No dimension of this building is stated here.
exempt.system.colonnade: The one sourced ground colonnade opening. Its x span is ground.north.boardwalk's own measured extent, carried verbatim, because the Nov 2024 photosphere frames the boardwalk and the colonnade behind it in a single shot; `spans` is round(width / (columnSpacingBays x module)) and the test recomputes it. Nothing here is an independent figure.
exempt.court.mural: A RECORDED, UNBUILT block. `painted` is a year, and `framedWidth`/`framedHeight` are the photograph's own frame converted by its measured 31.92 px bed-joint pitch at 8 in coursing — the derivation is written out in court.mural.note and recomputed by the test. Nothing in this block is drawn, so none of it is a dimension of the model.

estimates.why: The ultra standard's third tier. Each entry is a figure no rung of the ladder resolved — labelled [estimated], recording the sourced pattern of THIS building that it extends, replaced the day a real source turns up. A legacy retention is an estimate too: where a revision corrects only the evidence that changed, the untouched figure is recorded here as retained rather than re-invented. SINCE THE R2 ARBITRATION (S1 ii) EVERY ENTRY ALSO CARRIES A MACHINE-READABLE `band: [lo, hi]` and the SHIPPED value is asserted inside it by tests/helpers/axiom-gate.mjs, because prose is not a band and R1 shipped grid.floorToFloor able to reach 2.25 m — 0.41 m outside the band this section itself published — with every gate passing. `bandWhy` states what the band excludes. Where the section or a code clause bounds a figure, that bound IS the band edge; where the only evidence is a qualitative read of a frame that does not measure the thing, the band is the half-to-double range such a read supports, which is a statement of how little is known and is never to be widened to make a value fit.

grid.floorToFloor.extends: derivations.figures['grid.parapetFrac'] and the N18 pixel scale: 46.6 px = 1.246707 m gives 37.3785 px/m, so F = 102.75 / that = 2.7489 m, with a 2.66-2.85 m band over the +/-1-bay count uncertainty (module 1.207-1.290 m)
grid.floorToFloor.why: [estimated] 2.80 m, the research dossier's recommended working value inside the MEASURED 2.66-2.85 m band. The pixel solve alone gives 2.7489 m; no drawing exists to pick a point inside the band, so the value is declared rather than presented as measured. It is the whole band that is sourced. A 3.048 m (10 ft) floor-to-floor is RULED OUT by this solve: it leaves a 1.46 m ground storey, which no one can walk under.
grid.floorToFloor.bandWhy: THE SECTION'S OWN PUBLISHED BAND, not a new one: the N18 bay-count scale puts the storey pitch at 2.7489 m and the +/-1-bay count uncertainty (module 1.207-1.290 m) carries it to 2.66-2.85 m. 3.048 m (10 ft) is outside it and is ruled out by the solve; 2.25 m is 0.41 m outside it and is not a value this section can reach.

reads.why: Figures taken directly off a named frame, survey or code clause with the tolerance that source supports. These are citations, not derivations: the test pins them as literals, because changing one changes what the source is claimed to say.

grid.storeys.source: Webcor: six levels above grade; campus-arcgis massing[99].levels = 6; and five window bands over one ground storey counted down N18's east elevation. Three independent sources, one answer.

grid.longFaceBays.source: webcor-argo-N18.jpg pier-peak count across the storey-3 window band: 31 module pitches over 1440 px at 46.6 px each, i.e. 30 bays per outer elevation. A COUNT is foreshortening-immune; the metre module is this count divided into the surveyed face.

system.window.widthFrac.source: webcor-argo-N18.jpg, opening measured pier-to-pier against the 46.6 px bay module — the window is about 0.68 of the bay. Argo's is the NARROW window; Blake's glazed panel is a different system.

system.parapet.jointEveryBays.source: webcor-argo-N18.jpg — precast panel joints at roughly every 2 bays across the parapet band.

court.sconce.size.source: webcor-argo-N9.jpg — a white rectangular wall luminaire beside each unit door, roughly 0.35 m, throwing up and down.

roof.registration.dx.source: derivations.readings.ortho — four agreeing features, two of them interior to the court and therefore immune to the sun-angle bias that killed the south edge.

roof.registration.dz.source: derivations.readings.ortho — same four features; the two interior rims agree with the two accepted outer edges to 0.01 m in x and 0.11 m in z.

roof.membrane.jointSpacing.source: docs/data/textures/chunk_4_6.jpg (2026 ortho): a fine expansion-joint grid at roughly 3 m across the membrane.

roof.membrane.stains.count.source: 2026 ortho: heavy grey and pink-brown patch staining across the membrane; fourteen patches counted.

roof.membrane.stains.minR.source: 2026 ortho: the smallest counted stain patch reads about 1.2 m across the short axis.

roof.membrane.stains.maxR.source: 2026 ortho: the largest counted stain patch reads about 3.4 m.

roof.coping.width.source: 2026 ortho: a raised pale band about 0.5 m wide with an outer shadow line, around BOTH the outer perimeter and the court rim. This is the same 0.5 m that makes the parapet band 9.6 % of the plate in derivations.readings.survey.massHeightSource.

ground.plankWidth.source: .cache/qa/revelle/sv/argo.jpg — Google photosphere, Mass Interact, Nov 2024: the timber boardwalk runs in narrow planks with open joints, reading about 0.14 m wide.

draw.why: Render offsets and texture repeats, not dimensions. Nothing here is a claim about the building: they exist so coplanar surfaces resolve in depth, so no terrain triangle runs through a face, and so the material library tiles at a sane density. They are declared here rather than left as literals in the module, and the test checks the module carries no numeric geometry of its own.

grid.solve: 18.70 = groundStorey 3.167154 + 5 x floorToFloor 2.8 + parapet 1.532846 — zero residual by construction, against the LiDAR massHeights read of the ring campus-massing.js extrudes. SUPERSEDES the shipped '18.7 = 6 x 2.9167 + 1.2', which made six EQUAL storeys under a 1.2 m parapet: the facade's own coping-to-soffit ratio (5.547445 F, measured in N18) says the ground storey is TALLER than a residential storey and the parapet is taller than 1.2 m. Both corrections come from that one measurement.
grid.anchorNote: [estimated] The inventory anchored Argo on the repo's 3.05 m dorm floor-to-floor, an ASSUMPTION with no drawing behind it, and the previous build derived ~2.92 m by dividing 18.7 by six equal storeys. Both are superseded: the N18 elevation measures the coping-to-soffit distance at 5.547445 storey pitches, which fixes the SHAPE of the stack, and a bay-count scale puts the storey pitch at 2.75 m with a 2.66-2.85 m band. A 3.048 m (10 ft) floor-to-floor is ruled out — it leaves a 1.46 m ground storey. The 3.05 m figure stays declared so a future drawing can referee. Bay COUNTS and per-bay ratios are foreshortening-immune and are what this section builds from.
grid.bayNote: 30 bays measured across a full elevation (webcor-argo-N18.jpg pier-peak count, foreshortening-immune). Module = the GIS ring's east face 37.401203 m / 30 = 1.246707 m, superseding the shipped 1.28 m, which divided the OSM ring's 38.5 m face — a ring that is not the one campus-massing.js extrudes. CONFLICT DECLARED and carried in conflicts[]: the inventory's anchor-immune bay:floor ratio (Argo 0.435 vs Blake 0.618, 'the single most important difference between the two buildings') is contradicted by the count-over-ring derivation, and this session's N18 pitch measurement is a THIRD read that lands Argo at 46.6 / 102.75 = 0.453 — close to the counts and far from the claimed 1.4x Argo/Blake difference. Counts win for now; the losing ratios stay on the record.

facades.source: .cache/qa/revelle/sv/argo.jpg (Google photosphere, Mass Interact, Nov 2024) — the north entry: recessed colonnade with square columns and a deep flat soffit, people walking under it, the timber boardwalk, corten planter and bench in front. Endpoints are ring-0 vertices; this is the one outer face where the ground COLONNADE is sourced, and its extent is taken from the measured boardwalk it stands behind.

webcor-argo-N18.jpg (near-orthographic east elevation, c.2015-16) and webcor-argo-N17-p3200.jpg (SE corner). Every pixel reading in derivations.readings.px comes off this face. Ground condition: a SOLID pale panelled base wall behind a low white planter wall and clipped hedge run, with a recess at the north end toward the Argo-Blake gap.

webcor-argo-N17-p3200.jpg, ground crop — a SOLID pale panelled base wall for the whole photographed length with the planter wall and hedge in front and a lava-rock retaining wall at the west end. NOT a colonnade: this frame is what refutes the shipped continuous peristyle.

[estimated] — rear/service face; the ladder was exhausted (photos, Street View, drone, planning docs, archives) and only psphere-2024-11-argo-WEST-oblique-b185.png exists, at an oblique. The standard bay module is extended from the three sourced faces, which all carry the identical system. NO entrance and NO service door is invented: whether one exists is genuinely unknown, and whether the base wall is punched anywhere on this face is unknown too.

window.note: the opening is 0.68 of the bay, measured pier-to-pier against the 46.6 px module [read, N18]. Argo's is the NARROW window, not Blake's glazed panel.

bands.note: fixed light 0.582524, awning/hopper sash 0.194175, spandrel 0.223301 — all three read inside the SAME 103 px head-to-head interval of N18 and therefore fractions of it, summing to exactly 1. Supersedes the shipped 0.58 / 0.13 / 0.29, whose window was right and whose awning was 0.065 too thin and spandrel 0.068 too deep; they also summed to 1, which is why nothing caught it. The head-to-floor offset within the storey is NOT resolved by any frame, so the three bands are stacked from the floor line.

cant.note: The fins are canted precast window surrounds, not flat blades [sourced, N17's oblique, where the whole elevation reads as a sawtooth]: each opening sits in a frame whose vertical reveals splay outward, one lit and one shadowed face per bay. Built as two opposed splayed reveal planes. Webcor calls this restoring the exterior concrete fins to their original design intent. ANGLE, DEPTH AND THICKNESS ARE ALL [estimated] and retained unchanged — no frame measures the splay.

awning.note: bottom-hinged sash below each window, several standing open in both Webcor frames. The projection is now DERIVED from the sash's own height and the estimated opening angle rather than carried as a bare number.

parapet.note: plain parapet band 1.532846 m derived from the facade's own coping-to-soffit ratio, with a thin projecting drip cap and precast panel joints at roughly every 2 bays [read, N18]. This is the SAME object as roof.coping's parapet: the roof deck is 1.532846 m below the 18.70 m coping plane, and everything on the roof sits on the deck, not on the coping.

corner.note: wider blank pilaster return at the corners and a small projecting bracket at every floor line — the stack of five cantilevered blocks resolved at the SE corner in N17. The pilaster is now WIDER than a bay, which is what the source says; the shipped 1.0 m was narrower than the derived 1.2467 m bay and contradicted it.

ground.note: THE GROUND STOREY IS NOT A CONTINUOUS COLONNADE. The shipped section recessed the whole perimeter behind square columns at every third bay; webcor-argo-N17-p3200.jpg contradicts that over the south face's full photographed length — the base is a SOLID pale panelled wall roughly 3 m tall with large panel joints, fronted by a low white planter wall and a continuous clipped hedge, with a deep flat fascia oversailing it. N18 shows the same wall-and-hedge condition along most of the east face. The colonnade is real at the NORTH ENTRY (the Nov 2024 photosphere) and at the breezeway through to the court (UC Regents 2008 p11), so the model is a solid base wall PUNCHED at the entries. The north opening is set to the extent of the MEASURED boardwalk it stands behind, which is the only plan datum any source gives it; the breezeway's position on the ring is unresolved and it is not built. The recess behind the columns is the photographed near-black VOID, built as a matte opaque plane so lighting cannot lift it into a pale striped screen.

colonnade.note: The one sourced colonnade opening. Its extent is DERIVED, not placed: the Nov 2024 photosphere frames the boardwalk and the colonnade behind it in one shot, so the opening runs the measured boardwalk's own x span -52 to -40 (ground.north.boardwalk, carried verbatim). Column count = round(width / (columnSpacingBays x module)) + 1 = 4, evenly across the opening.

court.note: THE 78.20 m OF ELEVATION THE MODEL HAS NEVER HAD. Argo's court is single-loaded open-air GALLERY ACCESS over painted running-bond CMU — a completely different structural and material system from the outer precast sawtooth, and it always was. webcor-argo-N9.jpg settles it: an open unit door and its window look onto a gallery with a guardrail, a white painted-CMU back wall, a bronze door, a sconce, a room-number plate, a white soffit with a projecting downstand edge beam, slat screens, and a facing gallery beyond. UC Regents 2008 p11 corroborates it seven years earlier, in the dead blue epoch, with two stacked galleries over a ground-level breezeway. Webcor's 'new interior and exterior railings at all balconies' names the same object: Argo has no balconies on its outer elevations. DO NOT extend the outer sawtooth into the court and do not extend the gallery onto the outer faces — they are two systems and both are sourced.

guard.note: White-painted vertical picket guard: closely spaced round pickets between a top rail, an intermediate rail and a bottom rail [sourced, N9]. Every dimension is a code clause rather than a guess — 42 in height, no opening passing a 4 in sphere — and the code height falls inside N9's own 1.05-1.10 m read. The 2008 dark mesh infill is a dead epoch: Webcor replaced the railings at all balconies in 2015-16.

gallery.note: Five stacked open-air galleries, L2 to L6, running the full inner loop of ring 1 so the lift lobby on the core's east face has gallery access at every level. Each carries a white painted-CMU back wall, a deck, a projecting downstand edge beam at the open edge, and a white-painted vertical picket guard. THE DECK AT INDEX s IS ALSO THE SOFFIT OF THE GALLERY BELOW, so five galleries need SIX deck-and-beam pairs and the top gallery is ceilinged by a sixth pair at the roof deck — 48 decks over eight faces, not 40. The R1 revision emitted five and left the top gallery's doors, screens, sconces, plaques, pickets and rails standing under open sky around the whole 78.20 m court loop; the section's own arithmetic proved it unintended, because court.screen.height reserves the beam depth at a level whose beam was never built. Only the deck and the beam run to the sixth pass: the CMU back wall, the guard, the doors, the screens, the sconces and the plaques stop at five, because the extra pair is a ceiling and not a new gallery. GROUND LEVEL CARRIES NO GALLERY: the 2008 frame shows an open breezeway there, and its position on the ring is unresolved, so the base condition ships closed and absent[] says so. THE GALLERY'S DEPTH IS THE SINGLE WEAKEST FIGURE IN THIS BLOCK — no source measures it, so it is built at the IBC minimum corridor clear width, 1.1176 m, the smallest value the photographed gallery can lawfully be. It under-claims deliberately.

cmu.note: painted concrete masonry in running bond with legible bed joints [sourced, N9]. The 8 in course is not assumed: it is the only coursing that makes the El Mac mural's framed width equal a surveyed wall on this building.

door.note: Flush dark bronze/brown unit door with a lever handle and an electronic card reader on the jamb, widely spaced with long blank CMU runs between [sourced, N9]. Six per gallery level at 9.583486 m centres, two on each of the three long court walls; the west legs are shorter than one suite frontage and carry none. The core's east face carries one lift-lobby door per level. Leaf size is the IBC minimum.

sconce.note: a white rectangular wall luminaire beside each door, throwing up and down [read, N9], mounted at the door head.

plaque.note: the small orange/tan room-number plate beside each unit door [sourced, N9]; sized at one CMU course square, the smallest module the wall itself provides, and mounted at the A117.1 sign height.

screen.note: White vertical-slat / louvred panels hung between gallery levels [sourced, N9]. The ELEMENT is sourced; the RHYTHM is not, so one screen per long court wall per level is built, midway between that wall's two sourced doors, and absent[] records that no frame shows the real rhythm.

floor.note: THE WORST LIVE FAULT IN THE SHIPPED SECTION WAS THAT THIS DID NOT EXIST. The extruded well runs from the roof down to baseY = lowest - 1.5, below grade, so from any court opening you saw through the planet. The floor is now laid over ring 1 (216.695 m^2, the hole minus nothing, because ring 1 already follows the core's three faces) on the campus-overlay 'pad' rung above campus-terrain's surfaceAt — the height of the DRAWN triangle, never heightAt. It is laid as cells on the building's own bay module, each seated on its own local surface, so it follows the drawn ground instead of hovering over it at one datum. Its MATERIAL AND FINISH ARE [estimated]: no frame in the set shows the court floor at all.

tree.note: A persistent courtyard tree: the 2008 aerial resolves a tree in this court and the 2026 ortho resolves a crown in the same place. It stands ON THE COURT FLOOR, 18.70 m below where the shipped section drew it — the shipped 'emergent crown on the roof plane' was a consequence of the false lid. Plan position is the ortho read re-registered; height and crown radius are [estimated] and retained unchanged, because the elevation was wrong, not the size.

This is the one court face a photograph is tied to, and every other face extends it.
