mural.note: RESOLVED BUT DELIBERATELY UNRENDERED. Subject: a woman's head seen from below, looking up, both hands raised to shade her eyes, in El Mac's concentric-line and stippled-dot modelling, over soft blue cloud forms with a pale sea-and-horizon band across the bottom-left; a cool near-monochrome blue-grey palette with one small warm accent where the hands cross the brow. Scale is DERIVED, not assumed: the bed joints of the wall it is painted on scan an exactly regular 31.92 px over 13 intervals, and at 8 in coursing the frame is 6.51 m wide by 9.17 m tall (45.1 courses, about 3.3 storeys). 6.51 m is the court core's surveyed 6.5 m to within 0.01 m, and no other surface on this building is 6.5 m wide; 16 in coursing would give 13.0 m and 12 in would give 9.77 m, and neither exists here. IT IS NOT BUILT, for two independent reasons that each suffice: the photograph may not become a texture map under this zone's own rule that texture maps are code-generated and never photo pixels, and a procedurally approximated version of a specific, attributed artwork by a LIVING ARTIST is worse than an honest absence. The palette above is recorded so a future decision has the data, and it is NOT in colors[] because nothing draws it.

signage.position: parapet band, top-left / north end of the east elevation
signage.note: recorded [measured], not rendered — lettering needs a texture pass this module does not do

roof.source: The 2026 Google ortho chunk_4_6.jpg (z20, 8 px/m), registered to the DRAWN mass by the four-feature edge fit in derivations.readings.ortho: correction (+0.93, +3.78) m [measured plan]. SUPERSEDES the shipped (+1.75, +4.15), which was a plate-centre alignment that does not reproduce and put every plan feature ~0.82 m too far east and ~0.37 m too far south. NO oblique or drone view of this roof exists, so every HEIGHT here is [estimated] and declared. THE ROOF DECK IS NOT AT 18.70 m: 18.70 is the top of the parapet coping, and the membrane, the curbs and the west recess sit 1.532846 m below it.
roof.lidNote: THE ROOF-PLANE LID OVER ARGO'S COURT WAS INVENTED AND IS DELETED. The premise it stood on — 'The measured extrusion is SOLID, so the well and everything in it is a roof-plane read' — is false: campus-arcgis.json massing[99] carries two rings and campus-massing.js:826 already extrudes the second as a hole. Five independent sources agree the court is open: the survey's second ring; Webcor's published 74,836 sf, which the donut reproduces to +2.1 % and a solid prism misses by +20.8 %; the UC Regents 2008-11-18 deck p5 aerial, in which stacked galleries are legible down the court's east wall; the 2026 Google ortho, in which the court reads as a shadowed shaft and the survey notch is reproduced on three sides to better than 0.15 m; and Webcor N9, an open unit door looking onto the court gallery. Deleted with the premise: the dark void decal, the kerb ring across the opening, the 0.5 m 'core' bump and its 0.3 m south wing, the trellis strip, and the roof-plane tree. The court's floor now goes at surfaceAt; the core is the already-extruded full-height notch; the tree stands on the court floor, 18.70 m below where it was drawn. NOTHING replaces the lid: there is no roof over Argo's court.

deckGate.why: THE DRAWN MASS HAS NO ROOF RECESS, so nothing that stands on Argo's roof DECK can be drawn (visual round 2, 2026-08-21). THE ARITHMETIC: campus-massing.js extrudes the GIS ring FLAT to campus-lidar.json heights['Argo Hall'] = 18.70 m, which this section measures as the top of the PARAPET COPING and not the deck; the deck is grid.parapet = 1.532846 m below it. On the drawn terrain that is roofElevation 42.57 m for the mass top against 41.04 m for the deck, so the membrane, its stains, the ten curbs and the west recess were every one of them being built 1.53 m INSIDE a solid extrusion. THIS IS NOT THE REGRESSION IT LOOKED LIKE. The round-2 critic read Argo's roof as one unbroken white plane and diagnosed the R1 surgery as having taken the roof furniture out with the false lid. It did not: all ten curbs, the west recess, the membrane and the stains are still built, still registered at (+0.93, +3.78) and still court-rim clipped — the white plane the render shows is the MASSING's own top cap at 42.57 m, drawn over them. What changed at R1 was the deck DATUM: R1 established that 18.70 is the coping plane, which is a correct finding and which is what put the deck inside the mass. INVISIBLE AND INTERSECTING is the pair blake.level4 is withheld for, and this is withheld for the same pair. AND THE OTHER ROAD IS CLOSED TOO: standing the same furniture on the drawn 18.70 m plane would put a 0.45 m curb core 0.45 m ABOVE the measured LiDAR maximum for this mass, which is exactly the ceiling blake.roof.anchorGate refuses to cross, and it would be a 1.53 m lie about where Argo's roof is. Both readings fail, so the RECORD is kept complete — plans, registration, clip rule, tones, heights and their tiers all unchanged and still gated — and nothing is drawn. STILL DRAWN, because they belong at the coping plane rather than on the deck: roof.coping's band around both the outer perimeter and the court rim, and the court parapet. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: a stepped top for the drawn mass, which is campus-massing.js's to give and not this section's to take. See conflicts['flat-topped-mass'] and absent[].

membrane.note: weathered white single-ply with heavy grey and pink-brown patch staining and a fine expansion-joint grid at about 3 m [measured plan, ortho]. Drawn as the procedural roofMembrane class (code-generated) plus hash-scattered stain decals; the ortho feeds ONLY the colours, never its pixels. The membrane is clipped to the roof PLATE — the outer ring less the court hole — because there is no roof over the court.

coping.note: a raised pale band with an outer shadow line around BOTH the outer perimeter and the court rim [measured plan, ortho]. Its 0.5 m width is the figure that makes the parapet band 9.6 % of the plate and so identifies 18.70 m as the coping plane. The PARAPET is grid.parapet, 1.532846 m; the 0.35 m here is the coping CAP standing proud at its top, which is what the shipped 'coping.height' always was.

curbs.note: 10 square mechanical curbs with dark centres, four of them on the court-rim corners and six across the field [measured plan, ortho], re-registered to (+0.93, +3.78); heights [estimated] and declared in absent[]. `core` 0 means the whole unit reads dark; core >= s means the dark centre IS the unit.
curbs.clipNote: NOTHING MAY HOVER, and deleting the lid took the floor out from under one of these. Nine of the ten re-registered curbs sit wholly on the plate; the curb at the court's north-east rim overhangs it, because the ortho read is a plan position for a curb the survey rim cuts through. It is TRIMMED BACK TO THE RIM along the axis of least intrusion — here the x axis, by 0.42 m of a 2.4 m unit — so the three read edges that are genuinely on the plate keep their measured positions and only the overhang goes. The rule is stated rather than the trimmed number, so a re-registration re-derives it; campus-photo-argo.js applies it and the test checks the BUILT footprints against ring 1, not the declared ones.

westRecess.note: a dark recess in the roof plate west of the court, with a pale kerb along its west and south edges [measured plan, ortho], re-registered to (+0.93, +3.78); depth is a decal read and the kerb height is [estimated].

north.source: Google Maps photosphere Nov 2024 — post-2015 landscape work at Argo's north entry

ground.eastNote: The sourced east-frontage planter wall, clipped hedge and bike-rack run are NOT built — see absent[]. The shipped staging route passes 1.6-2.3 m off the measured east face and no source measures the planter's plan standoff; placed anywhere plausible it would obstruct the route.
ground.racksNote: CROSS-FINDING, RECORDED FOR ARBITRATION, NOT ACTED ON HERE. Legacy revelle.racks places eleven rack items at z = 362.5 along Argo's north side, on 2.2 m centres from x -53 to -31; seven of them fall inside ground.north.boardwalk (x -52..-40, z 361.2..365.2) and the one at x -48.6 sits 0.67 m from the centre of the 2.6 m bench, which is an outright overlap. THE NEWEST GROUND-LEVEL SOURCE SETTLES IT AS A POSITIVE OBSERVATION, NOT AN EPOCH TIEBREAK: the Nov 2024 photosphere frames the whole north entry — boardwalk, planting bed, gravel apron and colonnade — and there is not one bike hoop anywhere in it. The racks did not disappear, though: brightened and resampled over the Argo-Blake gap the 2026 ortho shows two back-to-back rows of uniformly raked bright slashes at z ~355.5 and ~358.0 running roughly x -59 to -33, which reads as double-sided angle parking, corroborated by the dense mass of parked bicycles N17 shows in that gap in 2015-16. The recommendation is to MOVE the run to two rows at z 355.5 / 358.0 spanning x -59..-33 tiered [measured, ortho 2026, LOW CONFIDENCE] — 8 px/m in building shadow is a reading, not a certification — with the conservative alternative being to drop only the seven items at x -53..-39.8, which needs none of the ortho interpretation. The 2026 ortho is a VERIFIED NEGATIVE for the boardwalk itself and must not be cited either way on it: Argo's roof plate is displaced 3.78 m north, so its north edge lands at z 362.59 in image coordinates and the building leans over its own forecourt. revelle.racks is not this section's file and nothing here touches it.

counts.note: CURBS IS ZERO, and that is the declaration, not an omission: the ten curbs are MEASURED and their record is intact in roof.curbs.items, but the roof deck they stand on is 1.532846 m inside the flat-topped drawn mass, so none of them is built — see roof.deckGate, conflicts and absent[]. The membrane, its stains and the west recess are withheld with them and were never counted here. Terrain-independent counts only. The base-wall runs, the court floor cells and the north colonnade's columns are SOLVED against the survey ring and the measured boardwalk extent, so the test recomputes them from the same inputs rather than trusting the numbers here.

conflicts: THE DRAWN MASS IS FLAT-TOPPED AND ARGO'S ROOF IS NOT (visual round 2, 2026-08-21). Argo's real top is a step: a parapet whose coping tops out at 18.70 m over a roof DECK 1.532846 m below it, at 17.167154 m. The DRAWN mass is a flat extrusion of one ring to one height, and campus-massing.js extrudes it to 18.70 m — the coping plane — so the drawn building has a solid top exactly where the real building has an open deck. SIDE ONE, the measurement: grid.solve puts 18.70 = groundStorey 3.167154 + 5 x 2.8 + parapet 1.532846 with zero residual, against the coping-to-soffit ratio measured on webcor-argo-N18.jpg, and roof.source states outright that the membrane, the curbs and the west recess sit 1.532846 m below 18.70. SIDE TWO, the drawn massing: one ring, one height, no mechanism for a recessed deck, and not this section's file to edit. NOT AVERAGED AND NOT FAKED. The deck is not raised to the coping plane to make it visible — that would be a 1.53 m lie about where Argo's roof is, and it would put a 0.45 m curb core above the measured LiDAR maximum, which is the ceiling blake.roof.anchorGate refuses. The deck furniture is WITHHELD with its record complete: see roof.deckGate for the arithmetic and absent[] for what is not drawn. This is the same conflict blake carries as conflicts['flat-topped-mass'], on the sibling building, from the same cause, and the two are now resolved the same way. Arbitration should decide whether the Revelle masses gain stepped tops; until they do, both roofs are honestly bare.

BAY COUNT vs BAY:STOREY RATIO. The inventory's anchor-immune ratio calls Argo 0.435 and Blake 0.618 and names it 'the single most important difference between the two buildings'. Dividing the measured 30-bay count into the surveyed rings lands Argo at 1.2467 m and Blake at about 1.23 m — Blake slightly NARROWER, not 1.4x wider. This session's N18 pitch measurement is a third, independent read and gives 46.6 px / 102.75 px = 0.453, which agrees with the counts. Counts win for now because they and the ring are the two strongest reads. The losing ratios stay on the record for a drawing to referee; they are NOT averaged with anything.

CONSTRUCTION DATE 1966 vs 1967 vs 1968. Three dates are on record and none is confirmable on the open web today. Vasquez Marshall's own Blake page says Blake was 'originally constructed in 1968', and Blake and Argo are siblings. The most likely reconciliation is DESIGN vs OCCUPANCY — a 1967 design and drawing date against a 1968 first-occupancy date — but that is a reading, not a source, and it is written here as a reading. The 'Tucker, Sadler & Bennett, 1967' attribution in label is an INHERITED claim from the inventory, demoted here to unverified. NO GEOMETRY DEPENDS ON ANY OF IT.

PUBLISHED AREA vs SURVEYED AREA. Webcor publishes 74,836 sf; the donut's six levels over the surveyed plate give 76,377 sf, +2.1 %. The residual is ordinary gross-area convention — the survey ring is the outer wall face and published gsf is usually measured to it, less light-well subtractions already made. Declared rather than reconciled, because the important number here is the comparison: a solid prism gives 90,372 sf, +20.8 %, and no convention accounts for that.

LiDAR 18.4 (OSM ring) vs 18.7 (GIS ring). The same 2014 flight over two different polygons. 18.4 is a valid number over the wrong ring: the OSM ring overhangs the roof by about 1.0 m on north and west, so ground returns drag its high percentile down. 18.7, over the ring campus-massing.js extrudes, is the number the facade closes against. Both are carried; neither is averaged. campus-arcgis's h = 18.3 is a FORMULA (6 x 3.050) and is not in this comparison at all, and campus-3d's OSM h = 22.8 is the levels fallback that once stacked the shell a storey past the drawn roof — it stays dead.

N18's TWO SPAN READS DO NOT RECONCILE. The parapet band is read corner-to-corner at 1415 px = 30.4 modules, and the first-pier-to-last-pier run at 1440 px = 31 modules. A corner-to-corner span cannot be SHORTER than the pier run it contains. Both readings are recorded in derivations.readings.px and NEITHER is used to derive a metre — in particular the corner pilaster's width is an [estimated] 1.2 bays extending the qualitative 'wider than a bay' read rather than the arithmetic these two numbers would give.

THE RESEARCH DOSSIER'S ROUNDED FIGURES vs ITS OWN ARITHMETIC. research-argo.md recommends parapet 1.53 m and ground storey 3.16 m. Recomputed from its own pixel table those are 1.532847 m and 3.167153 m: the dossier rounded the storey pitch to 102.8 px where (599 - 188) / 4 is 102.75. The ARITHMETIC WINS and the shipped figures are the recomputed ones, exactly as the Keeling bar requires. The same applies to the band splits: the dossier's 0.583 / 0.195 / 0.222 come from dividing by the mean pitch, but all three sub-bands are read inside the same 103 px head-to-head interval, so they are fractions of THAT and sum to exactly 1.

LEGACY RACK POSITION 2012 vs 2026 ORTHO. revelle.racks reads one row at z 362.5; the current evidence puts two rows at z 355.5 and 358.0, on Blake's side of the gap. This is a position error of about 5 m, not an epoch casualty — the same object, seen in a different year and on the wrong side of a courtyard. Recorded in ground.racksNote for arbitration; revelle.racks is not this section's file and is untouched.

THE NOV 2024 PHOTOSPHERE IS CITED BUT NOT CACHED. Nineteen of this section's hexes are attributed to a Google photosphere that exists in this repo only as a prose reference and as one 640 x 400 QA capture. The hexes are carried UNCHANGED rather than re-sampled or replaced, because a new value would be a new claim on a source nobody can re-open. This is the same failure mode as the shipped sources[] entry for vmarch-bradley_vma_argo_7a.jpg, a file whose page 404s today. Cache the frame, then re-cite it.
absent: West/rear entrance or service door — no frontal source exists; the ladder was climbed to the top and only an oblique photosphere covers this face. The standard bay module is extended [estimated] from the three sourced faces but NO door is invented, and whether the ground base wall is punched anywhere on the west is unknown too.

EL MAC'S 'AN ENDURING SPELL' — RESOLVED, AND DELIBERATELY UNRENDERED. This entry no longer withholds the mural for want of a frame, a palette or a location: the artist's own blog (mac-arte.blogspot.com, posted 2016-03-23) names the work, places it at the interior courtyard of Argo Hall, and serves two images now cached in this repo; the work is signed ELMAC MMXV, so it was painted 2015 and published 2016. Subject, five-hex palette, and a 6.51 x 9.17 m framed size derived from the wall's own 8 in CMU coursing are all recorded under court.mural. What remains unresolved is WHICH core face carries it — I5 (6.50 m) or I3 (6.40 m), the only two surfaces on this building of that width — and the height of its base above the court floor. It is NOT BUILT for two independent reasons, either of which suffices: this zone forbids photo pixels as texture maps, and a procedural approximation of a specific attributed artwork by a living artist is worse than an honest absence.

SUPERSEDED, KEPT IN THE RECORD — 'Courtyard / light-well interior: access galleries, dark metal railings, glazed central block on pilotis, exit signs — inside the solid measured extrusion; only the roof-plane read of the well is built.' That entry rested on the false premise that the extrusion is solid. The court is open, the galleries and their guards are now BUILT from webcor-argo-N9.jpg and UC Regents 2008 p5/p11, and the 'glazed central block on pilotis' was a mis-read of the full-height notch core, which the survey has carried all along. See superseded[] and roof.lidNote. Two things the old entry named are still absent and are listed separately below: the exit signs (no text mechanism in this repo) and the ground-level breezeway.

East-frontage low white planter wall, clipped hedge and bike-rack run — sourced in webcor-argo-N18.jpg, but no source measures their plan standoff and the shipped staging route passes 1.6-2.3 m off the measured east face; placed anywhere plausible they would obstruct the route. The SOLID BASE WALL behind them is now built, because it is on the building line and cannot foul the route. Better absent than wrong. The rack run is separately the subject of a cross-finding — see ground.racksNote.

Dark globe-headed and cantilever-head lamp posts — Zone 1 lamps are the plaza section's; not double-built here. The Nov 2024 photosphere also shows a dark cylindrical bollard light at the planting bed's corner and a tall dark lamp post on the boardwalk, and both belong to the same owner.

The TWO mature plane/sycamore-type trees in the north boardwalk planter — trees are LiDAR/plaza-owned; the planter is built, its trees are not. Corrected from ONE tree to TWO: the Nov 2024 photosphere plainly frames two mature trees with a shrub understorey in the raised corten bed.
'ARGO HALL' parapet lettering — position, face and cap height are recorded under signage; this repo has no text rendering mechanism and must not grow one for a building name.

Roof mechanical curb HEIGHTS — plan positions are measured off the ortho tiles and re-registered, but no source gives heights. NO oblique, drone or Street View image of Argo's roof exists: the ladder was climbed to its planning-document rung, the 2008 UC Regents deck, and that is a near-nadir aerial. The built 0.35 / 0.45 m are [estimated] and declared.
Loading dock, trash enclosure, mechanical yard — no source shows one for Argo; nothing invented.

Ground-floor lobby doors and interior glazing detail — the dusk photography does not resolve them. The near-black recess is now built ONLY inside the north colonnade opening, where a photograph shows a recess; the rest of the ground storey is the solid panelled base wall those same photographs show.

Construction date 1966 / 1967 / 1968, and the 'Tucker, Sadler & Bennett' attribution — three dates on record, none confirmable on the open web today, and an architect attribution inherited from the inventory and demoted to unverified in label. The likeliest reconciliation is design-versus-occupancy, which is a reading and is written as one in conflicts[]. No geometry depends on any of it.

THE COURT BREEZEWAY'S POSITION ON THE RING. UC Regents 2008 p11 proves a ground-level breezeway passes clean through the building into the court — you can see lawn on the far side, square columns, a flat soffit, bikes racked in it — and the Nov 2024 photosphere proves a colonnade at the north entry. Nothing in the set ties the breezeway to a segment and an offset: p11 is a tight eye-level frame with no context, and from nadir the breezeway is under 18.70 m of building. The court's ground storey therefore ships CLOSED, and the sourced opening is not guessed into a position.

THE GALLERY'S DEPTH. No source measures how far the court galleries project. They are built at the IBC 2021 §1020.3 minimum corridor clear width, 1.1176 m, plus the downstand beam — deliberately the smallest value the photographed gallery can lawfully be, so the error is an under-claim rather than an over-claim. A single frame that shows a gallery against a known width replaces it.

THE GALLERY SLAT SCREENS' RHYTHM. webcor-argo-N9.jpg shows the element and its character — white vertical-slat panels hung between gallery levels — and does not show a rhythm or a count anywhere. One screen per long court wall per level is built, midway between that wall's two sourced suite doors, which is the only position the sourced door rhythm supplies; it is labelled [estimated] and it is not a claim about how many there are.

THE COURT FLOOR'S MATERIAL AND FINISH. The floor is not visible in any frame in the set: N9 looks across at gallery level, UC Regents p11 looks along the breezeway, the ortho sees only shadow, and the 2008 aerial resolves a tree and nothing else. The floor MUST be built — without it the court has nothing to stand on and you see through the planet — so it is built on the building's own bay module in the building's own measured shaded-concrete hex, adding no new colour claim, and its surface is [estimated].

THE NORTH BENCH'S LENGTH AND THE PLANTING BED'S PLAN ARE KNOWN WRONG AND ARE NOT GUESSED AT. The Nov 2024 photosphere shows a bench running the full open edge of the bed, which reads as roughly 8-10 m against the shipped 2.6 m, and a raised bed carrying two mature trees and a shrub understorey, which a 3.0 x 1.4 m planter cannot be — it is a long raised strip of order 10 x 3 m. A 640 x 400 oblique cannot replace either with a number. Both figures are carried UNCHANGED and flagged here, because a declared error beats an invented correction.

THE PRECAST SURROUND'S SPLAY ANGLE, DEPTH AND PLATE THICKNESS. N17's oblique resolves the sawtooth unambiguously — that the reveals splay outward, one lit face and one shadowed face per bay — and no frame in the set measures the angle or the projection. The shipped 0.45 rad / 0.30 m / 0.07 m are retained unchanged and labelled [estimated], so this revision changes only the figures whose evidence changed.

THE COURT'S GROUND-STOREY CONDITION other than the breezeway. Between the breezeway and the court walls the 2008 frame shows square columns and a flat soffit, in the dead blue epoch, and nothing shows what is there now. The court's ground storey ships as the same closed base condition as the outer elevations rather than a guessed arcade.

A CACHED COPY OF THE NOVEMBER 2024 PHOTOSPHERE. Nineteen hexes in colors[] are attributed to it and it exists in this repo only as prose and one 640 x 400 QA capture. Its hexes are carried unchanged rather than re-sampled or replaced. This is the same failure the section already carries once: sources[] used to cite vmarch-bradley_vma_argo_7a.jpg, a file whose page 404s today.

EXIT SIGNS, WAYFINDING AND NOTICE BOARDS in the court and under the north colonnade. UC Regents 2008 p11 shows notice boards on the gallery back wall and the Nov 2024 photosphere shows dark notice panels on two colonnade columns. This repo has no text rendering, and a blank rectangle standing in for a sign is a claim about a sign's size that nothing supports.

ARGO'S LEGACY BIKE-RACK RUN IS NOT REBUILT HERE. The evidence says the eleven hoops at z 362.5 are about 5 m out of position and belong in two rows against Blake at z 355.5 / 358.0. They live in revelle.racks, which is not this section's file; the finding and both the recommended and the conservative actions are recorded in ground.racksNote for arbitration and nothing is moved from inside this section.

THE ARGO-BLAKE GAP'S GROUND SURFACE — the gravel apron and the walk, x -58..-16 over z 358.4..366.4. This strip is argo's ground under the R2 arbitration (P5 / A3) and argo builds the boardwalk in it and nothing else. The Nov 2024 photosphere frames a pale gravel or decomposed-granite apron between the boardwalk's north edge and a walk running east-west across the gap, and it is the only dated frame that covers the strip: it is a 640 x 400 oblique QA capture of a photosphere that is NOT CACHED in this repo, so it gives the apron's existence and its character and NOT ONE plan dimension — no edge, no width, no boundary with the walk. The 2026 ortho cannot settle it either and must not be cited on it, because Argo's roof plate is displaced 3.78 m north there and the building leans over its own forecourt in image coordinates. Paving either surface would mean inventing its extent inside 300 m^2 that three sources see and none measures, so the strip ships as drawn LiDAR ground. A cached frame, or any plan source, replaces this entry.

THE ROOF DECK AND EVERYTHING THAT STANDS ON IT — the single-ply membrane, its stain field, the ten mechanical curbs and the west recess with its kerb. Not withheld for want of a source: all four are MEASURED on the 2026 ortho, re-registered at (+0.93, +3.78) by the four-feature edge fit, court-rim clipped by a stated rule, and their whole record is carried here unchanged and still gated. They are withheld because there is nowhere in the DRAWN world to put them. campus-massing.js extrudes Argo flat to 18.70 m, which is the top of the parapet coping; the deck is 1.532846 m below that, so every one of these was being built inside a solid mass — invisible, and intersecting, the pair this project forbids. Standing them on the drawn 18.70 m plane instead is refused separately: it misplaces the roof by 1.53 m and lifts a curb core above the measured LiDAR maximum. The ladder is not the issue and is not climbed here; the mass is. See roof.deckGate and conflicts. Restored the day the drawn mass gains a stepped top.

argo.supersededNote: RETIRED FROM THE DRAW, KEPT IN THE RECORD. Every entry above names what it was, what replaced it and the evidence that moved it. Nothing is deleted: absent[] entries that were resolved are REWRITTEN IN PLACE to say so and the array never shrinks. This is the mechanism the eighth section uses for retired item keys, applied here to retired CLAIMS, because what Argo's revision retires is not geometry keys but assertions about the building. SINCE THE R2 ARBITRATION (S2) `supersededClaims` carries the OTHER direction: a predecessor item elsewhere in the batch flags this section with `sup`, and this section declares what actually happened to it — `transferred` (this section ships the object, and `ships`/`count` say so) or `deleted-on-evidence` (this section ships nothing and the ground is stated). Only the prose could tell those apart before, and the machine-readable field said the opposite of what happened.

blake.label: Blake Hall — Revelle College residence hall (Tucker, Sadler & Bennett; see conflicts[] for the 1967-vs-1968 year split; renovated LEED Gold and repainted WHITE by Vasquez Marshall, complete by Jan 2014). NOT a Fleet hall. Argo's sibling — same family language, a DIFFERENT module — and a four-storey COURTYARD DONUT: the well at its centre is open to the sky, landscaped, and inhabited on three gallery levels.
blake.epoch: Photographs 2008-2026. The Vasquez Marshall set is EXIF-dated 2014-01-12 and 2014-01-13 (Canon EOS 5D Mark II, Lightroom 5.3) — nine files on the 12th, one on the 13th — so Blake was already white and photographed finished in January 2014. That is NOT Webcor's Argo renovation, which ran 2015-16: two projects, two dates, two contractors. The repaint falls between UCOP's Nov 2008 aerial (Blake TAN, colonnade blue) and Jan 2014. The 2013-09-13 flickr west-end frames are PRE-repaint and are used for geometry only, never colour. The 2026 Google ortho is the newest epoch and decides roof and courtyard PLAN; the Jan 2014 photographs decide what the courtyard IS — twelve years apart, both right about their own year, and neither reconciled to the other.
blake.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. LiDAR/OSM keep deciding scale and position: every facade hangs off two vertices of the ring campus-massing.js actually extrudes, and the storey grid is the drawn LiDAR mass height (12.4 m) read back. Bays are built from COUNTS against the measured ring, never from absolute metres. The courtyard well and its core notch are the drawn massing's own INNER ring, carried verbatim — campus-massing.js pushes it into shape.holes, so the void has always been there and the previous build painted a lid over it. Nothing measured may ever read from this section.
sources: https://www.vmarch.net/blake-hall-student-residence-renovation-interior — Vasquez Marshall Architects, architect of record for the renovation photographed in Jan 2014: "Originally constructed in 1968, Blake Hall is a four-story concrete structure"; 12 residential suites, 72 bedrooms, the fourth floor Residence Lounge, the College Commuter Lounge, "concrete fins", "a new exterior building color scheme" and "a completely renovated courtyard concept at the building's center". 38,880 sf, $5,000,000, LEED Gold, photographer credit Bradley.

Revelle-College-Sources/renders/blake-sources/vmarch-bradley_VMA_UCSDBlake_67.jpg — the near-orthographic dusk SOUTH elevation, EXIF 2014-01-12, 2500x1283. The single best frame of either residence hall: it carries the four-step storey stack, the 30-bay fin rhythm, the ground colonnade with Roger's Market and the Commuter Lounge roundel, the parapet band, and the lava-rock terrace wall across the full foreground. Every px reading in derivations.readings.px comes from this file.

Revelle-College-Sources/renders/blake-sources/vmarch-bradley_VMA_UCSDBlake_3.jpg — EXIF 2014-01-12, across the OPEN COURT from a Level 4 room: gallery walkways on three levels, pale metal picket guards on stub posts over a separate slab-edge line, pale horizontal board cladding, a repeating dark-framed room door plus window with a square wall light between bays, chartreuse level graphics, and a Washingtonia fan palm rising past the galleries. This is the frame that refutes the roof-plane lid.

measured.ringNote: the ring campus-massing.js actually EXTRUDES: the university massing ring for Blake Hall (campus-arcgis.json massing, /10 to metres), copied verbatim INCLUDING the closing vertex so roofElevation rim-median ground matches the drawn roof plane sample for sample. The OSM-side campus-3d ring is suppressed under this one and registering the detail to it left the east treatment up to half a metre inside the drawn wall.
measured.courtyardRingNote: the drawn massing INNER ring, verbatim — the courtyard well the extruder opens through the mass. campus-massing.js:826 pushes every ring after the first into shape.holes, so this void has ALWAYS been drawn; the four vertices [-47.3,336.2] [-44.4,336.1] [-44.4,333.3] [-47.4,333.3] are the core notch, a solid volume of building standing into the court from its west side, and they are why the core is DRESSED rather than built.
measured.heightNote: LiDAR per-mass 2014 roof plane: massHeights[m:-43,330] = heights[Blake Hall] = 12.4 m — the height the drawn mass extrudes to, and (see derivations.figures['grid.roofSlab']) the top of the Level 4 roof slab, not the top of the outer parapet. The campus-3d builder 15.6 m on the suppressed OSM ring is a LOSING read (recorded here): building to it hung the whole roofscape 3.2 m over the drawn roof plane.
measured.source: docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing 'Blake Hall' (the builder's rename of the GIS 'Revelle Residence Hall - Blake') (both rings, verbatim, /10) + docs/data/campus-lidar.json massHeights/heights — ring and height are the survey record the massing draws, copied never moved

derivations.why: THE KEELING BAR. keeling.roofs.pv states a real product dimension and its own arithmetic for every figure it draws. This block does the same for Blake: `readings` are the raw citations (pixel counts on one named frame, ortho plan reads, survey lengths, published areas, code rules, stock sizes) and `figures` is every drawn metre value with the expression that produces it. tests/campus-photo-blake.test.mjs recomputes every one of these independently from `readings` and fails if the section's own value drifts from its own derivation — so a fabricated figure cannot pass by being self-consistent, which is exactly how 22 presence gates passed on fabricated values in the Eighth audit.

units.note: Exact by definition. Every code and product figure below is a whole number of inches and converts here.

px.source: vmarch-bradley_VMA_UCSDBlake_67.jpg at its original 2500x1283, all band edges read in ONE vertical strip at x 1470-1620 so every reading shares one perspective. The horizontal scale in that strip comes from the fin rhythm, which is a COUNT and therefore foreshortening-immune: 30 bays over a drawn 37.5 m face is a 1.25 m module against a measured 58.5 px fin pitch, i.e. 46.8 px/m locally. The lava-wall stations are read at image x 800, 1250 and 1600 with their own local scales.

ortho.source: docs/data/textures/chunk_4_6.jpg at 8 px/m, 2026 epoch. Raw plan reads are corrected by the +1.1 m x / +3.6 m z top displacement the recon MEASURED on Argo over this same chunk (revelle-recon.md 1.2 / Rung 5 item 24) — a correction imported, not fitted here.

survey.source: campus-arcgis.json massing 'Blake Hall' (the builder's rename of the GIS 'Revelle Residence Hall - Blake') rings at /10 and campus-lidar.json heights['Blake Hall']. outerArea and wellArea are the shoelace areas of the two verbatim rings. The four notch* values are vertices of that inner ring, carried verbatim. countedBays is a count on _67, not a length.

published.source: squareFeet from vmarch.net's own project data sheet. sqftPerSqm is exact by definition (1 m^2 = 10.7639 sf). lavaDistanceFactor is D/(D-3.9) at D = 50 m, the wall standing 3.9 m nearer the camera than the facade it is scaled against.

code.source: IBC 2021 §1015.2 — guards at an occupied roof or open-sided walking surface are 42 in minimum; §1015.4 — a 4 in sphere may not pass through a required guard's openings. Both are what makes 'closely-pitched vertical pickets' a number instead of an adjective.

product.source: Stock sizes, the Keeling `panel [1.65, 0.99]` class: 1-1/4 in square picket stock; 2 in flat rail and stub-post sections; a 36 in x 80 in door leaf; a 48 in sash; 8 in nominal horizontal board cladding; a 12 in square wall-mounted light fixture.

scale.pxPerMetre.why: 548 px of elevation is the LiDAR's own 12.4 m, so the whole south elevation converts to metres without a photogrammetric scale. The fin-pitch scale (58.5 px / 1.25 m = 46.8 px/m) is a SEPARATE, local read and is 6% apart; the difference is the podium — the colonnade floor stands ~0.7 m over the LiDAR ground datum — and that residual is recorded, not hidden.

grid.floorToFloor.why: The four-step stack read off _67 (grade 1046 -> 909 -> 772 -> 635 -> 498, four EXACT 137 px steps, every line an independently visible feature) divides the drawn LiDAR height with zero residual. Corroborated twice and independently: the photo's own fin-pitch scale gives 137/46.8 = 2.93 m, and the arcgis levels x 3.05 formula gives 3.05 — a 0.17 m spread over three unrelated methods. LiDAR decides height, so 3.10 is what is built.

grid.terraceDeck.why: Level 4 floor = the roof-terrace deck. 411 px = 3 x 137, so this is also exactly 3 x floorToFloor.

grid.parapet.why: The outer parapet stands 57 px above the L4 terrace deck. Sanity: IBC 2021 requires a 42 in (1.067 m) guard at an occupied roof and 1.29 m clears it. This REPLACES the shipped 1.2 m guess, which was whatever the 12.4 = 4 x 2.8 + p solve needed.

grid.parapetTop.why: 10.59 m — the top of the outer wall of the donut. Everything above this on the north and south elevations is set-back terrace in the real building.

grid.roofSlab.why: The top of the Level 4 roof slab IS the drawn LiDAR maximum. This is the anchoring the LiDAR builder's own guard proves: build-campus-lidar.mjs withholds massHeights when p98 - p75 > 2 m, Blake HAS a massHeights entry, and the alternative anchoring (12.4 m = grade to parapet) would put a 2.12 m step between planes and would have fired that guard.

grid.slabProud.why: The L4 roof stands 1.81 m proud of the outer parapet. Under the alternative anchoring it would be 2.12 m and the LiDAR guard would have withheld Blake's mass height.

grid.slabThickness.why: The oversailing L4 roof slab reads 10 px thick in _67; the same edge band is used for the gallery slab edges inside the well.

system.bands.spandrelFrac.why: Scale-free: a ratio of two lengths in one strip, so it survives any perspective error. 27/137. The shipped 0.333 is the LOSING read and is kept in conflicts[].

system.bands.openingFrac.why: 27 + 110 = 137, so spandrelFrac + openingFrac = 1 exactly and the storey is fully accounted for.

system.bands.awningFrac.why: The bottom-hinged awning sash reads 40-45 px; 42.5 is the midpoint of that band. As a fraction of the OPENING that is 42.5/110 = 0.386, against the shipped 0.24 — the same direction the shipped note already confessed it was drifting, only further.

system.bands.panelFrac.why: What is left of the opening above the awning sash is the fixed glazed panel.

system.bayModule.why: A COUNT (30 bays, confirmed independently of the shipped value by peak detection on the L2 and L3 glazing bands: median pitch 60 px against 1797 px / 37.5 m = 47.9 px/m, i.e. 1.25 m) against a MEASURED face length. Foreshortening-immune both ways.

level4.x0.why: The +1.1 m / +3.6 m top displacement is the recon's own measurement over this same ortho chunk (revelle-recon.md 1.2 / Rung 5 item 24), taken on Argo, not fitted here.

level4.x1.why: The bar east edge. The same imported displacement; the residual inset from the drawn ring here is 1.7 m, which is inside the ortho own registration tolerance and is declared measured-but-at-tolerance in absent[] rather than built as a certain step.

level4.z0.why: The bar north edge, and therefore the south edge of the north roof terrace the mechanical screen stands on. The z displacement is the larger of the two corrections (+3.6 m) and it is the one that moves this figure most.

level4.z1.why: The bar south edge. This is the figure the south elevation photograph appears to contradict — _67 shows the set-back storey over only the central 19 m — and reads['level4.visibility'] records why the plan wins and the photograph is a section, not a plan.

level4.width.why: An east-west bar 35.5 m long — nearly wall to wall across a 37.8 m ring, which is what makes the north and south setbacks, not an east-west one, the shape of this storey.

level4.depth.why: 19.1 m deep, with the 16.5 m courtyard well punching through its middle — so of the bar depth only about 1.3 m survives north of the well and 1.3 m south of it, and those two strips are the galleries.

level4.insetWest.why: 0.6 m — inside the ortho's own registration tolerance; declared at tolerance, not built as a certain step.

level4.insetEast.why: 1.7 m of inset on the east. Same caveat as the west: it is inside the ortho own registration tolerance after the displacement correction, so it is declared measured-but-at-tolerance and no step is built as if it were certain.

level4.insetNorth.why: 9.3 m of roof terrace on the north. This is the band that carries the mechanical screen.

level4.insetSouth.why: 9.5 m of roof terrace on the south — clean membrane, stains and vents in the ortho, and _67 shows a picket guardrail standing on the parapet at its west end, so at least part of it is occupied terrace rather than bare roof.

level4.westLegDepth.why: The west leg of the bar: 10.0 m of accommodation between the bar west edge and the well. This is where Vasquez Marshall fourth floor Residence Lounge, the Dean apartment and the offices are, and _39, _12r and _40 photograph all three from inside.

level4.eastLegDepth.why: The east leg: 9.0 m, one metre shallower than the west because the bar sits 1.7 m inside the ring on this end against 0.6 m on the other. It carries the same programme as the west leg.

level4.northStrip.why: 1.3 m — the north gallery walkway round the court, which is what _3 photographs on the far side of the well.

level4.southStrip.why: 1.3 m — the south gallery walkway, the mirror of the north strip, and the plan position the ortho second unresolved grid structure coincides with.

level4.plateArea.why: Donut plate. Corroboration only, and weak: 1148.8 x 4 x 10.7639 = 49,461 sf gross against Vasquez Marshall's published 38,880 sf gives a 78.6% net-to-gross, normal for a residence hall; a SOLID Blake would give 64.2%, which is low enough to be odd.

level4.netToGross.why: 0.786 — see level4.plateArea. Never used to decide a metre; recorded because it points the same way as everything else.

core.width.why: 3.0 m. All four notch coordinates are vertices of the drawn inner ring, carried verbatim; the test asserts that before it uses them.

core.depth.why: 2.9 m north-south, against 3.0 m east-west — a very nearly square stair or lift core, which is what a full-height volume standing into a courtyard from one side normally is.

core.orthoCheckX0.why: Independent confirmation that the notch is a REAL full-height volume and not a drafting artefact: the ortho's pale block, displacement-corrected, lands within 0.6 m of the drawn notch — under the ortho's 0.125 m/px times its registration tolerance. It reads at ROOF brightness with a crisp top edge, so it rises to about the roof plane.

core.orthoCheckZ0.why: The z half of the same independent check: corrected, the ortho pale block lands at z 333.1 against the drawn notch z 333.3, a 0.2 m agreement on the axis carrying the larger correction.

gallery.guardHeight.why: IBC 2021 1015.2. _3 and _39 show a guard of exactly this proportion; the code figure is what it is built to.

gallery.picketWidth.why: 1-1/4 in square picket stock — the section that, at the tightest pitch the 4 in sphere rule permits, produces the closely-pitched picket field _3 and _39 photograph.

gallery.picketClear.why: IBC 2021 1015.4 — a 4 in sphere may not pass. This is what 'closely-pitched vertical pickets' means numerically.

gallery.picketPitch.why: The tightest pitch the code permits, which is what the photographs show.

gallery.railFace.why: A 2 in flat section for both the top rail and the mid rail. _3 resolves that the guard is a flat top rail over a mid rail rather than a pipe rail, which is the sourced fact; the section is the stock size for it.

gallery.midRailHeight.why: _3 shows exactly one mid rail, at about half the guard height, so it is placed at half. With the picket field already satisfying the sphere rule the mid rail is a stiffener rather than a required member, which is why half is the right default rather than a code figure.

gallery.postWidth.why: Stub posts standing off the slab edge — the slab edge reads BELOW the rail as a separate line in _3, which is why the guard is modelled on posts and not as a solid upstand.

wellFace.bayModule.why: [estimated] The ladder failed on this face (see absent[]): no orthographic view of a well face exists on any rung. This EXTENDS THE SAME BUILDING'S measured 1.25 m module by the smallest whole count that can hold the sourced door-plus-window pair — a 36 in door leaf plus a room window plus two reveals does not fit one module, and _3 shows a bay plainly wider than the outer facade's fin pitch. The count itself stays declared absent.

wellFace.doorWidth.why: A 36 in stock door leaf. _3 resolves that every bay carries a glazed room door in a dark frame; nothing resolves its width, so the door is the stock leaf that a residence-hall room door is.

wellFace.doorHeight.why: An 80 in stock leaf height, and the datum the window head is aligned to — which is the relationship _3 actually shows, door head and window head on one line.

wellFace.boardPitch.why: [estimated] 8 in nominal horizontal board. _3 resolves that the cladding IS horizontal boarding; it does not resolve the course.

wellFace.windowWidth.why: What is left of the bay once the door leaf and a one-board reveal at each end are taken out.

wellFace.windowHeight.why: A 48 in stock sash. _3 resolves that the bay carries a window beside the door and that the two heads align; the sash height is the stock size for a room window of that width.

wellFace.windowSill.why: Window head aligned with the door head, which is what _3 shows.

wellFace.fixture.why: [estimated] The square wall-mounted light between bays; _3 resolves the object, not its size.

wellFace.fixtureHeight.why: One board course above the door head. _3 puts the square wall fixture above the door line and below the storey line; tying it to the cladding course rather than to a picked height means it moves with the board pitch if a better read of the course ever appears.

court.palmHeight.why: [read] In _3 (from a Level 4 room) and _25 (from the ground breezeway) the fan-palm crowns sit at about the Level 3 gallery deck. Tolerance +/- 0.8 m — one storey is 3.10 m and the read is good to about a quarter of that. The shipped 2.4-3.5 m heights were measured from the ROOF-PLANE LID and are meaningless once the lid is gone.

system.ground.storefrontMullion.why: A 2 in storefront mullion face, the stock size for the aluminium storefront system _67 shows behind the colonnade — the Keeling product-dimension class, the same one that makes product.railFaceIn a number. The mullion PITCH is not a stock size and is not here: it is a read, reads['ground.storefront.mullionPitch'], because what _67 resolves is that the storefront rhythm is the facade's own 1.25 m bay module and not a rhythm of its own.

lavaWall.exposedWest.why: The wall stands 3.9 m nearer the camera than the facade (z 357.6 against 353.7), so the local fin-pitch scale is corrected by D/(D-3.9) = 1.085 at D = 50 m. Error budget: +/-4 px on the base line (+/-6%), +/-2% on the local scale, +/-2.3% on the distance factor -> 1.16 +/- 0.08 m.

lavaWall.exposedMid.why: The second of three stations, at image x 1250: 1.17 m against the first station 1.16 m. Two independent picks a third of the elevation apart agreeing to a centimetre is what makes the western reading trustworthy and the eastern one interesting.

lavaWall.exposedEast.why: Third station, ~2.2 m. The wall is a RETAINING wall on falling ground and its exposed face nearly doubles toward the east end; the single scalar height is an average of something non-uniform and the section says so.

gallery.bottomRailHeight.why: [read] _3 at full resolution shows the picket panel occupying roughly the TOP 60% of the guard, closed by a BOTTOM RAIL, with the stub posts continuing down to a bracket on the slab face and an open gap of about a third of the guard height beneath — a continuous stripe of light under every rail on three levels and eight faces. Tolerance +/- 0.1 of the guard height. Tied to guardHeight as a third, the same way gallery.midRailHeight is tied to it as a half, so both proportions move with the code figure rather than with a picked metre. The shipped build ran the pickets deck-to-top and modelled no bottom rail at all.

level4.terraceX0.why: The north and south roof terraces run the FULL WIDTH of the drawn ring — that is what level4.terraces[].what has always said in prose, and this is the number behind it. Taken from the ring campus-massing.js extrudes, not from the bar, because the terraces are what is left of the plate outside the bar and the bar is inset 0.6 m west and 1.7 m east.

level4.terraceX1.why: The east end of the same full-width terrace band. Same argument as level4.terraceX0: the terrace is the plate outside the bar, so its x extents are the ring's and not the bar's.

faceBayFit.why: The arithmetic behind system.wellFace.faceBays, recorded because R2 stage 7 found the section declaring one bay module and shipping five different bays (audit-blake Major 4). Ruled option (a): the fit is legitimate, the record was not.
faceBayFit.rule: for each edge of measured.courtyardRing: length = hypot(b - a); core = both endpoints on the survey notch rectangle; bays = max(1, round(length / wellFace.bayModule)); bay = length / bays; windowWidth = bay - wellFace.doorWidth - 2 * wellFace.boardPitch
inputs: measured.courtyardRing — the surveyed well ring, byte-gated against the survey
derivations.readings.survey.notchX0/X1/Z0/Z1 — the solid core rectangle, which carries no room bay
faceBayFit.spread: bay 3.3004..4.1003 m, window 1.9796..2.7795 m. Declared per face rather than presented as one number.

wellFace.bayModule.extends: the SAME BUILDING's measured 1.25 m south-elevation module (derivations.figures['system.bayModule']), by a whole count
wellFace.bayModule.why: [estimated] Extends the SAME BUILDING's measured 1.25 m south-elevation module by a whole count of 3. Ladder for a direct read: photos — _3 is oblique and shot through a window; Street View — no pano enters the court; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the 2008 UCOP deck carries no Blake plan; archives — 1960s UCSD DC aerials show the roof, not the well faces. Every rung fails, which is what licenses the extension. Replaced the day an orthographic well-face view appears.
wellFace.bayModule.bandWhy: The band is the whole-count range the sourced content admits: 2 x 1.25 = 2.50 m is the smallest module that could hold a 36 in door leaf plus any window at all, and 4 x 1.25 = 5.00 m is the widest that _3's bay rhythm can be read as. The shipped 3 x 1.25 = 3.75 m is the smallest count that holds the sourced door-plus-window pair with reveals.

wellFace.boardPitch.extends: nothing measurable — it is the STOCK SIZE for the material _3 resolves (horizontal board cladding), the Keeling product-dimension class
wellFace.boardPitch.why: [estimated] Extends nothing measurable — _3 resolves that the cladding IS horizontal boarding and not precast fins (which is the load-bearing fact, and it is sourced), but not its course. An 8 in nominal board is the stock size for the material the photograph shows.
wellFace.boardPitch.bandWhy: 6 in to 12 in nominal is the stock range for horizontal board cladding; 8 in is the common size and is what ships. _3 resolves that the cladding IS boarding and not precast fins, which is the load-bearing fact and is sourced; it does not resolve the course.

wellFace.fixture.extends: nothing measurable — the STOCK SIZE for the square wall-mounted fixture _3 resolves as an object
wellFace.fixture.why: [estimated] _3 shows a square wall-mounted fixture between bays. A 12 in square is the stock size; the photograph resolves the object, not the size.
wellFace.fixture.bandWhy: 8 in to 16 in square is the stock range for a wall-mounted exterior fixture of this kind; 12 in ships. The photograph resolves the object, not the size.

court.beds.extends: the sourced planting of _25 (tan decomposed granite, grey granite boulders, agave and succulents) onto the MEASURED crown positions of the 2026 ortho
court.beds.why: [estimated] The DG/gravel beds' EXISTENCE, material and contents are sourced (_25: tan decomposed granite, grey granite boulders, agave and succulents). Their PLAN is not: no source gives bed outlines. Each bed is generated as a 4.0 m square centred on a MEASURED crown position, which is the smallest claim that carries the sourced planting without inventing a shape.
court.beds.bandWhy: The band is the bed side length. 4.0 m is the shipped square; the band's width is what a bed round a crown of the measured 1.7-2.6 m radius can be without either failing to hold it or lapping its neighbour. bed-4 is 4.0 x 3.8 m because the well clips it, which is inside the band. No source gives bed outlines and the value is the smallest claim that carries the sourced planting.

court.boulders.extends: the same sourced _25 planting as court.beds — one boulder per bed, at a bed corner so it never sits under a measured crown
court.boulders.why: [estimated] Same argument as court.beds. One boulder per bed, placed at a bed corner so it never sits under the measured crown, sized inside the 0.6-1.2 m band _25 shows. Positions [estimated], existence and material sourced.
court.boulders.bandWhy: The band is the 0.6-1.2 m boulder radius _25 shows; the value is the LARGEST shipped radius, so the assertion bites at the top of the range. All five shipped radii (0.6, 0.75, 0.9, 1.05, 0.6) lie inside it. Positions [estimated], existence and material sourced.

ground.south.lavaWall.profileKnee.extends: THIS SECTION'S OWN SOURCED PROSE — 'about 1.2 m across the western two-thirds growing past 2.2 m toward the east end' — onto the geometry, as the u fraction at which the western plateau ends
ground.south.lavaWall.profileKnee.why: [estimated] The three exposed-face stations are MEASURED and derived (derivations.figures['lavaWall.exposedWest'], ['lavaWall.exposedMid'], ['lavaWall.exposedEast'] — 1.16, 1.17 and 2.17 m). WHERE ALONG THE WALL they sit is not: they are read at image x 800, 1250 and 1600 of _67, and converting an image x to a world x on the WALL needs a frame registration this section does not have — the wall stands 3.9 m nearer the camera than the facade the frame's only horizontal scale (the foreshortening-immune fin count) is taken on, so the facade's px/m does not carry across to it. Ladder for a direct read: photos — _67 is the only frame that shows the wall's full run and it is the frame in question; Street View — no pano stands south of the wall; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the 2008 UCOP deck carries no Revelle site plan at this scale; archives — the 1960s UCSD DC aerials predate this grade. Every rung fails, which is what licenses the extension. Replaced the day the frame is registered.
ground.south.lavaWall.profileKnee.bandWhy: The band is the u fraction at which the western plateau ends. 0.5 is the floor: two stations agreeing to a centimetre (1.161 and 1.171 m) cannot be read as a plateau shorter than the interval between them, and the second station is at worst the halfway point of the run. 0.8 is the ceiling: past it the eastern rise is compressed into a fifth of the wall and reads as a step rather than the continuous grade change _67 shows. The shipped 0.666667 is this section's own sourced word 'two-thirds' taken literally, which is the smallest claim that carries the prose.

ground.south.lavaWall.thickness.extends: the shipped 0.5 m, kept for continuity and re-tiered honestly rather than inherited as [measured]
ground.south.lavaWall.thickness.why: [estimated] Not measurable from _67 and never was: the camera sits ~0.4 m above the wall top at ~50 m, so a top face of depth t projects to t x (0.4/50) x 53 = 0.42t px — 0.2 px at t = 0.5, i.e. invisible. The shipped 0.5 is exactly as unsourced as revelle.lavaWalls' 0.7 was; it is kept for continuity and re-tiered honestly rather than inherited as a measurement, which is what it was shipped as and never was.
ground.south.lavaWall.thickness.bandWhy: The band is bracketed by the only two figures this campus has ever carried for a lava-rock rubble retaining wall: blake's 0.5 and revelle.lavaWalls' college-wide 0.7 default, widened to the nearest tenth either side. It is a band over shipped practice, not over a measurement, and the entry says why no measurement is possible: at ~50 m with the camera ~0.4 m above the wall top, a 0.5 m top face projects to 0.2 px.

system.ground.extends: the SAME BUILDING's sourced south colonnade (_67) onto the north, east and west faces, mirroring Argo's west-face declaration
system.ground.why: [estimated] The open colonnade is SOURCED only on the south (_67). Its existence on the north, east and west extends the same building's sourced south pattern, mirroring Argo's west-face declaration; the Jul 2022 north panos establish only '2 fin storeys over a ground floor' and the east/west end sources do not show the base condition. Column rhythm is on the bay grid on every face.
system.ground.bandWhy: The banded number is HOW MANY FACES carry the colonnade. 1 is the floor — the south is the only face any source shows the base condition of. 4 is the ceiling — the drawn ring has four faces. The shipped 4 sits at the top of its own band, which is exactly the claim the extension makes, and dressing a fifth face would fail. Column rhythm is on the bay grid on every face.

wellFace.groundLevel.extends: the SAME FACES' sourced upper-level pattern (_3: levels 2, 3 and 4), down one storey to grade, minus the guard
wellFace.groundLevel.why: [estimated] Levels 2, 3 and 4 have SOURCED gallery access (_3). The ground level of the well faces is dressed with the same board cladding and door/window bay minus the guard, extending the sourced upper-level pattern of the same faces down one storey. _25 shows glazed doors and pale wall at grade, which corroborates the family but does not resolve the bay.
wellFace.groundLevel.bandWhy: The banded number is HOW MANY LEVELS of the well faces are dressed with the door/window bay. 3 is the floor — _3 sources levels 2, 3 and 4. 4 is the ceiling — the building has four storeys. The shipped 4 is the extension itself, and a fifth level would fail. _25 shows glazed doors and pale wall at grade, which corroborates the family but does not resolve the bay.

reads.ground.storefront.mullionPitch: The storefront mullions behind the colonnade fall on the facade's OWN bay module [read, _67, tolerance +/- 0.15 m]. Along the west shopfront the mullion pitch measures about 54 px against the 58.5 px fin pitch in the same frame, and the ground storey stands nearer the camera than the fin field above it, which is the direction that difference has to go. So the storefront is built at one mullion per bay boundary on system.bayModule, not on a pitch of its own. What is read is that the two rhythms are the SAME rhythm — a count, not a length — which is why this is a read with a tolerance and not a figure. The per-bay SHOP layout it does not resolve is declared in absent[].
reads.system.panel.widthFrac: 0.85 of the bay [read, _67, tolerance +/-0.05] — a large fixed glazed panel filling most of the bay; the rooms behind are almost universally blind-down so the panels read frosted/pale. This is the single most important difference from Argo, whose bay carries a 0.66 narrow window.
reads.court.palmHeight: Crowns at about the Level 3 gallery deck [read, _3 and _25, tolerance +/-0.8 m]. Recorded as a read rather than a figure because it is an eye judgement against a known datum, not a pixel measurement.
reads.roof.screen.tone: The north-terrace checkerboard samples #b6af9b in the 2026 ortho at world (-38, 318.5) [read, tolerance: an 8 px/m nadir sample of a field of blocks and gaps]. Genuine PV in the SAME imagery (Keeling) is unmistakably dark blue. That is the whole of the 2026-08-18 adjudication and it is re-verified here.
reads.court.palmTrunkRadius: The fibrous Washingtonia trunk reads about 0.6 m across at chest height [read, _25 and _3, tolerance +/-0.15 m], so 0.30 m of radius. The geometry is near-parallel above a swollen base, which the trunk mesh carries as a fixed 1.4x flare at the foot rather than as a taper along the whole trunk.
reads.level4.visibility: In _67 the set-back storey reads above the south parapet over only the central ~19 m of the 37.5 m elevation, while the ortho plan says it runs nearly the full width. At a 9.5 m setback and 1.81 m of rise the sightline from a ~1.6 m eye at ~55 m GRAZES the parapet — 1.55 m of the 1.81 m is consumed — so visibility along the elevation is decided by tenths of a metre of camera geometry. THE ORTHO PLAN IS THE DATUM; THE PHOTOGRAPH IS THE SECTION. The L4 is not narrowed to 19 m on the strength of what happens to clear a parapet in one frame.
reads.gallery.picketPanel: The picket panel occupies roughly the top 60% of the guard, closed by a bottom rail over an open gap of about a third of the guard height [read, _3, tolerance +/- 10% of the guard height]. An eye judgement of a proportion against a known code datum, not a pixel measurement — recorded as a read for the same reason court.palmHeight is. It is what derivations.figures['gallery.bottomRailHeight'] is built from.

draw.crownClearNote: THE RULE, NOT THE TRIMMED NUMBER (the pattern argo.roof.curbs.clipNote sets). Each palm crown's DRAWN radius is min(its measured radius, the distance from its measured centre to the nearest edge of the drawn courtyard well ring, less this clearance). The crowns' centres and radii are measured off the 2026 ortho and are not moved or shrunk in the record; what is clipped is the cone the renderer draws, so a canopy can never grow into the gallery slab, the guard or the solid core notch. It bites on ONE palm: palm-4 at (-44.8, 338), whose measured 2.6 m crown reaches 0.8 m into the core notch's z extent. 0.06 m is the clearance and it is a render offset, not a measurement — it is set just clear of draw.wellFaceProud (0.04), which is how far the cladding stands out of the ring's chord plane, so the clip is against the face the eye sees and not the chord behind it.
draw.storefrontProudNote: A render offset, not a dimension: the storefront mullions stand this far outward of the ground-recess glazing plane so they read as a frame against it instead of z-fighting it. The colonnade columns are further out still (system.ground.columnProud + columnSize), and the mullions fall on bay BOUNDARIES while the columns fall on bay centres, so the two never meet.
draw.courtRungNote: The court floor is GROUND: it seats on surfaceAt + overlayLift('pad'), the height of the DRAWN triangle plus the paving rung, never heightAt. Everything standing in the court — palm trunks, boulders, bed decals — seats on that same datum, so the court has ONE datum and nothing in it can disagree about where the floor is.
draw.wellFaceProudNote: Cladding, doors, windows and fixtures are offset this far outward of the well ring's chord plane so they read against the massing's own inner wall instead of z-fighting it. A render offset, not a measurement.
draw.railProudNote: The guard stands on stub posts just proud of the slab edge, which is what _3 shows; this is the render offset that expresses it.
draw.boulderBuryNote: A granite boulder set in a decomposed-granite bed sits INTO it; each boulder's underside is sunk this fraction of its own radius below the court datum, which is why the court's 'nothing sinks' gate is written against the datum minus this figure and not against the datum. A boulder that does not sit into its bed reads as a ball.
draw.finProudNote: The outer facade's fin proud/return figures are unchanged from the shipped section and are read off the 2013 west-end frame, which is pre-repaint and therefore geometry-only — exactly the use that frame is licensed for.
draw.surveyOvershootNote: Between grid.parapetTop (10.59 m) and grid.roofSlab (12.40 m) the OUTER elevations have no building in them: that band is set-back roof terrace in the real Blake. The drawn mass is flat-topped, so the band is dressed as plain precast and labelled for what it is. See conflicts['flat-topped-mass'] — this is the section's largest open item and it is not the section's to fix.
draw.slabEdgeProudNote: The gallery slab edge reads BELOW the rail as its own line in _3; this is the render offset that keeps that line off the cladding plane it would otherwise z-fight. A render offset, not a measurement.
draw.membraneInsetNote: How far inside the drawn ring the membrane decal stops, so the field does not bleed over the rim of the extruded mass. It was previously taken from roof.coping.width, which made a render inset depend on a piece of withheld geometry; it is a render offset and it is declared here as one.

grid.solve: 12.40 = 4 x 3.10 with ZERO residual, and the parapet is INSIDE that height, not on top of it: terrace deck 9.30 + parapet 1.29 = 10.59, and the Level 4 roof slab stands 1.81 m proud of it. The shipped 12.4 = 4 x 2.8 + 1.2 also closed arithmetically but put four full storeys under a parapet that stands proud of all of them, which the photograph refutes.
grid.anchorNote: [measured] The stack is read off vmarch-bradley_VMA_UCSDBlake_67.jpg: grade 1046 -> colonnade fascia 909 -> L3 head 772 -> L4 floor 635 -> L4 roof slab 498, four EXACT 137 px steps with every line an independently visible feature. Three unrelated methods cluster on the storey: the photograph's own fin-pitch scale gives 2.93 m, the arcgis levels x 3.05 residential FORMULA gives 3.05 (corroboration only — a formula may never be cited as a height), and the LiDAR 12.4/4 gives 3.10. Spread 0.17 m. LiDAR decides height, so 3.10 is built and the shipped 2.8 m [estimated] guess is retired.
grid.bayNote: 30 bays over the full south elevation [measured, vmarch-bradley_VMA_UCSDBlake_67.jpg, near-orthographic] — foreshortening-immune. Confirmed INDEPENDENTLY of the shipped value by peak detection on the intensity profile across the L2 and L3 glazing bands (a clean run at 322, 384, 447, 508, 569, 630, 692 ... and 1477, 1534, 1596, 1653, 1711 ...), median pitch ~60 px against 1797 px / 37.5 m = 47.9 px/m, i.e. 60/47.9 = 1.25 m = 37.5/30. Module = measured face length / 30 = 1.25 m. The inventory's absolute 1.88 m bay was read at an assumed anchor against a 58 m elevation the LiDAR ring draws at 37.5 m; counts win. The ORTHO cross-check is at its resolution limit and must NOT be used to referee: peak detection over the laid-over south facade returns 25 peaks / 1.46 m pitch, but the true module is 10 px at 8 px/m, right at Nyquist, so under-counting is expected — it corroborates the order of magnitude and cannot decide 30 vs 25. The sibling DIFFERENCE from Argo survives in what fills the bay (a large glazed panel at 0.85 of the bay against Argo's 0.66 narrow window) and in the storey counts (2 fin storeys against Argo's 5). The inventory's count-vs-ratio conflict is carried in conflicts['bay-ratio'].
grid.penthouseNote: RETIRED AND REPLACED. The shipped note claimed the set-back storey 'lives below the flat-topped 12.4 m drawn LiDAR maximum ... the set-back cannot be carved'. The first half is backwards — the 12.4 m IS the top of the set-back storey (derivations.figures['grid.roofSlab']) — and the storey's plan is measurable and is now in level4. The second half is still true and is the section's open item: see conflicts['flat-topped-mass'].

parts.what: accommodation — Vasquez Marshall's fourth floor Residence Lounge, the Dean's apartment and offices, photographed from inside in _39 (signed 'level 4 LOUNGE'), _12r (a kitchen opening to a terrace) and _40 (an apartment terrace)
accommodation, 9.0 m deep — the mirror of the west leg across the well, and the shallower of the two because the ortho puts the bar east edge 1.7 m inside the drawn ring against 0.6 m on the west

the 1.3 m gallery walkway round the north side of the court — exactly what _3 photographs on the far side of the well, and the strip that makes the ortho north grid structure most likely a pergola over the gallery rather than a free-standing roof trellis
the 1.3 m gallery walkway round the south side of the court — the same 1.3 m strip as the north, and the plan position of the second unresolved grid structure the ortho reads at the well lip

terraces.what: 9.3 m deep, full width, at deck level 9.30 m behind the 10.59 m parapet. THIS is where the mechanical screen stands.
9.5 m deep, full width. Clean membrane, stains, vents. _67 shows a white picket guardrail standing on the parapet at the west end, so at least part of it is an occupied terrace and not bare roof.

level4.note: MEASURED PLAN, UNBUILT VOLUME. The plan is the ortho's raised plate corrected by the recon's own +1.1/+3.6 top displacement, and the height decomposition is derivations.figures. The VOLUME is not built and neither are the terraces: campus-massing.js extrudes Blake's drawn ring flat to 12.4 m, so a 9.30 m terrace deck would be three metres inside a solid mass — invisible, and intersecting, which this project forbids. Better absent than wrong. THE SHIPPED CLAIM THAT A SINGLE EDIT WOULD MAKE THIS BUILDABLE IS WITHDRAWN (R2 item B1): what is and is not recorded is now stated exactly in conflicts['flat-topped-mass'], and the largest gap is that the bar has no facade system of any kind.
level4.terraceNote: 'Full width' is now a number on both terraces: x0/x1 are the drawn ring's own x extents (derivations.figures['level4.terraceX0'/'level4.terraceX1']), not prose. Both decks are at grid.terraceDeck 9.30 m; `depth` is the z depth, not a height.

bands.note: Re-measured off _67 at 46.8 px/m in the one strip: spandrel band 27 px and opening 110 px of a 137 px storey, so spandrel + opening = 1 exactly; the bottom-hinged awning sash is 40-45 px, taken at its 42.5 px midpoint. The SHIPPED fractions (spandrel 0.333, awning 0.13, panel 0.537) are the LOSING read and are carried in conflicts['band-fractions'] rather than deleted — the shipped note already confessed its awning/panel ratio was drifting to 0.24 against a sourced ~1/5, and this read pushes further the same way.

fin.note: white precast fins between bays, storey-tall, stopping at the spandrel bands; faceted/stepped in section — a wider flat face plus a narrow return [measured]

surveyOvershoot.note: The band from grid.parapetTop (10.59 m) to grid.roofSlab (12.40 m). In the real Blake there is NO building here on the north and south elevations — it is open roof terrace 9.4 m behind. The drawn mass is flat-topped at 12.40 m, so the band is dressed as plain precast and named for what it is. Renamed from the shipped `upperBand`, whose note called it 'the set-back penthouse level' — it is not the penthouse, it is the survey's overshoot over the terrace.

parapet.note: The outer parapet is the upstand around the Level 4 roof terrace: it starts at the 9.30 m terrace deck and tops out at 10.59 m, 1.29 m [measured, 57 px on _67]. It is INSIDE the 12.4 m, not on top of it. Precast panel joints at roughly every 2 bays [measured].

glazedGrid.note: east end wall treatment [measured, webcor-argo-N17.jpg]: a glazed grid with mullions and flat pilasters over the fin-storey band

storefront.note: Recessed glazed storefront behind the colonnade, differentiated by its bay rhythm and nothing else. ONE mullion per bay boundary (pitchBays 1) on the measured 1.25 m module — see reads['ground.storefront.mullionPitch'] — running the full glazing height, at the stock 2 in face derivations.figures['system.ground.storefrontMullion'] derives. skipEnds 1 drops the boundary at each end of every face, which is the building corner and not a mullion. NO LETTERING and NO per-bay tenancy: signage.built is false because no text mechanism exists in this renderer, and which bay is a door, a shopfront or the solid panel is declared in absent[]. This is the round-2 critic's storefront-differentiation minor answered at the level the source actually supports — the rhythm is sourced, the layout is not.

Its existence on the north, east and west is [estimated]: the sourced south pattern extended, mirroring Argo's west-face declaration — see estimates['system.ground']. wellFace.note: THE WELL FACES ARE A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT SYSTEM FROM THE OUTER ELEVATIONS, and this is the single biggest gain over the shipped section, which extended ARGO's courtyard language into a well it had painted a lid over. Sourced directly from _3 and _25 (both 2014-01-12): gallery access on levels 2, 3 and 4; a pale white metal guard of closely-pitched vertical pickets between a flat top rail and a mid rail, carried on stub posts standing off the slab edge, with the slab edge reading below the rail as a separate line; pale white HORIZONTAL BOARD cladding behind the gallery, not precast fins; a repeating bay of a dark-framed glazed room door plus a window with a square wall-mounted light fixture between bays. The core notch's four faces take the same language and the galleries pass it.
wellFace.depthNote: The gallery walkway's open DEPTH is not built. The drawn mass is solid where the walkway is open, so a projecting deck would be geometry inside a wall; the section dresses the well-face plane with the gallery's sourced language and declares the depth absent. The L4 strips measure 1.3 m in plan (level4.parts) if a future stepped mass wants it.

wellFace.faceBaysNote: THE SHIPPED BAY IS PER FACE, AND THIS TABLE IS IT. `bayModule` 3.75 m is the GENERATOR NOMINAL — the divisor that decides how many bays a face gets — and it is NOT the bay that ships on any face. The builder fits a whole number of bays to each surveyed face length (bays = round(length / 3.75), at least 1) and divides the face by it, so a 16.401 m face ships 4 bays of 4.1003 m and a 6.601 m face ships 2 of 3.3004 m. That is a legitimate per-face fit against a measured ring, not drift, and the geometry is unchanged by this record; what was wrong was the DOCUMENT, which declared one 3.75 m bay and one 2.4292 m window and then drew a -18.5%/+14.4% spread around them with nothing saying so. Every figure here is derived from `measured.courtyardRing` by the arithmetic in derivations.faceBayFit and is re-derived from the ring, and compared to the BUILT scene face by face, in tests/campus-photo-blake.test.mjs. 5 faces carry room bays, 3 are the solid core and carry none; 16 bays x 4 levels = 64, which is the shipped wellDoors and wellWindows.
wellFace.bayModuleNote: GENERATOR NOMINAL, not a shipped dimension. It is the 3 x system.bayModule figure the fit divides by; the bay that ships on each face is in faceBays. The nominal identity bayModule = doorWidth + windowWidth + 2 x boardPitch still holds and is still gated — it is what makes 3.75 the right divisor — but `windowWidth` 2.4292 is likewise the nominal consequent and not the width of any shipped window.

court.note: THE WELL IS OPEN. The shipped roof.courtyard decal capped it 'AT the drawn roof plane with no visible void', and four independent sources say otherwise: the survey itself (massing[58] carries two rings and campus-massing.js pushes every ring after the first into shape.holes, so the extruder has always built this void); the 2026 Google ortho, looking straight down at crowns, beds, paving and the crowns' shadows on a floor eleven metres below; Vasquez Marshall, whose own scope includes 'a completely renovated courtyard concept at the building's center'; and two photographs taken INSIDE it. The floor is at surfaceAt on the paving rung, and everything in the court seats on that one datum.
