screen.note: cream/tan checkerboard MECHANICAL SCREEN enclosure on the north roof terrace [measured plan, chunk_4_6.jpg, registered to the drawn ring]. ADJUDICATION 2026-08-18 HOLDS and is RE-VERIFIED: the prior build read this field as a dark-blue PV array — a source-reading error. Genuine PV in the SAME imagery (Keeling rooftops, chunk_4_6 / ortho-keeling-east) is unmistakably dark blue; this field samples #b6af9b at world (-38, 318.5), a warm grey-cream, a checkerboard of ~35-40 blocks over a screened enclosure, measured 12.4 x 7.1 m. The LOSING PV read stays recorded and is not built: x -53.5..-25.5, z 317.6..321.8, 2 rows of 1.9x1.0 panels, colours #26303c/#8a8d90. Its TRUE deck is the 9.30 m north roof terrace (`deck`), which is what the ortho and level4 say; IT IS NO LONGER BUILT. The shipped compromise stood it on the drawn 12.40 m roof plane, where its [estimated] 2.00 m enclosure plus 0.45 m blocks top out at 14.91 m — 2.51 m ABOVE the measured LiDAR maximum this whole section is anchored on, and 4.32 m over the parapet. That magnitude was never on the record. At its recorded true 9.30 m deck it would top at 11.75 m and clear the anchor comfortably, but that deck is three metres inside a solid flat-topped mass, so there is nowhere to seat it. Withheld under roof.anchorGate; plan, tone and the not-PV adjudication all KEPT — see conflicts['flat-topped-mass'] and absent[]. Enclosure and block heights [estimated] — no oblique exists.

vents.note: round white-curbed roof penetrations [measured plan, chunk_4_6.jpg]: four large curbed vents at the Level 4 bar's corners, smaller ones across the plates. The R1 re-read of the ortho puts the four large ones at corrected (-49.4, 326.1) (-30.0, 325.7) (-49.4, 343.1) (-29.9, 342.9); the SHIPPED positions are within ~1.3 m of these and are already registered to the drawn ring, so they are KEPT rather than churned. Curb height and cap [estimated]. NOT BUILT: a 0.5 m curb plus its cap on the drawn 12.40 m plane stands above the measured LiDAR maximum (roof.anchorGate), and the 9.30 m terrace deck seven of them belong to is inside solid mass. The twelve measured plans and their levels are KEPT; the geometry is withheld — see absent[].
vents.levelNote: EVERY item carries `level`: "terrace" (the 9.30 m roof-terrace deck, grid.terraceDeck) or "bar" (the 12.40 m Level 4 bar roof, grid.roofSlab). Classified by testing each measured plan position against the level4 rectangle (x -57.5..-22.0, z 325.1..344.2) and its parts: 7 terrace, 5 bar. Before this the twelve were undifferentiated, so the moment the massing carries a stepped top seven of them would float 3.10 m over the terrace they belong to with nothing in the document to say so.

trellises.note: NOT BUILT. Two grid structures ~14.3 m long at the well's north and south lips [measured plan, chunk_4_6.jpg, corrected]. Their LEVEL is unresolved and a nadir ortho cannot separate 'at the roof plane' from 'at the Level 4 gallery'. Now that the L4 gallery strips are known to sit at exactly z 325.1..326.4 and z 342.9..344.2, these two grids COINCIDE with them in plan, and the likeliest reading is that they are the galleries themselves or a pergola over them rather than free-standing roof trellises. The shipped build put them at the roof plane on a 2.6 m [estimated] beam height; that is a guess at an unresolved section and it is withdrawn. Declared, not guessed.

roof.plateNote: There is ONE roof plane, the drawn 12.40 m. The shipped roof.plates raised an inner plate 0.4 m [estimated] over outer bands on shadow lines at z 324.3 / 344.6, which put geometry 12.80 m over grade — ABOVE the LiDAR maximum the whole section is anchored on — on an estimate. It is withdrawn. The real step is the other way and is three metres, not 0.4 m: the Level 4 bar's plan (level4) is the measured version of those shadow lines, and everything outside it is terrace 3.10 m BELOW, which the flat-topped mass cannot express.

anchorGate.anchorSource: docs/data/campus-lidar.json heights['Blake Hall'] = massHeights['m:-43,330'] = 12.4 m, read at build time. The two LiDAR reads AGREE, so this anchor is not itself contested; the only competing figure in the section is the campus-3d builder's 15.6 m on the SUPPRESSED OSM ring, which measured.heightNote already records as a losing read.
anchorGate.note: THE ROOF-PLACEMENT CEILING IS THE MEASURED LiDAR MAXIMUM, not a figure derived from the roof block being gated (R2 item B2; audit-blake major 2). The retired gate read `roofY + screen.enclosureHeight + screen.blockHeight + 0.5`, so whatever the screen said its height was, the screen passed. Under the new ceiling the R1 build put 65 solid placements above the anchor, to +2.510 m — the same sin roof.plates was withdrawn for, six times larger. Nothing is re-seated below the anchor because there is nowhere below it to stand: the only lower datum in this building is the 9.30 m terrace deck, which is three metres INSIDE a solid flat-topped mass. So the coping, the mechanical screen and the vent geometry are WITHHELD, their measured plans kept, and each is declared in absent[] with the frame that would settle it. What still draws on the roof is the membrane, which is a decal ON the drawn surface and is lifted only by the repo's own declared pad rung. The ceiling is never widened to admit a placement.

south.source: vmarch-bradley_VMA_UCSDBlake_67.jpg (near-orthographic, dusk, EXIF 2014-01-12) — the wall is the foreground subject across the full frame

profile.rule: exposed(u) = piecewise-linear interpolation of the three station figures at u = 0, knee and 1, where u is the fraction of the wall's own a->b length, west to east. The DRAWN height at u is height + (exposed(u) - exposed(0)): the measured non-uniformity carried ADDITIVELY onto the retained 1.35 m scalar, so the datum disagreement stays exactly where conflicts['lava-height'] put it and only the SHAPE of the wall changes. That gives 1.350 m at the west end, 1.360 m at the knee and 2.355 m at the east end, which is the 'about 1.2 m across the western two-thirds, past 2.2 m toward the east end' this entry has always stated in prose and never drew.
profile.note: THE WALL IS NOT ONE HEIGHT, and the shipped scalar said so in prose while the geometry ignored it — every rock row rode the terrain at a fixed offset, which on flat drawn ground is a wall of constant 1.35 m. The three stations are already derived (derivations.figures['lavaWall.exposedWest'], ['lavaWall.exposedMid'], ['lavaWall.exposedEast'], read at image x 800, 1250 and 1600 of _67 with their own local scales); this is the rule that puts them on the geometry. The knee at two-thirds is [estimated] — see estimates['ground.south.lavaWall.profileKnee'] — because the stations' image positions do not convert to world positions without a frame registration this section does not have.

lavaWall.note: substantial lava-rock rubble retaining wall — dark reddish-brown angular volcanic rock, no coping, wrapping the raised lawn terrace; the best instance on campus of the Revelle lava-rock walls. THIS SECTION IS THE SOLE OWNER: revelle.lavaWalls.items[30..44] is the SAME wall shipped twice and interpenetrating (identical extent to the metre, centrelines 0.1 m apart, thicknesses 0.5 and 0.7) — see superseded['revelle.lavaWalls#30-44']. HEIGHT 1.35 is kept: the R1 re-measurement gives 1.16 +/- 0.08 m at two western stations, which sits just below it, and the difference is inside one bad base-line pick, so it is recorded in conflicts['lava-height'] rather than churned. NON-UNIFORM, and this is the important part: it is a retaining wall on falling ground, ~1.2 m across the western two-thirds growing past 2.2 m toward the east end as the lawn drops away — a single scalar height is an average of something that nearly doubles. THICKNESS 0.5 is [estimated], not measured, and never was: see estimates. The END WRAPS are SOURCED AND UNBUILT: in _67 the wall visibly wraps at both ends rather than stopping square — the east wrap is unmistakable, turning south past the Roger's Market bay — and its west end reads further west than a straight -54 endpoint at that depth would project; but the frame gives neither wrap a length nor a bearing and both run out of it, so a return of invented extent would be a fabrication and they are declared in absent[] instead. THE DEFECT THEY WERE BLAMED FOR IS NOT THEIRS: the round-2 critic's hovering green plane was the raised lawn deck, which _67 refutes outright — see terrace, now built:false, and conflicts['terrace-step']. Daylight colour per the prior inventory's #6e4b3b-#8e6b54 estimate; the dusk sample #b5916e is recorded and not used.

terrace.note: MEASURED PLAN, UNBUILT DECK (visual round 2, 2026-08-21). The plan and the lift are kept as the record; the deck is NOT drawn, for two reasons that arrived together. FIRST, THE MATERIAL WAS INVERTED: _67 shows the ground the wall retains is the PAVED colonnade apron — Roger's Market and the Commuter Lounge open onto it, the bike racks stand on it, a member of staff is standing on it in the frame — and the GRASS is the LOWER ground falling away SOUTH of the wall, on the plaza side. The shipped note had this exactly backwards ('raised lawn terrace behind the wall') and drew a green plane on the building side. SECOND, THE LIFT HAS NOTHING TO STAND ON: 1.1 m is an [estimated] stand-in for a grade step the 2014 LiDAR terrain does not carry — sampled along z=357.6 from x=-56 to x=-20 the drawn surface runs 23.79 to 23.84 m, flat to 0.05 m over 36 m and to 0.03 m across the wall line. Drawn against that flat surface the deck became a green plane hovering 1.2 m over the plaza with open daylight under its east, west and north edges, and its north edge at z=354 sliced the colonnade columns, whose south faces reach z=354.17 at the west end. That is what the round-2 critic caught at standing eye height in az135-low, az225-high and az090-low. Better absent than wrong: the wall is measured and ships, the grade step it retains is not in the drawn terrain and is not invented into it. See conflicts['terrace-step'] and absent[]. The ground here is the plaza section's, which is what this block's own module comment has always said.

blake.colorNote: THE SHIPPED PREMISE WAS FALSE. It read 'Blake was repainted white in the same programme as Argo, so the base whites are Argo's DAYLIGHT precast values'. The Vasquez Marshall photographs are EXIF-dated 2014-01-12/13 and show Blake already white and finished; Webcor's Argo renovation ran 2015-16. Two projects, two dates, two contractors — the borrowing had no basis. NOTHING HERE JUSTIFIES BORROWING ANY LONGER (R2 colour rulings C0, C-column, C-mullion, C-parapet, C-precastAmbient, C-spandrel, C-windowFrosted). Five roles that were byte-identical copies of Argo's hexes — column, parapet, precastAmbient, spandrel, windowFrosted — are REMOVED and declared absent; they are drawn in `precast` per colorFallback, which is a fallback and not a source. `mullion` is kept UNDER PROTEST as a pragmatic call with no evidential weight (see its colorSources line). What remains is ONE declared borrowed white, `precast`, and the family that hangs off it — not six copies pretending to be six independent reads, which is what two buildings holding the same hex because one copied the other actually is. The Blake-specific evidence is _67's dusk strip, where every surface samples in the #ce-#e0 NEUTRAL range against the shipped tan #c4bcb0 / #cdc6ba: Blake reads PALER AND MORE NEUTRAL than what ships. But _67 is civil twilight with blue-sky fill and warm interior spill (a sample on an L3 fin came back #f8d9b3, pure interior spill), so it is usable for RELATIVE ORDERING ONLY and cannot replace the values. The retained whites are therefore KEPT and RE-TIERED [estimated — Argo daylight values, borrowed], the dusk samples are on the record in colorSources, and the whole group is replaceable the day a daylight Blake elevation appears. The Jul 2022 backlit Street View samples (#5b595e-#6d6863) stay recorded as unusable. The pre-repaint 2013 frames and every LiDAR-2014-derived tan are a dead epoch.

terraceLawn.source: [estimated] the raised lawn terrace behind the lava wall; a neutral irrigated-turf green, unsampled — _67 is dusk. RENAMED from `lawn` (R2 colour ruling C-lawn): the shared name went to plaza's measured #6f8054 and this value KEEPS its own hex. It is Blake's raised terrace lawn behind the lava wall, a different piece of ground from the plaza turf, and it must not be read as a second opinion about the same grass. The value is unchanged and the tier is unchanged.

conflicts.what: THE SECTION'S LARGEST OPEN ITEM. Blake's real top is a step: the outer donut stops at a 10.59 m parapet and a 35.5 x 19.1 m Level 4 bar stands 1.81 m proud of it to 12.40 m, with 9.3 m and 9.5 m roof terraces at a 9.30 m deck between them. The DRAWN mass is a flat-topped extrusion at 12.40 m, because campus-massing.js extrudes one ring to one height.
sides: The photograph and the ortho, which measure the step and give its plan to the decimetre (level4, derivations.figures).
The drawn massing, which has no mechanism for a stepped top and which this section may not edit.
conflicts.resolution: NOT AVERAGED AND NOT FAKED. The measurement is recorded complete in level4 with built:false; the geometry is not built, because a 9.30 m terrace deck inside a solid 12.40 m mass is invisible and intersecting, and this project forbids both. The band from 10.59 m to 12.40 m on the outer elevations is dressed as plain precast under the honest name system.surveyOvershoot. Arbitration should decide whether Blake's mass gains a stepped top. WHAT THE RECORD ACTUALLY HOLDS, stated exactly, because the shipped claim that the record was a single edit short of buildable was FALSE and is withdrawn (R2 item B1). RECORDED: the bar's plan (level4.x0/x1/z0/z1, derived from the ortho with the recon's imported displacement); the height decomposition (grid.terraceDeck 9.30, grid.parapetTop 10.59, grid.roofSlab 12.40, grid.slabProud 1.81); the four programme parts with their extents; both terraces with x AND z extents and their 9.30 m deck; every roof vent's level (7 terrace / 5 bar); and the membrane's three-plane split at the bar edges (roof.membrane.split). NOT RECORDED, and each is work rather than an edit: THE LEVEL 4 BAR HAS NO FACADE SYSTEM AT ALL — no bay module, no fenestration, no parapet or guard for the set-back storey, so built today it would be a blank 35.5 x 19.1 m box; the two trellises' level is unresolved (roof.trellises, built:false); the roof-terrace guard's type and extent are unsourced (absent[]); and the roof furniture that would stand on the terraces is itself withheld under the LiDAR-anchor ruling (absent[]). So the record is four pieces short of buildable, and one of the four is not an edit at all but unstarted work.

conflicts.what: Whether there is a grade step across the lava wall's line at all, in the terrain this project draws.
sides: _67 (EXIF 2014-01-12), which photographs a retaining wall with 1.16 m of exposed face at its west station and 2.17 m at its east, and lower ground falling away south of it. A wall with that much exposed face is retaining something, and the section measures it three times.

docs/data/campus-lidar.json terrain, the 2014 ground surface this project draws, which along z=357.6 from x=-56 to x=-20 runs 23.79 to 23.84 m: flat to 0.05 m over 36 m, and to 0.03 m across the wall line itself. There is no step in it to retain.
conflicts.resolution: DECLARED, NOT AVERAGED, AND NOT INVENTED. The wall is built where it is measured and at the height it is measured, now carrying its measured non-uniformity (ground.south.lavaWall.profile). The grade step is NOT modelled into the terrain, because terrain is LiDAR's and this section may not edit it. The shipped compromise — a 1.1 m raised lawn deck standing on the flat drawn surface — is WITHDRAWN: it was an invented terrain step wearing a lawn's clothes, it hovered on three edges, it cut the colonnade columns, and _67 shows the ground it claimed to be is paving rather than grass. The honest consequence is that the wall stands on flat drawn ground and visibly retains nothing, which is a smaller and truer error than a green plane a metre in the air across the front of the building. A 2026 terrain source, or a LiDAR rebuild that resolves the step, closes this.

conflicts.what: Blake's completion year. The FIRM is no longer in doubt — Tucker, Sadler & Bennett is corroborated twice independently — but the year is.
sides: 1967 — modernsandiego.com's project list for the firm (Argo Hall 1967, Blake Hall 1967, both Revelle College), and the 2013-09-13 flickr caption that is the ORIGIN of this repo's inherited claim.
1968 — Vasquez Marshall, the architect of the renovation, who had the original drawings: 'Originally constructed in 1968'.
conflicts.resolution: DECLARED, NOT AVERAGED. This is the classic design-vs-occupancy one-year split. The label stops asserting 1967 flat and points here. revelle-recon.md Rung 2 item 14 flagged the whole attribution as unverified inherited; the firm half of that flag is now closed and the year half is not.

conflicts.what: The within-storey band fractions of the outer facade — how much of a 3.10 m storey is the solid spandrel between floors, how much is the glazed opening, and how much of that opening the projecting awning sash takes.
sides: SHIPPED (losing): spandrelFrac 0.333, awningFrac 0.13, panelFrac 0.537. Its own note already confessed a drift — 'awning/panel = 0.13/0.537 = 0.24, nearer 1/4 than the sourced ~1/5'.
R1 (built): spandrel 27/137 = 0.197, opening 110/137 = 0.803, awning 42.5/137 = 0.310 — so the spandrel is THINNER and the awning much DEEPER (0.386 of the opening, not 0.24).
conflicts.resolution: The R1 read wins because it is taken at 46.8 px/m in a single strip of a near-orthographic frame and because spandrel + opening closes to 1 exactly. But it is ONE frame, so the shipped fractions are recorded as the losing read rather than deleted. Note that the R1 read pushes FURTHER in the direction the shipped note already knew it was drifting, which is weak corroboration of the direction if not the magnitude.

conflicts.what: The inventory's anchor-immune bay:floor ratio for Blake, 0.618, against the built count.
sides: The ratio 0.618 (against Argo's 0.435, called the single most important difference between the two buildings) times 30 bays and the storey implies a ~67 m elevation.
The drawn ring draws the south face at 37.5 m, and 30 bays over it is a 1.25 m module — which INVERTS the ~1.4x-wider sibling relationship the ratios describe (Blake 1.25 against Argo 1.28).
conflicts.resolution: Counts win per the ring; the losing ratios stay on the record for a future drawing to referee. Carried forward unchanged from the shipped section — R1 did not re-open it and found no new evidence either way.

conflicts.what: The roof membrane field colour and the colour of its patch staining — the two hexes the code-generated membrane texture is baked from, so between them they decide what the whole of Blake roof looks like.
sides: SHIPPED (losing): membraneBase #dad6cc, membraneStain #b07a52 — a warm off-white with rust staining, inherited from Argo's roof on the one-repaint-programme premise.
R1 (built): #ebf0ee field (north plate; #f1f2f6 south) with #d5d6d7 staining, both measured off the daylight nadir ortho.
conflicts.resolution: The ortho measurement wins: it is a daylight nadir sample of THIS roof, and the premise that licensed borrowing Argo's values is refuted (colorNote). The shipped values are recorded here.

conflicts.what: The courtyard colours — the floor, the planting beds, and the water feature the previous build placed at the centre of the well, all of which descend from the same reads on the same imagery.
sides: SHIPPED (losing, and WRONG): plantingDark #2e333b, waterDark #1d232b, and the note 'the rest of the floor is dark planting'. Every one of those descends from ortho samples INSIDE the well — #31474a, #414f5c, #3d4953 — taken when the court is in FULL SHADE at that sun angle. That is shadow sampled as material.
R1 (built): _25 and _3, in daylight from inside, show light grey concrete paving, tan decomposed granite, pale grey granite boulders, green fan palms and chartreuse umbrellas.
conflicts.resolution: The dark palette is NOT carried forward. The retired hexes are recorded here so the mistake is legible; the water feature and basin they coloured are withdrawn with them — see absent[].

conflicts.what: What is planted in the court, and therefore what the five crowns the ortho reads in plan actually are — fan palms with fibrous trunks, or something twelve years older than the only photographs that see them.
sides: Jan 2014 (_25, _3): Washingtonia fan palms with thick fibrous trunks, decomposed granite, grey granite boulders, agave and succulents.
2026 (chunk_4_6.jpg): five broad lumpy crowns, in shade.
conflicts.resolution: NOT RECONCILED — twelve years apart and both probably right about their own year, which is the repo's epoch rule exactly. The build takes PLAN and crown radii from 2026 (the only source that gives positions) and SPECIES and materials from 2014 (the only sources that see the court). Both reads are dated in court.palmNote. The 2026 state of the planting is declared absent.

conflicts.what: The exposed height of the south lava-rock retaining wall — the figure the whole rubble course count is built from, and the one the shipped section carried as measured on the strength of a 1.2-1.5 m source band rather than a measurement.
sides: SHIPPED (built): 1.35 m, inside the note's declared 1.2-1.5 m source band.
R1 re-measurement off _67 at three stations, distance-corrected: 1.16 m, 1.17 m and ~2.2 m, giving 1.16 +/- 0.08 m (1.08-1.24) for the western two-thirds.
conflicts.resolution: 1.35 IS KEPT. The direct measurement favours ~1.2 m and sits just below the shipped value, but the difference is inside one bad base-line pick and churning a shipped figure on a single re-read is not worth it. What IS carried is the finding the shipped section did not have: the wall is a retaining wall on FALLING GROUND and is not uniform — ~1.2 m across the western two-thirds growing past 2.2 m toward the east end. A single scalar is an average of something that nearly doubles, and ground.south.lavaWall.note now says so.

absent#1.retired: Courtyard interior: galleries, rails, palms — the drawn massing opens the courtyard well but nothing below the roof-plane cap is sourced; only the roof-plane read is built (the decal caps the drawn opening), its gallery language extended from Argo sourced courtyard [estimated].
absent#1.why: FALSE at both ends. 'Nothing below the roof-plane cap is sourced' is refuted by vmarch-bradley_VMA_UCSDBlake_3.jpg and _25.jpg, both EXIF 2014-01-12, which photograph the court from inside on two levels; and the Argo extension it fell back on was extending the WRONG BUILDING's language — the well faces are pale horizontal board cladding with picket-guarded galleries, a completely different system from Argo's precast courtyard. The entry is RETIRED, not deleted: it stays verbatim in absent[] and this record names its successors.
absent#1.claims: the courtyard interior — galleries, rails and palms — which the retired entry withheld
absent#1.countNote: 8 dressed well faces carrying the gallery system on three levels, plus 5 palms and 5 beds in an open court. The retired entry withheld ALL of it, so this is a transfer from nothing to something and the count is the successor's, not a reduction.

revelle.lavaWalls#30-44.retired: revelle.lavaWalls.items[30..44] — 15 segments at 2 m pitch spanning x -54..-24 at z 357.5, height 0.75, thickness 0.7, sourced to 'Revelle_Plaza.jpg (2006), Argo_Hall.jpg (2012)'.
revelle.lavaWalls#30-44.why: The same wall, shipped twice and interpenetrating: identical extent to the metre, centrelines 0.1 m apart, thicknesses 0.5 and 0.7, so the two solids overlap through almost their whole section. Blake wins the ladder and by more than a summary suggests — revelle.lavaWalls carries ONE height and thickness for all 45 segments including the two plaza runs at x 32 and x 45, so its 0.75/0.7 is a COLLEGE-WIDE DEFAULT and never a Blake measurement, and its two cited sources are undated generic filenames. Blake's figures come from a near-orthographic, precisely dated (2014-01-12) photograph in which this wall is the foreground subject across the full frame. THE REMAINING 30 PLAZA SEGMENTS KEEP THE 0.75/0.7 DEFAULT — this adjudication says nothing about them. The retirement itself is the PLAZA builder's docket, not this section's: this record is the adjudication, and blake claims sole ownership of the geometry.
revelle.lavaWalls#30-44.claims: revelle.lavaWalls.items[30..44] — the 15 segments of the Blake south lava wall
revelle.lavaWalls#30-44.countNote: A COUNT CHANGE, declared as a count and not only in prose: 15 retired revelle segments are replaced by ONE continuous blake run (ground.south.lavaWall a->b), built as 165 rubble instances. 15 -> 1 is a change in how the wall is described, not in how much wall exists — the extent is identical to the metre, which is the whole reason the two interpenetrated.

counts.note: windows = 3 panel faces x 2 fin storeys x 30 bays + the east grid one field. fins = 3 x 2 x 31 bay boundaries. columns = 4 faces x ceil(30/3). wellFaces = every segment of the drawn inner ring, the core notch three included. wellDoors/wellWindows = 16 bays over the FIVE non-core faces x 4 levels: the three core-notch faces carry cladding, slab edge and guard but NO room bay, because the notch is solid stair/lift core and nothing photographs it (R2 item B4/7). wellRailRuns is top + mid + BOTTOM rail on 3 gallery levels x 8 faces — the bottom rail is new: _3 holds the picket panel off the deck over an open third (R2 item B4/6). membraneBands is FIVE: four round the open well and a fifth over that same solid notch, which the four were cutting a 3.0 x 2.9 m hole in (R2 item B4/8) — one rectangle, notchRect, feeds both. groundMullions is the storefront rhythm: 4 faces x (30 bays - 2 x skipEnds 1 + 1) = 4 x 29 = 116, one mullion on every bay boundary but the building corners (visual round 2). wellPickets is the IBC 4-inch-sphere pitch counted along each face. courtFloorCells is the 1 m tessellation of the well whose cell centres fall inside the drawn inner ring — it moves only if the ring does. NO screenBlocks AND NO vents: the mechanical screen and the twelve vent curbs stood above the measured LiDAR anchor and are withheld — see roof.anchorGate and absent[].

absent: RETIRED — see superseded['absent#1']. Kept verbatim because absent lists do not shrink: 'Courtyard interior: galleries, rails, palms — the drawn massing opens the courtyard well but nothing below the roof-plane cap is sourced; only the roof-plane read is built (the decal caps the drawn opening), its gallery language extended from Argo sourced courtyard [estimated].'

The Level 4 VOLUME and its two roof terraces. The plan is measured to the decimetre and is in level4; the geometry is not built, because campus-massing.js extrudes Blake's ring flat to 12.40 m and a 9.30 m terrace deck would be three metres inside a solid mass — invisible and intersecting. See conflicts['flat-topped-mass']. This replaces the shipped claim that 'the set-back cannot be carved', which was true about the mass and wrong about the height.

Bay counts on the NORTH, EAST and WEST elevations. Ladder: photos — none near-orthographic on those faces; Street View — the Jul 2022 north pano is backlit and oblique; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the 2008 UCOP deck carries no Blake plan or elevation; archives — 1960s UCSD DC aerials show the roof, not the elevations. Every rung fails. The south's measured 1.25 m module is extended by count against each face's drawn length, which is what the module already does.

The WELL-FACE bay count, and the door and window widths as built. _3 is oblique and shot through a window at an angle; no orthographic view of a well face exists on any rung. The bay is built at 3 x the south's measured module — see estimates['wellFace.bayModule'] — and the true count stays unmeasured here.

The COURT FLOOR DATUM and any steps in it: whether the court floor sits at the surrounding grade or is stepped, and where. _25 shows a level threshold at the breezeway and nothing more; no rung resolves it. The floor is built at surfaceAt, which is the honest default and is declared as such in court.datum.

The BREEZEWAY that connects Revelle Plaza to the court. Sourced twice (it is where _25 was taken from, and UCOP 2008 p11 photographs it pre-repaint) but its plan position is given by nothing — neither its court end nor its plaza end — and the drawn mass has no opening for it. Recorded in court.breezeway with built:false.

The two TRELLIS structures at the well's north and south lips. Plan measured off the ortho; LEVEL unresolved, and a nadir ortho cannot separate 'at the roof plane' from 'at the Level 4 gallery' — with which they coincide in plan. The shipped build guessed a 2.6 m beam at the roof plane; that guess is withdrawn. Recorded in roof.trellises with built:false.

The Level 4 set-back on the EAST and WEST (1.7 m and 0.6 m). Both are inside the ortho's own registration tolerance of about +/-1.5 m after the displacement correction, so they are declared measured-but-at-tolerance and no 0.6 m step is built as if it were certain.

The ROOF-TERRACE GUARD type and extent on the north and south bands. _67 shows a white picket guardrail standing on the parapet at ONE location at the west end; whether it runs the whole terrace is unsourced.

The COURTYARD PLANTING in its 2026 state. The ortho's five crowns are in shade and are twelve years newer than the only photographs that see the court. The 2014 court is what is built and the gap is declared — see conflicts['court-epoch'].

The WATER FEATURE and round basin the shipped section built at the centre of the well. Their plan came from dark blobs in an ortho of a court in FULL SHADE, and the same shadow produced the plantingDark / waterDark palette that conflicts['court-palette'] retires. Neither daylight photograph of the court shows a water feature. Withdrawn rather than recoloured: a plan read out of a shadow is not a plan.

The GALLERY WALKWAY DEPTH inside the well. The galleries are open walkways; the drawn mass is solid where they are open, so the section dresses the well-face plane with their sourced language and does not project a deck. The 1.3 m plan strips are recorded in level4.parts for the day the mass can carry them.

'Blake Hall' parapet lettering, the Commuter Lounge circular hanging sign, Roger's Market lettering, street number 9259, the well faces' circular chartreuse level discs and rectangular banners, and the breezeway soffit's directional lettering — positions recorded; there is no text rendering in this renderer, which is a renderer limitation and not a source gap. NOTE, corrected: the Residence Lounge is on level 4 (_39 is signed 'level 4 LOUNGE') and the Commuter Lounge is on the ground floor (its circular window graphic is in _67). The shipped absent entry treated them as one sign; they are two rooms on two levels.

Movable court furniture: patio tables, sling chairs, chartreuse market umbrellas and the festoon lights strung diagonally across the court, all in _25 — and the three blue market umbrellas at the south colonnade in _67. Movable, not fixed to any measured position.

North-slope Torrey pines and mounded shrubs. They are real and they are in the Jul 2022 Street View, but trees and slope planting are landscape/LiDAR-owned across this whole project and are drawn from the survey, not from a building photo section; double-building them here would put two sets of trees on one slope.
The dumpsters and loading dock on the north service road — they belong to UCSD Machining & Additive Prototyping Services, NOT to Blake [sourced]; attributing them to Blake would be wrong twice.

Roof equipment HEIGHTS — the mechanical screen enclosure, its checker blocks and the vent curbs are all [estimated]; plan positions only are measured (chunk_4_6.jpg), because no oblique of this roof exists.

Lamp posts. Blake are globe-headed and are visible in _67 along the south apron, but campus lamp posts are the PLAZA section to place across Zone 1 as one family; building Blake own here would ship them twice, which is exactly the failure the lava wall supersession record exists to correct.

Blake own loading, trash and service specifics — where its bins stand, where deliveries arrive, where the service entry is. The ladder is exhausted: no photograph, pano, planning document or archive in this dossier shows any of it, and the one service yard visible nearby belongs to a different department. Left unbuilt rather than guessed onto a face.
Bike racks at the south colonnade — visible in the dusk elevation but with no measured plan positions; better absent than guessed onto the colonnade.

The lava wall's END WRAPS. In _67 the wall visibly wraps at both ends around the raised terrace rather than stopping square, and its west end reads further west than a straight -54 endpoint at that depth would project. The straight a->b run is kept and the wrap is unmodelled. EXPANDED 2026-08-21 (visual round 2), same claim, now with the ladder that keeps it absent and one correction. THE CORRECTION: 'around the raised terrace' is withdrawn — there is no raised terrace, see ground.south.terrace (built:false) and conflicts['terrace-step']; what the wall wraps is the grade change itself. THE LADDER, because round 2 asked for the wraps to be built: photos — _67 is the only frame that shows the wall's full run and BOTH wraps leave its frame, so it gives their existence and neither their length nor their bearing; Street View — no pano stands south of the wall; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the 2008 UCOP deck carries no Revelle site plan at this scale; archives — the 1960s UCSD DC aerials predate this grade. Every rung fails. A return of invented extent is a fabrication and this project forbids it, so the wall ships with square ends. What the round-2 critic saw hovering was never the wraps: it was the lawn deck, and that is what was withdrawn.

The ROOF COPING as geometry. A 0.25 x 0.4 m coping standing on the drawn 12.40 m plane tops out above the MEASURED LiDAR maximum for Blake (campus-lidar.json heights['Blake Hall'] = 12.4), which is exactly what roof.plates was withdrawn for; it also never carried a derivation, an estimates entry or a source line, and the real parapet is already capped at 10.59 m by the measured system.parapet.dripCap. Ladder: photos — no frame shows Blake's roof edge in section; Street View — the Jul 2022 north pano is backlit and oblique and sees no coping; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the 2008 UCOP deck carries no Blake roof detail; archives — the 1960s DC aerials are nadir. THE FRAME THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: any oblique or elevation resolving Blake's parapet cap in section. The two shipped figures stay in roof.coping with built:false.

The ROOF MECHANICAL SCREEN as geometry — its enclosure, deck and 32 checker blocks. Its PLAN is measured (chunk_4_6.jpg, 12.4 x 7.1 m) and the 2026-08-18 not-PV adjudication stands and is recorded in full; its HEIGHTS are [estimated] because no oblique of this roof exists, and at those heights on the drawn 12.40 m plane it tops out at 14.91 m — 2.51 m above the measured LiDAR maximum. At its recorded TRUE 9.30 m deck it would top at 11.75 m and clear the anchor, but that deck is three metres inside a solid flat-topped mass. Ladder for the heights: photos — none; Street View — no pano sees this roof; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — no Blake roof plan; archives — nadir only. THE FRAMES THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: an oblique or drone frame of Blake's north roof terrace giving the enclosure's height, OR the massing gaining a stepped top so the 9.30 m deck exists to stand it on.

The twelve ROOF VENTS as geometry. Their plan positions are measured (chunk_4_6.jpg) and each now carries the level it belongs to (7 terrace, 5 bar); their curb height and cap are [estimated] and absent[] already declares roof equipment heights unresolved. A 0.5 m curb plus cap on the drawn 12.40 m plane stands above the measured LiDAR maximum, and the 9.30 m terrace deck seven of them belong to is inside solid mass, so there is nowhere below the anchor to seat them. THE FRAMES THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: an oblique of Blake's roof giving curb heights, OR the massing gaining a stepped top. The measured plans and levels are kept in roof.vents.

Blake's PRECAST COLUMN COLOUR. The shipped hex was Argo's, copied on the one-repaint-programme premise this section's own R1 work refuted, so it was never a Blake read. Blake's ONLY frame of the ground colonnade is _67, which is civil twilight with blue-sky fill and warm interior spill — usable for relative ordering and never for an absolute value, and its columns are additionally in the deepest shade in the frame. Ladder: photos — only _67, at dusk; Street View — Jul 2022 is backlit; drone/video — nothing; planning docs — the 2008 UCOP deck photographs the colonnade PRE-repaint (blue); archives — nadir. Every rung fails. THE FRAME THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a daylight elevation or oblique of the Blake colonnade. Drawn in `precast` per colorFallback in the meantime.

Blake's PARAPET BAND COLOUR. The shipped #b9b1a5 was Argo's value on the refuted one-programme premise. Blake's own dusk sample of this band in _67 is #dfd8d5, which says the band reads PALER and MORE NEUTRAL than what shipped — a relative ordering, not a replacement value, because _67 is civil twilight. Ladder as for the column colour; every rung fails. THE FRAME THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a daylight south or north elevation of Blake resolving the parapet band. Drawn in `precast` per colorFallback.

Blake's AMBIENT PRECAST COLOUR (the shaded-face variant). The shipped #a6b5b7 was Argo's value on the refuted one-programme premise and Blake has no sample of a shaded precast face at all — _67 is dusk and the Jul 2022 panos are backlit. Ladder: every rung fails. THE FRAME THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a daylight frame resolving a Blake precast face in open shade against one in sun. Drawn in `precast` per colorFallback.

Blake's SPANDREL COLOUR. The shipped #bdb5a9 was Argo's value on the refuted one-programme premise. Blake's own dusk sample at the L3/L2 spandrel in _67 is #e0d8d4, again paler and more neutral, and again usable only for relative ordering. Ladder: every rung fails. THE FRAME THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a daylight near-orthographic Blake elevation resolving a spandrel band. Drawn in `precast` per colorFallback.

Blake's FROSTED GLAZING COLOUR. The shipped #cbc7c0 was Argo's value on the refuted one-programme premise. Blake's own dusk sample of a frosted panel in _67 is #c7c9c4 — relative ordering only, since a dusk frame cannot give an absolute value and glazing additionally carries whatever the sky is doing. Ladder: every rung fails. THE FRAME THAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a daylight elevation of a Blake panel face. Drawn in `precast` per colorFallback, which reads as a pale translucent panel through the library's glass material and claims nothing about the tint.

The RAISED TERRACE DECK behind the lava wall. Its plan is carried in ground.south.terrace with built:false and its 1.1 m lift is retained as the [estimated] figure it always was. NOT BUILT for two reasons: the 2014 LiDAR terrain this project draws is flat to 0.05 m across the wall's line, so the deck had nothing to stand on and drew as a plane hovering 1.2 m over the plaza with daylight under three edges; and _67 shows the ground the wall retains is the PAVED colonnade apron, not lawn, so the deck was the wrong material as well as the wrong height. See conflicts['terrace-step'].

The COLONNADE's per-bay SHOP LAYOUT: which bay is a glazed entrance door, which is a shopfront, which is the solid panel _67 shows east of centre, and where each tenancy begins and ends. The storefront BAY RHYTHM is built — see system.ground.storefront, whose mullions fall on the same measured 1.25 m module as the facade above — and the Roger's Market fascia panel is placed at its measured u. The layout is not: _67 is a dusk frame in which a 1.35 m wall occludes the lower half of every storefront, the interiors are lit and the glass is blown out, and no orthographic daylight view of the colonnade exists. Ladder: photos — _3, _25 and _40 are courtyard and roof frames; Street View — no pano enters the colonnade; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — no Blake ground-floor plan on any rung; archives — UCOP 2008 p11 photographs the colonnade PRE-repaint and pre-renovation, so its tenancies are a different building's. Every rung fails. Signage lettering stays separately absent under signage.built:false.
blake.supersededNote: DISPOSITION IS MACHINE-READABLE (R2 item S2). `sup` alone reads as a transfer whether the object moved or was deleted on evidence, so every record here declares which, names what it claims, names what actually ships it, and declares any change in count as a NUMBER. Both of blake's retirements are transfers and blake is the successor in both, so blake's own shipped counts are the reciprocal — tests/campus-photo-blake.test.mjs asserts them through assertDispositions rather than trusting the prose.

colorFallback.note: THESE FIVE ROLES HAVE NO COLOUR OF THEIR OWN AND ARE DECLARED ABSENT. Each was ARGO's hex, copied on the premise of one 2015 repaint programme, and Blake's own R1 work REFUTED that premise (EXIF 2014-01-12/13 against Webcor's 2015-16 Argo renovation — two projects, two dates, two contractors). Five copies of one borrowed value are not five measurements, so they stop being presented as five roles. Until a DAYLIGHT Blake elevation appears, each surface draws in `precast`, the ONE borrowed white the section still carries and declares as borrowed. This is a fallback, never a source: nothing may read a hex out of this block, and every key here has an absent[] entry naming what would settle it.

azad.label: Azad Hall (TDLLN "BLDG 2") — the nine-storey west bar of Eighth College: prefabricated panel wall, one six-degree rotated pop-out window per bedroom bay, an open round-column colonnade at Level 1, an east entry porch off The Ramble, and a white membrane roof with NO photovoltaics
azad.epoch: BUILT 2023-24 (construction Jan 2021 - Nov 2023, project complete 2024). Photography 2024-25 (EYRC/Lawrence Anderson, SWA Group); Apple Maps 3D capture in-repo 2026-08-06; architect's drawings 2020-09-16. The 2014 LiDAR is BLIND to this building and the 2021 renderings are a DEAD EPOCH for its roof.
azad.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail under the third declared tier. Nothing here is a measurement of the campus: the drawn ArcGIS prism and its ring carry every position and every height, and this section only dresses them. The 2014 LiDAR has no massHeights entry for this mass (campus-massing.js:16 records that it 'measures Sankofa at parking-lot height'), so the 'smooth LiDAR therefore no steps' argument that campus-eighth.js uses to withhold stairs and terraces is VOID over Eighth and is not used here.
azad.confidence: High on identity, plan form, the window system, materials, ground storey and roof composition — three independent rungs agree (UC Regents design package, the gbd magazine six-degree text, three dated built photographs). Medium on absolute facade metres: every figure is a ratio measured against a 91 px floor-to-floor in phf47 and converted at 3.048 m, which is the GIS levels x 10 ft FORMULA, not a survey. Low/unresolved on the prism's true LENGTH (three sources disagree by 23%), on the west elevation (no source of any kind) and on all vertical roof dimensions (an oblique photogrammetric mesh cannot give a vertical).
