mass.name: TDLLN - Azad
mass.source: docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing[452], ring copied VERBATIM at /10 (the decimetre convention). h = 27.4 m is the GIS levels x 3.048 m (10 ft) FORMULA, not a survey — every Eighth mass except Sankofa Base carries exactly levels x 3.048. It is nevertheless the height campus-massing.js extrudes and therefore the only wall this dressing may hang on.
mass.lidar: NONE. campus-lidar.json massHeights has no entry for this mass; the 2014 flight is blind to a 2023 building. No LiDAR height is read anywhere in this section.

geometry.note: shoelace area and perimeter of the drawn ring; bbox 39.7 m (E-W) x 17.7 m (N-S)

conflicts.about: prism LENGTH — unresolved, and it is the highest-priority open item on this building
conflicts.drawn: ArcGIS massing[452]: x -196.4..-156.7 = 39.7 m, max chord 41.90 m, area 557 m2
conflicts.others: OSM campus-3d.json buildings[869] 'Azad': 51.1 m, max chord 54.1 m, area 846 m2. UC Regents p.6 typical-upper-level plan registered to world coordinates by a 4-point Umeyama fit (s = 0.0796 +/- 0.0035 m/px at 400 dpi): 53.6 m, max chord 54.7 m. Those two agree to 1 percent; the drawn ring is 23 percent short, about 7.1 m at the WEST end and 4.4 m at the EAST
conflicts.thirdRead: INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION measured here: in phf47 the tower spans about 1550 px of visible north facade at the same 91 px floor-to-floor = about 52 m, which is the OSM/architect figure and not the drawn 39.7 m
conflicts.resolution: The DRAWN prism wins, because it is the wall campus-massing.js extrudes and moving a measured mass is forbidden. Nothing here re-cuts the ring. Every facade system is expressed as a metre MODULE so it tiles whatever ring ships, and the bay counts below are the counts of the short drawn building, not of the real one.

conflicts.about: storey grid — a CORROBORATION, not a conflict
conflicts.drawn: the drawn prism read back is 27.4 / 9 = 3.0444 m per storey
conflicts.others: the sourced floor-to-floor is 3.048 m (the GIS levels x 10 ft formula, independently corroborated by a 91 px vertical autocorrelation peak in phf47, r = 0.51, unambiguous between 40 and 160 px)
conflicts.resolution: The two agree to 0.12 percent, so the drawn prism is used without argument. The 1.07 m parapet is dressed ABOVE the drawn prism rather than carved out of it — the convention campus-photo-york.js and campus-photo-argo.js already ship, because the massing extrudes a SOLID box to the prism top and a parapet solved inside it would be buried. Every vertical facade dimension is nevertheless carried as a FRACTION of the storey, so it rescales with the anchor instead of floating off it.

conflicts.others: the research read gives 2.98 m (84-92 px against 90 px floor-to-floor in phf47)
conflicts.thirdRead: REMEASURED here on the same photograph: nine consecutive window-column centres run from x = 313 px to x = 1317 px in phf47 at a mean spacing of 111.6 px against a 91 px floor-to-floor = 1.226 x 3.048 = 3.74 m. At 2.98 m that span would hold thirteen columns; there are ten. 3.74 m also agrees with the independently measured 4.06 m colonnade column spacing (one window per structural bay), which 2.98 m does not.
conflicts.resolution: 3.74 m is shipped; 2.98 m is superseded and recorded.

conflicts.about: which way the window box rotates, bay to bay
conflicts.others: the research read says the rotation MIRRORS bay to bay, which is what makes the elevation read as a zigzag
conflicts.thirdRead: REMEASURED here: in the 2x crop of phf47 five consecutive bays each show an amber jamb return at uniform 222/204/168/183 px spacing with dark glass strictly to one side of it. A bay-to-bay mirror would show a visible return on ALTERNATE bays only. CAVEAT: phf47 views that run obliquely from one side, so a return on the far jamb would be hidden regardless — the negative is one-sided.
conflicts.resolution: rotationMirrors = false is shipped, and the module carries the flag so one frontal frame flips it. The zigzag read survives either way: it comes from the projection and its shadow, not from the mirroring.

conflicts.about: campus-eighth.json's style string for this mass
conflicts.others: the photographs show prefabricated fibre-cement / metal PANEL with PROJECTING ROTATED window boxes
conflicts.resolution: Both halves of the style string are falsified. This section does not write to campus-eighth.json (one-way rule); the correction is recorded here so a later pass can make it. bay_m 3.2 is close to nothing measured here — the shipped bay is 3.74 m.

grid.bayFitSource: The bay COUNT on a run is the rounded number of modules, not the floored one. The drawn runs are 3.8-25.9 m; flooring a 25.9 m run at 3.74 m leaves 1.75 m of dead panel at each end, which phf47 and the Apple south elevation plainly do not show — the bedroom rhythm runs to the corner. Rounding keeps the effective pitch inside 3.40-3.83 m against the measured 3.74 m.
grid.source: storeys and the prism from arcgis massing[452]; floorToFloor is the drawn prism read back under the declared conflict; bay 3.74 m remeasured in phf47 (see measured.conflicts). Level 1 is the colonnade and carries no bedroom bay, so eight residential floors carry windows.

window.source: Rotation 6.56 deg measured off the Regents p.7 VECTOR plan (a box top edge running 75 px vertical over 652 px horizontal at 300 dpi); published figure 'six degrees' (gbd, 2025). Opening width 1.62 m [three reads of phf47 span 1.36-1.81 m; the research read of 46-51 px against 90 px floor-to-floor is taken]. Opening height 0.63 of the storey [two independent reads of phf47 agree: 55-59 px of 90, and 360 of 560 px in the 3x crop]. Sill fraction and head band from the same crop: head band flush under the slab above, spandrel below the sill. Box depth 0.29 m is the amber jamb return seen in elevation (7-10 px of 90); at 1.62 m wide and 6.56 deg the geometric projection of the deep jamb is 1.62 x tan(6.56) = 0.19 m, and the two agree within the read. Two leaves per box, one fixed and one outward-swinging casement — the swing arc is drawn dashed on Regents p.7 and open casements are visible in phf47.
window.note: The box is a rotated open tube, not a flat surround: the deep jamb comes forward and the shallow jamb sits flush with the panel plane, which is what the head hood's asymmetric overhang shows in phf47. Head, sill soffit and the deep jamb are amber/ochre metal; the shallow jamb is the dark frame.

panel.source: Regents p.8 'Exterior Materials' names PREFABRICATED FIBER CEMENT PANEL and METAL PANEL; Regents f2.pdf p.10 confirms the wall is factory-finished panel shipped to site. Width 1.02 m from horizontal autocorrelation of blank spandrel strips in phf47 (repeated peaks at 30 px and 60 px against 90 px floor-to-floor = 0.333 and 0.667 x 3.048); REMEASURED here on the 2x crop, vertical joints at about 60 px against a 182 px floor-to-floor = 1.00 m, which agrees. Confidence moderate (r about 0.15) — nominal, not survey-grade. Horizontal joints on the floor line with one intermediate joint at the window head, i.e. two courses per storey.
panel.note: Panel COUNT is never hard-coded: the module tiles the shipped run length, so it survives the length conflict.

colonnade.source: Regents p.5 Ground Level Plan draws a continuous dark band with ROUND COLUMN SYMBOLS outside the enclosed line on BOTH long faces — the enclosed ground floor is set back behind an open colonnade and the eight residential floors oversail. Built confirmation in phf47 (round pale concrete columns forward of a cream linear-brick / burnished-block wall with tall dark-framed storefront, recessed soffit downlights) and in SWA Learning-20 in daylight. Column diameter 0.61 m = 18 px against the same photograph's 90 px floor-to-floor (a standard 24-inch round form), +/- 0.08 m. Spacing 4.06 m = 120 px = 1.33 x 3.048, one column per structural bay. Regents p.8 names EXPOSED CONCRETE and BURNISHED CONCRETE BLOCK.
colonnade.note: The drawn prism is SOLID and may not be carved, so the 2.4 m colonnade depth is RECORDED and not cut: the recess reads as a near-black matte void plane tight to the drawn face with the round columns standing 0.46 m proud and a deep soffit fascia at the Level-1 head — the same device campus-photo-argo.js uses for Argo's ground storey, and for the same reason.
colonnade.depthSource: [estimated] 2.4 m from the drawn grey band width on Regents p.5 (about 30 px at 400 dpi at the registered s = 0.0796 m/px). No frame resolves it.
colonnade.columnProudSource: [estimated] 0.46 m — the clear gap between the storefront plane and the back of the column shaft. No frame gives it in plan; it is set so the shaft stands one half-diameter clear of the glass line, which is what phf47's shadow separation shows and what the planting strip below it needs. Recorded as estimated because a frontal photograph cannot give a plan dimension.
colonnade.soffitFasciaSource: 0.42 m — CORROBORATED here rather than assumed: the storefront head in az_base_47 stands 2.52 m above the Level-1 floor (325 px at the crop's 133 px/m ruler, see `scale`), and the drawn storey is 3.044 m, so the fascia between the storefront head and the floor above measures 3.044 - 2.52 = 0.52 m at the head line; 0.42 m is the fascia BELOW the slab soffit and reads 0.10 m shallower, inside the read.

scale.crop: az_base_47.png — the Level-1 crop of EYRC/Lawrence Anderson phf47, 1650 x 930 px, cut from the frame named in `sources`
scale.source: TWO INDEPENDENT RULERS, agreeing to 5.5 percent, fix the crop's TRUE scale. (1) The colonnade column silhouette is 83 px wide (a luminance scan across rows 380-560 gives its lit left edge at x = 1070 and its dark silhouette edge against the sunlit wall at x = 1153); a round shaft's silhouette width is its diameter whatever the view angle, so at the sourced 0.61 m form that is 136 px/m. (2) The base wall's coursing autocorrelates at lag 8.4 px with peaks at 8, 17, 25 and 33 (r = 0.69-0.77 in two separate wall windows, x 1250-1450 and x 620-740); at a standard modular brick course of 2 5/8 in = 0.0667 m that is 126 px/m. Take 133 px/m for VERTICAL dimensions and for the round column. HORIZONTAL dimensions on the wall plane are foreshortened: two colonnade columns two bays apart stand 787 px apart (left edges at x = 283 and x = 1070) against a true 2 x 4.06 = 8.12 m, giving 97 px/m along the wall, i.e. a foreshortening factor of 0.73; taking the mean of the two column widths as the local perspective scale gives 0.76. Every horizontal figure below is quoted at 101 px/m and every vertical one at 133 px/m.
scale.note: This block exists because the round numbers this section used to carry had no ruler behind them. Anything derived from az_base_47 now names its axis and its px count.

storefront.source: az_base_47 (the EYRC phf47 Level-1 crop) resolves the ground-storey system directly, and it is NOT one undivided dark plane. A horizontal luminance scan of rows 480-620 puts frame members at x = 362, 437.5, 518 and 599 - an outer jamb, two mullions and the far jamb, i.e. a THREE-LIGHT aluminium storefront 241.5 px wide with three near-equal lights of 79 / 79.5 / 83 px. At the wall's 101 px/m that is an assembly 2.39 m wide of three 0.80 m lights, which sits inside the 4.06 m colonnade bay with 1.66 m of burnished block each side - exactly what the photograph shows. A vertical scan of columns 455-505 puts the head rail at y = 326, a continuous horizontal rail at y = 447 and the bottom rail at y = 651: at 133 px/m the head stands 2.52 m and the rail 1.58 m above the Level-1 floor. Mullion members read 6-8 px = 0.06-0.08 m. Frame width 0.06 m is carried from the window system's independently measured mullion.
storefront.doorSource: ONE LIGHT PER ASSEMBLY IS A GLAZED DOOR LEAF. In the RZ_door zoom of az_base_47 (image x 215-380) the left light carries a vertical PULL HANDLE - a bright bar spanning image y 511-567, i.e. 0.42 m long centred 0.87 m above the bottom rail at the crop's 133 px/m vertical ruler. 0.87 m is the standard 34-48 in door-handle height, which is what independently CONFIRMS the 133 px/m ruler: at any smaller scale the handle sits at an impossible height. A second pull is visible on the assembly at x 361-602. The leaf is therefore 0.80 m wide (a 32-in leaf, the code minimum clear width) and full height to the 2.52 m head.
storefront.cadenceSource: [estimated] ONE door per drawn colonnade face, at its centre bay. The photographs cover about 15 m of the north colonnade and resolve door leaves within it; NO frame gives the cadence along the remaining 60 m of colonnade, and Regents p.5 colours Level 1 Residential Support + Core without drawing door swings. One per drawn face is the smallest claim that still lets the building be entered; it extends nothing and is replaced the day a plan with swings turns up. See `absent`.
storefront.note: The near-black matte VOID stays - it is the shadowed colonnade recess behind the glass, and phf47/Learning-20 both read it that way - but it is now the BACKING to a real storefront rather than the storefront itself.

eastCore.source: Regents p.6 draws the east end as CORE / CIRCULATION — two lifts (the X symbol) and a stair — with residential common space at the extreme east on both rows; Regents p.5 puts the entry porch under it. In .cache/eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png this plane reads darker and more glazed than the long faces, with no bedroom rhythm.
eastCore.note: [estimated] on dimension: no frame resolves the corridor window or the stair slot to the metre. One corridor window per floor per strip plus one continuous stair slot; the opening sizes extend nothing from the bedroom bay and are declared here as inferred.

westEnd.extendsPattern: Azad's own NORTH elevation — the sourced panel grid, opening size, amber reveal, box rotation and floor-to-floor are carried across unchanged; only the bay LAYOUT is inferred, from this building's own Regents p.6 plan (residential common space on the south strip, the north row plus the stair core on the north strip)
westEnd.source: [estimated] NO rung of the ladder resolves this face. Searched: the EYRC set (17 images), the SWA set (19 images), the Regents package, Street View, and the 153-frame Apple .cache/eighth-area capture. The visual precedent for the composition is Pulse's west end in .cache/eighth-area/r2c1-oblique-01-west.png — one central column of paired windows with blank panel either side and a blind stair plane — but that is a DIFFERENT BUILDING and is named here only as precedent, never as a source for Azad.

porch.source: Regents p.4 rendering and its caption 'ENTRY PORCHES ALONG RAMBLE BLDG 5 (ABOVE) & BLDG 2 (BELOW)', and Regents p.5 Ground Level Plan, which draws the porch as a brown paved outdoor room at the east end. Legible in the rendering: flat exposed-concrete soffit, large SQUARE concrete columns (unlike the round colonnade columns), unit-paver floor in a running pattern, a round fire-pit table at centre, two long grey upholstered sofas facing each other with round side tables, the glazed lobby door line at the back, and planting beds with a low wall between the porch and the Ramble.
porch.note: The plan notches the porch INTO the footprint about 9 m; the drawn prism is solid and cannot be notched. The porch therefore builds EASTWARD off the drawn east face, 4.25 m deep, which is inside the 4.4 m the drawn ring is short at that end (see measured.conflicts) — and ArcGIS ground ring #2989 surveys 'walk' from x -158.0 eastward, which is exactly where the Regents plan puts the porch FLOOR. Clear height is the Level-1 storey.
porch.widthSource: The porch WIDTH is not typed and is not the ring's bounding box: it is the drawn length of the single face it backs onto, `east-3`, which the shipped ring measures at 8.20 m. This CORRECTS the first build, which took the width from min(ring.z) to max(ring.z) and shipped a 17.70 m soffit across the whole east elevation — twice the plan's roughly 9 m, and standing 1.25 m clear of the wall for 7.5 m of its length because the drawn east face STEPS at z = 613.2 (east-3 at x = -156.7, east-4 at x = -157.95). Backing the porch onto one drawn face makes every millimetre of the soffit's inner edge sit on a wall, and 8.20 m is the plan's roughly 9 m to within the declared length conflict.
porch.dimensionSource: [estimated] on every furniture and trim dimension. The fire-pit radius, sofa, side table, low wall, bed depth, soffit thickness, column size and column count are read off a RENDERING (Regents p.4) at no stated scale; they are the same site-furniture tier keeling.courtyard.lamp/chaise/rack ships. What is NOT estimated: the porch's width (the drawn face) and the LAYOUT, which is derived rather than typed — the columns stand at the soffit's outer edge inset by half their own size and are spread evenly between the two low end walls, clear of both; the sofas stand one `seatReach` clear of the fire pit (0.45 m, the standard 18-inch reach from a seat front to a low table); the side tables are tangent to the sofa ends; the low walls stand outside the porch ends by half their own thickness. The first build's 1.1 m, 2.2 m, 0.15 m and 0.5 m layout offsets existed in no field and are gone.

roof.source: .cache/eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png (Apple Maps 3D, repo cache, 2026-08-06 build) — the only roof source. Scale within that crop: 44.6 px/m along the ridge axis, 27.7 px/m across (foreshortened); every cross-roof figure carries that and is quoted +/- 20 percent.

parapet.source: Continuous on all four sides in the Apple capture; plan thickness 12-18 px = 0.30-0.40 m, take 0.35. HEIGHT above the membrane is not resolvable in an oblique photogrammetric mesh — [estimated] 1.0668 m, which is 42 in EXACTLY, the IBC roof-edge guard height, and is why a parapet is used here instead of a guardrail. Coping cap reads about 0.10 m.
parapet.copingOverhangSource: [estimated] 0.025 m = 1 in each side. NOT a photograph — the Apple mesh cannot resolve a coping drip. It is the nominal sheet-metal coping drip of the SMACNA standard edge detail, named here rather than eyeballed; the first build's 0.06 m came from nothing.

walkway.trimRule: trim = width — a band is pulled back from each end of its face by its OWN width, which is the smallest trim that guarantees it cannot poke out through the adjacent face at a concave corner whatever the corner angle. The first build typed 1.2 m separately; it is now read from `width` and cannot drift from it.
walkway.minRunRule: a face carries a band only if it is longer than 2 x width, i.e. only if anything survives the trim. The first build typed minRun = 3 m; the rule replaces it and changes no count on the shipped ring (the drawn runs step 1.9 -> 3.8 m, so nothing lies between 2.4 and 3.0 m).

crossBands.note: the east cross band, between the penthouse and the east end

CLIP. At x = -183.5 the drawn ring steps IN on both long faces — the mirrored 1.7 x 0.8 m niches — so the roof plate there spans z 608.7..620.8, not the building's full 605.7..623.4. A band drawn on the bbox would hover 0.8 m past the wall at BOTH ends. Nothing may hover.

walkway.source: A grey protection-mat / paver band set just inside the parapet on all four sides plus two cross bands running north-south that divide the membrane into three fields, clearly distinct in tone from the white membrane in the Apple capture. Band width 50-60 px at 44.6 px/m = 1.1-1.3 m; take 1.2 m.

ladder.extendsPattern: no dimension of any kind is legible in the Apple mesh — only that a rung-striped element with a cage stands on the penthouse's west face. Every figure is therefore the CODE MINIMUM of the fixed-ladder standard, named, not a photograph and not an eyeball
ladder.source: [estimated] against OSHA 29 CFR 1910.23(d) and ANSI A14.3 fixed ladders: rungs a minimum 16 in (0.4064 m) long, so the rails stand 0.4064 m apart; rungs a maximum 12 in (0.3048 m) apart, so the rung count is a CONSEQUENCE of the penthouse height and is not typed; a cage extending 27 in (0.6858 m) from the rung centreline. This REPLACES the first build's 0.75 m rail spacing, 13 typed rungs and 0.34 m cage, none of which was derived and the first of which is outside the standard's range in both directions.

penthouse.source: ONE large white box at roughly the east third of the roof with equipment on its own roof and a dark north face, and a caged vertical access ladder on its west face reading as a rung-striped element. Plan 360 px at 44.6 px/m x 230 px at 27.7 px/m = 8.1 x 8.3 m, +/- 20 percent. Function follows the plan: the east end is the core (Regents p.6, two lifts + a stair), so this is the lift overrun plus the stair bulkhead. HEIGHT is not resolvable — [estimated] 4.0 m, a two-lift overrun over one storey.

mechanical.extendsPattern: Azad's own sourced roof composition — these units are visible in the very frame that sources the membrane, the parapet, the walkway ring and the penthouse; only their dimensions and their exact count are inferred, because the photogrammetric mesh blurs them into smears
mechanical.source: 4-6 low mechanical (RTU / condenser) clusters scattered across the central membrane field in .cache/eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png, each roughly 1.5-2.5 m across and about 1.2 m tall. Five are shipped, inside the sourced range; the mesh resolves silhouettes, not edges, and a real count needs a nadir orthophoto.

drains.extendsPattern: Azad's own sourced perimeter walkway band, on which they stand in the same frame
drains.insetRule: the dome sits on the CENTRE LINE of the perimeter walkway band, so its inset is parapet.thickness / 2 + walkway.width / 2 = 0.775 m and is computed, never typed. The first build typed 0.75 m, which put every dome 25 mm off the band it is photographed standing on.
drains.startRule: the first dome on a face stands one walkway width in from the face's end — the same trim the band itself takes — so a dome can never sit on a mitre.
drains.source: A row of small white domes at regular spacing along the perimeter band — roof drains with dome strainers and/or vent-stack caps, about 0.30 m across and 0.15 m tall, spaced roughly 6-8 m. Take 7.0 m. Count is a consequence of the shipped perimeter, not a photograph.

ground.note: campus-eighth-furniture.js excludes everything within 5 m of a building BY DESIGN, so none of this currently ships anywhere. It is exactly the band the ultra standard requires be filled. Positions along the face are [estimated]: the photographs cover only about 15 m of the north colonnade, so nothing is extrapolated along the whole face — the run is placed on the photographed north-middle face and declared.
ground.layout: EVERY fitting here is placed FACE-RELATIVE — a drawn face id, `u` metres along it from its start, and `offset` metres proud of it — never as a world (x, z) pair. The first build typed absolute coordinates that existed in no source and that silently drove the guardrail straight through a planter cube. Face-relative placement is what lets the test sweep every ground instance against every other one and fail on interpenetration.
ground.bands: The colonnade's perpendicular section, read outward from the drawn wall, and the reason every `offset` below is what it is: 0.04 base wall / 0.09 storefront glass line / 0.11-0.44 the planting bed / 0.46-1.07 the round column shafts / 0.64-0.89 the in-ground uplights, between the columns / 1.20-2.00 bike racks / 2.10-2.70 planter cubes / 3.47 the raised terrace edge and its guardrail. Nothing occupies two bands at the same point along a face.

guardrail.offsetRule: offset = colonnade.columnProud + colonnade.columnDiameter + colonnade.depth = 0.46 + 0.61 + 2.40 = 3.47 m: the raised terrace runs out past the column line by the same 2.4 m the Regents p.5 grey colonnade band measures, and the guard stands at its edge. [estimated], and it EXTENDS this section's own recorded colonnade-band width rather than inventing a distance. The first build's 3.4 m came from nothing and put the rail through planter cube 1.
guardrail.picketRule: picket centres = 0.1016 m (4 in) with a 0.019 m (3/4 in) picket, so the clear opening is 0.0826 m. ARBITRATED 2026-08-19: this is the canonical Eighth guard, owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail and MEASURED there — grid-masked autocorrelation of swa-5 gives a 19.3 px pitch against a 197 px guard = 0.1046 +/- 0.005 m, and the 4 in module sits inside that bracket. It supersedes this section's earlier reading, which took 0.1016 m as the CLEAR OPENING and put the centres at 0.1206 m: that is the widest legal spacing rather than the built one, and the built one is now measured. The first build typed 0.11 m, which is neither.
guardrail.postRule: 1.829 m = 6 ft, the standard proprietary picket-panel length. [estimated]: no frame resolves a post.
guardrail.source: SWA Learning-20 (az_base_20, 2024-25 daylight): a galvanised vertical-picket guardrail along the raised terrace edge at Azad's north colonnade, with the red standpipe standing beside it. Regents p.8 names GALVANIZED METAL HANDRAIL explicitly. Height 1.0668 m is 42 in EXACTLY, the code guard height, and it reads at about that against the 0.61 m columns in the same frame. Position along the face and the run length are [estimated] — the frame covers about 15 m. ARBITRATED: height 1.0668 -> 1.067 m and picket centres 0.1206 -> 0.1016 m, to the one canonical guard spec for the whole college (eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail). Both are the same 42 in code guard on a 3/4 in picket; only the centres actually moved.

hedge.heightSource: MEASURED, not scaled by eye: in az_base_47 a luminance scan of columns 1200-1450 puts the foliage crown at y = 665 (the 50 percent point of the 164 -> 40 fall off the sunlit wall) and the bed's front foot at y = 735, i.e. 70 px, which at the crop's 133 px/m VERTICAL ruler (see `scale`) is 0.53 m +/- 0.04. The first build's 0.5 m was 'scaled against the 0.61 m columns' with no pixel read behind it.
hedge.depthRule: [estimated] and DERIVED, because a frontal photograph cannot give a plan depth: the bed fills the clear strip between the storefront glass line (colonnade.baseWallStandoff + 0.05 = 0.09 m) and the back of the column shafts (colonnade.columnProud = 0.46 m), less a 0.02 m clipping clearance at each side — 0.33 m deep, centred at 0.275 m. This CORRECTS the first build's 0.7 m at offset 1.15, which put the hedge in the band 0.80-1.50 m and drove it through all seven colonnade columns on these two faces by 0.27 m. It also matches the source string, which says the hedge runs 'along the base of the storefront': 1.15 m was on the far side of the columns from the storefront.
hedge.interruptionRule: the bed is INTERRUPTED where a ground fitting stands in it. On north-4 that is the standpipe, and the module drops the bed segments it occupies rather than growing a hedge through a fire-department connection.
hedge.source: EYRC phf47 (az_base_47) and SWA Learning-20: a low clipped evergreen hedge run along the base of the storefront, continuous through the colonnade and passing behind the column shafts.

planterCubes.source: EYRC phf47: dark-grey rectangular concrete planter cubes on the north terrace, each carrying a clipped shrub. Size scaled against the 0.61 m columns. Positions [estimated] — the frame fixes their character, not their coordinates. The 2.4 m offset puts them in the open band between the bike racks and the terrace edge, which is where phf47 shows them; the first build's absolute (x, z) pairs put cube 1 on top of the guardrail.
planterCubes.shrubRule: the shrub seats ON the cube: its base sits exactly at the cube's top, so the pair touches and never interpenetrates.

bikeRacks.source: EYRC phf47 (az_base_47: three inverted-U hoops legible in the paving between the column at x = 1153 and the planter at x = 1280) and SWA Learning-20. Standard inverted-U, 0.75 m tall x 0.9 m wide. Run position and spacing [estimated]; the 1.6 m offset stands them clear of the column band (0.46-1.07 m) and of the planter cubes.

standpipe.source: SWA Learning-20 (az_base_20): a red fire-department standpipe / FDC post standing AGAINST THE BASE WALL, immediately beside the guardrail run. Position along the face [estimated]. Offset 0.25 m is what 'against the base wall' means in plan; the first build put it at 0.978 m proud, buried inside its own hedge and a metre off the wall its own source names.
standpipe.dimensionSource: [estimated] against the product rather than eyeballed: height 0.91 m = 36 in, the usual centre height of a freestanding FDC inlet (NFPA 14 allows 18-48 in); radius 0.076 m is a 6-inch (DN150) FDC body. The first build carried a bare integer 1 m and a 0.09 m radius, neither of which is any product.

uplights.placement: one at the MIDPOINT between the columns of every second colonnade bay, on the column centre line (colonnade.columnProud + colonnade.columnDiameter / 2 = 0.765 m proud), so it stands in open paving 2.03 m from either shaft
uplights.radiusSource: [estimated] 0.0635 m — a 5-inch (0.127 m) in-grade luminaire, the standard aperture for this fitting. The first build's 0.13 m radius is a 0.26 m lens, which is no product.
uplights.source: EYRC phf47 (az_base_47): warm in-ground uplights recessed in the colonnade paving, standing in the OPEN paving between the columns and not at their feet. The first build put them at the column feet at 1.42 m proud, which is inside the planting bed — an in-ground uplight under a 0.5 m hedge. Count follows the column row.

wallPanel.source: docs/data/campus-eighth.json key m:-182,614 'Azad' walls — the median of a masked pixel patch from .cache/eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png and r2c1-oblique-00-south.png (Apple Maps 3D, epoch-valid). Azad's centroid is 13.7 m from that capture target, the closest station-to-mass match in the whole Eighth dossier. CAVEAT: scripts/tmp-sample.mjs, named as its provenance, exists in no commit, so this value cannot currently be re-derived; it is kept because it is the repo's own recorded measurement and every ratio below is anchored to it.

amberReveal.source: Ratio method against SWA Learning-20 (2024-25, golden hour): reveal raw #bd885e over adjacent sunlit wall panel raw #e3caae gives channel ratios 0.833/0.673/0.540, applied to the measured neutral wall #d8d3d3. Illuminant-robust; a direct sample is impossible because every published photograph of Azad is dusk or golden hour. A second sample in the same frame (#a87559 over #e5d1b8) gives #9f7667, so the true value lies in #9f7667..#b48e72. Do NOT sample phf47 — its dusk exterior uplighting makes the reveals read as saturated gold.

glazing.source: Ratio method against SWA Learning-20: glass raw #4b463e over wall raw #e3caae gives 0.333/0.347/0.359, applied to #d8d3d3. Reads dark blue-grey in phf47 and phf48, consistent.

windowFrame.source: Dark bronze / near-black anodised aluminium in EYRC phf47 (frontal, 2024-25) and SWA Learning-20; the darkest element on the facade in every frame. An extension of the same ratio method; no neutral-light sample exists.

baseBlock.source: Ratio method against SWA Learning-20 with the base wall in SHADE (raw #b9ab8b over sunlit wall #e3caae = 0.817/0.849/0.799, applied to #d8d3d3). Shade-blued: in phf47 under warm light the same wall reads ivory/bone, so the true value lies between this and a warmer #ddd6c6. Material named on Regents p.8 as BURNISHED CONCRETE BLOCK.

exposedConcrete.source: Named on Regents p.8 as EXPOSED CONCRETE and in the Regents Sept 2020 narrative p.10 as 'exposed cast-in-place concrete'. Reads a shade lighter and greyer than the base block in phf47 and Learning-20; no neutral-light sample exists, so this is a standard grey-concrete value inside the site palette.

roofMembrane.source: Reads uniformly white in .cache/eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png. The value is the repo's own ROOF_FALLBACK in docs/js/campus-massing.js:32, chosen because 'nearly every flat roof the drone saw is white TPO membrane'. Azad has no truecolor sample of its own.

roofWalkway.source: Clearly a mid-grey against the white membrane in .cache/eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png; that mesh's exposure is blown, so no reliable hex can be sampled. A standard grey walkway-pad value.

guardrailGalv.source: Named on Regents p.8 as GALVANIZED METAL HANDRAIL; reads as unpainted galvanised steel in SWA Learning-20 and EYRC phf47. No neutral sample.

copingMetal.source: The coping reads as a bright continuous line against the white membrane in .cache/eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png; the mesh cannot give a hex. The value is guardrailGalv lifted to the membrane's luma — a mill-finish metal cap inside the Regents p.8 METAL PANEL family.

penthouseWhite.source: The penthouse box reads the same white as the membrane in the Apple capture; the value is roofMembrane pulled a shade toward the wall panel because it is a wall, not a membrane.

penthouseDark.source: The penthouse's NORTH face reads as a distinctly darker plane in .cache/eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png (louvre or shaded panel). Value is a neutral mid-dark grey; the mesh cannot give a hex.

rtuGrey.source: Rooftop mechanical reads mid-grey and smeared in the Apple capture; standard galvanised-plant grey inside the site palette.

drainWhite.source: The perimeter domes read white-grey against the membrane in the Apple capture; value is roofMembrane pulled slightly grey.

recessVoid.source: The Level-1 recess behind the colonnade and the porch soffit shadow both read as a near-black VOID in phf47 and Learning-20, not as glazing. Value follows the same reasoning campus-photo-argo.js records for Argo's ground recess: a fully matte near-black so image-based lighting cannot lift it into a pale screen.

porchPaver.source: Regents p.4 rendering: brick / unit pavers in a running pattern on the porch floor, warm grey-tan. A RENDERING, so estimated — no built photograph of Azad's porch floor exists.

lobbyGlass.source: The glazed lobby door line at the back of the porch in the Regents p.4 rendering, and — added on the audit — the Level-1 STOREFRONT lights along the colonnade, which read the same warm interior-lit pale in az_base_47. Value is glazing lifted slightly, as an interior-lit lobby or lit ground-floor room reads paler than a bedroom window.

sofaGrey.source: Regents p.4 rendering: two long grey upholstered sofas. A rendering, so estimated.

firepitDark.source: Regents p.4 rendering: a round dark fire-pit table at the porch centre. A rendering, so estimated.

hedgeGreen.source: EYRC phf47 and SWA Learning-20: a low clipped evergreen hedge; dusk/golden-hour only, so the value is a mid evergreen inside the site palette.

planterCubeGrey.source: EYRC phf47: dark-grey rectangular concrete planter cubes. Dusk frame, so estimated.

rackBlack.source: EYRC phf47 and Learning-20: black-painted hoop bike racks.

standpipeRed.source: SWA Learning-20: a red fire-department standpipe / FDC post. Golden-hour frame, so estimated.

uplightGlow.source: EYRC phf47: warm in-ground uplights in the colonnade paving; the lens colour at dusk, estimated.

plantingSoil.source: Regents p.4 and p.5: planting beds between the porch and the Ramble; dark bark mulch, matching the raked bark field phf47 photographs immediately north.

doorPull.source: EYRC phf47 (az_base_47, the RZ_door zoom): the vertical door pull reads as a bright brushed-metal bar against near-black frame, the only element on the ground storey brighter than the frame it sits in. Dusk frame, so the value is guardrailGalv lifted toward the wall panel's luma — brushed stainless inside the Regents p.8 METAL PANEL family. No neutral-light sample of Azad exists.

absent: ROOFTOP PHOTOVOLTAICS — zero modules, zero racks, zero ballast trays. This is the Keeling trap running the OTHER way: the 2021 Revelle town-hall renderings (revelle.ucsd.edu/_files/tdlln.pdf slides 4 and 16) draw large dark PV fields on the low Eighth roofs, and the built-epoch Apple 3D capture (.cache/eighth-area/r2c1-plan-00-south.png) shows white membrane, a grey walkway ring and cross bands, one penthouse and scattered RTUs, and NO array anywhere. Under the epoch rule the rendering loses to the capture.

BALCONIES of any kind — none drawn on BLDG 2 in Regents p.6 or p.7 and none visible in phf47, phf48, Learning-20 or the Apple frames. Survivance's west end has a stacked balcony column; Azad does not.
VERTICAL FACADE FINS — the gbd text assigns fins to the TALLER towers only; Azad, the lowest, gets the rotated pop-out windows instead. None visible in phf47, which is frontal and unambiguous.
AN APPLIED WORDMARK — Sankofa and Podemos carry SANKOFA / PODEMOS on their brick bases (SWA Learning-8, Learning-9, EYRC phf01). No frame of Azad shows one. Do not letter this building.
A BLUE APPLIED STREET NUMBER — 9185 appears at the academic wing and 9145 at Survivance's garage portal; no frame of Azad shows one.
RETAIL, DINING OR ACADEMIC SPACE AT LEVEL 1 — Regents p.5 colours Azad's ground floor only Residential Support + Core.
A ROOFTOP DECK OR AMENITY TERRACE — eighth.ucsd.edu gives a rooftop deck to PULSE and not to Azad. No green roof, no pergola, no roof amenity of any kind.

SOUTH-FACE FORMED ALUMINIUM SUNSHADES — Regents f2.pdf p.10 says 'Formed aluminum sunshades and many of the south-facing elevations have been designed to aid in overall building energy performance and sun control', but no frame resolves whether AZAD in particular carries them, and the only south-face source is a blurred Apple mesh. Better absent than wrong; the text is on the record here so a future frame can settle it.
NORTH-FACE SUNSCREENS OR BRISE-SOLEIL — none in phf47, which is frontal.
A PORTE-COCHERE OR VEHICLE DROP-OFF at Azad — the Theatre Drop-Off is at the south edge of the site, not here.

THE WEST EXTERIOR STAIR — Regents p.5 draws an X-marked stair box just west of the enclosed footprint, so its EXISTENCE is sourced at rung 1, but no rung gives its rise, its run, its direction or the grade change it negotiates, and the 2014 LiDAR that would normally supply that grade is blind to this site. A stair built without its rise either hovers or buries. Better absent than wrong — and note this is NOT the void 'smooth LiDAR therefore no steps' argument, which is refused everywhere in this section.

WHAT THE TWO MIRRORED 1.7 x 0.8 m NICHES CONTAIN — they are surveyed in the ArcGIS ring at x about -184 on BOTH long faces and are therefore built as geometry, but no source says whether they carry a service riser, a trash chute or a scupper. Their backs ship as blank panel and nothing is invented inside them.

GROUND-FITTING COUNTS ALONG THE WHOLE FACE — the photographs cover about 15 m of the north colonnade. The guardrail, hedge, planter cubes, bike racks and standpipe are placed on that photographed run only; nothing is extrapolated along the remaining 60 m of frontage, and their positions along the face are declared [estimated].

THE SOUTH AND WEST GROUND PLANES — The Backyard (barbeque grills and ping-pong tables, per Regents f2.pdf p.10) and the west slope above North Torrey Pines Road belong to the Eighth landscape modules, not to this building's dressing. Nothing is built on them here.
TREES — 45 LiDAR canopies already stand across this site and the photographs show a later generation; the correct tree work in Eighth is subtractive, and it is not this module's.

THE REAL PRISM LENGTH — the drawn ring is 39.7 m against OSM's 51.1 m and the architect's 53.6 m. The missing 7.1 m at the west end and 4.4 m at the east end are NOT built: re-cutting a measured mass is forbidden. Every bay count in this section is the count of the short drawn building.

A NEUTRAL-ILLUMINANT COLOUR MEASUREMENT — every published photograph of Azad is dusk or golden hour, so every colour except the wall is ratio-derived against the repo's measured #d8d3d3, not directly sampled.
INTERIOR PROGRAMME above Level 1 — irrelevant to an exterior model, and not checked.

THE CADENCE OF ENTRY DOORS ALONG THE COLONNADE — az_base_47 resolves the ground-storey storefront completely (three 0.80 m lights, a continuous rail at 1.58 m, a head at 2.52 m) and resolves that ONE light per assembly is a glazed door leaf, because the vertical pull is legible at 0.87 m. What no frame gives is HOW OFTEN a door recurs along 74 m of colonnade: the photographs cover about 15 m and Regents p.5 colours Level 1 without drawing a single door swing. One door is therefore placed at the centre bay of each drawn colonnade face and the cadence is declared [estimated]. Six doors is the smallest claim that still lets the building be entered; it is not a count anybody measured.

THE PLAN DEPTH OF THE PLANTING BED, THE COLONNADE RECESS AND EVERY OTHER PERPENDICULAR DISTANCE AT LEVEL 1 — phf47 and Learning-20 are frontal, and a frontal photograph cannot give a plan dimension. colonnade.columnProud, colonnade.depth and ground.hedge.depth are therefore all [estimated]; what makes them safe rather than guessed is that they are DERIVED from one another (the bed fills the strip the columns leave, the terrace edge stands one colonnade band out past the columns) and that the test sweeps every ground object against every other one and fails on interpenetration. A nadir or oblique frame that resolves the colonnade in plan replaces all three at once.

THE POSITION OF THE RAISED TERRACE EDGE — Learning-20 shows a guardrail on a raised terrace at the north colonnade but no frame fixes where the drop is. The rail is placed one recorded colonnade-band width (2.4 m) out past the column line; that offset extends this building's own Regents p.5 band and is declared [estimated] rather than measured.

A DIMENSIONED FRAME OF THE ROOF-ACCESS LADDER OR OF ANY ROOFTOP TRIM — the Apple photogrammetric mesh resolves that a caged ladder, a coping cap and a drain dome exist and nothing about how big they are. Their figures are the named code and product standards (OSHA 1910.23 fixed ladders, the SMACNA coping drip, a 5-inch in-grade luminaire, a 6-inch FDC body, a 42-inch guard), carried as [estimated] with the standard named. They are not photographic measurements and must not be read as any.

expect.note: counts of the SHORT drawn prism; see measured.conflicts. Recomputed by the generator from the shipped ring, never typed. The module is gated against these. Added on the audit: doors, storefrontPanes, walkwayBands, drains, hedgeSegments, uplights, ladderRungs, guardrailPickets, porchSofas, porchWalls and porchWidth — every one of them was a count the module produced and no gate ever read, which is how six of them changed without a test noticing. porchWidth is the drawn length of porch.face and is asserted against the ring itself, not against this number.

eighthcourtyards.label: Eighth College / Theatre District Living & Learning Neighborhood — the COURTYARDS AND HARDSCAPE. HKS (design architect) + EYRC Architects with SWA Group (landscape); Kitchell GC; Walter P Moore structure. Construction Jan 2021 - Nov 2023, project complete 2024, the Market Hall (STATION8) still unopened as of Feb 2026. NOT Safdie Rabines and NOT OJB — that team designed North Torrey Pines LLN / Sixth College, and a search on those names documents the wrong buildings.
eighthcourtyards.epoch: 2024-2025 built-condition photography (EYRC/Lawrence Anderson phf01-phf49; SWA Group gallery 1-23) over a 2025-03 built-condition site plan (SDAF OH! San Diego), over the repo's ArcGIS facilities survey. THE 2014 LiDAR IS BLIND HERE: the college was a parking lot in 2014, campus-lidar.json massHeights has no entry for any Eighth mass, and campus-massing.js:16 records that LiDAR measures Sankofa at parking-lot height. Every argument of the form 'the LiDAR is smooth here so there is no step or wall' is therefore VOID over Eighth — it describes a demolished car park. That argument is what campus-eighth.js and campus-eighth-furniture.js used to withhold every stair, terrace, retaining wall and seat wall; this section re-decides it on eleven dated 2024-25 photographs. Google satellite over Eighth is MID-CONSTRUCTION and is never an existence or colour source. The 2021 Revelle town-hall deck is the DESIGN epoch and is superseded wherever it disagrees with the built photographs (its rooftop PV fields and its figure-of-eight meditation pavilion were not built).
eighthcourtyards.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail (README 'the second declared invented class'), quarantined in campus-photo-detail.json. Nothing measured may read from it. Photographs decide what exists and how it looks; the ArcGIS survey keeps deciding every ground EXTENT. Items labelled [estimated] are the third declared tier: each names the sourced pattern it extends and is replaced the day a real source appears. Textures are code-generated by campus-materials.js; sourced colours feed the materials.
eighthcourtyards.boundsNote: x -220..30, z 490..730. The shipped `eighth` section's bounds (x -220..-40, z 500..640) exclude the whole southern third of the college — Market Hall Plaza (walk #3045 runs to z 724.6 and x +26.0), The Backyard (#323 z 651.5, #114 z 654.5), Theatre Walk, the Theatre Drop-Off, the South Parking Entrance, the Loading Dock, the Survivance Front Porch, the mid-site parking-elevator pavilion and the mobility hub. This section's bounds are the corrected envelope. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: these bounds are the college ENVELOPE and they stay as they are — Market Hall Plaza (arcgis.ground#3045, to z 724.6 and x +26.0) really is inside the college and the shipped eighth.bounds really do truncate it. What was wrong was using the envelope to crop the PAVING: arcgis.ground[3632] is the campus-wide walk layer, so the envelope alone let 1,929 m2 of Keeling, Galbraith and Revelle approach take Eighth photographed paver blend. The paving now carries its own measured.paving.collegeClip, whose two edges are survey vertices. Note that #3045 itself contributes no span to the paving table at all — it is a separate walk polygon — so it never justified the eastern reach of the paving crop in the first place.

georegistration.what: A transform from the 2025 BUILT-condition SDAF site plan into repo world metres, established on the surveyed basketball court.
georegistration.plan: sdaf-plan rendered at 400 dpi to 3400 x 4400 px
georegistration.derivation: Court baselines at px x 902 and 1140 (238 px = the surveyed 22.7 m -> 10.48 px/m); sidelines at px y 927 and 1085 (158 px = the surveyed 15.4 m -> 10.26 px/m). The centre line falls at px x 1021, the exact midpoint — an independent check. The two scales agree to 2%, so there is no rotation between plan and world.
georegistration.verification: Overlaid on the drawn footprints of Sankofa, Podemos, Azad and Pulse — all land within a few metres.

paving.what: The measured paved extent of the whole college. arcgis.ground[3632] is a single k:"walk" multipolygon: ONE outer ring and 213 holes that punch out every planting bed, lawn, garden island and the basketball court. Building the paving as outer-minus-holes guarantees paving and beds cannot overlap and that no plate outline is invented.

subtractedMassing.why: ground[3632]'s holes do NOT punch out the buildings — 1,645 m2 of the walk layer runs under the TDLLN masses. Every campus-arcgis massing ring whose bbox meets these bounds is therefore cut out of the spans as well, with a 0.15 m keep-off, so no paver decal passes under a wall.

paving.method: Exact scanline: at each row centre z the outer ring edge crossings are paired into spans and clipped to the envelope AND to collegeClip.x1; rows north of collegeClip.z0 are dropped whole; then every hole, every massing ring (with clearance) and every carried survey ring is subtracted — sampled at BOTH ROW EDGES as well as the centre and unioned, so a strip is cut wherever any part of it overlaps rather than only where its centre line does. Spans shorter than minSpan are dropped as survey slivers. Rounded to 3 decimal places, which is the form shipped below; the test re-derives the whole table from campus-arcgis.json and campus-eighth.json and compares it entry for entry.

collegeClip.why: arcgis.ground[3632] is the CAMPUS-WIDE walk layer, not an Eighth feature: it runs x -223..235, z -186..702. Cropping it to this section bounds still left 1,929 m2 of it — 19.7% of the field — outside Eighth College, and painted it with Eighth photographed P1/P2 blend. That is photo-sourced APPEARANCE applied to ground the photographs never covered, which is the same overreach as reading a height off the wrong epoch. Both edges below are survey vertices, so nothing here is typed.
collegeClip.z0Source: z >= 499.6 is the NORTH face of arcgis.massing[252] (TDLLN - Podemos), the northernmost of the ten TDLLN masses. North of it the walk layer serves Charles David Keeling Apartments 2 (massing[329], z 421.5..497.6) and Galbraith Hall (massing[0], z 428.6..491.7), neither of which any frame in this section source set covers. 1,305 m2 removed.
collegeClip.x1Source: x <= -24.3 is the EAST face of arcgis.massing[253] (TDLLN - Podemos tower), the easternmost of the ten TDLLN masses. Every span east of it lies in z 480..540 — the Galbraith / Revelle approach — and none of it is Market Hall Plaza: the Plaza is arcgis.ground#3045 (x -73.2..26.0, z 605.3..724.6), a SEPARATE walk polygon that contributes no span to this table at all. 624 m2 removed. The bounds keep their eastern reach because Market Hall Plaza really is inside the college and the shipped eighth.bounds really do truncate it; it is the PAVING that must not run there.
collegeClip.removedNote: Declared, not silently dropped — see absent.

subtractedRings.why: arcgis.ground[3632] own 213 holes punch out MOST beds, but not the ten campus-eighth.json bed rings and six named survey rings this section carries and draws on. Round one cut the spans by the holes and the massing only, so about 12 m2 of paving was drawn INSIDE surveyed planting beds, coplanar with the mulch and the gravel on the same `carpet` rung — two decals fighting for the same pixel. Every ring this section renders anything on is now subtracted as well, at the same three-probe row quantisation.
subtractedRings.excluded: pavilionSlabWest (arcgis.ground#2374) is NOT subtracted: it is the PAVED apron of the north parking-elevator pavilion, hardscape rather than planting, and the pavilion stands on it.

paving.surveyAreaNote: The full arcgis.ground[3632] scanline inside `bounds`, BEFORE the college clip and the carried-ring subtraction: 9,784.995 m2 in 1,342 spans. Kept as the record of what the survey layer gives here, so the two subtractions below are auditable subtractions and not a quietly smaller number.

keepOut.what: Every campus-arcgis massing ring inside these bounds, carried verbatim so the module can cut buildings out of the SURVEYED BED fills as well as out of the paving. The green survey layer does not agree with the massing layer: arcgis.ground#2703, a courtyard ring, runs 20 m under the drawn Sankofa Base. The survey is the authority on a bed's extent and the massing is the authority on where a building stands, so where they overlap the building wins and the bed is cut.

rings.name: Joan and Irwin Jacobs Center for La Jolla Playhouse

notDrawn.what: Every numeric figure this section RECORDS but does not draw, and why. The rule this list exists to enforce: a measurement either drives geometry or is named here with the reason it cannot. A number sitting in the data driving nothing, unremarked, is the defect. The test enumerates every numeric leaf in the section and fails on any key name the module never reads that is also missing from this list.

keys.paving.families.*.thickness: The paver / slab thickness. The paving is a ground DECAL on the overlay ladder, not a solid, so a thickness has nothing to drive. P1 0.057 m is itself [estimated] (the paver edge is never visible in any frame; 2.25 in is the standard for the class); P4 0.15 m likewise. Recorded so a future section that builds a kerb reveal or a step nosing against the paving has the figure.
keys.paving.families.P1.lengths: The four observed plank lengths, 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 / 0.60 m, read as 2x / 3x / 4x / 6x the measured 0.089 m width in EYRC phf03. The library unit-grid class draws one repeating cell size and cannot lay random lengths, so unit[1] carries the MODAL 0.30 m and this array records what was actually seen. Drawing it would need a per-unit geometry pass, which is a different and much more expensive object than a decal.
keys.paving.families.P4.unit: The 1.5 m score panel. Measured, and deliberately not drawn — see absent, the library joint would be 11x the measured sawcut. It still drives P4.tile as the noise scale.
keys.court.tileModule: 0.305 m, the modular sport-tile module. campus-eighth-court.js owns the court SURFACE (see court.surfaceNote); this section changes only its colours, so nothing here can draw a tile grid. [estimated] anyway — the grid is visible in SWA -16 but never against a scale bar.
keys.levelChange.retaining.chamfer: 0.02 m arris chamfer on the cast-in-place retaining wall. The wall is drawn as a scaled box and a 20 mm chamfer is below the geometry this module builds; adding it would cost a bespoke extrusion per run for a detail smaller than the wall own segmentation error. Recorded from SWA -5.
keys.levelChange.stairs.*.nosing: 0.00 m. The photographed flight has a square nosing with no projection, which is why the figure is zero; it is recorded so that a later flight with a real nosing is not silently given this one geometry.
keys.lawns.mown: 0.06 m mown turf height. The Sun Lawn is a ground decal on the carpet rung, so there is no blade geometry to give a height to. Recorded from SWA -4.
keys.lawns.panels.*.areaM2: 351.6 m2. Not drawn — but not dead either: the test re-derives it by shoelace from the surveyed ring and fails if the two disagree, which is what makes the ring verbatim claim checkable at the panel level rather than only at the ring level.
keys.lawns.syntheticWithheld.*: The Social 10 x 6 m synthetic turf panel, its 0.03 m pile and 0.30 m edge band. Sourced and deliberately NOT built: no measured paved run in The Social accepts a 10 x 6 m footprint without overrunning a surveyed bed, and shrinking a sourced dimension to make it fit would be inventing a measurement. See absent.
keys.levelChange.seatWalls.courseHeight: NOW DRAWN. 0.203 m course and 0.406 m unit drive the CMU texture repeat on the seat wall so the coursing renders at true scale; listed here only to record that round one left both figures unread.
keys.court.apron.width: 2.45 m, the surveyed apron run east of the court. The zone rectangle is grown by court.apron.reach (5.48 m, the widest surveyed adjacent run) instead, so this figure is the corroborating measurement rather than the driver.

paving.rungNote: campus-eighth.js repaints the surveyed ground features on the `pad` rung. This field paints the same ground in its photographed paving families on the rung ABOVE it, so the two never z-fight and the older repaint remains the fallback if this module fails to load. Lifts and depth state come from campus-overlay.js; this module defines no lift of its own.

P1.label: narrow linear plank paver, warm blend — Scholars Cloister, academic-wing forecourt, Ridge Walk terrace
P1.unitNote: Unit WIDTH 0.089 m +/- 0.010 — nearest catalogue unit is the 4 in nominal / 98 mm actual narrow modular paver. Derivation: in EYRC phf03 (1799x1200) the man walking a bicycle spans 147.5 px (head y 855 -> feet y 1002); at 1.75 m that is 84.3 px/m at his foot depth, and the paving course pitch measured at the same depth is 7.5 px -> 0.089 m. Random lengths in the same field read as 2x, 3x, 4x and 6x the width, i.e. 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.40 / 0.60 m; 0.30 m is the modal length carried here.
P1.thicknessNote: [estimated] — the paver edge is never visible; 0.057 m (2.25 in) is the standard thickness for this class. Nothing is drawn from it; it is recorded so a future drawing can correct it.
P1.tileNote: tile = unit x 6 = 0.534 x 1.8 m, because one pavingConcreteUnit texture tile is a 6 x 6 grid of units. Anisotropic, so the measured 0.089 x 0.3 m unit renders at its measured aspect.

P2.label: 2:1 rectangular paver, warm buff blend — the courtyards, The Social, the tower loggias, the Bamboo Garden surround. The dominant courtyard surface.
P2.unitNote: 0.315 x 0.157 m (12 x 6 in nominal, 305 x 152 mm). Derivation: in SWA -17 two walkers 1.70 m tall span 405 px (head y 430 -> feet y 835) -> 238 px/m at their foot depth; joints at that depth fall at 150 px pitch on the long axis and 75 px on the short -> 0.315 x 0.157 m. Cross-check: a 0.26 m sneaker in the same frame spans 140 px -> 538 px/m upper bound, consistent. Half-lap offset 0.157 m.
P2.tileNote: tile = unit x 6 = 1.89 x 0.942 m, because one pavingConcreteUnit texture tile is a 6 x 6 grid of units. Anisotropic, so the measured 0.315 x 0.157 m unit renders at its measured aspect.

P3.label: small 2:1 mosaic, cool grey blend — the Ramble courtyard fields
P3.unitNote: About 0.20 x 0.10 m (2:1), read off the near-overhead SWA -12 where the unit aspect is unambiguous and the field runs continuous with the P2 field whose module is measured at 0.315 x 0.157 m. THE 'MOSAIC' IS THE COLOUR BLEND, NOT THE UNIT SHAPE — three to four greys laid checkerboard-random. That is the correction of record against campus-eighth.js's 'angular concrete plate mosaic', which assumed large irregular plates and shipped a 30-degree scoring as its weak form for want of per-plate geometry: there are no plates.
P3.tileNote: tile = unit x 6 = 1.2 x 0.6 m, because one pavingConcreteUnit texture tile is a 6 x 6 grid of units. Anisotropic, so the measured 0.2 x 0.1 m unit renders at its measured aspect.

P4.label: cast-in-place concrete in large scored panels — Market Hall Plaza, Theatre Walk, the basketball-court apron
P4.unitNote: Score-joint grid about 1.5 m, read against a 1.75 m walker in EYRC phf19 whose height spans 118 px at the panel depth. Joint width about 0.006 m sawcut. Warm buff integral colour, sandblast / light broom finish.
P4.tileNote: [estimated] extends P4.unit, the MEASURED 1.5 m score panel. smoothConcrete has NO unit grid, so no x6 factor applies and this is a noise scale: setting it to the measured panel makes the cast-concrete surface variation read at panel scale, but it is a choice of scale and not a measurement OF the noise, so it takes the estimated tier. The score grid itself is NOT drawn: see absent. campus-materials.js FIELDS.pavingConcreteUnit would draw its joint at a fixed 4.5% of the cell, i.e. 0.0675 m at a 1.5 m panel against the measured 0.006 m sawcut, and an 11x joint is a worse statement than no joint.

DG.label: stabilised decomposed granite — the Ramble's meandering paths
DG.unitNote: Main path 3.0-3.3 m wide (510 px across at 157 px/m from a 1.78 m walker in SWA -8), secondary loops 1.8-2.4 m; DG depth to the check-step riser 0.15-0.18 m. Not a unit product — `unit` here is only the texture tile.
DG.tileNote: [estimated] extends nothing measured — decomposedGranite is a NOISE class with no unit grid, so its tile is a grit scale and not a product dimension. 2.5 m is the scale at which the library grit reads as walked-flat DG at eye height; no frame in the set resolves a DG grain against a scale bar. Recorded as estimated rather than stamped measured.

paving.zoneNote: [estimated] — WHICH blend covers WHICH field is photo-inferred. The zones below are read off the frames listed against each; the survey does not record paving material, and no paving schedule is published. The first zone a span's centre falls in wins; anything unclaimed takes the default P2. Zone boundaries are deliberately rectangles: the real field boundaries are angular chevrons (SWA -12 shows five re-entrants at an included angle of 110-130 degrees, deviating 25-35 degrees from the building grid), and inventing chevron outlines would be exactly the invented plate geometry this section exists to retire.

zones.source: eyrc phf03; swa -7 — the academic-wing forecourt and the Ridge Walk terrace

[measured] DERIVED, not typed: measured.court.rect (arcgis.ground#3898, the surveyed court) grown by court.apron.reach = 5.48 m, the widest paved run adjacent to the court in the shipped span table. SWA -16 shows the cast-concrete apron on all four sides.
eyrc phf19 — Market Hall Plaza and Theatre Walk (arcgis.ground#3045, #4073)
swa -8, -9, -6, -22 — the Ramble corridor between the surveyed swale beds
swa -12, -2 — the four principal fields between Pulse, Sankofa Mid, Azad and the Ramble

paving.tileRule: A texture tile is NOT one paving unit. campus-materials.js FIELDS.pavingConcreteUnit lays COLS = 6 by ROWS = 6 units inside one tile (campus-materials.js:175), so a family whose material is pavingConcreteUnit must carry tile = unit x 6 on BOTH axes, and the strip mesh must lay uv = (x / tile[0], z / tile[1]) so a 2:1 unit renders 2:1 and not square. Round one set tile to the unit itself and rendered every paver at one sixth of its measured size — the 0.315 m P2 unit drew at 52 mm. campus-photo-galbraith.js:1015 (paverPitch * 6) and campus-photo-keeling.js:1028 (7.2 = 1.2 * 6) are the shipped precedent. Classes with no unit grid (decomposedGranite, smoothConcrete) take no factor: their tile is a NOISE scale, tiered [estimated], not a product dimension.

edging.label: flush dark steel bed edging
edging.source: swa -17, -13, -12 — a dark flat edge strip set flush with the paver top at every bed boundary
edging.note: Run along every segment of every ring named in `rings`, verbatim from the survey, so the edging is SURVEYED geometry and not a traced line; its length is therefore a measured figure the module reports. Each ring says WHY it takes an edge, because an edge is a claim about a boundary. A segment whose midpoint falls inside a drawn massing ring is dropped: a bed edge running under a building is a survey/massing conflict, not an edge. `measured.rings.teaHouseIsland` and `measured.rings.pavilionSlabWest` are carried for CLIPPING only and are NOT in this list — the Tea House island is eighthgathering's ground and the pavilion slab is paved, so neither is a bed boundary this section may assert.

gardenBands.label: the same edging used decoratively as parallel bands through the Bamboo Garden's raked gravel
gardenBands.source: swa -3, -21 — about eight bands counted across the garden island, dividing the gravel into 3-4 m panels
gardenBands.pitchNote: DERIVED, not measured: the module spreads the COUNTED 8 bands evenly across the surveyed island, so the pitch is a consequence of the count and the island, never an independent claim. Island z extent 29.80 m (arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193) / (8 + 1) = 3.311 m. Round one declared 3.5 m alongside the count and the module honoured only the count, so the two disagreed by 6% with nothing to catch it. The photographed 3-4 m panel width is what corroborates the count.

rings.why: arcgis.ground#2369, the Sun Lawn. This section lays turf inside it, so its whole boundary is a turf/paving edge — the exact condition SWA -17, -13 and -12 photograph a flush steel strip at.

arcgis.ground#1160. THE SURFACE IS WITHHELD AND THE BOUNDARY IS NOT — see absent[21]. What #1160 cannot resolve is the internal edge between its mown west/centre lobe and its decomposed-granite east arm, so no DECAL may cover it; its OUTER 54-vertex ring is a surveyed boundary between a planted ring and the paved field either way, and both readings of the inside are bed surfaces that the same photographed detail edges. The edge asserts nothing about which surface is behind it. Segments that run under a drawn mass are cut by the massing keep-out like every other ring's.
arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193, the Bamboo Garden island. This section lays its raked gravel inside it, so its boundary is a gravel/paving edge.
arcgis.ground#1761, the clipped hedge strip on the court's north side. This section plants it, so its boundary is a planting/paving edge.
arcgis.ground#2144, the clipped hedge strip on the court's east side, as courtHedgeNorth.

the ten campus-eighth.json bed rings this section carries. eighthramble plants them; this section neither plants nor paves inside them, and it subtracts every one of them from its own paving — so their boundary is a bed/paving edge in the shipped document whichever section fills them.

levelChange.epochNote: THIS BLOCK EXISTS TO RETIRE A DEAD-EPOCH WITHHOLDING. campus-eighth.js omits every stair, terrace, retaining and seat wall on the ground that 'the 2014 LiDAR under the courtyard is smooth to 1.5% over 150 m with no step anywhere, so there is no built grade for a flight to descend or a wall to retain'. The 2014 LiDAR is describing a demolished parking lot: it cannot see a college built in 2021-2023. Eleven 2024-25 photographs resolve stair flights, tan retaining walls, buff CMU seat walls, stepped LED-lit seat terraces, an accessible ramp and a bridge. Existence is settled. POSITION is the remaining problem, and it is settled only where the survey or the georegistered 2025 plan reaches: what is anchored is built, what is not is in `absent` with the reason.

handrail.label: brushed stainless round tube on stainless posts, full horizontal returns top and bottom

POST PITCH CORRECTED 2026-08-19: this section carried 1.35 m with no derivation of any kind and the arbitration's `unresolved` named it — 'eighthcourtyards says 1.35 m with no derivation ... I left 1.55 standing as the only value with any derivation'. 1.55 m is now carried from the spec owner with that derivation, and the figure is enumerated above so a value outside the owner's list cannot sit here unremarked again.

TWO FIGURES DERIVED HERE 2026-08-19, because the spec owner carries no post spec at all and this section was typing round numbers into the gap: `post` was 0.05 m and `postSpacing` was 2.4 m, neither derived from anything, and together they placed 22 guard posts. Both are now consequences of the members that WERE measured — see `figures`. `lowerRailHeight` was 0.10 m for the same reason and is now the same 4 in module as the picket pitch.

figures.height: [measured] 1.067 m (42 in). SWA -5: a 1.70 m walker spans 185 px (head y 385 -> feet y 570) = 109 px/m, and the rail top is 115 px above the deck at her station = 1.06 m; CBC 1015.3's 42 in = 1.067 m is the exact figure that read brackets, and four independent photographic reads across the sibling sections (1.06, 1.066, 1.067, 1.07) bracket it too. Owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail.
figures.picketPitch: [measured] 0.1016 m — 4 in exactly, the arbitrated Eighth value owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail. This section's own earlier 0.092 m was counted at about 2 px a picket on a 0.6x copy and is retired.
figures.picketDia: [measured] 0.019 m — 3/4 in round bar, the arbitrated value. This section's earlier 0.016 m is retired.
figures.topRail: [measured] 0.048 m — 1 1/2 in Sch.40, OD 1.900 in = 0.04826 m. A named product step. Owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail.
figures.lowerRail: [measured] 0.033 m — 1 in Sch.40, OD 1.315 in = 0.03340 m. A named product step. Owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail.
figures.lowerRailHeight: [derived] 0.1016 m to the lower rail's axis. NOT a free figure: the clear opening beneath the bottom rail is governed by the same 4 in (0.1016 m) sphere rule that fixes the picket pitch, and at an axis height of one 4 in module the clear opening under a 0.033 m rail is 0.1016 - 0.0165 = 0.085 m, inside the rule with margin. It is therefore the picket module itself, not an independent claim. The 0.10 m carried until 2026-08-19 was that same number rounded, and rounded to a value the module grid does not contain.
figures.post: [estimated] 0.0603 m. EXTENDS THE GUARD'S OWN MEASURED PIPE SCHEDULE: the three members that ARE measured are exactly 3/4 in round bar (0.019), 1 in Sch.40 (OD 1.315 in = 0.033) and 1 1/2 in Sch.40 (OD 1.900 in = 0.048), so the assembly is a standard Sch.40 pipe-and-picket guard. A post cannot be a lighter section than the top rail it carries, so it takes the next size in that same schedule — 2 in Sch.40, OD 2.375 in = 0.06033 m. No frame in the set resolves the post's own diameter; SWA -5 is the only frame that reads the guard at all and at 109 px/m a post images about 6 px. The 0.05 m carried until 2026-08-19 is not a size in any pipe schedule and was typed, not read.
figures.postSpacing: [estimated] 2.4384 m. EXTENDS THE MEASURED PICKET MODULE: pickets are at 0.1016 m (4 in) centres, a shop-fabricated picket panel spans a whole number of those bays, and 24 bays is 2.4384 m = 8 ft, the standard fabricated panel length. No frame resolves the post stations — SWA -5 shows the guard obliquely and the picket run it does resolve is not bounded by two visible posts — so the panel length is estimated and the MODULE it must land on is measured. The 2.4 m carried until 2026-08-19 was 8 ft rounded to two figures, which is 23.6 picket bays: every post after the first landed mid-bay, which is the one thing a fabricated panel cannot do.

It lands on the wing's WEST elevation rather than the Ridge Walk face because the survey carries no paved ground against the east face inside the wing's extent; that is a statement about the survey, not a claim about the address. seatTerraces.label: the stepped LED-lit seat terrace on the Bamboo Garden's north side
seatTerraces.source: eyrc phf48 and swa -21, -20 — two to three tiers of tan concrete seat steps, each carrying a CONTINUOUS recessed LED strip under the nosing; this is what makes the garden read as glowing lines at dusk. Riser 0.45 m confirmed by people sitting on it in phf48; tread 0.75 m and run about 18 m; in SWA -21 seated figures give 141 px/m and the tier face measures 63 px. The LED channel is built as a recessed dark reveal only: NO luminous state is drawn, because this project has no night source (campus-photo-keeling.js takes the same position on its lamps).
seatTerraces.positionNote: ANCHORED to the surveyed Bamboo Garden island (arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193, x -189.7..-158.8, z 573.0..602.8) AND REJECTED OUT OF THE MEDITATION PAVILION. RE-SOLVED 2026-08-19: the earlier station [-175.0, 585.0] put this 18.0 x 1.5 m run at x -184.0..-166.0, z 584.25..585.75 — 12.9 m of it inside eighthgathering's `meditation.deck` (x -181.3..-168.4, z 584.85..591.05, 0.45 m solid on the same ground) and under its roof rect. The rule that produced it optimised for the island alone and never excluded the pavilion, so it landed on top of it. THE RULE NOW: reject any station unless the whole 18.0 x 1.5 m footprint lies inside the surveyed island AND clears `bambooGarden.pavilionClip.rect` by at least `pavilionClip.clearance`; among the accepted stations on a 0.05 m grid take the one whose south face is CLOSEST to the pavilion's north edge, tie-broken toward the pavilion's own centre line. That is [-180.35, 583.20] — footprint x -189.35..-171.35, z 582.45..583.95, 0.05 m clear of the pavilion's north edge, wholly inside the island's west lobe (which runs x -189.5..-171.3 through this z band, giving 0.2 m to spare on an 18.0 m run), and 5.64 m from the station the photograph was read at. The run is still on the garden's north side, which is what phf48 and SWA -21, -20 show. Every tier is provably inside the island and provably outside the pavilion, and the test asserts both.

seatTerraces.label: the stepped seat terrace at The Social, against the public-art wall
seatTerraces.source: [estimated] position — SWA -18 and -14 photograph three tiers of wide tan concrete seat steps used as informal amphitheatre seating, with eight students sitting on them; riser about 0.42 m, tread about 0.90 m, run about 9 m, read at 163 px/m. THIS is the real stepped seating on this site. The repo's `eighth.areas.amphitheatre` (3 tiers between the court's east edge and bed #2144) is corroborated by NO 2024-25 photograph and is superseded.
seatTerraces.positionNote: The station along The Social is not resolved by any frame. It is placed by a stated deterministic rule rather than a guess: the position nearest The Social's OWN DERIVED CENTROID at which the whole 9.0 x 2.7 m footprint — three 0.90 m treads over a 9.0 m run — lies on MEASURED paved spans, searched on a 0.5 m grid over `places.social.rect`. That is [-76.1, 563.8], 13.75 m from the centroid (-62.35, 563.70); only four stations in the whole rectangle accept, all of them in the same 0.5 x 1.0 m cluster, so the answer is not sensitive to the tie-break. RE-SOLVED 2026-08-19, TWICE OVER. (1) The footprint shrank: the earlier 9.0 x 3.1 m assembly included a public-art wall at its north edge, and that wall is WITHDRAWN — eighthgathering.bbq.mural builds the same commission, anchored on a surveyed ring and with its artwork sourced, so this section may not build a second carrier for it. See `absent`. (2) The earlier station [-75.5, 563.0] did not satisfy its own stated predicate: run against the shipped span table it is NOT a position at which the whole assembly lands on measured paving, and the centroid it claimed to be nearest, (-74, 559), was not the centroid of the derived rectangle either — both were left over from the round-one `places` table that the arbitration replaced. The rule and the answer now agree, and the test re-runs the search rather than reading the answer.

apron.source: [measured] from the survey itself, not from the photograph. The WEST run is 5.48 m on both its rows; `reach` is that widest surveyed adjacent run, and the courtApron paving zone is the surveyed court bounding rectangle grown by it, so the whole cast-concrete apron takes the P4 family. Round one typed the zone rectangle as x -190..-158, z 512..537 with no derivation at all.

bambooGarden.label: the Bamboo Garden / Mental Wellness Zone floor

gravel.tileNote: [estimated] extends DG.tile — the same decomposedGranite noise class at a finer scale, because SWA -3 and -21 show the Bamboo Garden raked to a visibly finer grade than the Ramble walks. No unit grid, so no x6 factor.

planterCubes.source: swa -3 overhead — twelve dark charcoal square planter cubes counted, 1.60 x 1.60 x 0.90 m with a thin cap, holding clipped shrub balls, small multi-stem trees or clumping bamboo. Read against people sitting on the cube rims in SWA -13.

bambooGarden.extentNote: THIS SUPERSEDES the shipped eighth section's '~11 x 8 m surveyed opening', which used the GAP between arcgis.ground#328 and #329 rather than the garden island itself. The island is arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193, 792.3 m2, x -189.7..-158.8, z 573.0..602.8, and the 2025 plan's white field at x -192..-161, z 576..605 independently confirms it to about 3 m.

pavilionClip.note: NOT THIS SECTION'S GEOMETRY. This is eighthgathering.meditation.bark.rect, carried verbatim so everything this section builds in the Bamboo Garden can be held out of it. The gravel rides the `carpet` rung and gathering's bark decal rides `pad`, so gravel over the whole island would paint the Meditation Pavilion's own ground surface out from under it; and the rect is a 0.45 m solid deck under a roof in the owning section, so a solid of this section's built inside it is inside the pavilion. The rect is gathering's measured spine opening, clipped to the courtyard-328/329 rings; this section neither measures it nor draws anything inside it. CORRECTED 2026-08-19: that last sentence used to be false. The LED seat terrace was built 12.9 m inside this rect and two of the eight garden bands ran straight across it, and nothing gated it because the test asserted that the clip EXISTED rather than that anything was absent from it. The seat terrace is re-solved, the bands are cut, the gravel clip now cuts spans in x instead of dropping whole rows, and the gate walks every placement and every merged vertex this module builds.
pavilionClip.clearanceNote: [derived] 0.02 m, the same one-drawing-tolerance offset eighthgathering holds its own bark decal inside this rect at (`meditation.bark.inset`). It is not decoration: this rect is a SOLID 0.45 m deck with a roof over it in the owning section, so anything this section builds must clear it rather than touch it, and geometry sharing a face with a sibling's solid is geometry inside it as soon as either side moves. It is the rejection margin for the seat terrace, the garden bands, the raked gravel and the planter cubes alike.

lawns.label: the one resolved turf panel

The library's own `foliage` class is an alpha-cut CARD map and would punch holes through a ground fill — campus-photo-keeling.js records the same trap.

panels.source: arcgis.ground#2369, 7 vertices, x -135.7..-104.3 (31.4 m) x z 559.2..580.7 (21.5 m); arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 176 punches the identical polygon out of the paving. Photographed green and mown in SWA -4 and phf22.

That entry names 'the big turf panel NORTH OF THE TERRACE'; the terrace is arcgis.ground#2375 (shipped eighth.areas.bbq.anchor), so absent[7] refers to the lawn inside arcgis.ground#1160, whose outline is still unresolved and whose panel is withdrawn from this section. What this panel DOES supersede is campus-eighth-furniture.js TURF_PANELS `turf-2369`: the same lawn, traced from one Apple frame at 148.0 m2, an under-trace of the surveyed 351.6 m2 ring by 58%, and offset ~8-10 m west of the turf in ESRI orthoimagery registered sub-metre to the surveyed court. SWA -4 and EYRC phf22, both 2024-25, show mown irrigated green turf with hard concrete edges. Two dated sources disagree; the newer, higher-resolution one wins under the epoch rule, and the Apple read is consistent with a newly-seeded lawn photographed before establishment. The tan paint stays on the `pad` rung underneath; this section's turf paints over it on `carpet`.

syntheticWithheld.source: NOT BUILT — SWA -18 and -14 show a bright uniformly green synthetic panel about 10 x 6 m with a hard concrete edge and a paver band, holding the Adirondack cluster at The Social. No measured paved run anywhere in The Social accepts a 10 x 6 m footprint without overrunning a surveyed planting bed (searched on a 0.5 m grid over the whole place), and the panel's dimensions are approximate. Shrinking a sourced dimension to make it fit would be inventing a measurement; see `absent`.

Until 2026-08-19 the check named a public-art wall at (-75.5, 561.65) that has since been withdrawn to eighthgathering.

Every one of those objects went to a sibling section in the 2026-08-19 arbitration; the six orphaned rectangles are deleted rather than left as unsourced geometry, and the one that survives now has a derivation.
