supersedes.why: The centre trident is the same UCSD gold as the keys in SWA -16. The #576564 median is 24,470 rectified pixels of the same shadowed frame; the geometry it was measured on (campus-eighth-court.js's parametric trident) is unaffected and stays.

supersedes.target: campus-eighth-furniture.js TURF_PANELS[0], key "turf-2369" — a 15-vertex 148.0 m2 turf panel traced from one Apple frame inside arcgis.ground#2369
supersedes.replacement: lawns.panels[0] "sun-lawn" — the FULL surveyed arcgis.ground#2369 ring, 351.6 m2, on the `carpet` rung
supersedes.why: Same lawn, and only one of them may ship or the Sun Lawn is drawn twice on two rungs at two colours (#9d947c against lawnTurf). The shipped panel is a single-frame trace at 148.0 m2, a 58% under-trace of the surveyed ring, and in ESRI orthoimagery registered sub-metre to the surveyed basketball court it sits 8-10 m WEST of the turf while the surveyed ring lands on it; the shipped module's own note concedes the outline is 'declared as one frame's' and that its second frame ref8 was 5.7 m out. SHIPPED eighth.absent[7] IS NOT TOUCHED: 'the big turf panel north of the terrace' is the lawn inside arcgis.ground#1160 (the terrace is #2375), whose outline is still unresolved and which this section no longer paints.

supersedes.target: campus-photo-detail.json eighth.areas.amphitheatre (3 tiers between the court's east edge and bed #2144)
supersedes.why: No 2024-25 photograph corroborates stepped seating in that band; it was inferred from a zigzag tiered edge on the 2021 DESIGN plan. The real stepped seat terrace is at The Social (SWA -18, -14), with eight students sitting on it.

supersedes.target: campus-eighth.js omission "Stair flights, terraces, retaining and seat walls ... the 2014 LiDAR under the courtyard is smooth ... so there is no built grade for a flight to descend or a wall to retain"
supersedes.replacement: levelChange (built where anchored; declared in `absent` where not)
supersedes.why: The 2014 LiDAR predates the college by seven years and measures a parking lot. Its smoothness is evidence of nothing here. Eleven 2024-25 photographs resolve the flights and walls.

supersedes.target: campus-eighth.js omission "The angular concrete plate mosaic ... a 30-degree rotated scoring ships instead"
supersedes.why: There are no plates. SWA -12 (near-overhead) resolves the units as a narrow-modular 2:1 paver in a three-to-four-grey random BLEND; the 'mosaic' is the colour blend and the chevron FIELD boundaries, not irregular plate outlines. And the extent was never missing: arcgis.ground[3632] is a surveyed walk multipolygon that yields 9,785 m2 of paving inside these bounds with guaranteed non-overlap against every bed.

Market Hall Plaza, The Backyard, Theatre Walk, the Theatre Drop-Off, both southern portals, the Loading Dock, the Survivance Front Porch, the mid-site parking-elevator pavilion and the mobility hub all fall outside the shipped bounds, so the southern third of the college could not ship under the ultra standard at all.

absent: The artificial turf panel at The Social. SWA -18 and -14 photograph a bright uniformly green synthetic panel about 10 x 6 m with a hard concrete edge, holding the Adirondack cluster. No measured paved run anywhere in The Social accepts a 10 x 6 m footprint without overrunning a surveyed planting bed, searched on a 0.5 m grid over the whole place. The photographed dimension is approximate and the station is unresolved; shrinking the dimension to force a fit would be inventing a measurement.

The accessible ramp. Cast concrete, 1.80 m clear width, about a 14 m run between landings with a 0.10 m upstand kerb and a guard both sides, photographed in SWA -4 and -2. Its rise is inferred from the CBC 1:12 maximum, not measured, and NO source resolves where it starts or ends. A ramp placed at a guessed station on a terrain that predates the college would be a floating deck with an invented grade at both ends.

The bridge over the Ramble — RETIRED, BUILT BY A SIBLING. eighthramble.systems.bridges builds BOTH crossings on their surveyed walk rings, and its west-bridge correction is real: the survey's own ring there is a right TRIANGLE, 5.60 m on its legs, not the 5 x 2.4 m rectangle the shipped model 'shortened to fit'. The deck width 2.4 m this section measured (two men abreast in phf22) survives inside that. Nothing here is unresolved any more; the entry stays only so the measurement keeps its provenance and so the reader is sent to the section that owns it.

Stairs S2, S3 and S4 — PARTLY RETIRED. S2, the Pulse entry steps at the basketball court, is BUILT: eighthgathering.courtStair ships it with a derivation, 7 treads, clipped by the surveyed planting bed it runs into. Still absent are The Social steps (6-7 risers, about 6 m wide) and the two broad Ramble flights (6-7 risers each, about 3.5 m): both are photographed and neither is anchored to a surveyed ground feature or to a terrace anyone has built, so a flight placed by eye would be an invented grade change. The handrail spec they will take is eighthsiteworks.systems.handrail; the flights themselves land first.

Every retaining-wall run except the 26.8 m behind the basketball court. About 260 m of W1 is visible across SWA -2, -5, -6, -16 and phf19, but the survey does not carry walls and the level changes they hold are not in the 2014 terrain; only the run the surveyed hedge strip arcgis.ground#1761 anchors is built.

The Front Porches at Pulse, Podemos, Azad and Sankofa — RETIRED AS A GAP, RE-POINTED AT THEIR OWNERS. All four are named on the 2025 plan as raised entry terraces, and each is now its own building team's geometry rather than this section's: sankofa.frontPorch, azad.porch and pulse.groundStorey.porch ship, and Podemos' is being built in this same pass. This section never had a source that dimensioned any of them and it does not build one; what it withdraws is the claim that the porches are UNBUILT. They are simply not hardscape.

The mural artwork — RETIRED FROM THIS SECTION, BUILT BY A SIBLING. SWA -14/-18 resolve a panel of pale eucalyptus branches on a blue-lilac ground; the same eucalyptus-leaf motif is the interior lobby mural in phf32/phf35, so it is one commission. eighthgathering.bbq.mural builds it — 3.4 x 1.9 m on its service-enclosure face, anchored on the surveyed arcgis.ground#2375, with the branch and leaf figures code-generated from its seed and never a photographic texture — and gathering's note already retires the shipped eighth absent entry. This section's own read (a panel about 7.5 x 3.2 m on a board-formed wall at the top of The Social's seat terrace) is a DIFFERENT STATION for the same commission and it is the weaker of the two: gathering's is anchored on a survey ring and this one was an [estimated] position. One commission, one owner. This section no longer claims to supersede the shipped entry either.
The mid-site parking-elevator pavilion between Sankofa Base and Market Hall Plaza. Labelled on both site plans, photographed by nothing in the set.
The Loading Dock, the Theatre Drop-Off turnaround, the mobility hub and both parking-structure portals. Named on the 2025 plan, inside the corrected bounds, and photographed by nothing in the set.

The Market Hall / STATION8 pavilion itself and the Survivance and Podemos-academic masses. They are massing, not hardscape, and arcgis.massing[462], [464] and [252] are missing from campus-eighth.json entirely. This section cuts them out of the paving so nothing runs under them, and builds none of them.

Paving manufacturer, exact nominal unit sizes and the colour-blend recipe. Unit widths and aspect ratios are measured to about 10% (0.089 m for P1, 0.315 x 0.157 m for P2), but no catalogue product is named and no paving schedule is published. WHICH blend covers WHICH field is photo-inferred and ships as a rectangle approximation of angular chevron boundaries.

The chevron field boundaries themselves. SWA -12 shows five distinct re-entrants in one frame at an included angle of 110-130 degrees, deviating 25-35 degrees from the building grid. Their outlines are not traceable at that resolution and the survey does not carry them; drawing them would be exactly the invented plate geometry this pass exists to retire.

Luminaire manufacturer and model for both pole families, for the bollard and for the recessed riser step-light. Head and pole geometry are measured off 6x crops; product identity is not established and no cut-sheet, spec or campus lighting standard was found. No pole POSITION is sourced either — the grid rule is declared, not photographed.

Every night state. Two LED systems are photographed (the continuous strips under the Bamboo Garden seat nosings and the vertical slots between the pavilion's screen segments) and both are built as recessed dark channels only. This project has no night source; campus-photo-keeling.js takes the same position on its lamps.

The Meditation Pavilion's screen-segment count and radii — SETTLED BY A SIBLING. eighthgathering.meditation builds three free-standing curved vertical batten drums, 46 screen panels at a 0.95 m module with a 0.075 m slot on the three measured drum arcs, and three oculi counted in SWA -3. That retires this section's 'five to six individual cylindrical segments per frame, none of them resolvable'. The pavilion is not this section's geometry at all any more; the observation is kept so the count's provenance is not lost.

The Meditation Pavilion roof's plan dimension — SETTLED BY A SIBLING. This section read 14.9 x 8.6 m off the georegistered 2025 plan and SWA -3's overhead read close to square, and it shipped the plan figure with the conflict open. eighthgathering resolved it to 13.5 x 7.3 m by solving the horizon from two known heights, which cancels the unknown focal length and camera distance (12.6 m), and cross-checking against a 37.2 m surveyed ruler in SWA -3 (14.3 m). It is also the only figure that fits inside courtyard-328/329's measured 14.9 x 7.9 m opening without standing on either surveyed ring. Not this section's geometry.

The basketball backboard size conflict — SETTLED, AND NOT THIS SECTION'S OBJECT ANY MORE. This section measured 1.35 +/- 0.07 x 0.98 +/- 0.05 m against the 3.048 m rim and called it recreational, not the 1.83 x 1.07 m regulation board; eighthsiteworks asserted the regulation board without measuring its width. Arbitration measured it against the coplanar 24 x 18 in shooter's square and by affine rectification of the board plane on both hoops: it is a 54 x 42 in (1.372 x 1.067 m) institutional glass board — this section's WIDTH class was right and its height was wrong. The standards are built by eighthsiteworks.systems.courtHardware and this section builds no court hardware. Kept so the measurement keeps its provenance.

Plant species as identifications. Every species in this section's `species` list is a photograph-based reading: genus is confident and species probable for most, but no planting schedule is published, so cultivars, quantities and spacings are unknown and the drifts are visually estimated. Nothing is labelled with a species in the built geometry.

New trees. The footprint already carries 45 LiDAR canopies and the 2024-25 photographs show a later generation; adding unregistered trees would double-plant. campus-eighth.js's judgement that 'the correct tree work here is subtractive' still stands and is not this section's to make.

arcgis.ground#1127 (1,985 m2, the south-western slope) and the remaining unregistered rings inside the envelope. #2374 is now given a reading — it is the apron of the north parking-elevator pavilion — but #1161 (334 m2, east of the court) and the rest still have no colour source and are not painted.

The CEQA / EIR record — RUNG EXERCISED 2026-08-19, AND IT FAILS. ceqanet.lci.ca.gov/2016111019 is the UC San Diego La Jolla 2018 LRDP Update, a campus-wide Notice of Preparation filed 2016-11-04, not a project EIR for this college; its own page states that the record was posted before CEQAnet could host attachments and that the 28 project documents must be obtained from the lead agency by telephone. The Theatre District Living and Learning Neighborhood entry inside it (2016111019/7, Addendum No. 5, August 2020) hosts exactly two attachments: a 187 KB Notice of Determination and a 145 KB Department of Fish and Wildlife fee receipt. Neither is a plan set. There are therefore NO risers, no terrace levels, no ramp rise and no grading or landscape drawings on this rung, and the ladder is genuinely exhausted before the [estimated] tier is used for the academic stair, the ramp and the terrace levels. The one planning document that IS in hand, the 2020 Regents item f9attach6, is a design-approval narrative with renderings and no dimensioned plan. What would still settle these: a UC San Diego Physical and Environmental Planning records request for the Addendum No. 5 project description, or the Kitchell / HKS record drawings.

THE WELLNESS CORRIDOR LAWN, arcgis.ground#1160. The ring is 1,521.9 m2 and carries TWO surfaces, so it cannot take one decal. ESRI z20 orthoimagery, registered sub-metre against the surveyed basketball court, shows a mown irrigated lawn over the west and centre (chroma-normalised gn 0.4061, the greenest surface in the college) and decomposed-granite mulch with boulders, sparse bunchgrass and a serpentine concrete walk over the east arm and everything south of z 530 (gn 0.3684, indistinguishable from Ramble beds #332 and #2703). The SDAF 2025 plan agrees: dark-linework fraction 59.1% over the east arm, matching Ramble bed #2703 at 53.6%, against 18.1-27.8% over the middle and west and 15.0% over the Sun Lawn. THE DIVIDING EDGE IS NOT RESOLVED: no arcgis ring and no ground[3632] paving hole divides #1160, and every imagery classifier tried here confuses mown turf with bunchgrass (control medians gn 0.3757 lawn vs 0.3722 bunchgrass) or is broken by the tower shadow — one fitted edge, x = -0.6335z + 203.28, looked clean at rms 1.93 m and proved ~20 m wrong against the raw pixels. The lawn's east limit is somewhere between x -107 and -103; that is not good enough to ship. Shipped eighth.absent[7] therefore STANDS, and #1160 keeps campus-eighth.js's dry-lawn #ab9d83. Better absent than wrong. THE OUTER RING STILL TAKES ITS BED EDGE, and that is not a contradiction: what is unresolved is the internal boundary BETWEEN the two surfaces, so no decal may cover the ring; its outer 54-vertex boundary is a surveyed edge between a planted ring and the paved field under either reading of the inside, and the flush steel strip SWA -17/-13/-12 photograph at every bed boundary asserts nothing about which surface is behind it. `edging.rings` says so per ring rather than leaving it to a list in code — that list was previously hard-coded in the module with no justification anywhere, which is how ~226 m of the reported 1,152 m of edging came to be asserted on a ring whose surface this section withholds.

Site lighting — the three pole families this section proposed are superseded by eighthsiteworks' canonical schedule. Positions here were an invented 19 m/13 m grid, and this section's 5.5 m read of the Market Hall Plaza square-pole light is contradicted by phf26, where that family stands ABOVE the 5.75 m pedestrian post-top. eighthsiteworks.systems.l1Pole / l2Pole / bollardLight is the only fitted metrology in the set — two independently solved horizons 1.7% apart — and it is the only one that anchors positions to surveyed polygons by a declared rule.

The Meditation Pavilion and the Tea House — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION. Both were built here and by eighthgathering, whose versions win on evidence: the pavilion's plate is solved by cancelling the focal length between two known heights and cross-checked against a surveyed ruler, and this section's box overran courtyard-328/329's measured opening by 0.6 m in x and 3.2 m in z, i.e. it stood on two surveyed rings. The Tea House cube is EYRC phf44's, the only frame that shows the whole object unclipped; this section's 5.3 x 5.0 m plan is out by 55%. This section's own audit had already found its pavilion shipping a 30 mm-tall roof that missed its fascia by 1.48 m and hovered 50 mm over its screens.

Loose furniture, bike racks, bins, emergency towers, standpipes and cabinets — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION. Every one of them was placed here by a deterministic rejection scatter over `places` rectangles: the footprint had to land on a measured paved span, which keeps them out of beds and buildings but does not put any of them where a photograph shows one. eighthgathering anchors its furniture to the surveyed BBQ terrace ring and counts it frame by frame, and eighthsiteworks anchors its bike ranks, waste pairs and blue-light tower to named surveyed polygons by a declared placement rule. A scatter loses to an anchor. The standpipes and cabinets this section scattered have no anchored replacement and are therefore simply absent.

The two linear gas fire features. Both are real and both were built here, anchored at (-118.0, 561.0) and (-146.5, 594.5) — but eighthgathering builds the same object from the same frames, as a masonry wall with a real firebox opening and a lava-media bed rather than a glass pane on a box, and it already supersedes the shipped fire-feature and fire-seat-wall items. One fire feature, one section. This section withdraws its own; the anchored centres it measured are recorded here so the positions are not lost.

Colour roles for the objects that left this section. 21 roles went with their objects (pavilionRoof -> eighthgathering.colors.pavilionRoof; pavilionFascia -> eighthgathering.colors.pavilionFascia; pavilionSoffit -> eighthgathering.colors.pavilionSoffit; seatPod -> eighthgathering.colors.seatPod; woodScreen -> eighthgathering.colors.woodScreen; teaWood -> eighthgathering.colors.teaWood; adirondack -> eighthgathering.colors.adirondack; cafeChair -> eighthgathering.colors.cafeChair; tableTop -> eighthgathering.colors.tableTop; tableLeg -> eighthgathering.colors.tableLeg; fireGlass -> eighthgathering.colors.fireGlass; binCharcoal -> eighthsiteworks.colors (waste); emergencyBlue -> eighthsiteworks.colors (blueLight); rimOrange -> eighthsiteworks.colors.safetyOrange; backboardAcrylic -> eighthsiteworks.colors (courtHardware); cobble -> eighthramble.colors; mulch -> eighthramble.colors; boulderPale -> eighthramble.colors; slabStone -> eighthgathering.colors.standingStone; grassBlue -> eighthramble.colors; grassStraw -> eighthramble.colors) rather than staying here as a second hex for a surface a sibling already colours — two values for one surface inside one merged document is the defect the colour arbitration existed to close. THREE ARE DELIBERATELY KEPT although this section no longer draws them: courtNavy #404a5b, courtGold #cf9443 (the lanes) and courtTrident #e1c44b (the centre mark). All three are this section's own corrections of shipped campus-eighth.js hexes, they are named in `supersedes`, and eighthsiteworks carries the identical values — they are a record, not a second opinion. THREE MORE ROLES LEFT 2026-08-19 with the objects below: `safetyOrange` #d4622a went with the calisthenics rig (it survives as eighthsiteworks.colors.safetyOrange, which adopted THIS section's value and THIS section's derivation in the arbitration), and `fdcRed` #b02318 went with the grill station's protective bollards (it survives as eighthramble.colors.fdcRed, which likewise adopted this section's value). Neither hex is lost from the merged document; both are simply no longer this section's to carry, because a colour role for an object a section does not build is a colour for nothing.

1,929 m2 of arcgis.ground[3632] INSIDE this section bounds that is NOT Eighth College paving, and is no longer painted. ground[3632] is the campus-wide walk multipolygon (x -223..235, z -186..702); cropping it to the corrected bounds still left 1,305 m2 north of z 499.6 — the Charles David Keeling Apartments 2 and Galbraith Hall approach — and 624 m2 east of x -24.3, the Galbraith / Revelle side, all of it in z 480..540. Round one painted every square metre of it in Eighth PHOTOGRAPHED P1/P2 blend, which is photo-sourced appearance applied to ground that no frame in this section source set covers. It is now cut by measured.paving.collegeClip, whose two edges are the north face of arcgis.massing[252] and the east face of arcgis.massing[253], the northernmost and easternmost TDLLN masses. The survey outline of that ground is real and is still the survey; what is absent is any claim about what it LOOKS like. Note the trap this caught: the round-one boundsNote justified the eastern reach with Market Hall Plaza running to x +26.0, but the Plaza is arcgis.ground#3045, a separate walk polygon that contributes not one span to this table.

The 1.5 m sawcut score grid in the P4 cast-in-place concrete. The 1.5 m panel is MEASURED (EYRC phf19, against a 1.75 m walker spanning 118 px at panel depth) and the sawcut is about 0.006 m wide. It is not drawn. campus-materials.js has exactly one unit-grid class, FIELDS.pavingConcreteUnit, and its joint is a fixed 4.5% of the cell — 0.0675 m at a 1.5 m panel, eleven times the measured sawcut — so drawing the grid with the library would state a joint an order of magnitude wrong across the whole of Market Hall Plaza, Theatre Walk and the court apron. P4 therefore ships on smoothConcrete with no grid at all, and the measured panel size survives as the noise scale. Better absent than 11x wrong. What would settle it: a joint-width parameter on the library class, which is campus-materials.js work and not this section to do.

The paver blend AMPLITUDE. The three-to-four-grey random blend is real (SWA -12 resolves it) and it IS built — campus-materials.js FIELDS.pavingConcreteUnit gives every unit its own tone through N.cell(ci, ri), which multiplies the sourced hex, so the field is not one flat colour. What is NOT measured is how far apart those greys are: the library variation is a generic 0.86..1.02 of the base, about plus or minus 9%, and no frame in the set gives a clean enough unshaded patch to measure the spread between the lightest and darkest unit in one field. The MEDIAN of each family is measured (p1Paver, p3Paver, p4Concrete) and the amplitude around it is the library. Recorded rather than tuned by eye.

The LAYING DIRECTION of every paver family. The strip mesh lays uv = (x / tile[0], z / tile[1]), which aligns the measured unit long axis with world x everywhere. The measured units are strongly directional — P1 is 0.089 x 0.30 m and P2 is 0.315 x 0.157 m — so this is a real claim and no frame in the set fixes it: SWA -12 and -17 are the only near-overhead frames and neither carries surveyed control to resolve a bond direction against the building grid, and the field boundaries themselves are the unresolved chevrons already declared above. A single world-aligned direction is the honest minimum: it is stated here rather than presented as measured, and one rotation constant per family would fix it the day a georegistered overhead resolves the bond.

The Street View rung, and what it would and would not settle. It has NOT been exercised, and this entry says so rather than letting the [estimated] figures stand as though the ladder were exhausted. What it could settle: the academic stair risers and tread, the terrace levels, the ramp rise and the guard kerb — all things a camera at eye level on the flight resolves and a drone frame at 30 m does not. What makes it a weak lead here rather than a strong one: the objects still estimated stand in INTERIOR pedestrian courtyards between Podemos, Pulse and Sankofa, off any vehicle route, so they need Google pedestrian photo-path coverage rather than car coverage; and the section epoch rule already bars Google imagery over Eighth as MID-CONSTRUCTION, so any Street View pass has to be date-stamped after November 2023 before a single figure may be read off it. The two figures that most need it are stairs.S1.riser 0.17 and .tread 0.33, which are today bounded by CBC 1011.5 and proportioned from phf03, not measured.

The p1Paver / p2Paver duplicate hex, DECLARED NOT ACCIDENTAL. colors.p1Paver and colors.p2Paver are the same #cdbdaf and that is the honest answer, not an oversight: p1Paver is a [measured] median of a 400 x 70 px unshaded patch in EYRC phf03, and p2Paver is [estimated] carrying it verbatim because no frame gives the P2 field a clean unshaded median large enough to trust. The two families are the same warm three-tone narrow-modular blend photographed at different unit sizes, so extending the measured hex is the ultra standard third tier used exactly as written — it names the sourced pattern it extends and it is replaced the day a clean P2 patch is sampled. What DOES separate the two families on screen is the tile: 0.534 x 1.8 m against 1.89 x 0.942 m, both derived from their measured units.

THE SAFETY-ORANGE CALISTHENICS RIG — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION, OWNED BY campus-photo-pulsefitness.js. The rig beside the basketball court at the Pulse base is real: SWA -16 shows an orange steel rig with a top bar about 2.4 m above the pad, about 5.0 x 2.0 m overall in 0.09 m OD tube, read against the 1.75 m players at 70 px/m. It was built HERE at [-169.5, 534.5] and independently by eighthsiteworks at a different size 4.9 m away, and round two never arbitrated the collision — two orange rigs 4.9 m apart is worse than either. `pulseFitness` now owns it outright, at one size and one station. This section builds no part of it and carries no figure for it; its `safetyOrange` colour role went with it (see the colour-role entry above).

THE BBQ / GRILL STATION — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION, OWNED BY eighthgathering.bbq.grill. EYRC phf22 and SWA -4 do show a buff-CMU counter with TWO built-in grills, a thin flat canopy and red protective bollards, and this section built it at [-110.0, 557.5] on the measured paving just outside the Sun Lawn's north-east corner — an [estimated] POSITION. eighthgathering builds the same object ANCHORED on the surveyed arcgis.ground#2375 with the counter run measured at 4.6 m off crop_grill.png, plus the bays, splashback, end piers, extinguisher and service enclosure this version never had. The two stood about 30 m apart. Under this section's own rule — an anchored object beats a scattered one — gathering wins, and the claim this section made against the shipped `eighth.areas.bbq` anchor is withdrawn with it. Its `fdcRed` bollard colour went with it.

THE PUBLIC-ART CARRYING WALL AT THE SOCIAL — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION. This section built an 8.5 x 4.0 x 0.4 m board-formed concrete wall at [-75.5, 561.65] as the carrier for the eucalyptus commission, with the artwork itself left undrawn for want of a sampled palette. The commission is eighthgathering's (see the mural entry above), and a carrier for an artwork built 40 m away in another section is an invented wall. It is deleted rather than kept as scenery, and the seat terrace it stood behind is re-solved on its own 9.0 x 2.7 m footprint. If a frame is ever found that shows a board-formed wall at the head of The Social's seat terrace INDEPENDENTLY of the mural, this is the entry to replace.

STAIR S6, THE TEA HOUSE PLINTH STEPS — WITHDRAWN FROM THIS SECTION, OWNED BY eighthgathering.teaHouse.plinth. This section recorded two risers, riser 0.175 m, tread 0.45 m, width 3.2 m from EYRC phf44/phf45 and SWA -23, anchored to the georegistered Tea House plinth — and then the Tea House itself went to eighthgathering in the 2026-08-19 arbitration and took the plinth with it, leaving these four figures in the file with nothing to build and nothing to be anchored to. Gathering builds the object with its own derivation (2 risers counted in SWA -23, riser 0.165 m extending the college's measured 0.155 m court-stair riser, tread 0.45 m extending the measured 0.42 m terrace-stair tread), so no geometry is lost. A second, disagreeing record of a sibling's object is not a measurement this section may keep.
species: Juncus patens (California grey rush) — stiff blue-grey upright clump 0.6-0.9 m x 0.6 m; the dominant swale and bed-edge plant through the Ramble, the Bamboo Garden mulch and the Tea House surround. Species probable, genus confident.
Muhlenbergia rigens (deer grass) — straw fountain tussock 0.9-1.2 m with 1.5 m flower spikes; Ramble slopes, Sun Lawn edge.
Verbena lilacina 'De La Mina' — airy 0.9 x 1.2 m shrub with lilac ball flowers; the purple flowering mass in SWA -5, -6, -2. Species probable.
Agave 'Blue Glow' / Agave attenuata — rosette 0.45-0.9 m; the gravel and cobble zones at the Tea House and the Bamboo Garden.
Westringia fruticosa or Pittosporum tenuifolium 'Golf Ball' — clipped sphere 0.6-0.9 m; the shrub balls in the charcoal planter cubes and at The Social.
Podocarpus macrophyllus or columnar Pittosporum — clipped upright column 2.5-3.0 m x 0.8 m; The Social planters and the basketball-court hedge.
Bambusa multiplex 'Alphonse Karr' — clumping bamboo with golden culms 4-6 m; the Bamboo Garden planters in SWA -13.
Agonis flexuosa, Cercis occidentalis, Arbutus 'Marina', Platanus racemosa, Quercus agrifolia — the tree palette read off phf22, SWA -8 and -12. NOT built: see `absent`.
Lomandra longifolia 'Breeze' or Carex divulsa — fine green tuft 0.6 x 0.6 m at the tower bases. Genus uncertain between the two.
Turf, tall-fescue blend, mown 0.06 m — the Sun Lawn (arcgis.ground#2369) and the Wellness Corridor lawn (arcgis.ground#1160). Blend probable.

eighthgathering.label: Eighth College — the four gathering places: the Meditation Pavilion, the Tea House, the court stair that replaces the 'amphitheatre', and the BBQ / fire-feature terrace.
eighthgathering.epoch: BUILT condition, 2024-2026. The published photographs (EYRC / Lawrence Anderson 2024-25; SWA Group, uploaded 2025-04) and the San Diego Architectural Foundation Open House site plan (2025-03) are the newest epoch and decide what exists. The 2021 Revelle town-hall deck is the DESIGN epoch and loses on existence wherever the two disagree — it is why three amphitheatre tiers shipped that were never built. The 2014 LiDAR is BLIND to this college (campus-lidar.json massHeights has no Eighth entry; campus-massing.js records LiDAR measuring Sankofa at parking-lot height), so no height here is a LiDAR height and the 'the LiDAR is smooth so there is no step' argument is void over Eighth. Google satellite over Eighth is mid-construction and is neither a colour nor an existence source.
eighthgathering.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. What is MEASURED here is the ground: every structure is anchored to a docs/data/campus-eighth.json ground ring copied verbatim into `measured` below, and where a photo estimate and the survey disagreed on a ground extent, the survey won and this file says so at the item. Photographs decide what exists, what it is made of and how it is put together; the survey decides where it stands and how far it may reach. Nothing measured may ever read from this section. Colours are data; the module holds no hex. Deterministic: every scatter is a hash of `seed`.

EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, the Tea House, portrait frontal dusk. The batten glow, the portal reveal, the plinth.
EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, the Ramble / Sun Lawn edge. Both pole-luminaire families, inverted-U bike hoops, white precast planter cubes, the green Adirondack colour.

SWA Group, Meditation Pavilion dusk 3/4. The battered deck face, the gravel margin, the in-grade uplight row, the three LED-lit seat steps with people on them, the ovoid seat pods.

SWA Group, the Tea House at dusk, near-frontal, 2560x1440. THE metric frame for the batten module: FFT/autocorrelation at five scan heights returns 24-26 cycles PER FACE and a direct peak read at x 1150-1230 gives an 11.83 px pitch, which is the 26-per-face module this section ships. CORRECTION 2026-08-19: round one described this frame as giving '68/66/60 peaks' and attributed that count to one face; the cube spans x 1105-1935 with its corner at 1500, so that scan ran across BOTH visible faces and doubled the screen. THE key frame: the 4 m glass-fronted linear fire feature in its precast block wall, nine lime-green Adirondacks, three black pedestal drink tables, teal wire chairs, plank benches, five conical precast planters, the grey grill counter with its red extinguisher post, the wide stair with its stainless handrail, the running-bond unit pavers, the artificial turf inset, and the blue eucalyptus mural.
SWA Group, the same fire feature at dusk, lit. Promotes the firebox from [estimated] to sourced in both states.

SWA Group, overhead oblique of the plaza. SWA Group, clean sunlit eye-level photograph of the whole basketball court. The 7-riser stair south of the court with its stainless pipe handrail on a mid-run standard, the low concrete seat wall beside it, the clipped hedge row on its retaining wall, and NO tiered zigzag anywhere east of the court.

plan2025.what: The 2025 Open House site plan registered to this repo's world frame. Reusable — do not re-derive.
plan2025.scaleDerivation: Colour transect across the surveyed basketball court (plan fill (231,214,188) against apron (237,228,199)): 241.0 px / 22.7 m = 10.617 px/m and 164.5 px / 15.4 m = 10.682 px/m, agreeing to 0.6 %. Adopt 10.65, anchored world (-185.9, 517.5) to plan px (905.5, 922.5).
plan2025.validation: Every ArcGIS Eighth massing ring overlays its drawn building within ~1.5 m across the whole 200 m site — the same order as this project's known 1.25 m Apple georegistration offset. Azad's drawn north facade lands at z 607.5 against the ring's 605.7.

spine.ringSource: docs/data/campus-eighth.json ground['courtyard-328'].points and ground['courtyard-329'].points, copied verbatim (ArcGIS ground rings, decimetres/10).
spine.openingDerivation: The Bamboo Garden's open spine is the gap BETWEEN the two surveyed courtyard rings, solved by sweeping z at 0.05 m and taking the worst case: courtyard-328's east edge never runs east of x -182.3 and courtyard-329's west edge never runs west of x -167.4 over z 584..591.9, so the measured opening is 14.9 x 7.9 m. Outside that z band the two rings close to within 1.5 m of each other and there is no opening at all. THIS RETIRES THE SHIPPED SCALE ARGUMENT: the eighth section's meditation area records the surveyed opening as '~11 x 8 m' and shrinks the pavilion to a 6.6 x 4.6 m slab to fit it. The opening is 14.9 m wide, the 2025 plan's own pavilion marker is 13.0 x 6.2 m and sits inside it, and phf47's photogrammetric 12.6 m and SWA-3's 14.3 m both land in the same place. Three independent reads agree and the shipped one was wrong.

teaHouse.gapDerivation: Sweeping z at 0.1 m across courtyard-1159 finds a lens-shaped gap between two lobes of the surveyed green polygon, 4.6-5.5 m wide and 4.7 m long over z 571.7..576.4, area 20.39 m2, centroid (-85.81, 574). The 2025 plan's Tea House highlight centroid converts to (-85.9, 575.3) — 1.3 m from that gap centroid, INSIDE the plan registration's own ~1.5 m validation residual. Two independent sources therefore put the Tea House in the same 5 m circle, 57 m east and 24 m north of where it currently ships. CLAIM LIMIT, recorded so nobody over-reads it: the gap's 20.39 m2 is within 8 % of this build's 18.9 m2 plinth and its 4.6-5.5 m width brackets the plinth's 4.2-4.5 m, but the gap is lens-shaped and the plinth does not nest inside it — the fit is CORROBORATIVE, not a surveyed footprint.
teaHouse.channelRotDerivation: Least-squares fit of the gap's own centreline: dx/dz = 0.3546 over the lens's 96 points, so rot = atan(0.3546) = 0.3410 rad, shipped 0.34. THIS IS THE DERIVATION OF teaHouse.rotY AND THE GATE ASSERTS THE TWO ARE EQUAL — round one left them as two independent numbers that happened to agree, which is a rotation that can drift away from the channel it was measured in with nothing to say so.
teaHouse.gapAreaDerivation: [derived] 20.39 m2 by the shoelace formula over the 96-point gap polygon above. The gate re-derives it; it exists so the gap cannot be quietly reshaped while the prose still calls it a 20.39 m2 lens.

The 2025 plan's tour marker for the pavilion converts to x -181.5..-168.5, z 584.5..590.7 and sits inside that opening; the marker's own linework is obscured by the tour's black-ring and green-box annotation, so the marker fixes POSITION only and the roof's size comes from the photogrammetry below. roof.form: shallow HIPPED, dark blue-grey standing-seam metal, hip and ridge creases visible from above
roof.pitchNote: [estimated] 10 deg, the middle of the 8-12 deg band the crease geometry in SWA-3 supports. It reads flat from every eye-level frame, which a shallow hip does. No rung resolved the angle numerically; extends nothing but its own sourced hipped form.
roof.seamNote: 0.406 m (16 in) is the standard standing-seam panel width; the same class of named-product dimension as the 1.65 x 0.99 m PV module in the keeling section. The seam COUNT follows from it and the measured plate.
roof.eaveBattenNote: the continuous row of small blocks / rafter-tail battens along the eaves on the roof's upper surface (SWA-3, and in silhouette in phf47). Pitch [estimated] at 0.45 m, read against the 0.406 m seam it sits over.
roof.lengthDerivation: In EYRC phf47 the dark fascia band measures x 182 -> 1689 px (1508 px) at y 555-575 with BOTH tips inside the 1799 px frame. Scale in the drum plane is 95 px/m, from the seated woman (crown y=722 by dark-hair mask over x 1210-1236, deck contact y=803, 81 px / 0.85 m), cross-checked by the in-grade deck uplights reading 15 px = 0.16 m. Solving the horizon from the deck at y=807 (1.00 m below eye) and the soffit at y=608.5 (1.08 m above eye) gives y_h = 711.3 px, which lands on the seated woman's neck — correct for a ~1.6 m eye height. Depth ratio fascia:drums = (711.3-581)/(711.3-608.5) = 1.261, so the fascia sits at 0.793x the drum distance and the width is 1508 x 0.793 / 95 = 12.6 m. THIS CANCELS THE UNKNOWN FOCAL LENGTH AND CAMERA DISTANCE. Corroboration: SWA image 3, using the 37.2 m clear gap between the Pulse ring's z=568.5 and the Azad ring's z=605.7 as a ruler at the pavilion's depth (780 px => 21 px/m), gives 300 px => 14.3 m. 13.5 m is adopted between the two reads and inside the 14.9 m measured opening.
roof.depthDerivation: The 2021 plan's drawn roof rectangle is 135 x 69 px at 600 dpi = 1.96:1, so 13.5/1.96 = 6.9 m; SWA-3's foreshortened vertical read of 140 px is 6.7 m before de-projection. 7.3 m is adopted at the top of that band because the measured opening is 7.9 m deep and the roof must still clear the two surveyed rings, which it does by 0.30 m each side.
roof.fasciaDerivation: 31 px at y 550-581 in phf47, at the fascia's own scale of 95 x 1.261 = 119.8 px/m => 0.26 m.
roof.soffitDerivation: The screen top at y=608.5 (where the drum silhouette meets the lit soffit) to its base at y=798 at x=1150, with a dark shadow gap at 799-800, is 198 px / 95 px/m = 2.08 m. GAP DECLARED: this is one ratio in one frame and 2.08 m is low for a covered space. The range the frame supports is 1.95-2.20 m. No planning document, drawing or archive reached gives a pavilion section; the CEQA/EIR record at ceqanet.lci.ca.gov/2016111019 is the unexplored rung that would close it. ARBITRATED 2026-08-19: reproduced independently from phf47 without this section's own numbers — seated woman 87.5 px (rows 721.3/808.8), drum 194.5 px (rows 605/799.5), deck-row depth ratio 1.1054, so drum/seated = 2.457 = 2.09 m at a 0.85 m cross-legged sitting height. The competing 2.90 m read is refuted.

drums.derivation: phf47 orange-pixel runs at y=660 give x 504->910 (406 px) and x 917->1333 (416 px), tangent at x=913, at 95 px/m: chords of 4.27 m and 4.38 m. A cylinder shows its full diameter, so DRUM DIAMETER 4.3 m. The third lobe is [estimated] at 3.2 m, extending the two measured drums — the 2021 plan draws its left circle noticeably smaller. SOURCE CONFLICT declared and resolved in favour of THREE: phf47 resolves two, but the 2021 plan draws three chained circles and SWA-3 shows three oval oculi; two independent sources, one of them built-condition, say three. The chain spacings here are SOLVED, not read: each centre-to-centre distance is the smallest that keeps the two cylinders from intersecting at the built 0.8 m cross-axis offset, plus 0.06 m — because nothing may intersect.

screen.note: [estimated] panel width ~0.95 m, slot 60-90 mm (0.075 built), thickness 0.10-0.12 m (0.11 built) — read against the panel joints in phf49, which is the definitive assembly frame: floor-to-ceiling curved veneer segments with open vertical slots between them. TENSION RECORDED: phf49 shows 3-4 joints per visible drum face while half a 4.3 m drum is 6.75 m of face, which at 0.95 m panels would show six or seven. The 0.95 m figure is carried as the researcher stated it and is the first thing a drawing should correct. The slots are both the way in and the light source, so they are real geometry, never a texture.
screen.arcNote: Each drum is a run of cylindrical panel segments broken by two kinds of opening, and BOTH are derived, not chosen. (1) WHERE IT MEETS ITS NEIGHBOUR IN THE CHAIN the screen stops over exactly the angle the neighbouring cylinder occults — asin(r_neighbour / centre distance) each side of the bearing to it — because that is the arc over which the two chambers open into one another and a panel there would face its neighbour's wall. (2) FACING THE NORTHERN APPROACH one panel module is taken out with its slots either side: openingNorth = panelWidth + 2 x slot = 1.10 m of omitted face, the smallest opening this screen's own module can make, half of it each side of northBearing. Where the face left BETWEEN two openings is shorter than one panel module (panelWidth + slot) at that drum's own radius, no segment can stand in it and the two openings merge — which is why west ships one arc and mid, which has room everywhere, keeps three. Arcs are world angles, atan2(dz, dx), each written on the branch that makes it increase from its own start. THE ROUND-ONE ARCS WERE BROKEN: mid's third arc was written -2.803 for 3.480 and east's second ended 4.262 for -2.021, each an angle put on the wrong branch, which made those two arcs span 7.065 and 6.669 rad — more than a full circle — so each swallowed its own siblings, 78 pairs of panels were built exactly coincident, 12 of the 46 declared panels were phantoms, and the declared openings did not exist on mid or east at all. The gate now re-derives every arc from the rule above and separately refuses any span >= 2 pi, any overlap between two arcs of one drum, and any arc too short to hold one whole panel.

figures.northBearing: [derived] -pi/2 rad. Angles here are world atan2(dz, dx) and +z is south, so -pi/2 is due north — the bearing of the approach into the Bamboo Garden's open spine. Not a reading: it is the frame's own north.

bench.note: A continuous curved bench cantilevered off the inside face of each drum with NO visible legs, same blond veneer as the screen, square front edge, a continuous LED strip recessed in the shadow gap beneath it, and a short dark blade bracket at the free end. Three independent sources put it beside Sankofa instead: the 2025 built-condition plan's own labelled highlight (centroid (-85.9, 575.3), extent 5.4 x 5.4 m, converted through the 10.65 px/m registration); the 2021 design plan, which prints TEA HOUSE immediately north-west of BLDG 4 (Sankofa), not in the western Ramble; and the built photographs — SWA-23 shows a tall tower directly behind, a lit residential arcade and a clothing-donation bin bank across the way, which is a plaza edge and (-142, 599) is not. cube.ridgeNote: the ridge sits OFF-CENTRE at 0.62 of the width, so one slope is short and steep and the other long and shallow — a symmetric roof loses the object.
cube.sizeDerivation: [measured] EYRC phf44 — the ONLY frame that shows the whole cube unclipped, with two occupants seated inside. Left edge x 746.7, corner x 980, right edge x 1181.7 give projected faces of 233 and 202 px, so kS = sqrt(233^2 + 202^2) = 308.4 px; corner top 365, base 747, so height = 382 px and height/plan = 1.24 — the object is TALLER than it is wide, which no round-one value had. The occupants read ~70 px bench-to-crown; at 0.88 m erect sitting height and ~1.5 m behind the near corner, S = 3.874 D/(D+1.5) and H = 4.805 D/(D+1.5), giving S = 3.26-3.60 m and H = 4.05-4.47 m for any camera distance D = 8-20 m. Shipped at the D = 10 m solution: plan 3.4 m, ridge 4.18 m, eave 3.65 m (phf44's top edge falls 4.07 -> 3.57 m across the cube, a 0.5 m rise). SWA -23 corroborates from the other side (plan/height <= 0.67 with its top clipped at row 0) and is NOT usable for absolute scale, because its single occupant sits on the outboard end of the bench in FRONT of the cube's face plane. This refutes both round-one cubes: 5.3 x 5.0 m is out by 55%, and 3.6 x 2.8 m has the right plan but a ridge 1.4 m too low. THE RIDGE BEARING IS NOT RESOLVED — see absent.

figures.size: [measured] 3.4 m plan side — EYRC phf44, the only frame showing the whole cube unclipped. Projected faces 233 and 202 px give kS = 308.4 px against a 382 px corner height, so height/plan = 1.24; the two seated occupants at ~70 px bench-to-crown fix S = 3.26-3.60 m for any camera distance 8-20 m. Shipped at the D = 10 m solution. See sizeDerivation.
figures.battenedFace: [derived] size - 2 x cornerReveal = 3.4 - 0.30 = 3.10 m. Re-derived by the gate.
figures.cornerReveal: [estimated] 0.15 m of solid corner each side of every face, so the batten screen stops short of the arris rather than wrapping it — which is what phf45 shows at the portal corner. Extends the 0.16 m portal reveal thickness, the same solid member turned round the corner.
figures.eave: [measured] 3.65 m — phf44's top edge falls from 4.07 m to 3.57 m across the cube; eave and ridge are the two ends of that measured fall, scaled by the same occupant-derived scale as `size`.
figures.ridge: [measured] 4.18 m — as `eave`. H = 4.05-4.47 m for any camera distance 8-20 m; shipped at the D = 10 m solution.
figures.ridgeFrac: [estimated] 0.62 — the ridge is off-centre, which both frames agree on, and the 0.53 m rise it carries is measured. WHICH WAY IT RUNS IS NOT RESOLVED (see `absent`): SWA-23 puts the high point at the near corner and phf44 at the west face's left edge. Extends the measured fall itself, placed at the fraction that reproduces it.

battens.derivation: [measured] 26 battens per face at 0.119 m pitch. CORRECTION TO ROUND ONE: the '66 peaks over 801 px' scan of SWA -23 was taken across BOTH visible faces of the cube (which spans x 1105-1935 with the corner at 1500), and 66 was then attributed to one face — doubling the screen. Independent counts: FFT/autocorrelation at five scan heights on each SWA -23 face returns 24-26 cycles; a direct peak read at x 1150-1230 gives 11.83 px pitch (peaks 1152/1163/1175/1187/1199/1211/1223); prominence-filtered peak finding over each full face returns 24 and 26; and phf44's direct profile at x 760-880 gives 8.83 px pitch over a 233 px face = 22-26. Both frames converge on 26 +/- 3 per face, which over the 3.10 m battened face is 0.119 m. The bright bar occupies 55-60% of each period in both frames, so the batten face is 0.070 m and the gap 0.049 m; depth 0.050 m. This retires BOTH round-one screens: 40 at 0.13 across a 5.2 m face, and 66 at 0.050 across a 3.30 m face.
battens.facesNote: Both gable ends, both side walls AND the roof planes are the same batten screen. Roof battens run parallel to the ridge at the same 0.119 m pitch down each slope — the arbitrated pitch, not the round-one 0.050 m, which was a scan across both visible faces of the cube attributed to one.

figures.pitch: [measured] 0.119 m — 26 battens over the 3.10 m battened face. FFT/autocorrelation at five scan heights on each SWA-23 face returns 24-26 cycles, a direct peak read gives 11.83 px, and phf44's profile gives 8.83 px over a 233 px face. See derivation.
figures.face: [measured] 0.070 m — the bright bar occupies 55-60% of each period in both frames, so face = 0.58 x pitch.
figures.depth: [measured] 0.050 m — the batten's projection off the frame, read in the same profiles as the gap between bars.
figures.perFace: [measured] 26 per face, the count both frames converge on at +/- 3. The gate asserts battenedFace / pitch rounds to it and that the module builds 4 x 26.

bench.note: A single L-shaped cast-concrete bench returning along the two closed faces. 80 px at 182 px/m at the occupant's depth.

figures.seatHeight: [measured] 0.44 m — 80 px at 182 px/m at the occupant's depth in SWA-23.
figures.depth: [estimated] 0.55 m. The bench's L-plan and its length are sourced in SWA-23; its depth is read at the occupant's own seat and extends the measured 0.44 m seat height at the usual bench proportion.

glow.note: A warm LED source inside the cavity back-lights the battens so the whole cube glows through the slots at night. That glow is the object's entire identity after dark and a build that omits it fails the frame. Built as an emissive core inside the batten screen, not as a light, and STANDING ON THE BENCH: its foot is exactly the bench top, so it rests on the bench instead of passing through it, and in plan it stops one bench depth short of the batten inner face on every side, so no face of it is ever inside a solid.

figures.core: [derived] the clear cavity the screen encloses above the bench. In plan it is twice (cube.size/2 - battens.depth/2 - bench.depth) = 2 x (1.70 - 0.025 - 0.55) = 2.25 m: the battens' own inner face set back by one bench depth, which is the L-bench's own reach on the two closed sides, applied on all four so that a centred core stays square. In section it is cube.eave - bench.seatHeight = 3.65 - 0.44 = 3.21 m: it starts at the bench top, because below that the bench itself blocks the light, and stops at the eave, because above that the roof planes take over. THIS REPLACES the round-one 2.6 x 1.5 x 2.6 m core, which was carried unchanged through the cube's re-measurement and then intersected BOTH legs of the L-bench by 0.140 m; the gate re-derives both numbers and separately checks in 3D that the core enters neither bench leg.
figures.centreHeight: [derived] bench.seatHeight + core[1]/2 = 0.44 + 1.605 = 2.045 m above the plinth — the centre of the core the figure above derives, standing with its foot exactly on the bench top. The round-one 1.05 m did not reproduce its own stated arithmetic (0.44 + 0.75 = 1.19) and belonged to a core height that no longer exists.

poleLight.note: Luminaire family L1b: the college's secondary pedestrian post-top, slim round pole with a small square top-mounted head on a round concrete base (SWA-23, SWA-14, phf22). ONE pole, and it is the ONLY luminaire this section still builds — everything else on the BBQ terrace went to eighthsiteworks in arbitration. It ships at that section's L1b dimensions rather than this frame's own read, so the same product is one size across the college; eighthsiteworks.systems.l1bPole.items is empty by the arbitration's instruction, so this position is not a duplicate today, and `absent` records what has to happen if that list is ever populated.

rail.note: Guardrail with round pickets on the upper terrace behind the tea house (SWA-23). It stands at the measured gap's east limit, where the cobble bed stops and courtyard-1159's east lobe begins, and runs the length of the bed clipped to the surveyed courtyard. Its section is the college's one guardrail product: specOwner eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail, and every dimension is that spec's, not a fresh read.

The 0.55 x 0.15 m this section shipped is that step rounded.
figures.rail.x: [measured] -82.6, the easternmost extent of the measured gap — the point where the cobble bed stops and courtyard-1159's east lobe, the upper terrace SWA-23 shows the rail standing on, begins. RE-DERIVED: round one put the rail at -83.6 and called that 'the measured boundary'. It is not a boundary at all — the gap's east edge is a curve running from -83.44 to -82.68 and back to -83.59 over the rail's own z-run, so -83.6 stood INSIDE the cobble bed for two thirds of the run and outside it for the rest, which is 22 of 36 pickets buried under this section's own decal and the other 14 on bare ground.

The gate re-derives the crossing from campus-eighth.json.

figures.rail.height: [sourced] 1.067 m (42 in) — the canonical guard height for Eighth, owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail and the exact metric equivalent of the 2022 CBC s1015.3 dimension the product is built to. Four independent photographic reads across this college bracket it (1.06 / 1.066 / 1.067 / 1.07). This rail is the SAME product as every other guard in the college and now ships at the same size; the round-one 1.05 m was that value 'read a little lower at this distance', which is an impression, not a measurement.
figures.rail.picket: [sourced] 0.019 m (3/4 in round tube) — the canonical Eighth picket, owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail and INHERITED here rather than re-read, so the college ships one guardrail product at one size. The spec owner derives it from a scale-free ratio: solid fraction (picket width / pitch) reads 0.18 +/- 0.02 on its own guardrail crops, 0.18 x 0.1016 = 0.0183 m, and 3/4 in is the product step that lands on. Chased through specOwner; this section declares no frame of its own for it and does not cite one. The round-one 0.028 m was this figure 'read heavier at this distance', which is an impression, not a measurement.
figures.rail.pitch: [sourced] 0.1016 m (4 in) — the canonical Eighth picket pitch, owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail and INHERITED here rather than re-read. It is the direct expression of the CBC 2022 s1015.4 102 mm sphere rule, which needs no photograph to establish, and the spec owner measured 0.1046 +/- 0.005 m on its own guardrail crops. Clear opening 0.1016 - 0.019 = 0.0826 m, inside the 102 mm rule. The round-one 0.11 m was this figure 'read wider at this distance'.
figures.rail.topRail: [sourced] 0.048 m (1 1/2 in Sch.40, OD 0.0483 m) — the canonical Eighth top rail, owned by eighthsiteworks.systems.guardrail and INHERITED here rather than re-read; the spec owner measured it at 5.7-8.2 px against 185 px/m on its own guardrail crops. Same tube family as both stairs' 1 1/4 in Sch.40 handrail, one product step up. The round-one 0.045 m was this figure rounded.

courtStair.label: The stair south of the basketball court — the BUILT element that replaces the invented 'amphitheatre' tiers.
courtStair.anchor: measured.courtStair — the 2025 plan rectangle, clipped by arcgis.ground#1760
courtStair.retires: SOURCE CONFLICT, declared and resolved on epoch. The 2021 DESIGN plan draws a zigzag tiered edge east of the basketball court and the eighth section built three amphitheatre-tier items from it (x -161.8..-159.8, z 516..533). The 2025 BUILT plan draws no zigzag and no tier run there — that area is a narrow diagonal hatched edge strip consistent with arcgis.ground#2144 (x -158.9..-156.7, z 514.3..535.0, 16.7 m2), a planting/retaining edge — and SWA-16 photographs the whole court in clean sunlight with nothing tiered east of it. Two epochs; the newer one wins on existence. The tiers are retired (see `supersedes`) and what actually stands south of the court is built instead.

stair.derivation: The 2025 registered plan draws the stair as a band of 5-6 parallel lines over x -178.5..-172.0, z 534..538; SWA-16 resolves SEVEN risers. 4.0 m of run over 7 gives a 0.57 m tread at a 0.155 m riser, a 1.09 m total rise. The west edge is clipped from -178.5 to -177.8 by planting-bed-1760's measured east edge, so the shipped stair is 5.8 m wide, not 6.5.

landing.note: The Pulse massing ring's north face is at z 538.1 and the top nosing is at z 538.0, so a 0.10 m landing lip closes the stair against the building rather than stopping in mid-air.

cheek.note: A raking cheek wall each side, stepping with the treads and standing 0.12 m proud of the nosing line — real stair construction, and it is what keeps the flight from reading as floating slabs.

handrail.note: A stainless pipe handrail on a MID-RUN standard (SWA-16) — two end standards and one intermediate, which is exactly what the photograph shows.

courtStair.epochWarning: THE 'SMOOTH LIDAR SO NO STEPS' ARGUMENT IS VOID HERE. campus-eighth.js and campus-eighth-furniture.js both withhold every stair, terrace, retaining wall and seat wall on it. The 2014 LiDAR over Eighth describes a demolished parking lot; the site is demonstrably terraced (EYRC phf03's full exterior stair with stainless handrails, SWA-7 and SWA-16's stepped seating terraces, SWA-12's retaining walls and ramp, phf47/48's LED-lit stepped seat edges, phf22's ramped walk with picket rail). This is the first of those decisions re-taken on a built source.

bbq.label: The BBQ / fire-feature terrace, on the surveyed courtyard north of Pulse Tower.
bbq.frameNote: Every position below is a LOCAL (u, v) in the measured terrace frame — u along courtyard-2375's own north-east edge, v across it into the courtyard. World = origin + u*(cos r, -sin r) + v*(sin r, cos r) with r = 0.36. Local coordinates are the [estimated] arrangement; the frame they sit in is measured, and every one of them is verified inside the surveyed ring.
bbq.unifiedNote: SOURCE CONFLICT, declared. The shipped eighth section puts the linear fire feature and four Adirondacks at (-112.5, 570.4) on courtyard-2369 and the grill counter at (-132.05, 531.12) on courtyard-2375 — two [estimated] placements 25 m apart. SWA image 14 photographs the fire feature, the Adirondacks, the conical planters, the grill counter AND the red extinguisher post in ONE frame, so they are one terrace. A sourced adjacency beats two independent guesses: the fire-feature population is brought onto courtyard-2375 with the grills, and the grills do not move because their arrangement is the one crop_grill.png shows.

counter.note: Counter run 4.6 m over two bays (crop_grill.png). Depth and height are the 30 in and 36 in product steps, which is what the round-one note meant by 'standard counter height read against the standing figure' — the round 0.75 and 0.92 are replaced by the steps they were rounded from. Built as a body with an overhanging top slab, a splashback on the back edge and an end pier each side, not a single box. Every figure is tiered in `figures`.

extinguisher.note: Red bollard-mounted extinguisher cabinet at the counter's west end (crop_grill.png, and again in SWA-14). Built as a base plate, a post and the cabinet, not one red cylinder.

fire.note: A free-standing masonry wall of large ashlar precast/CMU units with a glass-fronted horizontal firebox set into one face, a stainless frame, and a bed of lava rock / glass media behind the glass. Unlit by day (SWA-14), glowing by night (SWA-18). Course height 0.38 m is the standard 16 in / 0.406 m precast unit read at the wall, and 3 x 0.38 closes the measured 1.15 m wall with a 0.01 m residual the top course absorbs. Scale derivation: the lime-green Adirondack chairs beside it are a named product at 0.94 m back height and read the same as the wall's height minus one course. THE REPO ALREADY DECLARES A fire-feature ITEM TYPE AND SHIPS A SINGLE 2.6 x 0.45 m GLASS BOX WITH NO WALL AROUND IT; this is the terrace's dominant object and it ships as one.
fire.secondNote: At least two exist on the site — one free-standing on the open terrace (SWA-14/18) and one in a covered arcade (SWA-17). Only the free-standing one is modelled; the arcade one is in `absent`.

arrangement.extendsPattern: the photographed adjacency of SWA image 14 and crop_grill.png — which objects stand beside which, and in what order along the terrace — carried onto the measured courtyard-2375 frame, whose origin and bearing ARE surveyed
arrangement.note: EVERY (u, v) AND EVERY rot IN THIS TERRACE IS [estimated]. Nothing registers the furniture to the surveyed ring: the ESRI z20 ortho has the whole terrace in deep afternoon shadow, the 2025 plan draws no furniture, and SWA-14/17/18 offer no landmark that both frames share. What IS sourced is the adjacency — the fire feature with its two arcs of Adirondacks and three drink tables, the grill counter with the extinguisher at its west end, the cafe-table run with its wire chairs, the picnic tables with their sage chairs, the plank benches, the conical-planter row along the back, the canopy, the service enclosure with its mural, and the stair leaving east. The subsystem DIMENSIONS are separately tiered per figure; only the positions are estimated.
arrangement.solve: SEPARATION SOLVE, not a hand arrangement. Every loose object's oriented footprint in this frame is checked pairwise against every other and against the fixed pieces (counter, fire wall, canopy posts, enclosure, stair); any pair whose minimum-overlap axis penetrates by more than `separation` (0.05 m) is a defect and the arrangement is moved along that axis until it is not, preserving the photographed adjacency and the row spacings. The gate re-runs the same SAT check over the shipped numbers, so the solve cannot rot. This replaces the round-one arrangement, in which 26 pairs interpenetrated by up to 0.79 m — a chair inside a planter — while every figure was stamped `measured`.
arrangement.tuckNote: THE ONE DECLARED EXEMPTION, and it is a vertical argument, not a licence. These eight chairs are tucked under their cafe table, which is what SWA-14 shows and what a cafe table is for. Their footprints overlap the table's by 0.099 m and NOTHING of the two objects meets in 3D: the chair's seat tops out at seat + slab = 0.48 m and the table top's underside is at height - 0.05 = 0.68 m, so `tuckClear` = 0.20 m of clear air separates them; and the chair's tall members — the two back legs that run to 0.82 m and the back slats welded to them — stand on the chair's local -v side, which is the side AWAY from the table, because each chair is rotated to face the table it is tucked under. The gate checks all three of those facts for every pair named here rather than taking the exemption on trust. No other pair on this terrace is exempt, and the canopy roof and the mural are excluded from the footprint check because they are overhead and wall-mounted respectively.

figures.separation: [derived] 0.05 m. The gate's own tolerance: any pair of oriented footprints on this terrace whose minimum-overlap axis penetrates by more than this is a defect. It is the drawing tolerance the bark decal's 0.02 m inset is set at, doubled, because two solids need more clearance than a decal edge.
figures.tuckClear: [derived] 0.20 m. Not a chosen figure: it is cafeTables.height - 0.05 (the top slab's underside, 0.68 m) minus wireChairs.seat + 0.03 (the seat slab's top, 0.48 m). The gate recomputes it from those declared figures rather than trusting the number here.

WHITE PRECAST PLANTER CUBES ON THE BBQ TERRACE — WITHDRAWN. THE CHARCOAL PLANTER CUBES IN THE BAMBOO GARDEN — HANDED OVER. This section shipped two 1.2 m cubes fitted into the measured throats where courtyard-328 and courtyard-329 close to ~1.5 m. The cubes are real, but they are the same family eighthcourtyards.bambooGarden.planterCubes counts TWELVE of in SWA -3, at a size measured against people sitting on the rims (1.60 x 1.60 x 0.90 m) rather than fitted to a gap. Two owners on one island is a double count and the two sizes disagree; the throat fit is offered to that owner and nothing is built here.

THE BAMBOO ITSELF, AND ALL OTHER BAMBOO GARDEN PLANTING. This section owns only the Meditation Pavilion and the bark field inside the measured spine opening between courtyard-328 and courtyard-329; the garden island around it (arcgis.ground[3632] hole ring 193, 792.3 m2) is eighthcourtyards.bambooGarden, which ships its raked-gravel floor, its twelve planter cubes and their shrubs and holds itself out of this section's bark rect by name. So the absence of bamboo here is an ownership boundary, not a species judgement — and the species judgement stands too: the clumping bamboo is a MEDIUM-confidence genus read with no species, the same bar that keeps the agave a generic rosette.

A BUILT MEANS OF ACCESS ONTO THE MEDITATION PAVILION DECK. The deck stands 0.45 m above the bark field and this section builds no step onto it. The photographed access is the three LED-lit seat steps of absent[0], which are measured (3 x 0.15 m risers, ~0.60 m tread — exactly the deck height) and which do not fit: the measured spine opening leaves 0.70 m of clear width west of the roof and a run of steps needs 1.80 m. A step invented anywhere else on the perimeter would be a guess about which side people climb, and the 2025 plan's marker does not resolve it. The deck therefore ships as a plinth with a 0.45 m face all round and no access, which is the honest state of the sources; it is the one place in this section where a treated object is knowingly incomplete, and it is recorded here rather than papered over.

THE COLLEGE LUMINAIRE SCHEDULE IS eighthsiteworks', AND THIS SECTION KEEPS EXACTLY ONE POLE. Arbitration 2026-08-19 gave every luminaire on the BBQ terrace to eighthsiteworks and parked family L1b with an empty items[]; the tea house's own pole in SWA-23 is an L1b on a Ramble path and is the one this section still builds, because a photographed pole standing four metres from the object is part of the object's frame and withholding it would leave the tea house lit by nothing. It is built at eighthsiteworks' L1b dimensions (4.30 m, 0.09 m shaft, 0.56 x 0.10 m base) so the same product is one size across the college, and it carries specOwner eighthsiteworks.systems.l1bPole. WHAT IS ABSENT is the placement RULE: no source registers L1b positions to the survey, so this is one surveyed-adjacent read and not a schedule. If eighthsiteworks.systems.l1bPole.items is ever populated, this pole must be handed over in the same edit or the college gets two poles in one place.

eighthgathering.countsNote: What the module must produce, so a silent geometry change cannot pass. The SOURCED counts here are the ones the photographs give: 3 drums and 3 oculi (SWA-3), 3 standing stones (one per chamber), 2 seat pods and 3 slab stones (phf47/SWA-20/21), 26 battens a face x 4 faces = 104 on the tea house (SWA-23 and phf44 re-counted in arbitration: the round-one 66 was a scan across BOTH visible faces), 2 plinth risers, 7 court-stair risers (SWA-16), 2 grill bays (crop_grill.png — and still not three), 9 + 4 Adirondacks, 3 drink tables, 10 wire chairs, 4 cafe tables, 3 plank benches, 5 conical planters (all SWA-14). The rest follow from a sourced module dimension over a measured extent: 22 screen panels at 0.95 m + 0.075 m slot on the three drum arcs the opening rule leaves (the round-one 46 counted 17 phantoms, built by two arcs written on the wrong branch that each spanned more than a full circle and swallowed their own siblings; the gate now re-derives every arc from the rule and refuses an over-full or overlapping one), 66 standing seams at the 0.406 m product width across a 13.5 m plate, 20 in-grade uplights at 1.8 m centres round the deck, 92 eave battens at 0.45 m. The tea house roof battens (30) follow from the corrected 0.119 m pitch over the corrected 3.10 m battened face and the corrected eave 3.65 / ridge 4.18. The shoe blocks are 16, not 20: one block per six battens on four faces is five a face, but a shoe caps a batten base and the corner portal takes the base out of one bundle on each of the two faces it wraps — the four blocks that made 20 stood on the platform IN the doorway, under no batten, with the shoe rail running across the opening beside them. The plate mosaic and its checker infill are GONE: arcgis.ground#2369 is the Sun Lawn and this section paints nothing on it, so there is no `mosaicPlates` count to pin. NO SITE LIGHTING, BIKE HOOPS OR PLANTER CUBES ARE COUNTED HERE: all three families were handed to eighthsiteworks, eighthramble and eighthcourtyards in arbitration 2026-08-19, so poleA/poleB/bollards/bikeHoops/whitePlanterCubes/meditationPlanterCubes are gone from this list and from the module, and the gate asserts the module no longer produces them. SOLIDS AND DRAWS ARE PINNED HERE TOO: 1423 solids in 52 draw calls, so a silent change of geometry fails even where it changes no family count. 1423 is the HONEST figure: with the broken arcs the same module built 1555, of which 132 were exact duplicates standing inside their own siblings, and the gate's old floor of 1500 was a number only those duplicates could reach.

eighthramble.label: The Ramble — Eighth College / Theatre District Living & Learning Neighborhood, the landscape spine
eighthramble.epoch: BUILT CONDITION 2024-2025. SWA Group landscape; HKS design architect with EYRC, Kitchell design-build; construction Jan 2021 - Nov 2023, project complete 2024, photographed 2024-25. The 2020 UC Regents design rendering is a DEAD EPOCH here and nothing is built from it: it draws large pink/orange/purple flowering perennial drifts, mature canopy shade and people sitting on the boulders, and the built photographs show a sparser, younger, more structural rush-and-deergrass matrix with mulch and crushed rock visible between plants and trees at about 0.4 of mature size. Newest epoch wins.
eighthramble.note: INVENTED class, photo-sourced tier. Nothing in this section is a measurement of this campus except the rings under `measured`, which are copied verbatim from the ArcGIS facilities survey. The 2014 LiDAR under this site is a PARKING LOT — it is blind to everything here — so no height, grade or surface below comes from it, and the module never sculpts terrain: everything seats on `surfaceAt` as the drawn ground currently stands. No public planting schedule for this project exists (CEQA 2016111019, both UC Regents packets, plandesignbuild.ucsd.edu, SWA, EYRC and HKS all return nothing), so every species named here is a photograph-morphology read off the 2024-25 built set and is labelled as such. This section is read by nothing measured and is a source for nothing.
eighthramble.confidence: HIGH on the surveyed geometry — the 29 bed rings, the bed-to-bed walk moduli, both bridge footprints and the 1.0668 m (42 in) guard height are computed from campus-arcgis.json and measured against a scaled figure, not estimated. HIGH on the three structural plant masses, the boulder drift language, count band and size distribution. MEDIUM on the accent planting (Baccharis, Dianella, Agave) and on the arroyo braid's stone grading. LOW / UNRESOLVED on: the golden-flowered subshrub's species, the tan-DG vs grey-concrete walk conflict, check-weir dimensions, bed-by-bed species assignment, and any close-range read of the north and south reaches, for which no published photograph exists. The luminaire and bike-rack readings this section used to carry went to eighthsiteworks in the 2026-08-19 arbitration and are no longer claimed here. EVERY SYSTEM WHOSE GEOMETRY IS NOT MEASURED IS NOW LABELLED `estimated` AND NAMES THE PATTERN IT EXTENDS — that retier covers `areaDrains` and `minorFixtures`, whose own colour provenance said the frames resolve them only as a dark rectangle, a grey box and two red verticals.

sources.what: 'a series of stepped basins and bioswales known as The Ramble'; 10 acres, exponential ecology, native and climate-adapted planting, permeable paving.

Near-plan oblique: the braid running the full length of the central reach, the boulder drift as white dots along the swale margin, tan walks against grey plazas, two flush area drains in the invert, the bike-rack run and lamp on the west bridge's landing, three stairs in one frame.

The measurement frame: the crossing figure that sets 0.00688 m/px and gives the 1.066 m guard, the deck edge beam at 0.28 m, the picket band whose FFT closes on 0.108 m pitch, the one photographed check weir under the bridge, Agave in the wash, Verbena in the foreground.

Midday, neutral: three sunlit boulder colour medians, the deergrass spike mass at the right edge, Juncus with rust-orange lateral seed clusters at 1x, the tan stucco wall behind the stair, the 6.1 m lamp against an adult figure.

The definitive boulder-drift frame (14+ legible in one bed, none showing a ground gap or under-shadow), the 8-unit P-loop bike-rack run scaled off a 700c wheel, the mulch shadow line at the walk lip, the grey broom-finished concrete walk that conflicts with SWA -9.
Midday, neutral light: the tan decomposed-granite loop walk west of Sankofa, sampled sunlit and in shade; Juncus masses; Agonis and Platanus at built size.

The Ramble and Sun Lawn at eye level: the full-height elevation of luminaire family A, the funnel-head family B beside it, the planter cubes, a bike-rack run, the ramped walk with a picket guard, the golden-flowered subshrub at 7x.

The Tea House setting at close range: the crushed rock resolved as FLAT-FACED ANGULAR stones, not rounded river cobble; the blue-grey Juncus form beside the green one; Baccharis mounds, Dianella strap-leaf fans and Agave rosettes in the wash; the bark mulch shreds.
The Tea House from the second side; the wash running right up to the board-formed plinth face.

p.2 site plan prints key letter F (THE RAMBLE) in THREE places — a north reach between Pulse and Podemos, the central reach between Sankofa and Azad, and a south reach by the mid-site parking elevator — and supplies the full A-K legend. p.4 is the design rendering this section deliberately does NOT build from.
Team, completion, and the Lawrence Anderson photography credit that dates the built set.
'The Ramble follows historic drainage patterns and links five residential towers'; earth-toned materials referencing La Jolla's coastal cliffs.
2022 California Building Code 1015.4: the 4 in (102 mm) sphere rule, the constraint that closes the picket pitch at 0.108 m given a 0.025 m round tube.

Every ring in `measured` is copied verbatim from ground[] (decimetres / 10). Areas are shoelace, centroids are polygon centroids, and the walk moduli are pairwise polygon-to-polygon minimum distances — all recomputed by tests/campus-photo-eighthramble.test.mjs against this same file.

measured.note: ANCHORED TO THE ARCGIS FACILITIES SURVEY, NOT TO OSM. campus-3d.json's simplified OSM rings for Sankofa, Azad, Pulse and Podemos cover seven of these beds between them; the ArcGIS survey does not — no bed vertex here falls inside any TDLLN massing ring. The Ramble's beds are not drawn objects: they are literal HOLES punched in one campus-wide walk multipolygon (arcgis.ground[3632], 214 rings). That is why the bed-to-bed gaps ARE the paved widths with zero inference, and why the walk strips this section builds are derived from the gaps rather than drawn. Rings are verbatim from campus-arcgis.json (decimetres / 10); areas are shoelace; centroids are polygon centroids.

reaches.note: Three separate reaches, not one corridor — the UC Regents Sept-2020 site plan prints key letter F three times. The central reach is the sourced one: every published close-range photograph of the Ramble is inside it. The north and south reaches have NO close-range photograph in the published set, so their planting extends the central reach's sourced pattern and is labelled [estimated] at the system.
