absent: THE MARKET HALL ROOF'S PITCH - and now ONLY its pitch. Three built frames agree the plate is not flat: phf17 and Learning-1 read a folded plane whose zigzag follows the ring, phf19 reads a sloping standing-seam surface end-on. The RIDGE no longer needs a source - a uniform-slope hipped roof over a given polygon has a straight-skeleton ridge that is fully determined by the polygon, with no free parameter - so the only missing number is the slope itself. Nothing gives it: the plan draws no slope arrow or ratio, no elevation or section is published, and both aerials are obliques with no vertical of known height in the roof's own plane. The plate therefore ships FLAT at the drawn lid, and the day a slope arrow or a section turns up the whole fold follows from the ring.

THE MARKET HALL WING'S TRUE HEIGHT. Still 6.1 m, still 2 x 3.048, still a formula rather than a survey - and still what campus-massing.js extrudes. This section did not resolve it and deliberately did not try to build over it: York's 2026-08-17 audit failure was a skin solved on a taller claim than the drawn box.

THE SOUTH-EAST GLAZED PAVILION as a distinct taller volume. phf19 does show two roof levels at the wing's north-east corner - a lower oversailing canopy and a higher plane behind it carrying a horizontal louvred screen band - so the taller volume is real. Its height was measured as a ratio against the drawn lid and the measurement did not survive re-checking: the band is about ten pixels tall in the original frame and a row-profile through it shows no edge that separates the screen from the wall shadow behind. Nothing is built on a number that failed its own re-check.

THE COURTYARD VOID in the wing's western third. SWA Learning-1 resolves it clearly - a rectangular court cut through the roof deck with a pale coping all round and a SECOND, inner parapet inside it, with a run of about ten small pale openings along its south wall. Both its size and its position would need a ground-plane homography fitted to four identified corners in one oblique frame, which this pass did not have the budget to fit. Named here with the frame and the crop (Learning-1, orig px 215-300 x 541-587) so the next pass starts from a located object rather than from a rumour.

THE MARKET HALL PLAZA'S REFLECTING BASIN. EXISTENCE is now confirmed twice over and in two lightings: EYRC phf17 at dusk shows a rectangular raised basin with a pale coping and a dark water surface standing free in the plaza off the wing's north-east storefront, and SWA Learning-1 shows the same object in daylight with a blue water surface. Neither frame, and no plan, gives its plan dimensions or its position against a surveyed ring. It is not built. This retires survivance.absent[7]'s hand-off to 'the Eighth landscape section' - the section it was handed to is this one, and the answer is still no.

THE LOADING DOCK's dock doors and its walled service court. The 2025 plan resolves the block itself - a heavy-outlined volume at x -201.3..-176.0, z 631.3..~658, which is the north half of massing[462]'s west lobe, so it is already inside the drawn prism and needs nothing built. What is NOT resolved is the open walled court cut into its roof (Learning-1, phf17) or a single dock door on any face. Nothing invented.

THE SOUTH PARKING ENTRANCE's apron, ramp and retaining walls. They exist and the plan draws them, and they are unbuildable: the surveyed ring runs 8.6 m further south than the above-grade wall, so the whole forecourt lies inside the mass campus-massing.js extrudes. See conflicts[0]. Only the portal opening on the drawn face ships.

THE NORTH PARKING ENTRANCE. The plan resolves the throat - a paved entry off Scholars Drive South at about x -203.0..-196.5, z 545.5..556.5, with the tour plan's own arrow marker at (-203.0,547.3) - and that is all it resolves. The apron's material is not sourced in any daylight frame (phf26 is a tungsten dusk exposure and no colour may come from it), and colour sampling off raw Apple Maps pixels is closed by the project's unresolved 1.25 m georegistration offset. An apron in an unsourced colour is worse than no apron.

BOTH PARKING-ELEVATOR PAVILIONS. The mid-site one is PHOTOGRAPHED - EYRC phf17 shows it plainly at dusk, a small square block with a tall parapet and a dark coping, a glazed lift lobby with two doors and a lit interior, a small applied sign panel over the doors and low planting at its base - but it stands in the Market Hall Plaza, which the campus GIS ground layer does not cover, and no plan crop this pass rendered puts a drawn block under it. The north one is discussed in conflicts[1]: the shipped [estimated] position at (-197,526) is contradicted by the 2025 built plan. Neither is built.

THE THEATRE DROP-OFF and the MOBILITY HUB. The registered plan resolves the turnaround well - a large paved loop around a lens-shaped planted island carrying a regular grid of canopies, roughly x -100..-50, z 686..720 - but the island trace runs off the crop box on three sides, the ground under it is the 44,128 m2 campus-wide road ring #4331 rather than anything specific to the drop-off, and the 2014 LiDAR carries canopies over that same ground from the parking lot that stood there. A planted island painted over an unbounded road ring under existing canopies is three guesses stacked. The transit/mobility hub is named in the Regents item and in SWA's text and is resolved by nothing.

SWA'S PUBLISHED OUTDOOR CLASSROOMS. Searched for and not found. 'Outdoor classrooms' appears in the marketing copy for the neighbourhood; it appears on NO plan legend - not the 2025 Open House tour plan, not the 2020 design site plan with its A-K legend, not the Ground Level Plan - and in no photograph as an identifiable object. There is nothing here to model. Reported as a negative rather than filled with a plausible amphitheatre.

THE ONE-MILE WALKING TRAIL. Same result. It is a published statistic (today.ucsd.edu) about the length of the neighbourhood's paths, not a drawn or signed route: no plan draws it, no signage in any frame names it, and the paths it would run on are already the surveyed walk rings. There is no geometry to add.

SANKOFA BASE'S RESTAURANT/RETAIL FRONTAGE AND THE AMAZON HUB. Deliberately NOT duplicated - checked first, as instructed. eighth-sankofa-section.json already carries the one-storey Restaurant/Retail plinth (massing[461]) with the 2025 Open House plan's teal tenancy carried round onto its south-east edge as `base-se-storefront`, and the university's own Sankofa layout PDF closes the Amazon-locker question on the first floor. Nothing here.

THE FOUR SUBTERRANEAN PARKING LEVELS. ~1,165-1,200 cars under three of the towers (Walter P Moore; Revelle town hall deck slide 4). Nothing of them surfaces on this ground except the two portals and the two lift pavilions, and nothing below grade is drawn.

THE BACKYARD'S TERRACES, STEPS AND SEAT WALLS. The 2025 plan carries an 'UP' arrow at about (-167,640) and a short run of parallel lines near (-148,645) that reads as a flight of about five risers, and the courtyard is demonstrably stepped. Neither the tread, the riser, the flight width nor the retained height is measurable at 0.2479 m/px, and the 2014 LiDAR under this ground is VOID here - it is describing a parking lot. Better absent than a stair with an invented riser.
PLANT SPECIES anywhere in this section. The Backyard's bed ships as a bed. No frame resolves a species in it and none is named.

THE MARKET HALL'S INTERIOR and its shopfront doors. The 2020 design deck renders a double-height hall with round exposed columns, a mezzanine and a slatted soffit; that is DESIGN epoch and the built photographs do not corroborate the ceiling. STATION8 has not opened. Nothing inside the envelope is drawn, and no entry door is placed on the frontage the tenancy polygon identifies.

podemos.label: Podemos Hall — TDLLN Building 5, Eighth College, UC San Diego: the 16-storey residential tower (arcgis.massing[253]) and the two-storey academic wing on Ridge Walk (arcgis.massing[252]), with its pleated precast wall and sawtooth parapet screen
podemos.epoch: 2024-25 built photography (EYRC / Lawrence Anderson phf01, phf03, phf15; SWA Group Learning-1, Learning-7) over the 2025-03 SDAF Open House built-condition plan. The UCSD Aug-2020 Project Update and the 2021-04-29 Revelle town-hall deck are DESIGN epoch and lose wherever a built frame disagrees — the rooftop PV they draw is the case in point. The 2014 LiDAR is BLIND here: Eighth College was built 2021-2023 and campus-lidar.json massHeights has no entry for any Eighth mass, so the drawn prism is the university facilities massing ring and its GIS h, and no LiDAR height and no campus-3d OSM h is read anywhere in this section. Every argument of the form 'the 2014 survey is smooth here so there is no step' is void over this site: it describes a demolished parking lot.
podemos.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. Photographs and drawings decide WHAT EXISTS and HOW IT LOOKS; the measured survey keeps deciding WHERE and HOW BIG. Every facade layer hangs off two vertices of the DRAWN massing ring copied verbatim into measured.masses.*.ring (campus-arcgis.json massing, divided by 10 to metres, closing vertex included so the rim-median datum samples exactly as campus-massing.js roofElevation does), and floats at most 2.2 m proud of that face. The measured massing is never moved, carved or replaced. Nothing measured may ever read from this section. Colours labelled [estimated] in colorSources are derived from this building's own sourced colours and are replaced the day a real sample appears.

sources.what: UCSD, Theatre District Living and Learning Neighborhood Project Update, 33 pp. p.10-11 ground-level program plan (the 8,106 GSF lecture hall, 30,397 GSF administrative/College Provost/classrooms, the residential lobby and core at the south-west of the academic wing); p.12 typical housing-level plan (the RESIDENTIAL COMMON SPACES block at the east end of BLDG 5); p.14 NTP Road section, whose BLDG 1 (10 st) = 115 ft and BLDG 2 (9 st) = 105 ft fix the storey at 10 ft-0 in exactly. The live URL 404s; this is the archived copy

UCSD Revelle College town-hall deck. Slide 6 is the DESIGN site plan and labels BLDG 5 (16 STORIES). Slides 4 and 16 are the design-epoch renderings that DRAW a dark-blue photovoltaic array on Podemos's roof — superseded by the built aerials and cited here only as the source of the mistake this section refuses to make
San Diego Architectural Foundation Open House tour map — the BUILT-condition labelled site plan, and the document that names the college's 'Front Porch' entry rooms as a family

EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, Podemos from the north-east at dusk — the full tower over the academic wing. THE frame the 20-cycle count across the 33.50 m north face is made on, and the frame the per-floor slab reveal, the two-storey shingle step, the L2 punched slot windows and the faceted corner storefront are read from. Dusk: geometry only, never a colour source

EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, the 9185 Ridge Walk elevation in sun at high resolution — the primary colour and detail source: the tower's ribbed rainscreen and teal glass, the academic wing's pale architectural-precast pleat with its form-tie grid, the narrow dark metal return panels, the grey modular brick, the bronze storefront, the monumental entry stair with its stainless handrails, folded dark-grey metal cheek, tread inserts and brick seat wall, and the blue applied '9185' numerals

EYRC / Lawrence Anderson drone aerial from the east — the roof source: white membrane, continuous parapet, four penthouse volumes, the duct spine, the RTU row, the flat academic-wing roof behind the sawtooth screen with its painted yellow warning line, and the PV negative. Keeling Apartments' own rooftop PV is visible in the same frame, which is the positive control that makes the negative credible

SWA Group aerial from the east — Podemos at full height. The frame the 14-rung loggia ladder, the loggia opening, the slab-edge depth and the roof composition are measured on at 25.9 px/m, and the second independent frame in which there is no rooftop array

SWA Group project gallery. Frame Learning-7 is the academic base elevation: the sawtooth parapet screen with blue sky visible directly behind the teeth, the warm-tan coping-fascia band read through every notch, the flat metal canopy with its warm-tan soffit, and the grey modular brick whose 0.092 m course height is measured by autocorrelation on it. Frame Learning-12 is the Ramble courtyard, used to disprove the orange-reveal attribution

The facade's published design driver: HKS popped out and ROTATED WINDOWS SIX DEGREES on the lower towers for a 30 percent airflow gain, with fins on the taller sections; serrated facades for natural ventilation; LEED v4 Platinum achieved with an 80 percent predicted energy reduction. Podemos is in the rotated-window family, not the fin family

Structure: concrete shear walls, post-tensioned slabs, columns running full height in three towers, and a four-level subterranean garage — the sourced, entirely invisible substructure this section does not build
Architect of record's project page: 2,000 beds, 1,500,000 sf, complete 2024, photography credit Lawrence Anderson. Design architect HKS, GC Kitchell, landscape SWA

Eighth College's own 'Living at Eighth' pages: Podemos is 16 storeys with academic offices and classrooms on the first two floors — the L1-L2 academic / L3-L16 residential split this section builds to

The Triton, 'Where is Podemos?', October 2023 — 490 beds in 110 units, and Podemos as the first TDLLN building occupied. 490/14 residential floors = 35 beds and 110/14 = 8 units per typical floor, which is the cross-check that closes the facade cycle count

The university facilities massing survey — massing[253] (h 48.8, 16 levels, 12 ring vertices) and massing[252] (h 6.1, 2 levels, 78 ring vertices). The only measurement of position and plan this building has, and the prism campus-massing.js actually extrudes

conflicts: THE ACADEMIC WING'S HEIGHT. arcgis.massing[252].h = 6.1 m, which is exactly 2 x 3.048 m — the LRDP levels x 10 ft formula every Eighth mass wears, not a survey. The BUILT photographs disagree: SWA Learning-7 scaled at 25.9 px/m puts the parapet valley at about 9.5 m and the sawtooth peak at about 10.4 m, and an 8,106 GSF raked lecture hall on L1 independently requires the height. The conflict is about 3.5 m. PROJECT LAW SAYS THE DRAWN PRISM WINS: campus-massing.js extrudes 6.1 m and this section dresses the wall that is actually drawn, filled with 2 bands of 6.1/2 = 3.05 m. The sourced 9.5/10.4 m is recorded here and is NEVER extruded, because dressing to it would float the whole wing 3.4 m over its own drawn parapet — which is exactly how York's membrane came to hover 6 m over its parapet. The 3.4 m is not averaged and not split.

ROOFTOP PHOTOVOLTAICS. The 2021-04-29 Revelle town-hall deck (slides 4 and 16) DRAWS a dark-blue PV array across Podemos's roof. Two independent 2024-25 built drone frames — EYRC phf15 and SWA Learning-1 — show white membrane, parapet, penthouses, ducts and RTUs and no array. The control that makes the negative credible is that Keeling Apartments' rooftop PV is plainly visible in the very same phf15 frame, so the camera demonstrably records PV where PV exists. BUILT WINS: 0 panels, 0 racks, 0 ballast trays, on both roofs. This is the mirror of the Keeling deleted-canopy finding and it is recorded rather than built.

THE 9185 ENTRY STAIR IS CLAIMED BY TWO SECTIONS. eighthcourtyards.levelChange.terraces['academic-forecourt'] + stair S1 builds the SAME EYRC phf03 flight at (x -70.5..-65.5, z 496.5..503.5) on the academic wing's NORTH face, at 15 risers and a 2.55 m rise, and its own source note concedes the position is [estimated] because 'where along a 55 m elevation the address plate sits is not resolved'. This section resolves it: phf03 is a Ridge Walk (EAST) frame — it photographs the blue '9185' numerals, the pale precast pleat of the east run and a recessed glazed door of the kind the survey draws three of on the east elevation and nowhere else. The riser counts also disagree, 20 +/- 2 here against 15 there, off one photograph. This section builds the flight on the east elevation; the sibling entry should be retired by the merge, and until it is, the two must not both ship.

WHICH OF THE THREE EAST DOORS THE STAIR SERVES. The survey draws three identical 1.1 m-deep recesses on the Ridge Walk elevation, at z 518.6-520.3, z 529.0-530.7 and z 539.7-541.5, and no frame says which one phf03 photographs. It is decided by the SURVEY, not by taste: the drawn tower's east common-space bay reaches x -24.3, which is 1.0 m EAST of the academic wing's own east wall, so the wing's east elevation between z 519.9 and z 532 stands inside the tower footprint and is an interior partition. A 9.0 m-wide terrace and its 8.0 m flight fit clear of the drawn tower at the z 539.7-541.5 recess and at neither of the other two. That is the only measured discriminator available and it gives one answer.

THE WINDOW'S PROPORTION. The source gives three readings that cannot all hold: the window is 0.21 of the 1.675 m horizontal cycle (0.352 m wide); its aspect is about 1 : 2.4 (which would make it 0.844 m tall); and its sill is 0.75 m above the floor line with its head 'just under the slab reveal' (which makes it 1.934 m tall on a 3.05 m storey with a 0.366 m reveal band). The horizontal decomposition wins on width because it is the only reading that sums to 1.00 across a counted cycle, and the sill-and-head pair wins on height because it is two independent positions rather than one ratio. The 1 : 2.4 aspect is recorded and not built.

THE WINDOW-REVEAL COLOUR. The shared Eighth recon assigns Podemos 'orange-brown window reveals'. Every Podemos frame resolved — phf01, phf03, phf15, Learning-1 — shows dark grey/bronze frames on a light silver-grey panel with teal-blue glass. The building with orange-brown reveals in SWA Learning-12 is on the Ramble and is a different hall. Podemos's reveals are NOT painted orange here, and the recon's claim stays on the record.

THE BASE'S CLADDING, READ TWICE. EYRC phf01 (dusk) reads the academic wing as uniformly dark grey metal; EYRC phf03 and SWA Learning-7 (daylight) read it as pale architectural precast with narrow dark metal return panels. They are the same pleated system and phf01's darkness is the dusk light, not a second material. The daylight read is built. This is an epoch-free illuminant conflict, and both frames are correct about what they saw.

'SAWTOOTH ROOFLINE' vs SAWTOOTH PARAPET. The shared recon calls the wing's zigzag a folded north-light ROOFLINE. SWA Learning-7 at 7x shows blue sky directly above AND BEHIND the teeth, and EYRC phf15 shows the roof behind them as one smooth flat plane with a painted yellow warning line. It is a pleated PARAPET SCREEN standing in front of a flat roof. The recon's phrasing would have produced a folded roof and the wrong geometry entirely; the screen is what is built.

THE PALE PANEL'S COLOUR, SAMPLED TWICE. EYRC phf03 gives #c1c1c0 on the Ridge Walk run and SWA Learning-7 gives #d1caba on its run — a materially warmer value. Most likely two white balances, possibly two products. The phf03 value is built because phf03 is the frame this section's geometry is measured on and mixing a colour from one frame into geometry from another is how illuminant errors get laundered into fact; the Learning-7 value is carried in colors.precastWarm and is not painted.

THE LECTURE HALL'S SEAT COUNT. UCSD's Aug-2020 update says a 480-seat lecture hall; UCSD Today (2023-09) says a 150-seat lecture hall plus 19 classrooms. Design against built, both university sources. Nothing in this section is built on either figure — the hall is interior — but the 8,106 GSF the 480-seat version carries is one of the two independent reasons the drawn 6.1 m base height is too short, so the conflict is load-bearing for conflicts[0] and stays on the record.

THE EAST BAY'S CURTAIN WALL, 'BESIDE THE LOGGIAS'. The source describes a gridded curtain wall in deep teal-blue glass about 10 m wide 'beside the loggias, on the same bay'. The bay is only 12.10 m wide and the loggia opening is 9.6 m of it, so 'beside' cannot mean alongside. It is read here as BEHIND — the 10 m curtain wall is the loggia's back wall, which is what makes 10 m and 9.6 m the same dimension measured twice. The alternative reading is recorded and not built.

measured.note: Verbatim from docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing, divided by 10 (the file stores decimetres), closing vertex included. h is the GIS h for that mass. Both Podemos masses wear the LRDP levels x 3.048 m formula: 16 x 3.048 = 48.768 rounded to 48.8, and 2 x 3.048 = 6.096 rounded to 6.1. campus-lidar.json massHeights has NO entry for any Eighth mass — the 2014 survey measures this site at parking-lot height — so no LiDAR height is read here, and campus-3d.json carries no OSM height for this building that is extruded either. assembleMasses over the shipped files returns exactly these two rings at exactly these heights.

tower.hNote: 48.8 = 16 x 3.048 m to one decimal — a formula height, not a survey. Uniquely for Eighth, the formula and the photogrammetry AGREE here: the SWA Learning-1 floor pitch measures 79 px / 25.9 px/m = 3.05 m, and the drawn storey is 48.8/16 = 3.05 m. Learning-1 scaled off the surveyed 20.25 m east-end depth gives 47-49 m for the parapet, which brackets 48.8. This building's drawn prism is therefore corroborated rather than merely adopted.
tower.ringNote: A double-loaded slab 20.25 m deep and 66.4 m long that doglegs 20.75 degrees at x -61..-64, with a 12.10 m common-space bay projecting east (6.25 m proud of the north return, 3.05 m proud of the south return) and a triangular prow at the west end carrying a 4.14 m re-entrant notch.

base.hNote: 6.1 = 2 x 3.048 m to one decimal — the same formula, and here it is CONTRADICTED by the built photographs (about 9.5 m to the parapet valley, about 10.4 m to the sawtooth peak) and by an 8,106 GSF raked lecture hall. See conflicts[0]. The drawn prism wins and this section dresses 6.1 m.
base.ringNote: A solid two-storey plate that the tower sits on, not a ring around it: 81.6 percent of the tower's 1272.3 m2 plate stands on it, and 1038 m2 of the plate's 2610 m2 is under the tower, leaving about 1572 m2 of exposed roof. 26 of its 60 real ring segments fall wholly inside the drawn tower and are interior partitions.

envelope.note: Nothing in this section may leave the union bounding box of the two drawn rings expanded by pad metres. The pad has to carry the 9185 entry stair's 8.0 m run east of the east wall, the Front Porch's 6.0 m projection west of the SW wing, and the L1 canopy's 1.2 m eyebrow.

grid.storeyNote: 48.8/16 and 6.1/2 are the same figure, 3.05 m. The drawn prism divides with zero residual on both masses, so no band is stretched to fit.
grid.floorToFloorNote: 10 ft-0 in exactly, from the UCSD Aug-2020 update p.14 section (BLDG 1 10 storeys = 115 ft, BLDG 2 9 storeys = 105 ft, so the one-storey delta is 10 ft). Photogrammetric check on SWA Learning-1: 79 px floor pitch / 25.9 px/m = 3.05 m. Unlike Sankofa, the drawn storey and the sourced storey AGREE here to 2 mm, so there is nothing to withhold.
grid.levelsNote: L1-L2 academic (offices for Thurgood Marshall College, the School of Global Policy and Strategy and the Department of Economics, plus classrooms), L3-L16 residential. 490 beds in 110 units over 14 floors = 35 beds and 7.9 units per typical floor.
grid.cycleSource: COUNTED, not assumed: 20 +/- 2 cycles across the surveyed north face in EYRC phf01, so the module is that face's own chord divided by 20 = 1.675067 m (the dossier rounds the face to 33.50 m; the ring's chord is 33.501343 m and the chord is what is divided). Cross-checked against occupancy — 2 cycles serve one habitable room, giving a 3.35 m room module against the 3.3 m-ish bedroom width the Aug-2020 unit plans show, and 35 beds per floor. Every other face stores its own COUNT and its module is that face's surveyed length divided by that count, so no bay dimension is typed in anywhere.
grid.cyclePartsNote: Fractions of one cycle, measured left-to-right in EYRC phf03 and summing to 1.00 exactly: a wide vertically-ribbed metal panel, a narrow flat panel (the canted return of the pop-out), then the window. In metres on the 1.675 m module: 1.038542 ribbed, 0.284761 flat return, 0.351764 window.
grid.revealNote: A slab-edge reveal at every floor line — a thin dark recessed band with a small projecting drip, terminating at the corners in a small white wedge plate. Measured at 0.11-0.13 of the storey height in EYRC phf01, so 0.12 x 3.05 = 0.366 m deep, projecting 0.06 m.
grid.shingleNote: The wall plane steps in and out every TWO storeys: in phf01 the near silhouette carries a step at 290 px intervals against a 145 px floor pitch. Step depth measures about 0.02 of the storey, so 0.02 x 3.05 = 0.061 m, with the band above oversailing the band below.

facadeSystem.rotationSource: gbdmagazine 2025, quoting HKS: 'by popping out and rotating windows six degrees on the lower towers, they could enhance airflow by 30%'. 6 degrees = 0.10472 rad. It is a PUBLISHED figure, not a guess, and it is the one architectural idea that governs every face of this building. The sense alternates bay to bay so consecutive units form a shallow zigzag.

ribbed.source: EYRC phf03 (2024-25) — fine vertical corrugation, 10-11 ribs across the panel; the COUNT is sourced and the rib width is that count divided into the sourced 1.038542 m panel

flat.source: EYRC phf03 (2024-25) — the smooth unribbed panel that is the canted return of the pop-out box; 0.17 of the cycle

popOut.extendsPattern: Podemos's own sourced cycle decomposition: the 'narrow flat panel' of 0.17 of the cycle IS the return cheek of the projecting box seen in elevation, so the box's projection is that same 0.284761 m. The DEPTH is therefore derived from a sourced width rather than measured
popOut.source: EYRC phf01 and phf03 (2024-25) — every window unit is a shallow projecting box canted out of the wall plane, one cheek in light and one in hard shadow

window.source: EYRC phf03 (2024-25). Width 0.21 of the sourced 1.675 m cycle. Height from two sourced positions: sill 0.75 m above the floor line, head just under the 0.366 m slab reveal on a 3.05 m storey. Subdivided into a wide fixed pane plus a narrow operable leaf on one side — the natural-ventilation sash gbdmagazine documents. See conflicts[4] for the 1:2.4 aspect that is recorded and not built

slabReveal.source: EYRC phf01 (2024-25) at the near silhouette

cornerBay.source: EYRC phf01 (2024-25) for the north-east corner and SWA Learning-1 (2024-25) for the south-east: at both corners the field gives way to a full-height glazed bay in teal/blue-green vision and spandrel glass about 2 cycles wide, carrying one small square punched window per floor and a thin projecting plate at each floor

pier.source: SWA Learning-1 and EYRC phf15 (2024-25) — the four returns and cheeks of the east bay are the same field in FLAT (unribbed) panel and read as solid piers framing the loggia stack

loggia.countSource: One per residential floor. eighth.ucsd.edu puts academic offices and classrooms on the first two floors and the Revelle deck labels the building 16 STORIES, so L3-L16 is 14 floors — and in SWA Learning-1 the projecting slab edges read as a ladder of 14 rungs. Two independent closes.
loggia.source: SWA Learning-1 (2024-25) measured at 25.9 px/m — opening about 9.6 m wide x 2.5 m clear, depth about 2.2 m, slab edge 0.28 m and painted white; EYRC phf15 (2024-25) from above; UCSD Aug-2020 p.12 for the RESIDENTIAL COMMON SPACES block that this bay is
loggia.balustradeNote: [estimated] height — Learning-1 resolves a glass balustrade set back behind the slab edge but not its height; 1.067 m is the CBC 1015.2 / 42 in guard minimum these edges are built to, stated as the basis rather than measured.
loggia.note: An open recessed loggia at every one of the 14 residential floors of the 12.10 m east bay: a white slab edge across the full bay width, a glass balustrade set back behind it, an open ceiling to the slab above, a side cheek wall, and the gridded deep-teal curtain wall as its back (see conflicts[10]).

brick.source: SWA Learning-7 (2024-25) — course height 0.092 m by autocorrelation at 22 image px per course, which is the 3-5/8 in of the US modular brick family; EYRC phf03 for the same brick at the seat wall. The 0.194 m unit LENGTH is [estimated]: it is the 7-5/8 in nominal face of that same family, a 2.1:1 face, and it is the one figure no frame in the set resolves. The seat wall is the cross-check on the course: its sourced 0.46 m height is exactly 5 x 0.092 m.
brick.spandrelNote: NOT a second measurement and NOT a chosen number: the brick that remains above the sourced 2.7 m head line on the drawn 3.05 m storey. 3.05 - 2.70 = 0.35 m. This is the 'spandrel wall' half of the dossier's 'grey modular brick piers and spandrel walls'; the PIERS are withheld (see absent) because no frame resolves how wide they are or which bays they take.

storefront.source: EYRC phf03 and SWA Learning-7 (2024-25) — full-height glazed storefront in dark-grey/bronze aluminium, mullions at about 0.9 m, doors with full-height vertical pull handles, some vision panels frosted
storefront.headNote: The storefront is FULL-HEIGHT glazed to the shared L1 head line at academic.l1.head (2.7 m) — it does not sit on a brick band and it is not a ribbon. The brick above that line is the spandrel; see academic.l1.brick.spandrelNote.

colonnade.source: EYRC phf01 (2024-25) — a colonnade of square pale cast-in-place concrete columns about 0.60 x 0.60 m standing free of the glass and carrying the projecting L2 box, at about 6 m spacing, on the east and north runs, with recessed downlights in the L2 soffit
colonnade.recessNote: [estimated] setback: the glass line is pulled back far enough for the column to stand free of it and still leave the same covered walk the canopy gives elsewhere, so recess = the sourced 1.2 m canopy projection + the sourced 0.60 m column face = 1.8 m. Derived from two sourced dimensions, not chosen.
colonnade.columnLineNote: How the setback is BUILT, given that the drawn prism is solid and cannot be notched: the column occupies the band from the sourced 1.2 m canopy projection to the derived 1.8 m setback, standing PROUD of the drawn face — the same technique campus-photo-keeling.js uses for its undercroft columns. That leaves 1.2 m of covered walk between the glass line and the column face, which IS the covered walk the canopy gives elsewhere, i.e. exactly what recessNote derives. Pushing the glazing 1.8 m the other way would bury the whole ground floor inside the drawn massing prism.

canopy.source: SWA Learning-7 (2024-25) — a thin flat metal canopy/eyebrow over the storefront where there is no colonnade: fascia about 0.35 m deep, projection about 1.2 m, warm-tan soffit and a pale greige fascia edge

plantingBed.source: SWA Learning-7 (2024-25) — a narrow planting bed about 0.8 m wide on dark bark mulch, with a flush concrete kerb, at the foot of the glazing
plantingBed.runsNote: Sourced on a CANOPY run: SWA Learning-7 is the flat-metal-eyebrow elevation. EYRC phf01's colonnade runs read as a paved covered walk between the columns and the glass and resolve no bed, so the bed is built on the canopy runs and WITHHELD on the colonnade runs and under the Front Porch rather than carried across (see absent).

l1.headSource: SWA Learning-7 (2024-25) — the ONE measured datum of this storey, and it is read twice in the same sentence of the dossier: the grey modular brick wall band stands '2.7 m high before the glazing head', and the full-height glazed storefront's head is that same line. Earlier drafts of this section carried it as brick.bandHeight AND as storefront.head and then STACKED them, which left a 0.35 m 'full-height' storefront ribbon on 260 bays. There is one head line at 2.7 m; everything on L1 is measured from it.
l1.headNote: Corroborated on the drawn prism: the sourced canopy fascia is 0.35 m deep and hangs from the L2 line down, and 3.05 - 2.70 = 0.35 m. Two independently sourced figures — a head height read on the wall and a fascia depth read on the blade — close exactly on the drawn storey. That closure is why the head is built at the sourced 2.7 and not re-keyed.

l2.panelModuleNote: Half the sourced sawtooth pitch: two panels per tooth, 1.22/2 = 0.61 m. The panel COUNT per tooth is sourced from SWA Learning-7; the module is the sourced pitch divided by it.
l2.ratioNote: pale precast face : dark metal return = 2.1 : 1, measured in EYRC phf03. On the 0.61 m module that is 0.413226 m of pale precast and 0.196774 m of dark metal return.
l2.foldNote: Panels are alternately advanced and set back so a thin vertical shadow edge reads at every second joint — the same 6-degree folding logic as the tower, in panel. The offset is the module turned through the published 6 degrees: 0.61 x sin(0.10472) = 0.063763 m, which is the 'few centimetres' the frames show.

formTies.source: EYRC phf03 (2024-25) — the form-tie dots are visible in a regular grid, roughly 4 across a panel and 5 up a storey, which is what identifies the pale panels as architectural PRECAST and not stucco

slotWindow.source: EYRC phf01 (2024-25) — narrow vertical punched openings in the L2 pleated wall on the north/north-east run, aspect about 1 : 3.5, one per 2 teeth, dark-framed. Width is the sourced 0.413226 m pale precast face (the opening takes one pale panel); height is that width x the sourced 3.5 aspect

l2.runsWithSlotsNote: phf01 resolves the slot windows on the north/north-east run only. They are built on the east and north runs and withheld everywhere else — see absent.

copingBand.source: SWA Learning-7 (2024-25) — behind the teeth, set back about 0.3 m, a continuous warm-tan/bronze coping-fascia band about 0.20 m deep runs at CONSTANT height and is visible through every notch

sawtooth.heightDerivation: The RATIOS are the solid part of this measurement and they are preserved exactly. Sourced: tooth pitch = 0.249 x (height from the L1 canopy top to the tooth peak); notch amplitude = 0.70 x pitch; two panels per tooth. Sourced absolute: pitch 1.22 +/- 0.20 m. On the DRAWN prism the L1 canopy top is the L1/L2 line at 3.05 m, so the peak is 3.05 + 1.22/0.249 = 7.949598 m above the base datum, the valley is that less 0.70 x 1.22 = 0.854 m, and the screen therefore stands 0.995598 m from the drawn 6.1 m lid to the valley and 1.849598 m to the peak. Re-derived the other way as a check: peak 7.949598 less the 3.05 m canopy top is 4.899598 m, and 1.22 / 4.899598 = 0.249 exactly. No figure in this block is a round number that was chosen.
sawtooth.source: SWA Learning-7 (2024-25), crop at 7x: each tooth is a vertical rise on its left edge then a straight rake falling to the right into the next tooth's rise, about 35 degrees from horizontal. Blue sky reads directly above AND BEHIND the teeth, which is what proves this is a parapet SCREEN in front of a flat roof and not a folded roof — see conflicts[7]
sawtooth.note: The single most distinctive parapet in Eighth College and the reason this building had to be built. It follows the drawn ring exactly, on the exposed runs only.

roof.membraneNote: Flat, one smooth plane behind the sawtooth screen, with a painted yellow warning line set in from the edge. Read directly off EYRC phf15. No plant, no PV, no terrace — nothing else on it is resolved by any frame.

warningLine.source: EYRC phf15 (2024-25) resolves a painted yellow line and nothing else on this roof. The 1.83 m inset is the 6 ft of OSHA 1926.502(f)(2) that a warning line is set to, stated as the basis of the estimate rather than measured, exactly as the parapet heights elsewhere in this project are stated against CBC 1015.2

pv.note: ABSENT on the academic wing too, from the same EYRC phf15 frame that resolves the warning line. 0 panels, 0 racks, 0 ballast trays.

frame.note: The wing roof's (u, v) frame: u metres along the tangent of ring edge P57->P58 from P57, v metres inward on that face's inward normal. P57->P58 is the LONGEST segment of the drawn wing ring at 39.602 m (next longest 20.30 m), which is the only property of it that matters and the only one that cannot rot — the builder reads this index and the test re-derives it as the argmax over the ring, so a re-derived ring cannot silently rotate the whole roofscape.

parapet.source: SWA Learning-1 and EYRC phf15 (2024-25) — a continuous parapet with a light metal coping standing 1.0-1.2 m above the membrane, following the plan exactly including the dogleg and the east bay
parapet.note: [estimated] height, derived two ways that agree: 60 px in an OBLIQUE gives 0.98 m and an oblique is a lower bound, and 1.10 m is the 42 in guard height these roofs are built to (CBC 1015.2). 1.10 m is adopted; nothing in the frames contradicts it.

roof.membraneNote: Flat light TPO/PVC single-ply, near-white where sunlit, with a distinctly BLUE-GREY secondary field of walk pads and ballasted zones down the middle of the roof. The pale/dark contrast is the roof's dominant pattern at long range in both aerials.

frame.note: The roof's own (u, v) frame: u metres along the tangent of ring edge P8->P9 (the 33.50 m north face) from P8, v metres inward on that face's inward normal. In this frame the drawn plate spans u -6.25 to 60.13 (the 66.4 m length, with the east common-space bay reaching 6.25 m PROUD of the north return, which is the same 6.25 m the ring reading gives) and v 0 to 29.32.

walkway.extendsPattern: Podemos's own sourced roof: the blue-grey field is sourced as the roof's dominant secondary pattern in EYRC phf15 and SWA Learning-1, and it is laid here as the walk-pad and ballast run those frames read as. Its width and inset are RATIOS measured in those crops against the surveyed 20.25 m slab depth — the run reads 0.079 of the depth across and stands 0.059 of it in from the edge — and the metres are those ratios times the survey, not numbers chosen in metres. 0.079 x 20.25 = 1.59975 m and 0.059 x 20.25 = 1.19475 m.
walkway.note: Laid in 1 m strips and clipped to the drawn ring, with cross-legs to each penthouse. crossLegs are the four penthouse u values, verbatim.
walkway.stripNote: `strip` is the 1 m laying increment the run is tessellated and clipped in, a mesh resolution and not a measurement. Nothing is claimed by it.

penthouses.source: EYRC phf15 and SWA Learning-1 (2024-25) — the first of two LARGE volumes, near the dogleg, clad in the same light metal panel with a flat roof and a coping. Height MEASURED at 190 px = 3.10 m in the phf15 crop; footprint about 12 x 8 m
EYRC phf15 and SWA Learning-1 (2024-25) — the second large volume, over the east core. Same family, at the upper end of the measured 3.1-3.4 m band

penthouses.extendsPattern: the two sourced mechanical penthouses of this same roof — same light metal panel, same flat top and coping; only the 5 x 4 x 2.8 m is a ratio in the phf15 crop rather than a measurement
the two sourced mechanical penthouses of this same roof
penthouses.source: EYRC phf15 (2024-25) — the bulkhead with a louvred face and a personnel door

roof.equipmentSource: EYRC phf15 and SWA Learning-1 (2024-25) are the only frames that resolve individual units. Counted: a run of exposed ductwork along the roof's SPINE — round spiral duct about 0.6 m diameter with one large radiused elbow, plus rectangular plenum sections — and a row of about six packaged RTUs/condensers, each roughly 2 x 1.2 x 1.0 m, on rails on the EAST half, and a slim vertical mast near the centre.
roof.equipmentNote: [estimated] positions and sizes. Every dimension is a ratio to the SOURCED 3.10 m penthouse height and the surveyed 20.25 m slab depth in the same frame; the 3.10 m is the only absolute vertical this roof has. Positions are stated as u fractions of the 66.38 m frame span: the two large penthouses at 0.19 and 0.55, the bulkheads at 0.35 and 0.75, the mast at 0.50, the RTU row starting at the east end. Everything sits on the membrane field, never on a walk pad.

curbs.note: Scattered small curbs, vents and roof-drain pairs, counted only approximately in phf15, so they ship as a SEEDED SCATTER over the roof rectangle — and every candidate whose footprint corners are not all inside the drawn ring is dropped.

clips.why: North of the east common-space bay there is no roof deck — the bay projects 6.25 m east of the north return and the plate steps back. Nothing may stand in this rectangle and no walk pad may cross it, because nothing may hover.
South of the east bay, the same step: the bay is 3.05 m proud of the south return, so this rectangle is open air.

pv.note: ABSENT, and the absence IS the finding. The 2021-04-29 Revelle town-hall deck (slides 4 and 16) DRAWS a dark-blue photovoltaic array across this roof. Two independent 2024-25 built drone frames, EYRC phf15 and SWA Learning-1, show membrane, parapet, penthouses, ducts and RTUs and no array. The control that makes the negative credible: Keeling Apartments' rooftop PV is plainly visible in the SAME phf15 frame, so the camera and the resolution demonstrably record PV where PV exists. 0 panels, 0 racks, 0 ballast trays.

recesses.note: The southernmost of the three surveyed door recesses on the Ridge Walk elevation, entered on a 45-degree splay. Its 9.0 m stair footprint stands inside the drawn tower's east common-space bay, so it does not carry the flight.
The middle recess. Its 9.0 m stair footprint also stands inside the drawn tower's east bay; the whole run of the wing's east wall from z 521.4 to z 532 is an interior partition.

The northernmost recess, at z 539.7-541.5. The ONLY one of the three whose 9.0 m terrace and 8.0 m flight fit clear of the drawn tower — which is why the flight is built here. The rule is re-evaluated against the two rings at build time, so it cannot rot.

podemos.recessesNote: Three identical 1.1 m-deep by 1.7-1.8 m-wide recesses, each entered on a 45-degree splay, at z 518.6-520.3, z 529.0-530.7 and z 539.7-541.5. Copied from the ring by index, never by coordinate. EYRC phf03 photographs one of them — the recessed glazed door under the '9185' numerals — and does not say which.

terrace.depthNote: [estimated] — the sourced 1.80 m colonnade recess (the covered walk under the L2 box) plus the 1.525 m / 60 in clear landing CBC 11B-404.2.4 requires at the head of an accessible route. Both terms are stated; neither is chosen.

handrail.freeStandingNote: Sourced in EYRC phf03: 'three free-standing runs plus one wall-mounted run' across the four handrail lines. It is BUILT as that — the outermost lane, the one that lands against the stair cheek and the seat wall, is carried on brackets off the cheek and the other three stand on stanchions through the tread.

door.widthNote: DERIVED: two leaves at this building's own sourced 0.9 m storefront mullion module, 2 x 0.9 = 1.8 m. Not a chosen figure.
door.heightNote: [estimated]: no frame resolves the leaf height. 2.4 m is stated as the 8 ft-0 head an exterior storefront door takes, which leaves a 0.3 m transom under the sourced 2.7 m head line — the basis is stated rather than measured, exactly as the CBC figures elsewhere in this section are.

entryStair.riseDerivation: The SOURCED count is 20 +/- 2 risers with a 0.40 m tread and a 0.155 m riser, giving 3.1 +/- 0.4 m — the weakest figure in the dossier, bounded by CBC 1011.5.2 (max 178 mm riser, min 279 mm tread). The DRAWN prism gives an independent value for the same quantity: the terrace serves a door at the wing's L1/L2 line, which is one drawn storey, 3.05 m. The two agree to 1.6 percent. The riser height is therefore NOT typed in: it is the drawn 3.05 m divided by the sourced count of 20 = 0.1525 m, which sits inside the sourced 0.155 m +/- and inside the code maximum. The stair is the one place on this building where the drawn prism and the photogrammetry corroborate each other.
entryStair.source: EYRC phf03 (2024-25), a sunlit high-resolution frame of the whole flight: a broad straight cast-in-place flight in warm buff concrete about 9 m wide spanning four handrail lines; a continuous 15 mm recessed shadow line at the head of every riser; satin stainless round tube handrails 38 mm OD at 0.914 m / 36 in above the nosing with 180-degree returns, on round stanchions with circular base plates; small dark rectangular tread inserts about 0.18 x 0.06 m set flush near the riser, two per tread, staggered left and right; a solid triangular stair cheek clad in dark-grey flat metal panel with a flat capped top about 0.25 m wide; a grey brick seat wall about 0.46 m high x 0.45 m deep and 4 m long with a flush dark metal cap, with students sitting on it; and the blue applied '9185' numerals about 0.36 m cap height on the pale precast to the right of the stair head
entryStair.note: THIS IS THE ITEM THE SHIPPED campus-eighth.js EXPLICITLY WITHHELD on the argument that 'the 2014 LiDAR is smooth so there is no step'. That argument is void over Eighth — the 2014 survey is a parking lot — and phf03 is a sunlit high-resolution photograph of a full monumental exterior stair. It is built. See conflicts[2] and conflicts[3] for the sibling collision and the position derivation.

supersedes.reason: One EYRC phf03 flight, claimed twice, 40 m apart. The sibling builds it on the wing's NORTH face at 15 risers / 2.55 m and its own source note concedes the position is [estimated] because 'where along a 55 m elevation the address plate sits is not resolved'. This section resolves it on the EAST (Ridge Walk) elevation from the survey: exactly one of the three drawn door recesses can carry a 9.0 m terrace and an 8.0 m flight clear of the drawn tower, and phf03 photographs the pale precast pleat and the blue 9185 numerals of the east run. THE MERGE MUST RETIRE THE SIBLING'S TWO ITEMS AND RECORD THEM IN eighthcourtyards.absent NAMING podemos AS THE RESOLVER. Until it does, the two must not both ship. This section owns only its own three files and cannot make that edit.

frontPorch.extendsPattern: the college's own sourced FRONT PORCH family and this building's own sourced L1 colonnade. The 2025-03 SDAF Open House built-condition plan names 'Front Porch' as an entry room at the college's residential halls, and three of the four are already built from that plan by their own sections. Podemos's is carried across the gap here, at THIS building's sourced column dimensions: it is one sourced colonnade bay deep (the 6.0 m column spacing) and the surveyed 7.60 m of the SW wing's outer flank wide, with 2 columns at the sourced 0.60 m square and the sourced 6.0 m spacing. Nothing about it is scaled off a drawing, because no drawing of it was resolved.
frontPorch.source: UCSD TDLLN Project Update Aug-2020 p.11 ground-level plan places Podemos's residential lobby and core at the SOUTH-WEST of the academic wing, which is the flank this porch stands on; the 2025-03 SDAF plan names the Front Porch type. No photograph in the set resolves this face — see absent.
frontPorch.note: A covered entry room built OUTWARD off the drawn SW flank, not notched into it: the drawn prism is solid and cannot be notched. Its floor is the plaza paver on the overlay ladder, seated on surfaceAt; its soffit is the L2 box carried on two square concrete columns. The run it covers loses its L1 canopy eyebrow and its planting bed — a porch roof and a canopy eyebrow over one door is two eyebrows, and a planting bed under a covered floor is a bed under a floor.
frontPorch.clearHeightNote: DERIVED, not chosen: the porch's clear height is this building's own sourced L1 head line (academic.l1.head = 2.70 m), so the porch roof lands on the same line as the storefront head and the canopy fascia rather than on a height of its own.
frontPorch.soffitNote: DERIVED, not chosen: the same 0.35 m spandrel band the sourced canopy fascia occupies (academic.l1.canopy.fascia) and the same band the brick spandrel occupies — the drawn storey less the sourced head, 3.05 - 2.70. The porch roof is therefore 0.35 m deep and its top lands exactly on the L2 line. Earlier it sat a whole band higher and swallowed the bottom course of L2's form-tie grid.

signage.measured: EYRC phf03: blue applied sans-serif numerals, cap height about 0.36 m, on the pale precast panel to the right of the stair head, about 4.2 m above the terrace.
signage.note: Recorded, NOT rendered — the same standard the shipped argo, blake and sankofa sections hold: lettering needs a text mechanism this repo does not have and inventing one is not detail. There is a second reason here: 4.2 m above a terrace that sits at the drawn 3.05 m line puts the numerals at 7.25 m, ABOVE the drawn 6.1 m lid. That is conflicts[0] showing up as geometry, and it is another reason not to place them.

panelRibbed.source: EYRC phf03 — median of a sunlit facet of the tower's ribbed rainscreen panel

panelBody.source: derived from the sourced panelRibbed by removing the direct-sun lift at a constant 0.88 factor; extends this building's own sourced panel

panelFlat.source: the narrow flat canted return catches light at a different angle from the ribbed field in every frame; the RELATIONSHIP is sourced in phf03 and the hex extends this building's own sourced panelRibbed lifted

windowGlass.source: EYRC phf03 — deep teal-blue vision glass, median over a shaded pane

glassSky.source: derived from the sourced windowGlass by mixing it half-and-half toward a pale sky grey, so the field carries the two-tone reflectance a glazed elevation actually shows; extends this building's own sourced glass

curtainTeal.source: the east bay's gridded curtain wall reads DEEPER than the punched vision glass in SWA Learning-1; the relationship is sourced and the hex extends this building's own sourced windowGlass darkened

cornerGlassTeal.source: the corner bays read teal/BLUE-GREEN against the punched glass's blue in EYRC phf01; the relationship is sourced and the hex extends this building's own sourced windowGlass shifted green at constant luma

metalReturnDark.source: EYRC phf03 — shaded facets of the pleat, the dark metal return panel

metalReturnDeep.source: EYRC phf03 — the same element deeper in shade; with metalReturnDark it brackets the material

precastPale.source: EYRC phf03 — the sunlit pale architectural-precast panel on the Ridge Walk run. See conflicts[8]: SWA Learning-7 gives a materially warmer value on its own run and that value is carried in precastWarm rather than averaged in

precastWarm.source: SWA Learning-7 — the same material on a different run under a different white balance. RECORDED AND NOT PAINTED, so that the conflict stays visible instead of being laundered into an average

canopySoffit.source: SWA Learning-7 — the canopy underside, and the same warm tan as the coping-fascia band read through the sawtooth notches

canopyFascia.source: SWA Learning-7 — the canopy's fascia edge and the parapet coping band

brickSunlit.source: EYRC phf03 — 75th percentile of the seat wall's sunlit face (the median includes mortar shadow)

brickBody.source: SWA Learning-7 — brick with mortar, the mid tone of the wall as a whole

storefrontMullion.source: SWA Learning-7 — the dark storefront mullion, shaded; a dark neutral in daylight

addressNavy.source: EYRC phf03 — the applied '9185' numerals. Recorded only; the numerals are not rendered

plazaPaver.source: EYRC phf03 — the lower Ridge Walk plaza's warm-sand linear pavers

terraceConcrete.source: EYRC phf03 — the broom-finished concrete terrace at the stair head

walkPaverGrey.source: SWA Learning-7 — the adjacent grey walk pavers

roofMembrane.source: SWA Learning-1 gives near-white at the 75th percentile in golden-hour light. The sample was checked for a warm cast before use and is already neutral (red minus blue = 0), so no cast had to be removed and the value is carried — but it is labelled [estimated] because a golden-hour aerial is not a colour source this project trusts

roofFieldBlue.source: the blue-grey secondary field down the middle of the roof is the dominant pattern in both aerials; the RELATIONSHIP is sourced and the hex extends this building's own roofMembrane cooled and darkened

loggiaSlabWhite.source: the loggia slab edges read as continuous WHITE bands in SWA Learning-1; the relationship is sourced and the hex extends this building's own sourced precastPale lifted

loggiaSoffit.source: the shaded slab soffit and recess behind each loggia; extends this building's own sourced precastPale in shade

concreteColumn.source: the colonnade's pale cast-in-place columns read a shade warmer than the precast in phf01; no crop resolves them to a clean median, so the hex extends this building's own sourced precastPale warmed

railStainless.source: satin stainless round tube is sourced present in EYRC phf03 at 38 mm OD with 180-degree returns, but no crop resolves a 38 mm tube to a clean median; the hex extends this building's own sourced precastPale cooled toward a neutral metal

treadInsertDark.source: the small dark flush tread plates in phf03; too small to sample, so the hex extends this building's own sourced metalReturnDeep darkened

mulchBark.source: dark bark mulch in the 0.8 m bed at the foot of the glazing in SWA Learning-7; the material is sourced and the hex is derived from this building's own sourced brickBody darkened

mechanicalGrey.source: RTU, plenum and penthouse casings; no crop resolves one to a clean median, so the hex extends this building's own roofMembrane darkened

louvreDark.source: the louvred face of the east stair bulkhead in phf15; extends this building's own sourced metalReturnDark darkened

ductGalv.source: the exposed round spiral duct along the roof spine in phf15; extends this building's own railStainless darkened toward galvanised steel

warningYellow.source: the painted warning line is sourced present in EYRC phf15 but the frame is a small oblique and no median can be taken; the tone is derived as the safety yellow such a line is painted to, dulled to the weathered value a membrane roof reads at, and it is replaced the day a square-on frame appears

podemos.sliversNote: Ring segments of massing[252] shorter than 0.30 m — 18 of its 78 — including six of ZERO length from repeated vertices in the survey. They are surveyed noise, not faces: they carry no facade entry, nothing is built on them, and the list is stored so the count can be re-checked against the file rather than trusted.
absent: ROOFTOP PHOTOVOLTAICS, on BOTH Podemos roofs — 0 panels, 0 racks, 0 ballast trays. The 2021-04-29 Revelle town-hall deck (slides 4 and 16) draws a dark-blue array across this roof; the built aerials EYRC phf15 and SWA Learning-1 (2024-25) show membrane, parapet, penthouses, ducts and RTUs and no array, with Keeling Apartments' own roof PV plainly visible in the same phf15 frame as the positive control that proves the camera could record PV if PV were there. The design-epoch rendering is superseded and nothing is built.

The '9185' NUMERALS. Cap height (0.36 m) and position (4.2 m above the terrace, on the pale precast right of the stair head) are measured in EYRC phf03 and recorded in `signage`, and the navy is sampled in `colors.addressNavy`. Not rendered: lettering needs a text mechanism this repo does not have. There is a second, geometric reason — 4.2 m above a terrace at the drawn 3.05 m line is 7.25 m, which is above the drawn 6.1 m lid.

A 'PODEMOS' WORDMARK. The shared Eighth recon states there is one on the base. No frame resolved in this pass contains it — only the '9185' numerals and a small dark plaque or louvre on the brick, about 0.9 x 0.25 m in phf01. Letterforms are not invented, so nothing is built and the recon's claim stays on the record.

THE ACADEMIC WING'S REAL HEIGHT. About 9.5 m to the parapet valley and about 10.4 m to the sawtooth peak, measured on SWA Learning-7 at 25.9 px/m and independently required by an 8,106 GSF raked lecture hall, against the drawn ArcGIS 6.1 m formula prism. Anchored to the drawn box per project law; the sourced figure is recorded in conflicts[0] and nothing is built on it. The consequence is visible: the whole L1+L2 band is compressed by 3.4 m and the address numerals no longer fit on the wall.

THE WEST PROW's three faces — 27.3 m of tower facade at edges P10-P11, P11-P0 and P0-P1. No photograph in the set reaches this end. They ship as the sourced north-face field at the sourced module, labelled [estimated] and naming the pattern they extend, and the surveyed 4.14 m re-entrant notch ships as a blank shadow slot rather than as invented window bays.

THE TOWER'S LONG SOUTH AND SSE FACES at better than aerial resolution. EYRC phf15 and SWA Learning-1 resolve the field and positively resolve the ABSENCE of loggias, balconies and shading devices, which is what makes them sourced; no eye-level frame of Podemos from the south or the courtyard side was found, so the cycle counts on those faces are the north face's counted module scaled to their surveyed lengths.

THE ACADEMIC WING'S SOUTH FACE (20.3 m at z 552), ITS SW WING, ITS WEST FACE (12.6 m at x -79) AND ITS 39.6 m NORTH FACE (z 500) at elevation resolution. The SWA Learning-7 elevation is probably the west face or the north face and could not be registered to either. All four runs ship as the sourced Ridge Walk system carried across, labelled [estimated] and naming it.

THE FACADE CYCLE PITCH. 20 +/- 2 cycles across the surveyed 33.50 m north face, from a perspective count in a dusk frame, not from a drawing — so 1.675 m carries a +/- 0.17 m band. It is the weakest number in this section's geometry and a single square-on elevation would replace it.

THE ENTRY STAIR'S RISER COUNT AND TRUE RISE. Sourced at 20 +/- 2 risers and 3.1 +/- 0.4 m, which the source itself flags as its weakest figure, and read as 15 risers / 2.55 m by a sibling section off the same photograph (conflicts[2]). Re-keyed here to the drawn prism's own storey rather than typed in; the disagreement is unresolved.

THE SAWTOOTH PITCH IN ABSOLUTE METRES. 1.22 +/- 0.20 m. The RATIOS are solid and are preserved exactly — pitch : band height = 0.249, amplitude : pitch = 0.70, two panels per tooth — so a later re-keying of the absolute leaves the composition intact.

EVERY ENTRY EXCEPT 9185. The UCSD Aug-2020 ground plan shows a residential lobby and core at the south-west of the academic wing and a second core mid-block, and the survey draws three identical door recesses on the Ridge Walk elevation, but no photograph resolves those doors' width, height, leaf count or canopy. Only the one recess phf03 photographs is given a door; the other two surveyed recesses are built as recesses with no leaf.

THE FRONT PORCH's furniture and its edge. Three sibling halls' porches are built from a Regents rendering that shows a round fire-pit table, paired sofas, side tables and a low wall between the porch and the Ramble. That rendering was not resolved for Podemos in this pass, so the porch here is the covered room only — floor, columns and soffit — and nothing is furnished.

ROOF DRAINAGE — scuppers, overflows and the roof-access hatch on the tower. Not resolved in any frame. A single hatch is built on the sourced dogleg penthouse because the frame shows one there; nothing else is claimed.

THE ACADEMIC WING'S L2 SLOT WINDOWS on every run except the east and the north. EYRC phf01 resolves them on the north/north-east run only. Extending punched openings onto four unphotographed elevations would be a claim about where rooms are, so those runs ship as blank pleated wall.

EVERY INTERIOR. The 8,106 GSF lecture hall (480 seats designed, re-published as 150 seats plus 19 classrooms), 30,397 GSF of administrative and College Provost space, offices for Thurgood Marshall College, the School of Global Policy and Strategy and the Department of Economics, and 110 residential units. Sourced as programme, with no geometry.
THE FOUR-LEVEL SUBTERRANEAN PARKING GARAGE beneath the site (Walter P Moore). Sourced and entirely invisible; nothing is built and nothing is implied at grade.

THE LOWER RIDGE WALK PLAZA's paving. EYRC phf03 resolves warm-sand linear pavers in running bond at the foot of the flight and the hex is sampled and recorded, but the ground of Eighth College belongs to the landscape sections and painting a second decal on the same surveyed polygons is how two sections come to z-fight. Only the RAISED terrace at the stair head, which is 3.05 m off the ground and cannot z-fight anything, is built here.

THE OPERABLE VENTILATION LEAF'S OPEN STATE. gbdmagazine documents the natural-ventilation sash and phf03 resolves the narrow leaf beside the fixed pane, but no frame shows one open. The leaf ships as a mullion division in a fixed window, never as an operable sash.
TREES AND PLANTING beyond the building's own sourced 0.8 m bed at the foot of the glazing. The measured LiDAR canopies already stand on this site and the Eighth landscape sections own the ground.

THE PALE PANEL'S WARMER SAMPLE. SWA Learning-7's #d1caba against EYRC phf03's #c1c1c0 for what is described as the same architectural precast. Carried in colors.precastWarm, provenanced, and deliberately NOT painted or averaged — see conflicts[8].

THE CORNER GLAZED BAYS' EXACT WIDTH. Sourced as 'about 2 cycles' at the north-east and south-east corners in phf01 and Learning-1; built at exactly 2 of this building's own counted cycles because a count is the only honest way to express 'about 2 cycles', and the +/- is the cycle's own +/- 0.17 m.

THE CEQA / EIR RECORD, ceqanet 2016111019. Unmined in this pass and still the likeliest public source for a surveyed height in feet, a parapet elevation and per-building floor areas. It would close conflicts[0] outright, which is the largest open question on this building.

EVERYTHING OUTSIDE PODEMOS. Sankofa, Survivance and the Market Hall, Azad, Pulse, the Ramble, the courtyards, the basketball court and all of the college's ground surfacing belong to other sections and are deliberately untouched here.

THE FACETED NORTH-EAST ENTRY. EYRC phf01 resolves that at the north-east entry the L1 storefront is faceted in plan and wraps the corner, each pane canted a few degrees from the next. It is NOT built: the drawn ArcGIS ring has no faceted vertices anywhere on that corner, so building the facets would mean inventing plan geometry the survey does not draw, and no frame or plan resolves WHICH bay of that run the entry occupies. The observation stays on the record here and the storefront ships flat on the drawn face. Replaced the day a plan resolves the entry bay.

THE BRICK PIERS' WIDTH AND SPACING. SWA Learning-7 reads the L1 grey modular brick as 'piers AND spandrel walls' in running bond, but no frame resolves how wide a pier is or which bays take one. The SPANDREL is built — it is the 0.35 m band the sourced 2.7 m head line leaves under the drawn 3.05 m storey — and the piers are withheld rather than invented at a chosen width, which would be a claim about where the doors are. The measured 0.092 m course and the brick's own colours stay on the record and are drawn on the spandrel and the seat wall.

THE PLANTING BED UNDER THE COLONNADE RUNS. The 0.8 m bed on bark mulch with its flush kerb is sourced in SWA Learning-7, which is a CANOPY elevation. EYRC phf01's colonnade runs read as a paved covered walk between the columns and the glass and resolve no bed. It is built on the canopy runs and withheld on the colonnade runs and under the Front Porch.

THE HANDRAIL STANCHIONS' BASE PLATES. EYRC phf03 resolves circular base plates bolted to the treads under the free-standing stanchions, but no crop resolves a plate diameter. The stanchions ship without them rather than at an invented plate size; the three-free-standing / one-wall-mounted split the same frame resolves IS built.
podemos.colorsRecordedNotPaintedNote: Sampled, provenanced and NOT drawn by anything, each for a stated reason: precastWarm is the second sample of the same precast under a second white balance and averaging it away would launder conflicts[8]; addressNavy is the '9185' ink and the numerals are not rendered; walkPaverGrey is the adjacent grey walk paving, and the ground of Eighth College belongs to the landscape sections (absent). Every other key in `colors` is drawn. The test asserts both directions, so a colour cannot quietly become unused and an unused colour cannot quietly stay undeclared.

pulse.label: Pulse Hall (BLDG 1), Theatre District Living & Learning Neighborhood / Eighth College, UC San Diego — ONE 18.5 m deep double-loaded dog-legged bar drawn as TWO survey masses: arcgis.massing[463] 'TDLLN - Pulse Tower' (10 storeys) north of the party line and arcgis.massing[487] 'TDLLN - Pulse Mid' (9 storeys) south of it. Not two buildings, no slot between them. HKS design architect / design-build lead with EYRC Architects; Kitchell GC; SWA Group landscape; Walter P Moore structure; occupied Fall 2023.
pulse.epoch: 2024-25 built photography (EYRC / Lawrence Anderson; SWA Group) over the current-epoch UCSD facilities survey; Apple Maps 3D captured 2026-08-06 for plan geometry. THE 2014 LiDAR IS BLIND TO THIS BUILDING — campus-lidar.json massHeights has no entry for either Pulse key and campus-massing.js:16 records LiDAR measuring the Eighth site at parking-lot height, so no height here comes from LiDAR or from campus-3d's OSM h. The drawn TERRAIN under this building is the same dead epoch: a 2014 read of a parking lot that no longer exists, which is why the ground-storey datum here is the DRAWN PRISM BASE and not the drawn surface, and why the sourced 0.91 m level change between the court and the colonnade cannot be reproduced (see `absent`). The 2021 design renderings (Revelle town-hall deck) are a DEAD epoch wherever they disagree with the built photographs — most importantly on rooftop PV. Google satellite over Eighth is mid-construction and is never a colour or existence source.
pulse.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail under the README's second declared invented class. Photographs decide what exists and how it looks; the facilities survey ring and its h decide scale and position. Nothing measured reads from this section. Every ring coordinate below is the shipped arcgis ring divided by 10, copied verbatim by the generator that wrote this file. EVERY DRAWN DIMENSION IN THIS SECTION IS EITHER DERIVED (`derivations.figures`, with its own arithmetic over `derivations.readings`), READ off a named frame (`reads`, with its tolerance), or LABELLED `[estimated]` (`estimates`, naming the sourced pattern it extends). A number that is in none of those three blocks is a defect and tests/campus-photo-pulse.test.mjs fails on it by name.
pulse.confidence: HIGH on the massing, the one-bar reading, the three shared edges and the storey grid (survey rings plus three independent images of the one-storey roof step). HIGH on the north elevation's materials, colours, window size, gold picture frame and the 6-degree rotated window box (one certainly-identified high-resolution built photograph plus HKS's own published statement). HIGH on the PV negative (a built drone frame carrying Keeling's PV as an in-frame control). MEDIUM on the 4.43 m bay (two agreeing methods, one perspective-free, but it supersedes campus-eighth.json's shipped 3.5 m). MEDIUM on the rooftop terrace extent. LOW on the mechanical screen well footprints and positions, on the west-end loggias and on the street address — all withheld or flagged. THE GROUND STOREY'S RELATION TO THE GROUND IS AN OPEN EPOCH CONFLICT, not a confidence level: the sourced flight of about six risers between the court and the colonnade needs a 0.91 m level change that the 2014 terrain does not have, so the flight is solved against the drawn surface and the remainder is in `absent`.

Every guard, picket-spacing and handrail figure in this section is solved on these rules rather than eyeballed off a photograph — a code dimension is the strongest source a photograph of a compliant building can have
