derivations.why: THE KEELING BAR. Keeling's PV block states a real product dimension and its own arithmetic for every figure it draws. This block does the same for Pulse: `readings` are the raw citations (pixel counts, published feet, code rules, stock product sizes) and `figures` is every drawn metre value with the expression that produces it. tests/campus-photo-pulse.test.mjs recomputes every one of these independently from `readings` and fails if the section's own value drifts from its own derivation — so a fabricated figure cannot pass by being self-consistent.

units.note: Exact by definition. Every product and code figure below is a whole number of inches or feet and converts here.

px.source: SWA …Learning-16.webp at original resolution, all inside one image region at one depth (x 1400-1900, y 100-330) so perspective cancels; the ratios below are between two lengths in that region and are converted to metres by the SOURCED 3.048 m storey or by the ring-measured bay, never by a pixel-per-metre constant

published.source: storeyFeet: arcgis h / levels resolves to 3.048 m on both masses, i.e. a real 10 ft floor-to-floor. screenTopFeet: UCSD TDLLN Project Update August 2020 p.14. rotationDeg: HKS via gbdmagazine.

code.source: IBC 2021 §1015.2 guard 42 in; §1015.4 a 4-inch sphere may not pass a required guard's opening; §1014.2 handrails 34-38 in above the nosings, 36 in taken as the midpoint of the permitted band; §1011.5.2 riser and tread limits — a 6 in / 12 in exterior flight satisfies 2R+G = 24 in and is the broad proportion SWA-16 photographs

product.source: Stock sizes, the Keeling `panel [1.65, 0.99]` class: nominal 8 in unit masonry; a rainscreen cavity plus panel at 2 in per face; TPO walkway pad in 36 in rolls at 3/16 in; formed sheet-metal coping with a 3 in face and a 1 in drip; a 4 in vent through roof at the plumbing code's 6 in minimum projection; 24 in x 24 in x 2 in pedestal pavers; 24 in of soil for a small multi-stem tree; 1-1/4 in square picket stock; 1-1/2 in nominal Sch 40 pipe (1.9 in OD) for guards and handrails; the 6 in side clearance a split-system condenser is listed for

ring.source: The 48.7 m is the length of BOTH 48.7 m faces straight off the survey rings (T10 and M1); the 11 is a COUNT of window columns across that measured length in Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png, which is perspective-free. towerStripDepth is the survey ring's own north-strip depth. Nothing here is a photogrammetric scale.

grid.bayModule.why: The one metre scale this facade is built on. A COUNT across a MEASURED face, so it carries no perspective and no pixel-per-metre constant.

system.panel.width.why: Vertical rainscreen joint spacing, 28 px against a 125 px storey.

system.chimney.width.why: The accent chimney is a whole number of panels wide; the panel is derived and the count is the estimate.

system.window.width.why: The opening is 100 px in a 180 px bay, and the bay is the ring-measured 4.4273 m. THE RESEARCH DOSSIER'S 2.40 m DOES NOT REPRODUCE FROM ITS OWN RATIO — 100/180 of any bay this building has is 2.43-2.50 m, and 2.40 needs a 4.32 m bay that no source gives. The arithmetic wins and the discrepancy is recorded, exactly as it was for the fieldPanel colour.

system.window.height.why: 0.80 storey. Converted on the SOURCED 3.048 m storey, not the drawn 3.05/3.0444: the photograph measures the real building, and the drawn storey governs only where plates stack inside the drawn box.

system.window.sill.why: The residual of the storey after the opening and one head reveal. The head reveal is taken as one picture-frame face — the smallest detail dimension this facade actually has — which is the [estimated] half of this figure and is recorded in `estimates` as well.

system.window.projection.why: HKS's published six degrees against this section's derived opening width: the leading jamb stands proud by w sin 6 deg and the trailing jamb is flush.

system.window.transomFrac.why: 'a horizontal transom at roughly two-thirds height' — the source's own fraction, not a decimal someone chose.

system.frame.face.why: 6 px of frame against the 100 px opening.

system.frame.proud.why: A formed-metal trim of square section: the return equals the face. SWA-16 resolves the face and the fact that the frame projects, not the depth of the return.

system.stepWall.thickness.why: The step wall is the same exterior wall assembly as the parapet it caps.

lantern.rowsTower.why: One row of common-room windows per floor, ground storey included — the lantern is a stacked common room, not a residential field.

lantern.columnPitch.why: '2 columns fill roughly half of a bay' (phf15) — so the column pitch is a quarter bay.

lantern.opening.0.why: Adjacent frames in the grid share one frame face, so each opening takes the pitch less one face. Reproduces the dossier's read of ~0.9 m to 7 mm.

lantern.opening.1.why: The dossier calls them SQUARE openings and separately reads ~0.9 x 1.0; square is the stated form and the width is the derived one, so the height follows it. The 1.0 read is inside the frame's own 0.2 m face and is not separately claimed.

lantern.frameProud.why: Same square-section trim rule as the window picture frame: the return equals the face.

lantern.sill.why: One building, one sill datum. Replaces an invented 0.35 storey fraction.

groundStorey.clearHeight.why: 105 px of clear under the colonnade soffit against a 125 px storey in the same region — 0.84 storey. This is what proves L1 is NOT a taller plinth.

groundStorey.colonnade.pierProud.why: The pier's front face is flush with the facade plane above and its back face is the line the glazing sets behind, so its centre stands half its own depth off the wall. Nothing about the recess depth is invented — it IS the pier.

groundStorey.colonnade.oversail.why: Same reasoning: the facade oversails by exactly the depth of the pier that carries it.

groundStorey.colonnade.soffitFasciaTower.why: The soffit's visible edge is the storey MINUS the measured clear — solved per mass on that mass's own DRAWN storey so the band closes exactly onto the field wall. This retires the old declared-but-unbuilt 0.15 m 'slab zone', which left a 0.15 m strip of raw massing prism showing.

groundStorey.breezeway.width.why: One bay — the smallest opening that still reads as a through-route, and the only width the structural grid allows without removing a pier.

groundStorey.stair.width.why: 'A broad flight' is as broad as the bay it climbs to: the clear between two pier faces.

groundStorey.stair.going.why: 6 in / 12 in: 2R + G = 24 in, the comfortable exterior proportion, and both inside IBC 1011.5.2. Replaces an assumed 0.15 / 0.30.

groundStorey.stair.flightHeight.why: THE SOURCED LEVEL CHANGE between the court and the colonnade. The drawn 2014 terrain does not have it — see `absent` — so the flight ships as the risers the drawn surface actually supports and this figure stays on the record as what the photograph shows.

groundStorey.stair.handrails.why: One per side. IBC 2021 §1014.9 requires handrails on BOTH sides of a stairway, and this flight's derived 3.82 m width is far past the point where a single rail would serve — so the count is the code's, not a look.

groundStorey.northTerrace.deckDepth.why: The raised walking level under the oversail, which is the 'raised terrace' whose edge SWA-16 photographs a guard on. It is exactly as deep as the oversail because that is the only depth any source gives it.

groundStorey.northTerrace.picketPitch.why: The clear opening between pickets is the largest the code allows (a 4-inch sphere may not pass), so the pitch is that clear plus one picket. Replaces an invented 0.12 m that drove 698 instances.

groundStorey.envelope.why: How far outside the two drawn rings anything in this section's GROUND group may stand. Gated, so a later edit cannot push the porch into the Bamboo Garden.

roof.parapet.height.why: The 42-inch guard the occupied Mid deck legally needs; corroborated by silhouette (the parapet reads ~0.35 storey in phf15). The dossier's 1.07 m is this number rounded.

roof.parapet.thickness.why: The wall assembly continued above the roof: 8 in of structure with a 2 in rainscreen cavity and panel on each face = 12 in.

roof.walkPad.width.why: The dossier reads the pad as '~1.0 m wide'; the product step is 24/30/36 in and 36 in = 0.9144 m is the one inside that read.

roof.walkPad.inset.why: 'Just inside the north parapet' — so the pad's outer edge abuts the parapet's inner face and its centre is half a width in from it. The smallest claim the words allow.

roof.walkPad.segment.why: The pad is laid as square segments so it can be CLIPPED to the drawn ring and stopped at the plant instead of pushed through it as one long box.

roof.screenWells.height.why: The published 115 ft top-of-screen over the DRAWN 30.5 m deck. The dossier's 3.50 m is the same figure measured above the parapet against a 30.48 m nominal deck; both readings are on the record.

roof.screenWells.wallThickness.why: A screen enclosure is lighter than the building wall: 6 in of structure plus the same 2 in rainscreen each face.

roof.condensers.pitch.why: Unit width plus the listed 6 in side clearance. The row's own x station falls out of this and the gap between the wells — it is not a placed literal.

roof.bulkhead.height.why: 'One storey (3.0 m) tall' in phf15 — so it is the drawn storey, not a 3 m literal.

roof.vents.height.why: The plumbing code's minimum projection above the roof — the smallest claim consistent with 'small circular vents' in a drone frame.

roof.vents.edgeClear.why: A vent clears the parapet's inner face by its own radius and no more. There is no half-metre working margin: that was an invented number, and it is what made `clips.rule` quote 1.2 m while the field said 1.0.

terrace.xEast.why: The deck's east limit is its sourced 0.41 fraction of the MEASURED Mid south face, measured from that face's west end — so `uFrac` and `length` drive the geometry instead of sitting beside it as dead data.

terrace.paver.why: The checkerboard counts ~10 modules across the 6.1 m sourced depth = 0.61 m, and the pedestal-paver product step at that size is 24 in = 0.6096 m.

terrace.paverRotationDeg.why: 'A diagonal-reading grid'. Diagonal IS 45 degrees to the deck's own edges; this is the source's word made numeric, not a chosen angle.

terrace.edgeClear.why: A paver corner may reach the parapet's inner face and no further.

terrace.planterSize.1.why: The planter's HEIGHT is the soil depth a small multi-stem tree needs — 24 in — not a look. Its 1.5 m plan size is a read and is in `reads`.

estimates.why: The ultra standard's third tier. Each entry is a figure no rung of the ladder resolved, labelled `[estimated]`, recording the sourced pattern of this same building that it extends, and replaced the day a real source turns up.

system.chimney.panelsWide.extends: system.panel.width and SWA-16's read of chimneys '4-6 panels wide'
system.chimney.panelsWide.why: [estimated] the midpoint of the sourced 4-6 range. The panel it counts is derived; only the count is estimated.

system.chimney.jogBays.extends: SWA-16's read that the chimneys 'jog floor to floor'
system.chimney.jogBays.why: [estimated] at most one bay of jog per storey, deterministic from the section seed — the photographed stagger without a claim about its pattern.

system.chimney.chimneysPerBaysDivisor.extends: SWA-16's read of a staggered two-tone field rather than a grid
system.chimney.chimneysPerBaysDivisor.why: [estimated] one accent chimney per three bays. No frame in the set counts the chimneys across a whole elevation; one in three is the density that reproduces the staggered read at the 48.7 m face's own bay count without claiming a pattern.

system.window.headReveal.why: [estimated] the split of the storey's derived 0.6096 m residual between sill and head. Only the residual is derived; no frame stations the opening inside its storey. The head is taken as one picture-frame face, the smallest detail dimension this facade has.

system.commonRoom.glazingWidth.why: [estimated] one panel module wider on each side than the sourced window — the smallest widening the rainscreen grid allows. The 2020 typical-floor plan puts a Residential Common Space at the inner bend and does not dimension it.

groundStorey.colonnade.pierSize.extends: the sourced 'pale cream coursed unit masonry' pier in SWA-16 and the nominal 8 in unit
groundStorey.colonnade.pierSize.why: [estimated] three nominal 8-inch units square. The material and the visible bond are sourced; the count of units is not. Two units (0.41 m) is too slender to carry a ten-storey oversail and four (0.81 m) reads heavier than the frame. NOTE for the next agent: the superseded value here was 0.62, byte-identical to keeling.systemB.ground.columnSize — a borrowed number, now replaced by this building's own material.

groundStorey.breezeway.uFrac.extends: the 2020 GROUND LEVEL plan, which draws the through-breezeway but does not station it
groundStorey.breezeway.uFrac.why: [estimated] at mid-length of the west bar.

groundStorey.porch.depth.why: [estimated] five panel modules — the same five-panel count the sourced accent chimney uses. Neither the 2020 plan nor the 2025 SDAF plan dimensions the porch band, so the one dimension this section cannot source at least reproduces a module the building demonstrably has.

groundStorey.entrance.leaves.extends: the sourced full-height glazed storefront between the colonnade piers
groundStorey.entrance.leaves.why: [estimated] a pair of leaves. SWA-16 resolves the glazed frontage and the broad flight that climbs to it; no frame resolves the door itself. See `absent` for every OTHER opening on this building, which stays unbuilt.

groundStorey.entrance.leafWidth.why: [estimated] one panel/mullion module per leaf — 0.68 m, which is also a real leaf width. The storefront's own module is the only division this facade gives.

groundStorey.entrance.height.why: [estimated] the leaves run the full glazed height inside the storefront's own perimeter frame (clear less one frame face top and bottom), which avoids inventing a head height.

roof.vents.pitch.extends: the dossier's read of '~6-7 m centres' in r1c1-plan-00-south
roof.vents.pitch.why: [estimated] the midpoint of a read range.

roof.bulkhead.x.extends: phf15's read that the bulkhead stands at the roof's north-east in the east wing
roof.bulkhead.x.why: [estimated] station. The frame places it in the wing, not on a coordinate.

terrace.treeSpread.why: [estimated] the crown reads about the planter's own width in r1c1-plan-00-south, which is the only scale that frame gives it.

terrace.treeHeight.why: [estimated] one and a half times the crown spread — the habit of a small multi-stem container tree. No frame resolves the height: r1c1 is a near-plan and phf15 is too far.

terrace.treeTrunkFrac.why: [estimated] three fifths of the height is clear trunk below the crown — the habit of a small multi-stem. No frame resolves it.

terrace.treeCrownStems.extends: the sourced read 'a single small MULTI-STEM tree' in r1c1-plan-00-south
terrace.treeCrownStems.why: [estimated] three stems. 'Multi-stem' is sourced; the count is not. Everything else about the crown falls out of it: each stem's crown is a third of the declared spread across and each stands a sixth of the spread off centre, so offset plus radius is exactly the spread's half on either side.

terrace.treeTrunkBaseRadius.why: [estimated] one thirtieth of the height, the slenderness of a multi-stem at this size.

terrace.treeTrunkTopRadius.why: [estimated] two thirds of the base radius over the clear trunk.

reads.why: Figures taken directly off a named frame or plan, with the tolerance the frame supports. These are citations, not derivations: the test pins them as literals because changing one is changing what the photograph is claimed to show.

system.window.rotationDeg.source: HKS via gbdmagazine, published: windows 'popped out and rotated six degrees' on the lower towers

lantern.columnsPerFacet.source: EYRC phf15 — two window columns per chamfer facet

lantern.frameFace.source: EYRC phf15 — 'a raised white frame grid ~0.20 m wide'

grid.groundStoreys.source: UCSD 'TDLLN Project Update August 2020' p.11 GROUND LEVEL — BLDG 1 has ONE ground storey, all residential support and core/circulation/BOH, with no mezzanine and no double-height plinth; the 105 px colonnade clear against the 125 px storey confirms L1 is the same 3.048 m as a typical floor

terrace.planters.source: Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png — four square planters in two pairs on the deck's west half; the four (x, z) stations under `terrace.planters` are read straight off that frame at its calibrated scale and are the only coordinates in this section that are neither ring vertices nor solved from them

groundStorey.stair.risersSourced.source: SWA …Learning-16.webp — about six risers counted against the 2.56 m soffit height

roof.screenWells.size.0.source: EYRC phf15 — each well is roughly a quarter of the west bar's length

roof.screenWells.size.1.source: EYRC phf15 (Lawrence Anderson drone aerial from the east) — the well's depth across the Tower strip, read against the strip's own surveyed 11.6 m

roof.screenWells.uFromWest.0.source: EYRC phf15 cross-read in r1c1-plan-00-south; measured from the WEST end of the west bar

roof.screenWells.uFromWest.1.source: EYRC phf15 cross-read in Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png — the eastern well's station along the west bar, measured from its west end

roof.condensers.size.0.source: EYRC phf15 — split-system condenser, ≈0.9 x 0.35 x 0.8 m

roof.condensers.size.1.source: EYRC phf15 — the unit's height above the deck, the tallest dimension of the row and the only one the frame resolves cleanly

roof.condensers.size.2.source: EYRC phf15 — the unit's depth north-south, the shallowest dimension and the least certain of the three

roof.condensers.count.source: EYRC phf15 — a row of about five units

roof.bulkhead.size.0.source: EYRC phf15 — a plain box roughly 6 x 4 m

roof.bulkhead.size.1.source: EYRC phf15 — the bulkhead's depth across the east wing, roughly two thirds of its 6 m length in the same frame

terrace.sourced.uFrac.source: Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png, metre grid calibrated on the MEASURED 48.7 m Mid south face — the deck covers the western ≈20 m of the Mid roof

terrace.sourced.depth.source: Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png — the clear depth inside the parapets. IT DOES NOT FIT THE DRAWN LID; see terrace.clipNote

terrace.sourced.area.source: Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png — the sourced 20 x 6.1 m. The BUILT deck is smaller because it is clipped to the drawn ring; the clip is the finding, not a discrepancy to hide

terrace.planterSize.0.source: Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png — four square planters ≈1.5 x 1.5 m in two pairs

terrace.planterSize.2.source: Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png — the planters read square, so this is the same 1.5 m as the plan dimension beside it

terrace.longElement.size.0.source: Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png and EYRC phf15 — footprint only; the element itself is WITHHELD

terrace.longElement.size.1.source: Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png and EYRC phf15 — the narrow dimension of the withheld long element; footprint only, nothing is drawn

draw.why: Render offsets, not dimensions. Nothing here is a claim about the building: they exist so coplanar surfaces resolve in depth and so no terrain triangle runs through a face. They are declared here rather than left as literals in the module, and the test checks the module carries no numeric geometry of its own.
draw.buryDepthNote: 2 ft. Every face and every seated solid is carried this far below the drawn surface so no terrain triangle runs under it.

tiles.note: Material REPEAT tiles, not building dimensions: how much real surface one texture tile of campus-materials.js's woodSlat, roofMembrane and brick classes covers. The brick class tiles 8 courses by 4 units, so its tile is 8 nominal units square — the York convention. The panel, paver and pier repeats are driven off the derived figures instead and appear nowhere here.

measured.lidarNote: THERE IS NO LiDAR READ FOR PULSE AND NONE MAY BE INVENTED. campus-lidar.json massHeights has no entry for either Pulse geometry key; the 2014 survey predates the building by nine years. The only prism this project has for Pulse is the facilities massing ring and its GIS h, and every dressed datum in this section solves on it by campus-massing.js roofElevation.
measured.osmNote: campus-3d.json DOES carry a 9-vertex OSM ring named 'Pulse' with h = 37.2 covering the whole complex as one footprint. That h is an OSM levels guess over a footprint that merges the two masses, it disagrees with both GIS heights, and it is USED NOWHERE in this section — recorded so the next agent does not discover it and think it is a measurement. The two-source rule: OSM gives footprints and names, never height.

heightStack.note: TWO EPOCHS RECONCILE ARITHMETICALLY. The GIS h is the top of the structural roof DECK; the 2020 planning deck's published 115 ft is the top of the rooftop mechanical SCREEN. 115 - 100 (10 x 10 ft) = 15 ft, and Azad reproduces the same residual exactly (105 - 90 = 15 ft). So 3.048 m is a real 10 ft floor-to-floor and not a placeholder — Walter P Moore's post-tensioned flat-plate slabs with full-height columns and no transfer beams are precisely the structure that makes it buildable.
heightStack.conflict: DECLARED SOURCE CONFLICT: the sourced floor-to-floor is 3.048 m (10 ft) and 10 x 3.048 = 30.48 m, but the DRAWN prism carries h = 30.5 (Tower) and 27.4 (Mid), rounded to 0.1 m by the survey. The DRAWN PRISM WINS: the storey grid used to build is h / levels — 3.05 m on the Tower and 3.044444 m on the Mid — so the photographed plate COUNT fills the drawn box with zero residual and the parapet band stands ON the visible lid. Solved on 30.48 instead, the whole membrane would sit 0.02 m under the drawn deck and the step would come out 3.048 instead of the drawn 3.1. The PHOTOGRAPHED RATIOS, by contrast, convert on the SOURCED 3.048 m: a photograph measures the real building, and the drawn storey governs only where plates stack inside the drawn box. Both rules are used, each where it belongs, and the 2 mm between them is why.

tower.source: docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing[463] outer ring, decimetres/10, copied verbatim by the generator — the EXACT ring and h campus-massing.js extrudes as the drawn 'Pulse' gis mass. Every dressed datum solves on roofElevation(this ring, this h, heightAt).

mid.source: docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing[487] outer ring, decimetres/10, copied verbatim. Same rule; its own rim median, so the roof step is solved as roofY(tower) - roofY(mid) and never assumed to be 3.1 m on a grade.

sharedEdges.note: the corridor party line: 10-storey Tower strip north of it, 9-storey Mid strip south. The only thing drawn here is the STEP WALL.
the Mid's east return against the Tower's east wing.

sharedEdges.overlapNote: PARTIAL, not coincident: the Tower's segment 1 runs z 558.3-562.5 and the Mid's segment 4 runs z 558.0-562.5, so the shared stretch is the whole of T1 and all but 0.3 m of M4. (-197.7, 558.3) is a Tower vertex lying ON the Mid's segment 4, not a Mid vertex — which is why the endpoint test here is on-the-ring and not vertex-for-vertex. The remaining 0.3 m of the Tower's segment 0 (z 558.0-558.3) is likewise concealed behind the tab and is built anyway, because a concealed wall is not a hovering one.
sharedEdges.note: FOUND BY THIS BUILD, not in the inventory: the Mid's 3.0 m west tab stands against 4.20 m of the Tower's west wall (both at x = -197.7, z 558.0-562.5), so that stretch is internal below the Mid deck. It is why the externally visible perimeter is 216.6 m and not the inventory's 225.3 m — 225.3 counts these 4.20 m and the Mid's 4.50 m M4 as facade.

perimeter.note: Sum of the 12 full-height external runs. The inventory's 225.3 m counts the two shared edges at x = -197.7 (Tower segment 1, 4.20 m, and Mid segment 4, 4.50 m) as facade; the point-in-ring probe over both shipped rings says the Mid's 3.0 m west tab stands against them, so they are internal below the Mid deck. Tower segment 1 is still built — as the west return of the roof step, above the Mid lid only.

depth.note: 11.6 + 6.9 = 18.5 m matches the free-standing east wing's perpendicular depth of 18.17 m (the dot of the wing's ring span with the unit normal of its own direction) — the arithmetic that proves the two GIS masses are the two longitudinal strips of ONE double-loaded bar and not two buildings with a slot between them.

grid.bayNote: Bays are COUNTS against the measured ring, never absolute metres (the Argo rule). 11 columns across the MEASURED 48.7 m faces gives the 4.4273 m module every derived facade dimension converts on. Built modules, face by face: T-north-westBar 48.7/11 = 4.427, M-south 48.7/11 = 4.427, T-southEast 34.95/8 = 4.369, T-north-eastWing 35.75/8 = 4.469. The photogrammetric read on SWA-16 was 4.50 ± 0.5 m (window-column pitch 180 ± 20 px over a 125 px storey pitch) and contains all four.
grid.bayConflict: DECLARED SOURCE CONFLICT with the shipped measured world: campus-eighth.json carries bay_m 3.5 for both Pulse masses from a pier count, and its own note calls that a candidate figure. This section's 4.37-4.47 m comes from counting window columns across a measured 48.7 m face and supersedes it for the photo layer. A 10-column reading of the same face would give 4.87 m; the count is 11 and 4.87 is NOT used anywhere in this section. campus-eighth.json is NOT edited — the disagreement is recorded, not resolved by deletion.
grid.rowNote: Rows count DOWN from the DRAWN deck. Level 0 is the ground storey (residential support + core/circulation/BOH on the 2020 GROUND LEVEL plan — no retail, no academic), so residential window rows are levels - 1: 9 on the Tower, 8 on the Mid. Eight residential rows above a ground storey were counted directly on the Mid's south face in Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png.

panel.note: Large-format flat rainscreen panel with fine open vertical joints, 0.683 m wide by one storey tall — joint spacing 28 ± 4 px against a 125 px storey in SWA-16. Carried as the material repeat so the microstructure lands at true panel scale.
panel.conflict: The joint-to-storey ratio gives 0.683 ± 0.098 m on the long elevations (SWA-16) but ≈1.02 m on the near-orthographic end wall (SWA-3). Either the end walls use a larger format or one reading picks up sub-joints. 0.683 m is built everywhere; the 1.02 m read is in `absent`.

chimney.note: Slate blue-grey panel used as vertical chimneys 4-6 panels wide that jog floor to floor and each carry a window stack, so the elevation reads as a staggered two-tone field rather than a grid (SWA-16). The chimney is the SAME rainscreen plane as the field — `flush: true` — and is drawn at `draw.chimneyOffset` only so the two coplanar surfaces resolve in depth. The previous 0.02 m 'proud' was a render offset wearing a dimension's name.

window.note: One window per bay: 2.4596 m wide x 2.4384 m high, sill 0.4620 m above FFL, two lights with a horizontal transom at two-thirds height, dark teal glass. Each sits in a box rotated 6 degrees in plan — HKS's published move for the LOWER towers, which is Pulse at 10 storeys and not Sankofa at 21 or Podemos at 16 (those get fins) — so the leading jamb stands w x sin(6 deg) = 0.2571 m proud and the trailing jamb is flush. Every one of those figures is derived in `derivations.figures`; the dossier's 2.40 / 2.44 / 0.45 were the same ratios converted on a bay nothing sources, and the discrepancy is recorded there.
window.senseNote: [estimated] ROTATION SENSE. The 6-degree magnitude is sourced; which way each face rotates is not — the gold return reads on the frame-left jamb in SWA-16, but frame-left is east there and the sun was north-west, so the asymmetry cannot be separated from the lighting. One consistent sense is used on every face: a directional airflow effect is the simplest reading, and a per-face sense would be a claim with no source.

frame.note: A slim projecting picture frame wraps head, jambs and sill: gold/ochre on windows set in the pale field, charcoal on windows set in the blue-grey chimneys. That alternation is the north elevation's strongest cue. Frame face = 6 px against a 100 px window in SWA-16; the return equals the face because a formed trim of this kind is square in section and no frame resolves the depth separately.

system.serration: BUILT AS THE ROTATED WINDOW BOXES ONLY. SDAF and gbdmagazine describe 'serrated facades for natural ventilation' project-wide and the 2020 typical-floor plan shows repeated small trapezoidal projections along both long walls of BLDG 1, but that plan is a raster of a PowerPoint export and gives no projection depth or spacing independent of the 6-degree reading. The wall plane is NOT additionally folded — that would double-count one move.

commonRoom.note: [estimated] width, extending the sourced 2.4596 m window by one panel module each side. The 2020 typical-floor plan puts a Residential Common Space block at the inner bend of the dog-leg, so the bay there reads as a wider glazed room; the plan does not dimension it.

stepWall.note: One storey of blank pale rainscreen rising from the Mid roof deck to the Tower roof deck along the two shared edges — also the north enclosure of the rooftop terrace. Its height is solved as roofY(tower) - roofY(mid) on the drawn prisms, not assumed to be 3.1 m.

endWall.note: Solid pale rainscreen. No opening is invented: the Tower's west end shows about seven horizontal recesses in Apple's mesh which may be recessed loggias or may be photogrammetric smearing of a flat wall, and its slot windows are unmeasured. Both are in `absent`.

lantern.note: A stacked lantern of common rooms terminates BOTH ends of the bar — the building's signature element. Clad pale/white rather than in the two-tone field, carrying a grid of small square openings in a raised white frame: two window columns per facet, one row per floor. 3 facets x 2 x 10 = 60 openings at the east tip; 2 facets x 2 x 9 = 36 at the west. The 12.24 m east end wall is longer than two columns fill; the drone frame resolves two, so two ship and the rest is blank lantern cladding rather than an invented count. The openings sit on the same sill as every other window in the building rather than on an invented storey fraction.

groundStorey.program: RESIDENTIAL SUPPORT plus CORE / CIRCULATION / BOH on the 2020 GROUND LEVEL legend — no retail, no academic anywhere in BLDG 1. The L1 fitness centre (pelotons, weights, punching bags) fronts the basketball court on the north.
groundStorey.envelopeNote: The furthest outside either drawn ring anything in this section's ground group may stand, derived from the deepest ground element (the porch) plus half a rail. Gated by the test, so a later edit cannot push the porch into the Bamboo Garden.
groundStorey.fflNote: THE ONE GROUND DATUM. Every ground-storey element in this section — the colonnade recess, the storefront, the piers, the soffit fascia, the north entry terrace, the guard and the top of the exterior flight — is measured from the L1 FINISHED FLOOR LEVEL, which is the DRAWN PRISM BASE (roofElevation - h). It is not the drawn terrain: the drawn terrain here is a 2014 read of a parking lot that no longer exists. Anything that must MEET the ground (the terrace fascia, the flight, the porch deck, the skirts) is carried to the drawn surface from that datum and never hovers over it.
groundStorey.soffitFasciaNote: The soffit's exposed edge runs from the clear height to the mass's own DRAWN storey, so the band closes exactly onto the field wall above. Solved per mass: 0.48968 m on the Tower, 0.484124 m on the Mid. This retires the declared-but-unbuilt 0.15 m 'slab zone' of the previous revision, which left 0.15 m of raw massing prism showing between the fascia and the field.

colonnade.source: SWA …Learning-16.webp — the facade above oversails on piers of pale cream coursed unit masonry with a flat soffit, full-height glazed curtain wall between the piers with charcoal mullions. Pier spacing follows the derived bay module. The pier's plan size is [estimated] at three nominal 8-inch units and the oversail and pier stand-off both fall out of it, so the recess depth is not a separate invention.

entrance.source: [estimated] — SWA-16 resolves the full-height glazed frontage between the colonnade piers and the broad exterior flight that climbs to it, and a flight that climbs to a blank wall is not a reading any source supports. The pair is placed in the storefront bay the flight lands in and is built out of the sourced storefront's own module and charcoal mullion. EVERY OTHER OPENING ON THIS BUILDING — the service door under the address numerals, back-of-house doors, the porch's own doors — is in `absent`, because SWA-3 does not resolve WHICH of the two buildings flanking the Bamboo Garden is Pulse.

groundStorey.baseBandNote: A near-black base band east of the colonnade in SWA-16; extended to the other field faces as the ground-storey treatment they share, labelled [estimated] on those faces.

breezeway.note: [estimated] station, derived width. An open through-breezeway cuts the ground floor of the west bar from north to south at about mid-length, connecting the Wellness Corridor and the court to the Bamboo Garden (2020 GROUND LEVEL plan). The plan shows it; it does not station it, so it is placed at mid-length and given one bay's width. It is drawn as the VOID PLANE it reads as at each mouth: the measured massing is never cut (the Argo/York convention), so the plan's planting wedges and the steps within the opening cannot be built inside a mass this project does not carve — both are in `absent`.

stair.station: SOLVED, not stationed by any source. The flight is placed at the station along the sourced face where the DRAWN SURFACE falls furthest below the L1 floor, because that is the only station at which a descending flight is neither buried nor hanging. The previous revision's uFrac 0.22 was an invented station and its six risers ran 0.15-0.75 m under the drawn ground on flat terrain and 2.3-3.1 m under it on a rolling one.
stair.risersNote: THE BUILT RISER COUNT IS SOLVED AGAINST THE DRAWN SURFACE and is never more than the sourced 6: every riser's top must stand at or above the drawn surface under it, and the top riser's top is the L1 floor exactly. Where the drawn surface supports no riser, no flight and no handrail is drawn and the whole level change stays in `absent`. This is an EPOCH conflict, not a modelling choice — the built site was regraded and the 2014 terrain is the parking lot that preceded it.
stair.source: SWA …Learning-16.webp — a broad exterior stair with stainless/galvanised pipe handrails on the north, about six risers counted against the 2.56 m soffit height, climbing from the court's level to the colonnade level.

northTerrace.source: SWA …Learning-16.webp — 'dark grey/black vertical picket rail, ≈1.07 m, at the RAISED TERRACE EDGES north of the building'. That is the guard's sourced location and this is where it is built. THE PREVIOUS REVISION PUT THIS GUARD ON THE FRONT PORCH, on the SOUTH side, which the frame does not show. The terrace is the raised walking level under the colonnade's oversail: its top is the L1 floor, its outer edge is closed to the drawn surface by a solid fascia so it never hovers, the guard stands ON it, and the exterior flight descends from it.
northTerrace.note: The guard is broken over the flight's own width; the flight's two pipe handrails take over there.

porch.source: 'Front Porch' named at Pulse on the 2025 SDAF built-condition site plan; the brown deck band on the 2020 GROUND LEVEL plan. A wood-decked terrace runs the south side of the west bar and wraps the east wing.
porch.raisedNote: SHIPS ON GRADE, DRAPED. The 2020 plan's word for it is a deck band and the 2025 plan names it; NEITHER dimensions a step up from the court, and no frame in the EYRC or SWA sets shows the porch's edge. The previous revision called it 'raised' in prose and then shipped it as a flat decal with no riser, edge or fascia — the claim and the geometry disagreed. The claim is withdrawn here: it is a deck on grade until a frame shows an edge, and the step up is in `absent`. It carries NO guard: the picket guard SWA-16 photographs is on the north terrace, not here.

membrane.note: White / very pale grey single-ply TPO, no ballast, no pavers. Drawn as one polygon per lid, cut from the DRAWN ring itself, so it can never overrun the mass it sits on. Its lift off the deck is a render offset and lives in `draw`.

parapet.note: 42 in is the guard the adjacent occupied Mid deck legally needs, corroborated by silhouette — the parapet reads ~0.35 storey in phf15. It runs every Tower ring segment (including the two shared edges, where it caps the step wall and guards the Tower lid) and only the three EXTERNAL Mid segments: the Mid's other three edges abut a taller mass, so a parapet there would be a guard against nothing.

walkPad.crossNote: The cross run's station is DERIVED, not placed: it runs at the mid-point of the gap between the two screen wells, from the north pad's inner edge south to the condenser row's north face. The previous revision's literal rectangle {-176, -175, 551.6, 559.8} was an invented station and it drove the pad through the bulkhead.
walkPad.note: A grey walking pad runs the length just inside the north parapet with a cross run to the plant (phf15, r1c1-plan-00-south). It is laid as SQUARE SEGMENTS, each one clipped to the drawn ring and dropped where the plant already stands or where an earlier segment already covers the ground — which is how the two face runs meet at the dog-leg corner without overlapping and how neither of them runs through the bulkhead.

screenWells.stationNote: The two wells are stationed by their read u fractions along the WEST BAR, measured from its west end, and centred across the Tower strip's own surveyed depth — so their coordinates are solved off the ring rather than typed in.
screenWells.heightNote: 4.552 m above the DRAWN deck = the published 115 ft top-of-screen (35.052 m) minus the drawn 30.5 m deck. The inventory's 3.50 m is the same figure measured above the 1.07 m parapet against the 30.48 m nominal deck; both are recorded so neither reading is lost.
screenWells.confidence: LOW on the 11 x 8 m footprints and on the u = 0.30 / 0.62 stations — they are read off one oblique drone frame and are the weakest numbers in this section, carried in `reads` with their tolerances. The HEIGHT is derived and solid.

condensers.stationNote: The row is CENTRED on the gap between the two screen wells and set one listed side-clearance south of their south face — both solved from the wells, which are themselves solved from the ring. Nothing here is a typed coordinate.
condensers.note: A row of about five split-system condensers near the south parapet, in the gap between the two screen wells (phf15).

bulkhead.note: A plain stair/lift bulkhead at the roof's north-east, in the east wing (phf15), one drawn storey tall. Station [estimated] within the wing; it is clipped to the drawn ring like every other roof item and the walk pad is kept off it.

vents.note: A line of small circular plumbing vents at ~6-7 m centres (phf15, r1c1-plan-00-south), built as a nominal 4 in vent through roof at the plumbing code's 6 in minimum projection. Generated on a grid CENTRED on each lid and CLIPPED to the drawn ring — see clips. The grid is centred rather than started from a bounding-box corner because the Mid strip is only 6.46 m deep between the drawn edges and a corner-started grid put its only row 1.15 m off the parapet, which clipped every Mid vent away.

clips.rule: Every roof item is placed only where its own (x, z) is inside its mass's DRAWN ring and clear of the nearest ring edge by its own class clearance — `vents.edgeClear` for a vent, `parapet.thickness + walkPad.width / 2` for a walk-pad segment, `terrace.edgeClear` at all four corners for a paver. Nothing may hover: the two lids are an L and a stepped L, so a bounding-box grid overruns them on four sides. Nothing may intersect either: the walk pad is dropped where the plant stands and the vent grid is dropped where the plant or the pad stands, both at the same clearances.
clips.probeClearNote: Half the vent pitch: if a clip had failed, the grid would have put an item within half a pitch of the probe. Derived, so tightening the vent grid tightens the gate with it.

forbidden.why: the Tower's bounding box is a rectangle and the east tip is a taper: this point is inside the box, 1.5 m east of the T8 end wall, with no lid under it at all
the bounding box of the Tower lid covers the Mid strip, which is a whole storey lower — a Tower item placed there would hover over the Mid deck
the Mid's bounding box reaches north over the Tower's west bar. This point is inside the Mid's box and inside the TOWER's ring: a Mid vent here would hang 3 m in the air under the Tower's own roof

pv.note: THERE IS NO PHOTOVOLTAIC ARRAY ANYWHERE ON PULSE, AND THE ONE THE RENDERINGS DRAW IS NOT BUILT. The 2021 design renderings (Revelle town-hall deck slides 4 and 16) draw large dark-blue PV fields on the 9/10/11-storey roofs. In EYRC phf15 — one frame, one exposure — Pulse's lids show white membrane, parapets, two mechanical screen wells, ducts and condensers and nothing else, while KEELING APARTMENTS' rooftop PV array is plainly visible in the same frame a few hundred metres north. Keeling is the in-frame control that makes the negative credible; SWA …Learning-1 (aerial from the south-east) agrees. This is an epoch conflict resolved in favour of the newer source, recorded here in the exact form of Keeling's deleted-canopy note.

terrace.source: A named amenity, not an inference: eighth.ucsd.edu lists Pulse as 'fitness centre L1 … rooftop deck', and the UCSD Guardian (2024-09-30) reports Pulse's roof access still among the delayed items that autumn — so it is built, not built open. Square pedestal pavers on a diagonal grid over the western two-fifths of the Mid lid; four square planters in two pairs, each with one small multi-stem tree; the blank one-storey step wall as its north enclosure; the Mid's own parapet as guard on the other three sides. Measured on r1c1-plan-00-south.png with a metre grid calibrated at 21.0 px/m on the MEASURED 48.7 m Mid south face, rescaled to the roof plane by the ratio of drawn face length to image length (0.87). The `sourced` block above is what that frame gives; `xEast` is DERIVED from it and is what the build actually uses, so nothing in this block is dead data.
terrace.clipNote: THE SOURCED 6.1 m CLEAR DEPTH DOES NOT FIT THE DRAWN LID. The Mid strip measures 6.46 m gross between the drawn ring's north and south edges at the terrace, and 0.3048 m of that goes to the parapet and 0.3048 m to the step wall, leaving 5.85 m. So the deck is CLIPPED to the drawn ring rather than built at its sourced depth — nothing may hover. The sourced 6.1 m and its 122 m² stay on the record above; the built deck is smaller and that difference IS the finding. The clip picks up the 3.0 m west tab, which is Mid mass at the Mid deck, so the terrace is an L and not a rectangle.

longElement.note: WITHHELD. One long east-west element runs along the deck's north side in both r1c1-plan-00-south and phf15, but neither frame resolves whether it stands on legs (a communal table) or on posts (a pergola / trellis) — the two readings differ by about 1.7 m of height and by everything above the deck. Better absent than wrong: its footprint is recorded here and nothing is drawn.

program.note: Pulse was the ONLY one of the five TDLLN buildings finished for Fall 2023, and its 343 beds are exactly the beds UCSD could offer that autumn against a planned 2,000. The 2020 typical-floor plan draws a double-loaded corridor with 6-, 4- and 2-bedroom Studio (S1/S2/S3) and Apartment (A1/A2/A3) unit types. Construction Jan 2021 to Nov 2023; project complete 2024; Lawrence Anderson photography 2024-25. LEED v4 Platinum achieved; ~80% predicted energy reduction; the rotated-window facade is a CFD-driven natural-ventilation move. Team: HKS design architect and design-build lead, EYRC Architects, Kitchell GC, SWA Group landscape, Walter P Moore structure — NOT Safdie Rabines / OJB, which is Sixth College / North Torrey Pines LLN.
program.geometryNote: Recorded for provenance only. Nothing in this block drives geometry.

facades.source: Apple 3D .cache/eighth-area/r2c0-oblique-01-west.png (captured 2026-08-06) + arcgis massing[463] segment 0. Largely solid pale rainscreen; the slot windows Apple hints at are unmeasured and stay in `absent`. Its southernmost 0.3 m (z 558.0-558.3) is concealed behind the Mid's 3.0 m west tab.

arcgis massing[463] segment 1 against massing[487]: the Mid's tab stands in front of this 4.20 m of the Tower's west wall, so it is INTERNAL below the Mid deck and exposed only as the west return of the one-storey roof step. Apple r2c0-oblique-01-west.png shows the Tower's west end standing taller than the Mid's.

EYRC/Lawrence Anderson phf15.jpg (drone from the east, 2024-25) + UCSD 'TDLLN Project Update August 2020' p.12 typical-floor plan, which puts a Residential Common Space block at this inner bend. The 3.825 m glazing width is [estimated] and extends the sourced 2.4596 m window of T-north-westBar by one panel module each side.
phf15.jpg + Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png. Same panel, window, frame and rotated-box system as the sourced north elevation; [estimated] only in that no frontal photograph of this face exists.
phf15.jpg — the drone frame from the east resolves the chamfered stacked common-room lantern, its white frame grid and the row count.
phf15.jpg. The survey ring makes v7 (-114.1, 553.0) RE-ENTRANT: this facet faces SE while its neighbours face ENE, so the tip is a projecting bay with a reveal, not a simple chamfer.

phf15.jpg + UCSD 'TDLLN Project Update August 2020' p.12 (the red RESIDENTIAL COMMON SPACE wedge at the bar's east end). Two window columns are all the drone frame resolves on this 12.24 m facet; the rest ships as blank lantern cladding.

SWA UCSD_UC-San-Diego_Theater-District_Living-Learning-16.webp (frame left) + Apple r2c1-oblique-02-north.png. The three bays at the east end (u = 0 is the east end) are the blank stair/lift core; their narrow slot windows are unmeasured and stay in `absent`.

SWA …Learning-16.webp (Lawrence Anderson for SWA, 2024-25) — identification certain: the frame is the surveyed 22.7 x 15.4 m Eighth basketball court, Pulse's north face is 17.8 m south of the court's south edge, the PODEMOS wordmark is legible on the distant tower and the tan-brick Parking Elevator pavilion stands where the 2021 site plan draws it. Bay COUNT cross-checked on Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png. THE reference elevation: every other field face extends it, and every pixel reading in `derivations.readings.px` is taken on it.

facades.derivedFrom: arcgis massing[487] segment 0, split at z = 562.5 — the z of ring vertices w4 (-197.7, 562.5) and the top of the shared edge M4, so the split is the tab's own north-south extent and not an invented station
facades.source: Apple r2c0-oblique-01-west.png — both west ends, the 3.0 m setback and the white-framed grid; UCSD 'TDLLN Project Update August 2020' p.12 (RESIDENTIAL COMMON SPACE blocks at the bar's west end). The 3.0 m tab IS the projecting lantern bay: this facet and M-west-tabReturn are its two faces.

facades.derivedFrom: arcgis massing[487] segment 0, the remainder north of the tab split
facades.source: Apple r2c0-oblique-01-west.png. Solid pale rainscreen; no opening is resolved and none is invented.

EYRC/Lawrence Anderson phf47.jpg and phf48.jpg (2024-25 dusk, Meditation Pavilion in front of this face), SWA …Learning-3.webp and …Learning-20.webp, Apple r1c1-plan-00-south.png — eight residential window rows counted directly above a ground storey. The face the college presents: it opens onto the Bamboo Garden, the Meditation Pavilion and the Ramble.
Apple r2c0-oblique-01-west.png + arcgis massing[487] segment 5. The north face of the 3.0 m tab; the second facet of the west lantern.

counts.note: Terrain-independent counts only. The exterior flight's built riser count, its two handrails and the walk pad's segment count are SOLVED against the drawn surface and the drawn ring, so they are gated geometrically rather than pinned to a number here — see groundStorey.stair.risersNote and roof.walkPad.note.

absent: ROOFTOP PHOTOVOLTAICS, on both lids. The 2021 design renderings (Revelle town-hall deck slides 4 and 16) draw large dark-blue PV fields on the 9/10/11-storey Eighth roofs. EYRC phf15 — a 2024-25 drone aerial from the east — shows Pulse's lids as white membrane, parapets, two mechanical screen wells, ducts and condensers and nothing else, in the SAME frame in which Keeling Apartments' rooftop PV array is plainly visible. Keeling is the in-frame control that makes the negative credible; SWA …Learning-1 agrees from the south-east. Zero panels, zero racks, zero ballast trays.

THE STREET ADDRESS. SWA …Learning-3.webp shows black applied numerals '9175' on one and '9155' on the other of the two buildings flanking the Bamboo Garden. A solar/shadow reading of that frame puts Pulse at 9155; interpolating the three published numbers (9145 Survivance, 9165 Sankofa, 9185 academic wing) as a north-increasing sequence puts Pulse at 9175. Both derivations are defensible and they disagree, so no numeral is applied to this building.

EVERY DOOR ON THIS BUILDING EXCEPT THE ONE PAIR IN THE COLONNADE. SWA-3 photographs a dark SERVICE DOOR under the address numerals, but the same frame does not resolve which of the two buildings flanking the Bamboo Garden is Pulse (see the address entry), so the door's FACE is unknown and it is not placed. Back-of-house doors, the fitness centre's own secondary exits, roof-hatch doors and any door onto the Front Porch are likewise unresolved in every frame in the EYRC set, the SWA set and the 153 Apple captures. Only the colonnade entrance pair is built, and it is labelled [estimated] against the sourced storefront it is cut from — a broad photographed flight that climbs to a blank wall is the reading no source supports.

A PULSE WORDMARK. RSM Design produced the five names and the SANKOFA and PODEMOS wordmarks are photographed on their bases, but no frame in the EYRC set, the SWA set or the 153 Apple captures resolves a PULSE wordmark. None is invented.

ANY CLAIM ABOUT WHICH WAY EACH FACE'S 6-DEGREE WINDOW BOXES ROTATE. The magnitude is HKS's published figure; the sense is not sourced — the gold return reads on the frame-left jamb in SWA-16, but frame-left is east there and the sun was north-west, so the asymmetry cannot be separated from the lighting. One consistent sense is built and labelled [estimated]; a per-face sense is withheld.

THE SEVEN HORIZONTAL RECESSES ON THE TOWER'S WEST END WALL. Apple r2c0-oblique-01-west.png shows about seven of them; no photograph confirms them and Apple's mesh smears flat walls into exactly that pattern. Withheld until a photograph of the west end turns up.

SLOT WINDOWS — in the Tower's west end wall and in the three blank bays of the east wing's north elevation (the stair/lift core). Their EXISTENCE is sourced; their size, count and station are legible only at a steep oblique and are unmeasured. The blank fields ship blank.

THE LONG 11.3 x 1.3 m ELEMENT ON THE ROOFTOP TERRACE. Communal table or pergola/trellis — neither phf15 nor the Apple near-plan frame resolves whether it stands on legs or on posts, and the two readings differ by everything above the deck. Its footprint is recorded in `terrace.longElement` and nothing is drawn.

THE BREEZEWAY'S PLANTING WEDGES AND THE STEPS WITHIN IT. The 2020 GROUND LEVEL plan draws both inside the through-opening. Neither can be built here: the measured massing is never carved (the Argo/York convention), so the breezeway ships as the void plane it reads as at each mouth and there is no modelled interior for a step or a bed to stand in; and the planting would in any case be the landscape modules' territory, not this section's. Recorded rather than silently dropped.

THE 0.91 m LEVEL CHANGE BETWEEN THE COURT AND THE COLONNADE, and with it whatever part of the sourced six-riser flight the drawn ground cannot carry. SWA-16 photographs a broad flight climbing from the court to the colonnade level and the count reads as about six risers, which is 0.91 m at the code's exterior riser. The DRAWN TERRAIN IS A 2014 READ OF THE PARKING LOT THAT PRECEDED THIS BUILDING and has no such level change: along the whole north frontage it falls at most about 0.3 m below the L1 floor. So the flight is solved against the drawn surface and ships the risers that surface supports — every riser top at or above the ground under it, the top riser exactly at the L1 floor — and the rest of the level change is declared here. It is NOT withheld on the 'the 2014 LiDAR is smooth so there is no step' argument, which is void over Eighth: the step is asserted, sourced and recorded; what is missing is a terrain epoch to build it against.

THE FRONT PORCH'S STEP UP FROM GRADE. The 2020 GROUND LEVEL plan draws the porch as a deck band and the 2025 SDAF plan names it 'Front Porch'; neither dimensions a step, a riser or a fascia, and no frame in the EYRC or SWA sets shows the porch's edge. It ships as a deck ON GRADE, draped on the drawn surface. The previous revision of this section called it 'raised' in prose while shipping a flat decal; the claim is withdrawn rather than the geometry invented.

A GUARD ON THE FRONT PORCH. The dark picket guard SWA-16 photographs is at the RAISED TERRACE EDGES NORTH of the building and is built there. No frame shows a guard on the south or east porch, so none is placed — and the previous revision's 698 pickets along the porch edge were a transcription error, not a reading.

ANY ADDITIONAL FOLD OF THE WALL PLANE FOR 'THE SERRATION'. The serration is built AS the rotated window boxes and nothing else; folding the wall as well would double-count one published move on a source (a raster of a PowerPoint export) that cannot give a depth or a spacing.

THE 1.02 m PANEL MODULE. The joint-to-storey ratio gives 0.683 ± 0.098 m on the long elevations (SWA-16) and ≈1.02 m on the near-orthographic end wall (SWA-3). Either the end walls use a larger format or one reading picks up sub-joints. 0.683 m is built everywhere and the conflict stays declared.

EVERY INTERIOR. No interior of Pulse is documented anywhere — EYRC's phf07/09/11/32/35 are interiors of OTHER TDLLN buildings (the L11 conference centre is Survivance; the co-working render is Building 2). The L1 fitness-centre equipment behind the north curtain wall is named in the university's own program but photographed nowhere, so nothing stands behind the glass.

THE MID'S M4 RETURN AS A FACADE, and the lower 4.20 m of the Tower's west wall segment 1. A point-in-ring probe over both shipped rings shows the Mid's 3.0 m west tab standing against them, so they are internal below the Mid deck. This is why the external perimeter here is 216.6 m against the inventory's 225.3 m.

A THIRD MECHANICAL SCREEN WELL, ANY RTU CLUSTER ON THE EAST WING LID, DAVITS, LIGHTNING PROTECTION AND ROOF-HATCH HARDWARE. phf15 resolves two wells, one bulkhead, one condenser row and a vent line on the west bar and nothing above the parapet on the east wing. Nothing is added to fill the frame.

ROOF DRAINS AS A SEPARATE CLASS. The dots r1c1-plan-00-south and phf15 resolve along both lids are built as plumbing vents; some of them are certainly drains, which sit flush and are a different object. No frame separates the two, so one class ships and the conflation is declared.
BALCONIES. Pulse has none in any frame. The stacked projecting balcony column belongs to SURVIVANCE's west end and must not migrate here.

THE LANDSCAPE AROUND PULSE — the Bamboo Garden, the Meditation Pavilion, the Ramble, the Sun Lawn, the basketball court, the calisthenics rig, the tan-brick Parking Elevator pavilion, bike racks, luminaires and the Amazon locker bank. All of it is other modules' territory and none of it is drawn from this section, however clearly SWA-16 and phf22 photograph it.

THE FRONT PORCH'S CONTINUATION ACROSS THE INNER BEND. The 2025 SDAF plan says the porch runs the south side of the west bar and wraps the east wing; it is built on both of those faces and NOT across the 6.3 m return between them, because the two draped decks would overlap at the corner on one overlay rung and no frame shows how the deck turns. Its depth is [estimated] everywhere.

BIRD-SAFE GLAZING FRIT, WINDOW MANUFACTURER PATTERNING, SIGNAGE, BANNERS AND EXTERIOR LIGHTING FIXTURES on any Pulse face. LEED v4 Platinum was achieved and bird-safe glazing is plausible on this campus, but plausible is not sourced.

A HEIGHT IN FEET FROM THE CEQA/EIR RECORD. ceqanet 2016111019 was not mined; the Regents' November 2020 CEQA findings were checked and carry only project-wide figures. Addendum No. 5 to the 2018 LRDP EIR remains the unexplored source for a surveyed height, and until it is read the 115 ft planning figure and the GIS deck are the whole of the height evidence.

ANY LiDAR-DERIVED HEIGHT OR GROUND READ FOR THIS BUILDING. The 2014 survey is blind to a 2023 building; campus-lidar.json massHeights has no Pulse entry and none is fabricated. The terrain the module seats on is the drawn surface, which is a 2014 read of a parking lot that no longer exists — recorded here so that a future terrain epoch can be applied without anyone mistaking the current seat for a measurement of the built site.

sankofa.label: Sankofa Hall — TDLLN Building 4, Eighth College, UC San Diego: the 21-storey tower (arcgis.massing[488]), the 10-storey Mid wing (massing[489]) and the one-storey Restaurant/Retail plinth (massing[461])
sankofa.epoch: 2024-25 built photography (EYRC / Lawrence Anderson, SWA Group) over the 2026-08-06 Apple Maps 3D capture in .cache/apple-flyover; the 2021-04-29 Revelle town-hall deck is DESIGN epoch and loses wherever it disagrees with a built frame. The 2014 LiDAR is BLIND here — the site was a parking lot in 2014 and campus-lidar.json massHeights has no entry for any Eighth mass — so the drawn prism is the university facilities massing ring and its GIS h, and no LiDAR height and no campus-3d OSM h is read anywhere in this section.
sankofa.note: INVENTED class — photo-sourced detail per README. Photographs and drawings decide WHAT EXISTS and HOW IT LOOKS; the measured survey keeps deciding WHERE and HOW BIG. Every facade layer hangs off two vertices of the DRAWN massing ring copied verbatim into measured.masses.*.ring (campus-arcgis.json massing, divided by 10 to metres, closing vertex included so the rim-median datum samples exactly as campus-massing.js roofElevation does), and floats at most 1.8 m proud of that face. The measured massing is never moved, carved or replaced. Nothing measured may ever read from this section. Colours labelled [estimated] in colorSources are derived from this building's own sourced colours and are replaced the day a real sample appears. EVERY NUMBER THIS SECTION BUILDS FROM CARRIES A ROW IN `figures` — its tier, the arithmetic that produced it, and, when it is [estimated], the sourced thing it extends. A number with no row is a defect and the test fails on it.

24 Apple Maps 3D frames — sankofa-close-00..11 and sankofa-orbit-00..11, which is 12 + 12 and is what the directory and .cache/apple-flyover/manifest.json both hold — used for GEOMETRY ONLY (face-by-face corroboration and the near-true elevations at close-02-south-west, close-05-north-west, close-08-north-east and close-11-south-east). Never a colour source: the 1.25 m georegistration offset is unresolved and colour sampling off raw Apple pixels stays off

2022 California Building Code, Chapter 10 — the code dimensions this section derives from rather than invents: 1015.2 guards 42 in (1.0668 m) minimum; 1011.5.2 stair riser 4-7 in and tread 11 in minimum; 1012.2 ramp slope 1:12 maximum; 1012.3 ramp rise 30 in (0.762 m) maximum per run; 1012.5 ramp clear width

ASTM A53 / ASME B36.10M welded steel pipe — the guard and bike-rack product step this section names instead of rounding: NPS 1-1/2 Schedule 40 is 48.3 mm OD, NPS 2 Schedule 40 is 60.3 mm OD. These are the two sizes every galvanised pipe guard and inverted-U bike rack in North America is made from

conflicts: REAL HEIGHT vs DRAWN HEIGHT. Largo Concrete's record for Building 4 — 21 cast-in-place levels at 10'-6" (3.2004 m) typical with select levels at 11'-0" (3.3528 m) and 11'-6" (3.5052 m) — totals 67.67 m to the roof deck (67.21 m if every level were the typical). The DRAWN prism is arcgis.massing[488] h = 64.0 m, which is exactly 21 × 3.048 m (21 × 10 ft) — the LRDP formula, verified against every other Eighth mass, and NOT a survey. The conflict is one storey, 3.2–3.7 m. Per the Keeling rule the DRAWN box wins and is filled with 21 bands of 64.0/21 = 3.0476 m; the sourced 3.2004 m is never extruded and stays on the record here. Corroboration for the sourced figure, not used to build: on Apple close-11-south-east (camera 149.8°, face normal 143.7°, so 6° off a true elevation) the SE face scales 53.08 m / 1050 px = 19.78 px/m and the facade's dominant vertical period is 66.4 px = 3.36 m.

SANKOFA MID: 9 OR 10 STOREYS. arcgis.massing[489] levels = 10 and the 2021 Revelle site plan (slide 6) labels the wing '(10 STORIES)'; the 2021 aerial rendering on slide 4 tags it 9, and a syndicated project text says Sankofa has 'a nine-story section and a 21-story section'. The survey wins: 10 levels of 30.5/10 = 3.05 m. The 9 stays on the record.

THE NOTCH CHEEK BEARINGS. The research inventory gives the two notch cheeks P2→P3 and P3→P4 outward bearings of 323.8° and 52.5°. Solved from the ring's own winding (signed area −1079.745 m², clockwise, so the outward normal of an edge with tangent t is (−t.z, t.x)) and reported as compass bearings with north = −z, the cheeks face 53.8° and 142.5°. The inventory's 323.8° is in fact the NORTH-WEST LONG FACE's normal and its 52.5° is within a degree of the NORTH-EAST END's 52.7°, so the pair is not this edge pair at all. An earlier draft of this section wrote the cheeks as '53.7° and 143.7°'; 143.7° is the SOUTH-EAST LONG FACE's normal, and that number is corrected here — a stated derivation that does not reproduce from its own ring is the exact error this conflict exists to catch. The module computes every outward normal from the winding and never from a stored bearing, so neither the inventory's transposition nor the earlier draft's slip can propagate. Checked in the roof's own (u,v) frame: P1(0,0) P2(53.08,0) P3(53.09,3.23) P4(56.87,3.30) P5(56.57,19.64) P0(2.41,19.69), and the missing corner is u 53.08–56.87 × v 0–3.30 — a bite, not a bump, exactly as 16.34 + 3.31 = 19.65 ≈ the 19.67 m slab depth predicts.

THE NE END'S COMPOSITION. The inventory describes the north-east end as loggia, then a dark glazed curtain-walled bay, then 'a solid pier at the SE corner', while also stating that the surveyed re-entrant notch 'is exactly where that stack sits'. The notch is at the SE (P4) end of that face, so the two clauses cannot both hold, and the survey wins the ORDER: the loggia runs from P4 (against the notch) and the curtain-walled bay follows. The PIER is a second, separate question and the answer is now no. Apple close-08-north-east is 8° off a true elevation of this face (camera 60.7°, face normal 52.7°) and reads the dark glazed bay running unbroken to the P5 / north-west corner with no pale solid panel wider than about a metre before the silhouette edge; orbit-08 at 60.4° reads the same. The pier is therefore not built and is declared absent. The three WIDTHS are no longer three typed numbers: the face carries a counted 5 bays over its surveyed 16.34 m (module 3.2680 m) and the composition is 2 bays of loggia + 3 bays of curtain wall + 0 bays of pier, which is the same COUNT-over-the-survey rule every other face in this section uses. The resulting 6.536 m loggia brackets the two independent pixel reads of this frame (≈6.4 m re-measured here, ≈6.7 m in the round-one audit) and the disagreement between those two reads is itself why the metres are derived from a count and not asserted.

THE COLONNADE AND THE CANOPY ON THE PLINTH'S NE END. The inventory has the tower's ground colonnade returning ~5 columns round the north-east end AND the plinth's broad cantilevered canopy running that same 26.93 m edge. No frame in the set resolves how the two meet. The canopy is built (it is the stronger read in phf17 and phf19) and the colonnade return is declared absent rather than guessed.

THE WORDMARK'S WALL. The inventory assigns the SANKOFA wordmark to the plinth's 40.21 m north-west face — which is also the face phf22 photographs as the OPEN colonnade, and a 4.3 m wall cannot be both over its whole length. The wordmark is recorded on the same sourced system's 21.80 m north (Ramble) wall, the wall SWA Learning-9's square-on midday view and the Ramble path actually reach. The wordmark itself is not rendered (see absent) so the assignment costs no geometry.

THE MARKET HALL PLAZA TERRACE GUARDRAIL. phf19 plainly shows a galvanised picket guard along the terrace edge in front of the south-east storefront. It is real and it is not built here, because what it stands on is the PLAZA's level change and not the building: no frame in this set resolves how far the step lies from the plinth wall, and an earlier draft of this section carried it at an invented 1.20 m standoff with no source of any kind. The plaza, its steps and its rails belong to the Eighth landscape sections; better absent than at a guessed offset. Declared absent.

measured.note: Verbatim from docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing, divided by 10 (the file stores decimetres), closing vertex included. h is the GIS h for that mass — for the tower, the Mid and every other Eighth mass except the Base it is exactly levels × 3.048 m (10 ft), the LRDP formula rather than a survey. campus-lidar.json massHeights has NO entry for any Eighth mass (the 2014 survey measures this site at parking-lot height), so no LiDAR height is read here and campus-3d.json's OSM h = 37.2 for 'Sankofa' — a suppressed ring campus-massing.js does not extrude — is never read either. assembleMasses over the shipped files returns exactly these three rings at exactly these heights.

tower.hNote: 64.0 = 21 × 3.048 m exactly — a formula height. The floor plate is 1079.7 m² by shoelace and the perpendicular depth between the two long faces is 19.67 m (P0 to the P1→P2 line).

mid.hNote: 30.5 = 10 × 3.048 m exactly — the same formula. The Mid reuses the tower's P0→P1 edge as a shared party wall, so that edge is skinned on NEITHER mass: below 30.5 m it is interior, and above 30.5 m it is the tower's own south-west end. Nothing else may be hung on it either — no facade, no parapet and no coping — because everything on it would stand inside the tower's own drawn solid.

base.hNote: 4.3 m is NOT levels × 3.048 (which would be 3.05). Sankofa Base is the one Eighth mass whose survey height escapes the LRDP formula, so 4.3 m is treated as the plinth's real datum without the usual caveat. The plinth projects 5.865 m beyond the tower's SE face (perpendicular from (-42.1, 594.6) to the P1→P2 line) and 1.391–1.830 m beyond its NW face (the perpendiculars from the two ends of base edge 10→11 to the P5→P0 line) — which is exactly what makes the canopy and the colonnade read, and those two perpendiculars are where the canopy projection's sanity check and the colonnade recess come from.

envelope.note: Nothing in this section may leave the union bounding box of the three drawn rings expanded by pad metres — and that is now tested on the built group's real BOUNDING BOX, not on instance origins, because the round-one Front Porch ramp escaped by 1.49 m with every origin still inside. The pad has to carry the Front Porch (which lies outside every massing ring, ~12 m west of the plinth) with its 9.144 m ramp run, the canopy's 4.25 m projection and the loggia slabs' 1.65 m projection.

grid.baySource: COUNTED, not assumed: on phf17's top storey band 13 fins span 955 px of an 1113 px SE face; scaled to the surveyed 53.08 m face that is 15 bays at 3.539 m (≈ 11'-7½", a standard concrete-shear-wall residential bay and a standard dorm-double width). The NW face is 54.16 m and cannot share the identical module — 15 bays there is 3.611 m, and the 1.08 m difference is absorbed at the raked ends. Every face in this section stores a COUNT and the module is that face's surveyed length divided by the count, so no bay dimension is ever typed in.
grid.bandSource: bayBand is the tolerance the residential module has to stay inside: ±0.3 m of the counted 3.539 m, which is the spread the six tower and Mid faces actually produce (3.306–3.738 m). baseBrickBand is WIDER on purpose and is not a loosened version of the same gate — the plinth is a retail podium whose brick piers are not on the residential module, its stepped south edge carries surveyed lengths of 7.86 m and 8.50 m that no residential count divides, and its own spread is 3.301–4.250 m. baseGlazedBand is the storefront family: half the sourced bay, 1.7695 m ± 0.08, which the three glazed plinth faces produce at 1.763–1.796 m. The test hard-codes all three bands as literals and then asserts these declarations equal them, so widening a band here cannot widen the gate.

fin.note: One fin per bay boundary per storey, one storey tall, with a sloped top cap. The two-sided fin is why the building photographs neutral grey from the north-west (SWA Learning-9) and amber from the south-east (phf19, phf22). A BOUNDARY fin is dropped wherever it would land inside the mass it belongs to: at the re-entrant notch the edge normal of one cheek points into the neighbouring face's solid, and an earlier draft buried one fin per storey — twenty of them — inside the tower at P3.

window.extendsPattern: Sankofa's own sourced slot window — the SLOT, its dark frame, the wider recessed charcoal surround and the awning/hopper head vent are all resolved in the SWA Learning-9 3.2× crop and in phf22; the proportions are read in that crop against the sourced bay and the drawn storey, and the millimetres follow from them

parapet.extendsPattern: Sankofa's own sourced facade rainscreen: the photographs show the same panel and joint pattern continuing above the top window head, so the parapet is a CONTINUATION of the membrane, not a separate band or a different material, capped by a thin darker metal coping line
parapet.source: phf17 (2024-25) for the crown silhouette, the north-east step-down and the guardrail line; phf15 (2024-25) for the parapet band from above; 2022 CBC 1015.2 (42 in guard minimum) and ASTM A53 pipe sizes for the rail
parapet.note: The upstand is derived two ways that agree to a fifth of a millimetre: the parapet band reads one third of a storey in the phf17 4× crop, and the sourced 3.2004 m storey / 3 = 1.0668 m; the 2022 CBC 1015.2 guard minimum of 42 in is 1.0668 m. Both give 1.067 m, and the 0.10 m coping on top puts the assembly clear of the code minimum. The NE step-down is MEASURED at ~35 px against 31.25 px/m calibrated on the adjacent 100 px = 3.2004 m top storey band, i.e. 1.12 m, and is no longer rounded to 1.1 — and once both figures are honest they say something the rounded pair hid: 1.12 m is MORE than the 1.067 m upstand it steps off, so over the loggia stack the solid parapet is not lowered, it is GONE. The three stepped edges therefore carry a coping trim and the slender pipe guardrail and no solid band at all, which is what the phf17 silhouette actually shows and what makes the crown asymmetric from most of campus. Every roof edge is still coped — copings run on all eleven non-shared ring edges, parapets on the eight that have one — so the membrane never terminates raw.

loggia.countSource: eighth.ucsd.edu sankofa-layout-info.pdf (2025-08-05): 21 FLOORS, 1ST FLOOR LOBBY, 2ND–21ST RESIDENTIAL — 20 residential floors, one loggia each. c_phf17_ne.jpg at 7× resolves ~19 downlight positions before the crop cuts the bottom of the tower, and the layout PDF closes the count at 20. The count is a DOCUMENT, not a preference: the test pins it to 20 as a literal and requires this string to name the layout PDF.
loggia.source: phf17 (2024-25) — the definitive dusk frame; phf15 (2024-25) — the projecting slabs from above; Apple close-08-north-east and orbit-08-north-east (2026-08-06) — 8° off a true elevation of this face and the frame that removed the pier; phf01 (2024-25) — the SAME corner-stack device on Podemos, which is what makes this the project's family language rather than an invention here
loggia.note: A full-height stack of OPEN recessed loggias, one per residential floor, at the north-east end and wrapping the corner into the notch cheek. Each loggia is open at the corner, has a slab soffit above, a projecting floor slab below (continuous white bands in the phf15 aerial), a glazed lounge behind, a balustrade closing the open edge, and A DOWNLIGHT AT THE OPEN CORNER OF EVERY FLOOR — the continuous vertical run of bright points in phf17 is the single most recognisable night feature of this building. The three widths are no longer typed: the face carries a counted 5 bays over its surveyed 16.34 m and the composition is loggiaBays + curtainBays + pierBays = 2 + 3 + 0 of them. See conflicts[3].

roof.membraneNote: Flat single-ply membrane, light grey, with a CONTINUOUS PALE WALKWAY PAD running inside both long parapets for the full roof length and cross-legs branching to each equipment island; the field between the two pads is a distinctly darker grey. Read directly off the phf15 drone aerial at 5–6× and corroborated on Apple close-08-north-east, which looks straight down the roof and shows the pale runs inside both parapets and the darker field between them. No green roof, no terrace, no pergola, and NO PHOTOVOLTAICS.

frame.note: The roof's own (u, v) frame: u metres along the tangent of ring edge P1→P2 (the SE long face) from P1, v metres inward on that face's inward normal. In this frame the drawn ring is P1(0,0) P2(53.08,0) P3(53.09,3.23) P4(56.87,3.30) P5(56.57,19.64) P0(2.41,19.69) and the surveyed notch is the missing rectangle u 53.08–56.87 × v 0–3.30. Every position on this roof is stored as a FRACTION of the frame's own uMax/vMax and multiplied up by the module, because a fraction is what a photograph gives you and a round metre is what a keyboard gives you.

walkway.extendsPattern: Sankofa's own sourced roof: the pad is measured at ~0.09 of the 19.67 m roof width on the phf15 5× crop (1.5–2.0 m) and set roughly 0.8–1.2 m inside the parapet; the count of two longitudinal runs plus a cross-leg to every island is counted on that frame
walkway.note: Laid as 1 m strips and clipped to the drawn ring, so the south-east run STOPS at the surveyed notch instead of cantilevering over it. The CROSS-LEGS are not a stored list any more: a cross-leg is what connects a walkway run to a piece of plant, so the module derives one at the u of every penthouse and every equipment island and there is nothing left to type in.
