NARROWED AT AUDIT: that immunity belongs to the count and NOT to a band metre read at one station and converted by this mean scale — see conflicts['scale-locality'], which measures the residual systematic at about 0.9%.

bay.module.why: 17.0688 m over a COUNTED 11 panels = 1.551709 m. The count is the evidence; the round 5 ft (1.524 m) hypothesis loses by 1.8% and is recorded in conflicts as the loser, never carried.

band.parapet.why: The 1966 brown/taupe precast parapet band, top to soffit line. Both edges are 50%-luminance crossings between the local plateaus either side, read in the strip x 300..1000 that is clear of the sign, the doors and the foreground planting.

band.soffit.why: The 2014 cantilevered soffit, in elevation, between the parapet band's foot and the head of the glazing.

band.glazingDegrees.why: The full-height glazed storefront on the 64 Degrees block, head to plinth top. The lower edge is a TEXTURE crossing, not a luminance one: the plinth and the graphic's dark water read within 7 of each other in luminance, and the mean |dL/dx| along the row falls from 6.2 to 3.2 across the joint.

band.plinth.why: The pale smooth-concrete base wall, glazing foot to paving.

stack.degrees.why: Paving to parapet top on the 64 Degrees block, read as ONE span rather than summed, so it is an independent check on the four bands rather than their total by construction.

stack.sumCheck.why: The four bands summed. It must equal stack.degrees to the last place, or one of the five edges has moved.

stack.lidarResidual.why: THE DERIVATION CHAIN'S KEYSTONE. A 2014 photograph, scaled only by a published width, puts the 64 Degrees parapet 9.772 m over its paving; the 2014 LiDAR flight puts its roof plane at 9.90 m. 0.128 m apart, 1.3%, from two sources that share no method. This is what lets every band above ship as [measured].

stack.lidarResidualPct.why: The same residual as a percentage of the LiDAR height.

band.glazingCommons.why: The Commons block is 7.5 m and the measured 64 Degrees stack is 9.772 m, so the stack CANNOT be hung on it. The parapet, the soffit and the plinth are the same continuous 1966/2014 elements round both blocks (Studio E frames 16, 18, 30, 31, 33) and keep their measured values; the glazing is the one variable element (FE&S: 20 ft ceilings in the east big box, 10 ft in the west section) and is what absorbs the difference. Nothing is scaled and no measured figure moves.

transom.centre.why: Height of the transom bar's centre above the plinth top. RE-READ AT AUDIT: the bar is BRIGHT against the graphic, not dark — baseline L 99.6, peak 130.3 at y 479 — and its edges are the half-max crossings of that peak. The centre reproduces the shipped 479.0 to 0.15 px; what did not reproduce was the depth, see transom.depth.

transom.depth.why: The bar's face depth, as the full width at half maximum of its own bright peak. CORRECTED AT AUDIT from 0.146 m: the previous reading pinned y 474 and y 484 as two dark edges, but y 474 sits on flat baseline (L 98.2) and carries no gradient at all — those two rows were an artefact of a detector comparing each row with rows +/-5 away, which on a 3 px bright bar manufactures minima at exactly +/-5. The true width is 3.31 px.

sign.width.why: The 3-D yellow '64 degrees' sign's bounding width, from a saturation mask (R>150, R-B>70, G between) over 19,066 pixels — the only strongly saturated warm-yellow object anywhere in the frame.

sign.height.why: The same mask's bounding height. The mask's foot lands at y 631 against the plinth-top line at y 632.96, i.e. the sign stands ON the building's own plinth band and not on a separate base — which retires the dossier's 'low pale concrete plinth in front of the glazing' as a separate object.

graphic.heightFt.why: The graphic's measured height in feet against its published 22 ft. 19.80 vs 22 is a 10% shortfall; the camera stands below mid-height so the top foreshortens. DECLARED in conflicts, never reconciled by rescaling the elevation.

orthoFit.modelRatioZ.why: How much worse the height-proportional model is than a constant offset, in z. Above 1 means the constant wins.

orthoFit.modelRatioX.why: The same ratio in x, fitted independently. Both axes agreeing is what makes the finding more than one noisy fit.

residue.degrees.why: Undressed drawn mass standing above the degrees block's own LiDAR roof plane. The extruder closes ONE prism at 11.3 m over all three blocks; hanging the treatment upward from surfaceAt to each block's own height leaves exactly this much bare. It is declared, not hidden, and it is not painted over.

The extruder closes ONE prism at 11.3 m over all three blocks; hanging the treatment upward from surfaceAt to each block's own height leaves exactly this much bare. residue.degreesTreated.why: The bare band actually left on 64 Degrees, which is measured against the TREATMENT's top (9.772 m) and not against the LiDAR plane (9.90 m) — 0.128 m more than residue.degrees, and that difference is stack.lidarResidual.

face.dgEast.length.why: The chord length of this face on the DRAWN massing ring — the ring campus-massing.js actually extrudes, so the facade closes against the mass on screen. The OSM outline is 2-3 m tighter and the difference is declared in conflicts['gis-vs-osm-outline'] rather than silently split.

columns.dgSouth.count.why: A column on every fourth bay boundary, including both ends. The spacing is [estimated] and banded; the COUNT falls out of it and the surveyed face length, so it cannot be typed.

columns.dgSouth.spacing.why: The shipped centre-to-centre spacing on this face, which is a whole number of that face's own shipped bays so a column always lands on a mullion and the storefront can close against it.

columns.dgSouth.height.why: The columns stand free at the roof edge and carry the soffit, so their top is the soffit's underside: the plinth plus the glazing band of the block they stand against. They are NOT full-height.

columns.commonsSouth.count.why: A column on every fourth bay boundary, including both ends. The spacing is [estimated] and banded; the COUNT falls out of it and the surveyed face length, so it cannot be typed.

columns.commonsSouth.spacing.why: The shipped centre-to-centre spacing on this face, which is a whole number of that face's own shipped bays so a column always lands on a mullion and the storefront can close against it.

graphic.firstBay.why: THE CENTRING RULE, AS ARITHMETIC. The graphic is 11 counted bays of a 22-bay face and no source stations it, so it is placed as near centre as an integer bay allows. It shipped as a prose derivation, which meant assertExprs never evaluated it and the station could be moved 3 bays with a differently-worded rule and every gate still passing (audit finding 1). As an expr over the face's own bay count and the panel count, a different rule now fails.

signageWall.bays.why: The pale signage wall replaces the glazing over the smallest whole number of bays that contains the sign's own measured 3.498 m width. Studio E's plan calls this element the SIGNAGE WALL and puts it outside the dining floor plate (§10.3), which is why the plan's east edge lands 2.2 m beyond the OSM ring.

system.mullion.width.why: A BY-PRODUCT OF THE PANEL COUNT, and a measurement rather than a stock size. The full-height vertical-line detector returns each storefront mullion as a PAIR of dark edges — the two sides of one frame profile — and the nine interior pairs are 7.6, 8.1, 7.8, 7.8, 7.9, 7.7, 7.8, 8.1 and 8.4 px apart, mean 7.911. That is the mullion's own face width. It is preferred to blake's 2 in stock-product class because this building actually measures it.

signageWall.firstBay.why: The signage wall is the declared number of bays IMMEDIATELY NORTH of the graphic. CORRECTED AT AUDIT — it shipped SOUTH of the graphic and the photographs say otherwise; see conflicts['sign-and-doors-hand'] and superseded['build.compassHand'].

entry.bay.why: One bay, immediately north of the signage wall, which is the adjacency the one orthographic frame resolves: sign and doors side by side at the same end of the face.

orthoFit.edgesZ.why: Three usable edges in z, at three different LiDAR heights spanning 5.0 to 9.9 m. This is the DISCRIMINATING axis and the only one the section rests a model claim on.
orthoFit.edgesZ.derivation: A COUNT of the usable z edges after exclusions, not arithmetic over a reading: commonsN, degreesN and northN, at LiDAR heights 7.5, 9.9 and 5.0. Three points at three heights are what makes the z axis able to separate a constant from a rate at all.

orthoFit.edgesX.why: TWO usable edges in x after the audit withdrew 64 North's west edge. Two observations cannot separate two one-parameter models — whichever fits better does so by construction — so the x axis is recorded as NON-DISCRIMINATING and its ratio is published only so that the weakness is visible rather than implied.
orthoFit.edgesX.derivation: A COUNT of the usable x edges after 64 North's west edge was withdrawn at audit: commonsW and degreesE. TWO points cannot separate two one-parameter models — whichever fits better does so by construction — which is why the x ratio is published as evidence of weakness rather than as corroboration.

orthoFit.antiHeightZ.why: THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SURVIVES ANY MODEL FIT. The 5.0 m block's z displacement as a fraction of the 9.9 m block's. A height-proportional model REQUIRES this to be 5.0/9.9 = 0.505; it measures 0.881. The 5.0 m block displaces nearly as much as the block twice its height, which is the single fact no height model can produce and it needs no fitting at all.

orthoFit.antiHeightPredicted.why: What a height-proportional model REQUIRES orthoFit.antiHeightZ to be. The gap between this and the measured ratio is the refutation, stated without reference to any fitted parameter.

graphic.centreOffsetBays.why: How far the graphic's centre sits from the face's centre, in bays. The centring rule can only ever leave it within half a bay of centre — 22 bays less 11 is odd, so exact centring is impossible — and this figure is what the estimate's band is written against.

band.blankNorth.why: The band between the plinth and the soffit on the 64 North block, derived from that block's own LiDAR height exactly as the Commons' glazing band is. It ships as BLANK PRECAST and NOT as glazing: glazing is program-bearing and both Studio E plans put back-of-house behind these faces, so asserting it would assert a program the sources contradict. The parapet, the soffit and the plinth are not program-bearing and the section's own retirement of revelle.absent[4] argues from frames 16/18/30/31/33 that the 1966 band runs round the complex unchanged.

face.northNorth.length.why: The chord length of this face on the DRAWN massing ring — the ring campus-massing.js extrudes, so the band closes against the mass on screen.

face.northWest.length.why: The chord length of this face on the DRAWN massing ring — the ring campus-massing.js extrudes, so the band closes against the mass on screen.

face.northEast.length.why: The chord length of this face on the DRAWN massing ring — the ring campus-massing.js extrudes, so the band closes against the mass on screen.

f33.pxPerMetre.why: The local scale of studioe-64degrees-33.jpg at the canopy's own depth, taken from the round column standing beside it: the column's top is the soffit underside and its foot is the paving, which is a length this section already derives from measured bands rather than reads off the frame. Using an object at the SAME depth is what makes an oblique dusk frame usable at all.

canopy.fall.why: How far the canopy's free edge hangs BELOW its attachment. A vertical drop is the one canopy dimension an oblique frame gives honestly: foreshortening compresses lengths along the wall and across the projection, but not heights.

canopy.attachHeight.derivation: The soffit's underside on this block — band.plinth + band.glazingDegrees, which is also columns.dgSouth.height — less the declared draw drop that keeps the fabric clear of the soffit plane it hangs from. The drop is a render clearance and lives in system.canopy.dropBelowSoffit.
canopy.attachHeight.why: The canopy attaches just under the soffit in all three frames and the soffit's height is already measured, so the attachment needs no new read.

canopy.outerHeight.why: The free edge's height above the block datum. It must stay well clear of head height, which the test asserts against the building code's own 80 in door leaf as the shortest thing in the section with a headroom meaning.

facade.moduleExtension.extends: the 64 Degrees EAST face's counted 11 glazing panels at 1.551709 m — the only counted rhythm anywhere in the cluster (§3.4)
facade.moduleExtension.why: [estimated] The east face's module is measured. Carrying it onto the south, north and Commons-south faces is an extension and is labelled one: no south frame is orthographic, the awning covers the entry bays, and the structural rhythm visible in the Studio E plans carries that drawing's own +/-1.5 m registration residual, which is a whole bay. Ladder climbed and failed: photos (all oblique), Street View (Revelle is pedestrian and no pano stands here), drone/video (nothing found), planning docs (the +/-1.5 m residual), archives (the 1960s aerials are obliques from the east and south).
facade.moduleExtension.bandWhy: The band is the east face's own six interior panel spacings, 107.30 px +/- 0.68 sd at 68.3235 px/m, widened to the nearest centimetre either side: [1.53, 1.58]. It is the measured scatter of the pattern being extended, not a comfort margin, and the value checked against it is the WIDEST bay any face ships so the whole population is inside.

system.columns.spacingBays.extends: the same face's own shipped bay, so a column lands on a mullion and the 1966 storefront can close against it
system.columns.spacingBays.why: [estimated] The colonnade's spacing is counted nowhere. Studio E frame 16 resolves two columns and no third, which is the whole of the evidence. Ladder: photos (frame 16 shows two, obliquely, at an unknown depth so no scale); Street View (none); drone/video (none); planning docs (the plans draw the structural grid but at +/-1.5 m, a whole bay); archives (nothing). Every rung fails, so the sourced bay module is extended by an integer multiple and LABELLED.
system.columns.spacingBays.bandWhy: Bounded by what frame 16 does show: at fewer than three bays a third column would fall inside the frame's own width and it does not, and at more than six the two visible columns could not both appear at the depth they do. The shipped 4 sits inside [3, 6] and the band is in BAYS, so it moves with each face's own surveyed length rather than fixing a metre value the survey would contradict.

system.columns.diameter.extends: nothing dimensional in this building measures it; the value is the research dossier's own eye-read of the same sourced frames, carried with its stated range
system.columns.diameter.why: [estimated] §5.2 reads the columns at 0.6-0.7 m diameter off the oblique south frames and no source narrows it. Ladder: photos (oblique, no scale at the columns' depth); Street View (none); drone/video (none); planning docs (the plans show the columns but the +/-1.5 m registration swamps a 0.65 m object); archives (none). Every rung fails.
system.columns.diameter.bandWhy: The band IS the published read, 0.6 to 0.7 m, taken verbatim rather than narrowed. The shipped 0.65 is its midpoint and is declared as a midpoint, not as a measurement; a frame that resolves the true diameter replaces the value and the band together.

system.graphic.centreOffsetBays.extends: the east face's own 22-bay fit and the counted 11 panels, within which the graphic must sit somewhere
system.graphic.centreOffsetBays.why: [estimated] The graphic's STATION along the east face is resolved by nothing — suffolk-Desktop-2_1 shows 21.1 m of a 33.9 m elevation. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos (the one orthographic frame does not reach either corner, and the dusk frame that DOES reach the south-east corner resolves the HAND but not the station); Street View (Revelle is pedestrian, no pano); drone/video (nothing found); planning docs (frame 9 draws the floor plate, not the elevation); archives (none). So a rule is adopted and stated, and what is banded is the rule's own freedom.
system.graphic.centreOffsetBays.bandWhy: NARROWED AT AUDIT from [0, 11], which was the complete feasible range and therefore could not exclude anything — audit finding 1 moved the station 3 bays inside it with every gate passing. The band is now the actual freedom the CENTRING RULE has: centring 11 bays in 22 cannot be exact because 22 - 11 is odd, so the graphic's centre must land within half a bay of the face's centre, and [-0.5, 0.5] is that and nothing more. A station chosen by any other rule leaves this band.

system.canopy.bays.extends: the same face's own shipped bay, which is the rhythm this section already extends for the colonnade
system.canopy.bays.why: [estimated] The canopy's WIDTH is not measurable off any frame: all three that show it are oblique, and foreshortening along the wall is exactly the direction the width runs. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos (three frames, all oblique, none reaching both ends of the canopy); Street View (Revelle is pedestrian, no pano); drone/video (nothing found); planning docs (the plans draw the floor plate, not the canopy); archives (none). So the width is a whole number of the face's own bays and is banded.
system.canopy.bays.bandWhy: Bounded by what the frames DO show. Below 4 bays (6.2 m) the canopy could not span the entry group it shelters in frame 33, where it plainly covers more than the doorway and the bay either side. Above 12 bays (18.6 m) it would reach more than two thirds of the 29.4 m face and would run past the round column that stands clear of it at the west in frames 18 and 33. The shipped 8 is the midpoint of that bracket and is declared as a midpoint.

system.canopy.projection.extends: the canopy's own measured fall of 2.443 m, which sets the slope any credible projection has to make
system.canopy.projection.why: [estimated] How far the canopy projects OUT over the terrace. This is the second direction an oblique frame foreshortens, so it is estimated rather than read. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos (all three oblique); Street View (none); drone/video (none); planning docs (the site plan names the awning and does not dimension it); archives (none).
system.canopy.projection.bandWhy: Bounded by the measured fall of 2.443 m. At a 2.5 m projection the fabric pitches at 44 degrees, steeper than any frame shows; at 5.0 m it is 26 degrees, shallower than frame 33's silhouette against the lit soffit. The shipped 3.5 m gives 35 degrees and sits mid-band. A drone frame or a section drawing replaces the value and the band together.

reads.band.edges: The five band boundaries are 50%-luminance crossings between local plateaus, and glazingToPlinth is a 50% crossing of row texture. Repeat reads of the same joint with different plateau windows move the edge by under 0.5 px, i.e. a tolerance of +/-0.007 m at 68.32 px/m. The sky-to-parapet joint is the loosest: the sky is blown out and JPEG bloom spreads the ramp over 7 px, so that one edge carries +/-1.5 px, tolerance +/-0.022 m.
reads.graphic.panelCount: ELEVEN, a COUNT, and counts are foreshortening-immune, which is the B3 lesson. The vertical-line detector returns the mullions as PAIRS 7.8 px apart (the two edges of one frame profile) and the twelve pair-centres span 1166.2 px; the dossier's independent read of the same frame gave 1166 px. Tolerance on the span +/-1 px, on the count zero.
reads.ortho.edges: Each roof edge is the strongest luminance gradient in a +/-2.6 m window with a parabolic sub-pixel fit; repeat reads with windows from +/-2.0 to +/-3.0 m move an edge by under 0.1 px, tolerance +/-0.013 m. Five of the six originally read reproduce to 2 cm against an independent audit reimplementation. THE SIXTH DID NOT and is withdrawn rather than re-picked — see absent for 64 North's west roof edge. The rule as stated does not disambiguate a dark stripe with bright surface on both sides, and the honest response to an edge the rule cannot describe is to drop it, not to choose a branch.
reads.sign.bbox: The saturation mask (R>150, R-B>70, G between R and B) is stable within one implementation: moving the R-B threshold from 60 to 85 moves the bounding box by at most 3 px. ACROSS implementations it is looser — an independent audit reimplementation with connected-component labelling returned 19,041 px against 19,066 and x1 = 1222 against 1229, so the honest tolerance on an edge is +/-7 px, 0.10 m, which is 3% of the sign's 3.498 m width. Its FOOT is the tight end and the reason the reading matters: row 631 in both implementations, against a plinth-top line independently read at 632.96, 0.029 m apart.
reads.column.diameter: Not measured here at all — carried from the research dossier's eye-read of the oblique south frames with its stated 0.6-0.7 m range as the tolerance, and banded as an estimate rather than promoted to a figure. The band ENDPOINTS are pinned as literals in the test against that published range, so the band cannot be widened to admit a larger value (audit finding 5 inflated the diameter 31% by widening its own band).
reads.graphic.tone: Median #6f6f6f and mean #6f6c69 over 468,236 pixels of the graphic panel agree to three units per channel, tolerance +/-3, which is what says the printed image is neutral greyscale rather than toned. The sd of 44.3 is the photograph's own content and is not a read error.
reads.transom.bar: The transom presents as a BRIGHT bar against the graphic in the declared strip: baseline L 99.6, peak L 130.3 at y 479, half-max crossings at y 477.50 and y 480.81. Its edges are those crossings, tolerance +/-0.3 px on each, and its centre reproduces an independent read to 0.15 px. The section's original 'two dark edges' reading is retired in absent[].

draw.wallOffsetNote: A render offset, not a dimension: how far each band plane stands proud of the drawn ring's chord so it reads against the massing prism instead of z-fighting it. Nothing in the building measures it.
draw.mullionProudNote: A render offset: how far the storefront mullions stand outward of the glazing plane so they frame it rather than z-fight it. Blake's draw.storefrontProud, for the same reason.
draw.graphicProudNote: A render offset: the blank graphic panel sits this far proud of the plain glazing plane so the eleven panels read as a distinct object. It decides no dimension.
draw.signProudNote: A render offset expressing a SOURCED fact — suffolk-Desktop-2_1 shows the 3-D sign standing free in front of the signage wall — whose magnitude nothing measures.
draw.columnProudNote: A render offset: the columns stand FREE at the roof edge, outboard of the glazing line, and this is how far. It is set just past half the estimated 0.65 m diameter so the shaft clears the wall plane; §5.2 says they stand free and measures nothing about how far.
draw.skirtDepthNote: A render depth, not a measurement: how far below the lowest drawn surface along a face the plinth is carried, so a rolling terrain cannot open a gap under the facade. Pulse's draw.buryDepth, same purpose.
draw.seatEmbedNote: A render tolerance: the float slack below which a run is treated as zero-length and skipped, and the amount by which a seated object is embedded so a shared plane does not shimmer.
draw.courtRungNote: A NAME, not a number — the campus-overlay.js rung the courtyard floor decal rides, so it paints over the measured terrain in the repo's fixed order instead of z-fighting it. The module reads overlayLift(D.courtRung) and never a local constant.
draw.tilesNote: Texture repeat scales in metres for the procedural material library — code-generated microstructure at true panel, board and pane scale. They are render parameters, not claims about panel sizes; the one real panel dimension this section has is bay.module and it is a figure.
draw.signDepthNote: A render depth, not a measurement: how thick the blank sign plate is drawn. The sign is 3-D letters on standoffs and its WIDTH and HEIGHT are measured from a saturation mask, but nothing in any frame resolves how far the letters project, so the third dimension is declared here as a draw parameter rather than smuggled in as a figure.
draw.columnJitterNote: A render irregularity, not a dimension: the metres of deterministic outward lean each column is given, from hash(seed, ...), so a hand-set 1966 colonnade does not read as extruded. Bounded at 0.02 m, which is a fifth of the mullion width and far below anything a source could resolve.
draw.canopyOpacityNote: A render parameter, not a measurement: how much of the strut lattice and the wall behind shows through the tensioned fabric. The canopy IS translucent — that is the whole argument of conflicts['canopy-epoch'], which is why it reads silver in daylight and dark at dusk — and drawn opaque it becomes a slab with its radiating frame hidden behind it. Nothing in any frame measures a transmittance, so this is declared here as a draw value rather than smuggled in as a figure.

facades.source: 64 DEGREES EAST. The best-documented face in the cluster and the one that carries the whole §2.2 derivation chain: suffolk-Desktop-2_1-UCSD-64-degrees-3.jpg is near-orthographic, daylight and straight-on, and every band figure in this section is read off it.

64 DEGREES SOUTH. Seven oblique frames (Studio E 16, 18, 22, 30, 31, 33 and suffolk-Desktop-1_1). Materials, objects and the continuity of the band stack are sourced here; not one dimension is, so every metre on this face is carried from the east by count.

64 DEGREES NORTH. NO PHOTOGRAPH EXISTS in any of the five sets. The site plan (Studio E frame 7) labels this frontage DEMONSTRATION KITCHEN / FIRE PLACE / TERRACE SEATING / MEDIA ROOM / DINING ENTRY, which is a public dining frontage and not back-of-house, so the same building's own sourced band system is extended across it and LABELLED [estimated]. Its bay count and every opening stay withheld — see absent['degrees-north-openings'].

REVELLE COMMONS SOUTH. The colonnade frontage. Studio E frames 16, 18, 30, 31, 33 show the 1966 parapet band and the 2014 soffit running west from the 64 Degrees block across this face unchanged, which is the evidence that lets the parapet, soffit and plinth keep their measured values on a 7.5 m block.

64 NORTH's NORTH face. NO PHOTOGRAPH exists in any of the five sets. Ships the building's own non-program-bearing bands — parapet, soffit, plinth and a blank precast band between them — as a LABELLED [estimated] extension, per the audit ruling. Its glazing, its openings and its bay count stay withheld in absent[] because glazing is program-bearing and both plans put back-of-house here.

64 NORTH's WEST face. NO PHOTOGRAPH. Same treatment and the same withholding as its north face. This is also the face whose ortho roof edge was withdrawn from the displacement fit at audit — bright surface on both sides of a 0.5 m dark stripe — and the 2.3 m GIS/OSM disagreement about where this wall is sits exactly there.

64 NORTH's EAST face — the 1966 PLAZA CAFE frontage. ONE frame exists, UCOP 2008 Regents deck p11, and it is a DEAD COLOUR EPOCH: it shows the exposed-aggregate panel wall still standing behind the 2014 work and not one plan dimension, and its colours are 2008. Geometry epoch only, so the same [estimated] band extension ships and no colour is taken from it.

revellecommons.facadesNote: Four faces of the ten external runs the cluster has. The other six are declared in absent[] with their ladders climbed and failed, which is the ultra standard's second sanctioned option and not a silence. Each face's a and b are VERTICES of the drawn ring; the ring carries collinear intermediate vertices along three of the four and the test asserts they are collinear to 0.10 m rather than ignoring them.

bands.note: Bottom to top: plinth, glazing, soffit, parapet. The stack hangs UPWARD from each block's own drawn surface — §0.1's option (2) — so every sourced dimension keeps its measured value and the residue is one honest band of bare mass per block rather than a silent stretch applied to every figure. On the 64 NORTH block the band between plinth and soffit is BLANK PRECAST rather than glazing, derived the same way from that block's own LiDAR height — see band.blankNorth and absent['north-block-glazing'].

bay.moduleNote: GENERATOR NOMINAL, not a shipped dimension. It is the divisor each face's own whole-bay fit uses; the bay actually built is face.bay and it differs from the nominal on all four faces (1.541, 1.547, 1.542, 1.564). Declaring the nominal as the shipped bay is the defect blake's bayModuleNote was written against.

transom.note: One horizontal bar per treated face of the 64 DEGREES block only, at the measured height above that block's plinth top. It is NOT carried onto the Commons south face: the Commons' glazing band is a derived 3.762 m and no frame resolves a transom in it. See absent['commons-transom'].

graphic.note: The eleven counted panels ship as a BLANK panel carrying the graphic's own measured area-average tone. The printed black-and-white surf photograph itself is RESOLVED BUT UNRENDERABLE — there is no image mechanism in this renderer and none is invented, exactly as Argo's mural is recorded. Texture maps here are code-generated; no photo pixel becomes a texture.

sign.note: The 3-D yellow 64-degree sign ships as BLANK GEOMETRY at its measured bounding size, standing proud of the signage wall with its foot on the plinth top. The letterforms are not built and no text mechanism is invented — absent['lettering'].

signageWall.note: A pale concrete wall replacing the glazing over the bays the sign stands against, immediately NORTH of the graphic. Studio E's plans name this element the SIGNAGE WALL and place it OUTSIDE the dining floor plate (Section 10.3), which is why frame 9's east edge lands 2.2 m beyond the OSM ring. CORRECTED AT AUDIT — this note previously read <<immediately south of the graphic>>, which was the shipped hand and is reversed; see conflicts['sign-and-doors-hand'] and superseded['build.compassHand']. Retired wording is carried in delimiters so the correction stays legible without the note asserting it.

entry.note: One pair of glazed leaves in the bay immediately NORTH of the signage wall — the adjacency suffolk-Desktop-2_1 actually shows, sign and doors side by side at the same end of the face. Leaf sizes are stock product dimensions in whole inches, the blake product.doorLeafIn class. CORRECTED AT AUDIT on two counts. The hand: this note previously read <<immediately south of the signage wall>>. And an assertion that is now RETRACTED — it claimed research Section 5.1's north-end reading <<is contradicted by that frame>>. IT IS NOT. The elevation frame fixes the ADJACENCY of sign to doors and says nothing about the compass hand; the dusk frame that reaches the south-east corner puts the whole group at the NORTH end, which is what Section 5.1 said all along. See conflicts['sign-and-doors-hand'].

columns.note: Stout round exposed-aggregate columns standing FREE at the roof edge on both south faces, carrying the soffit. Built as plain cylinders: §5.2's flared/tapered top is real and visible in frame 16 but nothing measures the flare, so it is recorded and not built — absent['column-flare'].

canopy.note: The light translucent tensioned-fabric canopy on its radiating strut frame over the south entry — one of the six things 2014 added outside. BUILT AT VISUAL AUDIT, having shipped `built: false`. The withholding's ground was that the ENTRY's station along the face is unresolved, and that ground is now too broad: the critic ruled a building-mounted element is not covered by the withheld terrace landscape, and three frames agree on which END of the face it sits at. So it ships on a stated rule with the station banded, not on a coordinate: it stops `endClearBays` short of the face's EAST end and runs `bays` bays west from there. Its FALL is measured; its projection and width are estimates inside published bands. See conflicts['canopy-epoch'] for why frames 16, 18 and 33 are one object and not two.

fasciaSign.note: The applied 3-D yellow 64-degree letters on the brown fascia band above the south entry, on standoffs. BUILT AT VISUAL AUDIT as BLANK GEOMETRY at the same measured bounding size as the east sign — the two are the same wordmark at the same size in frames 16, 18 and 33, and the east one is the one with an orthographic frame to measure. It is centred over the canopy, which is where all three frames put it. No letterform is drawn and no text mechanism is invented; that limitation is unchanged and stays in absent['lettering'].

mullion.note: Dark anodised aluminium storefront mullion, one on every bay boundary of every treated face, both ends included. Its face width is measured (see the figure) and not taken from a stock table.

court.note: The floor and NOTHING else. Four sources put this court in the same 9.7 x 9.4 m place to +/-1.5 m and arcgis.ground#3267 types it as a `walk`, so it is paved; LiDAR terrain inside it reads 24.0 against 23.8 outside, i.e. at grade. Its four WALLS have no photograph in any source found — Studio E's 25 frames never enter it and the plan labels it without drawing it — so they ship bare rather than wearing the exterior's language into a room no source has seen. The ortho's dark L wrapping its south and east is not consistent with any San Diego sun position and is therefore probably not shadow; at 0.125 m/px that is as far as the imagery goes. See absent['courtyard-faces'].

parapetBand.source: [measured] Median of a 151 x 61 px rectangle at x 1310..1460, y 50..110 of studioe-64degrees-16.jpg (1500x1000, Studio E Architects / Hewitt-Garrison, the 2014 project photography) — a SUNLIT, frontal, unshaded run of the 1966 precast band, sd 6.8. A second rectangle at x 1060..1210, y 150..235 on the same band gives #9e8a74 at sd 19.4; the two bracket the incident-angle spread across a faceted precast face and the tighter one ships. This is the 2014-epoch fabric, not a repaint: §3.3 establishes there was no re-clad.

column.source: [measured] Median of a 26 x 41 px rectangle at x 1130..1155, y 430..470 of studioe-64degrees-16.jpg (1500x1000, Studio E Architects / Hewitt-Garrison, the 2014 project photography), on the sunlit patch of the free-standing round exposed-aggregate column below the soffit shadow, sd 14.5. The sd is the aggregate's own grain at this scale and not mixed content.

courtPaving.source: [measured] Median of a 401 x 28 px rectangle at x 350..750, y 863..890 of studioe-64degrees-16.jpg (1500x1000, Studio E Architects / Hewitt-Garrison, the 2014 project photography), on unshaded tan exposed-aggregate terrace paving, sd 6.3 — the tightest sample in the set. arcgis.ground#3267 types the courtyard floor as a `walk`, so the court is paved and this is the project's own 2014 paving tone.

soffit.source: [sourced] Median of a 151 x 61 px rectangle at x 1210..1360, y 190..250 of studioe-64degrees-16.jpg (1500x1000, Studio E Architects / Hewitt-Garrison, the 2014 project photography), sd 5.1. Tiered [sourced] and not [measured] for a stated reason: a soffit is self-shaded by definition and there is no frame anywhere in which this surface is sunlit, so the sample is the material under sky illumination and its true albedo is higher. The blake ruling that a full-shade sample is not a material is honoured by the tier, not by discarding the read.

storefrontGlass.source: [sourced] Median of a 146 x 76 px rectangle at x 1325..1470, y 285..360 of studioe-64degrees-16.jpg (1500x1000, Studio E Architects / Hewitt-Garrison, the 2014 project photography), on the clerestory glazing above the canopy, sd 14.3. Glass has no albedo of its own — this is what the 2014 storefront returns against a shaded interior — so it is [sourced] and never [measured].

mullion.source: [sourced] Median of a 9 x 88 px column at x 1302..1310, y 278..365 of studioe-64degrees-16.jpg (1500x1000, Studio E Architects / Hewitt-Garrison, the 2014 project photography), on one dark-anodised aluminium storefront mullion, sd 17.2. A 9 px sample is at the resolution floor and the tier says so.

signYellow.source: [sourced] Median of a 27 x 39 px rectangle at x 836..862, y 398..436 of studioe-64degrees-16.jpg (1500x1000, Studio E Architects / Hewitt-Garrison, the 2014 project photography), on the lit face of one stroke of the 3-D yellow 64-degree sign, sd 34.5. That sd is the letterform's OWN lit and shaded faces, not mixed content — a 3-D letter on standoffs has both in any one rectangle — and it is why this is [sourced] rather than [measured]. ONE rectangle only: the second candidate frame is the east elevation, and no hex is taken from it because it is entirely in shade.

graphicPanel.source: [sourced] The AREA-AVERAGE of the printed surf graphic itself, over the whole 1159 x 404 px panel run at x 235..1393, y 225..628 of suffolk-Desktop-2_1-UCSD-64-degrees-3.jpg (2014 fabric on a 2023 page — see conflicts). sd 44.3 over those 468,236 px, which is the PHOTOGRAPH'S OWN CONTENT and not a read error — the check that matters here is that median #6f6f6f and mean #6f6c69 agree to three units per channel, which independently confirms FE&S's description of a black-and-white photograph. The graphic ships as a BLANK panel carrying this one tone; the image is recorded as unrenderable in absent['graphic-image'] and no photo pixel becomes a texture.

plinth.source: [estimated] No frame anywhere shows the plinth band sunlit — the whole east elevation is in shade (see absent['east-face-colours']) and the south frames catch the plinth behind planting and furniture. This extends the smooth pale cast concrete sampled on the terrace seat wall at x 40..200, y 812..846 of studioe-64degrees-16.jpg (1500x1000, Studio E Architects / Hewitt-Garrison, the 2014 project photography), sd 14.7, which is the same material class laid by the same 2014 contract. Extension is labelled, not promoted.

signageWall.source: [estimated] Extends the same seat-wall concrete sample as `plinth`, for the same reason: the signage wall appears only in the shaded east elevation. Recorded as a distinct role rather than aliased to `plinth` because the two are different elements and a future frame may separate them.

canopyFabric.source: [sourced] Median of a 101 x 51 px rectangle at x 1230..1330, y 430..480 of studioe-64degrees-16.jpg (1500x1000, Studio E Architects / Hewitt-Garrison, the 2014 project photography), on the upper face of the tensioned-fabric canopy, sd 9.9 over 5,151 px. Tiered [sourced] and not [measured] for the same stated reason storefrontGlass is: a TRANSLUCENT surface has no albedo of its own — what this rectangle records is what the fabric transmits and reflects under a soffit, which is why its channel mean of 65.4 sits far below the sunlit bar. Two independent reads agree: this rectangle is the round-2 critic's, and an earlier rectangle taken by this build at x 1200..1265, y 450..490 returns #3e3e44 at channel mean 66.2, two units away. The LOWER sail reads #5d554b at 91.9, but at sd 25.8 against this rectangle's 9.9, because that region carries the struts, the ghost graphic and the wall behind them; the tight upper rectangle is the one sample of the fabric alone.

revellecommons.colorNote: Every hex is sampled by this build from a named cached frame with its sample rectangle, its pixel count and its standard deviation recorded in colorSources, and EVERY ROLE THE MODULE ASKS FOR IS DECLARED HERE — see absent['canopy-colour-white'] for the round-2 defect that rule exists to prevent — none is carried from the research dossier, which guessed none and required exactly this. THE EAST ELEVATION IS IN SHADE and that is measured, not assumed: sunlit paving in suffolk-Desktop-2_1 reads #d3c2a7 while the parapet band 600 px above it reads #554939, a factor of 2.5, and the band additionally runs #423b2e to #5c4e3b across the frame's width. So NO hex is taken from that frame's fabric — the dossier's §6 names it for four of its rows and all four are refused. The one thing sourced from it is the graphic's neutral area-average, which is a tone and not an albedo. No hex is sampled from a raw Apple pixel; the 1.25 m georegistration offset is still unresolved and this cluster's own ortho registration is worse.

colorFallback.note: Empty by construction. This section borrows no hex from a sibling — the R1 blake/argo borrowing was justified by a same-repaint-programme premise that blake's own work later refuted, and nothing here repeats it. A role with no sample is declared in absent[], not filled from a neighbour.

counts.note: Declared here and asserted equal to what the module builds. `blankBands` is the 64 North block's three faces, which carry the non-program-bearing bands and a derived blank precast panel where the glazed blocks carry glazing — so they have no bay, no mullion and no transom, and `mullions` and `glazingPanels` are unchanged by them. `glazingPanels` counts one panel per plain bay PLUS the transom-height panel that closes the entry bay above its door leaves, so no bay anywhere is left as a hole. `pv` and `roofObjects` are ZERO and are declared rather than omitted: the Keeling control returns negative on this cluster (no ballasted tilt rows, nothing at 2.0-2.3 m pitch), and every roof object §7 reads off the ortho would have to stand on a plane 1.4-6.3 m inside solid drawn mass. `canopies` is ONE fabric panel and `canopyStruts` its radiating frame at the declared bay interval; `fasciaSigns` is the south wordmark as blank geometry, the twin of `signPlates` on the east face.

conflicts.what: THE CLUSTER'S GOVERNING CONFLICT. This is ONE single-storey building with THREE roof planes, and the drawn world contains ONE prism closed at a single height over all three. campus-massing.js extrudes the GIS mass and closes it at massHeights['m:-100,359'] = 11.3 m, which is a p98 over a plate containing all three blocks AND the Commons rooftop mechanical yard.
sides: LiDAR 2014, per named mass: 64 Degrees 9.9 m, Revelle Commons 7.5 m, 64 North 5.0 m. Terrain under the whole cluster is flat at 23.8 m, so these are also absolute roof levels of 33.7 / 31.3 / 28.8 m.
The drawn prism: massHeights['m:-100,359'] = 11.3 m, lid at 35.1 m. Against the three real roofs that is +1.4 m on 64 Degrees, +3.8 m on the Commons and +6.3 m on 64 North.
arcgis.h = 8.5 is NOT admitted as a third opinion. It is 2 x 4.25, a formula over a levels field of 2 that §3.1 disproves, and a formula is not a measurement.
conflicts.resolution: NOT AVERAGED. §0.1's option (2) is taken: every band hangs UPWARD from each block's own drawn surface to that block's own LiDAR height, so every sourced dimension keeps its measured value, and the residue is declared as one bare band of undressed mass per block — 1.4 m on 64 Degrees (1.528 m measured against the treatment's own top), 3.8 m on the Commons, 6.3 m on 64 North. Option (1), hanging the bands DOWNWARD from the drawn lid, was rejected because it makes every figure 1.4-6.3 m wrong to buy visibility. Option (3), shipping nothing, remains the fallback if a critic rejects (2). The residue is not painted over and nothing is drawn on it.

conflicts.what: THE LOCAL RE-FIT §15 ITEM 2 DEMANDS, AND IT REFUTES THE FIGURE IT WAS ASKED TO CHECK. The research dossier corrects 2026-ortho roof edges for top displacement using a rate of (+0.0497, +0.2021) m per metre of height, imported from Argo's four-feature fit 40-75 m east and never fitted locally. Five roof edges on this cluster's own corners were measured here to test it; a sixth was measured, found not to meet the section's own edge criterion, and withdrawn at audit.
sides: THE IMPORTED HEIGHT-PROPORTIONAL MODEL: displacement scales with height. On the three usable z edges it leaves rms 0.376 m, worst 0.624 m. It is corroborated on exactly the two edges the dossier itself used (Commons N and 64 Degrees N) and fails on the third, which the dossier did not use.
A LOCALLY FITTED HEIGHT-PROPORTIONAL MODEL in z, rate 0.2166: rms 0.359 m. Refitting the rate barely helps, which is the diagnostic.
A CONSTANT OFFSET in z, -1.709 m: rms 0.103 m — better by a factor of 3.48 over three edges at three heights spanning 5.0 to 9.9 m.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT NEEDS NO FIT AT ALL: the 5.0 m block's z displacement is 0.881 of the 9.9 m block's. A height-proportional model REQUIRES 0.505. The short block displaces nearly as much as the block twice its height.

THE X AXIS IS NON-DISCRIMINATING AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH. After 64 North's west edge was withdrawn at audit it has only TWO usable edges, and two observations cannot separate two one-parameter models — the rate 'wins' there at a ratio of 0.791 purely by construction. The shipped claim that 'the two axes agree' was rhetorically stronger than the evidence and is withdrawn; the refutation rests on z.
conflicts.resolution: NOT AVERAGED. The measurement says the displacement on this cluster is not height-proportional: a constant beats a rate by 3.48x on the discriminating axis, and the fit-free diagnostic (0.881 against a required 0.505) refutes the rate without reference to any fitted parameter. CONSEQUENCE, AND ITS GROUND WAS CORRECTED AT AUDIT. The shipped ground was an analogy to CLAUDE.md's 1.25 m Apple offset, and that analogy was BACKWARDS: CLAUDE.md quarantines the Apple offset because it is UNRESOLVED and names the remedy as 'until a fitted registration passes gate' — and a fitted registration is precisely what this section produced. The correct ground is narrower and it is about COVERAGE, not magnitude: the fit is constrained by NORTH edges and by east/west edges, and BOTH SOUTH EDGES ARE EXCLUDED for a measured reason (no luminance step against bright terrace paving; a wall shadow line rather than a roof edge). So the constant is fitted 30-50 m north of the south terrace and is untested exactly where the terrace is. That is why no ortho-derived position ships on the south side. The roofscape's withholding does not depend on this at all — see absent['roofscape'], whose second ground is that the objects would stand 1.4-3.8 m inside solid drawn mass.

conflicts.what: The GIS massing ring and the OSM rings disagree about where this building's walls are, by 2-3 m on the north, east and south. This is the reverse of the usual precedence and it is measured rather than asserted.
sides: OSM is the building. Its Commons roof width in x is 44.3 m against an ortho-measured 44.32 m — exact to 2 cm — and on six of seven edges it beats GIS against the corrected ortho. GIS's east run for the Commons is 2.6 m out on its own.

GIS is what RENDERS. campus-massing.js extrudes massing[96] and suppresses the OSM rings underneath, so a facade hung on the OSM line would float 2-3 m inside or outside the mass the eye sees. GIS is also right about the one thing OSM misses entirely: the courtyard.
conflicts.resolution: NOT AVERAGED and NOT SNAPPED. Every facade in this section hangs off two VERTICES OF THE DRAWN GIS RING, so nothing floats and nothing z-fights, and the face lengths in derivations.figures are the drawn ring's own chords. What is NOT done is the thing §0.3 forbids: no sourced dimension is stretched onto the GIS ring. The sourced 1.551709 m module is applied by COUNT — a whole number of bays against each drawn face length — so the 2-3 m of inflation lands in a 0.01-0.02 m per-bay difference that is declared per face, rather than in a distorted module. Blake's per-face fit, ruled legitimate in R2 stage 7.

conflicts.what: The east graphic's height has three readings clustering between 19.8 and 22 feet, and the discrepancy is 10% rather than a rounding.
sides: FE&S 2015-02-01, published: '56-foot-wide, 22-foot-high'. The width half of this same sentence is what scales the entire elevation, so the source is not in doubt.
MEASURED HERE off the same frame the width scales: the glazing band is 6.034 m = 19.80 ft, 2.2 ft short.
Eric Naslund, quoted in Bisnow 2015-01-12, on the room behind it: 'The original hall had 22-foot-high ceilings'. FE&S says 20 ft for the same room in the same year.
conflicts.resolution: NOT AVERAGED and NOT RECONCILED BY RESCALING. The camera stands below mid-height so the top of the elevation foreshortens, which is the likely cause and is not quantified by anything available. The WIDTH is used as the scale and the height is left as the independent check it is — a check the section reports as failing by 10% rather than one it tunes away. The shipped glazing band is the MEASURED 6.034 m, because that is what closes the stack against LiDAR to 1.3%; the published 22 ft is recorded in system.graphic.heightFt and drawn by nothing.

conflicts.what: The east face's glazing module can be read as a counted 1.551709 m or as a round imperial 5 ft, and the two differ by 1.8%.
sides: COUNTED: 17.0688 m over 11 panels = 1.551709 m. The eleven is a count off a near-orthographic frame and counts are foreshortening-immune.
ROUND 5 FT = 1.524 m. Eleven of those is 55.0 ft against the published 56 ft, a 1.8% residual — close enough to be tempting and not close enough to be right.
conflicts.resolution: THE COUNT WINS and the 5 ft hypothesis is recorded as the loser. The count is the evidence; the round number is a hypothesis about the evidence. Specifically REFUSED: 'fixing' the count to 12 panels so that 56 / 12 = 4 ft 8 in comes out round. Twelve mullion centres were located independently here by a full-height vertical-line detector and there are eleven panels between them.

conflicts.what: How many storeys this building has above grade — which decides whether arcgis.h means anything here, because that field is the levels count times a formula and is the only source claiming a second level.
sides: campus-arcgis.json massing[96] says levels: 2, and its h of 8.5 is that number times a 4.25 m formula.

FE&S 2015-02-01 and School Construction News 2015-05-06 both describe 'approximately 27,000 sq ft of the 33,500-sq-ft, SINGLE-STORY building', plus separate infrastructure work in a 4,000 sq ft mechanical basement. Studio E's own two floor plans draw one level.
conflicts.resolution: GIS LOSES. There is one storey above grade and a mechanical basement below. Nothing in this section reads arcgis.h or arcgis.levels for any purpose; every height comes from LiDAR. The interior heights that set the parapet corroborate it — a 20-22 ft big box in the east and 10 ft in the west section, and that west 10 ft against the Commons' 7.5 m LiDAR is what leaves the 4.4 m the rooftop mechanical yard occupies and why massHeights reads 11.3.

conflicts.what: The year the Revelle Commons was built, which two independent kinds of source answer differently and neither of which this section depends on.
sides: modernsandiego.com lists 'Revelle College Commons (1964)', crediting Robert Evans Alexander as architect.
Every 2015 trade source describing the renovation says the Revelle Dining Commons was BUILT 1966. Calisphere holds a Charles H. Graves photograph of it dated October 1966.
conflicts.resolution: BOTH STAND, NOT COLLAPSED. Design or commission versus completion is the likely reading and no source says so. Nothing in this section depends on which is right: the fabric it dresses is dated by the 2014 photography and the 2014 LiDAR, and 'the 1966 building' is used throughout only as a name for the pre-2014 structure.

conflicts.what: Four published areas for this building disagree by a factor of 1.34, and nothing says which basis each is on.
sides: CEQA 2008101108, 'Revelle College Apartments and Commons Dining Renovation', received 2008-10-21: 25,183 gsf.
FE&S and School Construction News, 2015: 33,500 sq ft single-storey plus a 4,000 sq ft mechanical basement, of which approximately 27,000 sq ft was renovated.
Randall Lamb and Architizer: 25,000 SF, described as foodservice-assigned.
conflicts.resolution: THE SURVEY ADJUDICATES ONE OF THEM AND THAT RECONCILIATION SHIPS. The OSM union — ring 397 and ring 409, with ring 436 counted ONCE because 397 already contains it — is 3,165 m2 = 34,070 sq ft, which lands on FE&S's 33,500 within 1.7%. So 33,500 sq ft is the GROSS FOOTPRINT and the survey confirms it. The 25,000-25,183 readings are assignable or foodservice-assigned area and are left as that, unaveraged.

conflicts.what: There is a ~2.0 m wide gap between the Revelle Commons block and the 64 Degrees block, running the full 34 m depth of the east arm, and the drawn GIS mass bridges straight through it.
sides: OSM draws two rings with a gap: ring 397's east edge at x -95.2 and ring 409's west edge at x -93.1, a 2.1 m slot.

The 2026 ortho reads a clean 2.0 m dark slot between two bright membranes over the same run, and the 2.4 m height step between the two blocks (9.9 against 7.5) makes a continuous roof plane impossible there — a valley is forced.
The GIS ring's segment from (-92.6, 395.8) to (-92.7, 378.9) runs straight across it. That 16.9 m run is the inflation and is not a face of anything.
conflicts.resolution: DECLARED, NOT MODELLED. campus-massing.js:826 pushes only rings AFTER THE FIRST into shape.holes; this slot is not a ring but the space between two rings GIS merged into one, so unlike Argo's and Blake's courtyards the extruder cannot recover it and it will never appear. Modelling it would mean inventing a subtraction the extruder fights. Whether it is open to the sky or a lower link roof in shadow the ortho at 0.125 m/px cannot tell, and both plans show enclosed floor beneath it; the honest reading is roof-level separation, enclosed at grade. Both the answer and the object are withheld — absent['the-slot'].

conflicts.what: Which end of the 64 Degrees east face carries the entry doors, the signage wall and the freestanding sign. The section shipped them at the SOUTH end and the audit overturned it; this records both readings and the evidence that decided between them.
sides: THE SHIPPED READING, NOW WITHDRAWN: the group at the SOUTH end. Its only basis was that suffolk-Desktop-2_1 shows the sign to the RIGHT of the graphic together with an unstated assumption that the frame's right hand is south. That assumption was never evidenced and it was wrong.
RESEARCH §5.1 AND THE PHOTOGRAPHS: the group at the NORTH end. §5.1 places the glazed entry doors at the north end, and two independent reads confirm it.

READ 1, THE SOUTH-EAST CORNER. suffolk-Desktop-1_1-UCSD-64-Degrees.jpg is a dusk aerial of the south face whose right edge turns the corner onto the EAST face at the block's SOUTH-EAST corner. The two glazing panels visible there carry pale foaming wave crest over darker water — the content of the elevation's LEFT end (x 231..500 of suffolk-Desktop-2_1) — and NOT the yellow sign, the pale signage wall or the glazed doors, which occupy the elevation's right end (x 1127..1397). If the group sat at the south end it would be the first thing visible round that corner. It is not. Therefore elevation-left is SOUTH and the group is NORTH.

READ 2, THE APPROACH. The 2026 ortho shows the southern two thirds of the east face fronting a ~5.6 m shadowed service alley between this block and Blake, while the northern end opens onto a tan paved terrace. A main dining entry belongs on the terrace, not in the alley.
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED FOR THE NORTH END, and the section's own override is reversed. The adjacency of sign to doors was always right and is unchanged; what was wrong was the compass hand, which the section had inferred from an unevidenced assumption about which way the elevation frame faces while simultaneously declaring the hand withheld. Declaring a thing withheld and shipping a definite answer to it is the defect, not the answer. The geometry now places the signage wall and the entry NORTH of the graphic, gated in world coordinates (the built sign's z must be north of the graphic's, so a mirrored build fails), and the reversal is recorded in superseded['build.compassHand']. STILL WITHHELD, and separately: the graphic's STATION along the face — the corner frame resolves which END the group is at and fixes nothing about how far along the face the graphic starts.

conflicts.what: The frame that carries this section's entire derivation chain is published on a page about a project seven years younger than the frame.
sides: Suffolk Construction's page describes its own market fit-out with Amazon Just Walk Out, size 5,000 sq ft, delivered after September 2023, with HGW Architecture.

The exteriors that page illustrates itself with show the 2014 Studio E work: the printed surf graphic, the 3-D yellow sign, the deep cantilevered soffit and the 1966 parapet band, all as the Studio E frames show them in 2014.
conflicts.resolution: BOTH FACTS ARE REAL AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT YEARS. The 2023 Suffolk project is interior and changes no massing and no elevation. The two suffolk-Desktop exteriors are cited throughout this section as 2014 FABRIC on a 2023 page, and the reason is recorded here rather than left for a reader to notice. The epoch matters because it is what keeps the 2014 LiDAR valid against them: a re-clad between the flight and the frame would have broken the 1.3% agreement in stack.lidarResidual, and there was no re-clad.

conflicts.what: The big box's interior ceiling height, which is what sets the parapet, has two published values in the same year from the two people who would know.
sides: FE&S 2015-02-01: 20 ft ceilings in the east big box.
Eric Naslund FAIA, the design principal, quoted in Bisnow 2015-01-12: 'The original hall had 22-foot-high ceilings'.
conflicts.resolution: NOT AVERAGED, and nothing in this section depends on it. The parapet, soffit, glazing and plinth on the 64 Degrees block are read directly off the elevation and close against LiDAR to 1.3% without needing an interior dimension at all. The two readings are recorded because they bracket the third reading in conflicts['graphic-height'] and because a future frame that settles one may settle the other.

conflicts.what: The east elevation is not truly orthographic, so a single mean px/m scale and a band edge read at one station do not belong to the same geometry — and every band metre in this section is exactly that combination.
sides: THE GLOBAL SCALE, WHICH IS WHAT SHIPS: the graphic's whole 1166.2 px span over its published 17.0688 m, giving 68.3235 px/m, i.e. a mean panel pitch of 106.02 px. It is anchored on a count and on a published dimension and is the only scale with an external truth behind it.

THE LOCAL PITCH IN THE READING STRIP: the audit measured the eleven individual panel widths at 99.0, 106.0, 106.5, 106.2, 107.7, 107.6, 108.2, 107.7, 107.1, 105.7 and about 105 px — a 9% spread with the near-far gradient of a rectified oblique — and the pitch local to the x 300..1000 strip where every band edge is read averages about 107.02 px, which is 0.91% tighter than the global mean.

THE CONSEQUENCE IF THE LOCAL PITCH IS RIGHT: the stack reads about 9.677 m rather than the shipped 9.771895, and the keystone residual against LiDAR's 9.90 m grows from 0.128 m (1.29%) to about 0.223 m (2.25%).
conflicts.resolution: DECLARED, NOT CORRECTED, and the reason is that correcting it would trade a measured scale for a fitted one. The global scale is the only one anchored to an external published dimension; a local pitch is a fit to eleven panel widths in one frame with no independent check, and adopting it would make every band metre depend on an unpinned intermediate — which is the axiom-layer defect this whole batch exists to prevent. The two-source agreement survives either way: 1.29% on the shipped scale, 2.25% on the local one, both well inside what a photograph against a LiDAR flight can claim, and both better than the dossier's own 2.1%. What IS retired is the over-broad claim in scale.pxPerMetre's why that the reading is foreshortening-immune; immunity belongs to the COUNT alone.

conflicts.what: Whether the south frontage carries ONE canopy or two of different dates. The visual critic read the grey fabric sails of studioe-64degrees-16 and -18 and the dark faceted canopy of -33 as a later or other epoch and asked for the two to be reconciled and dated.
sides: TWO OBJECTS, TWO EPOCHS: the reading the critic offered — a pale fabric sail in two frames and a dark faceted panel in a third is two different things, and a section that ships one of them is shipping half an elevation.

ONE OBJECT, ONE EPOCH: all three frames belong to the SAME Studio E / Hewitt-Garrison shoot of the completed 2014 project, and the difference is illumination, not date. Frames 16 and 18 are daylight and the fabric reads silver because it is translucent and reflecting a bright sky; frame 33 is dusk and the same fabric reads dark against a deep blue sky with the soffit lit from below. The FACETED strut pattern that the critic reads as belonging only to the dark canopy is visible in all three: the radiating diamond frame is plainly there in 16 and in 18 as well.
conflicts.resolution: ONE OBJECT, and the section already held this reading before the critic raised it — research §5.2 records that the canopy 'reads dark in the two dusk/night frames and silver in daylight; it is translucent fabric reflecting the sky, not a dark panel', and names frame 16 as the deciding read on its material. Nothing here is dated later than 2014: the post-September-2023 Suffolk work on this building is an interior market fit-out that changes no elevation (see conflicts['suffolk-page-epoch']). So ONE canopy ships, in the 2014 epoch, and its colour is taken from the DAYLIGHT frame because a dusk silhouette is not an albedo — the same rule this section applies to the shaded east elevation.

conflicts.what: arcgis.ground#237, a 16 m2 ring surveyed as `green` at x -75.7..-66.1, z 380.0..381.8, lies 1.4 m south of the 64 Degrees south wall and renders as a lawn strip pressed against the storefront. The 2014 photographs show hard paving meeting the wall there.
sides: THE SURVEY: arcgis.ground#237 is typed `green` in the 2026-08-06 ArcGIS fetch and the base ground layer draws it as planting. It is one of the nine surveyed rings this section names in absent[] and declines to touch.

THE PHOTOGRAPHS: studioe-64degrees-18 and -33 show continuous tan paving running up to the storefront along this whole frontage, with the planting held back in gravel and succulent beds BEYOND the terrace edge. No frame shows turf against the curtain wall.
conflicts.resolution: DECLARED, NOT RESOLVED, and NOT ACTED ON BY THIS SECTION. The geometry is the base ground layer's, not this section's — nothing in campus-photo-revellecommons.js draws it — and this section's standing rule is that it lays nothing on a surveyed ring and paves nothing it has not been given. It is recorded here rather than left to the next reader because this same ring is the one this section cites as the near-miss that decided the whole south-terrace withholding, so a change to its type would change that argument too. Handed to whoever owns campus-colors / the ground layer, and to R6. If the ring is really paving, the terrace withholding gets easier, not harder.

revelle.absent[4].claims: The premise that a 2014 RE-CLAD happened on this building, which revelle.absent[4] withheld the details of and which this batch's brief repeated.
revelle.absent[4].why: NO SOURCE DESCRIBES A RE-CLAD AND THE PHOTOGRAPHS SHOW THE ORIGINAL FABRIC STANDING. suffolk-Desktop-2_1 shows the 1966 brown/taupe precast parapet band and the exposed-aggregate concrete piers left in place with new work below and in front of them, and Studio E frames 16, 18, 30, 31 and 33 show the same band continuing round the south face unchanged. So the entry is retired not by 'the re-clad now has a photograph' but by 'there is no re-clad' — which is the more useful fact and the reason it is recorded this way. What 2014 actually added outside is a closed list of six items: the deep flat cantilevered soffit, the full-height glazed storefront, the printed surfer graphic, the freestanding 3-D sign and its applied south-fascia twin, the tensioned-fabric canopy, and the terrace and landscape package. This section builds four of the six and declares the other two.

research.orthoDisplacementRate.claims: The research dossier §10.2's top-displacement rate of (+0.0497, +0.2021) m per metre of height, imported from Argo and applied to seven ortho edges on this cluster.
research.orthoDisplacementRate.why: REFUTED BY THE LOCAL RE-FIT §15 ITEM 2 ORDERED. Six roof edges of this cluster, at three LiDAR heights spanning 5.0 to 9.9 m, were measured on chunk_4_6.jpg. A constant offset fits them 3.37 times better in x and 3.48 times better in z than any height-proportional model, the two axes fitted independently and agreeing; and in x the 5.0 m block displaces MORE than the 9.9 m one, which no height model can produce. The dossier's own out-of-sample claim was not out of sample: it is corroborated on exactly the two edges the dossier used and fails on the third it did not. The consequence is recorded in conflicts['ortho-displacement-model'] and is that NO ortho-derived figure ships here at all.

research.signPlinth.claims: The research dossier §5.1's separate 'low pale concrete plinth' standing in front of the glazing to carry the 3-D yellow sign.
research.signPlinth.why: THE SIGN STANDS ON THE BUILDING'S OWN PLINTH BAND. A saturation mask over 19,066 pixels puts the sign's foot at y 631 in suffolk-Desktop-2_1-UCSD-64-degrees-3.jpg; the glazing-to-plinth line, read independently by a row-texture crossing in a strip that does not contain the sign, is at y 632.96. The two are 1.96 px apart, 0.029 m at 68.32 px/m — the sign's foot IS the plinth top and there is no separate base under it. What is real behind the sign is a pale SIGNAGE WALL replacing the glazing, which Studio E's plans name and place outside the dining floor plate, and that is what ships.

build.compassHand.claims: This section's own R2 build decision to place the signage wall, the 3-D sign and the entry doors at the SOUTH end of the 64 Degrees east face, overriding research §5.1's north-end reading.
build.compassHand.why: THE OVERRIDE WAS WRONG AND THE EVIDENCE IS PHOTOGRAPHIC. The build reasoned only that suffolk-Desktop-2_1 shows the sign to the RIGHT of the graphic, and silently assumed the frame's right hand is south; nothing supported that assumption. suffolk-Desktop-1_1-UCSD-64-Degrees.jpg turns the block's SOUTH-EAST corner and shows the two east-face panels there carrying pale wave crest over dark water — the elevation's LEFT-end content — with no sign, no pale signage wall and no doors. If the group were at the south end it would be the first thing round that corner. So elevation-left is south, the group is NORTH, and research §5.1 was right. A second independent line agrees: the ortho puts a 5.6 m shadowed service alley against the face's southern two thirds and a paved terrace against its northern end, and a main dining entry belongs on the terrace. Recorded as a deletion on evidence rather than a transfer because the shipped claim is simply gone; the geometry moved to the other end of the face and is now gated in world coordinates so it cannot move back silently.

absent.northBlockUntreated.claims: This section's R2 decision to ship the 64 NORTH block with NO facade treatment at all, and the two per-face absent entries that carried it.
absent.northBlockUntreated.why: THE ARGUMENT WAS HALF RIGHT AND THE CONCLUSION OVERSHOT. The shipped reasoning was that extending the east face's storefront glazing onto 64 North's back-of-house faces would assert a program both Studio E plans contradict. That half is correct and it STANDS — glazing is program-bearing and is still withheld on all three faces. What it does not carry is the conclusion, because the sourced pattern of this building is not one thing: the parapet band, the deep soffit and the plinth are NOT program-bearing, and this section's own retirement of revelle.absent[4] argues from frames 16, 18, 30, 31 and 33 that the 1966 band runs round the complex unchanged. The ultra standard's text is 'extend the same building's sourced pattern across the gap, labelled [estimated]', and the section already does exactly that on dgNorth where the program is known. So the non-program-bearing bands now extend onto ALL THREE faces as labelled [estimated], with a derived blank precast band where glazing cannot be asserted. That answers the shipped entry's own 'one-third dressed' objection, which only ever ruled out dressing ONE face of three. As shipped, a 5.0 m block rendered as 11.3 m of bare extruded mass, which is a larger falsehood than a labelled [estimated] parapet band. The three retired entries are carried COMPLETE and CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER inside absent[0], each delimited by double angle brackets, ladders included and nothing elided — the list does not shrink, and the first attempt at this carried truncated excerpts with ellipses, which is not a carry. A gate asserts each retired entry is a verbatim substring of absent[0].

absent.buildingMountedShade.claims: This section's decision to ship the 2014 entry canopy and the south fascia sign as recorded-but-unbuilt, on the ground that the entry's station along the south face is unresolved.
absent.buildingMountedShade.why: THE WITHHOLDING'S GROUND WAS TOO BROAD, and the visual audit is right. Both objects attach to the BUILDING, not to the terrace ground, so the withheld south-terrace landscape never covered them — and the reason given for withholding them, an unresolved entry station, withholds more than it needs to: the station is unresolved only in DEGREE. Frames 16, 18 and 33 agree on which END of the 29.4 m face the pair sits at, which is the same class of partial knowledge the graphic's centring rule already ships on. Withholding a plainly photographed element that is the most identifiable thing on the elevation, because one of its coordinates is banded rather than measured, is the wrong side of `better absent than wrong`. So both ship: the canopy on a stated end-referenced rule with its width and projection banded and its fall measured, the fascia sign as blank geometry at the east sign's measured size. What does NOT change is the lettering limitation, which is a renderer limitation and stays in absent['lettering'].

build.canopyFabricRole.claims: The canopy fabric's shipped appearance, which was the renderer's 0xffffff default standing in for a colour role this section never declared.
build.canopyFabricRole.why: AN UNSET VALUE, NOT A COLOUR JUDGEMENT. The canopy was added at the first visual audit and its material was written against `colors.canopyFabric` without that role ever being added to the palette — the ten declared roles predate the canopy and were never extended with it. campus-materials.js:465 destructures `color = 0xffffff`, so the reference resolved to opaque white rather than failing, and the sail shipped at a rendered #e6e6e6 against a fabric the deciding daylight frame puts at #3c3d43. The replacement is sampled from the frame this section already names as the deciding read on the canopy's material, at the round-2 critic's own rectangle, and it is [sourced] rather than [measured] because a translucent surface has no albedo. The material is also made translucent so the radiating strut frame reads through it, which is what the object is. THE CLASS FIX matters more than the hex: an undeclared role is now a hard error at runtime and a gate compares the module's referenced roles against the section's declared roles in both directions.

revellecommons.supersededNote: Every record carries a machine-readable `disposition`, because `sup` reads as a transfer whether the object moved to a named successor or was deleted on evidence, and only the prose could tell the two apart. All three records here are deletions on evidence and each states its ground.
absent:
RETIRED — see superseded['absent.buildingMountedShade']. Two withholdings are retired by the visual-audit ruling, NOT deleted: absent lists do not shrink. Both are carried COMPLETE below, character-for-character between double angle brackets, nothing elided.

RETIRED ENTRY 1 of 2 <<THE 2014 ENTRY CANOPY as geometry. The light-grey translucent tensioned-fabric canopy on its radiating diamond strut-and-cable frame over the south entry, cantilevered out and down over the terrace on slender diagonal struts with a scalloped tensioned edge. RESOLVED but NOT PLACEABLE: frame 16 in daylight is the deciding read on its material and settles that it is translucent fabric reflecting the sky rather than a dark panel (it goes dark in the two dusk frames), and FE&S confirms 'the new awning and patio are part of the extensive landscape project'. What is missing is the ENTRY's station along the 29.4 m south face, which no frame, plan or ortho figure available to this section resolves. Recorded in system.canopy with built:false — the class of blake.level4 and argo's roof furniture.>>

RETIRED ENTRY 2 of 2 <<THE SOUTH FASCIA'S APPLIED YELLOW 64-DEGREE LETTERS as geometry. Three-dimensional letters on standoffs on the brown fascia band above the south entry, plainly visible in frame 16. Withheld for exactly the reason the canopy is: they belong over an entry whose station along the face nothing gives. Recorded in system.fasciaSign with built:false. The EAST sign does ship, as blank geometry, because its bounding box is measured on the orthographic frame and its station rides on a stated rule.>>

RETIRED — see superseded['absent.northBlockUntreated']. The 64 North ruling narrowed three withholdings and they are retired here, NOT deleted: absent lists do not shrink, and a truncated quotation is not a carry. What supersedes them is the NARROWER entry immediately below — the non-program-bearing bands now ship on all three faces as labelled [estimated] and only the glazing, the openings and the bay counts stay withheld. The three retired entries follow COMPLETE, each between double angle brackets, ladders included and nothing elided.

RETIRED ENTRY 1 of 3 <<THE 64 NORTH BLOCK'S FACADE TREATMENT ENTIRELY. All three of its external faces are withheld above, so under the ultra standard — a treated building is never partially detailed — the block ships untreated rather than one-third dressed. Its drawn mass stands as the extruder makes it. This is §13's own escape taken deliberately: shipping fewer blocks complete is within the standard and shipping all three partially is not.>>

RETIRED ENTRY 2 of 3 <<64 NORTH'S NORTH FACE, z 330.0, x -110.3..-95.6, 14.7 m. No frame in any set frames this elevation. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos, Street View, drone/video, planning docs and drawings, archives. The only extension available would be the parapet-band-over-glazing pattern of the 64 Degrees east face, and applying it here means asserting GLAZING where both Studio E plans show back-of-house. The ultra standard permits extending a building's own sourced pattern; it does not permit extending it into a contradiction, so this face ships nothing.>>

RETIRED ENTRY 3 of 3 <<64 NORTH'S WEST FACE, x -110.3, z 330.0..349.4, 19.4 m. No frame in any set. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos, Street View, drone/video, planning docs and drawings, archives. Same reasoning as its north face: extending the east face's glazed pattern would assert glazing against both plans' back-of-house. Together these two faces are 34 m of run with nothing behind them.>>

64 NORTH'S GLAZING, OPENINGS AND BAY COUNTS, on all three of its faces — the north (z 330.0, 14.7 m), the west (x -110.3, 19.4 m) and the east (x -95.6, 19.4 m). NO PHOTOGRAPH exists of the first two in any of the five sets, and the third has exactly one dead-epoch frame (UCOP 2008 Regents deck p11) which gives the exposed-aggregate panel wall's existence and character and NOT ONE PLAN DIMENSION. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos, Street View, drone/video, planning docs and drawings, archives. WHAT SHIPS INSTEAD, and why the line falls here: the parapet, the soffit and the plinth are NOT program-bearing and the section's own retirement of revelle.absent[4] argues from frames 16/18/30/31/33 that the 1966 band runs round the complex unchanged, so those three plus a derived blank precast band extend onto all three faces as LABELLED [estimated]. GLAZING IS program-bearing and both Studio E plans put back-of-house behind these faces, so asserting it would assert a program the sources contradict. Nothing here claims a bay, an opening or a door.

The COURTYARD's four faces and its wall treatment. 9.7 x 9.4 m at x -126.9..-117.1, z 374.3..383.8. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos, Street View, drone/video, planning docs and drawings, archives. Studio E's 25 frames never enter it and the plan labels it EXISTING COURTYARD without drawing it; a court enclosed on four sides inside a building has no Street View pano; the 1960s aerials are obliques that cannot see into a 9 m well. What DOES ship is the floor, on surfaceAt, because four sources agree on its outline and arcgis.ground#3267 types it a `walk`. What is not invented is the wall treatment, any opening, and the meaning of the ortho's dark L wrapping its south and east — that L is not consistent with any San Diego sun position, so it is probably not shadow, and at 0.125 m/px that is as far as the imagery goes.

The WEST / SERVICE FACE of the Commons, x -139.5, z 349.5..393.2, 43.7 m, and its loading dock. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos, Street View, drone/video, planning docs and drawings, archives. No photograph exists in any of the five sets found; Revelle is pedestrian and no pano stands in a service yard; nothing on video; the plans give the dock's SIDE and not its size, section or material; the 1960s aerials are obliques from the east and south. KNOWN and recorded: both Studio E plans put DELIVERIES on this edge at roughly z 357 with +/-1.5 m of plan registration, LiDAR drops 1.1 m immediately west of the wall which is what a loading dock produces, and arcgis.ground#3069 is the 80 m2 service apron. UNKNOWN: the dock's size, level, retaining, doors and screening, and whether that 1.1 m drop is a dock pit or the natural fall.

64 NORTH'S EAST FACE, x -95.6, z 330.0..349.4, 19.4 m, as anything but a dead-epoch record. ONE frame exists — the UCOP 2008 Regents deck p11 storefront photograph, now positionally placed on this segment — and it is PRE-2014. It gives the existence and character of the 1966 exposed-aggregate panel wall still standing behind the 2014 work and NOT ONE PLAN DIMENSION, and its colours are a dead epoch that must not be sampled: they are 2008, before whatever the 2014 project did to adjacent fabric.

THE COMMONS' NORTH FACE, z 349.5, x -139.5..-110.3, approximately 29 m. The research dossier's §5 enumerates ten external runs and does not list this one at all; no frame in any set shows it. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos, Street View, drone/video, planning docs and drawings, archives. It faces the big lawn and tree grove of arcgis.ground#1171 and nothing else is known about it.

THE COMMONS ROOF'S 6.3 x 12.5 m GRIDDED RECTANGLE at approximately x -125.8..-119.5, z 353.4..365.9, and its identity. Two readings are live and the ortho at 0.125 m/px cannot separate them: a SKYLIGHT ARRAY (School Construction News 2015-05-06 says the project added skylights, and Studio E frame 25 shows a square interior skylight) or a SCREENED EQUIPMENT PLATFORM (the rooftop mechanical yard is immediately beside it).
