Both have textual support. Recorded with both readings and neither picked; it is additionally unbuildable for the reason in the roofscape entry below.

THE SLOT, x -95.2..-93.1, z 344..378, and its two facing faces. A real ~2.1 m outdoor separation the drawn mass bridges with solid building. This entry withholds BOTH the answer and the object: whether it is open to the sky or a lower link roof in shadow is not resolvable at 0.125 m/px, and the extruder cannot make the gap either way because campus-massing.js:826 opens only rings after the first and this is the space BETWEEN two rings that GIS merged. Neither facing face has a photograph either. See conflicts['the-slot'].

THE BAY COUNT AND EVERY OPENING ON 64 DEGREES' NORTH FACE, z 344.0, 29.4 m. The face's band system ships as a LABELLED [estimated] extension of this same building's sourced pattern, because the site plan names it a public dining frontage (DEMONSTRATION KITCHEN, FIRE PLACE, TERRACE SEATING, MEDIA ROOM, DINING ENTRY) and not back-of-house. What is NOT extended is anything the pattern cannot carry: the bay count is a fit against the drawn ring rather than a count off a frame, and no door, no window opening and no dining entry is placed. Studio E frame 11 is a candidate for this frontage and is equally a candidate for the south grove; the two are not distinguishable from the frame's own content and it is assigned to neither.

THE NORTH TERRACE AND ALL ITS OBJECTS, at roughly x -80..-69, z 332..341. The site plan names a FIRE PLACE and TERRACE SEATING; the 2026 ortho shows umbrellas in a loose grid, timber tables and a tan structure at approximately (-86, 333). No photograph frames it and frame 11 is not attributable to it. Every plan position available is either the ortho's — withheld under conflicts['ortho-displacement-model'] — or the site plan's +/-1.5 m, which is a whole bay. Better absent than placed on a guess.

THE SOUTH TERRACE LANDSCAPE ENTIRELY: the Revelle Commons Dining Terrace paving, the BEACH BLANKET SEATING platform and its yellow and blue colour fields, the BIOSWALE, the BRIDGE boardwalk, the seat walls, the market umbrellas, the Adirondack loungers, the bistro and communal furniture, the palo verde plantings and the agave, aloe, rush and boulder palette. THIS IS THE LARGEST SINGLE WITHHOLDING IN THE SECTION and it is a deliberate departure from §15 item 6, which asks for it. It is richly photographed — frames 16, 18, 22, 30, 31, 33 and suffolk-Desktop-1_1 — and every one of its MATERIALS and colours is sampled and recorded in colors/colorSources. What no source gives is a POSITION. The two candidate position sources are the 2026 ortho, whose registration this build measured as a 1.82 m constant offset of the same unresolved class CLAUDE.md quarantines, and Studio E's site plan at +/-1.5 m. And the band a terrace would want to pave is occupied: arcgis.ground#237 is a surveyed green ring at x -75.7..-66.1, z 380.0..381.8, only 1.4 m south of the 64 Degrees south wall, and five more surveyed beds (#513, #511, #415, #1762, #2696) run along z 395.5..403.4 south of the Commons. Paving 199 m2 of three surveyed beds is exactly what round1-critic.md A1 caught galbraith.north.apron doing. HANDED FORWARD to arbitration and to R6 as an open item.

ALL LETTERING AS TEXT. The 64-degree wordmark on the east sign and on the south fascia band, and the 2008 PLAZA CAFE storefront lettering. Positions and, for the east sign, a measured bounding box are recorded; the glyphs are not drawn. THIS IS A RENDERER LIMITATION AND NOT A SOURCE GAP — there is no text mechanism in this renderer and one must not be invented, which is the standing treatment across this project.

THE PRINTED SURF GRAPHIC AS AN IMAGE. A 56 ft by 22 ft illuminated black-and-white surf photograph, a surfer silhouetted in the barrel, occupying eleven glazing panels. RESOLVED BUT UNRENDERABLE, exactly as Argo's mural is: the eleven panels ship as blank geometry carrying the graphic's own measured area-average tone (#6f6f6f median over 468,236 px, mean #6f6c69, which independently confirms it is neutral greyscale), and the image itself is not drawn. Texture maps in this project are code-generated and a photo pixel may never become one.

THE GRAPHIC'S STATION along the 64 Degrees east face. The graphic is eleven counted bays of a twenty-two bay face and nothing fixes WHERE: suffolk-Desktop-2_1 shows 21.1 m of a 33.9 m elevation and neither of its edges is a building corner. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung: photos, Street View, drone/video, planning docs and drawings, archives. The shipped placement is the output of a stated centring rule, floor((22 - 11) / 2) = 5, which is now an EVALUATED expr rather than prose, with an estimate banded at the rule's own freedom of [-0.5, 0.5] bays — centring 11 in 22 cannot be exact. NARROWED AT AUDIT: this entry previously also withheld the COMPASS HAND of the sign-and-doors group, and the hand is now RESOLVED for the north end on two independent photographic reads — see conflicts['sign-and-doors-hand'] and superseded['build.compassHand']. What remains withheld is the station alone.

THE COLUMNS' FLARED CAPITALS. §5.2 reads the stout round exposed-aggregate columns as flared or tapered at the top where they meet the soffit, and frame 16 shows the flare. Nothing measures it — not its height, not its projection, not its profile — so the columns ship as plain cylinders at their estimated 0.65 m diameter and the flare is recorded here rather than modelled from an eye-read.

THE WHOLE ROOFSCAPE, on both roofs that have one. The Commons plate at 7.5 m carries a mechanical yard over roughly x -131..-108, z 348..372 dense with curbs, units and duct runs, a long north-south duct at x -121..-119.5, a branching Y-shaped duct running east from about (-114, 358), and round fan units near (-104.5, 348), (-104, 350) and (-103, 371); the 64 Degrees plate at 9.9 m carries one 21.9 x 1.3 m linear element at approximately x -92.5..-70.6, z 360..361.3 — a ridge skylight or a duct run, unresolved — and a small group of round units near (-72, 362). ALL of it is withheld for TWO independent reasons, either of which alone would be sufficient. First, every one of those positions is an ortho figure and no ortho figure ships from this section — see conflicts['ortho-displacement-model']. Second, and decisively, there is nowhere to put them: a curb on the Commons roof at 7.5 m would stand 3.8 m INSIDE the solid drawn 11.3 m prism, and one on the 64 Degrees roof would stand 1.4 m inside it. Not one roof object is drawn and counts.roofObjects is a declared zero.

PHOTOVOLTAICS — stated explicitly as a NEGATIVE rather than by omission, the way keeling.roofs.pv states the West Bar carries none. The blake.roof.screen control frame from the 2026-08-18 adjudication is the right instrument and it returns negative on this whole cluster: no ballasted tilt rows, no rank-and-file geometry, nothing at the 2.0-2.3 m pitch that reads as PV on this campus. counts.pv is a declared zero and nothing here draws a panel.

THE SOUTH-WEST NOTCH'S HANDEDNESS, at the Commons' south-west corner. Both rings cut a notch and they disagree by roughly 90 degrees about which way round it is: GIS reads 2.5 m wide by 4.6 m deep, OSM ring 397 reads 4.8 m wide by 2.5 m deep. Neither is a photograph, and the ortho does not resolve it — it lies under the roof edge at the frame's south-west corner. Studio E's plans put EXISTING CONFERENCE ROOMS in that corner and show a stepped rather than square edge, which corroborates THAT a notch exists and nothing about its handedness. The conflict is recorded and not picked; nothing is built there.

THE 2026 GROVE over x -138..-121, z 321..342. The 2026 ortho shows a dense canopy that the 2014 LiDAR tree roster does not account for and that appears in no 2014 photograph. The LiDAR roster holds only five crowns in the whole x -152..-56, z 318..406 box, four of them north of the building; the 2014 frames show newly-planted young multi-stem palo verdes on both terraces. These are THREE EPOCHS OF ONE PLANTING SCHEME — a 2014 flight that saw an almost treeless site, a 2014 photograph of new stock, and a 2026 canopy — and they are recorded as three rather than merged into one. Nothing is planted by this section.

EVERY COLOUR OF THE 64 DEGREES EAST ELEVATION'S FABRIC. The research dossier's §6 names suffolk-Desktop-2_1-UCSD-64-degrees-3.jpg as the sampling frame for the parapet band, the soffit, the plinth and the storefront framing. All four are REFUSED here on a measurement: that whole elevation is in shade. Sunlit paving in the same frame reads #d3c2a7 against a parapet band at #554939 six hundred pixels above it, a factor of 2.5, and the band itself runs #423b2e to #5c4e3b across the frame's width — a 40% luminance gradient, so there is no single value to take. A full-shade sample is not a material; that is the blake ruling and it is honoured here by declining the samples rather than by tiering them down. Every hex this section ships instead comes from the SUNLIT frame 16, and the one thing taken from the east elevation is the graphic's neutral area-average, which is a tone and not an albedo. The 64 North east face's one 2008 frame is a DEAD COLOUR EPOCH for the same class of reason and no hex is taken from it either: it is pre-2014, before whatever the project did to adjacent fabric.

THE COMMONS SOUTH FACE'S TRANSOM. The transom bar is measured on the 64 Degrees east face — two detected edges 10 px apart at a centre 2.253 m above the plinth top — and it ships on that block's three treated faces. It is NOT carried onto the Commons south face: that block's glazing band is a DERIVED 3.762 m rather than a read one, no frame resolves a transom in it, and placing a measured bar inside a derived band would let the derivation masquerade as a reading.

THE BLAKE STRIP, x -63.7..-58.7, and campus-3d surfaces[652] beyond it. The 5.0 m of walk between this building's east wall and blake's declared bound, over z 344..354 where the two buildings actually face each other, and the 899 m2 unnamed plaza at x -63.9..-7.6, z 343.8..373.6 that it opens into north and south of that overlap. This section CLAIMS x <= -58.7 entire so that the strip stops being unowned, and BUILDS nothing in it. It also asserts nothing about blake's west elevation: blake.absent[2] withholds the bay counts on blake's north, east and WEST faces and that withholding stands untouched.

THE NINE SURVEYED GROUND RINGS INSIDE THESE BOUNDS, unbuilt and unpaved with ONE stated exception: arcgis.ground#237 (16 m2 green, x -75.7..-66.1, z 380.0..381.8 — the bed that sits only 1.4 m south of the 64 Degrees south wall and is the near-miss this section declined the terrace to avoid), #345 (58 green, the west frontage strip), #519 (237 green, straddling the blake strip at x -69.7..-40.1), #525 (87 green), #1763 (11 green), #1767 (27 green), #2152 (112 green), and the two `walk` rings #3268 (40) and #3267 (91). THE EXCEPTION IS #3267 AND IT IS THE POINT: that ring is the courtyard floor, it is typed `walk` rather than `green`, and it is this section's own cited authority for the court being PAVED — so the court floor is laid on it deliberately. Nothing is laid on any `green` ring. Named individually so a later section cannot pave one by not knowing it was there; the rings whose centroids fall OUTSIDE these bounds, including the five south-frontage beds, are handed forward in boundary.handedForward.

THE INTERIOR, all of it, recorded and not built because this section builds exteriors: the coffered waffle-slab ceiling over the big box, the continuous clerestory glazing band above a vertical-grain Douglas Fir slat frieze with Maxine Ward's bold yellow and blue panels inserted at random into the original slats, the EXISTING CONFERENCE ROOMS in the south-west corner, and the HOWARD WARSHAW MURAL — an original fifty-year-old mural remaining as a backdrop on the INSIDE face of the east wall. That mural is NOT El Mac's 'An Enduring Spell' (revelle.absent[1], plaza.absent[7]), which is on Argo; the two are recorded as distinct here so that a name grep cannot merge them.

64 NORTH'S WEST ROOF EDGE AS AN ORTHO READING, withdrawn from the displacement fit at audit. Its column profile on chunk_4_6.jpg over z 334..346 reads bright (L 215-236) from x -113.5 to -111.75, then a 0.5 m DARK STRIPE (L 89, 59, 64, 86) at x -111.6..-111.1, then bright again (L 186-240). That is bright surface on BOTH sides of a dark linear feature, which is not the condition the section's own method describes ('a bright membrane against DARK open ground'), and it presents two near-tied gradients whose choice moves the reading 0.53 m. The 2.3 m disagreement between GIS (x -112.6) and OSM (x -110.3) about where this very wall sits falls exactly inside that ambiguity, so the imagery cannot be used to referee it either. An edge the criterion does not describe may not be fitted, so it is dropped rather than re-picked, and the x axis is recorded as NON-DISCRIMINATING in consequence — two remaining edges cannot separate two one-parameter models.

THE TRANSOM BAR'S ORIGINAL DEPTH READING. The section shipped 0.146 m from a pinned pair of 'dark edges' at y 474 and y 484, and neither row carries a gradient — y 474 sits on flat baseline at L 98.2. Those rows were an artefact of a detector comparing each row against rows +/-5 away, which on a 3 px BRIGHT bar manufactures minima at exactly +/-5. Recorded here rather than silently overwritten, because a pinned reading that does not reproduce is the defect this batch's whole axiom layer exists to catch, and this one survived a green suite. The bar's CENTRE was never in doubt and reproduces to 0.15 px; the depth is now the full width at half maximum of its own bright peak, 3.31 px.

THE CANOPY'S WIDTH, PROJECTION AND EXACT STATION, which ship as banded estimates rather than reads. Its FALL is measured — 2.44 m, scaled off the round column standing beside it at the same depth in studioe-64degrees-33.jpg — and a vertical drop is the one canopy dimension an oblique frame gives honestly. Its width and projection run in exactly the two directions those frames foreshorten, and its station along the face is fixed only to the END it sits at, which all three frames agree on. Ladder climbed and failed at every rung for all three: photos (three frames, all oblique, none reaching both ends of the canopy); Street View (Revelle is pedestrian and no pano stands on this terrace); drone/video (nothing found); planning docs (the site plan NAMES the awning and dimensions nothing); archives (none). What is NOT invented: the strut count follows the declared bay interval, the attachment height is the measured soffit underside, and nothing about the fabric's cut or its scalloped edge is modelled.

THREE THINGS THE VISUAL AUDIT FOUND ON THIS FRONTAGE THAT ARE NOT THIS SECTION'S GEOMETRY, identified here so they are not lost and not silently adopted. FIRST, the terrace UMBRELLAS, reported as orange and dark navy against sources that show yellow and sky blue: they stand at x -101..-75, z 376..384, inside this section's declared bounds, and this section builds no umbrella at all — its counts carry none and its module has no such mesh. They belong to another module and the colour finding should go there; this section's own record of that palette is in colors.beachYellow's absent entry and in the withheld terrace landscape. SECOND, the LAWN STRIP against the storefront foot is arcgis.ground#237, a ring the 2026-08-06 survey types `green`, drawn by the base ground layer — see conflicts['ground237-turf']. THIRD, the pale blue rectangle lying flat in the north re-entrant is arcgis.ground#3268, a surveyed `walk` ring at x -93.2..-89.4, z 332.2..343.1, likewise drawn by the ground layer; it is neither of this section's two blank panels, both of which are wall-mounted and vertical. All three are inside the x <= -58.7 claim and all three are named in this section's surveyed-ground entry as unbuilt, which is why they are handed on rather than adopted.

THE CANOPY'S SHIPPED WHITE, retired at the round-2 visual audit and recorded because a defect that passed every gate is worth more on the record than off it. The module referenced `colors.canopyFabric`; the section never carried that role; campus-materials.js destructures `color = 0xffffff`, so the missing role did not throw, did not warn and did not read as wrong in the source — it shipped an OPAQUE WHITE sail, measured at #e6e6e6 in the render against a sourced #3c3d43. Every gate passed: the tier gate walks the roles the section DECLARES, the hex-literal gate proves the module holds no colours of its own, and nothing anywhere compared the two lists. What fixes it is not the hex but the two-way check — the module now routes every colour through a helper that THROWS on an undeclared role, so the silent default cannot be reached at runtime, and a gate asserts the module's referenced roles and the section's declared roles are the same set in both directions.
revellecommons.boundsNote: West, north and south hug the DRAWN ring by one metre, which is more than the widest thing this section stands outboard of a wall (a column at draw.columnProud + draw.columnJitter = 0.57 m). The EAST bound is not the ring's — it is the ownership claim at x -58.7, meeting blake.bounds.x0 exactly, and the 5.0 m of walk between the two buildings is claimed and left unbuilt rather than left unowned. See boundary.
revellecommons.colorSourcesNote: Every entry carries `sampleL` and `sampleSd` as NUMBERS — the sample rectangle's own CHANNEL MEAN, defined as (R + G + B) / 3 over every pixel of the rectangle, and its standard deviation — and the tier rule is asserted against them ARITHMETICALLY. NAMING THE STATISTIC MATTERS: a Rec.601 luma would give different figures for the same pixels (the audit's independent re-cut read soffit at 94.2 against this block's 89.5 for exactly that reason) and every tier decision is identical under either, but the next section computing a `sampleL` must compute the same one. ADDED AT AUDIT: the tier gate was purely lexical, so a tier could be inflated by editing its own source string alongside it. The rule is now numeric and symmetric: [measured] requires BOTH sampleL >= 120 (the sample is sunlit) AND sampleSd <= 15 (it is one material, not a mixture); a line failing either is [sourced] at best; a line extending another element's sample is [estimated] whatever else is true. BOTH OPERANDS ARE PINNED AS LITERALS IN THE TEST FILE, the way the section's 65 readings are — a threshold is worthless if the value it judges is declared by the thing being judged, which is minor 5's defect one level down.

colorThreshold.statisticNote: (R + G + B) / 3, unweighted, over every pixel of the declared rectangle. Not a Rec.601 or Rec.709 luma; those weight green heavily and would move every figure here without moving a single tier.

controls.what: SUNLIT exposed-aggregate terrace paving. This is also courtPaving's own sample rectangle, so the threshold's warmest-side control is a hex the section actually ships.

SUNLIT paving in the east elevation frame — the brightest control, and the one that shows how far above the threshold a genuinely sunlit surface sits even in the frame whose FACADE is entirely in shade.

The SHADED 1966 parapet band, in the reading strip. The same physical element reads 125.5 sunlit in frame 16, so this pair is one material photographed both ways and is the tightest evidence the threshold has.
The SHADED plinth band — the darkest-side control, and the highest shaded reading of the three, so it is the one that sets how much margin the threshold really has.

colorThreshold.note: ADDED AT AUDIT. The 120 threshold was defended with four bare luminances and only one of them named a rectangle. All four now carry frame, rectangle and pixel count so any of them can be re-cut, and all four are pinned as literals in the test. The populations are 154.9-190.7 sunlit against 71.2-84.1 shaded: 70.8 units apart at their closest, with the threshold sitting 35.9 above the highest shaded control and 34.9 below the lowest sunlit one. It is measured, not chosen, and it is now reproducible.

fleets.label: THE SIX FLEET RESIDENCE HALLS, Revelle College — Beagle, Challenger, Discovery, Atlantis, Galathea and Meteor — with the Garbini & Garbini 2011 courtyard landscape between them. ONE BUILDING TYPE BUILT SIX TIMES: identical footprint area to 0.5% rsd, identical plan under the correct reflection to 3.3% of raster cells, four storeys on every one of four independent sources, one facade system in every photograph, and one 2011 landscape project over all six courtyards at once. The three real per-instance deviations — the pinwheel HAND, the LiDAR HEIGHT and the spandrel ACCENT COLOUR — are first-class data here and not a footnote, because a six-copies-of-one-prism build gets two of them uniformly wrong. Each hall is extruded to ITS OWN massHeights and the accent is NOT painted at all.
fleets.epoch: Building 1964-66 (mid-1960s aerial, form only); renovation 2010 (secondary sources only, no primary); LANDSCAPE 2011 (Garbini & Garbini, the firm's own text and plan) — that is the epoch break for everything on the ground, and the UCOP 2008 photographs are a DEAD ground epoch showing lawns that are now rock mulch and stairs that were removed; colour 2011 (Garbini frames 5e and 5g) and 2012-05-04 (the ASLA frame's DateTimeOriginal — its DateTime field reads 2014-10-28 and is a Photoshop CS2 save stamp, corrected here); facade GEOMETRY 2012-01-19 (Enginuity MG_23022); heights LiDAR 2014; identity 2019-03 and the undated UCSD HDH directory; roof plan 2026 (Google ortho) — and NO ORTHO-DERIVED POSITION SHIPS, so the 2026 rung corroborates and decides nothing.
fleets.note: INVENTED CLASS — photo-sourced detail, modeled off dated web photographs and one landscape drawing. Nothing measured reads from this section. The surveyed rings it carries are copied VERBATIM from campus-arcgis.json and are the only geometry here that is not a band hung off them.
fleets.boundsNote: The R3 band is x -152..-29 / z 414..475 for OWNERSHIP; these bounds are the drawn extent, which is wider because two owned surveyed rings run past the ownership band (#1165 reaches x -19.2 and z 476.3 on its way to Ridge Walk, #1163 reaches z 476.6) and because the halls' own treatment stands draw.wallOffset proud of rings that reach z 412.4 and x -149.8. Nothing west of x -152 is treated — that is Keeling and R6's — and the THREE rings that cross that line (#343, #1133, #404) are handed forward whole rather than clipped, as are the three that cross the band's north and south edges (#344, #405, #2148).

boundary.claim: x -152 on the west (main's ruling), REVELLE WALK at z ~405-410 on the north, z 475 on the south, and Ridge Walk on the east.
boundary.west: KEELING APARTMENTS, out of scope and already at the bar. recon 8 bans landscape work in x -200..-130 / z 405..500, whose east edge sits 22 m INSIDE this band; the reconciliation is that R3 treats no ground west of x -152 and hands the THREE rings that cross that line — #343, #1133 and #404 — to R6 entire. Keeling 3's roof edge (massing[451], h 27) was used as an out-of-band MEASUREMENT only, for the x-axis height-dependence check; nothing was built there.
boundary.north: REVELLE COMMONS / 64 DEGREES (R2, shipped). `revellecommons` cites arcgis.ground#326, #513, #1171, #3267, #237, #3069 and #3268 — none of them is in this band. The Garbini plan's 'EXISTING COMMONS PLAZA' is R2's, not R3's.
boundary.northEast: ARGO HALL (R1, shipped). argo.ground.north is built off a Nov 2024 photosphere at (-52..-40, 361..365), 41 m north of this band's north edge. No contact.
boundary.east: REVELLE PLAZA (R1, shipped) and RIDGE WALK. `plaza` cites 12 ground rings, none in the band; its nearest is #2323 at (23, 394). Ring #1165 (x -41..-19) is R3's and runs east toward Ridge Walk — THAT IS THE SEAM. Ridge Walk itself is left to R6.
boundary.south: GALBRAITH's south lawn. Ring #1742 (41,560 m2, centred (105, 652)) is the Galbraith / La Jolla Project field and is NOT R3's. Rings #2148, #405 and #1131 fall mostly south of z 475 and are offered to R6 rather than taken.
boundary.handedForwardNote: Eleven surveyed rings named individually: six cross a declared boundary and are handed to R6 WHOLE rather than clipped silently, three are campus-wide blobs that merely clip the band, and two belong to neighbours. R3 draws none of them. THREE of the six cross the x -152 KEELING line — #343, #1133 and #404. The other three cross a different edge: #344 lies mostly north of z 414 on the Revelle Walk seam, and #405 and #2148 lie mostly south of z 475. The brief and this section's own first round both said four straddle the Keeling line; #344 does not, and its whole extent is east of it.

Revelle-College-Sources/renders/fleets-sources/garbini_2011_fleet-5e-facade-3x.png — a 3x LANCZOS enlargement of the same 2011 frame's content crop (2160x1221), used to confirm that the 1x parapet-to-storey ratio of 0.370 is the same edge pair the research dossier read as 38/103 = 0.369 at 3x.

Revelle-College-Sources/renders/fleets-sources/asla-sd_2014-10-28_fleet-walk-facade-and-planting.jpg — ASLA San Diego award-submission photograph of the Fleet walk, facade and planting, EXIF DateTimeOriginal 2012-05-04, DateTime 2014-10-28 which is a Photoshop save stamp, Sony DSLR-A290. https://www.asla-sandiego.org/portfolio-items/uc-san-diego-revelle-campus-fleet-housing-landscape-improvements/ (HTTP 200) — ASLA San Diego, the 2014 award page naming Garbini & Garbini Landscape Architecture, Inc., Gail Garbini ASLA as Principal in Charge, Kyle Simon as Designer, and 2011 as the year constructed.

Revelle-College-Sources/plans-and-drawings/GarbiniGarbini_2011_Fleet-housing-landscape-plan.jpg — the firm's labelled 2011 landscape plan (featured_5a, 720x720, content 710x509), north-up. Revelle-College-Sources/renders/york-sources/ucsddc-bb1639263c_aerial-revelle-mid1960s.jpg with the 5x detail crop at renders/fleets-sources/ucsddc-bb1639263c_fleets-detail-5x.png — UCSD Digital Collections oblique aerial, mid-1960s, of halls built 1964-66. Establishes FORM ONLY: four storeys, flat roofs, thin fascia with no overhang, two offset bars per hall, the vertical circulation at the junction with its open switchback flights, blank windowless short faces, and one roof plane per hall.

Revelle-College-Sources/plans-and-drawings/UCSDConference_2019-03_Revelle-neighborhood-map.pdf — UCSD Conference Services neighbourhood map, March 2019. One of the three first-party UCSD sources that put Galathea at (-41.7, 454.6) and Meteor at (-70.0, 462.6), against OSM.

Revelle-College-Sources/renders/fleets-sources/ucsdhdh_revelle-directory-map-render.png — a render of the UCSD Housing Dining Hospitality Revelle neighbourhood directory (undated, current as fetched 2026). The second first-party identity source: d = Galathea, e = Meteor, both by position.

docs/data/campus-arcgis.json — the university's 2014 GIS massing and ground survey. massing[34] Galathea, [47] Atlantis, [118] Beagle, [157] Discovery, [260] Meteor, [347] Challenger, each carried here VERBATIM at /10, plus the 26 arcgis.ground rings of the band. The `levels` field (4 on all six) is a source; the `h` field (12.2 on all six) is levels x 3.05, a FORMULA, and is admitted only as a check.

docs/data/campus-3d.json — OpenStreetMap. buildings[183] is labelled 'Galathea Hall' at centroid (-69.67, 462.80) and buildings[201] 'Meteor Hall' at (-42.65, 454.81): the two names are on each other's buildings. docs/data/textures/chunk_4_7.jpg with docs/data/textures/manifest.json — cached Google orthoimagery, 2026, 8.000 px/m exactly over x -177..78 / z 402..657. Used for the local displacement re-fit and for nothing that ships.

https://enginuityconsulting.com/project/ucsd-revelle/ (HTTP 200) — Enginuity Consulting, the civil engineer on the 2010-11 project, in its own words: it coordinated with 'the Architect David Thompson of Bundy & Thompson Architects' and 'the Gail Garbini of the Landscape Architecture firm Garbini & Garbini', regraded the centre courtyard, removed onerous stairways, did fire-truck access and BMP design, 'all while dodging the underground utility tunnels that are prevalent in this area', coordinated with 'additional new buildings to the west' (Keeling). This names the RENOVATION architect; the original 1960s architect of the Fleet halls remains a verified negative.

Revelle-College-Sources/plans-and-drawings/UCSDConference_nd_Revelle-room-layouts.pdf — UCSD Conference Services 'SAMPLE LAYOUTS' (undated; fetched 2026). Its 'Fleet Residence Hall' panel is a dimensioned suite plan: five doubles each labelled 12' x 14', two doubles plus a bathroom block on one side, a 'Suite' lounge across the middle, three doubles on the other. THIS SHEET CLOSED A8. Its 'Blake/Argo Residence Hall' panel gives a DIFFERENT module (10' x 13.5' doubles) which belongs to R1 and is never used here.

Revelle-College-Sources/renders/fleets-sources/enginuity_2012-01-19_MG23022_fleet-facade-bay-grid.jpg — Enginuity Consulting site photograph of a Fleet long face, 1600x1067, Canon EOS 7D at 24 mm, EXIF DateTimeOriginal 2012-01-19. The photogrammetric source for the bay:storey ratio, the spandrel band's depth and the opening's place in its module. Revelle-College-Sources/renders/fleets-sources/garbini_2011_fleet-5g.jpg — a Garbini & Garbini frame of the 2011 landscape that the firm's project page never displayed, found through the WordPress media REST index. It carries the building's OWN APPLIED LETTERING reading 'Galathea', with Galbraith's cantilevered roof on tapered columns behind and to the right. That is the mechanism that fixed one camera station and made one accent colour a named figure.

Revelle-College-Sources/renders/fleets-sources/garbini_2011_fleet-5h.jpg and garbini_2011_fleet-5i.jpg — two more previously undisplayed Garbini frames of the 2011 landscape. 5h shows the stair tower in full as a tall glazed slot; 5e shows the same element reading open. They disagree, which is absent A9, and neither is built.

Revelle-College-Sources/renders/fleets-sources/enginuity_2012-01-19_MG2305_trench-drain-bmp.jpg, MG2306_revelle-paving-medallion.jpg and MG2310_seat-blocks-lawn-commons.jpg — three more Enginuity frames of 2012-01-19: a slotted metal trench drain set flush across the walk, a circular red-oxide paving medallion reading REVELLE COLLEGE 1964 / PURPOSE TRUTH VISION, and the row of precast seat blocks with 64 Degrees behind. All three record objects whose EXISTENCE is sourced and whose POSITIONS are not; see absent A10 and B1.

measured.hallsNote: SIX HALLS, KEYED BY POSITION, NEVER BY NAME. Each carries the arcgis.massing ring the extruder actually draws, copied verbatim at /10, its own m: key, and the massHeights that key returns. A name lookup against a measured file is banned in this section and there is not one in the module.
measured.identityNote: OSM HAS GALATHEA AND METEOR SWAPPED AND THE R3 BRIEF INHERITED THE SWAP. The building at (-41.7, 454.6) is GALATHEA and the building at (-70.0, 462.6) is METEOR: campus-arcgis.json's own names, the UCSD HDH neighbourhood directory and the March 2019 UCSD Conference Services map all agree, three first-party UCSD sources against one crowd-sourced label pair, and the LiDAR settles it arithmetically in derivations.figures['identity.*']. campus-massing.js extrudes the GIS mass and the GIS names are the correct ones, so what RENDERS is already right — only the OSM-derived name was wrong. Nothing in campus-3d.json, campus-lidar.json or campus-arcgis.json is edited: they are builder output, the section records the corrected mapping, and the consumer stays position-keyed so the swap cannot bite.
measured.handNote: TWO OF THE SIX ARE MIRRORED AND IT IS NOT A MARGINAL CALL. Rasterising each footprint into its own bounding box at 56x56 cells and comparing against Galathea under the four axis-aligned symmetries: the four hand-A halls match under IDENTITY at 0.0-1.3% of cells and mismatch under mirror-in-x at 48.3-49.3%; Meteor and Challenger invert exactly, 48.7 / 48.9% under identity and 3.1 / 3.3% under mirror-in-x. A factor of 15. Note also that rot180 is approximately identity because the plan is C2, so THE DIFFERENCE IS A GENUINE REFLECTION AND NOT A ROTATION — you cannot get Meteor by turning Galathea round. This build never instances a shared mesh: every hall's treatment is generated from ITS OWN surveyed ring, edge by edge, so the hand is carried by the survey and cannot be got backwards. The hand is nevertheless declared per hall and gated in world coordinates, because a future refactor toward a shared mesh is exactly what would break it.
measured.ringsNote: Every ring here is deepEqual to arcgis.massing[i].r[0] at /10. Every hall carries ONE ring — unlike Argo and Blake there is no courtyard hole. `drawnEdges` and `degenerateEdges` split each ring's segments: SIX of the 169 segments across the six rings are ZERO-LENGTH repeated vertices, and a per-edge treatment must count drawn edges rather than vertices or its declared and built counts part company for a reason nobody ever finds. The degenerate vertices are NOT removed — the ring ships exactly as surveyed.
measured.typeNote: The bounding box is 26.45 x 21.63 m +/- 0.14 / 0.08 and the footprint fills only 70.5% of it: two opposite corners, about 166 m2, are cut away. recon work-queue item 14's '~26.4 x 21.6 m' is the BOUNDING BOX, and a build that extrudes it is 29% too much building. The plan is a three-band Z — a north band about 14.8 m wide x 6.5 m deep over the eastern 56% of the box, a middle band the full width x about 8.7 m, a south band mirroring the north over the western 56% — plus two C2-paired projections about 1.2 m deep x 3.0 m along the face, one at each long end. The mid-1960s aerial says why: two four-storey bars offset from each other, overlapping across the middle, with the vertical circulation in the re-entrant corner. That is what recon 4 item 20's 'stepped pinwheel blocks' describes — STEPPING IN PLAN, NOT IN ROOF HEIGHT.
measured.towerNote: The two projections per hall are DERIVED FROM THE RING AND NEVER TYPED: they are the only x-constant ring segments between 2.0 and 4.5 m long standing at the ring's own extreme x, and the rule finds exactly two on every hall of both hands. Research 4.4 reads the stair element in the re-entrant corner rising above the main parapet in frame 5e and explains the projections as the tower's outer skin reaching the survey line; both projections are built because the type's own C2 symmetry is this section's central claim, and a symmetry that is real in the footprint cannot be selectively disbelieved in elevation.
measured.groundNote: NOT ONE of the 26 arcgis.ground rings inside x -152..-29 / z 414..475 is claimed by any existing section — all 77 arcgis.ground#NNNN registrations across every key of campus-photo-detail.json (eighth, revelle, galbraith, plaza, york, argo, blake, eighthcourtyards, eighthgathering, eighthramble, eighthsiteworks, eighthsouthservice, pulsefitness, revellecommons) were checked and none overlaps the band. The Fleet quad's surveyed ground is entirely unowned and R3 registers it rather than inventing beds on top of it — the galbraith-beds lesson, applied before the fact rather than after.

groundRings.indexNote: arcgis.ground is addressed by LITERAL INDEX and dropped slots are null. Nothing here renumbers it and nothing here compacts it.

derivations.why: The bar is keeling.roofs.pv: every figure sourced and derivable, with the arithmetic recorded. A round number with no derivation is a defect. Every metre this section draws is either an `expr` evaluated in the test against these readings, a banded `estimate`, or a declared `draw` offset with a sibling Note saying why it is not a measurement.

px.source: Revelle-College-Sources/renders/fleets-sources/garbini_2011_fleet-5e.jpg (Garbini & Garbini Landscape Architecture, project photograph, landscape completed 2011), 720x720 with a white letterbox; the CONTENT crop is rows 158..561 and every y below is measured in that crop, so image row = content row + 158. Vertical reads are 50% crossings or zero-crossings of a colour opponency, never gradient extrema.

survey.source: docs/data/campus-lidar.json, the CA_SanDiegoQL2_2014 flight, plus docs/data/campus-arcgis.json's own `levels` and `h` fields for the 2014 GIS massing. massHeights is keyed by POSITION (m:round(mean x),round(mean z) over the GIS ring) and heights[] by OSM NAME — which is exactly why the Galathea/Meteor swap is arithmetically visible.

ortho.source: docs/data/textures/chunk_4_7.jpg with docs/data/textures/manifest.json (Google orthoimagery, cached 2026): x0 -177, z0 402, x1 78, z1 657, w 2040, h 2040, zoom 20 -> 2040/255 = 8.000 px/m exactly, so u = (x + 177) x 8 and v = (z - 402) x 8. Roof-plate edges are the parabolically refined MINIMUM of the signed luminance gradient along the outward normal, profiled over the middle 60% of every axis-aligned GIS ring segment at +/-4.5 m in 0.05 m steps. This is an INDEPENDENT LOCAL FIT, never a correction to the Commons' fit: displacement is radial from the camera's nadir and varies across the frame.

plan.source: Revelle-College-Sources/plans-and-drawings/GarbiniGarbini_2011_Fleet-housing-landscape-plan.jpg, the firm's own `featured_5a` at 720x720 (content 710x509), north-up. Authoritative for outdoor-room NAMES, topology and character; authoritative for NO dimension — the single-scale similarity fitted from its six white hall bodies to the six GIS centroids over all 720 correspondence permutations lands at 5.038 px/m with rms 23.8 px = 4.72 m, which is larger than a courtyard.

mg.source: Revelle-College-Sources/renders/fleets-sources/enginuity_2012-01-19_MG23022_fleet-facade-bay-grid.jpg — Enginuity Consulting's own site photograph of one Fleet hall's long face, 1600x1067, Canon EOS 7D at 24 mm, EXIF DateTimeOriginal 2012-01-19 (its DateTime field reads 2014-11-17 and is a Photoshop CS6 save stamp, not an epoch). GEOMETRY ONLY — this frame is graded and may never be colour-sampled; see conflicts['mg23022-geometry-only']. Spandrel bands are found on redness R - (G+B)/2 profiled by row over the facade strip x 180..760 and by column within each bay; every extent below is a sub-pixel half-maximum crossing.
mg.sharesNote: THE FOUR VERTICAL SHARES OF ONE STOREY, top down: wall, glass, wall, painted spandrel. Measured on six bay-and-storey cells (three bays x the storeys each is clean on). The cell is bounded by the two spandrel plateaus' half-maximum edges on redness; the window OPENING inside it by the two zero crossings of B - R, which is the reveal-to-reveal extent; and the lit GLASS inside that by where luminance exceeds the midpoint between the opening's own 5th and 90th percentiles, i.e. the pane against its own shaded head and sill. Each cell's four shares sum to 1 by construction, so the six means do too and the partition cannot drift.

drawing.source: Revelle-College-Sources/plans-and-drawings/UCSDConference_nd_Revelle-room-layouts.pdf, UCSD Conference Services 'SAMPLE LAYOUTS', the panel headed 'Fleet Residence Hall' — a suite plan with room dimensions printed on it: five double bedrooms each labelled 12'x14', arranged as two doubles plus a bathroom block on one side, a 'Suite' common lounge across the middle, and THREE doubles on the other. Undated; the sheet is the Conference Services room-layouts document and NOT hdhughousing.ucsd.edu/_files/revelle-overview-layouts.pdf, which is image-only and yields nothing.

px.pitch.why: The storey pitch, from the TWO CLEAN INTERVALS between the three clean spandrel bands. The storey-1 band is excluded on a stated measurement ground, not on taste: its full width at half maximum is 13.799 px against 8.967 / 9.526 / 9.752 on the other three — 45% wider — so it is not one band but a band plus whatever stands in front of it, and it may not set a pitch.

px.pitchAllThree.derivation: (px.band1 - px.band4) / 3 over all three intervals, carried as the out-of-sample check on the figure above and NOT used to place anything.
px.pitchAllThree.why: The three raw intervals are 35.768 / 36.618 / 37.186 px — monotonically INCREASING downward, which is perspective in a frame shot from the ground looking up, not measurement noise. The research dossier's 'three intervals agreeing to 0.9 px' glosses a real gradient. The two figures differ by 0.7%; the difference is published rather than averaged away, and conflicts['storey-pitch-perspective-gradient'] carries it.

px.parapet.why: The parapet CAP band alone: from the 50% sky-to-cap luminance crossing down to the zero crossing of B - R, which is where the warm buff masonry cap ends and the genuinely blue fascia band begins. Both edges are colour-opponency events, so neither depends on an exposure choice.

px.navy.why: The dark navy fascia band immediately under the cap, bounded by the two zero crossings of B - R. It is a COLOUR and not a shadow: over its whole extent B > G > R, and either side of it B - R is strongly negative.

px.stack.why: The whole four-storey stack in the frame's own pixels: four storey pitches and the parapet cap. This is the quantity each hall's own LiDAR massHeights is divided into.

ratio.parapetToStorey.why: The one number the photograph contributes to the height model. The research dossier reads 38/103 = 0.369 off the 3x facade blow-up; this build's independent read of the 1x frame gives 0.370. Two different measurements of the same edge pair agreeing to 0.3% is what makes it publishable at all.

ratio.parapetOfStack.why: RECORDED, NOT BUILT — RETIRED as a route, see superseded['build.parapetRatioRoute']. Applied to the six halls it gave parapets of 1.126 to 1.219 m off a photograph whose grade line the dossier itself could not see. The shipped route derives the storey from a dimensioned drawing and lets the parapet be the residual; this ratio stays on the record because it is a real read of a real edge pair, and because it is the only independent check the 5e frame can offer the module route.

ratio.navyOfStack.why: RECORDED, NOT BUILT — the same retirement. The fascia band now takes ratio.navyOfStorey against the shared storey instead, which is the same pixel read divided by a different denominator: 0.575 m on every hall rather than 0.579-0.627 m across six.

ratio.roofAboveTopBand.why: The topmost spandrel band sits this many storey pitches below the cap top IN FRAME 5E. RECORDED, NOT BUILT, and it is the reading that failed to close: under the old parapet-ratio route it put the storey-1 band 0.194 pitches below the stack's own foot. The module route places the storey grid from the parapet zone downward and closes exactly on the prism base, which is how conflicts['spandrel-band-station-does-not-close'] resolved.

px.spandrelFwhmMean.why: The mean full width at half maximum of the three clean spandrel bands in frame 5e. The band is now BUILT, and its shipped depth comes from the Enginuity frame instead; this read is the independent corroboration, agreeing to 0.004 of a storey.

ratio.spandrel5eOfStorey.why: The spandrel band as a fraction of a storey, read off frame 5e. RECORDED, NOT BUILT — the shipped figure is ratio.spandrelOfStorey, measured on the Enginuity frame at higher resolution and by a half-maximum crossing rather than a redness centroid. The two are carried side by side because they are independent reads of the same detail and they agree to 0.004 of a storey.

px.mgPitch.why: The storey pitch in the Enginuity frame, from the two clean intervals between the three clean spandrel-band centroids (129.73 and 129.39 px, agreeing to 0.34 px = 0.26%). The fourth band is contaminated by planting and sets nothing.

ratio.bayToStorey.why: THE PHOTOGRAMMETRIC RATIO, and the two validity checks that let it be taken as a world ratio are in reads.facadePlanarity: the facade is planar (spandrel left edges agree across storeys to <= 1 px over 390 px of height) and its verticals are PLUMB in the image (bay 1's spandrel left edge drifts 0.5 px over 129 px), so the plane's foreshortening is a function of image-x alone and the LOCAL x-scale equals the LOCAL y-scale. That is why each bay pitch is divided by the storey pitch measured at the SAME x, and it is the step that would be wrong had the camera been tilted. 1.4028 and 1.4217 give 1.4123 +/- 0.0134, reproducing the dossier's 1.412 +/- 0.016 to 0.001.

bay.metres.why: The room module ON THE FACADE. The dimensioned drawing labels every Fleet double 12' x 14'; 14 ft is the facade dimension and 12 ft the depth. Reading B (12 ft on the facade) is refused in conflicts['which-room-dimension-is-the-facade'] because it gives a 2.59 m floor-to-floor.

roomDepth.metres.why: The room's DEPTH, carried for the record and drawn by nothing — this section builds no plan and no interior.

storey.shared.why: ONE STOREY HEIGHT FOR ALL SIX HALLS, from a dimensioned drawing divided by a measured ratio. It is not per-hall because nothing measured says the six differ: the six massHeights span 1.1 m while the ground under a SINGLE hall swings 0.8-2.7 m.

stack.fourStoreys.why: The four-storey stack, the same 12.086 m on every hall. What varies per hall is what is LEFT OVER above it.

check.arcgisStorey.why: THE OUT-OF-SAMPLE CHECK, and it is genuinely out of sample: arcgis.h is levels x 3.050 m, the facilities GIS formula (recon 0.1), and it was used nowhere in the derivation above. A dimensioned drawing and a photogrammetric ratio land 0.93% from it.

check.storeyResidualPct.why: The residual of that check, as a percentage. Under 1% between two completely independent routes to a floor-to-floor height is what closed A8.

parapet.Beagle.why: Beagle's parapet zone: what its OWN measured height leaves above the shared four-storey stack. It is NOT a measured parapet — it is the ground reference's width, and section 4.2's finding is why: the between-hall spread of 1.1 m is smaller than the within-hall terrain relief of 0.8-2.7 m that massHeights subtracts.

parapet.Challenger.why: Challenger's parapet zone: what its OWN measured height leaves above the shared four-storey stack. It is NOT a measured parapet — it is the ground reference's width, and section 4.2's finding is why: the between-hall spread of 1.1 m is smaller than the within-hall terrain relief of 0.8-2.7 m that massHeights subtracts.

parapet.Discovery.why: Discovery's parapet zone: what its OWN measured height leaves above the shared four-storey stack. It is NOT a measured parapet — it is the ground reference's width, and section 4.2's finding is why: the between-hall spread of 1.1 m is smaller than the within-hall terrain relief of 0.8-2.7 m that massHeights subtracts.

parapet.Atlantis.why: Atlantis's parapet zone: what its OWN measured height leaves above the shared four-storey stack. It is NOT a measured parapet — it is the ground reference's width, and section 4.2's finding is why: the between-hall spread of 1.1 m is smaller than the within-hall terrain relief of 0.8-2.7 m that massHeights subtracts.

parapet.Galathea.why: Galathea's parapet zone: what its OWN measured height leaves above the shared four-storey stack. It is NOT a measured parapet — it is the ground reference's width, and section 4.2's finding is why: the between-hall spread of 1.1 m is smaller than the within-hall terrain relief of 0.8-2.7 m that massHeights subtracts.

parapet.Meteor.why: Meteor's parapet zone: what its OWN measured height leaves above the shared four-storey stack. It is NOT a measured parapet — it is the ground reference's width, and section 4.2's finding is why: the between-hall spread of 1.1 m is smaller than the within-hall terrain relief of 0.8-2.7 m that massHeights subtracts.

ratio.navyOfStorey.why: The dark navy fascia band as a fraction of a storey, from frame 5e. The band keeps its MEASURED depth on all six halls (0.575 m); the masonry cap above it takes the whole of the ground reference's residue, which is what leaves every hall a cap between 0.64 and 1.74 m deep. Nothing sourced is scaled to fit.

fascia.shared.why: The fascia band in metres, one figure for all six because the storey is one figure for all six.

ratio.spandrelOfStorey.why: The painted spandrel band's depth as a fraction of a storey, from the three clean bands' full widths at half maximum. The dossier's 0.287 comes from a fixed threshold at redness 28; a half-maximum crossing is exposure-independent and gives 0.264, and the difference is recorded in conflicts['spandrel-band-depth-threshold-vs-fwhm'].

ratio.slabOfStorey.why: The bright slab line immediately under each spandrel, as a fraction of a storey. It is the floor structure's own edge and is drawn by nothing — it exists here so the window's height closes.

ratio.windowOfStorey.why: The window is the REMAINDER of its storey, not an independent read: window, spandrel and slab line partition the repeating unit exactly, so the three cannot drift apart.

ratio.spandrelOfStoreyMg.why: The painted spandrel band's share of its storey, from six cells of the Enginuity frame at sd 0.0021 — the tightest read in this section. It REPLACES the first round's 0.2643, which was the same band measured on three cells of the same frame by a different rule and lands 0.003 away.

ratio.wallAboveOfStorey.why: The solid wall above each window: the floor-line band and the window's own head reveal. sd 0.053 across six cells, because the reveal's edge is soft in a graded frame — but it is SOLID either way, and solid is the thing the first round spent on glass.

ratio.glassOfStorey.why: THE LIT PANE, and nothing else. sd 0.058 across six cells. The first round shipped 0.6817 — the whole storey less the spandrel, with no solid between storeys at all — so every bay read as one uninterrupted four-storey glass slot. That was a positive assertion of MORE glazing than the source shows, which is the inverse of everything else this section does. The visual critic's own re-profile of the same frame gives ~0.54; this build's is 0.4575, i.e. more conservative still, and it is the figure that ships.

ratio.wallBelowOfStorey.why: The solid wall between the window's sill reveal and the spandrel below it. sd 0.061, the same soft-edge caveat as the head.

check.storeySharesSum.why: THE PARTITION CLOSES. Each measured cell's four shares sum to 1 by construction, so their six means do; if this figure ever leaves 1 the four have stopped being a partition of one storey and one of them has been edited alone.

check.solidOfStorey.why: The solid share between one storey's glass and the next, which is the quantity the visual critic measured at ~0.23 and the first round shipped at ZERO. It is what makes four punched windows read as four windows.

facade.outerReturn.why: THE MASONRY RETURN AT THE OUTER CORNER, measured where the frame is most trustworthy: the last opening's outer jamb to the building's own arris, at the NEAREST end of the receding plane, expressed as a fraction of the local bay so foreshortening cancels. 10.81 px against a local bay of 184.5 px is 0.0586 of a module. The first round laid the first bay flush against the arris and the critic caught the glass wrapping the corner; the frame has a pier there.

ratio.openingWidthOfBay.why: The window-over-spandrel opening occupies this fraction of its bay. Each of the two measurable modules is a centre-to-centre bay pitch and takes the mean of the two spandrel widths that bound it, so foreshortening cancels rather than being corrected for.

ratio.openingOffsetOfBay.why: The opening is FLUSH TO THE BAY'S OUTER EDGE — the pier — so its inset from the bay's inner edge is the complement of its width. Corroborated independently by the measured gaps between consecutive spandrels: see check.gapOverModule.

check.gapOverModule.why: THE INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE OFFSET. The blank stretch between the end of one spandrel and the start of the next is the block infill of the next bay plus the pier; if the opening really is flush to the pier, that gap must equal the offset. 0.542 against 0.537 — 0.005 apart, on figures that share no arithmetic.

facade.baysPerFace.why: THREE BAYS PER LONG FACE, on three independent sources that meet on the same number: the drawing shows three doubles along one side of the suite, the Enginuity frame shows three bays ending at the building's outer corner with a recessed slot beyond the third, and the occupancy closes it — 80 beds over 4 storeys is 20 per storey, two suites of five doubles, one suite per bar.

facade.threeBays.why: Three bays in metres. Every long face in the survey is longer than this, and what is left is the stair slot.

check.fortyEightFt.why: THE ONE NON-CIRCULAR CHECK THE SLOT HAS. The dossier's clean imperial candidate for the whole long face is 48 ft = 3 x 14 ft + 6 ft, and 48 ft is a figure the survey never saw. The twelve merged faces run 14.50-14.90 m about a mean of 14.73 m, which sits 0.10 m — 0.7% — from it. That is a statement about the survey and the imperial hypothesis together; the slot band's agreement with the dossier is the same subtraction on both sides and is not.

check.bedsPerStorey.why: 20 beds per storey = two suites of five doubles = one suite per bar, which is the third independent route to 'three doubles on one side' and therefore to three bays.

check.parapetFormulaMin.why: The ArcGIS formula's own parapet residue on the SHORTEST hall, carried as the loser of conflicts['storey-height-vs-parapet']. The module route gives 1.214 m for Beagle against this 1.10 — 0.11 m apart on two independent storey heights.

check.parapetFormulaMax.why: The same residue on the TALLEST hall. Both methods hand the whole between-hall spread to the parapet, which is section 4.2's point: that spread is the ground reference's, not the buildings'.

identity.byPositionGalathea.why: THE PROOF. lidar.heights is measured over the OSM ring and keyed by the OSM NAME; lidar.massHeights is measured over the GIS ring and keyed by POSITION. Keyed by POSITION the building at (-41.7, 454.6) reads the same height twice, from two independent measurements over two different polygons: 0.00 m.

identity.byPositionMeteor.why: The same, at (-70.0, 462.6): 0.00 m. Two independent reads landing on the identical figure, twice, is the same building measured twice.

identity.byNameGalathea.why: AND THE COST OF BELIEVING OSM. Key the same two halls by NAME and both disagree by 0.7 m — a heights['Galathea Hall'] lookup puts Meteor's roof on Galathea. This section never performs a name lookup against a measured file.

identity.byNameMeteor.why: The mirror of the same error, 0.7 m the other way.

orthoFit.offsetZ.why: The z displacement of a Fleet ROOF plate in the 2026 ortho: 2.83 m toward -z, from 17 of 19 axis-aligned GIS roof edges 8 m or longer, trimmed at 1.2 m from the median.

orthoFit.northSouthGap.why: THE TEST THAT SEPARATES A TRANSLATION FROM AN INFLATION, and the reason the reading is usable at all. A shadow or a plate-growth artefact pushes north-facing and south-facing edges in OPPOSITE directions; these two move TOGETHER, 0.048 m apart on 11 and 6 edges. The plate is displaced bodily.

orthoFit.rateZ.why: A two-point rate in z: -0.567 m at h = 0 and -2.829 m at the Fleet roof band. PUBLISHED AND NOT USED. Its h = 0 leg rests on ONE clean z edge (arcgis.ground#2322's north edge, gradient 38.1), and the six halls span 13.3-14.4 m, an 8% range that gives no leverage at all to separate a constant from a rate.

orthoFit.xHeightDelta.why: x SHOWS NO HEIGHT DEPENDENCE AT ALL: -0.880 m at h = 0 (three surveyed ground edges) against -0.861 m at h = 13.9 (33 short roof edges). 0.019 m of difference over 13.9 m of height. On x this is a georegistration offset, not a displacement.

orthoFit.edgesX8m.derivation: A COUNT, and the count is the finding: not one x-constant GIS ring segment on any of the six halls reaches the 8 m length the z fit requires. The pinwheel's ears are 5-6 m long and that is the whole type.
orthoFit.edgesX8m.why: THE x AXIS IS NON-DISCRIMINATING BY CONSTRUCTION, not by bad luck. buildlog-revellecommons.md 13.5 established that an axis with too few usable edges must say so rather than be argued around; here the usable count is ZERO, and the 33 five-metre reads that do exist scatter with sd 1.50 m about a median of -0.861 m because each rests on a 6 m chord with a neighbouring plate 2 m away. Published below its own evidence threshold, with a gate that fails if a later agent promotes it.

orthoFit.edgesZ.derivation: A COUNT of the axis-aligned GIS roof segments 8 m or longer across all six halls.
orthoFit.edgesZ.why: 19 found, 17 kept. The two dropped are the two lowest-gradient south edges (240 and 190 against a population running to 1030), and they are dropped by the stated 1.2 m trim rather than by inspection.

orthoFit.correctionX.why: The x half of the correction to add to an ortho read of a Fleet ROOF feature. PUBLISHED BUT UNUSED: no ortho-derived position ships in this section, because the only two things the ortho would have placed — the roof membrane zone boundaries and today's bed outlines — are respectively withheld (absent A4) and already surveyed exactly (arcgis.ground).

orthoFit.correctionZ.why: The z half of the same correction, valid at the Fleet ROOF BAND ONLY. It may not be extrapolated to the tower cap and it may not be applied at ground level, where the same fit measures -0.567 m.

plan.registrationRms.why: The Garbini landscape plan's best similarity fit to the six GIS centroids leaves 4.72 m of residual. A 4.7 m residual is LARGER THAN A COURTYARD, so the plan gives this section every outdoor-room NAME and not one length.

ground.ownedRings.derivation: A COUNT of the surveyed arcgis.ground rings this section registers and draws: 13 planted beds, the one centralized lawn among them, and 2 paving patches.
ground.ownedRings.why: Not one of the 26 rings in the band is claimed by any existing section — all 77 arcgis.ground registrations across every key of campus-photo-detail.json were checked, with zero overlap. R3 inherits the Fleet quad's surveyed ground entire, and REGISTERS it rather than inventing beds on top of it.

ground.ownedArea.derivation: The sum of the 15 owned rings' outer-ring areas, in m2, by the shoelace over each ring as it is carried here. Summed UNROUNDED and rounded once at the end: summing the per-ring figures after each has been rounded to 2 dp gives 3257.13 and loses 0.03 m2 to accumulated rounding, which is small and is exactly the kind of drift an auditor is right to chase.
ground.ownedArea.why: The number exists so a later edit that drops or duplicates a ring moves it.

system.tower.overrun.extends: the single stair-tower cap read on Garbini frame 5e — parapet line at content y 65, cap at y 47, 0.50 storey pitches — carried to both C2-paired projections of all six halls on the type's declared symmetry
system.tower.overrun.why: [estimated] Ladder climbed and failed: photos — 5e is the only frame with a tower against sky and it is not orthographic, so 0.50 storey pitches converts to 1.5-1.7 m depending on which hall's storey height is used; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — none carry a section; archives — the mid-1960s aerial shows the element at the bar junction and its open switchback flights, and cannot measure its cap. The band is deliberately wider than the single read because a single oblique frame cannot carry a 0.1 m claim.
system.tower.overrun.bandWhy: 0.50 storey pitches across the six halls' own storey heights (3.043 to 3.295 m) is 1.52 to 1.65 m before any frame error. The band opens that to [1.2, 2.0] to carry the obliquity of a frame whose station is itself unfixed (absent A7), and it is the widest band in this section for that reason.

system.tower.depth.extends: the surveyed depth of the ring's own C2-paired projections — research 2.2 reads them as ~1.2 m deep x 3.0 m along the face, and this build re-derives their 2.3-3.2 m face lengths from the rings themselves
system.tower.depth.why: [estimated] Only the projection's OUTER skin reaches the survey line, so the ring gives the tower's width exactly and its depth into the building only approximately. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — no frame looks into a notch; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing; planning docs — the landscape plan draws the hall bodies as solid white and shows no notch; archives — the mid-1960s aerial shows the stair in the notch and cannot measure its depth.
system.tower.depth.bandWhy: The band is the survey's own ambiguity: the ring's projection stands 1.2 m proud of the face it interrupts, and the element behind it can be that deep or half a metre deeper without moving a surveyed vertex. Nothing outside [1.0, 1.5] is compatible with a stair.

reads.hand: Meteor and Challenger are mirrored in x relative to the other four. Read by rasterising each GIS footprint into its own bounding box at 56x56 cells and differencing against Galathea under the four axis-aligned symmetries; tolerance is the 15x separation between the matching and non-matching populations (3.1-3.3% against 48.3-49.3% of cells), not a threshold on either.
reads.roofPlane: ONE FLAT ROOF PLANE PER HALL. The ortho's two C2-paired 12x7 m rectangles inside each hall are membrane patches, not steps: their boundaries are a dark line 0.25-1.0 m wide with L 195-210 on BOTH sides, against the hall's own real cast shadow west of its west face which is 3.75 m wide at L 35-87. Tolerance: any level difference is under 1 m and is not resolvable at 0.125 m/px, so it is withheld rather than estimated.
reads.endWalls: The short end faces are blank and windowless in the mid-1960s aerial, against a fully modulated long face — the served/servant reading. Tolerance: this is a 60-year-old claim carried across an intervening 2010 renovation and NOT re-verified in any modern frame, so it decides nothing this build draws; both long and short faces receive the same two bands and no opening, and absent A3 carries the question.
reads.stairInNotch: An open switchback stair stands in the re-entrant corner of each hall in the mid-1960s aerial, and an element in that corner rises above the main parapet in Garbini frame 5e at 0.50 storey pitches. Tolerance +/- 0.4 m, which is why system.tower.overrun is banded [1.2, 2.0] rather than published as 1.6.
reads.wallFabric: Buff/sand concrete masonry laid in visible courses, ground- or split-face, ONE colour across all six halls in every frame that shows more than one. Tolerance: the three corroborating rectangles agree to 3 units in R and 1.4 units in G, well inside the 15-unit single-material bar.
reads.mulchSpread: Rounded river cobble / rock mulch, 50-150 mm, mean #ad9f86 with channel sd 57.8 / 60.7 / 63.0. Tolerance: THE SPREAD IS THE MATERIAL and no tile anywhere in it reaches sd <= 11, so the build must express it as a mean plus a declared spread and never as a flat colour — which is why the beds carry a coarse procedural relief rather than a plain fill.
reads.lawnSingular: Exactly ONE bright turf polygon exists in the band, arcgis.ground#2322, against twenty other green rings that read as rock-mulch beds with scattered specimen planting. Tolerance: none needed — this is a count, and it closes the landscape architect's own words ('One centralized lawn area was introduced', 'Large areas of lawn were replaced with non-organic ground cover of rock mulches') against the 2026 imagery exactly.
reads.orthoCorrection: The correction to add to an ortho read of a Fleet ROOF feature is (+0.861, +2.829) m, valid at the Fleet roof band only. Tolerance: sd 0.259 m on z over 17 edges; on x, NO TOLERANCE IS PUBLISHABLE because zero segments reach the fit's own 8 m length requirement. Nothing in this section consumes either figure.

draw.wallOffsetNote: A RENDER OFFSET, not a measurement: the treatment planes stand this far proud of the surveyed ring so they are not coincident with the extruded prism's own faces. It is not a claim that the masonry projects 60 mm.
draw.skirtDepthNote: A RENDER OFFSET: the wall plane is carried this far below each hall's datum so a rolling terrain cannot open a gap at its foot. The datum is already the MINIMUM drawn surface along the ring, so this only ever buries and never lifts.
draw.datumStepNote: A SAMPLING INTERVAL, not a dimension: the drawn surface is sampled every 2 m along each ring edge (and at every vertex) to find the hall's datum. Finer changes nothing measurable and costs a sampler call per metre of perimeter.
draw.towerDepthPadNote: A RENDER OFFSET: the tower box is inset this far from its projection edge at each end so its corners do not z-fight the two wall planes that meet it. It is not a claim about the stair's plan.
draw.faceMergeTolNote: A SURVEY-WOBBLE TOLERANCE, not a dimension: consecutive ring segments are merged into one facade run while every vertex stays within this distance of the run's own chord. The survey wobbles by up to 0.20 m along a single flat face and drops 0.1-0.3 m jogs into the middle of it. The value sits on a stable plateau — 0.20 and 0.25 both find exactly twelve long faces with identical lengths — and the test asserts that stability rather than trusting the number.
draw.openingProudNote: A RENDER OFFSET: the window and spandrel planes stand this much further out than the wall field so they resolve against it at grazing angles. It is not a claim that the glazing projects 20 mm; the real detail is a RECESS, and its depth is not measured in any source.
draw.bedRungNote: A LADDER RUNG, not a height: campus-world.js already draws every arcgis.ground ring on the `ground` rung, so this section's bed and lawn surfaces sit one rung above it on `carpet` and give the same surveyed polygon the Garbini project's material instead of the generic one. Nothing here re-outlines a ring.
draw.bedSegNote: A TESSELLATION TARGET, not a dimension: bed triangles are subdivided until no edge exceeds 3 m so the carpet follows the drawn terrain instead of spanning it. The ring's own boundary vertices are never moved.
draw.bedMaxDepthNote: A RECURSION CAP on that subdivision, so a pathological ring cannot generate an unbounded mesh. At depth 6 a 100 m triangle edge is already under 2 m.
draw.tilesNote: MATERIAL REPEAT LENGTHS in metres, not building dimensions: they set how often the code-generated texture repeats across a surface so the microstructure lands at true material scale — a 400 x 200 mm concrete masonry unit, a 1.2 m fascia panel, a 1.5 m patch of river cobble. The 1.0 m spandrel and window repeats are deliberately coarse: a painted panel and a pane have no unit at all, so the map is doing nothing but breaking a perfectly flat fill, and a finer repeat would invent a joint neither has. Texture maps are code-generated throughout; the sampled colours feed the materials and the photograph's pixels never do.

stack.storeysNote: FOUR, on four independent sources with no conflict: arcgis `levels` = 4 on all six, four window rows in the mid-1960s aerial, four window rows and four counted red spandrel bands in Garbini frame 5e, and four window rows in the Enginuity frame. A fifth now agrees arithmetically: 80 beds over four storeys is 20 per storey, two suites of five doubles, one suite per bar.
stack.model: 4 x storey + parapetZone = the hall's own massHeights, with storey SHARED and parapetZone the residual
stack.modelNote: ONE STOREY, SIX RESIDUES. The storey rests on a dimensioned drawing (12' x 14' doubles) divided by a photogrammetric bay:storey ratio, and is the SAME 3.0216 m on every hall because nothing measured says the six differ — the six massHeights span 1.1 m while the ground under a SINGLE hall swings 0.8-2.7 m, so the spread is the ground reference's. What varies per hall is the PARAPET ZONE, which is what that hall's own measured height leaves over the shared stack, and it is declared as the ground reference's width rather than as a measured parapet. This SUPERSEDES the earlier route that derived the storey from frame 5e's parapet ratio; see superseded['build.parapetRatioRoute'].
stack.parapetBandNote: The band is the residual's OWN range, evaluated and then rounded OUTWARD to two decimals so a two-decimal band cannot exclude its own endpoint: the shipped residues run 1.2138 m on Beagle to 2.3138 m on Atlantis. The research dossier publishes [1.21, 2.31], which rounds its upper endpoint INWARD and which its own arithmetic (14.4 - 12.088 = 2.312) does not permit. That is a correction to the dossier, recorded rather than silently adopted.
stack.splitNote: The parapet zone renders as TWO bands and neither is scaled to fit. The navy fascia band keeps its MEASURED depth of 0.5746 m on all six (frame 5e's own pixel read against the shared storey); the masonry cap above it takes the whole of the residue, 0.639 m on Beagle to 1.739 m on Atlantis. The cap is therefore the only element in this section whose depth varies per hall, and it varies because the ground reference does.

facade.baysNote:
THREE BAYS PER LONG FACE AT 14 ft, AND THE FACE IS NOT A RING EDGE. Every long face here is a maximal run of collinear ring segments — the survey wobbles by up to 0.20 m across a face and puts 0.1-0.3 m jogs in the middle of it — so the module merges them at draw.faceMergeTol and finds exactly TWELVE faces spanning 14.50 to 14.90 m, two per hall on both hands. Three bays is 12.802 m and the remainder is the stair slot, 1.698 to 2.100 m across the twelve.

THE SLOT'S AGREEMENT WITH THE DOSSIER'S [1.60, 2.10] IS NOT INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION AND THIS NOTE NO LONGER CLAIMS IT IS. The dossier derives that band by exactly this subtraction over exactly this survey, so both sides are the same arithmetic on the same source and a slot inside it is guaranteed by construction; the check is a consistency test that this build's face population matches the dossier's, and nothing more. What actually carries the bay count is three independent sources meeting on THREE — a dimensioned drawing, a photograph in which three spandrel runs can be counted directly, and an occupancy figure — plus one genuinely non-circular test the survey can run: a fourth bay does not fit any of the twelve faces, and three do, which is a statement about the survey and the drawing together rather than about either alone. The imperial hypothesis has its own out-of-sample check in check.fortyEightFt.
facade.slotEndNote: The slot sits at the RE-ENTRANT end of each long face and the bays run from the OUTER corner, which is what the Enginuity frame shows (three bays ending at the building's outer corner, a recessed slot beyond the third) and what the mid-1960s aerial shows (the vertical circulation at the junction of the two bars). The module chooses the end by distance from the hall's own bbox centre and never by a typed coordinate.
facade.outerReturnNote: The three bays start this far inboard of the face's OUTER arris, so the first opening cannot run into the corner. It is small — a pier's width — and it is measured at the least foreshortened end of the frame. What is left at the RE-ENTRANT end is the big blank panel the same frame shows, plus the stair beyond it, and it takes the whole of each face's own variation.
facade.openingRunNote: First jamb to last jamb: two bay pitches plus one opening width. This, not three times the bay, is the length the openings actually occupy on a face, and the two end margins are what is left of the face after it.
facade.reentrantMarginBandNote: What each face keeps at its re-entrant end: the face's own length less the outer return less the opening run. Evaluated over the twelve merged faces (14.50-14.90 m) it runs 3.738 to 4.139 m, and the band is those endpoints rounded outward to two decimals. It is BIG, and the Enginuity frame shows it: a whole unbroken block panel between the last window and the step back to the middle band.
facade.openingNote: ONE PANE OVER ONE PAINTED SPANDREL PER BAY PER STOREY, occupying 46.3% of its bay, with the block infill filling the rest. Vertically the storey partitions into FOUR shares, top down: solid wall 18.1%, glass 45.8%, solid wall 10.0%, painted spandrel 26.1%. THE TWO WALL SHARES ARE THE POINT. The first round gave the window the whole storey less the spandrel — 68.2% glass and no solid between storeys at all — so consecutive storeys' glazing touched and each bay rendered as one uninterrupted four-storey slot. That asserted MORE glazing than any source shows, which is the inverse of the withholding posture the rest of this section takes, and it is what the visual critic failed the halls on. The shares now come from six measured cells and the solid between storeys is simply the buff wall that was always there. See superseded['build.storeyGlassShare'].

groundClip.samplesNote: A SAMPLING COUNT, not a dimension: the drawn surface is read at nine stations across an opening's own 1.98 m width to find the highest ground under it. Finer changes no decision on this terrain and costs a sampler call per opening.
groundClip.rule: An opening ships only if its spandrel's FOOT clears the drawn surface at every station across its own width. Otherwise the whole opening is withheld and the bay carries plain wall.
groundClip.ruleNote: THE WHOLE OPENING GOES, NOT HALF OF IT. A window over no spandrel asserts a ground-floor detail nobody has photographed, which is exactly what absent A1 declines to invent. The clipped cells are all on storey 1 and all on the uphill side, which is where a building hung from one elevation meets a hillside. The count rose from twelve to sixteen when the storey's vertical shares were re-measured (superseded['build.storeyGlassShare']): the spandrel now sits at the very foot of its storey rather than 0.054 of a storey above it, so storey 1's band meets the ground sooner. That is the correction working, not a regression.
groundClip.terrainNote: These sixteen are a fact about docs/data/campus-lidar.json's drawn surface and not about the building: on flat ground the same section builds all 144. `counts` therefore declares the GRID the sources give (144) and this block declares what the real terrain withholds, so a change to either is visible separately.

facade.pierNote: NO PIER, MULLION OR TRANSOM IS BUILT. The bay module is sourced and the openings are placed on it, but the exposed concrete frame the Enginuity frame shows between bays has no measured width in any source, and a frame member at a chosen width would be an invented dimension laid over a sourced rhythm. The bays read as bays because the openings are on the module, not because a pier was drawn between them.

system.hangNote: THE STOREY GRID HANGS FROM ONE ELEVATION PER HALL — the parapet zone's foot — and steps down four times, so storey 1's slab line lands exactly on the drawn prism's own base. The alternative of seating it on the ring's ground MAXIMUM, so that no opening could ever be buried, was tried and REFUSED ON ARITHMETIC: it drives Beagle's masonry cap to -0.267 m and Galathea's to 0.054 m, i.e. it can only be paid for by squeezing or scaling the one element in this section whose depth is the ground reference's own width. See conflicts['where-the-storey-grid-is-hung'].

tower.note: The stair tower is the ONLY thing on these roofs that stands proud, and it is the only element in this section allowed above the drawn prism's own lid. Two per hall, on the ring's own C2-paired projections, derived from the ring and never typed. Its open switchback flights are NOT modelled (absent B2), and whether the slot beside them is glazed or open is unresolved and unbuilt (absent A9).

roof.note: ONE FLAT PLANE PER HALL AND NOTHING BUILT ON IT. campus-massing.js already closes each hall's prism at its own massHeights, so the plane exists; this section adds no roof object at all, and counts.roofObjects is a DECLARED ZERO rather than an omission. The two C2-paired membrane zones per hall are real, measurable in plan and recorded in `reads.roofPlane`; the level difference between them is under 1 m, is not resolvable, and is withheld in absent A4 rather than estimated.

wallBlock.source: [measured] garbini_2011_fleet-5e.jpg, content crop 720x407, x 536..548, y 164..176 (12x12 px, 144 px), channel means 151.2 / 137.9 / 111.5, channel sd max 1.2, Rec.709 luminance 138.8 (sd 0.8). Chosen by low-variance tile search over the sunlit left wall plane, not placed by eye. Corroborated twice on independent rectangles: x 530..542, y 164..176 gives #98896e (sd 1.7) and x 536..548, y 128..140 gives #958a72 (sd 1.9) — three rectangles inside 3 units of R. Buff/sand concrete masonry in visible courses; ONE colour across all six halls in every frame that shows more than one (2011).

parapetCap.source: [estimated] extends wallBlock's own sample. The cap is the same masonry fabric as the wall it finishes and no source distinguishes them: in garbini_2011_fleet-5e.jpg (2011) the cap band reads warm buff with B - R strongly negative over its whole depth, i.e. the same hue family in shade, and no rectangle inside it passes the sunlit threshold so no albedo can be sampled from it. It carries the wall's hex and is tiered [estimated] because it is an extension and not a sample.

fasciaBand.source: [sourced] garbini_2011_fleet-5e.jpg, content crop, x 464..470, y 76..82 (6x6 px, 36 px), channel means 38.8 / 41.8 / 49.8, channel sd max 2.4, Rec.709 luminance 41.8 (sd 1.5). Below the 120 sunlit threshold and therefore [sourced], never [measured]. It is a COLOUR and not a shadow: B > G > R across the whole band, and B - R is strongly negative on the masonry either side of it, which is what the two zero crossings that bound px.navy are (2011).

groundMulch.source: [sourced] garbini_2011_fleet-5e.jpg, content crop, x 60..320, y 300..390 (260x90 px, 23,400 px), channel means 172.8 / 159.1 / 134.3, channel sd 57.8 / 60.7 / 63.0, Rec.709 luminance 160.2 (sd 60.0). THE VARIANCE IS THE MATERIAL: no low-variance tile exists anywhere in the rock mulch at sd <= 11, because the material is 50-150 mm rounded river cobble. It fails the sd <= 15 single-material test by design, so it is [sourced] and the section says why rather than shrinking the rectangle until it passes (2011).

groundLawn.source: [sourced] asla-sd_2014-10-28_fleet-walk-facade-and-planting.jpg (ASLA San Diego award frame, EXIF DateTimeOriginal 2012-05-04, DateTime 2014-10-28 which is a Photoshop save stamp, Sony DSLR-A290), content crop 919x516, x 806..818, y 314..326 (12x12 px, 144 px), channel means 67.3 / 90.4 / 44.4, channel sd max 6.0, Rec.709 luminance 82.2 (sd 5.2). Below the sunlit threshold and therefore [sourced].

spandrelAccent.source: [sourced] garbini_2011_fleet-5g.jpg (Garbini & Garbini, landscape completed 2011), content crop rows 158..561 of 720x720, x 210..216, y 58..64 (6x6 px, 36 px), channel means 147.2 / 62.6 / 36.9, channel sd max 0.75, Rec.709 luminance 78.7 (sd 0.4). THIS IS GALATHEA'S OWN PAINT, and it is the only accent in this section attached to a NAMED hall: frame 5g carries the building's own applied lettering reading 'Galathea', with Galbraith's cantilevered roof on tapered columns behind and to the right, which puts the camera west of Galathea looking east. Below the 120 sunlit threshold at sd 0.75, so [sourced] and never [measured] — a perfectly clean sample demoted for being red, which is conflicts['tier-threshold-vs-saturated-colour'] doing exactly what it predicted.

spandrelAccentExtended.source: [estimated] extends spandrelAccent — Galathea's own sampled paint, carried to the five halls no frame names. The ladder is climbed in absent A2.
