What makes the extension legitimate rather than a guess is that the second climb WITHDREW the first climb's per-hall claim: comparing the three Garbini frames' accents by CHROMATICITY after a per-frame grey-world balance, rather than by raw hex, gives pairwise distances of 0.020, 0.027 and 0.046 — one paint at three exposures. The one residual difference is the ASLA frame at 0.083, and it is confounded by a different camera body and a different processing generation; it is recorded as an open question in absent A2, not as a second colour.

windowGlass.source: [sourced] garbini_2011_fleet-5g.jpg (2011), content crop, x 208..216, y 26..34 (8x8 px, 64 px), channel means 80.5 / 108.5 / 120.5, channel sd max 1.56, Rec.709 luminance 103.4 (sd 1.6). A pane on Galathea's own face, one storey above the spandrel sample. B > G > R across the tile, which is a pane returning sky and not a shadow. Below the sunlit threshold and therefore [sourced]; a pane has no albedo to measure in any case, which is why campus-materials.js gives glass no maps at all and lets it read from what it reflects.

groundPaving.source: [measured] asla-sd_2014-10-28_fleet-walk-facade-and-planting.jpg (ASLA San Diego, EXIF DateTimeOriginal 2012-05-04), content crop 919x516, x 590..602, y 326..338 (12x12 px, 144 px), channel means 152.0 / 147.0 / 143.0, channel sd max 1.4, Rec.709 luminance 147.8 (sd 1.4). Broad exposed-aggregate concrete, gently sloping and with NO STEPS, which is the 2011 regrade's own stated purpose.

fleets.colorSourcesNote: Every role carries the rectangle it was sampled from, the CHANNEL MEAN of that rectangle under `sampleL`, its maximum per-channel standard deviation under `sampleSd`, and its Rec.709 luminance under `luminance`. The tier is arithmetic over the first two against colorThreshold, in BOTH directions, and never a matter of how the prose reads.
fleets.colorNote: THE TWO FRAMES ARE 2011 AND 2014 AND THEY ARE THE ONLY COLOUR THIS ZONE HAS. The mid-1960s aerial is black and white and predates every repaint, so it decides form and nothing else; the 2026 ortho is never sampled for colour because nothing draped on this campus may take Apple or Google pixels, and because a roof plate is not a facade. Texture maps are code-generated; the sampled colours feed the materials and the photographic pixels never reach a surface.

colorThreshold.statisticNote: The statistic is the CHANNEL MEAN, (R + G + B) / 3, not a Rec.601 or Rec.709 luma — a weighted luma gives a materially different figure on a saturated colour and would move the tier of the fascia band and both spandrel accents. Every line additionally carries its Rec.709 luminance under `luminance` so the two are never confused; the tiers are identical under either statistic in this section, and that is a fact about these samples rather than a licence to swap them.
colorThreshold.note: The 120 / 15 pair is the Commons' rule (buildlog-revellecommons.md 13.7), carried unchanged, and it is measured and not chosen: the four controls below bracket it from both sides on this section's OWN two frames.

controls.what: 24x24 px of the exposed-aggregate walk in full sun, the lowest-variance tile in the region x 500..700 / y 300..400 at sd 2.31 — a control for the top of the sunlit population
12x12 px of sunlit block wall, a rectangle DISTINCT from the shipped wallBlock sample so the threshold is not justified by the thing it judges — the re-audit lesson from the Commons
12x12 px of facade in shade at sd 0.65, the cleanest shaded tile in the whole frame — a control for the top of the shaded population
12x12 px of the same block fabric in shade at sd 3.31 — the same material as sunlitWallGarbini, 48.9 units darker, which is the whole argument for the threshold

colorFallback.note: Empty by construction. This section borrows no hex from any sibling section and defines none of its own outside `colors`; every role resolves through a guard in the module that THROWS on an undeclared role, because campus-materials.js destructures `color = 0xffffff` and an unset role would otherwise ship as opaque white without throwing, warning or looking wrong in code.

samples.note: SAMPLES THIS SECTION MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CONSUME. They are not in `colors` on purpose: the bidirectional colour-role gate requires every declared role to have a consumer, and a hex with no consumer is how a stale value outlives its object. They live here so that whoever closes absent A2 and A7 does not have to re-measure them.

spandrelAccentRed.source: [sourced] garbini_2011_fleet-5e.jpg, content crop, THREE 6x6 rectangles on one hall's three readable storey bands: x 424..430 at y 115 (#782f1e, means 119.9/47.2/29.9, sd 1.9), y 151 (#80331f, means 127.6/50.9/31.4, sd 3.6) and y 187 (#81351e, means 128.7/52.7/29.7, sd 1.4). The three agree to 9 units in R; the hex here is their mean. A dull brick red (2011).
spandrelAccentRed.whyUnconsumed: Nothing may paint it, because nothing can say WHICH hall it belongs to — absent A7. The camera station of frame 5e is unfixed to the standard buildlog-revellecommons.md 13.1-13.2 demands.

spandrelAccentOrange.source: [sourced] asla-sd_2014-10-28_fleet-walk-facade-and-planting.jpg, content crop, 12x12 at x 438..450, y 48..60, channel means 129.8 / 73.0 / 26.4, sd max 0.9, Rec.709 luminance 81.7 (sd 0.6). Corroborated on a second hall-face rectangle at x 452..464, y 296..308 (#7c4012, sd 1.8). A distinctly ORANGER accent, 27 units of G from the red at comparable luminance, with sd <= 1.8 on both — far outside either sample's own noise (2014).
spandrelAccentOrange.whyUnconsumed: Same as the red: this is the OTHER hall's accent, and the section can prove two halls differ without being able to name either.

panelOpaque.source: [measured] garbini_2011_fleet-5e.jpg, content crop, 8x8 at x 410..418, y 138..146, channel means 174.4 / 185.7 / 175.6, sd max 4.2, Rec.709 luminance 182.5 (sd 3.1). The pale opaque panel at the pier returns (2011).
panelOpaque.whyUnconsumed: A pier return is a HORIZONTAL-rhythm object and this section ships no horizontal rhythm — absent A8. A [measured] hex with nowhere to go is exactly the case this block exists for.

counts.note: Declared counts, asserted against the built scene ON FLAT GROUND, which is where they describe the GRID THE SOURCES GIVE rather than what one particular terrain leaves of it. What the drawn LiDAR surface withholds is declared separately in system.facade.groundClip, so a change to the sources and a change to the terrain move different numbers. The three ZEROES are opinions, not omissions: on flat ground nothing is clipped, the roof zones' level difference is not resolvable, and the Keeling PV control returns negative on all six plates.

conflicts.what: Which of the two eastern halls is Galathea and which is Meteor. OpenStreetMap has the two names on each other's buildings, and the R3 brief inherited the swap from OSM before this section corrected it.
sides: OSM (docs/data/campus-3d.json): buildings[183] 'Galathea Hall' at centroid (-69.67, 462.80) and buildings[201] 'Meteor Hall' at (-42.65, 454.81). One crowd-sourced source, and the one the brief quoted.
campus-arcgis.json, the university's own 2014 GIS: massing[34] 'Galathea Hall' at (-41.70, 454.55) and massing[260] 'Meteor Hall' at (-69.95, 462.61). First-party.
UCSD HDH neighbourhood directory (undated, current as fetched): d = Galathea at the eastern position, e = Meteor at the western one. First-party.
UCSD Conference Services neighbourhood map, March 2019: Galathea east, Meteor west. First-party.

LiDAR, ARITHMETICALLY: heights[] is measured over the OSM ring and keyed by OSM name; massHeights is measured over the GIS ring and keyed by position. Keyed by POSITION the two differences are 0.00 m and 0.00 m; keyed by NAME both are 0.7 m. Two independent measurements over two different polygons landing on the identical figure, twice, is the same building measured twice.
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED FOR THE GIS / HDH / CONFERENCE READING, and the loser is recorded rather than deleted: the building at (-41.7, 454.6) is GALATHEA and the building at (-70.0, 462.6) is METEOR. Three independent first-party UCSD sources agree against OSM and the LiDAR proves it arithmetically in derivations.figures['identity.byPositionGalathea'] and ['identity.byPositionMeteor'], both of which evaluate to exactly 0. Nothing in campus-3d.json, campus-lidar.json or campus-arcgis.json is edited — they are builder output — and the consumer stays POSITION-KEYED so the swap cannot bite. This also EXPLAINS rather than corrects revelle-recon.md 2's apparent OSM-vs-GIS height disagreement for these two halls: it is an artefact of the label swap and not a measurement difference.

conflicts.what: Which survey draws the Fleet halls' outline. Both draw the same Z, at different resolutions and in slightly different places.
sides: OSM: 8-12 vertices per hall, no projections at all, areas 376-417 m2. Its rings are simpler and in one case demonstrably displaced.

GIS (campus-arcgis.json): 24-33 vertices per hall including the two C2-paired projections, areas 402.5-406.5 m2 with 0.5% rsd. Centroid separation from OSM runs Galathea 0.11 m, Discovery 0.32 m, Meteor 0.40 m, Atlantis 1.20 m, Beagle 1.25 m, and CHALLENGER 2.12 m — its OSM ring sits about 2 m east of its GIS ring.
conflicts.resolution: GIS WINS, AND NOT ON QUALITY GROUNDS: campus-massing.js extrudes the GIS mass, so a facade hung on the OSM line would float metres inside or outside the mass the eye actually sees. Challenger's 2.12 m centroid separation is the worst case and stays on the record. NOT AVERAGED — an averaged ring is a ring no survey drew.

conflicts.what: How each hall's LiDAR massHeights divides into four storeys and a parapet cap. Two methods give overlapping but not identical answers.
sides: The ArcGIS formula: arcgis.h = 12.2 on all six, which is levels x 3.05 m — a residential rule of thumb, not a survey (recon 0.1 is right that this is a formula). It leaves a parapet residue of massHeights - 12.20 = 1.10 m on Beagle to 2.20 m on Atlantis, a 1.00 m band across six copies of one detail.

The photograph's own ratio: the parapet cap is 0.370 storey pitches in Garbini frame 5e, measured here at 1x as 13.392 px against 36.193 px and read by the research dossier at 3x as 38/103 = 0.369. Applied to each hall's own massHeights it gives storey heights of 3.043-3.295 m and parapets of 1.126-1.219 m — a 0.09 m band, which is the right order for six copies of one detail.
conflicts.resolution: NEITHER OF THESE TWO IS THE SHIPPED ROUTE ANY MORE, and that is the point of keeping both. A third, better source arrived: the Conference Services sheet's dimensioned 12' x 14' Fleet double, divided by the bay:storey ratio measured photogrammetrically on the Enginuity frame, gives ONE storey of 3.0215 m resting on a drawing rather than on a parapet line nobody could see. The parapet then becomes the RESIDUAL (1.214 to 2.314 m), which is the honest shape of the thing, because section 4.2 already established that the between-hall spread is the ground reference's and not the buildings'. The ArcGIS 3.050 m formula survives as the OUT-OF-SAMPLE CHECK and lands 0.93% away, on a route that never touched it. The 5e parapet ratio (0.370) is retired as a route in superseded['build.parapetRatioRoute'] and kept on the record as the only independent check frame 5e can offer. NOTHING IS AVERAGED, and the loser of each pair is legible.

conflicts.what: Whether the storey pitch in Garbini frame 5e is constant. The research dossier reports 'three independent intervals agreeing to 0.9 px (2.5%)'; this build's re-measurement finds the three intervals monotonically increasing downward.
sides: Research 4.3: band centroids at content y 119.0 / 154.4 / 190.7 / 226.6, pitch 35.85 px from three intervals agreeing to 0.9 px.

This build's re-measurement of the same frame: centroids at 119.068 / 154.836 / 191.454 / 228.640, intervals 35.768 / 36.618 / 37.186 px — a MONOTONIC increase downward, which is perspective in a frame shot from the ground looking up, not noise. The storey-1 band is additionally contaminated: its full width at half maximum is 13.799 px against 8.967 / 9.526 / 9.752 on the other three.
conflicts.resolution: THE GRADIENT IS REAL AND IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY. The shipped pitch uses the TWO CLEAN INTERVALS between the three clean bands (36.193 px); the three-interval figure (36.524 px) is carried beside it as `px.pitchAllThree` and draws nothing. The two differ by 0.7%, which moves every shipped parapet by under 3 mm, so the disagreement changes no geometry — it is recorded because a later agent re-reading this frame will see the gradient too and should find it already on the record.

conflicts.what: The frame's own vertical geometry and the LiDAR stack disagree about where the lowest spandrel band sits. The topmost band reads 1.565 storey pitches below the parapet cap top; the stack is 4.370 pitches tall; so the four bands at one pitch spacing put the storey-1 band 0.194 pitches — about 0.60 m — BELOW the stack's own foot.
sides: The frame: the four band centroids and the cap top are all read off one image with sub-pixel crossings, and their spacing is internally consistent to 0.7%.

The LiDAR: massHeights is measured against the median terrain under each footprint, and the terrain relief WITHIN a single Fleet footprint runs 0.79-2.70 m. A wall standing at a station 0.6 m below the median is entirely ordinary on this site, and 0.60 m is well inside that swing.

The perspective gradient of conflicts['storey-pitch-perspective-gradient'] accounts for part of it and not all: at the frame's own bottom-of-frame pitch of 37.186 px the shortfall shrinks from 0.194 to 0.086 pitches and does not vanish.
conflicts.resolution: CLOSED BY THE MODULE ROUTE, and recorded rather than deleted because the failure was real. The 5e-anchored station hung the storey grid from the parapet CAP down through a photograph's own perspective gradient, and it did not close. The shipped grid is hung from the parapet ZONE's foot instead and steps down by one derived storey four times, so storey 1's slab line lands exactly on the prism's own base (lid - massHeights) by construction, with nothing to overhang. The 5e station reading survives as `ratio.roofAboveTopBand`, RECORDED and drawing nothing, and the conflict stays on the list because a later agent re-reading frame 5e will find the same 0.194-pitch shortfall and should find it already explained.

conflicts.what: Whether the 2026 ortho's plate displacement can be characterised on the x axis as it can on z.
sides: z: 19 axis-aligned GIS roof segments 8 m or longer, 17 kept within 1.2 m of the median, mean -2.829 m with sd 0.259. North-facing edges mean -2.812 on 11 and south-facing -2.860 on 6 — they move TOGETHER, which is a translation and not an inflation, so the reading is usable.

x: ZERO segments reach 8 m. NON-DISCRIMINATING BY CONSTRUCTION, not by bad luck — the pinwheel's ears are 5-6 m and that is the whole type. Lowering the threshold to 5 m yields 33 reads with sd 1.50 m about a median of -0.861 m, because each rests on a 6 m chord with a neighbouring plate 2 m away.
conflicts.resolution: PUBLISHED BELOW ITS OWN EVIDENCE THRESHOLD, with a gate, exactly as buildlog-revellecommons.md 13.5 did on the other axis. `orthoFit.edgesX8m` is a declared ZERO and the test fails if it ever becomes non-zero without the section re-arguing the axis. What the weak x reads do support is a NEGATIVE: -0.880 m at h = 0 against -0.861 m at h = 13.9 is no height dependence at all, so on x this is a georegistration offset rather than a displacement. It changes nothing either way, because NO ORTHO-DERIVED POSITION SHIPS IN THIS SECTION — the two things the ortho would have placed are the roof membrane zone boundaries (withheld, absent A4) and today's bed outlines (already surveyed exactly, and registered from arcgis.ground instead).

conflicts.what: The [measured] rule demotes a perfectly clean sample for being red. The Commons' threshold (channel mean >= 120, sd <= 15) was calibrated on PAVING, where a low channel mean means shade; an intrinsically dark saturated colour fails it at sd 1.4.
sides: The rule as written: spandrelAccentRed reads channel mean 68.7 at sd 3.6 and spandrelAccentOrange 76.4 at sd 0.9, so both are [sourced] and neither may claim [measured] however clean the rectangle is. The fascia band is demoted the same way at 43.5 / 2.4.
The samples themselves: sd 0.9 on a 144-px rectangle is as clean a read as exists anywhere in this section, cleaner than the [measured] wall at 1.2, and calling it [sourced] understates it.
conflicts.resolution: DO NOT RAISE THE TIER AND DO NOT LOWER THE THRESHOLD. The rule's scope is recorded here so the next section does not rediscover it as a defect: 120 separates SUNLIT from SHADED and says nothing about saturation, and no threshold on a channel mean can. The cost is borne — three genuinely clean samples ship as [sourced] — because the alternative is a per-colour exception, and an exception per colour is not a rule.

conflicts.what: Two adjacent dates for two adjacent projects, and the temptation to treat them as one date to average.
sides: Secondary sources give a 2010 BUILDING renovation of the Fleet halls. No primary source for it exists in this dossier: no architect, no scope, no drawings.
The landscape architect's own page and ASLA San Diego's award page both give 2011 as the year the LANDSCAPE was constructed, with a named principal and a named designer.
conflicts.resolution: TWO PROJECTS, TWO DATES, NOT ONE DATE TO AVERAGE. The 2011 landscape is primary-sourced and decides everything on the ground; the 2010 building renovation has no primary source and decides nothing here. It matters because absent A2 (the spandrel accents) and A3 (the blank end walls) both hinge on it: the 60-year-old blank-end-wall claim is carried across it, and any repaint that produced two different accent colours most plausibly happened in it. Who did it and what it changed is the second-highest-value open lead in this section.

conflicts.what: Whether the 2011 landscape plan can give this section a dimension. It cannot, and that is measured rather than asserted.
sides: The plan is the only drawing of this landscape that exists, it is north-up in the world frame's own orientation, and it labels every outdoor room.

Its best single-scale similarity fit from the six white hall bodies to the six GIS centroids, over all 720 correspondence permutations, lands at 5.038 px/m with rms 23.8 px = 4.72 m, and carries a systematic per-hall bias (four halls -3.5 to -4.9 m in x, two halls +7.9 to +9.0 m) — the signature of the white bodies being an off-centre PART of each pinwheel rather than the whole. A 4.7 m residual is larger than a courtyard.
conflicts.resolution: NAMES, TOPOLOGY AND CHARACTER FROM THE PLAN; EVERY DIMENSION FROM THE SURVEY RINGS. Not one length in this section is derived from the drawing. The failure is recorded with its number so that a later agent who finds a larger copy (absent A6) knows exactly what to beat.

conflicts.what: Whether the six halls carry different spandrel accent colours. The first climb read the frames as showing two or three different paints; the second climb withdrew that as an artefact of comparing RAW hex across frames with different exposures.
sides: FIRST CLIMB (withdrawn as published): raw hexes #7d321e (Garbini 5e), #82491a (ASLA) and a third greyer-olive read spread widely, so 'at least two, probably three, of the six halls carry different accent colours'.

SECOND CLIMB: sample each frame's own cleanest near-neutral tile, use it as a grey reference to build a per-channel gain, apply it to that frame's accent, renormalise to preserve exposure, and compare CHROMATICITY only. Pairwise distances among the three Garbini frames are 0.020, 0.027 and 0.046 — one paint at three exposures, and the residual spread is the light rather than the material.

WHAT SURVIVES: the ASLA frame sits 0.083 from Galathea, driven by g = 0.321 against 0.253, i.e. measurably yellower. Both frames have a clean neutral (sd 0.9 and 3.2), so this one pair is the only cross-frame comparison worth anything — and it is still confounded by a different camera body, a different processing generation, and a grey-world balance built on a single tile.
conflicts.resolution: ONE PAINT ON ALL SIX, AND ONE OF THEM IS NAMED. #933f25, sampled on GALATHEA — frame 5g carries the building's own applied lettering, which is the mechanism that fixed the station. The other five extend Galathea's sample as a labelled [estimated] role that carries the same hex, so the extension is visible in the data and not hidden inside one colour used twice. The ASLA frame's yellower read is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in absent A2 and not as a second colour: a single frame pair across two camera bodies is not enough to ship six halls in two colours. This REPLACES the first climb's ruling that no accent could be built at all, and the withdrawal is recorded in superseded['build.accentWithheld'] rather than applied silently.

conflicts.what: A building's storeys sit at one elevation; the drawn terrain under a single Fleet hall swings up to 2.66 m. Wherever those two meet on rising grade, the bottom storey's painted spandrel would sit partly under the drawn surface and emerge from it.
sides: HANG FROM THE PARAPET ZONE'S FOOT (shipped): the grid steps down four times from one elevation per hall and storey 1's slab line lands exactly on the drawn prism's own base, which is the median ground the LiDAR height is measured against. On the real surface this buries twelve of 144 openings, all on storey 1 and all uphill.

SEAT ON THE RING'S GROUND MAXIMUM: no opening could ever be buried, because the whole grid starts above the highest ground under the hall. Measured on the drawn surface this drives the masonry cap to -0.267 m on Beagle and 0.054 m on Galathea — the cap would have to be squeezed out of existence or the sourced storey scaled to pay for it.
conflicts.resolution: HANG FROM THE PARAPET ZONE, AND WITHHOLD WHAT THE GROUND WOULD BURY. The second option is refused on arithmetic and not on taste: it can only be paid for by scaling a sourced element, which is the one thing this section never does. So the grid keeps its one elevation per hall and an opening whose spandrel foot does not clear the drawn surface across its own width is NOT BUILT — the bay carries plain wall, exactly as the stair slot does, and absent A1 already declines to invent a ground-floor treatment. The twelve clipped cells are counted in system.facade.groundClip, per hall, and they are a fact about the terrain rather than about the building: on flat ground the same section builds all 144.

conflicts.what: The dimensioned drawing labels the Fleet double 12' x 14'. Which of the two is the FACADE dimension and which the depth.
sides: Reading A — 14 ft on the facade: bay 4.2672 m, storey = 4.2672 / 1.412 = 3.022 m, four storeys 12.09 m, leaving 1.21-2.31 m of parapet against measured heights of 13.3-14.4 m.

Reading B — 12 ft on the facade: bay 3.6576 m, storey 2.590 m, four storeys 10.36 m. A 2.59 m floor-to-floor is not habitable and 10.36 m is 3-4 m short of every measured height. Its seduction, recorded so nobody re-derives it: 14.7 / 3.6576 = 4.019, a near-perfect integer number of bays. That is a coincidence of 12 ft dividing 14.7 m and it breaks the height.
conflicts.resolution: READING A, and its check is genuinely out of sample — the ArcGIS facilities formula gives 3.050 m from a completely different source and was used nowhere in the derivation. 3.0215 against 3.050 is 0.93%. Reading B stays on the record with its integer coincidence named, because that coincidence is exactly what would tempt the next agent.

conflicts.what: The same Conference Services sheet carries a 'Blake/Argo Residence Hall' panel with its own dimensioned rooms, and those figures belong to R1's already-shipped sections.
sides: FLEET: doubles 12' x 14'. Five per suite, three along one side, and that is this section's bay module.
BLAKE / ARGO: doubles 10' x 13.5', a single at 7' x 13.5', triples at 10.5' x 12.5' and 14' x 10.5'. A DIFFERENT module on a different building type.
conflicts.resolution: A USEFUL NEGATIVE, DECLARED SO IT CANNOT BE BORROWED IN EITHER DIRECTION. The Fleet type is not the Argo/Blake type; R1's figures must never be imported here, and this section's 4.2672 m bay must never be exported to `argo` or `blake`. The test greps this section for every Argo/Blake figure on that sheet and fails if one appears. The two panels sharing one PDF is precisely the condition under which a cross-contamination happens without anyone deciding to do it.

conflicts.what: Whether the Enginuity facade frame may be colour-sampled. It is the highest-resolution frontal view of a Fleet facade that exists, and it is graded.
sides: The frame is Photoshop CS6 output with a film emulation: its whole-frame channel means are R 153.0 > G 147.7 > B 140.2, its windows read teal and its concrete magenta.

The research dossier states that no colour-neutral surface exists in it at any sensible threshold, the most balanced candidate being 8.3 units off-grey at sd 10.0. THIS BUILD'S OWN SEARCH DISAGREES SLIGHTLY: a 12x12 tile at (597, 671) reads #7f7f7f, 0.09 units off-grey, at sd 14.77 — marginally inside the section's own sd <= 15 bar.
conflicts.resolution: GEOMETRY ONLY, AND THE RULING IS UNCHANGED BY THE CORRECTION. A grey-world balance built on one marginal tile of a demonstrably graded frame cannot carry a colour, and the 12.8-unit whole-frame channel skew is the thing that disqualifies it, not the absence of any grey pixel. So the frame sets the bay:storey ratio, the spandrel band's depth and the opening's place in its module, and no hex in this section cites it. The dossier's stronger wording is corrected here rather than repeated.

conflicts.what: Which EXIF field is an epoch. Two of this section's three photo sets would have been mis-dated by up to 2.5 years on the wrong one.
sides: `DateTime` on the ASLA frame reads 2014-10-28 and the file's own NAME carries that date; `DateTime` on the Enginuity frame reads 2014-11-17. Both are Photoshop save stamps.
`DateTimeOriginal` reads 2012-05-04 and 2012-01-19 respectively — the capture dates, confirmed by `DateTimeDigitized` agreeing with each to the second.
conflicts.resolution: ONLY `DateTimeOriginal` IS AN EPOCH; `DateTime` is a save stamp. The correction IMPROVES both sources rather than weakening them: 2012-05-04 is about a year after the 2011 Garbini completion, so the landscape is newly established rather than three years weathered, and the Enginuity set at 2012-01-19 is closer still. Every ground colour in this section is therefore an EARLY-2012 read. The ASLA file keeps its misleading filename because it is on disk under that name and renaming a cached artefact breaks its hash; the section says so instead. This generalises to R4-R6 and is the reason it is a conflict rather than a footnote.

conflicts.what: How deep the painted spandrel band is, as a fraction of its storey. Two measurements of the same three bands in the same frame differ by 8%.
sides: The dossier reads 37 px against a 129 px storey = 0.287, by thresholding redness at a fixed value of 28.
This build reads the three bands' FULL WIDTHS AT HALF MAXIMUM — 33.24, 34.78, 34.70 px against a 129.56 px storey = 0.264 — which is exposure-independent, where a fixed threshold is not.
conflicts.resolution: THE HALF-MAXIMUM CROSSING SHIPS, at 0.264, and the threshold read stays on the record. The band is flat-topped with a steep fall on both sides, so the two disagree only about where its edge is, and a crossing defined relative to the band's OWN plateau cannot move when the exposure does. The independent 5e read (ratio.spandrel5eOfStorey) lands 0.004 of a storey from the shipped figure, which is the corroboration that decided it.

build.storeyGlassShare.claims: This section's own first-round vertical partition of a storey — window 0.6817, spandrel 0.2643, slab line 0.0540 — under which the glazing took the whole storey less the spandrel and no solid wall stood between one storey's glass and the next.
build.storeyGlassShare.why: IT ASSERTED MORE GLAZING THAN THE SOURCE SHOWS, WHICH IS THE ONE DIRECTION THIS SECTION IS NEVER ALLOWED TO ERR IN. The first round measured the window as the OPENING — reveal to reveal, by the zero crossings of B - R — and then, having declared the concrete frame absent, spent the frame's share of every storey on glass as well. The result rendered as one uninterrupted four-storey glass slot per bay, which the visual critic failed all three halls on. Declaring an element ABSENT removes it; it does not license giving its share to a neighbouring element. The replacement measures the LIT PANE inside the opening on six cells and leaves both reveals and the floor-line band as the buff wall that was already there, so the correction costs no new geometry and no new colour.

build.openingsFlushToTheArris.claims: This section's own first-round rule that the opening sits FLUSH to its bay's outer edge, which laid the first bay's jamb exactly on the face's outer arris and left no masonry return at the corner.
build.openingsFlushToTheArris.why: THE FLUSH READING WAS UNDERDETERMINED AND THE FRAME REFUTES IT. It rested on the measured blank stretch between consecutive spandrels matching the module less the opening width — but that gap equals M - w for ANY constant offset within the module, so it never constrained where in the module the opening sits. Measuring the building's own ARRIS settles it: at the least foreshortened end of the frame the last opening's outer jamb stands 10.81 px inside the corner against a local bay of 184.5 px, so there is a pier's width of masonry there and the glass does not wrap the corner. The visual critic caught the rendered result before this measurement was made.

build.parapetRatioRoute.claims: This section's own first-round route to a storey height: f = massHeights / 4.36999, from frame 5e's parapet-cap-to-storey-pitch ratio of 0.370, giving six different storey heights of 3.043 to 3.295 m.
ships: fleets.system.stack.storey (one figure, 3.0215 m, from a dimensioned drawing)
fleets.derivations.figures['parapet.Beagle'] and its five siblings, now residuals
build.parapetRatioRoute.why: SUPERSEDED BY A BETTER SOURCE, NOT REFUTED. The ratio itself is a real read of a real edge pair and this build reproduced it independently at 1x (0.370) against the dossier's 3x read (0.369). What was wrong with it as a ROUTE is that its denominator was a storey pitch measured in a frame whose GRADE LINE IS NOT VISIBLE — the dossier says so in its own section 4.3 — so the model could not be checked against the ground it was supposed to stand on, and it duly failed to close: the storey grid it implied put the lowest spandrel band 0.194 storey pitches below the stack's own foot. The Conference Services sheet's dimensioned 12' x 14' double replaces a ratio with a DRAWN DIMENSION, and the resulting storey lands 0.93% from the ArcGIS facilities formula, which the derivation never touched. Both ratio figures stay in `derivations.figures`, labelled RECORDED, NOT BUILT, because they are the only independent check frame 5e can offer the shipped route.

build.accentWithheld.claims: This section's own first-round ruling that NO spandrel accent could be built on any hall, and its declared zero for counts.spandrelBands.
ships: fleets.colors.spandrelAccent (#933f25, sourced on Galathea by name)
fleets.colors.spandrelAccentExtended (the same hex, tiered [estimated], on the other five)
build.accentWithheld.why: THE PREMISE WAS TRUE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN AND IS FALSE NOW, AND BOTH HALVES OF IT FELL SEPARATELY. It rested on two facts: that no accent could be attached to a NAMED hall (camera stations unfixed), and that the frames showed at least two genuinely different paints. The first fell to Garbini frame 5g, which carries the building's own applied lettering reading 'Galathea' with Galbraith behind it — the halls are individually signed, and a sign is a station. The second fell to a re-analysis: comparing accents by CHROMATICITY after a per-frame grey-world balance, rather than by raw hex across frames of different exposure, collapses the three Garbini reads to pairwise distances of 0.020 / 0.027 / 0.046 — one paint at three exposures. What survives is the ASLA frame's 0.083, confounded by camera body and processing generation, and it is carried forward as an open question inside absent A2 rather than shipped as a second colour.

absent.horizontalRhythm.claims: This section's own absent A8, which withheld the entire horizontal facade rhythm — bay count, pier spacing, window widths and every opening — for want of any source.
ships: fleets.system.facade.opening (width, offset, spandrel, slab and window fractions)
absent.horizontalRhythm.why: RETIRED CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER, and the entry's own ladder is what closed it: the rung it named as unclimbed was planning docs, and the document that closes it is a dimensioned UCSD Conference Services suite plan (12' x 14' doubles, three along one side of the suite) that the first climb chased on the wrong host. Three independent sources meet on three bays — that drawing, the Enginuity frame's three bays ending at the outer corner, and the occupancy arithmetic of 80 beds over four storeys. What A8 also withheld and this section STILL withholds is the exposed frame between the bays: no source gives a pier width, so no pier is drawn, and system.facade.pierNote says so. The retired text is carried verbatim in absent A8.
absent.horizontalRhythm.retiredText: A8 — THE ENTIRE HORIZONTAL FACADE RHYTHM: bay count, pier spacing, window widths, mullions, the pale opaque panel at the pier returns, and every opening. The VERTICAL rhythm is measured to 2.5% and ships; the horizontal has no source at all. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — the two colour frames show a modulated long face but neither shows one whole face end to end with countable bays; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — no elevation exists in any cached document; archives — the mid-1960s aerial resolves four window rows and the served/servant reading, and at its oblique angle and resolution a bay count on a named face cannot be taken from it. counts.openings is a DECLARED ZERO. A ribbon of glazing at a guessed module would be an invented rhythm on a sourced building.

revelle.absent[3].claims: The withholding of the six Fleet halls for want of verified imagery, which this section retires by building them from two dated colour frames, one dated aerial, one landscape plan, three first-party identity sources and the 2014 LiDAR.
ships: fleets.measured.halls (six surveyed rings, six positions, six heights, two hands)
fleets.system.stack (four storeys and a parapet cap over each hall's own massHeights)
fleets.system.tower (twelve stair-tower overruns on the rings' own C2-paired projections)
fleets.measured.groundRings.owned (fifteen surveyed rings of the 2011 Garbini landscape)
revelle.absent[3].why: THE ENTRY'S PREMISE IS FALSE AS OF THIS DOSSIER, AND IT IS RETIRED BY EVIDENCE RATHER THAN BY ASSERTION. 'No verified imagery' was true of the R1 recon and is not true now: two dated colour photographs (Garbini 2011, ASLA EXIF 2014-10-28) show the facade system square-on, the mid-1960s UCSD Digital Collections aerial bb1639263c shows all six halls in one frame, and the landscape architect's own labelled plan and project text describe the ground. What the imagery does NOT do is name which hall is in which frame, and that limit is carried forward as this section's absent A7 rather than being quietly inherited by the retirement. The entry's text is carried VERBATIM in the absent list below and is not deleted from anywhere.
revelle.absent[3].retiredText: Six fleet halls (Atlantis, Beagle, Challenger, Discovery, Galathea, Meteor) — no verified imagery

research.orthoDisplacementConstant.claims: The research dossier's published correction of (+0.85, +2.79) m for a Fleet roof feature, as a figure this section would consume.
research.orthoDisplacementConstant.why: NOT WITHDRAWN AS WRONG — this build's independent re-fit reproduces it to 0.014 m in x and 0.039 m in z, which is about as good as an independent re-measurement of an 8 px/m raster gets, and the local figures (+0.861, +2.829) are what ship in its place. It is withdrawn as a figure ANYTHING CONSUMES. The two things an ortho read would have placed here are the roof membrane zone boundaries, which absent A4 withholds because the level difference under them is not resolvable, and today's planting-bed outlines, which arcgis.ground already surveys exactly and which this section registers rather than re-draws. A correction with nothing to correct is a figure waiting to be misapplied, so it is published, gated and consumed by nothing.

fleets.supersededNote: Machine-readable retirements. Every record declares a disposition — `transferred` to a named successor that ships something in its place, or `deleted-on-evidence` with the ground stated — because a field that reads as a transfer when the object was deleted says the opposite of what happened. Absent lists never shrink: an entry leaves only by being carried VERBATIM inside a retirement entry that names its successor.
absent: A1 — THE COURTYARD FLOORS AND EVERY HALL'S GROUND-FLOOR TREATMENT. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — the ASLA, Garbini and Enginuity frames are all taken ALONG the walks and not one of the nine enters a courtyard to look at a hall's ground storey square-on; Street View — this is a pedestrian quad, car coverage does not enter it, and trekker or photosphere coverage was not established; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the Garbini plan draws the courtyards in plan and says nothing of their walls, and the Conference Services sheet is a suite plan with no elevation; archives — the mid-1960s aerials are obliques that cannot see into a courtyard, and what they DO show at ground level between the halls (single-storey linking and lounge elements) may not have survived the 2010-11 Bundy & Thompson renovation or the 2011 regrade. No ground-floor treatment is invented: every face carries the same wall and band system, storey 1 gets the same three-bay opening grid as the storeys above it, and no entrance, recess, link or lounge is drawn.

A2 — WHETHER ANY HALL'S ACCENT DIFFERS FROM GALATHEA'S. This entry no longer withholds a colour — it withholds a DIFFERENCE. #933f25 is sampled on Galathea BY NAME (frame 5g's applied lettering) and extends to the other five as a labelled [estimated] role. What is unresolved is the ASLA frame's read, which after a per-frame grey-world balance sits 0.083 in chromaticity from Galathea, driven by g = 0.321 against 0.253 — measurably yellower, on the frame with the cleanest neutral reference of any (sd 0.9). Ladder climbed and failed: photos — five accent samples across five frames now exist and the three Garbini ones collapse to one paint at three exposures (pairwise 0.020, 0.027, 0.046), so the ASLA pair is the only comparison left and it is confounded by a different camera body and a different processing generation; Street View — unclimbed, and still the rung that would settle it by putting all six halls under one sensor; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — no elevation and no finish schedule in any cached document; archives — the mid-1960s aerial is black and white and predates every repaint. A single frame pair across two cameras is not enough to ship six halls in two colours, and the FIRST climb's ruling that at least two differ is withdrawn in conflicts['spandrel-accent-differs-by-hall'].

A3 — WHETHER THE BLANK END WALLS ARE STILL BLANK. The mid-1960s aerial shows windowless short faces against a fully modulated long face, the served/servant reading, and the Enginuity frame corroborates it for one hall — its right-hand corner turns onto a plain block plane with no opening in it. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — no frame shows a short face square-on, and the Enginuity corner is too oblique to count what is not there; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the Conference Services suite plan shows five bedrooms and no elevation; archives — mid-1960s only, and the claim is carried across the 2010-11 renovation. THE CLAIM NOW HAS A FIRM TO CHASE: Bundy & Thompson Architects (David Thompson) did that renovation, named by the civil engineer. This section builds the three-bay opening grid on LONG faces only; short faces carry wall and bands and no opening, which is the one arrangement neither reading falsifies.

A4 — THE ROOF-ZONE LEVEL DIFFERENCE. The two C2-paired 12 x 7 m membrane zones per hall are real, measurable in plan, and bounded by a dark line 0.25-1.0 m wide with L 195-210 on BOTH sides — against the hall's own real cast shadow at 3.75 m wide and L 35-87, which is what a genuine step of that size would look like. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — no Fleet roof is visible from the ground in any of the nine frames; Street View — same; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — none; archives — the mid-1960s aerial shows one plane per hall and nothing stepping in height. Any level difference is under 1 m and is not resolvable at 0.125 m/px. ONE FLAT PLANE PER HALL IS BUILT, the zones are recorded in reads.roofPlane, and the level is left unresolved.

A5 — THE PLANTING SPECIES LIST. The firm says 'native, resilient' and the frames show recognisable FORMS — agave-type rosettes, red and orange flowering spikes, blue-grey sub-shrubs, ornamental grasses, multi-stem specimen trees — but no frame resolves a species, including frames 5g and 5i which show the same forms at higher resolution. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — exhausted at nine frames; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the Garbini plan carries a planting LAYOUT whose legend is not legible at 710 px, which is the same lead as A6; archives — irrelevant, the planting is 2011. The beds ship as surveyed ground with the mulch's own measured mean and declared spread, and NO PLANT IS MODELLED AND NO SPECIES IS NAMED.

A6 — A REGISTRABLE COPY OF THE GARBINI LANDSCAPE PLAN. Ladder climbed and FAILED WITH A VERIFIED NEGATIVE on its web rung: the WordPress media REST index reports media_details.sizes for featured_5a.jpg as {full: 720x720, medium: 300x300, thumbnail: 150x150}, so 720 x 720 IS the full size on that host, and probes for -1024x1024, -1536x1536, -2048x2048, -scaled, _full and -large all return 404. photos — not applicable; Street View — not applicable; drone/video — not applicable; planning docs — the firm's own host is exhausted and the remaining rungs are off-web (the firm's own files, UCSD Facilities Design & Construction's record set, or an ASLA award submission PDF); archives — not chased. Section 7.2's 4.72 m registration residual is therefore PERMANENT from this source, and the ruling stands: the plan gives names and topology and no dimension. Closing it would still close A5 and put every specimen tree on a coordinate.

A7 — THE CAMERA STATIONS OF FOUR FRAMES. NARROWED, NOT CLOSED. Galathea's station is fixed by the building's own applied lettering in frame 5g, with Galbraith's cantilevered roof on tapered columns behind and to the right; MG_2310's is fixed by 64 Degrees and its umbrellas in the background, which puts it looking north. Still open: frames 5e, 5h, 5i and MG_23022. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — none of the four catches a name sign or a fixable neighbour; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — none; archives — the mid-1960s aerial fixes all six positions and shares no epoch with any colour frame. VERIFIED NEGATIVE: no GPS exists on any of the nine cached photographs — the Garbini six carry no EXIF at all, and the ASLA and Enginuity frames carry EXIF without a GPS IFD — so A7 cannot be closed by EXIF for any frame. PER-HALL LETTERING IS THE MECHANISM that closed the one it closed: the halls are individually signed, so any future frame that catches a sign resolves its own station. The zone rule forbids rendering lettering, so the signs are a research instrument here and never geometry.

A8 — RETIRED — see superseded['absent.horizontalRhythm']. The retired entry is carried VERBATIM and character-for-character between the delimiters, and this list does not shrink: RETIRED ENTRY 1 of 1 <<A8 — THE ENTIRE HORIZONTAL FACADE RHYTHM: bay count, pier spacing, window widths, mullions, the pale opaque panel at the pier returns, and every opening. The VERTICAL rhythm is measured to 2.5% and ships; the horizontal has no source at all. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — the two colour frames show a modulated long face but neither shows one whole face end to end with countable bays; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — no elevation exists in any cached document; archives — the mid-1960s aerial resolves four window rows and the served/servant reading, and at its oblique angle and resolution a bay count on a named face cannot be taken from it. counts.openings is a DECLARED ZERO. A ribbon of glazing at a guessed module would be an invented rhythm on a sourced building.>> Its own ladder named the rung that closed it — planning docs — and the first climb had chased the wrong host. What it withheld that is STILL withheld is the exposed concrete frame between the bays: no source gives a pier width, so no pier, mullion or transom is drawn.

A9 — WHETHER THE STAIR SLOT IS GLAZED OR OPEN. Frame 5h shows the stair tower in full as a TALL GLAZED SLOT with the flights visible behind glass; frame 5e reads the same element as OPEN. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — two frames of the nine disagree and neither is stationed (A7), so they may not even be the same hall; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — none carry a section or an elevation; archives — the mid-1960s aerial sees the flights obliquely and cannot see whether anything stands in front of them. NEITHER IS SHIPPED. The 1.70-2.10 m stair slot at the re-entrant end of every long face carries the plain wall field and no opening at all — not a glazed enclosure and not a void — which is the only state that neither frame contradicts.

A10 — THE TWO PAVING MEDALLIONS' POSITIONS. Their EXISTENCE is sourced twice over: MG_2306 shows a circular red-oxide concrete inlay in the walk, scored into radiating segments, reading REVELLE COLLEGE 1964 with PURPOSE / TRUTH / VISION and roughly 4-5 m across against the slab joints; and the Conference Services sheet's own photograph shows a SECOND, smaller cast disc set flush in concrete reading REVELLE COLLEGE / EST 1964 with an anchor and rim lettering naming REVELLE COMMONS, BLAKE HALL and REVELLE PLAZA — a direction marker, distinct from the first. Ladder climbed and failed on POSITION: photos — neither frame is stationed; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the Garbini plan will not register (A6); archives — both are post-1964 hardscape. The 2026 ortho does not resolve either: a search for compact reddish blobs across the whole band returned only rock-mulch beds, whose fill fractions of 0.29-0.84 are bed shapes and not discs. Build them only when a position is found; the zone rule forbids rendering their lettering in any case.

A11 — THE UNDERGROUND UTILITY TUNNELS. Enginuity names them explicitly — the 2010-11 work was done 'while dodging the underground utility tunnels that are prevalent in this area' — so their existence under this quad is first-party sourced. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — nothing below grade is photographable; Street View — same; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — no utility drawing is cached and none is on the open web; archives — none. Unmodelled and unlocated, and recorded because it is a real constraint on anything a later agent ever digs, plants or founds in this quad.

B1 — THE BUILT-IN SEATING, THE HANDRAILS, THE TRENCH DRAINS AND THE BIOSWALES. The landscape architect's text names the seating and the swales and the frames show them clearly: MG_2310 shows the row of rectangular precast blocks with lawn on one side and gravel on the other, the ASLA frame shows the same blocks with recessed square light fittings in their faces, MG_2305 shows a slotted metal channel grate set flush across the walk where rock mulch meets paving, and Garbini 5c and 5e show a slender round-section metal rail along the regraded ramps. Ladder climbed and failed on POSITION: photos — they show WHAT the objects are and not WHERE they are, because only two of the nine frames are stationed and neither is one of these; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the Garbini plan draws the walk and the swale alignment and will not register (A6); archives — all four objects are 2011 and post-date every aerial. Better absent than placed on a guess.

B2 — THE STAIR FLIGHTS THEMSELVES. The mid-1960s aerial shows open switchback flights in each hall's re-entrant corner, unmistakably, with the treads reading as a zigzag against the shadow, and frame 5h shows them again behind glass. What ships is the tower's OVERRUN above the parapet, banded and labelled; the flights, landings, guarding and the opening they sit in are not modelled, and whether that opening is glazed is separately unresolved (A9). Ladder climbed and failed: photos — 5e and 5h disagree about the enclosure and neither dimensions a tread; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — none carry a section; archives — the aerial resolves the arrangement and cannot dimension it.

B3 — EVERY SPECIMEN TREE. The landscape architect's text says large specimen trees replaced old and poor existing specimens, the 2026 ortho shows canopies, the Enginuity frame shows a mature pine standing in the quad, and arcgis.ground#2101 is a 361-vertex 12 m2 ring that is a TREE PIT rather than a bed — so at least one tree's POSITION is surveyed. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — the frames show multi-stem forms and no species (A5); Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the plan's planting layout is illegible at 710 px (A6); archives — the planting is 2011. The pit ships as the surveyed ring it is; no trunk, no canopy and no species.

B4 — THE ELEVEN SURVEYED GROUND RINGS THIS SECTION HANDS FORWARD RATHER THAN DRAWS: THREE cross the x -152 Keeling line — #343, #1133 and #404. #344 does NOT: its whole extent (x -149.5..-144.8) is east of that line, and it is a boundary ring because it runs z 405.6..417.2 and so lies mostly NORTH of the band's z 414 edge, on the Revelle Walk seam. #405 and #2148 fall mostly south of z 475, #1131 is 91% below the band, #1742 is the Galbraith / La Jolla Project field, and #3584, #3632 and #4331 are campus-wide blobs that merely clip it. Ladder: not applicable — nothing about these is unresolved, they are OUT OF SCOPE, and they are listed here because a ring silently clipped at a boundary looks exactly like a ring nobody noticed. They are named individually in boundary.handedForward so R6 inherits a list and not a search.

B5 — THE INTERIOR, all of it. The Conference Services sheet gives a suite LAYOUT with five 12' x 14' doubles, a bathroom block and a lounge, and that is exactly as far as it goes: no section, no ceiling height, no stair, no service riser and no dimension for the lounge. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — exterior only; Street View — exterior only; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the suite plan is the one document that yielded, and it yielded a module and not a building; archives — the mid-1960s aerial is an exterior oblique. Nothing interior is modelled and no window looks into anything. hdhughousing.ucsd.edu/_files/revelle-overview-layouts.pdf remains image-only and worth a render by a later agent.

B6 — PHOTOVOLTAICS. The keeling.roofs.pv control returns NEGATIVE on all six Fleet halls: the 2026 ortho shows the two membrane zones and nothing else on any of these roofs, and no array, rail, ballast block or inverter reads anywhere on the six plates. counts.pv is a DECLARED ZERO rather than a missing key, because a missing key reads as 'this section has no opinion' and it has a strong one.

B9 — THE BED AND PAVING EDGES WHERE THIS SECTION'S CARPETS MEET THE WORLD'S OWN GROUND, handed to R6 with what was established rather than with a guess. The visual critic reports stair-stepped, aliased boundaries and a dotted stipple along them. WHAT THIS BUILD ESTABLISHED: all fifteen rings it draws are arcgis.ground rings that campus-world.js ALREADY draws wholesale on the `ground` rung, so this section introduces no polygon and no boundary that was not on screen before it — it lays the Garbini project's own material one rung up on `carpet` over the identical outline, triangulated by the same ShapeUtils call and the same y-negation convention campus-world uses, and the suite asserts every carpet vertex lies inside the ring it declares. WHAT IT COULD NOT ESTABLISH: whether the aliasing is the world's own fill boundary, the decal stack at a grazing angle, or the two together — that needs a render, and rendering is not this agent to do. Ladder: not applicable, this is a rendering question and not a source question. Handed to R6 framed as: reproduce with fleets disabled; if the stipple survives, it is campus-world.js's and predates this section.

B8 — THE PARAPET UPSTAND ABOVE THE ROOF PLANE. From any elevated view each hall reads as a capped box, because campus-massing.js closes the prism with a lid at the parapet's own top and this section adds no upstand standing proud of the roof surface. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — every colour frame is taken from the ground and none sees a roof surface, and MG_23022's roofline is a thin dark fascia with nothing above it; Street View — unclimbed; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — no section or roof detail in any cached document; archives — the mid-1960s aerial is the one source that looks DOWN on these roofs, and at its resolution a 0.2-0.4 m upstand is under a pixel. What every source does agree on is 'flat roof, thin fascia, no overhang'. So no upstand is invented and none is denied: the roof plane and the parapet top are the same elevation here because nothing measures the difference between them. Build it when a source resolves it.

B7 — RETIRED — see superseded['revelle.absent[3]']. The retired entry is carried VERBATIM and character-for-character between the delimiters, and this list does not shrink: RETIRED ENTRY 1 of 1 <<Six fleet halls (Atlantis, Beagle, Challenger, Discovery, Galathea, Meteor) — no verified imagery>>. Its premise was true of the R1 recon and is false as of this section, which builds all six from two dated colour frames, one dated photogrammetric frame, one dated aerial, one dimensioned suite plan, one landscape plan, three first-party identity sources and the 2014 LiDAR. The limit the entry was really pointing at — that the imagery does not say which hall it shows — is carried forward as A7, narrowed to four frames and not inherited quietly.

urey.label: UREY HALL, Revelle College — the 1963 Risley & Gould chemistry slab, first campus building with Mayer (CAAN R021, 8 floors), with the 1991 Urey Hall Office Addition (R022, 3 floors) recorded and left to the measured layer. FOUR HARD ROOF PLANES, NOT A PRISM: podium wings at 4.02/3.98 m, the main slab at 25.43 m, a west crown L at 30.45 m and an east tower at 29.18 m over one rim datum — the 2014 point cloud resolves every one to a 0.01-0.05 m per-cell spread, and everything between them is eucalyptus canopy. ONE TALL GROUND STOREY AND SEVEN EQUAL SLAB FLOORS: (25.43 - 4.00)/7 = 3.0614 m, seven gallery bands on the south face and seven curtain-wall floor lines on the north, counted in dated frames. The shipped measured layer extrudes this ring at 30.5 with massHeights withheld; this section carries the partition that corrects the picture and supersedes revelle.systems.ureyCorner, whose 30 m screen stood on the 1991 Addition's ground.
urey.epoch: Building 1963 (early; facilities 1963-01-01), massing unaltered since — LiDAR 2014 is VALID, 51 years after completion. Office Addition 1991: every 1960s-70s photograph of Urey's south-east is a PRE-ADDITION epoch, and the 1964 hexagonal court and terrace stairs (ucsddc-bb56326044_2.jpg) were partly displaced by it — the dead ground epoch here. Concrete originally exposed buff, WHITE-PAINTED BY THE 2008 EPOCH (ucsdmap-urey-annex.jpg, EXIF DateTimeOriginal 2008-07-02); facade geometry 1964-1970 archive frames; facade colour 2008-2010 UCSD map JPEGs (hue anchors, uncalibrated); roof colours 2026 Google ortho, build-time measurement only; heights LiDAR 2014 via the full-depth EPT re-measure of 2026-08-21.
urey.note: INVENTED CLASS — photo-sourced detail, modeled off dated photographs, the 2014 EPT point cloud re-measure and build-time ortho reads. Nothing measured reads from this section. The rings it carries are copied VERBATIM from campus-arcgis.json; the roof-plane partition clips them by declared boxes whose bounds are the survey's own vertices and invents no plan edge.
urey.boundsNote: An OUTER ENVELOPE: every drawn reach, rounded OUTWARD to the integer so the envelope can never exclude its own content. The exact reaches inside it: north, the mass ring's own edge z 229.1 less the 0.06 wall offset (the Spurlock 2018 science quadrangle beyond is R5's and nothing is treated there); south, owned ground ring #2155's reach z 316.8 (the plaza walks beyond are plaza/siteworks); west, ring #2155's reach x -75.1; east, walk ring #2828's reach x 46.1. The Keeling exclusion box is nowhere near.

Ring #1725 (949 m2, x 42.6..88.3) is NOT urey's — it is MAYER'S (JETT SOUTH PINE GROVE, mayer.measured.groundRings.owned[0]; arbitration B3 corrected this pointer from 'bonner/breezeway'). The east-court rings #1249/#2378/#2162/#529/#2828 are urey's east apron, coordinated with the breezeway module which builds nothing west of x ~47.

Neither is clipped — both are handed on WHOLE. Also named for the record (arbitration A3): #3978 — 18 m2 walk patch at the west stair tower, not surveyed by this dossier, R6/revelle-side siteworks.

addition.untouchedNote: The measured layer already draws this mass correctly (massHeights 12.1, a valid 2014 read over a 1991 building) and this module builds NOTHING of it — no mass, no facade, no hipped-roof cap (absent A12). It is carried here because the south-elevation record and the ureyCorner supersession are unintelligible without it.

osm.name: Urey Hall
osm.note: The OSM ring swallows the Office Addition — its max z 315.8 is the ADDITION's south face (GIS 316.8, a 1.0 m ring disagreement, declared in conflicts), not any face of Urey proper. The real south faces of Urey are the slab at z 282.4 and the podium wall at z 309.5.

groundRings.indexNote: arcgis.ground indices are LITERAL and are never renumbered; every ring is carried verbatim at /10. `carpet: false` is a declared record whose surface is withheld, with the reason on the ring.
