the west grove lawn (a camera-position claim for ucsddc-bb9352649m_2.jpg was STRUCK at arbitration D5: the frame is a probable archive mislabel showing Mayer, so if the building is Mayer the camera stood SW of Mayer, not in this grove)
east court planting between the east tower and Bonner — a remnant of the 1964 hexagonal-court epoch; in the 2026 ortho its west portion is OCCLUDED by the leaning image of the 29.18 m east tower
east court planting east of the Office Addition; the cleanest planting read of the four east-court rings
east court planting at the Addition's south-east corner
the narrow planting strip along the walk toward Bonner

the walk between Urey's east court and Bonner. RECORD ONLY, no carpet: the only 2026 ortho read of it is (59.7, 74.8, 85.2) with B > G > R — deep building shadow, not a paving colour — so the surface keeps the world's generic walk material until a lit read exists (samples.walkInShadow)

boundary.what: x -49..32, z 222.9..253.2 — OVERLAPS the north podium wing of GIS mass 22: the survey's own ground layer disagrees with its own massing layer here. Declared in conflicts['ground1246-overlap']; drawn by neither claim; north of z 229 is the science quad's in any case.

notMine.what: x 42.6..88.3, z 281.8..343.6, toward Mayer/York — MAYER'S (JETT SOUTH PINE GROVE, mayer.measured.groundRings.owned[0]), not urey's. Arbitration B3 corrected this pointer from 'bonner/breezeway' — bonner never received it.

derivations.why: The bar is keeling.roofs.pv: every figure sourced and derivable, with the arithmetic recorded. A round number with no derivation is a defect. Every metre this section draws is an `expr` evaluated in the test against these readings, a banded `estimate`, a `read` with citation and tolerance, or a declared `draw` offset with a sibling Note saying why it is not a measurement.

ept.source: USGS 3DEP EPT CA_SanDiegoQL2_2014 full-depth re-measure of 2026-08-21 (research-urey.md section 2): per-1.5 m-cell p90 of above-ground returns minus rim base, rim base = median ground return within 3 m of the mass-22 ring; canopy discriminator = per-cell p90 - p35 (real roofs 0.01-0.05 m, the 'steps' 4.2-12.3 m).

survey.source: docs/data/campus-lidar.json (datum, heights, massHeights) and docs/data/campus-arcgis.json (massing 22 and 351 h/levels) — quoted, never averaged; the GIS h fields are the levels x 4.27 formula.

px.source: Revelle-College-Sources/renders/urey-sources/ucsddc-bb6690636c_2.jpg (UCSD DC, 1965-70 colour, south face from the lawn), 768x768. Mean luminance per row over columns x 300..460 (a clean strip between the two towers); band-line centroids are half-maximum midpoints and FWHMs are sub-pixel half-maximum widths against each line's own local dark baseline (min within +/-13 rows). The five clean interior lines are floors 8 down to 4; the roofline (row 194) has sky above and takes no FWHM; the floor-3 line's FWHM is contaminated by the podium brightness below and the floor-2 line is hidden behind the podium wall from this low station.

ortho.source: docs/data/textures/chunk_4_6.jpg at 8.000 px/m per manifest (x0 -177, z0 147); world rects sampled per-pixel 2026-08-21 at the locally derived displacement of derivations.figures['ortho.rate*'] — parapet-edge fits on the 25.43 m plane gave north Dz -5.3 m and east Dx -2.7 m (south edge -6.5 discarded as facade-contaminated, west-lobe x -0.2 discarded as shadow-ambiguous), scaled linearly to lower planes. Ground-plane rects (height 0) take no displacement.

podium.datum.why: THE GROUND STOREY'S HEAD, and the storey grid's foot: the mean of the two podium plateau reads. That the mean is exactly 4.00 is the two wings agreeing about one deck to 4 cm.

storey.slab.why: SEVEN EQUAL SLAB FLOORS between the podium datum and the slab roof: (25.43 - 4.00)/7. Seven is counted on the south face (seven gallery bands, bb2151345x 1965 and bb6690636c 1965-70) and the north face (seven curtain bands, bb03423561 1964); facilities' 8 floors = these seven plus the tall ground storey. The GIS 4.27 m module is NOT this building's and its formula loses in conflicts['gis-h-formula'].

storey.floor3.why: Floor 3's line above the rim — the first gallery band above the podium head; the dossier's rounded 7.06.

storey.floor7.why: Floor 7's line, 19.31 m — the Watermelon Drop storey, ~19-20 m over plaza grade; the physics-course '21.0 m' is a textbook prop, cited for colour only.

storey.floor8.why: The top slab floor's line, 22.37 m; the roof plane sits one storey above it at 25.43.

crown.rise.why: The west crown L (penthouse + south stair tower) stands 5.02 m over the slab membrane.

eastTower.rise.why: The east stair/elevator tower stands 3.75 m over the slab. Its ~4-cell 32.95 spike (elevator overrun or stack) is absent A3 and is NOT built: the tower tops at 29.18 exactly.

rim.local.why: The EPT rim base in renderer y: 126.28 - 102.4 = 23.88. The module's runtime rim is the median drawn surface along the ring; this figure is the pinned check on it (they agree to 0.11 m on the drawn terrain).

rim.localAddition.why: The Addition's own rim, 24.23 — the ground rises 0.35 m eastward. One datum per mass, never one per prop; the Addition is the measured layer's and this figure only documents the grade step.

check.osmHeightIsCrown.why: heights['Urey Hall'] = 30.5 is the p98 over the OSM ring — which is the west crown to 0.05 m. It describes the crown, not a roof plane, which is why extruding the whole ring at it is wrong and why this section exists.

check.gisFormula.why: THE LOSER, RECORDED: GIS h 29.9 = 7 x 4.27, a formula whose 4.27 m module is not this building's 3.06 — off the real slab by +4.5 m. Declared in conflicts['gis-h-formula'], never averaged in.

check.gisFormulaAddition.why: The same formula on the Addition: 12.81 vs the valid LiDAR 12.1. The formula family identified twice on one page is what makes it a formula and not two coincidences.

addition.floor.why: 12.1 / 3 floors = 4.03 m — a different (1991) module from Urey's 3.06. Do not blend; recorded so nobody tries.

px.pitch.why: The band pitch on the 1965-70 frame: four clean inter-line gaps spanned at once, 27.45 px. Sub-pixel centroids, floors 8 down to 4.

check.pitchSpreadPct.expr: 100 * (Math.max(px.b7c - px.b8c, px.b6c - px.b7c, px.b5c - px.b6c, px.b4c - px.b5c) - Math.min(px.b7c - px.b8c, px.b6c - px.b7c, px.b5c - px.b6c, px.b4c - px.b5c)) / px.pitch
check.pitchSpreadPct.why: PITCH UNIFORMITY: the four gaps spread 2.08% — the photograph agreeing with the equal-floor arithmetic. If this opens up, the seven-equal-floors model needs re-arguing before anything is redrawn.

ratio.fasciaOfStorey.why: The white band's depth as a share of its storey: the mean FWHM of the two TOPMOST (least contaminated) lines over the pitch. The FWHM run grows monotonically down the face (6.19 to 8.12 px) as the thin pipe railing resolves nearer the camera, so the top pair is the fascia's own asymptote and the full run is the declared spread (estimates carry it).

fascia.metres.why: 0.2284 x 3.0614 = 0.699 m — the projecting walkway fascia (slab edge plus rail valance) drawn upward from each floor line. The in-band rhythm below it is absent A2 and nothing subdivides the band.

ortho.rateX.why: LOCAL ortho displacement rate in x: the east-parapet fit's -2.7 m at the 25.43 m plane, 0.106 m per metre of height. Derived HERE, never imported from another section's rate.

ortho.rateZ.why: LOCAL rate in z: -5.3 m at 25.43 m, 0.208 m/m, direction NNW. The south-edge -6.5 read was REFUSED for the fit — the visible south-face bands lean into the frame and contaminate the parapet edge.

ortho.dPodium.why: The displacement applied to 4 m-plane rects, rounded to the 0.1 m the rect grid carries. z twin: 0.8 = round(4.00 x 0.208, 1).

louvre.westHalfMax.why: The east limit of the louvre band: the midpoint of the podium south edge's own extreme surveyed vertices (-33.1 and 2.4, both ring vertices). 'West half' is what the 1964-65 frames show; the midpoint is the only non-invented reading of 'half'.

ground.ownedArea.derivation: The shoelace sum over the seven owned rings' outer boundaries at /10 — recomputed by the test from the verbatim rings, not trusted from here.
ground.ownedArea.why: What the apron claims, in square metres, so a silently grown or shrunk claim is a number moving and not a sentence changing.

curtain.lineDepth.extends: the south face's own measured gallery-band depth (fascia.metres, 0.699 m off ucsddc-bb6690636c_2.jpg) carried to the north face's thin white floor-edge lines
curtain.lineDepth.why: [estimated] Ladder climbed and failed: photos — ucsddc-bb03423561_2.jpg (1964) and bb30387229 (1969) show the lines but a luminance profile over x 150..300 resolves NO line peaks at 768 px; Street View — no captioned modern north-face frame found; drone/video — none found; planning docs — UCOP 2008 carries no Urey elevation; archives — no drawing set online (the OAC finding-aid lead is open). The same building's sourced floor-line pattern is extended across the gap per the ultra standard, at its own measured value.
curtain.lineDepth.bandWhy: The band is the SOUTH read's own spread: the five measured FWHMs run 6.19 to 8.12 px, i.e. 0.69 to 0.91 m at the shared storey — the fascia's own asymptote to its most railing-contaminated read. A north line outside what the south face's own population spans would be an invention, not an extension.

louvre.depth.extends: the same measured gallery-band depth (fascia.metres), carried to the louvre band at the head of the podium wall's west half
louvre.depth.why: [estimated] Ladder climbed and failed: photos — bb2151345x (1965), bb38919759 (1964-65) and bb35848038 (1975-86) show the continuous louvre band at the podium head but every frame is oblique and the podium head is partly behind planting, so no FWHM survives to gate tolerance; Street View — unclimbed for this face; drone/video — none; planning docs — none; archives — no drawing set online. The band ships at the building's own sourced band depth, labelled.
louvre.depth.bandWhy: Same population as curtain.lineDepth: the building's own measured band-depth spread, 0.69 to 0.91 m. The louvre reads DEEPER than the gallery fascia in the oblique frames, which the band's upper half covers; publishing a deeper point value would be trusting an oblique read the dossier itself refuses.

reads.planePartition: Each roof plane's plan is the verbatim ring clipped by its declared boxes (system.planes[*].clip). Box bounds are surveyed vertex coordinates: z 252.6 (the slab's own north-edge vertices run z 252.3..253.2 and the cut sits on the slab plateau's cell-bbox edge; any value in that 0.3 m band moves under 0.3 m of attribution at a 1.5 m cell), z 282.4 and x -31.4/-23.9 and z 287.0 (ring vertices of the slab south face and the crown-tower lobe), x 21.4 (ring vertex, the slab/east-tower seam), z 309.6 just south of the podium edge z 309.5. Tolerance: attribution slivers under 0.3 m wide at partition cuts; the areas still sum exactly.
reads.penthousePlan: x -31.8..-22.8, z 266..282 on the slab roof — the 30.45 m plateau's cell bounding box (cell centres +/-0.75 m), read from the EPT re-measure; the 2026 ortho corroborates a rooftop box against the slab membrane at the same station. Tolerance +/-0.75 m per edge, the cell's own half-pitch.
reads.towersProud: Two pale towers stand proud of the roofline in every south frame (bb2151345x 1965, bb6690636c 1965-70) — the measured west crown (30.45) and east tower (29.18). Count exact; this is the check that the crown planes are BUILDING and not canopy.
reads.roofFurniture: The 2026 ortho shows a row of 7-8 mechanical units along the west penthouse's east flank, pale safety-walkway lines on the slab membrane, and a rust-stained mech zone on the east tower (the 2007 helicopter-replaced exhaust fans live there). Seen, recorded, WITHHELD: the count is ambiguous (7-8) and no unit edge survives 0.125 m/px to gate tolerance — absent A9.
reads.additionRoofForm: 2026 ortho: the Addition carries a hipped red-brown roof in an L with a flat lighter well inside; ucsdmap-urey-b.jpg (2010) corroborates the buff precast walls and punched dark-frame windows. Recorded for A12; nothing of it is built here.
reads.boardForm: Horizontal board-form texture legible under white paint in ucsdmap-urey-annex.jpg (2008), with black 'Urey Hall' lettering — lettering recorded, never rendered (repo has no text mechanism; same status as revelle.absent[6]).

draw.wallOffsetNote: A RENDER OFFSET, not a measurement: every wall plane stands this far proud of its own plan polygon (mitred), so the two coincident walls at a partition seam separate by 0.12 m instead of z-fighting, and nothing here claims the concrete projects 60 mm.
draw.fieldStandoffNote: A RENDER OFFSET, measured FROM THE WALL FACE and not from the plan: the glazed field stands at wallOffset + fieldStandoff proud of the plan polygon, so it ALWAYS survives the depth test against its own carrying wall. The first shipped values put the field at a smaller absolute offset than the wall itself and every face rendered blank white with z-fight ticks (round-2 visual critic, after-r4/urey-hall/verdict.json) — the layering invariant is wall < field < band and it is gated, not remembered. The real detail is a RECESS whose depth no source measures; this is stacking order, not a claim.
draw.bandStandoffNote: A RENDER OFFSET: the fascia bands, curtain lines and louvre band stand fieldStandoff + bandStandoff beyond the wall face — one step proud of the field — so the band-over-field order reads at any distance. Not a claim about the walkway slab's projection, which no source measures.
draw.skirtDepthNote: A RENDER OFFSET: every wall's foot is carried this far below the lowest drawn surface along its own plan, so rolling terrain cannot open a gap under a mass. It only ever buries, never lifts.
draw.datumStepNote: A SAMPLING INTERVAL, not a dimension: the drawn surface is read every 2 m along ring and plan edges for the rim median and the wall feet. Finer changes nothing measurable.
draw.clipSamplesNote: A SAMPLING COUNT: the drawn surface is read at nine stations along a facade run to find the highest ground under it; a band whose level dips below that is withheld whole rather than drawn emerging from a hillside.
draw.minFacadeEdgeNote: A DEGENERACY GUARD, not a dimension: facade treatment is not hung on plan edges shorter than this — the survey's own 0.1-0.3 m jogs — because a band on a 10 cm edge is noise wearing paint.
draw.northNormalNote: A CLASSIFIER THRESHOLD, not a dimension: an edge whose outward normal has nz below -0.7 is a north face (curtain system), nz above +0.7 a south face (louvre eligibility); the slab's edges are axis-aligned to well beyond this margin either way.
draw.bedRungNote: A LADDER RUNG, not a height: campus-world.js already draws every arcgis.ground ring on the `ground` rung; this section's lawn and bed surfaces sit one rung above on `carpet`, giving the surveyed polygon its 2026 material. Nothing re-outlines a ring.
draw.bedSegNote: A TESSELLATION TARGET: carpet triangles subdivide until no edge exceeds 3 m so the surface follows the drawn terrain instead of spanning it.
draw.bedMaxDepthNote: A RECURSION CAP on that subdivision, so a pathological ring cannot generate an unbounded mesh.
draw.tilesNote: MATERIAL REPEAT LENGTHS in metres, not building dimensions: how often the code-generated texture repeats so microstructure lands at true material scale — a 0.6 m board-form lift, a 2 m membrane sheet, a 1.5 m patch of planting. Texture maps are code-generated throughout; the sampled colours feed the materials and the photographs' pixels never do.

system.planesNote: THE FOUR-PLANE PARTITION (five pieces: the two podium wings are separate plateaus of one podium system). Heights are the EPT plateau reads over one shared rim datum; plans are the verbatim ring clipped by the declared boxes; the module extrudes each to its own plane and the 30.5 prism is never drawn here. roofTier says whose colour the lid wears: the north wing's only ortho read is in slab shadow, the east tower's membrane is unreadable under the rust-stained mech zone, and both lids extend a sibling plane's sourced material as [estimated].

podiumN.note: The north wing and its east annex; two boxes split the connecting 0.2 m survey strip at x 7.45 so neither clip piece pinches. Every higher LiDAR read inside this wing is canopy (spread 4.2-12.3 m) — the trees are real, the steps are not.

slab.note: The eight-storey block, its west balcony/stair lobe (same plane, flush with the roof plus a thin parapet — established by the EPT lobe cells 25.37..25.5; bb9352649m is a disputed-identity frame, probable Mayer mislabel per arbitration D5, corroboration only) and the stepped west arm. Gallery bands south/east/west, curtain north.

eastTower.note: Stair/elevator + mech. The ~4-cell 32.95 spike is recorded (absent A3) and NOT built: the top is 29.18 exactly, and the test asserts nothing stands above it.

crownTower.note: The south stair tower — the full-height arm of the west crown L, breaking the slab's south face at x -31.4..-23.9 exactly as the 1960s frames show. Its rooftop penthouse arm is system.penthouse.

podiumS.note: The south terrace deck: tan paving in the 2026 ortho, with skylight boxes and mature tree wells rising through (the wells' canopy is the measured proof the deck has real trees; neither is built — absent A9/A5). The louvre band rides the head of its south wall's west half.

penthouse.note: The rooftop arm of the west crown L, slab roof to 30.45. Plan is the plateau's cell bounding box, a declared read at +/-0.75 m (reads.penthousePlan); the 7-8 mech units along its east flank are seen and withheld (absent A9).

storey.floorsNote: 8 = 1 tall ground storey (grade to the 4.00 podium datum) + 7 slab floors at 3.0614. GIS levels 7 counts the slab floors; facilities/Emeriti 8 counts the total. Both retained in conflicts['storey-count']; neither is wrong; only the GIS 4.27 formula loses.

gallery.bandsNote: SEVEN, counted twice (south gallery bands, north curtain bands) and closed by the storey arithmetic. Each band is one white fascia quad drawn UPWARD from its floor line — the walkway slab plus rail valance that reads as one bright line in every frame — over a dark glazed field. The in-band rhythm (posts, glazing/spandrel split) is absent A2 and is NOT drawn; the bays read as bands because the bands are on the measured grid.

groundClip.rule: A band whose line sits below the highest drawn surface along its run is withheld WHOLE, and counted; the glazed field's foot rises to the drawn surface. No source frame shows a band emerging from a hillside.
groundClip.ruleNote: TWO COUNTS, DECLARED SEPARATELY: `counts` describes the grid the sources give on flat ground; this block describes what the real drawn terrain leaves of it, so a change to the sources and a change to the terrain move different numbers. On this site the rim sits 4.00 m under the lowest band and the ground crests only 0.75 m over the rim, so the drawn terrain withholds nothing — a zero that is a measurement, not an omission.

curtain.note: The north face: a flush dark curtain field (glass, no balconies) with thin white floor-edge lines on the same seven-line grid, over the recessed ground storey. Mullion module absent (A1) — no vertical is drawn. lineDepth is estimates['curtain.lineDepth'], an [estimated] extension of the south face's measured band depth.

louvre.note: The continuous louvre band at the head of the podium wall's WEST half (bb2151345x 1965; bb38919759 1964-65), metal-seam material at the sampled louvre hue. depth is estimates['louvre.depth']; westHalfMax is the derived midpoint of the podium south edge's own extreme vertices.

urey.colorNote: Every hex is the byte-rounding of its own pinned channel means and the test recomputes that. The statistic is the CHANNEL MEAN, (R+G+B)/3, never a weighted luma; each line carries its Rec.709 luminance separately so the two are never confused. The 2008/2010 facade JPEGs are uncalibrated consumer cameras — hue anchors, not absolutes (absent A8) — and the 2026 ortho is a build-time measurement source only.

colorThreshold.note: The Commons' 120/15 rule, carried unchanged: [measured] needs a sunlit sample (channel mean >= 120) that passes the single-material bar (max per-channel sd <= 15); below either it is [sourced]; an extension is [estimated] whatever it cites. The two controls bracket the rule on this section's own frame.

controls.side: passes both bars — the one [measured] facade sample here
fails both bars — the same paint in shade, held in samples as the demonstration and never a colour source

wallPaint.source: [measured] ucsdmap-urey-annex.jpg (UCSD map photograph, EXIF DateTimeOriginal 2008-07-02), px rect (60,340)-(200,430), channel means 219.6 / 218.3 / 218.5, channel sd max 14.5, Rec.709 luminance 218.6. The sunlit white-painted board-form wall — the sd carries the board joints, 0.5 inside the single-material bar. White paint over 1963 buff concrete: the paint epoch is 2008-or-earlier and the sample is the standing surface (2008).

louvrePanel.source: [sourced] ucsdmap-urey-annex.jpg (2008), px rect (300,170)-(380,200) over the louvred shaft above the east entrance, channel means 79.1 / 79.3 / 82.0, channel sd max 62.1, Rec.709 luminance 79.5. THE VARIANCE IS THE MATERIAL: alternating lit slats and slot shadow — no low-variance tile exists on a louvre, so this is a hue anchor below the sunlit bar, [sourced] by rule.

glazingDark.source: [sourced] ucsdmap-urey-annex.jpg (2008), px rect (300,220)-(390,260) over the recessed dark glazing, channel means 81.5 / 81.3 / 83.5, channel sd max 61.6, Rec.709 luminance 81.5. Near-neutral dark — a pane returning the shaded soffit; below the sunlit bar and mixed with frame shadow, so [sourced]. RENDERED OPAQUE, NOT AS GLASS (round-3 visual critic, after-r4v2/urey-hall/verdict.json; the mayer V2 class): the library glass class is transparent at 0.35 and the white wall one standoff behind the fields showed through, washing every field to 85-90% of the fascia's luminance. With the in-band rhythm (A2) and mullion module (A1) withheld, the honest render is one uniformly dark matte plane at this sampled hue, and the suite pins the built material's transparency, opacity and colour.

galleryFascia.source: [estimated] extends wallPaint's own 2008 sample. The gallery fascias read as the same white paint family in ucsdmap-urey-a.jpg (2010) but no rectangle isolable on a band at 320 px passes the single-material bar, so the band carries the wall's hex as a labelled extension — and the mesh is NAMED estimated so a render shows the tier.

curtainLine.source: [estimated] extends wallPaint — the north face's thin white floor-edge lines, unsampled in any frame (the 1964/1969 north frames are B/W-era archive scans and the line is sub-pixel at 768). Same hex, same extension discipline, named estimated in the scene.

urey.colorSourcesNote: Per-hex provenance with the sample rectangle pinned; the test recomputes every hex from its channel means and pins every mean. [measured] needs the 120/15 rule; ortho reads cap at [sourced]; extensions are [estimated] and their meshes are NAMED estimated.

samples.samplesNote: Recorded reads that BUILD NOTHING — corroborations, demonstrations and shadow-blind rects held so the next agent does not resample them from scratch. All re-verified per-pixel 2026-08-21.

endTowerField.source: ucsdmap-urey-a.jpg (2010) — the end tower's field in part shade, (146.5, 143.0, 144.1): the same paint family between the lit and shaded wall reads; corroboration only, mixed lighting builds nothing.

conflicts.what: How many floors Urey Hall has.
sides: UCSD Facilities Information System (Bkey=516, fetched 2026-08-21): 8 Floors. Emeriti 'Know Your Campus' (2024 ed.): 'eight-story'. First-party, twice.
campus-arcgis.json massing[22]: levels 7. First-party GIS.
The LiDAR band: one 4.00 m podium storey plus a 21.43 m slab.
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED WITHOUT AVERAGING: both are right about different countings. GIS 7 counts the slab floors; facilities 8 counts those plus the tall ground storey inside the podium datum. Geometry follows the LiDAR planes: 1 x 4.00 + 7 x 3.0614. The only loser is the GIS h formula (see gis-h-formula).

conflicts.what: Urey's assignable square footage.
sides: Facilities (fetched 2026-08-21): 100,668 asf.
Emeriti 'Know Your Campus' (2024 ed.): 106,771 asf.
conflicts.resolution: UNRESOLVED, DECLARED, NOT AVERAGED. Facilities is the newer first-party record and would win if anything here drew from either; nothing does — no drawn figure derives from an area claim.

conflicts.what: build-campus-lidar.mjs's worked example says Urey has 'half its returns on ~16 m steps, crown at 30.4 — p75 lands at 25.4 m, a roof that does not exist', and withholds massHeights.
sides: The builder: no single roof plane exists; the mass shows ~16 m steps; 25.4 is not a roof.

The 2026-08-21 EPT re-measure: the canopy discriminator (per-cell p90 - p35: 0.01-0.05 m on real roofs, 4.2-12.3 m on the 'steps') shows the steps are EUCALYPTUS/FICUS CANOPY over and beside the podium, and 25.43 IS a real plane — 674 cells at p25-p75 = 25.39-25.48.
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED IN THE BUILDER'S FAVOUR ON THE DECISION AND AGAINST IT ON THE NARRATIVE: withholding massHeights was correct (there truly is no single plane) and this section gates that the withholding stands; the steps were canopy and the 25.43 slab plane is real, which is exactly what this section builds. The LiDAR builder is NOT touched.

conflicts.what: arcgis.ground#1246 (green, 973 m2, x -49..32, z 222.9..253.2) overlaps the north podium wing of arcgis massing[22] — the survey's ground layer disagrees with its own massing layer.
sides: The ground layer: planted green over that box.
The massing layer: the 4.02 m north wing over the same box.
The canopy evidence (EPT): real trees DO rise through and beside the wing — planted wells and edges are physically plausible.
conflicts.resolution: DECLARED, NOT RESOLVED. Neither ring is moved and neither claim is drawn over the other: the wing is built (it is measured), #1246 gets no carpet, and no eye-level source shows the wing's interior condition (absent A5).

conflicts.what: GIS h values for both masses versus the measured planes.
sides: campus-arcgis.json: massing[22] h 29.9; massing[351] h 12.8.
The arithmetic: 29.9 = 7 x 4.27 and 12.81 = 3 x 4.27 — one storey formula applied twice (derivations check.gisFormula / check.gisFormulaAddition).
The measurements: slab 25.43 / crown 30.45 (EPT); Addition 12.1 (valid massHeights).
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED FOR THE MEASUREMENTS: the h fields are a 4.27 m-module formula, not a survey — off Urey's real slab by +4.5 m because this building's module is 3.06. The formula is recorded as the loser and never blended.

conflicts.what: Where the Office Addition's south face is.
sides: GIS massing[351]: max z 316.8. This is what renders.
OSM 'Urey Hall' ring: max z 315.8 — and the OSM ring swallows the whole Addition under Urey's name, which is how revelle.systems.ureyCorner came to stand a 30 m screen there.
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED FOR THE GIS on position (it renders and it separates the two buildings); the OSM figure stays recorded because the ureyCorner supersession is stated against it. A 1.0 m ring disagreement between two surveys of a real wall, declared.

absent: A1 — THE NORTH-FACE CURTAIN-WALL MULLION MODULE. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — ucsddc-bb03423561_2.jpg (1964, 768 px) and bb30387229 (1969) show the grid but it aliases, and a luminance profile over x 150..300 resolves no line at all; Street View — no captioned modern north-face frame found, and the rung is now CLIMBED-AND-EMPTY (arbitration C3, 2026-08-21, citing mayer's dated record: the single published Revelle photosphere — 360cities.net, Norm Olson, captured 2016-11-19, stationed at the Jacaranda court — does not see this face, and Google pedestrian coverage is not enumerable non-interactively); drone/video — none found; planning docs — UCOP 2008 has no Urey elevation; archives — no drawing set online (the OAC Risley & Gould finding-aid lead is open). The seven floor lines ship as an [estimated] extension of the south face's measured band depth; NO VERTICAL MULLION IS DRAWN at any spacing.

A2 — THE SOUTH-FACE BAY RHYTHM: gallery post spacing and the glazing/spandrel split inside each band. Same ladder, same result (the Street View rung is likewise CLIMBED-AND-EMPTY per arbitration C3 — mayer's dated 2026-08-21 climb, one photosphere at the Jacaranda court, no dated frame of this face) — the seven-band count, the pitch and the band depth are measured (derivations.readings.px); the in-band rhythm is not, so each band is one unsubdivided fascia over one unsubdivided glazed field and no post is drawn. NOTE (arbitration C4): for the day the gallery rhythm is built — a 1970s railing colour direction (olive-bronze) exists in bonner's cached bb0137569z (Kodachrome, shot FROM a Urey balcony).

A3 — THE 32.9 m SPIKE ON THE EAST TOWER: elevator overrun versus exhaust stack. ~4 cells of returns (ept.spikeMax 32.95, x 25..27, z 262..265); the 2026 ortho shows the rust-stained mech zone but no measurable box edge; no photo resolves the top. The tower ships at 29.18 with the spike recorded, unmodelled, and the test asserts nothing stands above 29.18.

A4 — THE NORTH PODIUM ROOF'S MATERIAL AND COLOUR. The only ortho read is in slab shadow (samples.northPodiumShadow, B > G > R); the 1960s aerials are B/W; no other rung covers a 4 m roof. The lid ships [estimated] extending the south deck's sourced read (podiumRoofNorth) and is replaced when a different-sun ortho or aerial appears.

A5 — THE NORTH WING'S INTERIOR/COURT CONDITION, the ground#1246 overlap: no eye-level photograph of the wing's interior was found on any rung (photos, Street View, drone, planning docs, archives all blank here). The conflict is declared; nothing is invented inside it.

A6 — THE 'UREY HALL' LETTERING, black on the white board-form (ucsdmap-urey-annex.jpg, 2008). Recorded; the repo has no text mechanism — a renderer limitation, not a source gap; same status as revelle.absent[6].

A7 — THE PRE-1991 EAST COURT: hexagonal paving, single-column umbrella platforms and twin terrace stairs (ucsddc-bb56326044_2.jpg, 1964; bb61786853). Superseded ON THE GROUND by the 1991 Office Addition — a dead epoch. Do not rebuild a 1964 landscape under a 1991 building; historical record only.

A8 — FACADE COLOUR CALIBRATION. The 2008/2010 UCSD map JPEGs are uncalibrated consumer cameras and no 2020s colour photograph of Urey proper was found (the Bradley 2013 set is B/W-processed; Calisphere throttles verified; library.ucsd.edu/dc search still Anubis-blocked). Colour ships hue-anchored off the pinned rectangles with this caveat. NOTE (arbitration C4): a 1970s railing colour direction (olive-bronze) exists in bonner's cached bb0137569z (Kodachrome, shot from a Urey balcony) — a direction datum, not a calibrated sample.

A9 — THE ROOF FURNITURE: the row of 7-8 mechanical units along the west penthouse's east flank, the pale safety-walkway lines on the slab membrane, and the rust-stained mech zone on the east tower (the 2007 helicopter fan replacement). Ladder: photos — no rooftop frame exists; Street View — cannot see a 25 m roof; drone/video — none found; planning docs — none; archives — B/W obliques cannot resolve 2026 equipment. The 2026 ortho SEES them but the unit count is ambiguous (7-8) and no edge survives 0.125 m/px to gate tolerance. Seen, recorded (reads.roofFurniture), withheld — counts.roofObjects is a declared zero.

A10 — THE WEDGE ENTRANCE CANOPY AND ITS BENCH WALL: the thin tapering flat canopy flying off the slab's ground storey over the south approach — Urey's signature ground gesture (Flickr 9339373362 / Bradley, page-dated 2013-07-19; EXIF DateTimeOriginal absent from every frame, checked). Ladder climbed and failed for a SCALED source: photos — every frame is an unscaled oblique; Street View — unclimbed for this face; drone/video — none; planning docs — none; archives — no drawing set online; ortho — at the ~4 m plane an 8 px/m image cannot separate a thin canopy edge from the podium edge shadow. Position and span unmeasured; NOT BUILT. The UCOP 2008 p11 curved-canopy frame is consistent in family but is not identified as Urey and stays unattributed.

A11 — THE NW SCREEN-BLOCK WALL: the decorative perforated concrete-block screen at the north-west ground storey, clearly visible in 1964 (bb03423561). Its pattern module and extent do not survive a 768 px oblique to gate tolerance, and no other rung covers it (same five-rung climb as A1). Recorded; not built; the ground storey ships as the plain sourced wall.

A12 — THE OFFICE ADDITION'S OWN TREATMENT: window rhythm, the chamfered SE arcade corner's depth, and the hipped roof's ridge heights (ucsdmap-urey-b.jpg 2010; 2026 ortho; samples.additionRoof). The Addition ships as the measured layer's correct 12.1 m prism, UNTREATED — a different 1991 generation on purpose, and treating one face without the rest would break the ultra standard's per-face completeness. Its recorded reads wait here for the agent that takes it whole.

A13 — THE SOUTH DECK'S FURNITURE: the row of white skylight boxes (~4 in line near x -5..3, z 296..302, plus scattered singles) and the tree wells with mature canopies rising through (canopy cells 6.5-17 m over z 283..294 — the measured proof the deck has real trees). The boxes' count is ortho-legible but their heights have no source on any rung; the trees belong to the world's measured tree layer, not to an invented planting. Deck ships bare at its sourced colour; both recorded.

bonner.label: Bonner Hall (Risley & Gould, occupied December 1964) AND THE HEXAGONAL BREEZEWAY it shares with Mayer Hall — the signature structure of this half of Revelle. The building is a 4-storey N-S laboratory bar on its surveyed GIS ring with a TWO-storey west wing, its facades hung from the MEASURED ROOF PLATE (EPT elev 138.11 = repo 35.71, one plane to ±0.02 m); the old 19.2 m read included the rooftop louvre SPINE and was retired by the R4 massing override of 2026-08-21 (the file now ships 15.4, lid = plate). The breezeway is TWO ANTIPHASE ZIGZAG CHAINS of 7 hexagonal cells each (osm:917/osm:918 verbatim), deck plates at +4.2 / +8.0 / +11.6 m and a constant hex-umbrella canopy at +15.2 m over a court at repo 20.38, with the UCOP p11 mushroom-vault arcade as its own ground tier. Decks land NEAR Bonner floors 2-4 (per-face landing levels unresolved — datum question, arbitration D3) and on Mayer's face at z 278.0.
bonner.epoch: Geometry epoch 1963-1968 (building 1963-64, breezeway 1965-68 — date CONFLICT carried, not resolved); every height 2014 LiDAR (pre-2014 fabric, so the laser is VALID); facade colours 2013-07-19 (Flickr) and 2015 (Steinhart); existence today 2026 Google ortho (chunk_4_6 8 px/m, chunk_5_6 4 px/m — BUILD-TIME measurement only, never draped, and NO ORTHO-DERIVED POSITION SHIPS: every plan vertex is the survey's). The 1965-70 archive frames decide FORM only; the court ground has a DEAD epoch break — the 1968 paved-court-and-planters ground is superseded by today's two lawns and the surviving hex paving chain, and this section builds today's ground.

check.courtVsTerrain.why: The full-depth probe's court datum against the shipped decimated terrain grid read (20.4): 0.02 m — the two descriptions of the same ground agree.

height.plateAboveEastGrade.why: 138.11 - 122.25 = 15.86 m of building over the east grade.

storey.pitch.why: 15.86 / 4 = 3.965 m MEASURED storey pitch. The 4.28 m module in the R4 brief is the ArcGIS formula's artefact and ships nowhere.

check.arcgisStorey.why: 17.1 / 4 = 4.275: the levels-formula storey, admitted as a witness for the count of 4 and REFUSED as a metre — it is 0.31 m off the measured pitch and the suite gates that the shipped storey is the measured one.

stack.footRepo.why: 35.71 - 4 x 3.965 = 19.85 = the east grade exactly; the stack closes on the measured plate and the measured grade with nothing left over.

wing.roofRepo.why: 130.40 - 102.4 = 28.0: the west wing's own roof plane.

wing.height.why: 28.0 - 21.0 = 7.0 m over the west grade — two storeys, not four; the wing's walls stop here and the drawn prism's four-level extrusion over it is a recorded conflict.

wing.storeys.why: 7.0 / 3.965 = 1.77 -> 2 storeys, the only storey count the laser supports for the wing.

spine.crestAbovePlate.why: 140.91 - 138.11 = 2.80 m louvre crest over the plate (dossier band 2.5-2.8; the p98 read is the crest used).

spine.topRepo.why: 140.91 - 102.4 = 38.51: the highest sourced element on the building.

spine.crestAboveEastGrade.why: 140.91 - 122.25 = 18.66 — WHY the 19.2/19.4 p-high reads exist: they are plate + spine over the OSM ring's base, and neither is the parapet.

louvre.pitch.why: 74.0 m / 60 mean-crossings = 1.233 m louvre pitch [measured, low confidence — crossing count method; bb2799709r confirms the order of magnitude].

louvre.count.why: The blade count IS the crossing count: one blade per brightness crossing over the spine run, and the module builds exactly this many.

breezeway.envelopeW.why: 91.0 - 83.8 = 7.2 m chain envelope width, from the carried rings.

breezeway.legacyOffset.why: 87.4 - 71.25 = 16.15 m: how far west the shipped revelle.systems.breezeway was built. The ground of the supersedes record.

breezeway.corridor.why: 90.75 - 86.2 = 4.55 m strand corridor width at an east-bulge row; the west-bulge check 88.4 - 83.85 = 4.55 is asserted as a relation — symmetric.

breezeway.corridorWestCheck.why: 88.4 - 83.85 = 4.55 — the same corridor width read at a west-bulge row; symmetry is the check that the read is structural and not one row's accident.

breezeway.strandPitch917.why: (278.2 - 252.75)/3 = 8.48 m cell pitch per strand, from ring 917's four east-out rows.

breezeway.strandPitch918.why: (269.15 - 252.15)/2 = 8.50 m from ring 918's three west-out rows — the two strands agree to 0.02 m.

breezeway.rowPitch.why: Interleaved row pitch: the two antiphase strands halve the cell pitch — 4.24 m, and the estimated arcade column pitch extends exactly this measured rhythm.

breezeway.cellsPerStrand.derivation: Ring 917 carries 4 east-out + 3 west-out outer-face rows; ring 918 carries 3 + 4 — seven cells per strand, recomputed from the rings by the rows rule the test re-runs.
breezeway.cellsPerStrand.why: A COUNT read off the carried rings, and the plan of the 'double helix'.

breezeway.columns.why: One round column per hex cell (bb61786853), 7 cells x 2 strands = 14 — not the legacy object's 12, and on the zigzag cell centres, not two straight rows.

breezeway.canopyRepo.why: 20.38 + 15.2 = 35.58: the umbrella canopy, 345 returns, top plane 15.16-15.22 constant across the whole 30 m — the canopy does not step.

check.canopyBelowPlate.why: 35.71 - 35.58 = 0.13 m: the canopy sits just under Bonner's roof plate — the two measured planes are coherent.

check.deck1VsBonnerL2.why: |4.2 - 3.965| = 0.235 m. DATUM NOTE (arbitration D3): this gates deck-height-over-COURT (datum 20.38) against a pitch-multiple — NOT deck-vs-floor over the shipped foot 19.85; the two datums differ by 0.53 m and the true FFL is unresolved (gap g8). The check pins the measured plane against drift, which is its real job.

check.deck2VsBonnerL3.why: |8.0 - 7.93| = 0.07 m, the tightest of the three. DATUM NOTE (arbitration D3): gates deck-height-over-court against a pitch-multiple, not deck-vs-floor over the shipped foot; landing levels unresolved.

check.deck3VsBonnerL4.why: |11.6 - 11.895| = 0.295 m — the loosest of the three and still inside 0.3 m. DATUM NOTE (arbitration D3): gates deck-height-over-court against a pitch-multiple, not deck-vs-floor over the shipped foot; landing levels unresolved.

check.osm917IsDeck2.why: |8.4 - 8.0| = 0.4: OSM's h on ring 917 is a mapper's read of DECK 2, not a structure height (position-keyed identity; research-mayer.md reads the pair the same way).

check.osm918IsDeck1.why: |4.8 - 4.2| = 0.6: OSM's h on ring 918 is a read of DECK 1. The pair anchors the [sourced] strand assignment of decks 1 and 2.

podium.step.why: 24.0 - 20.4 = 3.6 m: the court's west end is a podium terrace, and the stair cascade of bb61786853/bb34824128 descends it at x ~ 66.

stairs.plannedRisers.why: 3.6 / 0.15 = 24 risers on the measured grade step at the estimated rise — the SOURCE-GRID count of the declare-and-withhold pair; the drawn decimated terrain carries a shallower ramp and the built count is gated separately.

arcade.westSoffitH.why: 126.97 - 122.78 = 4.19 m: the ground vault arcade's soffit plane west of the chain — the UCOP p11 vocabulary, measured.

arcade.eastSoffitH.why: The east-edge arcade plane, +5.3 m at x 91..96 (p50 of the probe) — the best siting of the p11 camera itself.

chain.landZ.why: The GIS authority puts Mayer's court face at z ~ 278.0; the chain lands ON it and every chain plate is clipped there.

check.osmOverrunAtMayer.why: 279.9 - 278.0 = 1.9 m of OSM ring past the GIS face — tracing error, not a gap; recorded in conflicts and clipped in the build.

wing.stepHeight.why: 35.71 - 28.0 = 7.71 m: the step between the main plate and the wing roof — the false building the retired prism used to carry over the wing, now a real treated step wall whose top and foot the suite gates.

reads.plate: [measured] The main roof plate is ONE plane: EPT elev 138.11, n~2700, p25-p75 spread 0.02 m across both flanks (research-bonner.md §2.3, the 2014 CA_SanDiegoQL2 flight); tolerance ±0.02 m.
reads.breezewayPlanes: [measured] Ground + three decks + canopy: 647 above-ground returns inside the chain footprint bin to +4.2 (34), +8.0 (28), +11.6 (187), +15.2 (345) over the court's 122.78 class-2 median; the canopy top holds 15.16-15.22 across every 2 m z-slice of the 30 m run (§3.4, 2014 flight).
reads.strandMap: [sourced] Decks 1 and 2 ride strands osm:918 and osm:917: the two OSM h values (4.8, 8.4) are position-keyed mapper reads of exactly those two deck planes (figures check.osm918IsDeck1 / check.osm917IsDeck2; research-mayer.md reads the pair the same way). Deck 3's strand and the per-level termination at the Mayer face are gap g8 and ship [estimated] on the alternation bb34824128 shows.
reads.spine: [sourced] The rooftop inclined-louvre spine is original 1964 fabric: photographed under construction in bb2799709r (Graves, 1963-67) and present in the 2026 ortho chunk_4_6 as the same transverse rib row; crest and pitch measured (§2.4).
reads.facadeSystem: [sourced] Per storey: continuous grey window band, gold exposed-aggregate spandrel, expressed cream slab edge — flickr-9339401716 (2013-07-19) and steinhart-2015_CADU171, both S/SE, i.e. the COURT face (true south, +z — arbitration D6), corroborated in B/W by the court frames bb7953510x/bb34824128 and in colour by bb0137569z; the SHARES are estimated, the system is not.
reads.paving: [sourced] Hexagonal exposed-aggregate paving chain on the court ground: bb61786853 (1965-70) AND the 2026 ortho chunk_5_6 — both epochs; drawn on the chain rings' own surveyed outline, one rung above the world ground fill.
reads.galleries: [sourced] Two-level railed galleries run attached along Bonner's court face and Mayer's court face in bb34824128 and bb46427343; the pointed-arch profile and scallop fascia are in frame but undimensioned and are WITHHELD (absent), the deck-and-post bays ship [estimated] in depth and extent.
reads.mayerJunction: [measured] Both chain rings terminate on z 279.9 but the GIS authority (campus-arcgis.json massing, via research-mayer.md, 2014 survey) puts Mayer's court face at z ~ 278.0: the 1.9 m is OSM tracing error and the chain lands ON the face; Mayer's photos show a ground passage plus decks landing NEAR Mayer levels 2/3 (research-mayer.md; landing levels unresolved — arbitration D3: the level-3 floor arithmetic +8.68 sits 0.68 m above the measured deck-2 plane +8.0, possibly real steps down the chain per bb61786853), so decks 1-2 and the canopy run to 278.0 and deck 3 is trimmed short pending g8.
reads.date: [conflicted] Breezeway date carried as 1965-68: the modernist blog and research-mayer.md say 1968; the Glasheen frame bb9362031p shows the hex plates being CAST while York (1965-66) is under construction in the same frame. Both witnesses stay named until a dated drawing settles it (conflicts['breezeway-date-1965-68']).

draw.wallOffsetNote: Render offset: facade bands sit 0.06 m proud of the surveyed ring so the treatment clears the massing prism's own face without re-drawing it. An offset, not a claim about the building.
draw.openingProudNote: Glass rides 0.02 m proud of its band so the two never z-fight. Render offset only.
draw.skirtDepthNote: Facade bands run 0.6 m below the local drawn grade so a terrain dip cannot open a sliver of daylight under the wall. Render device, not a foundation claim.
draw.groundClipSamplesNote: Stations sampled along a band run when testing whether the drawn ground buries it — a sampling density for the clip, not a dimension.
draw.deck3TrimZNote: Render trim: deck 3 stops at its last measured cell's outer face instead of running to the Mayer face, because its per-level termination is unresolved (gap g8) — a WITHHOLDING expressed as a clip, not a measurement of anything.
draw.railBarNote: Top-rail bar section for the render; the rail HEIGHT is the estimate, this is stroke width.
draw.picketWidthNote: Picket stroke width for the render; the SPACING is the estimate.
draw.bladeThicknessNote: Louvre blade slab thickness for the render; crest, pitch and count are measured.
draw.capitalFlareNote: The flared capital's top radius as a fraction of the cell's half-width — a render proportion for the photographed mushroom, not a measurement; its DEPTH is the estimate.
draw.arcadeInsetNote: Arcade column rows sit 0.8 m inside their strip edges for the render; the strips' extents are the probes' own and the pitch is the estimate.
draw.bedRungNote: Lawns, walks and the hex paving drape on the overlay 'carpet' rung — one rung above the world's own ground fill, exactly the fleets precedent.
draw.bedSegNote: Maximum drape triangle edge before splitting, so ground surfaces follow the drawn terrain.
draw.bedMaxDepthNote: Recursion cap on the drape split — a mesh budget, not a dimension.
draw.footingBuryNote: Every column, post and capital-bearing shaft starts 0.3 m below the drawn surface so a terrain dip can never open daylight under a footing. Render device, not a foundation claim.
draw.stairSlabThicknessNote: Depth of each terraced stair tread's slab below its own top — keeps the tread's body in the drawn slope. A render thickness, not a measured tread.
draw.galleryPostInsetNote: Gallery post rows start 0.5 m in from the bay's own x ends so no post lands on a corner arris. Render inset only; the bay extents and pitch are the section's.
draw.galleryPostSetbackNote: Gallery posts stand 0.3 m inside the deck's outer edge for the render; the deck DEPTH is the estimate.
draw.railSkipClipNote: Deck edges whose midpoint lies within 0.3 m of the clip line carry no railing — the deck runs into the Mayer face there. A clip tolerance, not a dimension.
draw.railSkipSeamNote: Deck edges within 0.5 m of the plate's own north end (min z — repo frame, +z = south) carry no railing — the deck lands on Bonner across the junction seam. A clip tolerance, not a dimension.
draw.tilesNote: UV tile sizes in metres per material role — texture scale for the shared material library, never geometry.

stack.note: Every value here IS a derivations figure (plate.repo, storey.pitch, stack.footRepo) and the suite gates the equality. The facade hangs from the measured plate DOWN — and since the R4 massing override (massHeights 15.4, 2026-08-21) the drawn prism's lid closes on the same plate to ~0.005 m; the retired 19.2 read is held in conflicts, not a datum. Since the R4 visual round the m:80,205 GIS prism is a declared skipGis retirement (main wires it) and photo-bonner REPLACES_MEASURED: this module ships BOTH measured roof plates (35.71 main, 28.0 wing), the 7.71 m step wall between them, and the far silhouette.

facade.faceTiersNote: REPO-TRUE COMPASS (+z = south; arbitration D6 — the first build shipped these names flipped, and the sourced systems face-swapped). SOUTH is the COURT face (nz > 0, z 248.2): it carries the sourced gold-aggregate window/spandrel system — flickr-9339401716 (2013) and steinhart-2015 CADU171 (both captioned S/SE, both showing the court-side corner in full direct sun), corroborated in B/W by the court frames bb7953510x/bb34824128 and in colour by the 1970s Kodachrome bb0137569z. NORTH (z 164.7) is UNPHOTOGRAPHED: it extends the same gold system [estimated] per the ultra standard, and its meshes say -estimated. East has no dated photograph (gap g3: Street View rung CLIMBED-AND-EMPTY 2026-08-21 per mayer's dated record — the single published Revelle photosphere, 360cities.net Norm Olson 2016-11-19 at the Jacaranda court, sees no Bonner face, and Google pedestrian coverage is not enumerable non-interactively; arbitration C3) and west has only the 1963-64 construction geometry — both extend the south system [estimated]. CAUTION for R5: the [estimated] faces extend the GOLD system; the retired 'dark curtain wall' was a B/W misread of this same system (conflicts['bonner-curtain-bw-misread']) and must not be re-promoted from B/W tone.
facade.wingRoofRepoNote: Mirror of figures['wing.roofRepo'] (130.40 - 102.4) — the suite gates the equality; the wing's blank walls stop here, two storeys below the plate.

spine.note: x/z extents are the ortho brightness-profile band the pitch was measured over (readings.ortho.spine*); crest/pitch/count are figures. Since the R4 massing override (2026-08-21) the drawn prism's lid sits AT the plate, so the spine stands visible above it — the occlusion recorded in conflicts['bonner-drawn-prism-overshoot'] is history, kept as the record of why the override exists.

breezeway.strandMapNote: Decks 1/2 -> strands 918/917 is [sourced]: the OSM h pair are position-keyed reads of exactly those planes (figures check.osm918IsDeck1 / check.osm917IsDeck2). Deck 3 -> 918 is [estimated]: the alternation bb34824128 shows, replaced the day a drawing or drone frame appears (gap g8), and its mesh is named -estimated.
breezeway.arcadeNote: The two strips are the probes' own extents (west x 78..83.8 read at z 248.5..279, clipped at the Mayer face; east x 91..96 held to lawn #2166's own z range so no column stands past the surveyed court edge); soffit heights are figures. The soffit planes are [measured]; the column grid under them is the [estimated] pitch.
breezeway.galleryNote: Face-attached two-level gallery bays only (gap g2): along Bonner's court face from the podium stair to the chain, and along Mayer's face inside the measured west-arcade strip. measured.groundNote: Three arcgis.ground rings, none previously claimed by any key of campus-photo-detail.json (checked against every arcgis.ground#NNNN registration and every structured groundRings list), drawn as carpets one rung above the world's own ground fill over the IDENTICAL surveyed outline. derivations.why: The bar is keeling.roofs.pv: every figure sourced and derivable, with the arithmetic recorded. A round number with no derivation is a defect. Every metre this section draws is an `expr` evaluated in the test against these readings, a banded `estimate`, or a declared `draw` offset with a sibling Note saying why it is not a measurement.

survey.source: docs/data/campus-arcgis.json massing[112] (Mayer Hall) and massing[110] (Mayer Hall Addition), rings verbatim at /10; docs/data/campus-lidar.json massHeights keyed by POSITION (m:round(mean x),round(mean z)) and heights[] keyed by OSM name; docs/data/campus-3d.json buildings[395], the single OSM ring tagged 'Mayer Hall'. terrain.source: docs/data/campus-lidar.json terrain (CA_SanDiegoQL2 2014, decimetres /10), bilinear heightAt at the GIS ring's own corners — the same interpolation campus-terrain.js makeHeightSampler performs. surfaceAt (the drawn triangle) is what the MODULE seats on; these corner READS are the bilinear values, each reproduced by the suite to 0.01 m.

circle.source: The Addition ring's own east vertices: every vertex with x > 140 and z in [259.9, 323.8] — 108 of the 156 drawn — fed to a Kåsa least-squares circle fit. The suite recomputes the fit verbatim from the carried ring; the selection bounds are pinned so the population cannot drift.

storey.mayer.why: Mayer's floor-to-floor: the 2014 LiDAR height over the GIS ring divided by five storeys — five confirmed twice over (GIS levels; the physics department's own 1xxx-5xxx room series 1701/2218/3405/4322/5301). Quoted as measured 4.34 against the 4.26 the ArcGIS formula implies.

storey.addition.why: The Addition's floor-to-floor: LiDAR 23.8 (valid — 2004 predates the 2014 flight) over five storeys (GIS levels; tsilvaarch's 'five story addition'; the MYR-A room series). 4.76 m is credible for 2004 lab floors with interstitial services.

check.arcgisFormulaStorey.why: THE FORMULA, NOT A SURVEY: arcgis.h = 21.3 on both masses is levels x 4.26, the facilities rule of thumb (recon 0.1). It is storey-count evidence only — 5 levels, twice — and this figure exists so the loser of the height conflict stays legible.

check.additionOverMayer.why: The Addition tops Mayer by 2.1 m while standing on ground 0.1-0.6 m lower, so its parapet rides ~1.6-2.1 m above Mayer's — which is what the 2026 ortho's longer Addition shadow shows.

check.osmDraggedUp.why: THE CONTAMINATION, QUANTIFIED: heights['Mayer Hall'] = 23.2 sits 1.5 m ABOVE Mayer's own GIS-ring read because it was measured over the merged OSM blob and dragged toward the Addition's 23.8.

check.osmBelowAddition.why: The same percentile sits 0.6 m BELOW the Addition's own read — 23.2 is between the two buildings because it is a statistic over both, and is therefore a figure for NEITHER.

grade.westMean.why: The bilinear LiDAR ground at Mayer's two west corners, averaged: the high end of the site.

grade.eastMean.why: The same at the two east corners: the low end, level with the breezeway court. Cited from the LiDAR surface itself per R4 addendum 5 — never copied from a sibling section's number.

grade.fall.why: THE 4.1 m WEST->EAST FALL under Mayer (4.13 by this arithmetic; the dossier rounds to 4.1). junction.zOnMayerFace.why: The breezeway junction plane: Mayer's GIS north face interpolated at the OSM rings' x-midpoint — z 278.0. link.widthSouth.why: The link strip's width at the south end of the shared boundary: the Addition ring's (126.7, 308.9) against Mayer's east face at x 124.0.

reads.galleries: Continuous cantilevered floor plates run as OPEN GALLERIES on both long faces — full-length balconies behind solid balustrades with a thin rail, the same family as Bonner but deeper (1964 photograph; intact in the 2018 frame and tsilva-mayer-08). Tolerance: the system is certain, its depths are [estimated] and banded; the thin rail itself has no dimension and is not drawn (absent A7).
reads.endCurtainWall: The short ends are floor-to-roof mullioned curtain wall in 1964. EPOCH LIMIT: since 2004 the EAST end is the Addition's party boundary and no longer exists as a facade — only the WEST end ships glazing. Mullion module unsourced; the plane ships without mullions. Tolerance: a 60-year-old claim for the west face, corroborated by no modern frame square-on.
reads.pilotisRecessedGround: The ground floor is RECESSED glazing behind plain round/square pilotis with low storefront glazing and stepped planter walls absorbing the site fall — and NO ARCADE: the UCOP 2008 p11 mushroom arcade is the breezeway court's ground tier, bonner's, not a Mayer facade (research-mayer 7, all four eliminations). Tolerance: the recess ships as the storey-1 glass line at the gallery recess; pilotis and planters have no dimensions and are withheld (absent A6, A11).
reads.pvBands: Two long E-W PV arrays flank the monitor spine: north raw z 276..281 (true 280.7..285.7), south raw z 294..302 (true 298.7..306.7), block runs as carried in readings.ortho at threshold L < 135. Tolerance: ±0.5 m per edge at 4 px/m plus threshold sensitivity; runs shorter than 2 m are noise and dropped. POST-2014: present in the 2026 ortho, absent from the 2014-measured fabric.
reads.monitorSpine: The central clerestory/mech spine: true z ~289.7..296.7 (±1 m, ortho brightness profile), period fabric — it is the ridge element in the 1964 photograph. Its x extent is NOT resolvable in the ortho (panel and walkway clutter) and ships [estimated] between the measured arrays.
reads.orthoCorrection: A Mayer ROOF feature displaces (-0.8, -4.7) m in the raw 2026 ortho (west edge 52.0 vs face 52.7-52.9; parapets ~4.7 m north of their faces) — 0.22 m per metre of height, ~NNW, LOCAL to this pair. Ground reads are undisplaced. Tolerance: ±0.3 m per component; cross-checked against Argo's independent 0.204 m/m, never imported from it.
reads.eastGrade: The ground along Mayer's east face and the link strip is the LiDAR surface's own 20.40 m (bilinear reads at the NE and SE corners and at (125, 293)), level with the breezeway court's ~20.4. Cited from the surface itself per R4 addendum 5 — bonner derives the court figure and this section copies nothing from it.
reads.linkGlazed: The seam strip between the masses is a GLAZED LINK (tsilva-mayer-08 shows its blue mullioned curtain wall beside Mayer's galleries), and it is INSIDE the Addition's ring. Its exposed north and south stub faces ship as glass; its west boundary is Mayer's own east face and carries nothing. Tolerance: which stub the tsilva frame shows is unfixed (no station), but both stubs glazed is the only reading no frame contradicts.
reads.roofProfileDepth: The roof band table spans raw z 274..304 = 30 m against the ring's 31.2 m depth — self-consistent to the parapet bands the profile cannot separate from the plate edge.

draw.wallOffsetNote: A RENDER OFFSET, not a measurement: band planes stand this far proud of the surveyed ring so they are not coincident with the extruded prism's own faces. Not a claim that any fascia projects 60 mm.
draw.fieldOffsetNote: A RENDER OFFSET: the Addition's field and band planes stand this far proud of its ring, slightly inside Mayer's band offset so the two treatments cannot z-fight where the rings meet at the shared corner.
draw.topLiftNote: A RENDER OFFSET: horizontal deck and overhang top surfaces sit this far above their nominal plane so they resolve against the prism's own lid at grazing angles.
draw.datumStepNote: A SAMPLING INTERVAL, not a dimension: the drawn surface is read every 2 m along a ring or face (and at every vertex) to find datums and curtain feet. Finer changes nothing measurable.
draw.skirtDepthNote: A RENDER OFFSET: the Addition's wall field is carried this far below its datum so rolling terrain cannot open a gap at its foot. The datum is already the minimum drawn surface along the ring, so this only ever buries.
draw.faceMergeTolNote: A SURVEY-WOBBLE TOLERANCE: consecutive ring segments merge into one facade run while every vertex stays within this of the run's own chord. Mayer's 71 m north face arrives as six segments wobbling 0.1 m; 0.2 and 0.25 find the same four faces.
draw.glassSegNote: A CLIP GRANULARITY, not a dimension: the gallery glass line is drawn in runs of at most 3 m so the ground clip can withhold exactly the stretch the drawn terrain buries instead of the whole face.
draw.clipSamplesNote: A SAMPLING COUNT: the drawn surface is read at five stations across each glass segment's width to find the highest ground under it.
draw.clipGraceBelowNote: A NUMERICAL TOLERANCE, one centimetre, so a segment whose foot sits exactly on flat ground is built rather than withheld by floating-point noise.
draw.partyTolNote: A COINCIDENCE TOLERANCE: a face or edge whose endpoints and midpoint all lie within 0.08 m of the OTHER mass's ring polyline is the shared party boundary and is skipped. The shared segment matches at 0.0 exactly; the tolerance only guards float noise.
draw.linkBoxNote: A CLASSIFICATION BOX, not geometry: Addition edges whose midpoint falls inside it (and that are not party edges) are the glazed link's exposed stub faces and take glass instead of metal field. The box hugs the link strip the two rings define (x 123.7..126.7, z 277.7..308.9) with 0.3-0.6 m of slack.
draw.fieldMetalnessNote: A MATERIAL PARAMETER, not a measurement: the corrugated field is factory PAINT over steel — a dielectric coat — so its BRDF metalness is low and the declared tan albedo carries the read. The class default of 0.9 (raw metal) handed the surface to environment reflection and rendered the pinned #a79894 as espresso (visual critic V1); the suite pins this value and the texture's analytic mean so that class of defect cannot recur.
draw.fieldRoughnessNote: A MATERIAL PARAMETER, the same declaration's other half: weathered painted corrugation is matte enough that reflection does not dominate the albedo. Pinned by the suite alongside fieldMetalness.
draw.pvLiftNote: A RENDER OFFSET: the PV blocks float this far above the lid so the epoch-labelled layer never z-fights the 2014-measured plate it sits on.
draw.pvThicknessNote: A RENDER THICKNESS for the PV layer — panels plus rails read as decimetres from orbit and no source measures them; the layer is deliberately thin so the 21.7 LiDAR plane stays the roof.
draw.bedRungNote: A LADDER RUNG, not a height: campus-world.js already draws every arcgis.ground ring on the `ground` rung; this section's three carpets sit one rung above on `carpet` and give the same surveyed polygons the JETT project's materials. Nothing here re-outlines a ring.
draw.bedSegNote: A TESSELLATION TARGET: carpet triangles subdivide until no edge exceeds 3 m so they follow the drawn terrain instead of spanning it.
draw.bedMaxDepthNote: A RECURSION CAP on that subdivision so a pathological ring cannot generate an unbounded mesh.
draw.tilesNote: MATERIAL REPEAT LENGTHS in metres, not building dimensions: how often the code-generated texture repeats so microstructure lands at true material scale — a 1.2 m fascia panel, 0.6 m of exposed aggregate, a 0.9 m corrugated metal sheet, coarse planting. Texture maps are code-generated throughout; the sampled colours feed the materials and the photographs' pixels never do.

gallery.storeyNote: 21.7 / 5 = 4.34 m, the measured module (derivations figures['storey.mayer']); the ArcGIS 4.26 formula is the recorded loser. The storey grid HANGS FROM THE LID and steps down five times, so storey 1's foot lands exactly on the prism's base — the median-ground elevation the LiDAR height is measured against.
gallery.longFaceMinNote: A CLASSIFIER, not a dimension: Mayer's merged faces are ~71.1 m (two long gallery faces), ~31.3 m (west curtain end) and ~31.0 m (east party boundary); 60 separates the first pair from the rest with 10 m of slack on either side.
gallery.curtainFaceRangeNote: The same classifier's second bin: the two ~31 m short ends. The east one is then excluded by the party test, leaving exactly one curtain face — the WEST end.
gallery.systemNote: THE HORIZONTAL SYSTEM ONLY, per face and complete on every face it touches (the ultra standard): slab fascia + balustrade band + recessed glass line on both long faces, curtain glass on the west end, NOTHING on the east party plane, and the roof fascia riding the overhang. No bay, pier, stair, opening grid or mullion is drawn anywhere — the bay count has no source (absent A1) and a rhythm at a guessed module would be an invented rhythm on a sourced building.

groundClip.rule: A glass segment ships only if its storey's FOOT clears the drawn surface at every one of five stations across its own width (one centimetre of grace). Otherwise the WHOLE segment is withheld and counted — glazing emerging from the dirt is a ground-floor condition no source shows.
groundClip.terrainNote: THE R4 TWO-COUNT RULE: the source grid gives 240 gallery glass segments per the declared segmentation; on flat ground all 240 of the clip-eligible ones build (0 withheld), and on the drawn LiDAR surface 34 are withheld — every one on the uphill (west) stretch, which is the 4.1 m fall doing exactly what figures['grade.fall'] says it does. Both counts are gated; a change to the sources and a change to the terrain move different numbers.

addition.storeyNote: 23.8 / 5 = 4.76 m (derivations figures['storey.addition']), LiDAR-derived — the 2004 building predates the 2014 flight, so massHeights is a valid measurement of it.

circle.note: THE MEASURED ARC: every Addition ring vertex with x > 140 between z 259.9 and 323.8 lies on one circle — centre (75.1, 305.4), R 74.3 m, worst 0.70 m over 108 vertices (Kåsa fit, recomputed by the suite from the carried ring). The module never re-draws it: the treatment hangs off the ring's own chords, so gating the ring gates the facade.

addition.systemNote: Field + floor bands, complete on every drawn edge: tan corrugated metal panel between buff concrete bands at the four floor lines, a parapet fascia at the crown, a skirt below the datum, the link's stub faces in glass — and NO WINDOW: the punched rhythm is photographed but unscaled, and which glazing system sits on which face is unresolved (absent A8). The north stair drum is the ring's own north jogs and takes the same complete treatment; its slot windows are withheld (absent A9).

roof.monitorNote: PERIOD FABRIC (1963): the ridge element in the 1964 photograph, the mid-grey spine in the 2026 ortho at true z 289.7..296.7. z band read; x extent and height [estimated], and the mesh is named mayer-roof-monitor-estimated so the tier is visible in a render.

pv.epoch: POST-2014, POST-LiDAR FABRIC: the two arrays are present in the 2026 ortho and absent from the fabric the 2014 flight measured at 21.7 m. They ship as a thin layer ON the 2014 lid (draw.pvLift + draw.pvThickness) and are never absorbed into a taller prism — LiDAR stays the height authority and the arrays stay an epoch label.
pv.dxTrueNote: The x half of this pair's own local ortho correction (figures['ortho.correctionX']), applied to the raw block runs below to place them in the true frame. z bands are carried in true frame already.
pv.arraysNote: The block runs are readings.ortho's own dark runs VERBATIM (the suite asserts deepEqual); z bands are the corrected band-table extents. North array: four blocks split by service gaps. South array: three blocks, nearly continuous. The W plate (raw x 53..60) is plain roof — neither array reaches the west end.

breezeway.note: BONNER'S ENTIRE (R4 addendum 4) — chains, decks, umbrellas, court, the ground vault tier, both junctions and the landing planes at Mayer's north face. This section records the junction plane only: Mayer's GIS north face at z ~278.0 (figures['junction.zOnMayerFace']), x 84.1..91.0; the decks land NEAR Mayer levels 2/3 — landing levels UNRESOLVED (arbitration D3: the level-3 floor arithmetic +8.68 over the ~20.4 court sits 0.68 m above bonner's measured deck-2 plane +8.0; possibly real steps down the chain, bb61786853 — deferred with bonner's g8). counts.breezewayElements is a DECLARED ZERO.

mayer.colorSourcesNote: Channel mean is (R+G+B)/3 with the sample rectangle pinned (R4 addendum 3) — never the word 'luminance' for that quantity; Rec.709 luminance is carried separately where computed. samples.note: SAMPLES THIS SECTION MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CONSUME.
