counts.note: Declared counts, asserted against the built scene ON FLAT GROUND, where they describe the grid the sources give rather than what one terrain leaves of it. What the drawn LiDAR surface withholds is declared separately in system.gallery.groundClip (the R4 two-count rule), so a change to the sources and a change to the terrain move different numbers. The zeroes are OPINIONS, not omissions.

conflicts.what: Which height Mayer Hall stands at. lidar.heights['Mayer Hall'] says 23.2; the GIS-ring read says 21.7; the OSM tag says 20; the ArcGIS field says 21.3.
sides: lidar.heights['Mayer Hall'] = 23.2 — REAL MEASUREMENT, WRONG POLYGON: it is a percentile over osm:395, ONE ring covering Mayer + the whole Addition + a SE service yard to x 162.9 (26 verts, x 54.5..162.9, z 247.9..326.9), so it is dragged toward the Addition's 23.8 and is a figure for neither building. The suite recomputes the blob's bbox and proves it spans both GIS rings.
lidar.massHeights['m:91,290'] = 21.7 and ['m:140,286'] = 23.8 — the same flight over each building's OWN GIS ring, keyed by position: the only per-building heights that exist.
OSM tag h = 20 — a mapper's guess on the merged ring; no measurement behind it.
arcgis.h = 21.3 on BOTH masses — levels x 4.26, the facilities formula (recon 0.1): storey-count evidence only (5 levels, twice), never a height source.
The 2026 ortho corroborates the blob's SE annex (x ~149..163, z ~300..327) as a paved service yard with parked vehicles and low utility structures — not five-storey building (research-mayer 8.3).
conflicts.resolution: GIS RINGS WIN WITH THE MECHANISM STATED: Mayer anchors to 21.7 and the Addition to 23.8, each over its own ring. The losers — 23.2 (merged-ring percentile), 20 (OSM tag), 21.3 (formula) — are all recorded and none is used. The arithmetic that shows the contamination ships as figures['check.osmDraggedUp'] (+1.5) and ['check.osmBelowAddition'] (+0.6): 23.2 lies BETWEEN the two buildings because it is a statistic over both. The module performs no name lookup against any measured file.

conflicts.what: How big and how expensive the 2004 Addition project was. Three first-party project pages, three areas, two costs.
sides: tsilvaarch.com (senior project architect's own page): 'Renovation and five story addition … 130,000 gross square feet … $31 million', design architect credited Perkins+Will.
jett.land (landscape architect, 2009): 'a major renovation and 45,000 SF addition', architect 'MBT Architecture (now Perkins & Will)'.
p2sinc.com (MEP engineer): existing Mayer '112,000 SF', addition '80,000 SF', cost '$45,000,000', five stories both.
conflicts.resolution: DECLARED, NOT AVERAGED, NOT RESOLVED — the figures plausibly measure different scopes (project total gsf vs addition-only sf vs assignable) but no source says which, so no figure ships. What every source agrees on ships: five storeys, one architect lineage (MBT -> Perkins&Will), renovation + addition done together, completed 2004 — which is what makes LiDAR 23.8 a valid measurement of it.

conflicts.what: Whether Mayer and the Addition are two masses separated by a 1.3-2.7 m open seam. The research dossier's 0.5 says the Addition's west edge stands at x 125.3..126.7 leaving a gap against Mayer's face; the carried ring says otherwise.
sides: research-mayer.md 0.5 and 4.2: 'Mayer's east face x 123.7..124.0, the Addition's local west edge x 125.3..126.7 at the same z. The ~1.3-2.7 m seam is the glazed link + the mural walk' — read off the ring's end vertices at the notch and the south corner.

arcgis.massing[110].r[0] verbatim, vertices 30..35: (125.3, 277.7) -> (123.7, 277.7) -> (123.7, 277.8) -> (124.0, 308.7) -> (124.0, 308.9) -> (126.7, 308.9). The Addition's ring runs ALONG Mayer's east face for the whole shared z range: the link strip is INSIDE the Addition's surveyed ring and the two prisms are contiguous. x 125.3 and 126.7 are the strip's EAST edge at its two ends, not a west edge.
conflicts.resolution: THE RING WINS — it is the survey, and the extraction is pasted in the buildlog. Consequences shipped: no link volume is invented (the extruder already closes the strip at 23.8, so no daylight slot exists to fill); Mayer's east face and the Addition's coincident segment are PARTY PLANES and neither module hangs a facade there (both skips counted); the link's exposed stub faces take the sourced glass. The dossier's seam widths survive as figures['link.widthNorth'/'link.widthSouth'] = 1.6 / 2.7 — the STRIP's widths, correctly attributed. Recorded in superseded['research.seamAsGap'] rather than silently built around.

conflicts.what: Which road flanks Mayer on which side — an inherited habit of calling the eastern road Ridge Walk.
sides: Casual usage in earlier zone notes placed Ridge Walk east of the Revelle buildings it passes.

The JETT labelled plan and the campus map: RIDGE WALK is the N-S walk WEST of Mayer (between Urey Addition and Mayer); the road east of the Addition is EUCALYPTUS LANE, with FIRE ACCESS off it and the PARK BOUNDARY beyond.
conflicts.resolution: THE LABELLED PLAN WINS: Ridge Walk west, Eucalyptus Lane east. It matters because two boundary decisions hang on it — the bunch-grass crescent (#1254) is bounded by the LANE, not by Ridge Walk, and the western boundary against R5/R6 is the WALK. Recorded so no later agent re-inherits the swap.

conflicts.what: When Mayer Hall became an APS historic site.
sides: today.ucsd.edu (2021-07-02 story): designated 2021, plaque photographed.
blink named-buildings snippet: 'in 2022 … recognized'.
conflicts.resolution: DECLARED AND COSMETIC: nothing geometric hangs on it. The 2021 story is first-party and dated; the blink page is JS-gated and read only through search snippets, so 2021 is quoted where a single year is needed and the split stays on the record.

research.seamAsGap.claims: research-mayer.md 0.5's reading that the Addition's local west edge stands at x 125.3..126.7, leaving a 1.3-2.7 m OPEN seam between two nearly-touching masses, to be modelled as a glazed link volume filling a daylight slot.
ships: conflicts['mayer-seam-dossier-vs-ring'] — the ring extraction that replaces it
derivations.figures['link.widthNorth'] and ['link.widthSouth'] — the strip's widths, correctly attributed to the strip INSIDE the Addition's ring
counts.partyFacesMayer and counts.partyEdgesAddition — the shared boundary skipped from both sides
the link's stub faces in glass (counts.linkPanels), on the ring's own edges, inventing no volume
research.seamAsGap.why: DELETED ON EVIDENCE: arcgis.massing[110].r[0] vertices 30..35 run (125.3,277.7) -> (123.7,277.7) -> (123.7,277.8) -> (124.0,308.7) -> (124.0,308.9) -> (126.7,308.9) — the Addition's surveyed boundary runs along Mayer's east face for the whole shared range, so the seam is a strip INSIDE the Addition's ring, not a gap between rings. A link volume built to fill the dossier's gap would have DOUBLED geometry the extruder already draws at 23.8. The dossier's two width figures were correct as distances and mis-attributed as a gap; both survive, re-attributed.

mayer.supersededNote: One record. Mayer absorbs nothing from revelle.systems (that is urey's and bonner's mechanism, R4 addendum 2) and no revelle absent entry names Mayer, so main has NO revelle.superseded flip to apply for this section.
absent: A1 — THE BAY RHYTHM, all of it: structural bay count, pier spacing, window widths, mullion modules, and the opening grid on every face of Mayer. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — the 1964 corner frame is oblique and the 2018/tsilva frames look along the galleries, none shows one long face end to end with countable bays; Street View — attempted 2026-08-21 and yielded nothing: a web search for Street View / photosphere coverage of the Revelle science spine finds one published Revelle photosphere (360cities, Norm Olson, captured 2016-11-19) stationed at the Jacaranda court by Urey and Natural Sciences, which does not see this face, and Google's pedestrian (trike) coverage cannot be enumerated non-interactively from this environment — no dated frame of this face surfaced; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — UCOP 2008 carries no Mayer elevation and no drawing set is cached; archives — no Risley & Gould set found, OAC finding aids unprobed. The long faces ship the HORIZONTAL system only and counts.openings is a DECLARED ZERO — a ribbon at a guessed module would be an invented rhythm on a sourced building.

A2 — 'MAYER HALL AUDITORIUM', named in the R4 brief and UNLOCATABLE. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — no frame shows an auditorium volume; Street View — attempted 2026-08-21 and yielded nothing: a web search for Street View / photosphere coverage of the Revelle science spine finds one published Revelle photosphere (360cities, Norm Olson, captured 2016-11-19) stationed at the Jacaranda court by Urey and Natural Sciences, which does not see this face, and Google's pedestrian (trike) coverage cannot be enumerated non-interactively from this environment — no dated frame of this face surfaced; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the physics department's own room lists top out at MH 4322 'Mayer Room' (55-60 seats) and two 50-seat MYR-A classrooms, and the School's facilities page offers a 70-seat 'full meeting space' at 1701 Mayer Hall — no auditorium; archives — nothing in LiDAR or the 2026 ortho shows a massing bump for one. ABSENT: no auditorium volume is modelled and none is denied a future source.

A3 — THE 'MAYER HALL' NAME MURAL's exact wall. The 2018 frame shows it (portraits, vertical lettering) on a wall at the covered east-end walk by the Addition link, but no source pins the wall to a coordinate. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — the night frame has no fixable background; Street View — attempted 2026-08-21 and yielded nothing: a web search for Street View / photosphere coverage of the Revelle science spine finds one published Revelle photosphere (360cities, Norm Olson, captured 2016-11-19) stationed at the Jacaranda court by Urey and Natural Sciences, which does not see this face, and Google's pedestrian (trike) coverage cannot be enumerated non-interactively from this environment — no dated frame of this face surfaced; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — none; archives — the mural is modern. The zone rule forbids rendering lettering in any case, so the mural is recorded and not placed.

A4 — THE GILDED SPHERE on its plinth near the link (tsilva-mayer-08, rect px 290..350 x 400..440, RGB ~(135, 116, 73)). Identity and position unsourced. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — one frame, unstationed; Street View — attempted 2026-08-21 and yielded nothing: a web search for Street View / photosphere coverage of the Revelle science spine finds one published Revelle photosphere (360cities, Norm Olson, captured 2016-11-19) stationed at the Jacaranda court by Urey and Natural Sciences, which does not see this face, and Google's pedestrian (trike) coverage cannot be enumerated non-interactively from this environment — no dated frame of this face surfaced; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — the JETT plan marks no sphere; archives — nothing. An unnamed landmark on a guessed coordinate is exactly the invented entity this file exists to refuse.

A5 — THE DIAGONAL EXTERNAL STAIRS that cut across the gallery faces between levels (1964 frame, two visible; dc-bb9352649m corroborates the type). Their EXISTENCE is sourced; their POSITIONS are functions of the bay rhythm A1 withholds. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — both frames oblique, neither fixes a stair to a bay; Street View — attempted 2026-08-21 and yielded nothing: a web search for Street View / photosphere coverage of the Revelle science spine finds one published Revelle photosphere (360cities, Norm Olson, captured 2016-11-19) stationed at the Jacaranda court by Urey and Natural Sciences, which does not see this face, and Google's pedestrian (trike) coverage cannot be enumerated non-interactively from this environment — no dated frame of this face surfaced; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — none; archives — no drawing set. No stair is drawn; when A1 closes, the stairs close with it.

A6 — THE PILOTIS: the ground floor's plain round/square columns (1964 frame — and NOT an arcade order, research-mayer 7). No diameter, spacing or count in any source; the recessed storey-1 glass line ships and the columns in front of it do not. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — oblique; Street View — attempted 2026-08-21 and yielded nothing: a web search for Street View / photosphere coverage of the Revelle science spine finds one published Revelle photosphere (360cities, Norm Olson, captured 2016-11-19) stationed at the Jacaranda court by Urey and Natural Sciences, which does not see this face, and Google's pedestrian (trike) coverage cannot be enumerated non-interactively from this environment — no dated frame of this face surfaced; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — none; archives — none.

A7 — THE BALUSTRADE'S THIN RAIL and the gallery soffit detail. The solid band ships at its banded estimate; the rail above it (1964 and tsilva-08, a thin steel line) has no dimension. Ladder climbed and failed: photos — visible in both frames, unmeasurable in either; Street View — attempted 2026-08-21 and yielded nothing: a web search for Street View / photosphere coverage of the Revelle science spine finds one published Revelle photosphere (360cities, Norm Olson, captured 2016-11-19) stationed at the Jacaranda court by Urey and Natural Sciences, which does not see this face, and Google's pedestrian (trike) coverage cannot be enumerated non-interactively from this environment — no dated frame of this face surfaced; drone/video — nothing found; planning docs — none; archives — none. Drawn: nothing.
